# WHY v12 == 8 â€” OFFLINE INVESTIGATION (2026-08-08)

Question: CL_ParseGamestate @ 0x462B00 bails at `if (v12 != 7) { while (v12 == 1) ...
return sub_DC6C0(a2); }`. Measured v12 = 8. Why?

## PROVEN â€” the field model is correct; there is no hidden read

Call sequence taken from DISASSEMBLY (not decompiler statement order), 0x462B00..0x462CA5:

    sub_45AF50, sub_6C520, sub_665C00, CL_GetLocalClientActive,
    MSG_ReadLong  @0x462B73     <- serverCommandSequence
    sub_B8C40,
    MSG_ReadString@0x462BB2     (r8d = 20h -> maxlen 32)   <- mapname
    MSG_ReadLong  @0x462BBA
    MSG_ReadString@0x462BD4     (r8d = 20h)                <- gametype
    sub_DC870     @0x462BDC     <- v9  (MSG_ReadBit)
    Dvar_SetBool, sub_DC870 @0x462BF5 <- v10, sub_857A10,
    MSG_ReadLong  @0x462C10     <- v11
    CL_IsDemoPlaying (+ the !demo-only branch: sub_DEE80/DEF90/769050/DFAF0/Com_Error)
    MSG_ReadBits  @0x462C57     `mov edx, 4`  <- v12, 4 BITS confirmed
      then: cmp eax,7 / jz LABEL_12 ; cmp eax,1 / jnz -> sub_DC6C0 (error exit)

The opcode read in CL_ParseServerMessage_Internal @0x463730 is likewise `mov edx, 4`.
So: no hidden reads, no wrong widths. The model matches the engine exactly.

Cursor model also verified against ALL FOUR readers â€” byte reads touch only +36,
bit reads only +40, and they resync only when (bitpos & 7) == 0:
  MSG_ReadBits 0xDC910, MSG_ReadBit 0xDC870, MSG_ReadLong 0xDD0B0,
  MSG_ReadString 0xDD310 (byte loop to NUL; the `32` is the DEST size, not a length).
  sub_665C00 is just `*(DWORD*)(msg+44) = -1` â€” touches neither cursor.

## PROVEN â€” the exact bytes, identical in every demo

airshipdemo pkt0 decoded (1242 B, byte0 = 0x20):

    [0]      0x20            opcode nibble 0 (+ bits 4,5 read later as v9,v10)
    [1..4]   01 00 00 00     serverCommandSequence = 1
    [5..15]  "mp_airship\0"
    [16..19] long
    [20..23] "war\0"                          readcount = 24
    [24..27] 00 00 00 00     v11 = 0
    [28..30] 36 6C 00        <- 3 bytes before the serverinfo string
    [31..]   "\scr_game_allowkillcam\1\scr_team_fftype\0\..."

dday is identical in shape (gap bytes 00 00 00 00 36 6C 00, byte for byte).

Engine's own probe reported `size=1249 byte0=0x20` for dday, BYTE-EXACT with the
offline decoder â€” so tools/s2_huffman.py is validated against the live engine.

## Why the engine computes 8

After the 4-bit opcode: bitpos = 4, readcount = 1. Byte reads advance readcount only,
so bitpos is STILL 4 when the two MSG_ReadBit calls run â€” they take bits 4 and 5 of
byte0 (0x20 -> v9 = 0, v10 = 1). MSG_ReadBits(4) for v12 then takes the remaining
bits 6,7 of byte0 (= 0) as its LOW two bits and 2 bits of byte[28] (0x36 & 3 = 2) as
its HIGH two:  v12 = 0 | (2 << 2) = 8.

## DISPROVEN â€” every alignment hypothesis tried

  * faithful engine model                      -> v12 = 8
  * "writer was byte-aligned" (bit reads restart at readcount) -> v12 = 0
  * every 4-bit window of byte 28 (0x36)       -> 6, 11, 13, 6, 3
  * BRUTE FORCE over bit offsets 160..272, requiring v12 in {1,7} THEN a byte-aligned
    u16 count in 1..6994 THEN printable string bytes: **ZERO plausible candidates.**

## â­ THE CLUE â€” `36 6C 00` is the ASCII STRING "6l"

Not v12 + count. S2 names things with numeric strings everywhere (dvar "1762",
commands "365"/"373", Com_Error ids "439"/"458"), so "6l" reads as a configstring
VALUE, with the serverinfo as the next string.

STRONG INFERENCE: the demo's gamestate does NOT contain the inline
`[v12 nibble][u16 count][per-entry bit + string]` block that CL_ParseGamestate and
CL_ParseConfigStrings_Internal expect. This is the SAME class of defect already proven
for the 2-byte length prefix â€” the demo writer and the live reader disagree on framing.
That is now two independent framing mismatches in the same message.

For reference, CL_ParseConfigStrings_Internal @ 0x462930 expects:
    u16 count
    per entry: 1 bit â€” set => index = last+1, clear => index = MSG_ReadBits(13)

    netconststring indices (sub_DFC80) go to sub_DFF10 instead.

# â­â­â­ THE DEMO GAMESTATE DEFECT, ISOLATED BY LIVE-vs-DEMO DIFF (2026-08-08)

Method: decode a KNOWN-GOOD live gamestate (captured by our own recorder into
.dm_s2 TLV id 7) and diff it against a demo's, both fully offline.

## PROVEN â€” the msg_t cursor model is CORRECT (validated on live data)

Simulating CL_ParseServerMessage_Internal + CL_ParseGamestate over the live capture
`demos/d_day.0000.dm_s2`:

    [0] op=2 cmd seq=1 '2 A 6 A A A A A 20 21 0 0 0'
    [1] op=0 GAMESTATE cmdSeq=1 map='mp_d_day' gt='war' v9=0 v10=0 v11=104816208
            v12=1  -> configstring count=117
              cs[0] = '\scr_game_allowkillcam\1\scr_team_fftype\0\2043\0\2299\1...'
              cs[1] = ''
              cs[3] = '144'          <- serverId, exactly as CL_ConfigstringModified expects
              cs[6] = '0'

117 configstrings with correct indices and strings. The model is not a guess.

Live gamestate_message TLV: [u32 seq][u32 flags: low31=entry readcount, bit31=useZlib]
[msg data]. For d_day.0000: readcount=8, useZlib=1, int16 length=1047 -> 2257 bytes.

## PROVEN â€” the layout of the 7-byte region after the gametype string

    LIVE : C4 | 50 5E 3F 06 | 75 00     flags=0xC4, v11=0x063F5E50, count=117
    DEMO : 00 | 00 00 00 36 | 6C 00     flags=0x00, v11=0x36000000, count=108

Same structure, same field order. The flags byte packs FOUR things:

    bit0    = v9        (-> Dvar_SetBool off_1BD3708)
    bit1    = v10       (-> if set, dword_8BDA060 = 1 and the install is skipped)
    bits2-5 = v12       (1 = configstrings follow, 7 = EOF)   <-- THE GATE
    bit6    = the FIRST configstring's delta bit (1 => index = last+1)

**LIVE has 0xC4. ALL FIVE DEMOS have 0x00.** With v12 = 0, CL_ParseGamestate takes
`if (v12 != 7) { while (v12 == 1) ...; return sub_DC6C0(a2); }` â€” the early error exit â€”
before configstrings, before sub_70830(client, map, gametype), before anything that
could advance connstate. That is why connstate stays 5 and the priming loop runs away.

Patching the demo's flags byte to live's 0xC4 makes it decode:
`cs[0] = '\scr_game_allowkillcam\1\scr_team_fftype\0\2043\0\2299\18\...'`, 106/108 sane.

## PROVEN â€” a second, related misalignment

In LIVE the gamestate is the SECOND record: the preceding op=2 command consumes byte0's
low nibble, so the gamestate opcode is read from the HIGH nibble and bitpos ends at 8 â€”
BYTE-ALIGNED. Its v9/v10/v12 then come from a fresh byte.

In every DEMO the gamestate is the FIRST record, so its opcode comes from the low
nibble, bitpos sticks at 4, and every later bit read is stolen from byte0's leftover
nibble (that is the mechanical reason v12 computed as 8).

## STRONG INFERENCE â€” S2's demo writer serialised the gamestate BYTE-ALIGNED

Reading the demo's configstring block as plain sequential NUL-terminated strings
(no per-entry bits at all) consumes every entry cleanly:

    demo          flags  count  entries      sane  leftover
    airshipdemo   0x00   108    108/108      89    35 bytes
    egyptbots     0x00   108    108/108      89    35
    gibraltar     0x00   108    108/108      89    35
    dday          0x00   108    108/108      89    35
    publicmatch   0x00   119    119/119      98    35

    all: cs[0] = '\scr_game_allowkillcam\1\scr_team_fftype\0\2043\0\2299\...'

So the writer emitted NO packed bits â€” no v12 nibble, no per-entry delta bits â€” which
explains the zeroed flags byte and why the bit-level reader cannot walk the block.
This is the same class of writer/reader framing mismatch already proven for the missing
2-byte length prefix. Native demo playback cannot work in the shipped game.

## â­ publicmatch is NOT a special case

Structurally identical to the four private demos: same zeroed flags byte, same
sequential block, all 119 entries read. Its only differences are 119 configstrings
instead of 108 (more players) and a different serverinfo tail (\12\3175\2 vs \18\5656\C).
Its earlier unique failure was the priming runaway, which is already fixed. Whatever
repairs the private demos repairs publicmatch.

## NOT YET RESOLVED â€” do not ship a fix until these are answered

  1. ~82-88% of entries are "sane"; the rest carry a leading binary byte, e.g.
     entry[3] = 0x18 + "32" where LIVE has cs[3] = "144" (serverId). So the per-entry
     INDEX encoding is not pinned down.
  2. A constant 35-byte tail remains after the last string in EVERY demo â€” unexplained.

Installing 108 configstrings at WRONG indices would be worse than installing none
(CL_ConfigstringModified special-cases index 3 = serverId, and the netconststring
ranges are index-sensitive). Resolve 1 and 2 first.

# CONFIGSTRING BLOCK DECODED â€” the reconstruction works on all 5 demos (2026-08-08)

## CORRECTION â€” the block IS bit-packed; "sequential strings" was my wrong model

Raw hex of dday's decoded gamestate after the serverinfo string:

    191  00 | 00 | 00 | 18 | 33 32 00       ...."32"
                      ^^ BIT BYTE, not a string prefix
    199  30 00 | 08 A0 | 2D 32 31 2E ...    "0"..-21.699951
    279  ...   | FF    | 30 2E 34 20 ...    ..0.4 0.6

Those bytes are what the inline MSG_ReadBit in CL_ParseConfigStrings_Internal consumes
when bitpos is byte-aligned: ONE byte supplies up to 8 entries' delta bits while the
strings advance readcount separately. 0xFF = eight consecutive sequential-index deltas.
My earlier "no per-entry bits, just sequential strings" reading is WITHDRAWN.

    u16 count
    per entry: 1 bit  -> set   : index = last + 1
                      -> clear : index = MSG_ReadBits(13)
               then a NUL-terminated string via sub_DC7C0 @ 0xDC7C0
                    (byte loop from readcount, maps '%' (37) -> '.' (46),
                     into the 16 KB static buffer byte_5C41240)
    Com_Error "458" if index > 0x1B61 (6993); "459" if stringData would exceed 0x20000

# THE 2% ANOMALY RUN TO GROUND â€” a single-byte reconstruction is NOT sufficient

## Traced: it is a phase discontinuity in the first few entries

Instrumented per-entry trace of dday with flags := 0xC4:

    [ 0] bit 222->223  rc  34-> 197  delta      idx=0    '\scr_game_allowkillcam\1\...'
    [ 1] bit 223->224  rc 197-> 198  delta      idx=1    ''
    [ 2] bit 224->1598 rc 198-> 203  RESYNC(byte198) explicit13 idx=3072  '32'
    [ 3] bit1598->1636 rc 203-> 206  explicit13 idx=0    ''        <- ate the "0" string
    [ 4] bit1636->1637 rc 206-> 242  delta      idx=1    '\x08\xa0-21.699951 3180.6...'
    [ 5] bit1637->1638 rc 242-> 250  delta      idx=2    '0 0 0 1'
    [ 6] bit1638->2012 rc 250-> 254  explicit13 idx=138  '0'       <- recovers, clean from here

Entry 3's 13-bit index consumes the bytes that actually hold the string "0", and entry
4 then inherits `08 A0` (real index bits) as string data. From index 138 onward every
entry is clean and monotonic.

## PROVEN â€” no flags-byte value can fix it

Brute force over all 256 values, dday and publicmatch:

    flags=0xC4/0xC5/0xC6/0xC7  sane=106/108  monotonic=106/107  lastIdx=6943   <- tied max
    flags=0x87/0x86            sane= 91/108  monotonic= 68/107  lastIdx=0

0xC4..0xC7 tie because the low two bits are v9/v10, which do not affect parsing. So
0xC4 is the best a single-byte reconstruction can achieve, and it is not enough.

## â›” WHY THIS MUST NOT SHIP AS-IS â€” serverId lands at the wrong index

Expected sequence (from the LIVE gamestate and from the earlier .dm_s2 analysis in this
file): 0, 1, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, then the 138.. settings block.
LIVE produced exactly cs[0], cs[1], cs[3], cs[6].

Reconstruction produces:

    expected:  0    1    3       6    7    8    9    138 ...
    got:       0    1    3072    0    1    2    138 ...

'32' â€” which should be cs[3], the SERVERID â€” lands at 3072. CL_ConfigstringModified
special-cases index 3 (it fires CL_ServerIdChanged), and the netconststring ranges are
index-sensitive, so installing this would corrupt state in a new way rather than fix
anything. Strings are ~98% correct; the INDICES of the opening entries are not.

# â­ FOUND THE DEMO CONFIGSTRING WRITER â€” sub_9111B0 (2026-08-08)

`sub_9111B0` @ IDA 0x9111B0 is CL_Demo_WriteConfigStrings. Behaviour-proven:

    sub_DD8B0(msg, 1, 4);                 // MSG_WriteBits(value=1, bits=4)  <- writes v12 = 1
    count = number of indices where !NetConstString(i) && (i < 2 || stringOffsets[i])
    MSG_WriteShort(msg, count);
    last = -1;
    for (i = 0; i < 7010; ++i) {
        if (NetConstString(i)) continue;              // sub_DFC80
        str = (i == 1) ? sub_664FE0(4096)
                       : (i && !stringOffsets[i]) ? skip
                                                  : stringData + stringOffsets[i];
        if (i == last + 1) sub_DD850(msg);            // MSG_WriteBit(1)  -> delta
        else { sub_DD810(msg); sub_DD8B0(msg, i, 13); } // MSG_WriteBit(0) + 13-bit index
        last = i;
        sub_DD7C0(msg, str);                          // MSG_WriteString
    }

Newly named MSG writers (behaviour-proven from this use):
    sub_DD8B0  MSG_WriteBits(msg, value, bits)
    sub_DD850  MSG_WriteBit1        sub_DD810  MSG_WriteBit0
    sub_DD7C0  MSG_WriteString      sub_DFC80  NetConstStrings_HasIndex

Callers (all demo write path): sub_914790 (0x914790, also called from
CL_Demo_ProcessPacket_Type2_3 and CL_Demo_ReadDemoMessage â€” the keyframe writer),
sub_91B130 (0x91B130), sub_91C710 (0x91C710), sub_91D190 (0x91D190).

âš  The loop bound is **7010**, not MAX_CONFIGSTRINGS 6994 â€” the same 7010 the .dm_s2
scanner flagged in the recorded gamestate offsets blob. Consistent with a stale
constant in the demo path.

## CONSEQUENCE â€” the configstring block is framed CORRECTLY by construction

The writer emits v12 as 4 bits, then the count as a short, then per-entry
[1 bit delta | 1 bit + 13-bit index] + string. That is EXACTLY what
CL_ParseGamestate + CL_ParseConfigStrings_Internal read. So the block itself is fine.

The defect is therefore UPSTREAM: whatever writes the gamestate header (opcode,
serverCommandSequence, mapname, long, gametype, v9, v10, v11) before calling
sub_9111B0 leaves the BIT PHASE different from what CL_ParseGamestate assumes. That
single phase error explains all three observed symptoms at once:
    * the missing 2-byte length prefix
    * the zeroed flags byte (v9/v10/v12 land in bits nobody wrote)
    * the opening entries' indices being wrong while everything from index 138 is clean

## NEXT STEP

Decompile the header writer â€” the caller of sub_9111B0 that also writes the mapname and
gametype strings; sub_914790 @ 0x914790 is the prime candidate (it is already known to
be called from CL_Demo_ProcessPacket_Type2_3 and CL_Demo_ReadDemoMessage). Compare its

will be visible there, and it should be fixable as ONE defect rather than three

DO NOT ship the flags-byte reconstruction meanwhile: brute force over all 256 values

# â­â­â­ ROOT CAUSE OF THE GAMESTATE FAILURE â€” A ONE-BIT WRITER BUG (2026-08-08)

`sub_91D190` @ IDA 0x91D190 is **CL_Demo_WriteGameState**. Behaviour-proven, and it is
the twin of MW3's CL_Demo_WriteGameState @ 0x1e2bd0 (same shape, same position, calls
the configstring writer in the same place).

    MSG_WriteLong (msg, clc[77]);          // leading message sequence
    MSG_WriteBits (msg, 0, 4);             // svc_gamestate opcode
    MSG_WriteLong (msg, clc[32849]);       // serverCommandSequence
    MSG_WriteString(msg, mapname);
    MSG_WriteLong (msg, clientActive+25556);
    MSG_WriteString(msg, gametype);
    MSG_WriteBit  (msg, sub_B8C70());      // <-- ONE bit
    MSG_WriteLong (msg, 0);                // v11 == 0  (every demo has v11 == 0)
    CL_Demo_WriteConfigStrings(client,msg,0);   // writes v12 = 1 as 4 bits, then count...
    MSG_WriteBits (msg, 7, 4);             // EOF
    MSG_WriteLong (msg, clc[4]);           // clientNum
    MSG_WriteLong (msg, clc[76]);          // checksumFeed
    MSG_WriteBits (msg, 7, 4);             // EOF

CL_ParseGamestate @ 0x462B00 reads, at the same point:

    sub_DC870(msg)   -> v9      // MSG_ReadBit
    sub_DC870(msg)   -> v10     // MSG_ReadBit   <-- SECOND BIT, NEVER WRITTEN
    MSG_ReadLong     -> v11
    MSG_ReadBits(4)  -> v12

**THE WRITER WRITES ONE BIT WHERE THE READER READS TWO.** One missing MSG_WriteBit.

## The one-bit shift predicts all three measured values exactly

    v9  = the writer's real bit                       = 0   (measured 0)
    v10 = steals v12's low bit; written v12 = 1       -> 1   (measured 1)
    v12 = (written_v12 >> 1) | (first delta bit << 3)
        = (1 >> 1) | (1 << 3) = 0 | 8                 = 8   (measured 8)

Three independent values predicted from a single missing bit. This supersedes every
earlier hypothesis about the flags byte, alignment, or a "byte-aligned writer":
  - the "zeroed flags byte" was the one-bit shift seen from the wrong side;
  - the wrong opening configstring indices were the same shift propagating;
  - CL_Demo_WriteConfigStrings is CORRECT (it writes exactly what the reader expects).

## â­ THIS IS A RECORDING BUG, NOT A PLAYBACK BUG

S2's demo writer emits a gamestate its own reader cannot parse. That explains why ALL
FIVE shipped demos fail identically, why publicmatch is not special, and why native
theater has never worked in this build.

Consequences for the fix:
  * Demos we RECORD ourselves: fix the writer (add the missing bit) and they will play
    with NO read-side compensation at all.
  * The five SHIPPED demos: already on disk, so they still need read-side handling.

## Fix direction (NOT yet implemented)

Live gamestates have v10 == 0 (measured from our own .dm_s2 capture). So making the
READER consume one bit and treat v10 as 0 matches BOTH the live wire format and the
demo â€” it is not fabrication, unlike the flags-byte reconstruction, which is hereby
abandoned (brute force topped out at 106/108 and put the serverId at cs[3072]).

Open question before implementing: the read path must stay correct for LIVE play, where
the server presumably does write both bits. So any read-side change must be gated to
native demo playback only.

## Newly named (behaviour-proven from CL_Demo_WriteGameState / WriteConfigStrings)

    0x91D190  CL_Demo_WriteGameState
    0x9111B0  CL_Demo_WriteConfigStrings
    0xDDD60   MSG_WriteLong        0xDDE70  MSG_WriteString
    0xDDA40   MSG_WriteBit         0xDD8B0  MSG_WriteBits(msg, value, bits)
    0xDD850   MSG_WriteBit1        0xDD810  MSG_WriteBit0
    0xDD7C0   MSG_WriteString (configstring variant)
    0xDFC80   NetConstStrings_HasIndex

# â­â­ PERMANENT RULE A13 â€” AFTER ANY CRASH, READ THE MINIDUMP FIRST

Call of Duty WWII writes a minidump next to the exe on every fatal fault:

    E:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\common\Call of Duty WWII\s2_mp64_ship.exe.CL0.<id>.dmp

**Read it BEFORE writing any new probe or bracket.** User made this a standing rule
on 2026-08-08, and it immediately replaced a whole build-probe-run cycle.

    python tools/s2_crash_dump.py            # newest dump
    python tools/s2_crash_dump.py --all      # sweep every dump, oldest fixes visible
    python tools/s2_crash_dump.py --list
    python tools/s2_crash_dump.py <file.dmp>

Reports: exception code/name, the fault address converted to `IDA_0x...`, what
address was read/written (with a NULL+offset call-out), the faulting thread's
registers, and a heuristic scan of the stack for module return addresses.

Caveat: the stack walk is a SCAN, not a real unwind. Stale slots survive, so treat
the SET of frames as evidence and the ORDER as unreliable â€” the same caveat as
tools/dump_stacks.py.

**Why this beats bracketing.** A dump answers "where and why" directly; brackets only
narrow it down. And because dumps ACCUMULATE, `--all` reconstructs which fix moved
which crash â€” that is how the 64-byte qword_2537508 stand-in was caught.

## â­â­â­ WHAT THE DUMPS PROVED â€” sub_7BFD0 IS CL_InitCGame (2026-08-08)

Named in the IDB. BEHAVIOUR-PROVEN, not mapped: its tail is

    CL_SetClientState(client, 8);
    sub_416BD0(client, clc[32848], clc[32850], clc[4]);
    CL_SetClientState(client, 9);            <-- PRIMED
    sub_4A0B80; sub_276A70; ... sub_91C710(client);
    sub_BD020(0, "cgame_init_complete", qword_1BD3D08);   <-- decisive literal

### THE GATE INTERPRETATION WAS BACKWARDS â€” CORRECTED

`byte_1BAF450[1976*client + 2]` CLOSED is **correct and normal on a first connect**.
sub_70830 branches:

    gate SET   -> 2048x entity teardown + re-init + CL_SetClientState(9)   = RECONNECT
                  (valid only because cgame ALREADY exists)
    gate CLEAR -> Dvar_SetInt(cl_paused,1); CL_InitCGame(client)           = FIRST CONNECT
                  (CL_InitCGame itself sets connstate 8 then 9)

So BOTH paths reach PRIMED. The demo was never blocked by the gate.

**MY `demo_native_gate` PROBE WAS WRONG and is now DEFAULT OFF.** Forcing the gate ran
the reconnect path on a first connect, walking list heads at `unk_8AEA400` that were
never initialised. `sub_3FEF50` walks them as an intrusive circular list:

    if (v6 != v5) { do { ... *(DWORD*)(v6 + 16) ... } while (...); }

An initialised EMPTY list has head->next == head; an all-zeros one has head->next == 0,
so the emptiness test passes and it derefs NULL. Dump: 12:43, IDA 0x3FEFA0, READ 0x10.
All 8 xrefs to unk_8AEA400 are walkers â€” no visible initialiser, same as the gate byte.

    12:20-12:39   IDA 0x47E670  READ unmapped      my 64-byte stand-in was TOO SMALL

   reads TWO.** A RECORDING bug -- all five shipped demos are affected identically.

## qword_2537508 â€” what finally worked, and why the obvious approaches did not

Unguarded consumers found, each by ONE crash dump (RULE A13):

    IDA 0x462DA3  CL_ParseGamestate   *(QWORD*)(q + 16)          READ  0x10
    IDA 0x47E670  via CL_InitCGame    a1[399636] == byte +1598544
    IDA 0x47D1C0  via CL_ParseSnapshot return *(QWORD*)(a1 + 8)  READ  0x8
    IDA 0x1FEB80  via CL_ParseSnapshot *(BYTE*)(p + 171) = a2     WRITE 0xAB
    IDA 0x1FEC20  via CL_ParseSnapshot *(BYTE*)(p + 172) = a2     WRITE 0xAC

FAILED â€” 64-byte stand-in. sub_47E670 indexes byte +1,598,544, so the read landed
~1.6 MB out of bounds. Moved the crash, did not fix it.

FAILED â€” null-guards alone, no object. CL_ParseGamestate derefs *(q+16) INLINE while
building an argument, so no accessor hook can reach it. Back to 0x462DA3.

FAILED â€” installing the stand-in in play(). CL_Demo_Play_f READS this global itself
(0x910892, 0x9108C0) and its level load is multithreaded; the game hung intermittently
inside DB_LoadLevelXAssets. Main thread blocked in ntdll with IDA_0x910B34 on its
stack and cls_realtime FROZEN (12112 across two reads) â€” a real deadlock, not slow
loading.

FAILED â€” guarding the tiny setters one at a time. The crash walked forward one setter
per rebuild (0x465211 -> 0x465228 -> 0x46523A) because they all write through the SAME
pointer. Whack-a-mole.

WORKS â€” an 8 MB zero-filled block installed AT THE GAMESTATE (not at play()), with
**one** field filled in: `*(block + 8)` points at a scratch area inside the block, so
sub_47D1C0 returns a valid writable address and the whole setter family writes
harmlessly into memory we own. Everything else stays zero because fields like +16 are
null-CHECKED by their consumers, and making those non-null would send the engine down
paths that need a real object.

# OMNVAR BLOCKER â€” MECHANISM IDENTIFIED, FIX NOT YET CHOSEN (2026-08-08)

## MEASURED in game

    [native] NCS after gamestate: dword_5098948=1  blockList[23]=0000000000000000

So the 24 `ncs_*_level` tables ARE loaded (the engine's own loaded-flag is set) and
type 23 is simply NOT one of them. **Calling NetConstStrings_Load again is pointless**
â€” that hypothesis is DEAD, do not retry it.

## The mechanism, end to end

    CL_Demo_Play_f -> CL_Demo_ReadFooter -> CL_Demo_ReadNetConstStringTable @0x5DC0E0
        sub_DFA70()                       <-- UNLOADS ALL block lists
        ... per type present in the footer: sub_5DC390 -> sub_DFCD0 (register block)

    CL_ParseGamestate @0x462B00:
        if ( !CL_IsDemoPlaying(client) ) {
            if ( !sub_DEE80() ) { sub_DEF90(); sub_769050(); }   <-- SKIPPED FOR DEMOS
        }

Two separate storages, and only one is restored for a demo:

    qword_A60D180 + 0x20000 + 8*index   pointer table   index -> string   demo FILLS this
    qword_5A00C30[2*type]               block lists     name  -> index    left NULL

`sub_DED60(type, name, &out)` (the "420 %s" gate in sub_183810) searches the BLOCK
LISTS by name. airshipdemo's footer carries types
0,1,2,3,4,6,8,12,14,16,20,21,24,25 â€” **no type 23**, and the same holds for all five
shipped demos (proven offline with `tools/s2_demo_read.py --ncs`).

So the demo install DESTROYS type 23's block list and never rebuilds it, and every
name->index lookup against it fails.

## â›” NOT YET PROVEN â€” do the control first

Nothing yet shows blockList[23] is non-NULL in a LIVE match. Until that is measured,
"the demo install destroyed it" is STRONG INFERENCE, not fact â€” type 23 might be
populated by something else entirely (script/GSC at match start, or a different asset
suffix; note sub_DEF90 formats "ncs_%s_%s" with "level", so other suffixes may exist).

TEST: join a live match, read `qword_5A00C30 + 2*8*23` (VA = module_base + 0x5A00DA0).
  * non-NULL live -> the demo path destroyed it. Fix options:
      (a) do not unload types the demo does not carry, or
      (b) re-register the missing types after the demo's install.
  * NULL live too -> type 23 is never a block list at all, and sub_183810 must be
    reached only on a path live play does not take. Investigate its caller instead.

## The 24 per-level NCS tables (decoded from off_D90AE8, 24-byte stride)

    mdl mat rmb veh vfx loc snd sbx shk mnu tag ...   -> assets "ncs_<name>_level"

That is the origin of the long-standing `Waited 3453 msec for asset 'ncs_mdl_level'`
line in the logs.

## âš  SELF-INFLICTED â€” the _b static-init pitfall, hit again

A build declared, at NAMESPACE scope:

    void(*NetConstStrings_Load)() = reinterpret_cast<void(*)()>(0xDDF90_b);

`base` is assigned in init(), so the file-scope initialiser ran FIRST and the pointer
resolved to the bare literal. Crash dump: **"EXECUTE at 0xDDF90, OUTSIDE any module"**.
This is exactly the standing memory `b-operator-static-init-pitfall`.

**RULE: never cache a `_b()` address at file or namespace scope. Resolve it inside the
function, or assign it in init().**

## âš  SELF-INFLICTED â€” a diagnostic gated on the thing it was diagnosing

The first version of the NCS probe printed only INSIDE `if (blockList[23] == 0)`, so a
run where the condition was false printed nothing at all and could not be told apart
from "the code never ran". A whole game run was wasted.

**RULE: a diagnostic must report unconditionally. Never gate it on the condition it
exists to measure.**

## â­ THE OMNVAR FIX â€” proven by a live-vs-demo control

`sub_DED60(23, "OmnvarChanged", &idx)` searches the netconststring BLOCK LISTS at

for a demo:

    qword_A60D180 + 0x20000 + 8*index   pointer table   index -> string   demo fills this
    qword_5A00C30[2*type]               block lists     name  -> index    WIPED

CL_Demo_ReadNetConstStringTable @0x5DC0E0 calls sub_DFA70 (UNLOAD ALL) and then
re-registers ONLY the types the demo footer carries. Measured in game, the surviving
set was EXACTLY the footer's 14 types:

            16=Y 17=. 18=. 19=. 20=Y 21=Y 22=. 23=. 24=Y 25=Y

(`if (!CL_IsDemoPlaying(client)) { if (!sub_DEE80()) { sub_DEF90(); ... } }`).

## âš  TWO SELF-INFLICTED BUGS â€” now permanent rules

**RULE A14 â€” never cache a `_b()` address at file or namespace scope.**
`void(*f)() = 0xDDF90_b;` at namespace scope runs BEFORE init() assigns `base`, so it
yields the bare literal. Crash dump: "EXECUTE at 0xDDF90, OUTSIDE any module". This is
the standing memory `b-operator-static-init-pitfall`, hit anyway. Resolve inside the
function or assign in init().

**RULE A15 â€” a diagnostic must report UNCONDITIONALLY.**
The first NCS probe printed only inside `if (blockList[23] == 0)`. When the condition
was false it printed nothing, which is indistinguishable from "the code never ran", and
a whole game run was wasted. Never gate a diagnostic on the condition it exists to
measure.

# â­â­â­ THE ASSET ALLOCATOR AND THE POOL-SIZE TABLE â€” FOUND (2026-08-08)

CLAUDE.md previously recorded, under "â›” STATIC ANALYSIS CANNOT REACH THE ALLOCATOR":
the "Exceeded limit of %d '%s' assets." string has ZERO xrefs, displacement searches
find nothing, and the pool-size table was never located. **All of that is now solved,
from a MINIDUMP STACK** (RULE A13) taken at the publicmatch image-limit error.

    DB_AllocXAssetEntry_Checked   0x9E640    (was sub_9E640)
    DB_RaiseAssetLimitError       0x78AC90   (was sub_78AC90)

    DB_AllocXAssetEntry_Checked(assetType, a2, a3, a4):
        result = sub_AF9B70(*(QWORD*)(8*assetType + 0xB2F780), ...);   // Arxan thunk
        if (!result)
            DB_RaiseAssetLimitError(byte_B36D70,
                                    *(DWORD*)(4*assetType + 0xD90990),
                                    *(QWORD*)(8*assetType + 0xF89A60));
        return result;

## THREE TABLES, all indexed by asset type

    0xD90990   POOL SIZE   dword per type   <-- the table that was never found
    0xF89A60   TYPE NAME   qword -> char*
    0xB2F780   per-type allocator context (qword)

**VERIFIED**: index **21** gives name `"image"` (0xF89A60 + 8*21 = 0xF89B08 ->
0xB757F0) and pool size **40192** (0xD90990 + 4*21 = 0xD909E4 = 0x9D00). 40192 is
exactly the number in the fatal error AND the per-tier stride of the image residency
bitmap at 0x79DB100. Two independent confirmations.

CORRECTION to an earlier note in this file: `0xF89B00` is **"techset"**, not "image".
The old type-name walk was off by one entry.

## Why the Com_Error hook never caught this

`DB_RaiseAssetLimitError` does NOT route through `Com_Error @0x90750`. That is why no
`[comerr]` line has EVER appeared for an asset-limit error, despite the hook being
live â€” measured repeatedly. **Hook 0x78AC90 instead** to capture the failing type, or
hook 0x9E640 to count registrations.

## NEXT STEP â€” hook DB_AllocXAssetEntry_Checked and count by type

The question "what registers 40192 images during demo playback" is now directly
answerable: hook 0x9E640, tally calls per assetType, and print the tally when the
allocation fails. Read the type name straight from `*(QWORD*)(8*type + 0xF89A60)`.

That converts the image limit from a guessing game into a measurement.

  - the demo path using a different level-load idiom (identical five-call sequence)

# â­ USER OBSERVATION 2026-08-08 â€” THE VIEWMODEL IS LATENCY, NOT FAILURE

egyptbots, native playback: after roughly **20 seconds** the first-person viewmodel
AND all third-person player models APPEAR. They are not permanently missing.

## What this overturns

The long viewmodel investigation earlier in this file concluded that `hide` latches to
1 forever and the weapon images are "never" resident. **That was measured against the
CUSTOM THEATER and does not describe the native path.** On native:

  - the images DO eventually become resident,
  - `CG_UpdateViewModel` @0x5D0C0 then flips `hide` 1 -> 0 and forces a rebuild with the
    gun XModel (its self-healing path, already documented above, works as designed),
  - so the viewmodel appears with no intervention.

Therefore the problem is **streaming LATENCY**, not a broken residency chain, and the
StreamSync / registration-path theories built on "never resident" do not apply here.
Do not resume that line of work without re-measuring on native first.

## The unified picture for BOTH open problems

The demo installs its own model table (type 0: 678-782 entries of whatever every
recorded player wore). Everything is requested at once and the streamer works through
it over ~20 s:

  - LIGHT map (mp_egypt_02, mp_airship): the streamer finishes -> models pop in,
    playback is fine.
  - HEAVY map (mp_d_day, mp_gibraltar_02): the asset REGISTRATION count crosses the
    40192 image pool before it settles -> DB_RaiseAssetLimitError.

This is consistent with every surviving fact: it is a registration COUNT limit (pool
exhausted at 40192 while residency was only ~12% used), it tracks map weight, and it
is not explained by the demo's model-table SIZE alone (egypt 779 works, gibraltar 778
fails) because what matters is map baseline PLUS demo contribution.

STRONG INFERENCE, not proven. The measurement that settles it is the one now unblocked
by finding the allocator: hook DB_AllocXAssetEntry_Checked @0x9E640, tally calls per
asset type, and dump the tally at failure.

## Consequence for what to fix

If this holds, the target is not "make images resident" â€” they already become resident
eventually. The target is the REGISTRATION COUNT on heavy maps. Raising the pool is
ruled out by the user, so the question becomes what is being registered that a live
match on the same map does not register.

# â­â­ THE UNLOAD PATH â€” WHERE ASSETS ARE RELEASED, AND HOW THE DEMO PATH MISSES IT

## USER OBSERVATION 2026-08-08 â€” replaying the SAME demo fails

egyptbots (a LIGHT map that plays fine) plays once; a SECOND `cl_demo_play egyptbots`
in the SAME process hits "Exceeded limit of 40192 'image' assets."

This is independent of the frontend-baseline question and much sharper: the demo path
does not release the previous level before loading it again. Any explanation of the
image limit must now also explain this.

## PROVEN â€” DB_LoadXAssets @ IDA 0xA4F60 is where the unload lives

`DB_LoadXAssets(zoneInfo[], count, syncMode)`, entry stride 16 (+0 name, +8 flagsA,
+12 flagsB). Decompiled in full:

    v8 = 0
    for each incoming entry:
        for each LOADED zone z:
            zf = g_xzones[z].flags            // +896
            if ((zf & entry.flagsB) == 0) continue
            if (zf & 0x80) { if (entry.name && I_stricmp(entry.name, g_xzones[z].name)) continue; }
            v8 |= zf                          // mark this zone's group for release
    ... build the index list of every zone matching v8 ...
    sub_ADE50(list, n, 1)                     // FREE (Arxan thunk, not decompilable)
    ... sub_ADDA0(zone); --g_loadedZoneCount; compact g_loadedZoneIndices ...

**A loaded zone is released ONLY when its flag group is named by the incoming load.**
A NULL incoming name matches every name-tagged zone, which is how a whole group is
dropped at once.

## PROVEN â€” DB_LoadLevelXAssets @ IDA 0xA4840 issues that unload itself

    DB_AcquireLoadLock (sub_A0A80)
    sub_4DBCB0(0x1506700, 160768)             // clear image stream requests; 160768 = 4*40192
    >>> EARLY RETURN <<<
    for (i = 0; i < g_loadedZoneCount; ++i)
        if (!I_stricmp(g_xzones[ids[i]].name, mapName)) return;   // NO unload, NO load
    DB_LoadXAssets({name=NULL, flags = 396 or 512}, 1, 3)         // release the current level
    sub_A04F0(list, mapName)                                      // build the map's zone list
    sub_1FAAC0(list, ..., (flags & 2) ? 0x1900000 : 0, 0)
    DB_LoadXAssets(list, n0, 0) / (.., n1, 1) / (.., n2, 2)       // load it

Both the ordinary map-load path (sub_48C0C0) and CL_Demo_Play_f reach this through the
identical five-call idiom (CL_ShutdownAll -> Com_Restart -> CL_InitRenderer ->
CL_StartHunkUsers -> DB_LoadLevelXAssets), so the two paths are NOT different here â€”
which is consistent with the already-recorded DISPROVEN "the demo path loads level
assets differently".

## â­ STRONG INFERENCE â€” the early return explains the second-play failure

If a zone whose NAME equals the requested map is still loaded, DB_LoadLevelXAssets
returns before doing anything â€” skipping the unload as well as the load. That is
exactly the shape of "first play fine, second play of the same demo fails", and it is a
mechanism, not a correlation.

NOT PROVEN. It is an inference from the decompile; nothing has yet observed the early
return firing, nor what registers images afterwards when it does. The bracket below
reports it as fact instead.

## MEASUREMENT SHIPPED â€” build CD324F88 (deployed, hash-verified)

`DB_LoadLevelXAssets` @ IDA 0xA4840 - 0x1000 = 0xA3840 is now hooked. It brackets EVERY
level load â€” live map loads and demo playback alike, so the A/B is free â€” and reports:

  - the map name and flags,
  - loaded zone count and every zone's name+flags BEFORE and AFTER,
  - image registrations before and after (so the per-load cost is explicit),
  - and, computed with the ENGINE'S OWN test, whether the early return will fire.

RULE A3.1 was checked: demo_playback.cpp contains a `map_zone_load_orchestrator_stub`
for this address but NEVER installs it (no Hook::create references it), so there is no
duplicate. Zone-table literals are corroborated by that file's existing soft-gate probe.

New command: `demo_zones` dumps the loaded zone list on demand.

## THE RUN THAT DECIDES IT â€” one session

  1. main menu: `demo_zones`, `demo_asset_images menu`
  2. `cl_demo_play egyptbots`, let it load  -> read the DB_LoadLevelXAssets bracket
  3. back to the menu, `cl_demo_play egyptbots` AGAIN  -> the failing case

What each outcome means on the second play:
  - "EARLY RETURN" printed  -> proven; the map zone survived the first play, the engine
    skips the unload, and whatever registers images afterwards does so on top of a full
    pool. Fix direction: make the demo path release the level the way disconnect does.
  - no early return, zone count does NOT drop across the load -> the unload ran but
    matched nothing, i.e. the flag groups do not overlap. Fix direction is then the
    flags word passed by the demo path, not the call itself.
  - no early return, zones DO drop, images still climb -> the leak is outside the zone
    system entirely and this whole section is wrong; say so and start again.

Do NOT raise the pool size (ruled out twice by the user).

## NAMED / COMMENTED IN THE S2 IDB (idb saved)

Behaviour-proven from their own bodies, with the basis recorded in the IDB comments:

    0xA4840   DB_LoadLevelXAssets(mapName, flags)
    0xA4F60   DB_LoadXAssets(zoneInfo[], count, syncMode)   <- the unload lives here
    0x290B124 g_loadedZoneCount     (data)
    0x59ADC90 g_loadedZoneIndices   (data) u16 per loaded zone
    0x58360E0 g_xzones              (data) stride 1456, +832 name, +896 flags

Left unnamed on purpose: `sub_ADE50` (the actual free) is an Arxan thunk whose body is
`JUMPOUT(...)`, so RULE A5 applies; `sub_A0A80` is a plain DB lock acquire and was not

## MW3 cannot help here

Checked on port 14200: MW3's IDB has NO DB_LoadXAssets / DB_LoadLevelXAssets /

# â­â­â­ THE LEAK IS PROVEN, AND THE MECHANISM IS ONE BOOLEAN (2026-08-08)

Measured run, build CD324F88, egyptbots -> egyptbots -> airshipdemo in one process.

## PROVEN â€” the early return fires, exactly as predicted

    DB_LoadLevelXAssets('mp_egypt_02', 0) ENTER: 16 zones  <<< EARLY RETURN
    DB_LoadLevelXAssets('mp_egypt_02') LEAVE: zones 16 -> 16, image registrations +0

with `mp_egypt_02(8)` still in the loaded list. So on a REPLAY the engine skips the
whole function. That half of the hypothesis is now fact.

## â­ PROVEN â€” but the early return is NOT the real bug. Nothing is EVER released.

    1st egyptbots   zones 11 -> 14   (+1285 images)   nothing freed
    2nd egyptbots   zones 16 -> 16   (early return)   nothing freed
    airshipdemo     zones 16 -> 17   (+0 in-call)     nothing freed  <<< DIFFERENT MAP

**Loading mp_airship on top of mp_egypt_02 freed nothing.** Both maps stayed resident,
the pool crossed 40192 and DB_RaiseAssetLimitError fired at 40102/40192. Across the
whole session the freed count never rose above ~650. Zones only ever accumulate:

    11 -> 14 -> 16 -> 17

Observed zone flags: code_pre_gfx / code_post_gfx / common_mp = 1,
common_shared_core = 2, **ui_mp = 4**, common_core_mp / <map>_path / the map = **8**,
<map>_load = 0xA.

## â­ THE MECHANISM â€” DB_LoadLevelXAssets' release mask collapses to a no-op

    v11 = 396;                       // 0x18C = 0x100|0x80|0x08|0x04
    if (!sub_38F590()) v11 = 512;    // 0x200
    DB_LoadXAssets({name=NULL, 0, v11}, 1, 3);

  - mask 396 covers bit 8 (the map zones) and bit 4 (ui_mp) -> the level IS released.
  - mask 512 covers NOTHING in the observed set â€” no loaded zone carries bit 0x200 â€”
    so the release is a guaranteed no-op.

The measured behaviour (zones only ever grow) is exactly mask 512, i.e.
`sub_38F590()` is FALSE on the demo path.

    sub_38F590() = !(dword_E236DA0 == 1) && !byte_1BD36F8
                   && (*(u32*)(sub_197040() + 56) == 1)

âš  NOT YET MEASURED â€” which of the three inputs is responsible. Build D03877A8
(deployed, hash-verified) prints the gate, both globals, the resulting mask, and the
exact set of zones that mask WOULD release versus keep, at every DB_LoadLevelXAssets.
Do not guess between the three; read it.

## PROVEN â€” the three OTHER release sites, for contrast

    sub_48C0C0  live map spawn        {NULL, 0, 388 = 0x184} (|0x200), issued BEFORE
                                      the CL_ShutdownAll/Com_Restart/CL_InitRenderer/
                                      CL_StartHunkUsers teardown, then DB_LoadLevelXAssets
    sub_837E0   map change            {NULL, 0, 136 = 0x88}, and it carries the SAME
                                      already-loaded-name early return
    sub_8DE90   back to the frontend  {NULL, 0, 0x3BC = 956} â€” releases nearly
                                      everything â€” then DB_LoadXAssets({"ui_mp", 4}, 1, 0)
                                      to bring the frontend back. Gated on
                                      `if ((dword_28FB118 & 4) == 0)`. This is the real
                                      "unload the level" call, and it also deallocates
                                      the demo download memory (CL_Demo_* calls inside).

**CL_Demo_Play_f calls DB_LoadLevelXAssets DIRECTLY (0x910B2F).** It does not go through
sub_48C0C0, sub_837E0 or sub_8DE90, so it issues no release of its own and depends

Corroborating: the first demo ended with `PLATFORM_DISCONNECTED_FROM_SERVER` and
`----- Server Shutdown -----`, and the zone list STILL did not shrink. So the disconnect

## What this retires

  - the standing "map weight" correlate is finally explained: with nothing ever

## PROVEN â€” why the cursor was pinned, and the correct lever

`Mouse_UpdateClipAndRecentre` @ IDA 0x788220 runs every frame:

    if (Mouse_ShouldCaptureAndAccumulateDelta(...)) { ClipCursor(clientRect);

`Mouse_ShouldCaptureAndAccumulateDelta` @ IDA 0x81350 opens with an early-out ladder,
every branch reading `g_keyCatchers` @ IDA 0x1BAF4E0:

    (kc & 0x10) && sub_91D9A0(0) && !off_1BD3D60[16]  -> return 0 (release)
    (kc & 0x01)                                       -> return 0 (release)   <-- console bit
    sub_319020() && (kc & 0x40)                       -> return 0 (release)
    !sub_7887B0()                                     -> return 0 (release)
    otherwise                                            accumulate dx/dy, return 1 (capture)

**`g_keyCatchers` IS the word `GameUtil::blockGameInput` writes** â€” `0x1BAE4E0_b` ==
IDA 0x1BAF4E0. So setting bit 0 makes the predicate return 0, which releases the clip
and skips the recentre. That is the engine's own mechanism, not a workaround, and it is
exactly what the internal console already relies on.

FIX: `update_input_capture()`, called every frame from the Present hook, sets bit 0
while the UI is open and clears it on close. Re-asserted per frame because the engine
and LUI also write this word and a map load can drop the bit. On close it clears only
if WE set it AND `InternalConsole::DEVONLY_consoleOpen()` is false â€” bit 0 is shared
with the console. Also sets `io.MouseDrawCursor` while open: the release branch calls
sub_7888E0 with an unexamined visibility argument, so the OS cursor may stay hidden and
a free-but-invisible pointer would be no better.

## The F9 bug â€” WantCaptureKeyboard was the wrong test

`ui_hotkeys_allowed()` required `!ImGui::GetIO().WantCaptureKeyboard`. With
`ConfigFlags_NavEnableKeyboard` set in init_imgui, that flag is true for as long as any
of our windows is focused â€” i.e. essentially the whole time the UI is open â€” so F9 was
ignored until you clicked the game behind the window to defocus it.

FIX: gate on `WantTextInput` instead, which is true only while a text field has focus.
That matches what the comment there always claimed the intent was ("while typing into
an ImGui field"). Transport keys are unaffected: they additionally require `!g_open`.

## Named / commented in the IDB (saved)

    0x788220  Mouse_UpdateClipAndRecentre              descriptive, behaviour-proven
    0x81350   Mouse_ShouldCaptureAndAccumulateDelta    descriptive, behaviour-proven
    0x1BAF4E0 g_keyCatchers  (data) bit 0 = console/overlay owns input

## â­ THE COMPLETE STORY â€” and it needs TWO fixes, not one

The live paths release in two places, for two different purposes:

    sub_48C0C0 (live map spawn)  mask 388  drops **ui_mp** â€” the frontend
    sub_837E0  (map change)      mask 136  drops **the level**
    DB_LoadLevelXAssets          mask 396  drops both, but only when sub_38F590() is true

`CL_Demo_Play_f` calls DB_LoadLevelXAssets DIRECTLY and goes through neither helper, so
it releases nothing at all. That produces exactly the two observed shortfalls:

  1. **The frontend is never dropped** -> baseline stays at 36890 and only 3302 slots
     remain. A heavy map (dday 3211+, gibraltar) cannot fit even from a cold menu.
  2. **The level is never dropped** -> zones accumulate, so a SECOND map always fails
     regardless of weight (airship, a known-good map, died as map #2).

Releasing the level alone fixes (2) but NOT (1): dday still would not fit in 3302.
Releasing ui_mp alone fixes (1) but not (2). Both are required, and that is precisely
what the live path does with its two separate calls.

At the failure the census counted 40102 live images against a pool of 40192 â€” 90 slots

# CANDIDATE FIX SHIPPED â€” the demo path now performs the live paths' releases

Build DD148621, deployed and hash-verified. NOT yet tested in game, so per the Fix
Declaration Rules this is a CANDIDATE FIX, not "fixed".

## What it does

In the existing DB_LoadLevelXAssets hook, when and only when the caller is
CL_Demo_Play_f, issue the two releases the engine's own map paths issue â€” with the
engine's own masks, the engine's own precursors, and at the same point in the sequence:

    level     sub_1906B0();  DB_LoadXAssets({NULL, 0, 136}, 1, 0)   <- sub_837E0's call
    frontend  sub_196110();  flags = 388; if (!sub_38F590()) flags |= 0x200;
                             DB_LoadXAssets({NULL, 0, flags}, 1, 0) <- sub_48C0C0's call

Nothing is invented: both are transcriptions of real call sites. A NULL name matches
every name-tagged zone, which is how the engine releases a whole flag group (the name
comparison in DB_LoadXAssets is guarded by `if (entry.name)`).

## â­ CORRECTION â€” "sub_38F590() is false" is NOT the bug

`sub_B8C60` is a THUNK to `sub_38F590`, so sub_48C0C0 tests the SAME boolean and simply
ORs 0x200 when it is false. A false gate is therefore normal, and DB_LoadLevelXAssets'
mask-396 branch is its "I was called directly, so I will release for myself" path.
Otherwise the engine expects the CALLER to have released. CL_Demo_Play_f is a direct
caller that releases nothing â€” that is the whole defect, and this fix does not depend on
why the gate reads false. The earlier note that framed the gate as the mechanism is
superseded by this.

## Why the caller is identified by return address

`_ReturnAddress()` converted to IDA form, tested against CL_Demo_Play_f
(IDA 0x910650, size 0x5A0 -> [0x910650, 0x910BF0)). Exact, needs no state flag, and
works however playback was started â€” our play() or a bare `cl_demo_play` at the console.
Every OTHER caller of DB_LoadLevelXAssets is deliberately left alone: sub_48C0C0 and
sub_837E0 already release, and CL_InitCGame / sub_6DC350 run mid-session where releasing
would be destructive. Live play is untouched.

Side effect, intended: releasing the level first also clears the map's own zone, so
DB_LoadLevelXAssets' already-loaded-name early return can no longer skip the reload.
That fixes the replay case without special-casing it.

## Predicted outcome, so the test is falsifiable

    [assets] RELEASE level ...: mask 136 (0x88), zones N -> N-6
    [assets] RELEASE frontend/ui_mp ...: mask 388/900, zones N-6 -> N-8
    [assets] IMAGE <<36890>>/40192 ... with a large positive "freed" count

  - egypt/airship: should still play, and should now play TWICE, and in either order.
  - dday / gibraltar / publicmatch: should now fit. dday needed 3211+ against 3302
    headroom; dropping the frontend returns thousands of slots (the customization bulk
    â€” em_icon 1225, playercard 837, charm 744, camo 651, paintshop 400 â€” is all in the
    menu baseline, not in any map).

## Known risk, stated up front

Dropping ui_mp is exactly what a live map spawn does, so gameplay without it is normal.
BUT the demo load restarts LUI ("LUI: Starting up... LUI.mp_menus.main") BEFORE our
release point, so there is a real chance LUI has assets pulled from under it. If the HUD
or menus misbehave, turn off the frontend half only:

    demo_release_frontend      toggles sub_48C0C0's mask-388 release  (default ON)
    demo_release_level         toggles sub_837E0's  mask-136 release  (default ON)

With the frontend half off, the replay/map-change leak is still fixed but heavy maps
will still not fit from a cold menu â€” the two shortfalls are independent.

## Tool

`tools/s2_asset_log.py` â€” offline accounting of any saved console log plus census diffs.
Use it on the next log instead of reading the brackets by hand.

# NEW FRONTIER â€” Com_Error "4780" on publicmatch, in DELTA PARSING

    [native] svc msg #1: firstNibble=3 (hi=3) size=8605 byte0=0x33   (svc 3, zlib)
    [comerr] code=1 caller=IDA_0x66BA5F msg="4780"

## PROVEN â€” what "4780" means

`MSG_ReadMonotonicDeltaIndex` @ IDA 0x66B9E0 (named this session, behaviour-proven):

    MSG_ReadBit -> idx = ++msg[44]                          the common +1 case
    else if (bits != 11 || MSG_ReadBit) { idx = MSG_ReadBits(bits);
                                          if (idx <= msg[44]) Com_Error(1,"4780"); }
    else { v = MSG_ReadBits(9); if (v <= 0) Com_Error(1,"4780"); msg[44] += v; }
    if (msg[0] || idx < 0) Com_Error(1,"4781");

State is msg+44, which `MSG_ResetDeltaIndex` @ 0x665C00 sets to -1 at the top of
CL_ParseGamestate. So:

    "4780" = the delta field/entity index did not increase -> the bitstream is out of phase
    "4781" = message overflow, or a negative index

Callers are the snapshot delta readers sub_463000 / sub_463A20 / sub_463E90 / sub_4642C0.
This is SNAPSHOT/ENTITY delta parsing, not the gamestate.

## Almost certainly NOT caused by the asset fix

  - The fix only changes which zones are resident. Asset residency cannot alter the bit
    phase of a message being decoded.
  - publicmatch had never reached snapshot parsing before: it always died on the image
    limit DURING CL_ParseGamestate. This is virgin territory, not a regression.
  - The gamestate itself parsed fine in this very run (connstate 5 -> 9).

NOT PROVEN, and the honest check is one run of a known-good demo (airshipdemo or
egyptbots) with the fix active. If those still play, this is publicmatch-specific.

## Why publicmatch is the likely special case (from facts already in this file)

publicmatch is structurally unlike the four private demos: snapshot:archive ~1:1 instead
of ~1:11, packets padded to 1244 bytes, **gaps in the sequence numbers (10, 12, 13, 14)
consistent with real internet packet loss**, and it is the ONLY demo that RETRANSMITS a
message (msgSeq=3, three byte-identical copies). Delta-compressed snapshots are decoded
against a baseline; if a lost packet means the baseline was never established, the delta
read desyncs and the index stops increasing â€” which is exactly "4780".

## NEXT (in order, cheapest first)

  1. Run airshipdemo / egyptbots / dday.demo / gibraltar.demo with the fix. Confirms the
     fix is safe and tells us whether 4780 is publicmatch-only. dday.demo and
     gibraltar.demo are the two that previously failed on images, so they are the real
     prize.
  2. Only if 4780 also hits a private demo: extend tools/s2_huffman.py to walk svc
     opcodes with the proven MSG_ cursor model (already validated against the engine for
     the gamestate) and find where the phase is lost â€” offline, no game.
  3. publicmatch's retransmits and sequence gaps: CL_Demo_ProcessPacket_Type2_3's drop
     gate (`if (msgSeq >= clc[77] - 128) parse; else drop`) is the place to look at how
     a lossy recording is meant to be replayed.

## PROVEN â€” gibraltar no longer hits the image limit

Build DD148621, `cl_demo_play gibraltar`, a map that had NEVER loaded:

    RELEASE frontend/ui_mp  mask 900 (0x384), zones 11 -> 9
    census  at cl_demo_play        36890/40192   headroom 3302
            before CL_ParseGamestate 35517/40192 headroom 4675   released 2669
            after  CL_ParseGamestate 37716/40192 headroom 2476   released 2669

    CL_ParseGamestate #1: connstate 5 -> 9
    Loading Map: maps/mp/mp_gibraltar_02.d3dbsp
    connstate 9 -> 10                       <-- ACTIVE
    svc msg #2/#3/#4 firstNibble=6          <-- snapshots parsing

No asset-limit error. Gibraltar's own cost is 3495 images against 3302 headroom without
the release, which is why it always failed and why 2669 freed slots are enough. dday is
the same shape (3514 vs 3302).

## â›” BUT IT CRASHED TO DESKTOP â€” AND IT WAS MY FIX'S TIMING

RULE A13, one minidump, no probe:

    exception 0xC0000005 ACCESS_VIOLATION, fault at IDA_0xB0F0E0, READ from an
    unmapped address; stack carries UI_UpdateTime @0x3195B0.

`sub_B0F000` is **the Lua VM interpreter**, identified from its own literals
("C stack overflow: too many (%d) nested C function calls.", "Invalid type on assignment
of in instance of '%s'"), called only from the LUI bindings sub_308800 / sub_308BD0.

The census gives the mechanism outright: **luafile 1773 -> 941** across the release. And
the log ordering is decisive:

    Adding fastfile 'mp_gibraltar_02_load' ...
    LUI: Starting up...
    LUI: Loading LUA File "LUI.mp_menus.main"    <-- LUI binds luafiles that live in ui_mp
    [assets] RELEASE frontend/ui_mp ...          <-- and THEN we freed them

A textbook use-after-free that I introduced. The gate/mask/asset analysis was right; the
POSITION was wrong.

## FIX â€” release the frontend where the engine does: EARLY

`sub_48C0C0` issues its ui_mp release BEFORE its teardown and before the map's zones
load, so nothing is bound to ui_mp when it goes. Our release was inside
DB_LoadLevelXAssets â€” the LAST call of CL_Demo_Play_f's sequence, long after the loading
screen restarted LUI.

Build E0C9080D (deployed, hash-verified) splits the two halves by lifecycle point:

    frontend (mask 388|0x200)  at CL_Demo_Play_f's ENTRY   (IDA 0x910650 - 0x1000 = 0x90F650)
                               -> ahead of the loading screen and the LUI restart, so LUI
                                  comes up in a world without ui_mp, as it does for a
                                  live map spawn
    level    (mask 136)        still at DB_LoadLevelXAssets, which is safe: those are
                               flag-8 map zones, not UI

RULE A3.1 checked: nothing else in src/ hooks 0x90F650.

## LESSON â€” worth generalising

Calling the engine's own function with the engine's own arguments is NOT sufficient.
**Where in the lifecycle you call it is part of the contract.** The doctrine's
"Native Ordering Is Critical" section says exactly this; I matched the call and not the
position, and it cost a crash. When transcribing a call site, transcribe WHERE it sits
relative to the other subsystems, not just the arguments.

## Unresolved

  - publicmatch still fails with Com_Error "4780" in MSG_ReadMonotonicDeltaIndex â€” a
    delta-parse phase error, almost certainly its lossy/retransmitting structure and
    unrelated to assets. See the previous section.
  - Whether gibraltar/dday now play through with the retimed release is UNTESTED.

# â­ 4780 â€” OFFLINE svc WALK. THE MESSAGE STREAM IS FINE; THE DEFECT IS INSIDE
#     THE DELTA BLOCK (2026-08-08)

New tool, offline, no game: `tools/s2_svc_walk.py`. Decodes every type-2/3 demo
packet (zlib or Huffman) and walks the svc opcode stream with a FAITHFUL model of
S2's msg_t reader, printing snapshot headers.

    python tools/s2_svc_walk.py <demo.demo> [--max N]

## PROVEN â€” the reader model, transcribed from MSG_ReadBits @ IDA 0xDC910

    if bits == 32: return MSG_ReadLong(msg)      # 32-bit reads take the BYTE path
    if bits == 64: return MSG_ReadInt64(msg)
    rem = bitpos & 7
    if rem != 0:
        val = data[bitpos >> 3] >> rem;  shift = 8 - rem
        if bits <= 8 - rem: bitpos += bits; return val      # readcount NOT touched
        bits -= 8 - rem
    bitpos = bits + 8 * readcount        # jump to the BYTE cursor
    consume whole bytes from readcount, updating readcount

Consequence, and the whole subtlety of this format: a 4-bit opcode read at a byte
boundary consumes a WHOLE byte and leaves bitpos mid-byte; the NEXT opcode comes from
the high nibble of that same byte without moving the byte cursor. That is why byte0 =
0x22 means "two svc 2s" and byte0 = 0x33 means "two svc 3s". Byte reads
(Long/Short/Byte/String) move readcount only and never touch bitpos.

VALIDATED against real data: airshipdemo decodes into perfectly readable commands
(`q 75 "180" 77 "80" ...`, `; c 32 -1 1.00`, `8 b 0 "clut_mp_blackout"`) and sane
snapshot headers. The model is right.

## â­ DISPROVEN â€” "publicmatch is a lossy/desynced recording"

That was my hypothesis and it is WRONG. publicmatch's stream decodes just as cleanly:

    pkt#0  seq=10  huff 2581B   svc 0 gamestate
    pkt#1  seq=12  zlib 8605B   svc 3 x6 (len 86,13,52,20,27,32), then svc 2 x19,
                                then svc 6 snapshot
                                serverTime=11700 msgNum=11 deltaNum=0 (FULL) flags=0x0C
    pkt#2  seq=13  zlib 8605B   identical commands, snapshot msgNum=12 deltaNum=0 flags=0x0C
    pkt#3  seq=14  zlib 8611B   identical commands, snapshot msgNum=13 deltaNum=0 flags=0x0C
    pkt#8  seq=15  huff  583B   snapshot msgNum=14 deltaNum=0 flags=0x0C

Compare airshipdemo, which WORKS:

    pkt#1  seq=85  zlib 1320B   svc 2 x19 + one svc 3, then
                                svc 6 snapshot msgNum=84 deltaNum=0 (FULL) flags=0x0C

**Same shape. Both begin with a FULL snapshot (deltaNum=0, flags=0x0C).** So:
  - the framing is NOT broken,
  - the first snapshot is NOT delta-coded against a missing baseline,
  - the "retransmits" are ordinary Q3 behaviour â€” each packet re-sends the unacked
    reliable commands AND carries its own new snapshot (msgNum 11, 12, 13). The private
    bot demos never retransmit because the local connection acks instantly.

The only structural difference at the head is that publicmatch leads with SIX binary
(svc 3) commands where airship leads with text (svc 2).

## PROVEN â€” where 4780 must come from

`MSG_ReadMonotonicDeltaIndex` has exactly four client callers, and CL_ParseSnapshot
@ 0x464C00 calls three of them, each preceded by MSG_ResetDeltaIndex:

    MSG_ResetDeltaIndex; sub_4642C0(...)   entities
    MSG_ResetDeltaIndex; ... sub_463E90(...)
    MSG_ResetDeltaIndex; sub_463A20(...)

(sub_463000 is only on the flags&0x80 archived path, which is not taken here.)

**Key logical point: the delta INDEX comes from the bitstream, not from the baseline.**
A wrong or missing baseline produces wrong VALUES, never a non-increasing index. So
4780 does not mean "bad baseline" â€” it means the reader and the data disagree about the
FIELD LAYOUT at that point. The baselines are in any case guarded: `sub_461EF0`
validates v18 and the engine bails cleanly via sub_DC6C0 (`cursize = readcount;
overflow = 1`) when it fails.

One unguarded baseline does exist and is worth remembering: for a FULL snapshot
(deltaNum == 0) CL_ParseSnapshot reads an EXTRA byte and derives `v31` from it with NO
sub_461EF0 validation, then passes it to sub_463E90. It cannot cause 4780 by the
argument above, but it can produce garbage values.

## Where this leaves it

The message stream is healthy end to end up to and including the snapshot header. The
disagreement is inside the entity/playerstate delta block, which needs the netfield
tables to model â€” the one part `s2_svc_walk.py` deliberately stops at.

NEXT, cheapest first:
  1. Confirm 4780 is publicmatch-only by playing dday.demo (same map, private, client 0).
     If dday.demo plays, four of five shipped demos work and only the public one fails.
  2. Model the netfields. MW3 has `CL_Demo_SetupNetFieldListsForDemo` @0x1E4C63 which
     swaps g_netFieldList / g_entityStateNetFieldList for demo playback; CLAUDE.md
     records S2 as having no equivalent, and CL_ParseSnapshot (now decompiled in full)
     indeed contains no swap. If S2's tables differ between what publicmatch was
     recorded with and what this build reads, that is exactly a field-layout
     disagreement â€” which is what 4780 reports.
  3. The six leading svc 3 binary commands are the one structural difference at the
     head. CG_ExecuteBinaryServerCommand's opcode switch (sub_431B20) decodes them;
     opcode 98 is StreamSync. Worth decoding those 86/13/52/20/27/32-byte payloads
     offline before assuming they are inert.

## â­ publicmatch leads with SEVEN StreamSync commands. The others do not.

Decoded offline from the svc walk (`tools/s2_svc_walk.py` + the binary-command dump).
CG_ExecuteBinaryServerCommand's switch is `firstOpcodeByte - 45`, so **0x62 == 98 == 53
== CL_StreamSync_ParseServerLoadRequest**:

    publicmatch pkt#1:  svc3 seq=2  len=86  0x62  StreamSync
                        svc3 seq=3  len=13  0x62  StreamSync
                        svc3 seq=4  len=52  0x62  StreamSync
                        svc3 seq=5  len=20  0x62  StreamSync
                        svc3 seq=6  len=27  0x62  StreamSync
                        svc3 seq=7  len=32  0x62  StreamSync
                        svc3 seq=13 len=17  0x3B  opcode 14
                        svc3 seq=25 len=14  0x62  StreamSync
    airshipdemo pkt#1:  svc3 seq=7  len=17  0x3B  opcode 14
                        svc3 seq=20 len=12  0x47  opcode 26
                        svc3 seq=21 len=4   0x62  StreamSync (tiny)

This is the data the long viewmodel investigation was looking for: a real match's
per-player customization/model load requests, carried in the demo. A bot match barely
uses it (4 bytes); a public match sends 244 bytes across seven commands. Worth
remembering for the viewmodel work â€” but note these are STORED at parse time and
EXECUTED later by cgame, so they are not what throws 4780.

## What 4780 is, and what is ruled out

`MSG_ReadMonotonicDeltaIndex` @ 0x66B9E0 raises it when the delta field/entity index
fails to INCREASE. The index comes from the BITSTREAM, not from any baseline, so this
means the reader and the data disagree about FIELD LAYOUT at that point.

RULED OUT by the offline walk:
  - broken framing / desync (publicmatch's opcode stream decodes perfectly, 25 opcodes)
  - a delta snapshot against a missing baseline (its first snapshot is FULL,
    deltaNum=0 flags=0x0C â€” structurally identical to airship's, which works)
  - lossy recording (the "retransmits" are ordinary Q3 reliable resend; each packet
    also carries its own NEW snapshot, msgNum 11/12/13)
  - packet-level or zlib/Huffman problems (all decode)

So the fault is inside the delta block of the FIRST snapshot, after the header. In order,
CL_ParseSnapshot runs: CG_InterpolatePlayerState_S2 (playerstate) -> sub_66A900 ->
sub_668820 -> a `MSG_ReadBits(6)` counted loop of sub_666430 -> **sub_4642C0** (entities,
own error id "452") -> **sub_463E90** ("453") -> **sub_463A20** ("454"). Only the last
three use the monotonic index, so the phase is already wrong by the time the first of
them runs â€” i.e. something BEFORE them read the wrong number of bits, most likely the
playerstate delta.

## Two ways forward, honestly costed

  A. ONE small probe, one run. Our Com_Error hook records the immediate caller, which
     for 4780 is always the shared helper (IDA 0x66BA5F) and so names nothing. Walking
     ONE more return address would name which of sub_4642C0 / sub_463E90 / sub_463A20
     was executing, which turns an open-ended netfield question into a specific one
     (entities vs. the 453 reader vs. the 454 reader). Cheap, safe, decisive.

  B. Zero runs: extract and model the netfield tables from the IDB, then simulate the
     playerstate and entity delta in s2_svc_walk.py until the phase error reproduces
     offline. Much larger: the tables must be located (qword_BA3B98 in sub_4642C0 is a
     candidate but reads 0 in the static dump, so it is runtime-initialised), extracted,
     and the delta encoding modelled field by field.

RECOMMENDATION: A first. It costs one build and one run and it scopes B by a factor of
three. Do not start B without it.

2-byte length prefix, and the one-bit gamestate shortfall). A third disagreement â€” in a
netfield the private/bot demos never transmit but a public match does â€” would fit every
fact here and would explain why exactly one demo of five fails.

# â­â­â­ ROUTE B â€” THE DELTA PROTOCOL IS RECOVERED. 4780 IS A TABLE-SIZE MISMATCH.
#     (2026-08-08, entirely offline)

## PROVEN â€” S2's netfield tables, located and extracted

`CG_InterpolatePlayerState_S2` @ 0x668A90 loads `off_F931B0` and indexes it as
`[rax+60h]` / `[rax+70h]` / `[rax+78h]`. off_F931B0 holds 0xF93120, and THAT object is a
plain array of (tablePtr, count) pairs -- eight netfield lists:

    idx  rva          entries   maxOffset
    0    0xF96420     145       0x145        <- the list the playerstate reader loads first
    1    0xF969D0      65       0xBB
    2    0xF96C60     402       0x593C       <- largest + highest offset: entityState shape
    3    0xF97C20      10       0x2C
    4    0xF97C90      48       0xBE
    5    0xF97E70      19       0x27
    6    0xF934F0      68       0x1D0
    7    0xF97F30       5       0x10                                    762 fields total

**Record stride is 10 bytes, and that is not a guess:** every table ends exactly where the
next begins, to within alignment padding, for all eight (145*10 ends 6 bytes before the
next, 65*10 ends 6 before, 402*10 ends 12 before, 48*10 lands EXACTLY on the next, ...).
Eight independent confirmations.

Layout, 5 x u16: `{u16 offset, i16 size, i16 bits, u16 x, u16 y}`. Names are stripped from
the ship build. `bits` carries plain widths (1,2,8,16,32) AND ~48 distinct NEGATIVE codes
(-8, -16, -64..-112) which select special encodings.

TOOL: `python tools/s2_netfields.py [--table N] [--histogram]` -- extracts them offline
from s2x_dump.exe (NOT the retail exe, which is Arxan-packed; same trap s2_huffman hit).

## â­â­ PROVEN â€” the delta protocol, from MW3's FULLY NAMED twin (port 14200)

MW3 exports the entire set, which removes all guesswork:

    MSG_ReadDeltaFields      0x36DF80    the loop -- THIS defines the phase
    MSG_ReadDeltaField       0x36CF22    the per-field value decoder (huge switch on bits)
    MSG_ReadDeltaStruct      0x36C0EF    MSG_ReadDeltaPlayerstate  0x36C246
    MSG_ReadDeltaEntity      0x36BD5D    MSG_ReadDeltaClient       0x36C196
    MSG_ReadDeltaHudElems    0x36E1B6    MSG_GetLastChangedField   0x3712C7
    MSG_ReadNumFieldsSkipped (called by MSG_ReadDeltaFields)
    MSG_SetupNetFieldListsForGame 0x36F5E3
    g_netFieldList / g_entityStateNetFieldList / g_demoNetFieldLists / g_demoEntityStateNetFieldLists

`MSG_ReadDeltaFields` decompiled in full. The protocol is:

    1. read ONE bit inline. If clear -> copy every field from the baseline and RETURN
       (no further reads at all).
    2. width = 32 - CLZ(numFields)                  <-- bits needed to index the table
       lastChanged = MSG_ReadBits(msg, width)
       if (lastChanged >= numFields) -> MSG_Discard  (clean abort, not an error)
    3. i = -1
       do { skipped = MSG_ReadNumFieldsSkipped(msg, width)
            i += skipped
            copy the skipped fields from the baseline
            MSG_ReadDeltaField(msg, ..., &fields[i], ...)
       } while (i < lastChanged)
    4. second pass re-reading every field whose bits == 2
    5. copy the remaining fields from the baseline

## â­â­â­ THE KEY CONSEQUENCE â€” what 4780 actually diagnoses

**The index bit width is derived from the TABLE ENTRY COUNT**, and the same width is used
for the initial lastChanged read and for every skip read. S2's
`MSG_ReadMonotonicDeltaIndex` takes exactly that width as its `bits` argument, and its
`a2 != 11` special case exists because 11 bits == 2048 == the entity count.

So **"4780" means the reader and the writer disagreed about how many entries the netfield
table has.** A count mismatch shifts every index read by a bit or more; the indices stop
increasing; the guard fires. It is NOT a per-field encoding problem, and it is NOT a
baseline problem â€” both of which are now ruled out.

This also explains the shape of the failure perfectly: a wrong width does not corrupt
gradually, it fails on the FIRST index read, which is exactly where publicmatch dies (its
first snapshot, in the first message after the gamestate).

## Why this is the same class of bug as the two already fixed

S2's demo writer has now been proven to disagree with its own reader twice (the missing
2-byte length prefix; the one-bit gamestate shortfall). A netfield-table-count
disagreement would be the third instance of the same root problem: **the demo write path
and the live read path were built against different assumptions.**

MW3 makes the mechanism concrete: it keeps SEPARATE demo tables,
`g_demoNetFieldLists[2 - demoVersion]` and `g_demoEntityStateNetFieldLists[...]`, swapped
in by `CL_Demo_SetupNetFieldListsForDemo` @ 0x1E4C63 precisely so a demo decodes with the
table it was recorded against. CLAUDE.md previously recorded "LIKELY: S2 has no demo
netfield swap" -- and CL_ParseSnapshot has now been decompiled in full and contains none.
**If S2 dropped MW3's demo-table swap but kept demo recording, that is the bug.**

## NEXT (still offline, and now bounded)

  1. Find S2's equivalent of MSG_SetupNetFieldListsForGame / the list SELECTION. Eight
     lists exist in the descriptor at 0xF93120; establish which index each consumer picks
     and whether any selection is version- or demo-dependent. If two lists differ only in
     COUNT, that pair is the smoking gun.
  2. With the counts in hand, compute the index width both ways and re-walk publicmatch's
     first snapshot in s2_svc_walk.py. A width that makes the indices come out monotonic
     identifies the correct table, and the fix is to make playback use it.
  3. Only then model MSG_ReadDeltaField's per-encoding bit costs -- and note it may not be
     needed at all, since step 2 only requires the index widths.

# â­â­ NETFIELD STRUCTURE FULLY RECOVERED â€” AND TWO OF MY OWN CLAIMS CORRECTED

## CORRECTION 1 â€” there is ONE array, not several descriptors

0xF93120 is NOT a separate 8-list descriptor. **0xF92F90 + 16*25 = 0xF93120 exactly.**
There is a single flat array of `(tablePtr, count)` pairs at **IDA 0xF92F90, 33 entries,
stride 16**, and different subsystems simply hold pointers to different BASES inside it.
That is why CG_InterpolatePlayerState_S2 loads `off_F931B0` (= &array[25]) and then
indexes `[rax+60h]` (= array[31]) and `[rax+70h]/[rax+78h]` (= array[32], count 5).

    [ 0..24]  per-ENTITY-TYPE field lists    17, 31, 68..87 fields
    [25]      145 fields, max offset 0x145    entityState-sized
    [26]       65
    [27]      402 fields, max offset 0x593C   playerState-sized
    [28..32]   10, 48, 19, 68, 5

`tools/s2_netfields.py` now models this correctly and extracts all 33 offline.

## CORRECTION 2 â€” S2 DOES have MW3's demo-list array, and it is INERT

Immediately after the array, at 0xF931A0, sit TWO groups of three pointers:

    0xF931A0  ENTTYPE(&array[0])   0xF931A8  SMALL   0xF931B0  &array[25]   <- group 0
    0xF931B8  ENTTYPE(&array[0])   0xF931C0  SMALL   0xF931C8  &array[25]   <- group 1
    0xF931D0  (1<<n)-1 mask table begins

This is the shape of MW3's `g_demoNetFieldLists[2 - demoVersion]`. **But both groups are
byte-identical**, and only group 0 is referenced (17 xrefs to 0xF931B0; slots 1-3 have
zero xrefs).

So my earlier statement â€” "if S2 dropped MW3's demo-table swap, that is the bug" â€” is
WITHDRAWN. S2 kept the structure and collapsed both versions onto the same tables, so
there is no per-version table difference for a demo to disagree about. Whatever selection
happens, the counts are the same.

## â­ THE SURVIVING MECHANISM, and it is sharper than the one it replaces

The index width is `count.bit_length()` (MW3: `32 - CLZ(numFields)`), and it is used both
for the initial lastChangedField read and for every index read. Across the 33 lists:

    3 bits x1    4 bits x1    5 bits x3    6 bits x1    7 bits x25    8 bits x1    9 bits x1

The per-entity-type lists are almost all **7 bits** (68-87 fields) â€” but **two are 5 bits**
(list [2] with 31 fields, list [8] with 17 fields).

**So entity delta decoding picks its field list BY ENTITY TYPE, and the index width
changes with the type.** If the type resolved while reading differs from the type used
while writing â€” by even one â€” every subsequent index is read at the wrong width, indices
stop increasing, and MSG_ReadMonotonicDeltaIndex raises "4780". A two-bit shift (7 -> 5)
is a violent desync that fails on the first index, which is exactly where publicmatch
dies.

This fits the evidence better than any earlier theory: publicmatch is the only PUBLIC
match, so it is the only demo carrying the entity types a real 12-player game produces
(real player models, killstreaks, vehicles). The bot demos exercise a narrow set of types
and never hit the 5-bit lists.

STATUS: STRONG INFERENCE, not proven. What would prove it: decode publicmatch's first
snapshot far enough to read the entity type field, then show that the width implied by
that type's list makes the indices monotonic while the default does not.

## NEXT

  1. Find where the entity-type index is read and how it selects array[0..24]. That is
     the last unknown in the chain; the reader is sub_4642C0 (its own Com_Error id is
     "452"). MW3's named twin MSG_ReadDeltaEntity @0x36BD5D shows the intended shape.
  2. `MSG_ReadDeltaField`'s per-encoding bit costs are still NOT needed â€” the phase

# â­â­ NETFIELD MACHINERY FULLY MAPPED â€” AND IT IS INTACT. MY TABLE-MISMATCH
#     HYPOTHESIS IS DEAD. (2026-08-08, offline)

Three functions found and TWIN-PROVEN against MW3's named build. Together they close the
netfield question completely.

## The three, and their MW3 twins

    S2 0x91E310  CL_Demo_SetupNetFieldListsForDemo   <- MW3 0x1E4C63
        v3 = 29 - version;
        if (version != 29) Com_Error(1, "432 %i %i", v3, version);
        g_netFieldList            = g_demoNetFieldLists[v3];
        g_entityStateNetFieldList = g_demoEntityStateNetFieldLists[v3];
        (+ a third list). MW3's twin is the same gate, swap and position, with
        `v = 2 - demoVersion` and "Invalid Version Handling. Grab Bat !!!".
        Version is read from clc[client] + 0x40928, inside the demo header blob.
        **Com_Error "432" == demo netfield version mismatch.** It never fired in any run.

    S2 0x66F050  MSG_SetupNetFieldListsForGame       <- MW3 0x36F5E3
        the LIVE setup: points the three globals at the base tables.

    S2 0x66EFD0  MSG_GetStateFieldListForEntityType  <- MW3 0x36F5FC
        MW3: v = (type < 19) ? type : 18; return g_entityStateNetFieldList + 8*v
        S2 : v = (type <= 24) ? type : 24; return g_entityStateNetFieldList[2*v]
        25 types (MW3 has 19), stride 16 (MW3 8, x86). Same clamp shape.

Named in the IDB, with the data globals: g_netFieldList (0xF931B0),
g_entityStateNetFieldList (0xF931A0), g_demoNetFieldLists (0xF931C8),
g_demoEntityStateNetFieldLists (0xF931B8), g_netFieldLists_all (0xF92F90).

## â›” DISPROVEN â€” "4780 is a netfield table-size mismatch"

That was MY hypothesis from earlier today and it is now dead. The chain is intact end to
end:

  - there is ONE table array (33 lists) and both the live and demo groups point at
    IDENTICAL tables, so the demo swap is a functional no-op;
  - the demo version gate exists, is version 29, and would raise "432" on a mismatch â€”
    it never fired;
  - the per-entity-type selector exists, clamps correctly, and is the same shape as MW3's;
  - so reader and writer necessarily agree on every table and every index width.

The clamp also means an out-of-range entity type cannot read out of bounds; it silently
maps to list[24] (70 fields, 7 bits) â€” the same width as almost every other type.

## What that leaves

The tables are right, the selection is right, the framing is right (proven earlier by the
svc walk), and the baselines are guarded. So the remaining explanation is that
**publicmatch's snapshot bitstream is itself malformed** â€” a third instance of S2's demo
WRITER emitting data its own READER cannot parse, after the missing 2-byte length prefix
and the one-bit gamestate shortfall. Both of those were writer bugs; both were invisible
until something downstream tripped over them.

To prove that offline the delta stream has to be decoded for real, which finally does
require `MSG_ReadDeltaField`'s per-encoding bit costs â€” the expensive piece I had hoped
step 2 would let us skip. MW3's MSG_ReadDeltaField @0x36CF22 is the named twin to read
them from, and S2's `bits` codes (-8, -16, -64..-112 plus plain widths) would map onto it.

HONEST COST NOTE: that is a large job â€” ~48 encoding codes, a huge switch in both
binaries, and then a full playerstate+entity simulation before the first index is even
reached. It is the only remaining offline route.

## Cheaper alternative, if a single run ever becomes acceptable

Walking ONE more return address in the Com_Error hook would name which of sub_4642C0
("452"), sub_463E90 ("453") or sub_463A20 ("454") was executing. That distinguishes
"entities desync" from "the two later readers desync", which would cut the simulation
work by roughly two thirds. Recorded here so the option is not forgotten.
