# â­â­â­ 4780 LOCALISED â€” sub_4642C0's SECOND ENTITY INDEX READ (2026-08-08, in game)

Probe build 2A4F2D39, `cl_demo_play publicmatch`. One run, and it answered both questions.

    [comerr] code=1 caller=IDA_0x66BA5F msg="4780"
    [native] 4780 call-site scan:
    [native]    IDA_0x4643BD  sub_4642C0  entities        (own id 452)
    [native]    IDA_0x4651FD  CL_ParseSnapshot
    [native] last 2 delta-index reads of 2 total:
    [native]    #0    bits=11  last=-1     -> 255
    [native]    #1    bits=11  last=255    -> DID NOT RETURN <<<

(The scan also printed IDA_0x66BA5F labelled as CG_InterpolatePlayerState_S2. That was MY
probe's fault: I gave that function a 0x3000 range when its real size is 0x1DFB, ending at
0x66A88B, so the range wrongly swallowed the helper at 0x66B9E0 and mislabelled Com_Error's
own return address. Corrected in build 3584628F. The conclusion is unaffected -- the two
genuine frames are sub_4642C0 and CL_ParseSnapshot, and 0x4651FD is exactly the return
address of the `sub_4642C0(...)` call at 0x4651F8.)

## PROVEN

1. **The failure is in sub_4642C0, the ENTITY delta reader** -- not the playerstate, not
   sub_463E90, not sub_463A20. CL_ParseSnapshot's own frame confirms the chain.
2. **Only TWO delta-index reads happen in the entire playback.** The first entity index
   read returns 255; the second raises 4780. Everything upstream (playerstate, sub_66A900,
   sub_668820, the sub_666430 loop) never calls this helper, which is consistent with the
   xrefs -- so this probe cannot see a desync that happened earlier.
3. **`bits` is 11 on both reads and never varies.** 11 bits is the entity-number width
   (0..2047), not a netfield-count-derived width.

## â›” THE ENTITY-TYPE / INDEX-WIDTH HYPOTHESIS IS DEAD

I proposed that a per-entity-type list selection changes the index width (7 vs 5 bits) and
desyncs the stream. The measurement says the width is a constant 11 on every call. The
width never changes, so it cannot be the desync. Withdrawn.

## What 255 means, and the two readings still open

With `last = -1`, the helper can only produce 255 via
`MSG_ReadBits(11) == 255`, or via the 9-bit skip path with `v == 256`. The second read then
failed, so it was either an absolute index <= 255 or a skip of 0.

  (a) 255 is GARBAGE, and the stream was already out of phase before sub_4642C0 ran --
      i.e. the desync is in the playerstate/sub_66A900/sub_668820/sub_666430 block, which
      this probe is blind to.
  (b) 255 is REAL and the entity stream itself is malformed from the second entity on --
      a writer bug in publicmatch's snapshot, the third of its kind.

## THE NEXT RUN DECIDES IT, AND COSTS NOTHING NEW

Build 3584628F is deployed. It fixes the range mislabel and adds the msg cursor
(`readcount`, `bitpos`) to every ring entry, so a failing read can be located exactly in
the decoded message and cross-checked offline with tools/s2_svc_walk.py.

Run BOTH, in this order:
  1. `cl_demo_play airshipdemo`  -- the WORKING control. Expect MANY delta-index reads
     with a small first entity number. If airship also starts at 255, then 255 is normal
     and reading (b) is right.
  2. `cl_demo_play publicmatch`  -- expect the same 2-read failure, now with cursor
     positions.

A healthy control showing first-read = 0/1 and hundreds of reads would make publicmatch's
255 obviously garbage and point at (a); a control that also reads 255 first points at (b).
Either way the next step is determined by one comparison, with no further build.

#     WEAKENS the "255 is garbage" reading

The one-shot healthy sample fired. 56 reads captured. Abridged:

    #8    bits=11  last=266  -> 268    readcount=898   bitpos=7147
    #9..#21  bits=11, climbing 268 269 270 272 273 274 275 276 277 278 279 281 282 283
    #22   bits=11  last=283  -> 501
    #23   bits=11  last=501  -> 502
    #24   bits=11  last=502  -> 2047   <-- END OF LIST
    #25   bits=6   last=-1   -> 0      readcount=1288
    #26   bits=11  last=-1   -> 337    readcount=206   <-- NEW message, list restarts
    #27..#33 bits=11, climbing 407 409 411 416 417 418 419
    #34   bits=11  last=419  -> 2047   <-- END OF LIST
    #35..#40 bits=7, climbing 48 49 50 51 52 53
    #41..#55 the whole shape repeats for the next snapshot

## PROVEN from this

1. **2047 is the end-of-entity-list sentinel.** Every 11-bit run terminates with
   `-> 2047`. That is (1<<11)-1, as expected for an 11-bit entity number space.
2. **`bits` VARIES by reader, exactly as the netfield analysis predicted.** 11 for the
   entity numbers in sub_4642C0, then 6 and 7 for the readers that follow
   (sub_463E90 / sub_463A20) â€” widths derived from netfield list COUNTS
   (48 fields -> 6 bits; 65-87 fields -> 7 bits). The width machinery is healthy.
3. **â­ A HEALTHY FIRST ENTITY INDEX IS IN THE HUNDREDS â€” 266, 337 â€” NOT 0 or 1.**

Point 3 matters most, and it corrects the expectation I set before the run.

## Consequence for publicmatch

    #0  bits=11  last=-1    -> 255
    #1  bits=11  last=255   -> DID NOT RETURN

255 sits squarely inside the normal range (266, 337, 501, 502 all appear in the healthy
demo). So **255 is NOT obviously garbage**, and reading (a) -- "the stream was already
out of phase before sub_4642C0" -- is WEAKENED, not confirmed.

That shifts weight onto reading (b): the entity stream is malformed at the SECOND entity.
Note what the healthy demo does at that point: it steps by 1-2 (266->268->269->270) or
jumps (283->501). publicmatch's second read instead produced either an absolute index
<= 255 or a 9-bit skip of 0 -- neither of which the writer should ever emit.

STILL NOT PROVEN. A first read that happens to land in a plausible range is not proof
that it is correct; a desync upstream could produce a plausible-looking 255 by chance.

# â­â­â­ 4780 REPRODUCED OFFLINE, BIT FOR BIT (2026-08-08)

Build 43A60AEC gave publicmatch's cursor, and the failure now reproduces exactly in
tools/, with no game:

    ENGINE   #0  bits=11 last=-1  -> 255   readcount=904 bitpos=7228
             #1  bits=11 last=255 -> DIED  readcount=905 bitpos=7240

    OFFLINE  #0  bp=7228  last=-1   -> 255  skip9=256              removedBit=1
             #1  bp=7240  last=255  -> 0    abs11=0  **<= last -> 4780**

Identical values, identical bit positions. So at the position the engine reaches, the
bitstream encodes:

    entity 255 (reached by a 9-bit skip of 256), no field data,
    then an ABSOLUTE 11-bit entity number of 0 -- which is <= 255, and therefore illegal
    in a list that must strictly increase.

## The model is validated on HEALTHY data as well

Against airshipdemo's engine-measured healthy read:

    ENGINE   #8  rc=898 bp=7147 last=266 -> 268
    OFFLINE      rc=898 bp=7147 last=266 -> 268   via skip9=2      MATCH

So the offline reader is correct on both a working and a failing demo, at the same code
path. tools/ now models MSG_ReadBit, MSG_ReadBits and MSG_ReadMonotonicDeltaIndex to
bit-exactness against the live engine.

## Three plausibility checks on the failing position, all of which PASS

  - 255 is a normal first entity number. airship was already at 266 by its 8th read, so
    its block began around 250-260.
  - the pre-entity block is a sane size: publicmatch's snapshot header ends at
    readcount=727 and entities begin at 904, so 177 bytes of playerstate/etc. airship's
    header ends at 483 with entities starting at or before 898.
  - an offset scan over bp = 7228 +/- 40 finds NO alternative that produces a better
    walk (best alternatives reach 2 monotonic reads vs the measured 1, which is noise --
    every walk stalls at the first entity that actually carries fields).

## âš  WHAT IS STILL NOT PROVEN, STATED PLAINLY

None of the above proves that bitpos 7228 is the CORRECT place for the entity block to
start. The offline model faithfully follows the engine, so it would reproduce the same
decode whether or not the engine arrived there in phase. Two readings remain:

  (b) 7228 is correct -> publicmatch's snapshot genuinely encodes an illegal entity
      index, i.e. a THIRD S2 demo-writer bug, and there is no client-side fix: the file
      is broken. Consistent with the two writer bugs already proven (missing 2-byte
      length prefix; one-bit gamestate shortfall).
  (a) 7228 is wrong -> the desync happened in the playerstate/sub_66A900/sub_668820/
      sub_666430 block that precedes it, and 255 is a coincidence.

Settling it requires modelling the playerstate delta, which needs MSG_ReadDeltaField's
per-encoding bit costs (~48 codes, MW3 twin at 0x36CF22). That is the expensive job that
has been deferred three times; it is now the ONLY remaining route.

## Practical stake

publicmatch is the only PUBLIC-match recording of the five, and the only failure. If the
user records their own demos from public matches, they may hit the same defect -- that,
not the shipped file, is the reason to care.

A POPULATION count cannot see a SET change: one bit cleared and another set leaves the

moved, NOT that the request set is frozen. Do not conclude "nothing is asking" from this
alone â€” the next build hashes both bitmaps so set churn is visible at constant
population.

# â­â­â­â­ THE VIEWMODEL ANSWER â€” STREAMSYNC, FOUND OFFLINE (2026-08-08)

User pushed back on more live probing: "wouldn't it be better to dissect the demo file
and check the S2 IDB and see how it is enabling the viewmodel. Surely this can be done
offline." That was correct and it produced the answer in one pass. Recorded as a method
note as much as a finding.

## PROVEN (IDB) â€” the page-in setter, which this file recorded as UNKNOWN

CLAUDE.md previously said "the actual page-in setter is still UNKNOWN and is the one
remaining hole in this chain". It is found. Only TWO instructions OR bits into the
residency bitmap 0x79DB100:

    sub_A73A0 @ 0xA79DC   or rva dword_79DB100[r14+r8*4], edx
    sub_A9AE0 @ 0xA9BCF   or rva dword_79DB100[r15+rax*4], r8d   (from sub_A9970 only)

and sub_A73A0 is reachable ONLY through sub_A6DD0 / sub_A6BD0, both called from the
streamer tick:

    sub_A68C0   (driven regularly: sub_AC9C0 -> sub_A60D0 -> sub_AD670 -> here)
        if ( dword_11112E4 != 1 && !sub_1FAEC0() )      // 11112E4 == the LOADING flag,
            ... sum outstanding stream bytes ...        // set to 1 by every load path,
            if ( !dword_27D109C ) { sub_1FB0E0(total); v2 = 1; }
        sub_A6DD0(v2)  -> sub_A73A0    // ORs residency
        sub_A6BD0(v2)  -> sub_A73A0    // ORs residency

## â­â­ PROVEN (demo files) â€” the gun appears when a STREAMSYNC COMMAND ARRIVES

Binary server commands are svc 3 with `opcode = firstByte - 45`; **0x62 == 98 == 53 ==
CL_StreamSync_ParseServerLoadRequest**. Extracting every one with its snapshot serverTime:

    gibraltar   StreamSync t=4350 (4B), t=11650 (19B), then NOTHING FOR 58 SECONDS,
                then t=70400 (32B), t=98450
                measured pop: +68135ms after CA_ACTIVE -> demo t ~= 72485
                -> the pop is 2085 ms after the 32-byte StreamSync that ends the silence

    egyptbots   StreamSync burst t=1600..5450 (~50 commands), then NOTHING FOR 35 SECONDS,
                then t=40900 (12B), t=41950 (95B)
                measured pop: +40780ms after CA_ACTIVE -> demo t ~= 41130
                -> the pop is 230 ms after the StreamSync that ends the silence

**In BOTH demos the viewmodel appears immediately after the first StreamSync command
following a long silence.** The silences are 58 s and 35 s, so this is not a coincidental
window match.

## THE EXPLANATION, and it fits every observation

In a live match the server sends StreamSync load requests AT CONNECT; the client latches
the players' models per slot and streams them (MWR blocks behind wait-bits/loadbar until
they are in). **That connect-time request happened BEFORE the recording started, so it is
not in the demo file.** Playback therefore begins with nothing latched for the local
player's weapon, and the gun only appears when some LATER, incidental StreamSync happens
to cover it â€” 35-58 seconds in.

This explains, with one mechanism:
  - why the delay exists at all, and why it differs per demo (40.8s vs 68.1s);
  - why the streamer looked "idle" â€” it was: nothing had asked for those images;
  - why a weapon change did not help (gibraltar 269 -> 308 -> 269, hide stayed 1);
  - why residency was FLAT then jumped +146 in one burst;
  - and why the old theater-era conclusion "the images are never resident" was wrong â€”
    it just never watched long enough.

## CORRECTIONS this retires

  - "the streamer is working through the demo's 678-782 model table and the viewmodel is
    far down the queue" â€” DEAD. Residency was flat for 40+ seconds, not climbing.
  - my bipod hypothesis ("the pop is a swap to an already-resident model") â€” DEAD, the
    log said "NO weapon change". The bipod observation was most likely the user noticing
    the moment a StreamSync landed.

## THE FIX DIRECTION â€” and the engine already has the function

CLAUDE.md's earlier StreamSync work found `CL_StreamSync_BuildAndCommitLocalPackage`
@ 0x91A970, which builds a model package FROM LOCAL STATE and commits it via
CL_StreamSync_CommitModelPackage @ 0x1923C0 -> CL_StreamSync_DataList_CommitNewSyncData â€”
with NO server command required. That is exactly the missing connect-time request.

So: at the start of native playback, once the gamestate is installed and the local
client's weapon is known, commit a local StreamSync package. Do NOT hand-author the
9-list bitstream for sub_6608D0 â€” the engine's own builder exists.

âš  NOT YET PROVEN and must be checked before writing the fix: the correlation is two
demos, and the StreamSync payload has NOT been decoded to confirm it actually names the
local player's weapon. Also unresolved from the old notes: the caller chain of
sub_91A970 (via sub_439EA0 <- sub_43BCB0) was never shown to be the demo path.

# â­â­â­â­ THE VIEWMODEL ROOT CAUSE â€” THE ENGINE'S OWN DEMO STREAMSYNC PATH IS
#     GATED OFF (2026-08-08, all offline)

Both pre-fix checks the user asked for are done, and the second one produced the
mechanism outright.

## CHECK 2 â€” is CL_StreamSync_BuildAndCommitLocalPackage on the demo path? YES.

    CG_DrawActiveFrame -> sub_43ADA0 -> sub_43BCB0 -> sub_439EA0
                       -> CL_StreamSync_BuildAndCommitLocalPackage @0x91A970

CG_DrawActiveFrame is the per-frame cgame entry, so this runs during playback. CLAUDE.md's
old note "NOT YET SHOWN TO BE THE DEMO PATH ... its caller lives in the CG region" is
RESOLVED. sub_439EA0 is the clientinfo parser (it reads CL_GetConfigString(model+1270)
and (+4983)).

## â­ THE GATE, and it is explicitly DEMO-AWARE

sub_439EA0 contains:

    if ( *(int*)(a4 + 236) > 0 ) {
        sub_43E310(...);                                   // build the local model set
        if ( CL_IsDemoPlaying(a1) && !CL_StreamSync_IsCustomizationEnabled(a1) )
            CL_StreamSync_BuildAndCommitLocalPackage(a1, a4 + 236, &pkg);
        ...

**Sledgehammer anticipated exactly this problem.** A demo has no connect-time server
StreamSync, so the engine builds the package LOCALLY from clientinfo â€” but only when
customization is DISABLED.

    CL_StreamSync_IsCustomizationEnabled @0x193630
        return s_streamSyncCustomizationEnabled[12968 * client];    (stride 51872 bytes)
    ONE code caller: sub_439EA0 @0x43A077.

The two StreamSync paths are mutually exclusive by design:

    CL_StreamSync_ParseServerLoadRequest @0x193B20 : if (!flag) return;   server drives, flag SET
    sub_439EA0                                     : if (demo && !flag)   local build, flag CLEAR

This also UPGRADES the confidence in the global's name, which this file had flagged as
"mapped-by-position, weaker basis" â€” the two uses are now coherent and complementary.

## The complete explanation

With customization enabled (the normal MP case), the engine expects the SERVER to drive
the loads. The demo recording began AFTER connect, so the connect-time server StreamSync
is not in the file. The local builder that would have covered for this is gated off by
the same flag. Result: nothing latches the local player's weapon until some later,
incidental server StreamSync happens to cover it â€” the 35-58 second silences measured in
both demos, and the 40.8s / 68.1s pops.

## THE FIX â€” surgical, and it uses the engine's own demo branch

`CL_StreamSync_IsCustomizationEnabled` has exactly ONE code caller. Hooking it to return
0 **during native demo playback only** makes sub_439EA0 take the branch the engine
already wrote for demos, while leaving the real global untouched â€” so
CL_StreamSync_ParseServerLoadRequest (which reads the global directly, not through this
accessor) keeps working. Nothing is fabricated; no bitstream is authored.

## âš  NOT PROVEN â€” which gate is actually shut

The reasoning above assumes the flag is non-zero during playback. That is an INFERENCE
from behaviour (the local build demonstrably does not happen), not a measurement. Three
other conditions could equally be responsible:

    (b) CL_IsDemoPlaying(a1) false at that moment
    (c) *(int*)(a4 + 236) <= 0, skipping the whole block
    (d) sub_439EA0 never called for the local client

The fix is safe under all four: if the flag is not the reason, forcing it simply changes
nothing and we learn that. So the implementation should LOG all four conditions at the
call site, making one run both the fix and its own diagnosis.

## Check 1 (decode the server StreamSync payload to confirm it names the local weapon)
is now MOOT for the fix: the engine builds the package from local state itself, so we
never need to author or understand the server's 9-list bitstream.

            | CL_IsDemoPlaying=1 | customizationFlag=0 (0 required) -> local build BLOCKED upstream

## DISPROVEN â€” my hypothesis

I predicted the customization flag was NON-ZERO and was suppressing the engine's own

vehicle for the diagnostic. Shipping it as a "fix" would be dishonest.

## â­ PROVEN â€” the real blocker, one level further out

    if ( *(int*)(a4 + 236) > 0 ) {          // <-- THIS is what is shut, and it is 0
        sub_43E310(...);                     // build the local model set
        if ( CL_IsDemoPlaying && !flag ) CL_StreamSync_BuildAndCommitLocalPackage(...);

So the whole block â€” including the model-set build â€” is skipped. a4 is a per-client
struct (its byte[0] is the client index; at the call site 0x43C28A a4 = r13). The local
model/customization set is EMPTY for the demo's local client, so there is nothing to
build a package from. The clientinfo takes the plain else-branch instead
(`CL_GetConfigString(*(u16*)(a4+22) + 1270)`), which assigns a base model and no loadout.

## âš  CONTRADICTION â€” DO NOT BUILD ON THE STREAMSYNC TIMING STORY UNTIL RESOLVED

`CL_StreamSync_ParseServerLoadRequest` @0x193B20 opens with `if (!flag) return;`. With
the flag measured at 0, **the server-driven StreamSync path is ALSO disabled** â€” so the
demo's opcode-98 commands do nothing. That directly undercuts the earlier finding that
the viewmodel pop correlates with those commands (gibraltar +2085ms, egyptbots +230ms
after a 35-58 second silence).

Both cannot be true as stated. Candidates, none yet checked:
  - the flag is PER-CLIENT (`[12968 * client]`) and only client 0 was sampled;
  - the flag was only sampled during the FIRST SIX clientinfo parses, early in playback,
    and may become non-zero later â€” the pops are at 40-68 seconds;
  - the correlation is coincidence (weakened by the length of the silences, but not
    excluded);
  - something other than StreamSync sets residency at those moments.

Per the Contradiction Rule this must be resolved BEFORE any further fix attempt. The
cheapest resolution: sample the flag periodically (it is one dword) rather than only at
the first few clientinfo parses â€” the existing [vmnative] heartbeat is the natural place.

## Also measured, and it revises an earlier claim

In THIS egyptbots run the streamer was NOT idle: residency climbed steadily from 6964 to
~7885 between t=+12s and t=+24s, in ~10-60 image steps. The gibraltar run showed it flat
for 40 seconds. So "the streamer is idle" is NOT a general property â€” it varies per
demo/run, and the earlier gibraltar-only conclusion was over-generalised.

`requests pop=11304 setChanges=0` for the entire run: the request bitmap never changed at
all, in population OR content. Nothing new is ever requested.

Viewmodel remains UNFIXED on the native path. What is now solid:

Measured on native `cl_demo_play egyptbots`, weapon 353 = `vm_usa_springfield_base`,

    per-tier resident: t0=126 t1=0 t2=0 t3=0

## PROVEN â€” only SEVEN DISTINCT images are missing

77 missing refs == 7 distinct images x 11 references. The other 126 refs are resident
and stable from the first sample. `XModel_AreImagesResident` requires ALL images, so
these seven alone hold `hide` at 1 and omit the gun XModel.

**This retires the framing the whole earlier viewmodel investigation was built on.**
"The weapon's images are never resident" is FALSE on the native path: 96% of them are
resident within seconds. Anything above in this file that reasons from "nothing streams"
â€” including the StreamSync-latency story and the residency-chain conclusions measured
against the CUSTOM THEATER â€” does not describe native playback and must be re-measured
before it is used again.

## PROVEN â€” the tier question is closed

`xflags = 0x00076A00` carries neither 0x200000 nor 0x400000, so the model takes

"broken weapons are on a stricter tier" idea was already DISPROVEN statically; this
confirms it dynamically on the native path. Do not revisit.

## CORRECTED â€” `+941344` is NOT an independent request array

I introduced this offset because `sub_A68C0` tests
`*((_DWORD*)&unk_1506700 + (imageIndex >> 5) + 941344)`, and used it to argue my earlier
"requests never change" reading was unreliable. Measured, it equals `resident` EXACTLY
(126/203) at every sample, tracking it as it climbs. It mirrors residency and carries no
independent signal. The only real request reading is `reqBASE` = 35/203, which does not
cover the seven.

## Why 7 images x 11 materials is the interesting shape

Seven textures shared across 11 of the 19 materials is a COMMON set, not per-material
art. That is the right shape for camo/customization/shared-lookup textures â€” which would
connect to the customization path â€” but that is a GUESS. The next build resolves the
image and material NAMES (scanning each 96-byte GfxImage record for a pointer to
printable ASCII rather than assuming a struct offset), which answers it directly.

Residency climbs steadily (6946 -> 7700+) while these seven never arrive and never

requests these seven, or something requests them and they are refused. `reqBASE` says

# â­â­â­ THE VIEWMODEL FIX â€” StreamSync REPLAY (build 101AA0A3, 2026-08-08)

Everything below was established OFFLINE, with no game run, at the user's request.

## PROVEN â€” the StreamSync payload format, decoded

`tools/s2_ss_decode.py` implements CL_StreamSync_DataList_ParseRequiredData
@0x6608D0 and decodes every command in every shipped demo with **slack = 0** --
each parse consumes its payload to the exact bit. That is the validation; a wrong
model overruns or leaves bits.

    per-list index width   asc_B419D8 (u16[6]) = {9, 9, 8, 8, 12, 9}
    per-list cap           word_B419F8(u16[6]) = {389, 150, 100, 120, 3000, 386}
    count width            lists 0-5: 5 (or 6);  list 6: 7 (or 9);  lists 7,8: 3
                           (the alternative is sub_B8C40(); offline the clean
                            answer is always the narrow one)

âš  `asc_B419D8` is TYPED as char in the IDB but is really u16[6] -- the char
reading gives width 0 for list 1, which is nonsense. Every width's range covers
its own cap, which is the cross-check.

âš  OPCODE: CG_ExecuteBinaryServerCommand switches on `(firstPayloadByte - 45)`, so
StreamSync is **switch case 53**, raw byte 98 (0x62). Earlier notes saying
"opcode 98" mean the RAW byte.

ALIGNMENT (proven): CG_ExecuteBinaryServerCommand does MSG_ReadByte for the
opcode, which advances ONLY the byte cursor; the inline bit reader then resyncs
bitpos = 8*readcount. So the bitstream starts at byte 1 of the payload.

## PROVEN â€” the pop is the first command that ADDS TO LIST 8

    demo         pop      what first appears at that instant
    egyptbots    40780    t=40550  list8   += 788891
    gibraltar    68135    t=66050  list6+8 += 50595085

Nothing else first-appears in a 5 s window around either pop. Note 788891 was
already in LIST 6 from t=3950 -- so it is not a new item, it is the same item
finally requested in list 8. list 8 is the category that drives the viewmodel.

## CORRECTED â€” my own claims, killed by the measurements above

  - "the missing images are 7 distinct textures" -- WRONG, that was a truncated
    log line read as a repeating cycle. It is 32+ distinct across 77 refs.
  - "list 8 is first non-empty at the pop" -- WRONG. list8 is non-empty from
    t=2050 in egyptbots. What is new at the pop is the (list8, item) PAIR.
  - "a clientinfo update at t=40550 drives it" -- DEAD. Dumped every server
    command in t=[39000,42500]: no configstring update, only StreamSync.
  - "my ui_mp release starved the viewmodel" -- DEAD by the user's observation
    that the pop time is identical on builds predating that code.

## THE FIX â€” replay the demo's own recorded requests up front

A live client receives the load request at CONNECT. The recording starts after
connect, so the demo carries only later incremental requests. So:

  1. `prescan_streamsync()` walks the .demo once at cl_demo_play, collecting every
     opcode-98 binary server command. Packet + svc walk are implemented in the mod
     (transcribed reader, no assumed signatures); the ONLY engine call is the
     Huffman decoder, whose signature is proven from its own body:
         char sub_DCAB0(src, dst, srcLen, dstMax, int* outLen)   @0xDCAB0
  2. At the first ACTIVE frame they are replayed through
     CG_ExecuteBinaryServerCommand, which dispatches each to case 53.
  3. The gate is opened ONLY for the duration of each
     CL_StreamSync_ParseServerLoadRequest call and restored immediately -- the
     five other readers never see the forced value. (CommitNewSyncData reads the
     same flag and is called from inside Parse, so the scope covers it.)

**Nothing is synthesised.** The bytes are the demo's own recorded requests,
delivered before they are needed instead of 40-68 s late.

### The replay POLICY, and why "replay everything" is wrong

CommitNewSyncData DIFFS -- items absent from the new list are released via
sub_194170. Validated offline:

    egyptbots  replay all       -> final list8 [9569,198,46794107,34,853403,307]  NO 788891
    egyptbots  monotone-list8   -> final list8 [854309,9569,459969,198,788891]    HAS IT
    gibraltar  either policy    -> [21234957,50595085,308]                        HAS IT

So a command is SKIPPED when its list 8 would drop an item already accumulated.
66 of 78 replay for egyptbots, all 4 for gibraltar, and list 6 is unaffected
either way (31 items under both policies). The union is NOT usable: list 8's
count field is 3 bits, capping it at 7 items, and the union is 13.

Toggles: `demo_streamsync_prescan`, `demo_streamsync_gate` (both default ON).

## NOT YET TESTED IN GAME â€” this is a CANDIDATE FIX

Per the Fix Declaration Rules this is not "fixed" until it is run. Expected:

    [ss] pre-scan: N packets walked, 78 StreamSync command(s) collected
    [ss] REPLAYED 66 recorded StreamSync request(s) up front (12 skipped ...)
    [vmnative] ... hide 1->0 ... at a few SECONDS, not 40780 ms

Honest risks, in order:
  - the early requests may not be what the local weapon needs -- the correlation
    is with list-8 membership, and the item's link to the springfield is INFERRED
    from timing, never confirmed by name;
  - committing the union registers more assets than stock; there were 2457 image
    slots spare on dday, so watch the census;
  - if the flag opens naturally before t=40550, the gate-forcing half is a no-op
    and only the replay half matters.

## â­ THE RULE â€” the gun appears when StreamSync LIST 8 gains a THIRD entry

Two entries is a base pair every demo carries. The third is the local player's
weapon customization.

    demo         list 8 evolution                        viewmodel
    airship      [9569, 198]            never grows      NEVER   (user-confirmed)
    dday         [21234957, 308]        never grows      NEVER   (predicted)
    egyptbots    2 -> 3 at t=40550                       40780   (+230 ms)
    gibraltar    2 -> 3 at t=66050                       68135   (+2085 ms)

`tools/s2_viewmodel_predict.py` reproduces all three known outcomes, INCLUDING
the never-case. A model that predicts a negative as well as two timings is much
stronger than one that only fits positives.

## â›” THE REPLAY FIX ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH â€” airship and dday have nothing to replay

Their demos NEVER request the local weapon, so no replay policy can help. The
StreamSync pre-scan/replay (build 101AA0A3) only helps egyptbots, gibraltar and
publicmatch. This was found offline, before it cost a game run.

## â­ THE FIX THAT WORKS FOR ALL DEMOS â€” issue the engine's own request

Traced end to end:

    CommitNewSyncData -> sub_193F90 -> sub_196220(model, list, idx, tier, fb)
                      -> sub_1A4240(model, cat, prio, tier, fb)
                      -> sub_1A2F40(model, lo, hi, ctrl)
                      -> per image: sub_198B10(imageIndex, category, priority)
    streamer tick sub_A68C0 -> sub_A6DD0/sub_A6BD0 -> sub_A73A0 ORs 0x79DB100

`sub_1A2F40` is PROVEN to be per-image streaming, from its own body:
  - `if ((flags & 0x20000) == 0) return 1;`  model must be streamable
  - `if (flags & 0x200)` recurse over children (+8, stride 48, count at +42) --
    exactly the child/material layout the [vmimg] walk found
  - else walk the model's u16 image-index ranges and request each one

Our viewmodel measured `xflags = 0x00076A00`:
    & 0x20000 = set  -> streamable
    & 0x200   = set  -> has children, so the recursive branch is taken
    & 0x200000, & 0x400000 both CLEAR -> residency test is sub_196040(m, 0, 5)

So the mod issues `sub_196220(vm, list 8, idx 0, tier 0, fb 5)` while `hide` is
set, rate-limited to 2 Hz. That maps to `sub_1A4240(vm, cat 2, prio 127, 0, 5)`
-- category 2, MAXIMUM priority, image ranges 0..5 (all of them), and the (0,5)
pair matches the residency test that gates `hide`.

The XModel flags are deliberately NOT modified: setting 0x400000 would switch
XModel_AreImagesResident to its STRICT variant and could make things worse.

**This is not the old `demo_stream_hard`.** That used XModel_StreamHard @0x4DD3A0
to OR advisory bits into unk_1506700, which nothing services. This is the
customization streamer's own entry point -- the call the engine itself makes for
every StreamSync item -- issued for the model the ENGINE selected via
BG_GetViewModel(ps.weapon). Nothing is invented or fabricated.

Toggle: `demo_viewmodel_request` (default ON). Build 2CA64B0C.

## OUR CUSTOM .dm_s2 DEMOS HAVE THE SAME DEFECT

The predictor now reads both containers. network_data (TLV id 2) is
`[u32 seq][u32 flags: low31 = entry readcount, bit31 = useZlib][msg data]`.

    d_day.0000.dm_s2      list8 = 5 entries at t=0     works already
    d_day.0001.dm_s2      never exceeds 2              NEVER
    wolfslair.0000.dm_s2  gun at ~3600 ms
    wolfslair.0001.dm_s2  never exceeds 2              NEVER

Two of four never request the weapon. Our recorder starts at the connect
gamestate, so when it happens to catch the real connect-time request the demo is
fine (d_day.0000) -- and when the capture starts later, it is not.

## CORRECTIONS to my own earlier claims in this file

  - "the gun appears when list 8 is FIRST non-empty" -- WRONG. list8 is non-empty
    from t=2050 in egyptbots. It is the THIRD entry that matters.
  - "replaying the demo's own requests fixes the viewmodel" -- only for demos that
    contain such a request. airship and dday do not.

## HONEST LIMIT OF THE OFFLINE TEST

The predictor validates the DIAGNOSIS (3/3) and the STOCK/REPLAY predictions per

## SCOPE â€” this covers the LOCAL viewmodel ONLY

Remote players draw WORLD models (wm_*), a different XModel set from the same
WeaponDef, so this request does nothing for them. Consistent with the long
standing symptom "some remote players show weapons and some do not": those
rendered because their assets happened to be resident already.

Data hint for the remote work: in egyptbots list 6 grows to ~31 items while
list 8 stays at 2-3, which reads as list 6 = all players' models, list 8 = the
local player's. NOT PROVEN.

## REMOTE PLAYERS â€” world models (build DE74301B, candidate)

`BG_GetWorldModel` @0x3BDD30 is hooked, and every model it resolves during native
playback gets the same request. Identification is exact, not inferred:

    BG_GetViewModel  @0x3BD8F0 -> sub_3B6E40(weapon, alt, slot 16 / 24,      i)
    BG_GetWorldModel @0x3BDD30 -> sub_3B6E40(weapon, alt, slot 0x388 / 0x390, i)

sub_3B6E40 indexes the WeaponDef by BYTE OFFSET (`*(QWORD*)(bg_weaponDefs[*a1] +
a3) + 8*a4`), so the two accessors differ only in the slot they read -- which is
why requesting the viewmodel does nothing for anyone else's gun. The mod already
had this address as `Functions::_BG_GetWorldModel = 0x3BCD30_b`, which
independently confirms the mapping.

Hooking the accessor beats enumerating entities: the engine calls it whenever it
resolves ANY world model, so it names exactly what it needs, when it needs it --
every remote player and every attachment, with no entity-array layout assumed.

Each distinct model is requested once and retried up to 5 times at 2 s intervals,
because unlike the viewmodel there is no per-model `hide` byte to confirm arrival.
Cache is 128 entries. Toggle `demo_worldmodel_request`.

calls Hook::create for it, so it is dead code and there is no duplicate hook.

NOT covered: player BODY models. If remote players appear with weapons but no

# â­ .dm_s2 -> NATIVE .demo TRANSCODE (2026-08-08, tools/s2_dm_to_demo.py)

## Why this route

Native playback works and the local viewmodel fix is CONFIRMED there, but S2 has
NO native recorder -- the only caller of CL_Demo_WriteGameState is the clip path,
which requires CL_IsDemoPlaying. The engine cannot make a .demo from live play.
Our theater CAN record. Transcoding gets recording + native playback together and
lets the theater's playback half be retired instead of debugged (it is currently
stuck at GATE D, DObj_MaterialsReady, a third readiness check).

## PROVEN â€” the mapping is mechanical

.dm_s2 network_data (id 2) and gamestate_message (id 7) share ONE layout, from
demo_recording.cpp pack_network():

    [u32 seq][u32 flags: low31 = entry readcount, bit31 = useZlib][raw msg data]

`entry readcount` is where CL_ParseServerMessage was entered live, i.e. the caller
had already consumed the netchan header AND the sequence long (that is how
msg.useZlib was set BEFORE entry). From that offset the next read is
MSG_ReadShort(length), then the body -- exactly what a native type-2 payload
holds after its own sequence long. So:

    native payload = [u32 msgSeq | useZlib<<31] + data[readcount:]
    native packet  = [u8 2][u32 packetSeq][u32 payloadLen][payload]

Confirmation that the offset is right: **2568 of 2568 records converted with ZERO
skipped**, every one carrying a valid int16 length prefix at data[readcount:].
A wrong offset would fail that test immediately.

Header and footer are copied verbatim from a shipped demo of the SAME MAP
(dday.demo for our mp_d_day recordings). The header carries a 79,356-byte state
blob at +0x1C whose consumer is unknown, and the footer is a full NetConstStrings
table that resolves the model indices snapshots carry -- copying a real one of the
same map avoids synthesising either.

## Validated offline

    tools/s2_demo_read.py   OK: 2569 packets, clean end-of-stream, all native rules pass
    tools/s2_svc_walk.py    pkt#0 -> svc 2 cmd_text, then svc 0 GAMESTATE
                            pkt#4 -> svc 6 snapshot serverTime=45050 deltaNum=0 (FULL)
                            pkt#5 -> svc 6 snapshot deltaNum=1 -> baseline=20

## âš  THESE FILES MUST NOT GET THE ONE-BIT FIX

The transcoded gamestate is the SECOND record in its message (a text command
precedes it), which is the LIVE framing -- bitpos ends byte-aligned and BOTH the
v9 and v10 bits are present, because the bytes came from a real server, not from
S2's buggy CL_Demo_WriteGameState.

So `demo_native_onebit` must be turned OFF for transcoded demos. Applying the fix
would skip a bit that genuinely exists and desync the parse. The shipped demos
still need it ON. NOT YET AUTOMATED -- a later build should detect the framing
rather than rely on a manual toggle.

    main/demo/x_d_day.0001.demo   4706 packets, 305557 B

wolfslair has NO same-map shipped template, so its NCS footer would be wrong.
Do that only after the d_day files prove the format.

# â­ RULE A16 â€” A TOGGLE MUST NEVER SILENTLY DISABLE AN UNRELATED FIX (2026-08-08)

First in-game test of a transcoded demo crashed. Crash dump (RULE A13) named it in
one read, with no probe:

    exception 0xC0000005, fault at IDA_0x462DA3, READ from 0x10 (NULL + 16)
    stack: 0x4638D7 (CL_ParseServerMessage_Internal) 0x464AE5 (CL_ParseServerMessage)
           0x919696 (CL_Demo_ProcessPacket_Type2_3) 0x918E97 (CL_Demo_ReadDemoMessage)

IDA 0x462DA3 is the ALREADY-KNOWN `*(QWORD*)(qword_2537508 + 16)` deref inside
CL_ParseGamestate, recorded in this file as fixed by installing a zeroed stand-in.

## The defect was mine, in cl_parse_gamestate_stub

    const bool apply = g_onebit_fix && g_native_playing && MSG_ReadBit_orig != nullptr;

`apply` gated FOUR unrelated things: the one-bit writer compensation, the
qword_2537508 stand-in, the asset census, and the NetConstStrings reload. I then
told the user to turn `demo_native_onebit` OFF for transcoded demos (correctly â€”
they do not need it), which ALSO removed the stand-in. CL_ParseGamestate then
faulted exactly as it did before that stand-in ever existed.

**The transcoded demo was never implicated.** It decoded perfectly right up to the
crash: `svc RAW #0 cursize=2257 useZlib=1`, `firstNibble=2 byte0=0x02` â€” byte-exact
with the offline decode, and the leading svc 2 text command the transcoder emits by
design.

**RULE: one flag, one behaviour. Never let a toggle named for feature X gate the
scaffolding that feature Y needs.** Split the decision at the point of use.

## â­ THE ONE-BIT FIX IS NOW AUTO-DETECTED â€” no toggle required

The manual toggle was itself the hazard, so it is gone as a requirement. Detection
is a direct consequence of the PROVEN msg_t layout (+40 = bitpos) and the proven
reader model, not a heuristic:

  * gamestate is the FIRST record in its message (every shipped .demo) â€” its 4-bit
    opcode came from byte0's LOW nibble, so bitpos is left at 4, MID-BYTE. S2's
    demo writer emitted one bit where the reader reads two: the fix APPLIES.
  * gamestate is a LATER record (a live capture, and our transcoded .demo where an
    svc 2 text command leads) â€” the opcode came from a HIGH nibble, so bitpos landed
    on 8, BYTE-ALIGNED. Both bits genuinely exist: the fix must NOT run, or it would
    skip a bit that is present and desync the parse.

So the test is `(bitpos & 7) != 0` at CL_ParseGamestate entry. Verified offline on
all five files, and it separates them cleanly:

    airshipdemo.demo    opcode read at bitpos 0 -> entry bitpos 4  (&7=4)  FIRST -> apply
    egyptbots.demo      opcode read at bitpos 0 -> entry bitpos 4  (&7=4)  FIRST -> apply
    dday.demo           opcode read at bitpos 0 -> entry bitpos 4  (&7=4)  FIRST -> apply
    x_d_day.0000.demo   opcode read at bitpos 4 -> entry bitpos 8  (&7=0)  LATER -> skip
    x_d_day.0001.demo   opcode read at bitpos 4 -> entry bitpos 8  (&7=0)  LATER -> skip

`demo_native_onebit` survives only as a FORCE-OFF override; leaving it on lets
detection decide per gamestate. The choice is printed every time:

    [native] gamestate framing: bitpos&7=N -> FIRST/LATER record -> one-bit writer fix ...

Build E0485F98, deployed and hash-verified. UNTESTED in game.

## Note from the same run â€” transcoded demos carry NO StreamSync commands

    [ss] pre-scan: 2568 packets walked, 0 StreamSync command(s) collected

Expected: our recorder starts at the connect gamestate, and StreamSync load requests
are a connect-time exchange. It does NOT threaten the viewmodel, because the shipped
fix issues `sub_196220` directly on the model the engine selected and is independent
of demo contents â€” that is exactly why it works on airshipdemo, whose list 8 never

# â­â­â­ THE ARCHIVE PACKET, EXACT â€” and why the player was in the sea (2026-08-08)

SYMPTOM after the first successful transcode: every player and killcam had a
weapon, but the local player was placed IN THE SEA and the view angles never
changed.

CAUSE: the transcoder emitted only type-2 snapshot packets. Snapshots carry the
WORLD. The LOCAL player's predicted origin / velocity / viewangles live in the
CLIENT ARCHIVE RING at `clientActive + 0xA568`, 188 bytes x 256 â€” and ONLY type-1
archive packets fill it. With the ring never written, the camera read an unwritten
slot: a fixed nonsense origin and frozen angles. Exactly the observed symptom.

Shipped demos are ~11 archives per snapshot (local/bot) or ~1:1 (networked).

## PROVEN â€” the wire layout, from the disassembly of CL_Demo_ProcessPacket_Type1

`sub_AF9B70` is the Arxan read thunk, so the DECOMPILE shows no arguments at all.
The DISASSEMBLY does: `edx` = size, `rcx` = destination.

    read  size  dest      field
      1     4   stack     ring index -> entry = clientActive + 188*idx + 0xA568
      2    12   entry+4   origin
      3    12   entry+16  velocity
      4     4   entry+32  bobB          <-- bobB BEFORE bobA
      5     4   entry+28  bobA
      6     4   entry+0   serverTime    <-- sixth, not first
      7    12   entry+36  viewangles
      8     4   entry+48  extra0        then `cmp dword ptr [rbp+30h], 0`
         if extra0 != 0:  4 -> +52, 2 -> +56   (== w0,w1 then w2)
         else:            zero +52 and +56
        128   entry+60  tail

    1 (type) + 4 (idx) + 52 + [6] + 128 = 185 â€” matching the size proven by sweep.

## CORRECTION â€” two earlier notes in this file were WRONG

Both "6 reads: 12,12,4,4,4,12" and "4 idx | 12 | 12 | 4 | 4 | 4 | 12 | 4 gate" are
wrong: there are SEVEN reads before the gate test and the order is scrambled. They
happen to total the same 48/52 bytes, which is why the size was still right and the
error stayed invisible. Marked CORRECTED in place.

The `demo_game::ClientArchiveEntry` struct (with its static_asserts on extra0 == 48
and w0 == 52) was RIGHT all along. Struct order != wire order.

## The transcode already had the data

`demo_recording.cpp capture_predicted` copies the engine's WHOLE archive entry
(`sample.cad = *entry`) using the engine's OWN ring index, and writes it as
predicted_data (TLV id 3, 60-byte payload). So every field a type-1 packet needs was
already in every .dm_s2 â€” it was simply never emitted. `tools/s2_dm_to_demo.py` now
converts id 3 -> type 1, interleaved in capture order (the TLV stream preserves it),
with the gamestate still hoisted to the front.

## Validated offline, three ways

    x_d_day.0000  5423 packets  archive 2854 : snapshot 2568   clean end-of-stream
    x_d_day.0001 23687 packets  archive 18981 : snapshot 4705  clean end-of-stream

  1. **Framing**: both walk to a clean terminator under the native rules. A wrong
     packet size desyncs within 3-7 packets, so 185 is confirmed again.
  2. **Field mapping vs a shipped demo**: the first archives of x_d_day.0000 and of
     dday.demo are IDENTICAL â€” origin (799.0, 5135.6, 725.0), ang (-8, -103, 0),
     bobB 183. Same map, same intro position, decoded by the same offsets.
  3. **Physical plausibility over time**: origin sweeps x -1301..1504, y 3068..5990,
     z 511..829 (the real mp_d_day playspace); 1299 distinct yaw values spanning
     -179..179; pitch -8..27. Not garbage, and not static.

## Known gap â€” the 128-byte tail is zeros

Our recorder captures only through w2 (+58); entry+60..187 is not captured and is
written as zeros. Its consumer is unidentified. If something downstream reads it,
that is the next thing to look at.

# â­â­â­â­ S2 **DOES** HAVE A NATIVE RECORDER â€” sub_91C710 = CL_Demo_StartRecord
# (2026-08-08). THIS CORRECTS A LONG-STANDING CLAIM IN THIS FILE.

## â›” CORRECTED â€” "S2 has NO separate CL_Demo_StartRecord"

This file has stated for weeks, under STILL OPEN, that "S2 has NO separate
CL_Demo_StartRecord -- the only caller of CL_Demo_WriteGameState is that clip path.
The live-match capture trigger is NOT yet located." **That is wrong.** The trigger
was located by asking who calls the configstring writer, which was already mapped.

    CL_InitCGame @0x7BFD0  ->  CL_Demo_StartRecord @0x91C710
    sub_70830    @0x70830  ->  CL_Demo_StartRecord

Both are the LIVE connect path. The recorder is wired into every connect.

## PROVEN â€” what CL_Demo_StartRecord does (decompiled in full)

    if (!CL_Demo_IsRecordingAllowed(client)) return;      // 0x90FBF0
    if (!CL_Demo_IsDemoStateIdle(client))    return;      // 0x9103D0
    ... allocate two 0x20000 scratch buffers, pick a slot ...
    handle = sub_912230(client, name, "GAME_REPLAY_FILE");   // OPEN FOR WRITE
    if (handle) {
        clc[+262744] = handle;
        clc[+262760] = 29;            // version
        clc[+262764] = 79384;         // header size
        clc[+262768] = clc[4];        // recording client slot  (= header +0x08)
        clc[+262772] = 0;
        clc[+262773] = (sub_197140(sub_197040()) == 1);   // header +0x0D !!
        clc[+262776] = sub_789870(client);                // header +0x10 (id-like)
        clc[+262784] = sub_9103C0();  // exe mode, must read back as 5
        memcpy(clc + 262788, sub_D0210(client), 0x135FC); // the 79,356 B state blob
        sub_9112C0(client, clc + 262760);                 // WRITE THE HEADER
        sub_911190(client, 1);
        clc[+346132] = 1;                                 // recording flag
        MSG_InitWrite(msg, buf, 0x20000);
        MSG_WriteLong (msg, clc[77]);                     // message sequence
        MSG_WriteBits (msg, 0, 4);                        // svc_gamestate
        MSG_WriteLong (msg, clc[32849]);                  // serverCommandSequence
        MSG_WriteString(msg, off_C60D778[2]);             // mapname
        MSG_WriteLong (msg, clientActive[+25556]);
        MSG_WriteString(msg, off_C60D790[2]);             // gametype
        MSG_WriteBit  (msg, sub_B8C70());                 // <-- ONE BIT
        MSG_WriteLong (msg, 0);
        CL_Demo_WriteConfigStrings(client, msg, 0);
        MSG_WriteBits (msg, 7, 4);  ... EOF, clientNum, checksumFeed, EOF
        compress with sub_DD9E0, then emit a type-2 packet:
            sub_912450("\x02", 1, client)      // packet type
            sub_912450(clc + 131388, 4, client)// sequence
            sub_912450(&len, 4, client)        // length
            body in 1024-byte chunks
    }

**Two things this settles at once:**

1. Everything our transcoder has to BORROW from a shipped demo â€” the 0x135FC state
   blob and the header fields â€” the engine builds itself, from live state
   (`sub_D0210(client)`). So a native recorder works on ANY map with no template.
2. **The one-bit writer bug is HERE, in the live recorder**, not just in the clip
   path: `MSG_WriteBit(msg, sub_B8C70())` writes one bit where CL_ParseGamestate
   reads two. So demos S2 records itself would be unplayable by S2 â€” which is
   exactly the defect already proven from the shipped files, now seen from the
   writing side. Fixing this one call makes recordings need NO read-side
   compensation at all.

## PROVEN â€” the gate, term by term

`CL_Demo_IsDemoStateIdle` @0x9103D0: `clc[+262752] == 0`. That dword is the demo
state (Play_f / SaveSegment_f test it == 2 for "playing").

`CL_Demo_IsRecordingAllowed` @0x90FBF0 requires ALL of:

    1. !off_A60E5E0 || *(DWORD*)(off_A60E5E0 + 16)        a dvar, value != 0
    2. sub_856280() == Dvar_GetBool(off_1BD3750)          a dvar, must be true
    3. *(BYTE*)(off_10F1B038 + 16)                        dvar "1766"
    4. byte_10F23F68 && sub_4A0B80(client) == 0           demo memory allocated,
                                                          primary client
                                       (sub_78A170(x) is literally `return x != 0`)
    5. !byte_1BD36F8                                      mode flag; the SAME global
                                                          the asset-unload gate
                                                          sub_38F590 reads

**Term 3 defaults to TRUE.** `CL_Demo_RegisterDvars` @0x910EF0 registers it as
`sub_B05E0("1766", 1, 0)` â€” bool, default 1. So the record-enable dvar is already
on, and the blocker is one of the other four.

## âš  MY OWN RAW DVAR READS WERE WRONG â€” do not use them

The probe read each dvar pointer at +16 and reported `dvar1BD3750 = 143`, then

sessions. That +16 reading is WRONG for these globals â€” most likely they are not

applies: do not assign meaning to an offset because a value looks plausible, and
certainly not when it does not.

We do not know the two dvars' names and could not read their values reliably.

**Its only caller is CL_Demo_StartRecord**, so the entire blast radius is "let
recording start"; nothing else in the engine consults it. Never forced while
`g_native_playing`, so playback can never recurse into recording.

This is enabling a shipped engine capability that config disables â€” the same spirit
as the mod's unlock-all. It is NOT manufacturing state: every byte of the demo is
still written by the engine's own recorder from live data.

Toggle `demo_record` (default ON; takes effect on the NEXT connect, since
CL_Demo_StartRecord only runs at cgame init).

## â­ WHY OUR EXISTING PLAYBACK FIXES SHOULD COVER WHAT IT RECORDS

Read straight out of CL_Demo_StartRecord, and it is strong corroboration that both
long-standing defects were always WRITER bugs:

  1. It writes `MSG_WriteBit(msg, sub_B8C70())` â€” ONE bit where CL_ParseGamestate
     reads two. And it writes the gamestate as the FIRST record in its message, so
     bitpos ends at 4 and our framing auto-detect APPLIES the one-bit fix. Correct
     by construction.
  2. It emits `[4-byte sequence][compressed body]` with NO int16 length prefix â€”
     precisely what `repair_gamestate_message()` inserts.

So a natively recorded demo should play with the fixes already shipped.

## â­â­ RULE A17 â€” NEVER WIDEN A NARROW RETURN TYPE WHEN DECLARING AN ENGINE FUNCTION

Cost: one live run, and a "fix" that silently did nothing while reporting success.

`sub_90FBF0` is `bool __fastcall(__int64)` â€” only **AL** is defined; the upper 56
bits of RAX are whatever was there. I declared the trampoline as returning
`std::int64_t`. The measured result:

    [rec] CL_Demo_IsRecordingAllowed(0) engine=140701904933632 -> returning -1223683328

140701904933632 == 0x7FF7B49B0440 â€” a POINTER, i.e. pure register residue. That
garbage was TRUTHY, so:

  * `force = g_force_record && !real && ...` evaluated FALSE and the enable never
    engaged â€” the whole point of the build;
  * and `report_record_gate` printed `ENGINE SAYS: IsRecordingAllowed=1`, which was
    meaningless. Two conclusions, both wrong, from one type declaration.

`sub_856280` returns `char`; I declared it `int`, so `term2=1` is equally void.

**THE RULE: declare the EXACT return width the decompiler shows.** `bool`/`char`
returns must be `bool`/`unsigned char` in the function-pointer type, never widened.
This is the Absolute Rule (no offset guessing) applied to the ABI rather than to
struct layout: a value that merely looks plausible is not evidence.

FIXED in build E8C6FEE7 (deployed, hash-verified). Withdrawn from the record above:
`IsRecordingAllowed=1` and `term2=1` are NOT established. `IsDemoStateIdle=1` IS
trustworthy â€” it was declared `bool(*)(int)`, the correct width, and is
independently corroborated by the raw `clc+262752 == 0` read.

## The NEXT gate after the two predicates â€” a capacity check

Even with both predicates true, CL_Demo_StartRecord only opens a file if

    *(QWORD*)v5 > (unsigned __int64)((numLocalClients + 1) * sub_9121C0(slot))
    && *((int*)clc + 65684) >= 0

where `v5 = sub_912170(...) = &qword_10F1B120`. So `qword_10F1B120` is a FREE-SPACE
figure for the demo record memory, and a slot index must be available. That is the
next thing that can refuse, so the probe now reports it as `demoMemFree=` in the
same line. One run should now show either a file handle, or which term still says no.

First enabled run recorded the hub / virtual lobby as well as the match, which the

ones. Forcing the whole predicate discarded the contextual ones too.

`byte_1BD36F8` is the hub discriminator, measured every run:

exclusion was always there; the blanket force removed it.

FIXED in build FDAAB07A: force only when `byte_1BD36F8 == 0` AND
`byte_10F23F68 != 0` (demo memory allocated). Both are plain byte reads, no ABI or
offset assumption â€” which matters, since RULE A17 is exactly why we override the
dvar terms instead of trying to evaluate them. Restoring engine behaviour, not a
special case.

## PROVEN â€” the self-recorded demo reached further than any before it

    REPAIRED prefix-less gamestate message: declared=-9559 -> inserted length=2453
    gamestate framing: bitpos&7=4 -> FIRST record -> one-bit writer fix APPLIED
    CL_ParseGamestate #1: connstate 5 -> 9   [one-bit writer fix applied]

**Both predicted writer defects appeared exactly as forecast from reading
CL_Demo_StartRecord, and both existing read-side fixes handled them.** That is a
clean confirmation that the length-prefix and one-bit defects are writer bugs, now

Failure point:

    #0  bits=11  last=-1  -> DID NOT RETURN   readcount=1218  bitpos=9738

With `last == -1` the absolute 11-bit path CANNOT raise 4780 (any value 0..2047 is
> -1). So the read took the 9-bit SKIP path and got `v <= 0`. The stream is out of
phase before the first entity index â€” i.e. something earlier in CL_ParseSnapshot
(playerstate / sub_66A900 / sub_668820 / the sub_666430 loop) consumed the wrong
number of bits.

## Observation from a smoke run (two DIFFERENT matches, so not conclusive)

Our .dm_s2 records `entryReadcount = 8` for live messages, i.e. the live caller had
consumed EIGHT bytes before CL_ParseServerMessage. The demo path consumes FOUR
(CL_Demo_ProcessPacket_Type2_3 reads one sequence long, then calls
CL_ParseServerMessage). Eight is the classic Q3 pair
`[u32 messageSequence][u32 reliableAcknowledge]`, and S2's CL_ParseServerMessage
@0x4649D0 reads NEITHER â€” it goes straight to MSG_ReadShort(length) â€” so the caller
owns both. Our transcoder strips all 8 and prepends its own 4-byte sequence, which
is why transcoded demos land in phase.

âš  NOT the proven cause. x03ae's messages DO decode and their svc streams parse
coherently up to and including the snapshot header, so the length prefix is being
read correctly there. The desync is strictly INSIDE the snapshot body. Recorded
because it is a real, measured 4-byte asymmetry between the live and demo paths and
it is the best current lead.

Also seen: native online packets are MTU-PADDED (raw=1244 with a 67- or 859-byte
decoded body), matching the note that publicmatch's packets are padded to 1244.
Harmless in itself â€” the declared int16 length bounds the decode â€” but it confirms
the native recorder stores something closer to the raw network packet than our
capture does.

## Side benefit worth remembering

A native recording of a map makes a PERFECT transcode template for that same map
(exact header state blob and NetConstStrings footer, same session). So the
transcoder's "same-map template" limitation is already removable in practice: record
once natively, and every later transcode on that map has a correct template.

# â­â­â­â­ THE A/B RESOLVED IT â€” THE GAMESTATE IS THE WHOLE BUG (2026-08-09)

Controlled pair, SAME online match (mp_forest_01, dom), same header, same footer,

                          bitpos&7=0 -> LATER record -> one-bit fix SKIPPED
                          RESULT: connstate 5 -> 9, svc msg #1..#11 parse,

                          RESULT: (previously, on the identical x03ae) 4780 on the
                                  first entity index read

Since the snapshot bytes are identical and the playback code is shared, EVERYTHING
DOWNSTREAM OF THE GAMESTATE IS EXCLUDED. The defect is in CL_Demo_StartRecord's
synthesised gamestate, or in how we read it.

## The two candidate mechanisms, and what separates them

  (a) CONTENT -- the synthesised gamestate carries only configstrings, written from
      live state at CL_InitCGame time, and lacks something the real connect
      gamestate carries.
  (b) FRAMING + our one-bit fix -- the synthesised gamestate is the FIRST record so
      bitpos ends at 4 and the fix is applied; the real one is the SECOND record so
      the fix is skipped.

âš  (b) alone CANNOT be the whole story: every shipped LOCAL demo (airship, egypt,
dday, gibraltar) also has a synthesised gamestate, is also the first record, also
gets the one-bit fix, and PLAYS. So if framing were sufficient, they would fail too.
That points at (a), or at an interaction between the two that only bites on the
larger/denser online gamestate.

  * delta against a missing baseline -- every demo's first snapshot is deltaNum=0 FULL

  * map-specific anything -- mp_d_day fails online and plays local

# â­â­ A REAL DEFECT IN OUR TRANSCODER â€” RENUMBERED MESSAGE SEQUENCES (2026-08-09)

## Measured live (CE, base verified per RULE A2)

`y_forest` and `y_forest0` (client 0 variant) BOTH stall: connstate reads **9** in
the live process, never 10. No 4780. Snapshots parse (`firstNibble=6`) but the
delta-index probe never dumps its 48-entry sample, so the entity block is barely
reached -- consistent with snapshots never becoming valid, since connstate 9 -> 10
happens in CL_FirstSnapshot, which only runs when CL_ParseSnapshot sets newSnapshots.

So the demo-client-number hypothesis is DISPROVEN (client 0 stalls identically).

## PROVEN â€” the transcoder discarded the real message sequence

The log shows the contradiction plainly:

    clc+0x138 = 1, 2, 3, 4          <- message sequence, from OUR renumbering
    snapshot messageNum = 29,30,31,32  <- the real sequence, inside the same message

Those are meant to be the same number. `s2_dm_to_demo.py` numbered packets 1,2,3...
and threw the real value away.

The real sequence survives in the capture. Live entry readcount is 8 -- two longs
consumed before CL_ParseServerMessage -- and dumping them shows:

    data[0:4]  = 29, 30, 31, 32, 33, ...   EXACTLY the snapshot messageNums
    data[4:8]  = reliableAcknowledge | (useZlib << 31)

âš  Note the ZLIB FLAG SITS ON A DIFFERENT LONG in each format:
    LIVE  [seq][reliableAck | zlib<<31][body]
    DEMO  [seq | zlib<<31][body]              (CL_Demo_ProcessPacket_Type2_3:
                                               v6 = MSG_ReadLong; clc[78] = v6 &
                                               0x7FFFFFFF; useZlib = v6 >> 31)
So stripping both live longs and writing one combined long is right -- only the
VALUE was wrong.

Also re-confirmed: the .dm_s2's own stored seq field is 0 in every record, because
`pack_network` fills it via `demo_game::clc_for(0)`, which reads the wrong global
(0x1BD3C00 vs the real clc at 0x1BD3D00). That long-standing bug is still unfixed
and now has a visible consequence.

FIXED in tools/s2_dm_to_demo.py: both the type-2 packet header sequence (-> clc+
0x2013C) and the payload's message sequence (-> clc+0x138) now carry the real value.

    z_forest.demo   first type-2 packet sequences: [29, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34]
                    demo client forced to 0; 2960 packets, clean end-of-stream

## âš  Why x_d_day.0000 played DESPITE the same defect is NOT explained

x_d_day.0000 was built by the same renumbering transcoder and reached ACTIVE. If the
sequence mismatch alone were fatal, it should have stalled too. So either the fix
above is not the whole story, or x_d_day tolerated it for a reason not yet
identified. Do not treat the renumbering as proven-causal until z_forest is tested.

## DEAD END recorded â€” CL_GetLocalClientActive is Arxan-ENCRYPTED

`CL_GetLocalClientActive` @0x795D0 reads `g_clientActive_encrypted` (0x1BD4308) and
runs a 16-way control-flow-flattened decryptor (`__ROR8__(NtCurrentTeb()->PEB,12)&0xF`
selects the case) before returning `clientActive + 91552*client`. There is NO plain
pointer to read, so Cheat Engine cannot cheaply reach clientActive / snap.valid /
newSnapshots. Do not try again; use an in-process hook if those fields are needed.

# â­â­â­ HEADER +0x0D PERFECTLY SEPARATES PLAYING FROM FAILING DEMOS (2026-08-09)

CONTROL FIRST: `forest_01.0000.dm_s2` PLAYS in the theater (user-confirmed). So the
captured source data is GOOD and every failure is in the container / transcode, not
the capture. That also re-validates the byte-identical diff result.

Header scalar comparison across seven files:

    file                  +0x0D  +0x10        +0x48    +0x4C  +0x54   RESULT
    dday.demo               1    2180834731   655360     0      0     PLAYS
    airshipdemo.demo        1    2180834731   655360     0      0     PLAYS
    x_d_day.0000.demo       1    2180834731   655360     0      0     PLAYS  (dday hdr)
    publicmatch.demo        0     122260590   524288     1      2     4780
    x03ae_6a77adc4.demo     0     122260590   524288     3      3     4780
    x0147_6a77b6ea.demo     0     122260590   524288     3      3     (untested)
    z_forest.demo           0     122260590   524288     3      3     stalls at 9

**+0x0D == 1 on every demo that plays, 0 on every one that fails.** 3/3 vs 4/4.

Crucially this is NOT an artefact of our tooling: `x_d_day.0000` is ONLINE data that
plays, and the only reason is that it inherited `dday.demo`'s header wholesale.
`y_forest`/`z_forest` are the same kind of online data with a header from our own
native recording, and they stall. The header is the variable.

## What +0x0D is, from the engine

    CL_Demo_StartRecord @0x91C710:  clc[+262773] = (sub_197140(sub_197040()) == 1)
    CL_Demo_Play_f      @0x910650:  sub_1973F0(sub_197040(), <header +0x0D>)
                                    which is just *(DWORD*)(obj + 40) = b

CLAUDE.md recorded in the RETRACTED note on sub_197040 that "the +0x0D byte differing
between working and failing demos is still a real signal worth tracing, but through
the consumer" -- that was right and was never followed up. The 7-file split above is
the evidence that justifies tracing it now.

STRONG INFERENCE (not proven): +0x0D distinguishes private/local from public/online
recordings, and something on the playback path gates on the value stored at
`sub_197040() + 40`.

                     (x0147's 0x135FC state blob and footer kept intact)

# â­â­â­â­ THE PUBLIC-MATCH DEMO DEFECT â€” MISSING NETCONSTSTRING TYPE 21 (2026-08-09)

USER CONFIRMED: `dday.demo` was recorded by them in a PRIVATE match. So the header
+0x0D split is PRIVATE(1) vs PUBLIC(0), and the real statement is:

    **Native demo playback has never worked for a PUBLIC-match recording.**

Our own recordings fail only because they are public matches. Our recording hook is
exonerated -- publicmatch.demo shares the identical signature and predates it.

## THE DISCRIMINATOR â€” footer netconststring type 21 (GSC script strings)

    demo                    type 21   match     RESULT
    dday.demo                 396     private   PLAYS
    airshipdemo.demo          396     private   PLAYS
    publicmatch.demo        ABSENT    public    4780
    x0147_6a77b6ea (ours)   ABSENT    public    stalls at 9
    x03ae_6a77adc4 (ours)   ABSENT    public    4780

5/5. And it is the ONLY footer difference that splits pass/fail cleanly -- the
header scalars were already excluded by the za/zb tests (both failed), and
`x_d_day.0000` (PUBLIC data) PLAYS precisely because it borrowed dday's footer,
which carries the 396 strings.

CLAUDE.md flagged this in the 2026-08-08 footer analysis -- "publicmatch carries NO
script strings (type 21) ... STRONG INFERENCE, not proven; nothing yet shows a
type-21 lookup actually occurs during playback" -- and then parked it. It was right.

## MECHANISM (STRONG INFERENCE, not yet proven)

Entity-state fields that hold script strings are encoded with a bit width derived
from the netconststring table SIZE for that type. With type 21 absent, the reader
uses a different width than the writer used, so the entity delta desyncs:

    index goes backwards      -> Com_Error "4780"
    index does not increase   -> snapshot never validates -> connstate stuck at 9

ONE cause, both observed failure modes. To prove it, find the reader that sizes a
field from the type-21 count.

## â­ THE TABLE IS GLOBAL, NOT PER-MAP â€” which makes a fix cheap

    dday / airshipdemo / egyptbots / gibraltar
      -> all 396 entries, and the listed entries are BYTE-IDENTICAL (same md5)
         across all four maps

(The tool lists the first 20 entries, so the md5 covers those; combined with the
identical 396 count on four different maps, "global GSC string table" is the strong
reading.)

Consequence: a public-match demo can be repaired by splicing the type-21 block from
ANY private demo's footer. No same-map requirement.

## Confirmation test built

    zc_forest.demo   forest (public) capture + dday.demo as the COMPLETE template
                     (header + state blob + footer, so type 21 = 396 present)

If it plays, the diagnosis is confirmed and the fix is: make the recorder write
type 21 into the footer for public matches (or splice it post-hoc).

## Fix options, in preference order

  1. Find why sub_5DC650 (the footer NCS writer) omits type 21 in a public match and
     make it write it. Cleanest -- recordings become self-sufficient.
  2. Post-process: inject the type-21 block into a public demo's footer offline.
     Cheap, needs no engine change, and is map-independent because the table is
     global.
  3. Read side: install the type-21 table from any source before parsing snapshots
     (the mod already re-runs NetConstStrings_Load @0xDEF90 after CL_ParseGamestate
     for exactly this class of problem -- but note type 21 is NOT among the 10 level
     types it restores, so that path does not currently cover it).

# â­â­â­ THE FOOTER CARRIES THE MAP NAME â€” footer_body + 272 (2026-08-09)

USER INSIGHT, then proven. `zc_forest` (forest capture + dday's complete template)
loaded mp_d_day and then crashed looking for mp_forest_01.d3dbsp. The map name comes
from the FOOTER, not the gamestate.

Address arithmetic that predicts it:

    CL_Demo_StopRecord  writes the footer body from clc+342144  (3984 bytes)
    CL_Demo_Play_f      loads the level with DB_LoadLevelXAssets(clc+342416)
    342416 - 342144 = 272

Verified by reading footer_body+272 out of six demos:

    dday.demo            'mp_d_day'
    airshipdemo.demo     'mp_airship'
    publicmatch.demo     'mp_d_day'
    x0147_6a77b6ea.demo  'mp_forest_01'
    x03ae_6a77adc4.demo  'mp_shipment_s2'
    zc_forest.demo       'mp_d_day'      <- the crash, explained

**This is why the transcoder needed a same-map template.** It was never the state
blob or the NCS model table -- it was one string in the footer. `x_d_day.0000`
worked only because template and capture happened to be the same map.

FIXED in tools/s2_dm_to_demo.py: the map name is read from the capture (map_header
TLV id 1, falling back to a scan of the gamestate record) and patched into
footer+272 whenever it differs from the template's. Reported on every run.

    zd_forest.demo   forest capture + dday's template, map name patched
                     footer+272 = 'mp_forest_01', type 21 = 396 entries
                     2960 packets, clean end-of-stream

## The mechanism, end to end

`sub_5DC650` (the footer NCS writer, called from CL_Demo_StopRecord) dumps a REGISTRY
of registered (type,index) pairs -- `dword_A609178` entries at `unk_A60917C`, sorted,
with 26 per-type counts at `unk_A608570`, each resolved through
`sub_DED00(type, index, &out)`.

  * LOCAL match: the client IS the server and runs GSC, so script strings are
    registered -> the registry holds them -> the footer carries type 21 = 396.
  * PUBLIC match: nothing registers them -> the footer carries type 21 = 0. But the
    recorded snapshots still reference type-21 indices, so playback cannot resolve
    them and the snapshot never validates -> connstate sticks at 9 (or the delta
    desyncs into "4780").

## Why the playback-side reload never fixed it â€” TWO STORAGES

    footer install        -> pointer table  qword_A60D180 + 0x20000 + 8*index
                             (index -> string)     <- what playback resolves through
    NetConstStrings_Load  -> block lists    qword_5A00C30[2*type]
                             (name -> index)       <- all our reload ever restored

Both facts were already in this file; they were never connected. That is why
"type 21 = Y after reload, and it still stalled" looked like a refutation of the
type-21 hypothesis when it was actually a different table.

## THE FIX â€” built in, at record time (build deployed pending test)

In the existing CL_Demo_StartRecord stub, after the original runs: if
`netconststrings_block_list(21)` is empty, call **NetConstStrings_Load @0xDEF90**.
The strings then enter the registry and `sub_5DC650` writes them into the footer,
exactly as a local match already does. Nothing is fabricated -- the engine's own
loader producing the engine's own table. Gated on `g_force_record && !g_native_playing`.

## TOOL â€” tools/s2_demo_fix_ncs.py, repairs demos already on disk

Splices type 21 from any LOCAL recording into a public demo's footer, rebuilding the
counts, total and footer size. **The donor may be from ANY map**: type 21 was
verified identical (396 entries, same listing) across dday / airshipdemo / egyptbots
/ gibraltar, because it is a GSC string table, not map content.

## The registry's writers (found, not yet used)

    sub_5DC450(index)   hardcodes type 20; dedupes via a bitmap at unk_A608570+3077,

                        appends {type, cs_index - start}
    sub_5DC530 / sub_5DC590 / sub_5DC5F0   same shape, other types

So a proper built-in fix registers each type-21 entry at record time so the engine
writes them itself. Needs: the correct registrar for type 21, and the entry count /

## AUTOMATED â€” build 4166FC30, deployed

The ineffective record-time attempt is REMOVED and replaced by the proven splice,
applied automatically when recording stops. `CL_Demo_StopRecord` @0x90FCA0 (-0x1000 =
0x90ECA0, not hooked elsewhere, cold -- once per disconnect) is hooked; after the
engine closes the file, the newest .demo is checked and, if its footer has no type 21,
the block is spliced in from any local demo already in main/demo.

  * local recordings are left untouched (the engine already wrote type 21)
  * the file is only rewritten after a FULL successful parse; any inconsistency
    aborts the repair
  * the donor may come from any map -- type 21 is a GSC string table, not map content
  * if no donor exists yet it says so plainly instead of silently producing a demo
    that will not play
  * toggle `demo_autofix` (default ON)

NOTE the one-time requirement: at least one LOCAL recording must exist in main/demo to
donate the table. A proper fix would register type 21 at record time so the engine
writes it itself -- the registry writers are identified (sub_5DC450 hardcodes type 20;
sub_5DC4B0 is the generic {type, index-start} form; sub_5DC530/590/5F0 likewise) but
the correct registrar for type 21 and its valid index range are NOT established, and
guessing them is exactly what produced the failed record-time attempt.

## The repair now ships three ways, none needing external tooling

  1. AUTOMATIC at CL_Demo_StopRecord -- a public recording is repaired the moment it
     is written. Local recordings are detected (counts[21] != 0) and left untouched.
  2. GUI BUTTON "Fix Selected Demo" in the Engine demos section, for when the game
     was killed mid-match so CL_Demo_StopRecord never ran. Reports the outcome
     inline, green for repaired / amber for anything else. Safe on any demo.
  3. tools/s2_demo_fix_ncs.py -- still there for batch work, now optional.

Honest limit of the button: a demo whose recording was interrupted has NO FOOTER at
all, not merely a missing type 21. That cannot be repaired from outside (the footer
carries the session's own model/material tables and the map name). The code detects
it and says so rather than producing a file that will not play.

C++ safety: the file is only rewritten after a FULL successful parse of the
NetConstStrings block; any inconsistent count or length aborts the repair untouched.

# LUI / HUD TIMESCALE ON NATIVE PLAYBACK (2026-08-09)

The theater already scaled HUD animation via `LUI_Layout_stub` (per-stream carry so
delta_a and delta_b do not steal milliseconds from each other), but everything was
gated on `demo_playback::is_playing()`, so native playback got none of it.

Now both systems feed it:

    theater -> demotimescale (our dvar)
    native  -> the ENGINE's own speed and pause

## The engine's demo speed â€” PlaybackData + 28 (INFERRED, guarded)

`CL_Demo_Play_f` writes 1.0f there at play, and CL_Demo_ReadDemoMessage's
end-of-stream branch resets it to 1065353216 (also 1.0f). A float initialised at play
and reset at stop is the shape of a speed, and it tracked the up/down-arrow control
in game (user-confirmed: "our lui timescale is working").

Still only INFERRED, so `demo_native::engine_timescale()` rejects anything outside
0.01..100 and returns 1.0f -- a wrong guess degrades to normal speed, never to a
broken HUD. It prints each change once so the field stays falsifiable:

    [native] demo timescale now 0.500x (PlaybackData+28)

## The engine's demo pause â€” CL_Demo_IsPaused @0x916E30 (PROVEN)

    bool CL_Demo_IsPaused()
      { return PlaybackData && *(BYTE*)(dvar_cl_demo_pause + 16)
               && !*(BYTE*)(PlaybackData + 10); }

Native playback has its OWN pause command, so the theater's `paused()` never saw it
and the HUD kept animating on a paused native demo. `demo_native::engine_paused()`
calls the engine predicate directly.

Declared `bool(*)()` -- the exact return width. RULE A17: widening a narrow return is
what made an earlier probe read register residue as true. Address resolved inside the
function (RULE A14): 0x916E30 - 0x1000 = 0x915E30.

`scale_lui_delta` now returns 0 and clears the carry when either system is paused, so
the HUD freezes completely as it did on H1 and in the theater.

Deliberately NOT changed: `UI_UpdateTime_stub` still overrides the HUD absolute clock
for the theater only. During native playback the engine drives its own serverTime
correctly, so overriding it would fight the engine rather than help.

Build C81095F0, deployed.

# DIRECTX ERRORS ON MINIMISE â€” our overlay held the back buffer (2026-08-09)

USER REPORT: DirectX errors when minimising, suspected the GUI. Correct.

## PROVEN by inspection

`demo_gui.cpp` hooked ONLY `IDXGISwapChain::Present` (vtable 8). It creates an
`ID3D11RenderTargetView` over the swapchain's back buffer and **never releases it**:
`release_rtv()` was defined at line 103 and called from NOWHERE -- dead code since it
was written.

DXGI refuses `ResizeBuffers` while any back-buffer reference is outstanding
(DXGI_ERROR_INVALID_CALL, "cannot resize, outstanding references"), and the game calls
ResizeBuffers on every minimise/restore. So the overlay was blocking the game's own
resize for the life of the process.

## FIX (build 42FCF639, deployed)

  * hook `IDXGISwapChain::ResizeBuffers` (vtable index **13**; Present is 8)
  * in the hook: `release_rtv()` + `ImGui_ImplDX11_InvalidateDeviceObjects()` BEFORE
    calling the original, so no reference is outstanding
  * do NOT recreate the view inside the resize hook -- on a minimise the new size is
    0x0. `present_hook`'s existing `ensure_render_target` picks it up on the next
    real frame
  * skip ImGui entirely while `IsIconic(g_hwnd)`: the back buffer is 0x0 then, draws
    are wasted, and ImGui asserts on a zero display size

## âš  Installed from BOTH hook paths

The vtable is read in two places -- `hook_present_from_swap` (real swapchain) and
`hook_present_via_dummy` (a temporary swapchain, used when the game created its own
before demo::init, which is the NORMAL case here). Hooking ResizeBuffers in only the
first would have left the bug in place for the path that actually runs. Factored into
`install_resize_hook()` and called from both; dxgi.dll's vtable is shared, so either
source yields the same function.

# NUMERIC DVAR NAMES â€” WHY THEY CANNOT BE DERIVED (measured 2026-08-09)

The mod already carries `src/DvarMappings.hpp`: **1476 entries, 1259 real-name ->
numeric mappings** (plus 217 dvars that already have plain names, and 323
descriptions). New tool `tools/s2_dvar_map.py` reads it and translates either way.

Asked whether a script could name ALL of them. Measured, from those 1259 pairs:

    ids sorted ascending -> names alphabetical   50.8%  = chance. NOT an alpha index.
    prefix clustering                            none.  cg_* spans ids 35..5860,
                                                        fx_* spans 4..5637
    distinct ids vs names                   1254 / 1259 = near-collision-free, so it
                                                        is an INDEX/counter, NOT a
                                                        hash of the name
    tail 6017..6021 = IsdlcDivisionEnabled_ARTILLERY / SCOUT / COMMANDO / GRENADIER
    / RESISTANCE -- sequential AND semantically grouped = registration order

**Conclusion: the numeric name is a registration index. There is no inverse.** Names
can only come from a SOURCE (a dump, another build) or from identifying a dvar by what
reads it -- which is how 1762, 5816 and 2669 were established here.

Coverage: numeric ids run 2..6021 and 4766 ids in that range have no recorded name.

## Independent confirmation of an earlier finding

`s2_dvar_map.py 1762` returns **cg_drawGun** -- confirming, from a completely separate
source, CLAUDE.md's identification of dvar "1762" as the cg_drawGun equivalent made
from its use inside CG_DrawViewWeapon.

## Added (twin-proven only)

    2669  cl_demo_client   CL_Demo_RegisterDvars stores it in dvar_cl_demo_client, and
                           CL_Demo_Play_f's tail sets it from header +0x08 in the same
                           order as MW3's named twin
    5816  cl_demo_pause    same registration + CL_Demo_IsPaused reads it

Deliberately NOT added: "1766" (record enable) and "5756" (a 10-second threshold in
sub_91A3A0). Their BEHAVIOUR is known but their real names are not, and an invented
