# â­â­â­ THE THEATER CAMERAS â€” FOUND, INCLUDING THE FREECAM SPEED (2026-08-09)

User hint: MW3 has `player_spectateSpeedScale`. It does (string @0x46FFCE) but only
BG_RegisterDvars references it, so the name was a dead end -- S2's equivalent is a
baked constant, found instead by tracing the camera path.

## The routing, from CG_PredictPlayerState @0x4EFA0

    if (CG_IsTheaterFreeCamera(c) || CG_IsTheaterOrbitCamera(c)) {
        ... load the newest usercmd from clientActive+25928 (ring, & 0x7F) ...
        if (CG_IsTheaterOrbitCamera(c)) { sub_913AE0(c, cmd); return 0; }
        sub_9135D0(c, cmd); return 0;
    }

    sub_9135D0  FOLLOW / third-person: origin = the demo client's entity, z += 35
                (eye height), angles from the usercmd, then sub_913830 pulls the
                camera back 85.0 units along the view vector with a trace.
    sub_913AE0  the FLY camera: friction, accelerate toward a wish velocity, then
                sub_9140A0 integrates position with a trace.

Camera mode lives at PlaybackData + 6297228 (0/1/2); mode 2 is the orbit/fly camera
(CG_IsTheaterOrbitCamera tests == 2). sub_91AB50(client, mode) sets it and is what
action 4/168 (F2) cycles.

## THE SPEED

    v18 = ((maxAbs * 190.0) / (magnitude * 127.0)) * 3.0;     wish-speed scale

    913d65  mulss xmm11, cs:dword_B639A8   ; 190.0  <- the speed
    913d72  divss xmm11, xmm0
    913d77  mulss xmm11, cs:dword_B37828   ; 3.0

âš  SCALING THE INPUT CANNOT WORK. `maxAbs / magnitude` is scale-invariant
(analog-stick normalisation), so multiplying forwardmove/rightmove changes nothing.
The constants are the only lever.

    dword_B37828 (3.0)    15+ xrefs across the whole game -- UNTOUCHABLE
    dword_B639A8 (190.0)  only TWO xrefs, one of which is this instruction

## FIX â€” repoint ONE instruction, don't patch a shared constant (build 3EE569DD)

Even 190.0 has a second user (sub_354030), so instead of patching the constant we
rewrite the rip-relative displacement of the single instruction at IDA 0x913D65 to
point at a float the mod owns. Nothing else in the game is affected, and the value is
then live-adjustable with no re-patching.

Safety: the opcode is verified byte for byte (F3 44 0F 59 1D disp32) before writing,
the displacement is range-checked against INT32 (our DLL could load too far from the
game module), and every failure path leaves the engine stock and says why.

GUI: "Freecam speed" slider 10..400 with a Reset to the stock 190, in the Engine
demos section. Shows "not patchable in this build" if the patch declined.

`MENU_DEMO_SCREENSHOT_CAPTURE_FAILED` and calls sub_916870 with 240x180 and 1440

# NEW AREA â€” FORCE HOSTING / LISTEN SERVER (started 2026-08-09)
# â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•â•

GOAL: make a real match run on the player's own exe (a listen server) instead of a
Demonware-provisioned one, while other players can still find and join it.

## Context from the user's existing "semi force host" tool

It worked by BLOCKING joins to other lobbies until the game made them lobby host;
other players then joined them. Map and player count were controlled with the
`playlist` command plus `ui_mapname` / `ui_gametype`. But once the match started they
had NO in-game control -- i.e. the match ran elsewhere, seeded from their lobby
settings. The user's expectation, which matches the evidence: if the server were
truly local, the playlist spoofing would be unnecessary because the spawn would read
their own dvars.

## â­ S2 ALREADY SPAWNS LOCAL SERVERS â€” proven by our own demo logs

Every lobby entry produces:

    ------ Server Initialization ------
    Server: mp_hub_allies_slim
    Loading Map: maps/mp/mp_hub_allies_slim.d3dbsp
    ------- Game Initialization -------

with com_sv_running set. So "can this build host?" is ALREADY ANSWERED YES. The
question is only what routes a real match away from that path.

## â­â­ THE LOBBY PARAMS STRUCT â€” Party_SetLobbyParamFromCmd @0x196D70

Found offline by string search (`matchmaking_allowJoiningListenServer` @0xB467D8 has
exactly ONE xref). Parses `<var> <value>` or `set/rule <var> <value>` and writes:

    params[0]  party_minplayers
    params[1]  party_maxplayers                        <- the 12 -> 18 lever
    params[2]  party_matchedplayercount
    params[4]  party_minlobbytime
    params[6]  ui_mapname   (sub_688B70)               <- the map lever
               ui_gametype  (sub_197320)
    params[13] requireOpenNat
    params[15] matchmaking_allowJoiningListenServer    <- THE SWITCH
    params[17] rankedMatch

Live object when called with NULL: `qword_6CF8698`, else
`sub_470F20(sub_470D30(0)) + 592`. NOTE the same `+592` object appears in the demo
work as `sub_197040() = sub_470F20(sub_470CB0()) + 592`, whose +40 receives the demo
header's +0x0D byte. Same object family, already half-known.

**This is exactly the surface the semi-force-host tool drove -- and params[15] is the
one it never touched.**

## â­ THE SHIPPED PLAYLISTS DISAGREE, WHICH IS THE WHOLE CLUE

Playlist var blobs are baked into the binary as text:

    0xABF5560  "... matchmaking_allowJoiningListenServer 0; ... rankedMatch 0;"
    0xABF60F6  "party_maxplayers 32; ... matchmaking_allowJoiningListenServer 0;"
    0xABF62B0  "party_maxplayers 4;  ... matchmaking_allowJoiningListenServer 1;"
    0xABF6343  "party_maxplayers 4;  ... matchmaking_allowJoiningListenServer 1;"

Small (4-player) playlists ALLOW listen servers; the large public ones do not. So the
capability is live in the shipped game and is switched off by playlist data.

## Other listen-server strings, each with ONE xref (offline leads, not yet followed)

    0xB33930  gamePreventListenServer              -> sub_93260  (0xf1b)  <- a GATE
    0xB33470  EXE_DISCONNECTEDFROMOWNLISTENSERVER  -> sub_909D0
    0xB3F3C8  OnHubListenServer                    -> data (LUI callback table)
    0xB51838  AllowGameBattlesListenServers
    0xB51858  IsRestrictedToListenServers

## NEXT, all offline

  1. `sub_93260` and `gamePreventListenServer` -- the most likely hard gate.
  2. Find the READER of params[15] (offset +60). That is the decision point between
     "advertise/allow a listen server" and "ask Demonware for one".
  3. `IsRestrictedToListenServers` / `AllowGameBattlesListenServers` look like a
     GameBattles/competitive path that FORCES listen servers -- if that exists, it is
     a shipped code path that already does what we want, and the job becomes making
     the normal path take it.

## âš  THE HONEST RISK, RECORD IT NOW

None of this proves other players' matchmaking can be made to route to our machine.
If Demonware brokers and validates the session server-side, the client can host all
it likes and nobody will find it. Establish the DISCOVERY half before building on the
hosting half.

## Static-analysis limit already hit

`sub_48C0C0` (the map-spawn path) has NO code xrefs -- its only reference is a .pdata
unwind record ({BeginAddress, EndAddress, UnwindInfo}), so it is reached through
Arxan's indirect dispatch. Do not expect to trace the host-vs-remote branch by
callers; go via the strings and the params struct instead, which is what worked here.

## FORCE HOST â€” two candidate gates ELIMINATED (2026-08-09, offline)

### â›” `gamePreventListenServer` is NOT the blocker

Registered in the dvar block sub_93260 @0x9379B:

    93799  xor edx, edx                       ; default value = 0
    9379b  lea rcx, "gamePreventListenServer"
    937a2  call sub_B05E0                     ; Dvar_RegisterBool
    937a7  xor edx, edx                       ; <- the returned dvar_t* is DISCARDED

A bool defaulting to **0** (i.e. NOT preventing), and no global keeps the pointer, so
no client code reads it through a cached dvar. It cannot be what blocks listen
servers. Dropped as a lead.

Incidental: it is one of the few PLAIN-named dvars in a block otherwise full of
numeric ones ("1449", "1316", "2507", com_maxfps, "5351"=sv_paused, "183"=cl_paused,
"1080"=com_sv_running -- the last of which cross-checks DvarMappings' `sv_running
1080`).

### â›” The GameBattles pair is a SEPARATE feature, not the general path

A `{name_ptr, func_ptr}` script-binding table at 0xB51020 maps:

    0xB51830  AllowGameBattlesListenServers -> Script_AllowGameBattlesListenServers 0x299120
    0xB51840  IsRestrictedToListenServers   -> Script_IsRestrictedToListenServers   0x2991C0

Both are thin script marshallers over:

    GameBattles_AllowListenServers @0x29DBB0
        return *(qword*)(session+272) && *(dword*)(that + 16);      // a bool dvar
    GameBattles_IsRestrictedToListenServers @0x29E910
        return sub_A05200(*(qword*)(*(qword*)(session+296) + 16), sub_837100()) != 0;
                          // a STRING dvar, membership-tested against sub_837100()

So they are two dvars hanging off a session/config object, gating the GameBattles
(competitive) feature. They prove listen servers are a live concept in this build but
they are not the general matchmaking lever. Named in the IDB; not pursued further.

### The lever is still params[15]

`matchmaking_allowJoiningListenServer` -> `Party_SetLobbyParamFromCmd` params[15],
which the shipped playlist blobs set to 0 for the large public playlists and 1 for
the small ones.

`Party_SetLobbyParamFromCmd` has 15+ callers, including **sub_9CDA0** -- already
known from the demo work as the function that loads the "hub" and services the
`dword_8BDA060` latch. So lobby params are applied on the same path that brings up
the virtual lobby.

### NEXT â€” find the READER of params[15]

That is the actual decision point between "allow/advertise a listen server" and "ask
Demonware for one". The struct base is `sub_470F20(sub_470D30(0)) + 592`, so
params[15] is `+652` from that object. Offline approach: look for code that loads
that object and tests a byte/dword at +652, starting with the party/matchmaking
region around 0x193000-0x197000 where Party_SetLobbyParamFromCmd and
CL_StreamSync_ParseServerLoadRequest both live.

âš  Still unproven, and still the thing that decides feasibility: whether other
players' matchmaking can be made to route to our machine at all.

# Ã¢Â­ÂÃ¢Â­ÂÃ¢Â­Â FORCE HOSTING Ã¢â‚¬â€ THE MECHANISM, FOUND (2026-08-09, entirely offline)

S2 has a complete **System Link** subsystem: a real client-side listen server on your
own exe, advertised on the network, joinable through the game's own browse menu, with
Demonware out of the loop. That is the "fully controllable peer-to-peer server" target,
and the switches that select it are now proven.

## PROVEN Ã¢â‚¬â€ the matchtype decision tree

`sub_651910` builds the match-type telemetry tag and states the logic outright:

    if      (Com_IsOnlineGame() && sub_197140(sub_197040()))  -> "matchtype/private"
    else if (Com_IsOnlineGame())                              -> "matchtype/online"
                                                                 (+ "cl_dcid/%d", and
                                                                  "sv_dcid/%d" when
                                                                  obj+1598540 != 0)
    else if (Com_IsSystemLink())                              -> "matchtype/systemlink"

Both predicates are plain dvar reads (S2 dvar layout: +12 type, +16 value):

    Com_IsSystemLink   0x856750   *(u8*)(dvar_systemlink + 16)     dvar @ 0xD8ACE10
    Com_IsSystemLink_2 0x856770   identical body
    Com_IsOnlineGame   0x856280   Dvar_GetBool(dvar_online)        dvar @ 0x1BD3750
    Com_IsPublicOnlineMatch 0x857B90  online && !private && !systemlink

## Ã¢Â­Â PROVEN Ã¢â‚¬â€ the same triple decides WHERE SETTINGS COME FROM

`sub_745050` (the UI element dispatcher), case 389:

    if ( sub_197140(sub_197040()) || Com_IsSystemLink() || !Com_IsOnlineGame() )
        read the gametype from "mp/gameTypesTable.csv"   <-- LOCAL
    else
        read it from the playlist                        <-- SERVER-SUPPLIED

That is exactly the user's own observation that "the spawned server grabs my current
dvar values". private OR systemlink OR offline => the match is configured locally.
It also explains why the semi-force-host tool needed the `playlist` spoof: it stayed
in the online branch, so the playlist was still the authority.

## Ã¢Â­ÂÃ¢Â­Â PROVEN Ã¢â‚¬â€ the LAN advertise, and its gate

`SystemLink_BroadcastServerInfo` @ 0x479DD0 (descriptive; behaviour-proven):

    if ( !Com_IsOnlineGame() )
      if ( Com_IsSystemLink() )
        if ( (!byte_1BD36F8 && sub_852810()) || (off_1BCF4E0[16] && sessionType != 2) )
          if ( *(DWORD*)(a1 + 1598540) )        // <-- WE ARE THE SERVER
            *a3 = 3;
            gather gametype sub_1970A0, maxplayers sub_197110, sub_1970E0,
                   the player block at a1+1032, mapname from the cmd args
            return sub_6DDB00(...)              // send it

So a locally hosted match is DISCOVERABLE only when all four hold. The counterpart is
the browse menu, issued from sub_747DF0 as a literal Cbuf command:

    "forcenosplitscreencontrol UI_SetActiveMenu_SYSTEMLINKJOINGAME\n"   @ 0xBA0DF0

`a1 + 1598540` is the host flag: it is the same field that gates the "sv_dcid/%d" tag
in sub_651910, and sits 4 bytes below `a1 + 1598544`, which the IsServerDedicated chain
(`sub_481720` -> `*(DWORD*)(a1+1598544) && sub_480D80()`) reads. Session type is at
`a1 + 1598460`. This is the same multi-megabyte object as qword_2537508 from the demo
work (CLAUDE.md records sub_47E670 indexing a1[399636] == byte 1598544).

## Ã¢Â­Â PROVEN Ã¢â‚¬â€ systemlink also SHORT-CIRCUITS THE ONLINE-SERVICE GATES

Two of the online requirement checks return "allowed" as soon as systemlink is set:

    sub_856200: if (sub_B8CB0(a1) || systemlink || sub_BA660() || !sub_FEC20() ...) return 1;
    sub_856790: if (sub_B8CB0(a1) || systemlink || sub_BA660()) return 0; else return sub_FEC20();

So the switch is not cosmetic Ã¢â‚¬â€ the engine deliberately drops its online-service
preconditions in system-link mode. That is what makes a Demonware-free session legal
to the rest of the engine rather than something that has to be forced past checks.

## Ã¢Â­Â PROVEN Ã¢â‚¬â€ the two parameter surfaces (they are NOT the same table)

**1. `g_sessionParamTable` @ 0xF924A0** Ã¢â‚¬â€ 15 entries, stride 32,
`{const char* name, u32 flags, const char** enumNames, u32 size, u32 offset}`:

    playlist     0x00  64      online       0x64  2  {mp, sp}
    playlist_sp  0x40  32      matchtype    0x66  4  {online, private, splitscreen, systemlink}
    localplayers 0x6A  4       party        0x6E  1
    gamebattles  0x78  1       cl_dcid      0xC8 64   sv_dcid 0x108 64
    nods_dcid / 50ms / 75ms / 100ms / 150ms / maxms _dcid, 64 each

`playlist` being entry 0 of THIS table is why the semi-force-host tool's playlist
command worked at all. `s_matchtypeNames` @ 0xF923F8 is the NULL-terminated enum
{online, private, splitscreen, systemlink}.

**2. `Party_SetLobbyParamFromCmd` @ 0x196D70** Ã¢â‚¬â€ the PLAYLIST RULE names, a different
set entirely: ui_mapname, ui_gametype, party_minplayers, party_maxplayers,
party_matchedplayercount, party_minlobbytime, requireOpenNat,
matchmaking_allowJoiningListenServer (params[15]), rankedMatch (params[17]).

Do not conflate them. The first selects the SESSION KIND; the second configures a
lobby once a kind is chosen.

## THE ROUTE TO A CONTROLLABLE CLIENT-SIDE SERVER

Set, before the match is created:

    dvar_online     (0x1BD3750) -> 0        Com_IsOnlineGame() false
    dvar_systemlink (0xD8ACE10) -> 1        Com_IsSystemLink() true

Consequences, each one already evidenced above rather than hoped for:
  - matchtype resolves to systemlink,
  - map and gametype are read from LOCAL dvars / gameTypesTable.csv, not a playlist,
  - the online-service gates short-circuit,
  - once we hold the host flag (obj+1598540), SystemLink_BroadcastServerInfo advertises
    the match, and other machines join it through UI_SetActiveMenu_SYSTEMLINKJOINGAME.

## Ã¢Å¡Â  THE HONEST LIMITATION Ã¢â‚¬â€ SYSTEM LINK IS LAN

`SystemLink_BroadcastServerInfo` broadcasts to the local network. Players on the open
internet will NOT see it without a virtual-LAN layer (ZeroTier / Radmin / Hamachi),
which is exactly how the MW3 and BO2 system-link server communities operate. Within
that constraint this IS a fully controllable peer-to-peer server on our own exe, with
no Demonware brokering.

Whether S2's public matchmaking can be pointed at a client-hosted server INSTEAD is a
separate question and is still UNPROVEN. The relevant field is
`matchmaking_allowJoiningListenServer` (params[15]) Ã¢â‚¬â€ shipped small playlists set it 1,
the large public ones set it 0 Ã¢â‚¬â€ but nothing yet shows the matchmaker will route
strangers to us rather than merely permit a listen server in principle.

## CORRECTIONS to the GRIIMS-WWII-Tool offsets

Its `s2offsets.hpp` FUNCTION addresses come from a different dump and do NOT transfer:

    claimed SV_SpawnServer 0x745050  -> in OUR IDB that is a UI element draw dispatcher
                                        (switch on element ids, gametype names, images)
    claimed StartServer    0x7B2AA0  -> no match
    claimed PartyHost_StartMatch 0x307620 -> no match

Its DATA offsets marked "same rva" do line up. Its ForceHost() is three data pokes
(oDisableJoining=0, five maxplayers bytes, minplayers) which make you the LOBBY host
only Ã¢â‚¬â€ it never touches the session kind, which is why it could not fully control the
spawned match.

## Named in the S2 IDB (saved)

    0x856750  Com_IsSystemLink            0x856770  Com_IsSystemLink_2
    0x856280  Com_IsOnlineGame            0x857B90  Com_IsPublicOnlineMatch
    0x479DD0  SystemLink_BroadcastServerInfo   (descriptive)
    0xD8ACE10 dvar_systemlink   (data)    0x1BD3750 dvar_online   (data)
    0xF923F8  s_matchtypeNames  (data)    0xF924A0  g_sessionParamTable (commented)

Deliberately NOT named: `sub_6DDB00` (the send), `obj+1598540` / `+1598460` (host flag
and session type Ã¢â‚¬â€ read by several sites but no writer located, so ownership is

# Ã¢Â­ÂÃ¢Â­ÂÃ¢Â­ÂÃ¢Â­Â FORCE HOSTING ON THE INTERNET Ã¢â‚¬â€ THE FULL CHAIN, FOUND (2026-08-09, offline)

The previous section found System Link (LAN). This one finds the **public matchmaking**
route: how a client-hosted (listen) server is qualified, assigned and ADVERTISED to
strangers. It is all engine code plus one GSC-visible parameter.

## Ã¢Â­Â THE SCRIPT BINDING TABLE Ã¢â‚¬â€ the whole force-host surface

`{const char* name, void* func}` pairs, stride 16, at **0xB50C60** (~60 entries):

    IsJoinComplete 296C10        StartServerGame 296EC0     StartClientGame 296F50
    IsServerGameStarted 296FC0   AssignServer 297170        ClearServer 297240
    AdvertiseServer 2972B0       IsSessionInitialized 2974E0
    IsLobbyMigrationActive 2976A0  IsHostMigrationActive 297740
    IsReadyToLaunch 2977E0       IsGameStartReady 297880    IsMinPlayersReady 2979C0
    IsServerAssigned 297B00      IsServerAdvertised 297CE0  IsServerDedicated 297BA0
    IsServerListen 297C40        AreWeHost 297D80           MigrateBeforeSearch 297E10
    ResetServerAcquire 2981C0    CanStartAcquiringDSNow 298230  StartServerAcquire 2982C0
    GetDataCenterId 298520       IsHostingBanned 298B10     IsHostingEnabled 298B50
    GetNatType 298B90            CanHostServer 298BE0       IsPlaylistAlwaysSearch 298CC0
    RequiresOpenNAT 298D90       IsServerAdvertiseEnabled 298E30
    AllowGameBattlesListenServers 299120   IsRestrictedToListenServers 2991C0

This is the API the lobby GSC drives. Everything below hangs off it.

## Ã¢Â­ÂÃ¢Â­Â PROVEN Ã¢â‚¬â€ params[15] IS the advertise switch, and the offsets are PROVEN not guessed

    Script_IsServerAdvertiseEnabled @0x298E30   (GSC "IsServerAdvertiseEnabled")
        = (GetMatchmakingSpace(lobby) != 2)
          || LobbyParams_GetAllowJoiningListenServer(Lobby_GetParams(lobby))

    LobbyParams_GetAllowJoiningListenServer @0x1970C0  = *(int*)(rawObj + 0x28C)

Why that offset is PROVEN. `Party_SetLobbyParamFromCmd` resolves
`v2 = sub_470F20(...) + 592` and writes `v2[15]` for
`matchmaking_allowJoiningListenServer`, so params[15] = 0x250 + 15*4 = **0x28C**.
Cross-checked by the SIBLING, independently: GSC **"RequiresOpenNAT"** @0x298D90 reads
`LobbyParams_GetRequireOpenNat` @0x197190 = `rawObj + 0x284` = params[13] =
**requireOpenNat**. Two independently-NAMED script functions landing on two
independently-NAMED param fields. This is not offset inference.

`sub_1970C0` has exactly ONE reader: Script_IsServerAdvertiseEnabled.

## Ã¢Â­Â THE SHIPPED PLAYLIST RULES, VERBATIM Ã¢â‚¬â€ this is the whole reason it never worked

    0xABF5560 (public, 466 B):  ... rankedMatch 0; matchmaking_allowJoiningListenServer 0; ...
    0xABF60F6 (public):  party_maxplayers 32; ... matchmaking_allowJoiningListenServer 0;
    0xABF62B0 (small)  :  party_maxplayers 4;  ... 1936 1; matchmaking_allowJoiningListenServer 1;

Public playlists ship the switch OFF. In matchmaking space 2 that makes
IsServerAdvertiseEnabled false, so a client-hosted server is never published and
strangers can never be routed to it. The 4-player playlists ship it ON Ã¢â‚¬â€ which is why
listen servers demonstrably work in this engine, just not for public playlists.

## Ã¢Â­ÂÃ¢Â­Â THE HOST GATE Ã¢â‚¬â€ Session_CanHostServer @0x8534B0

Reached from GSC `CanHostServer` @0x298BE0, called as
`Session_CanHostServer(Lobby_GetParams(lobby), maxplayers)`:

    if (dvar_systemlink && dvar_systemlink[16]) return 1;   // SYSTEM LINK ALWAYS HOSTS
    if (!g_hostingEnabled) return 0;
    if (LobbyParams_GetRequireOpenNat(p) && natType == 3) return 0;   // strict NAT
    if (!bandwidthTestReady(unk_10DC800)) { g_hostingEnabled = 0; return 0; }
    if (!isPrivate(p) && !off_1BD3708[16]) {          // <- PRIVATE SKIPS QUALIFICATION
        if (sub_663B40(maxplayers) > sub_789860()) return 0;   // required upload > measured
        if (sub_663BA0(maxplayers) > sub_7890B0()) return 0;   // required ping > measured
    }
    return 1;

So a public match must additionally pass a NAT test and an upload/ping qualification
scaled by player count, while a private match and a system-link match skip it entirely.

## Ã¢Â­Â g_hostingEnabled @ IDA 0xF9E9D8 Ã¢â‚¬â€ enabled by default, LATCHED OFF, never restored

    static image value = 1                       (hosting is enabled by default)
    Session_IsHostingEnabled  @0x856F80  = g_hostingEnabled          (GSC IsHostingEnabled)
    Session_ClearHostingEnabled @0x857A80: `if (g_hostingEnabled) g_hostingEnabled = a1;`
        -- ONE-WAY. It can only ever CLEAR. There is no path that sets it back to 1.
    sub_853400 and Session_CanHostServer both clear it when the bandwidth-test object
    unk_10DC800 is not ready.

That asymmetry matters: once anything decides we are not host-worthy, hosting stays
off for the rest of the process. Re-asserting the byte is a legitimate repair of a
latch, not a fabricated capability Ã¢â‚¬â€ the default IS 1.

## THE COMPLETE RECIPE, and which lever serves which goal

    LAN / private / full control, no Demonware:
        dvar_online     0x1BD3750 -> 0
        dvar_systemlink 0xD8ACE10 -> 1
        Session_CanHostServer then returns 1 unconditionally, map+gametype come from
        local dvars, and SystemLink_BroadcastServerInfo advertises to the subnet.

    PUBLIC matchmaking, strangers routed to us:
        1. g_hostingEnabled (0xF9E9D8) = 1        -- re-assert if the latch cleared it
        2. matchmaking_allowJoiningListenServer = 1  -- params[15], set AFTER the playlist
                                                       applies, because the playlist sets 0
        3. optionally params[10] (the private flag, setter sub_1973F0 / getter sub_197140)
           to bypass the upload/ping qualification
        Then GSC's CanHostServer -> AssignServer -> AdvertiseServer runs and
        IsServerAdvertised becomes true.

**Step 2 needs no hook.** `Cmd_ExecuteString` @0x740280 calls
`Party_SetLobbyParamFromCmd(0)` for EVERY console command before anything else, so
typing

    matchmaking_allowJoiningListenServer 1

at the console writes params[15] on the live lobby object. That is the engine's own
command surface Ã¢â‚¬â€ the same one the playlist blobs use. ORDER IS THE WHOLE PROBLEM:
the playlist applies its rules when the playlist loads, so the value must be re-asserted
after that, not before.

## STILL UNPROVEN Ã¢â‚¬â€ state it before anyone builds on it

  - Nothing here shows the SERVER SIDE (Demonware) will honour an advertised client
    host for a public playlist. The client-side gate is now fully mapped and openable;
    whether the service accepts the advertisement is not visible from the binary and
    can only be settled by trying it.
  - `GetMatchmakingSpace(lobby) == 2` is assumed to be the public space because that is
    the case the param guards. The space enum itself has not been decoded.
  - `sub_828170` (the actual advertise send) is not decompiled.
  - `unk_10DC800` (the bandwidth-test object) and `off_1BD3708` are unidentified; both
    gate the qualification path.

## Named in the S2 IDB (saved)

    0x298B10 Script_IsHostingBanned        0x298E30 Script_IsServerAdvertiseEnabled
    0x298D90 Script_RequiresOpenNAT        0x2972B0 Script_AdvertiseServer

# FORCE HOST + KICK/BAN TOOL Ã¢â‚¬â€ SHIPPED, NOT YET TESTED (build 28FD9A93)

New module `src/host/force_host.{hpp,cpp}`, plus GUI tabs in demo_gui.cpp.
Per the Fix Declaration Rules this is a CANDIDATE: it builds, deploys and is
hash-verified, but it has NOT been run in game.

## PROVEN Ã¢â‚¬â€ the kick path

    SV_KickClient   sub_6D6CC0  IDA 0x6D6CC0     (GSC "kick" -> sub_5A1FF0 calls it)
    SV_DropClient   sub_F4030   IDA 0xF4030      ("disconnect %s", EXE_LEFTGAME)

    void SV_KickClient(char clientNum, const char* reason)
        if (!com_sv_running[16]) return;                  // must BE the server
        client = qword_C5FBA58 + 1173616 * clientNum;
        if (!client[0]) return;                           // slot free
        if (client[12] == 2) "EXE_CANNOTKICKHOSTPLAYER"   // +48 == loopback == host
        else SV_DropClient(client, reason, 1);

Server client array, cross-checked two ways (SV_KickClient indexes bytes,
sub_F30D0 indexes `(int*)base + 293404*i`, and 293404*4 == 1173616 exactly):

    qword_C5FBA58  svs.clients base      dword_C5FBA50  maxclients
    client +0        state (0 free, 1 zombie, >=5 in game)
    client +48       netadr type; == 2 -> loopback -> the host, cannot be kicked
    client +269816   name, 48 bytes      [dword idx 67454, from SV_DropClient]
    client +270680   isBot               [dword idx 67670, from sub_F30D0]

The name offset comes from ONE decompile, so read_name() rejects anything that
is not printable ASCII and the GUI shows "(slot N)" instead. A wrong offset must
look wrong, not convincing.

## What the module does

  * reads the session kind (online / systemlink / com_sv_running / g_hostingEnabled)
  * reads the lobby params struct and shows map, gametype, player counts,
    private, ranked, requireOpenNat and allowJoiningListenServer
  * re-asserts g_hostingEnabled and allowJoiningListenServer on a 4 Hz latch
  * lists server clients, kicks by slot, and keeps a persistent name ban list

Console commands (all run on the client thread):

    fh_status                fh_kick <slot> [reason]
    fh_ban <name>            fh_unban <name>
    fh_systemlink <0|1>      fh_online <0|1>
    fh_hosting <0|1>         fh_allowlisten <0|1>

## Two design points that matter

**Everything that WRITES goes through a console command.** The GUI runs on the
DXGI Present thread; kicking touches server state. The GUI therefore queues
`fh_kick N` via Cbuf and the engine runs it on the client thread when the buffer
drains Ã¢â‚¬â€ the same pattern demo_gui already uses for seeking.

**`online` must NOT be written directly.** Com_IsOnlineGame reads it through the
OBFUSCATED getter sub_AF180, so the mod's GameUtil::decodeDvarSecureBool /
setDvarSecureBool are used. `systemlink` IS a plain byte at dvar+16, because
Com_IsSystemLink does a raw load. Getting these the wrong way round would write
a value the engine decodes as garbage.

## Two defects found in review and fixed before shipping

  1. `enforce_bans` ran every frame: it would re-queue fh_kick hundreds of times
     per second while a kicked client sat in ZOMBIE, flooding the command buffer.
     Now a 1 s scan plus a 3 s per-slot cooldown.
  2. Both `enforce_bans` and the re-assert ran at frame rate; players() issues
     two VirtualQuery calls per occupied slot and params_ptr() can fall through
     to two engine accessor calls. Re-assert is now 4 Hz.

## HONEST LIMITS Ã¢â‚¬â€ say these before anyone relies on them

  * A NAME ban is evaded by changing name. It is not an account or hardware ban
    and the UI says so. The engine's own addip/removeip is gated on an unproven
    server-mode enum (sub_6D9A00 requires dword_BC50B10 == 2), so it was not used.
  * Kicking only works while com_sv_running. If the match is not on our exe the
    list is empty and kick is a no-op Ã¢â‚¬â€ which is exactly why kick is the right
    proof that force hosting worked.
  * The params struct string fields (+0x18 mapname, +0x20 gametype) are read as
    interned pointers. That is inferred from sub_688B70's use, not proven; the
    reads are guarded and show "?" on failure.
  * Whether Demonware honours an advertised client host for a public playlist is
    still unproven and is what the live test decides.

## THE TEST

  1. Boot, open the GUI (F9 / Insert) -> "Host" tab. Read the status line.
  2. Tick "Force hosting enabled", "Force allowJoiningListenServer",
     "Auto re-assert every frame". The re-assert is REQUIRED Ã¢â‚¬â€ the playlist
     writes allowJoiningListenServer when it loads.
  3. Start a public match. Watch the status line and `fh_status`.
  4. "Players" tab: if the client list is populated and Kick works, the match is
     running on our exe. That is the proof.

# FORCE HOST Ã¢â‚¬â€ THE ADVERTISE CHAIN, RECOVERED OFFLINE (2026-08-09)

Measured first, then read. The autotest report from a live run said:

    1 search results seen : YES (48 refused)   2 com_sv_running : YES
    3 real map hosted     : YES  mp_sandbox_01 4 remote player  : no (peak 1 client, 0 remote)
    online=0 systemlink=0 hostingEnabled=1 blockJoin=1 allowJoinListenServer=1

**We DID host a real map, with one client: us.** Hosting was never the gap. The gap is
being ADVERTISED so anyone can find the session.

## Ã¢â€ºâ€ CORRECTION Ã¢â‚¬â€ the join gate is NOT "the mechanism"

Earlier this session I called the `sub_29BFF0` search-result refusal "what stops you
joining other people's lobbies". Measured with CE while the user sat in a stranger's
match, every result being refused:

    connstate = 10 (CA_ACTIVE)   com_sv_running = 0   maxclients = 0

i.e. a CLIENT in someone else's game. So refusing search results is NECESSARY BUT NOT
SUFFICIENT Ã¢â‚¬â€ matchmaking also reaches us through GSC's AssignServer:

    Script_AssignServer 0x297170 -> sub_29A620(lobby, serverId, flag)
        params = *(QWORD*)(lobby + 31552)
        sub_700850(*params, (u16)serverId)          <- sets which server the lobby uses
        sub_828170(*params, lobby+31560, flag)
    other callers of sub_29A620: sub_1FBF10, sub_476D70

DO NOT blind-block sub_29A620: hosting almost certainly assigns through it too, with
our own id. Diagnostic logging is shipped instead (fh_blockassign is default OFF).

## Ã¢Â­Â PROVEN Ã¢â‚¬â€ the advertise chain, end to end, all static

    Script_IsServerAdvertised 0x297CE0 -> sub_4816A0(params)
    sub_4816A0(p) = sub_4810F0(p) && sub_827760(*p)
    sub_827760(a1) = *(u8*)(a1 + 122)        <- THE ADVERTISED FLAG
    sub_828170(p, _, flag): if (flag != p[122]) { p[122] = flag; sub_7009A0(); }

So `params + 122` is the advertised flag, written by sub_828170 and read by sub_827760.
Both ends identified; the loop is closed.

`sub_7009A0` is the publish: gated on `sub_827710(obj) = *(QWORD*)(obj+32) != 0`, then
sets obj[400]=state, obj[401]=1 dirty, and when turning ON calls sub_828890.

### The eligibility test Ã¢â‚¬â€ sub_4810F0

    v2 = *(DWORD*)(obj + 1598460) <= 2;      // session type
    v3 = LobbyParams[10] == 1;               // PRIVATE match  (sub_197150)
    v5 = Com_IsSystemLink();
    v6 = sub_8565F0();                       // dvar @ 0x1BD3758, sibling of dvar_online
    v7 = Com_IsOnlineGame();
    v8 = sub_28D8A0(*(uint*)(obj + 1639776));
    v9 = v2 && (!v3 || v8) && !v5 && (!v6 || v7);
    if (sub_BA660() && sessionType == 2) return 0;

**TWO HARD REQUIREMENTS: `!systemlink` AND (when v6) `online`.**

Consequence worth stating plainly: **SYSTEM LINK AND PUBLIC ADVERTISING ARE MUTUALLY
EXCLUSIVE.** `!v5` is explicit. There is no combined route where a system-link host is
also advertised to matchmaking Ã¢â‚¬â€ stop looking for one.

## Ã¢Â­Â PROVEN Ã¢â‚¬â€ what turns `online` off: THE HUB

    Com_SetOnlineGame 0x857AD0 = Dvar_SetBool(dvar_online, a1)   (18+ callers)

sub_9CDA0 (the hub loader) @0x9CF35:

    cmp [off_87F4AA8+16], 0 -> jz skip
    cmp [off_14DBDE0+16], 0 -> jz skip
    cmp byte_1BD36FA, 0     -> jz skip
    test al,al (Com_IsSystemLink) -> jnz skip
    byte_14DB5DB = 1; Com_SetOnlineGame(0); sub_857AF0(1)

So RETURNING TO THE HUB SETS online = 0. The `online=0` in the autotest report is
AFTERMATH (RULE A8) Ã¢â‚¬â€ the match had already ended Ã¢â‚¬â€ not proof that online was 0 during
the match.

Ã¢Å¡Â  AND THEREFORE: **do not force `online`.** It is engine-managed session state with 18+
writers, gating far more than advertising. An earlier build of the autotest forced it
to 1; that was wrong (it is exactly the "manufacture missing state" the doctrine
forbids) and has been reverted to a report-only note. `systemlink` IS ours to set and
is still asserted off.

## Ã¢â€ºâ€ DEAD END Ã¢â‚¬â€ the matchmaking space cannot be decoded statically

    sub_29AD30 = (Script_CallByName_ExpectInt(lobbyIdx, "GetMatchmakingSpace") == 2)

`Script_CallByName_ExpectInt` @0x2A5860 is NOT a data lookup: it drives the script VM at
qword_1BD3D08, pushes the arg, calls a script function BY NAME and pops an int
("Expecting an integer on top of the stack after calling '%s'").

**The matchmaking space is decided by SCRIPT.** So `Script_IsServerAdvertiseEnabled`'s
`(space != 2) || allowJoiningListenServer` cannot be resolved from the binary at all.
Do not go looking for a space enum Ã¢â‚¬â€ there isn't one to find. It needs either runtime,
or the LUI/GSC scripts unpacked from the fastfiles.

Related: matchmaking logic lives in LUI Lua (`ui/utility/mp/mpmatchmaking.lua`,
`mpmatchmakingresults.lua` appear in the LUI error log), not GSC Ã¢â‚¬â€ so deps/gsc-tool
does not reach it. Extracting LUI needs a zone unpacker.

## Named this session

    0x857AD0  Com_SetOnlineGame              (commented: hub sets it to 0)
    0x2A5860  Script_CallByName_ExpectInt    (commented: kills the space-enum hunt)

Deliberately NOT named: sub_8565F0 (reads the dvar at 0x1BD3758, sibling of
dvar_online, purpose unknown), sub_28D8A0, sub_827710, sub_4810F0, sub_4816A0 Ã¢â‚¬â€ all
understood in terms of their inputs but not confidently nameable.

## Where this leaves it

Client-side, the gates we can prove are open or openable:
  hosting works (fact 3 measured), allowJoiningListenServer forced 1, systemlink off,
  join blocking live.
Unresolved, and NOT resolvable offline:
  whether GSC calls AdvertiseServer for us Ã¢â‚¬â€ gated on a script-decided matchmaking
  space. The `ADVERTISE #n` hook shipped in build B78114E8 answers it in one run.


## PRIVATE MATCHES CAN BE ADVERTISED â€” one dword (2026-08-09, offline)

sub_4810F0's private term is `(!v3 || v8)` where v3 = "this is a private match"
(LobbyParams[10] == 1, via sub_197150) and

    v8 = sub_28D8A0(*(DWORD*)(obj + 1639776))
    sub_28D8A0(a1) = (a1 != 0)                 <- a trivial non-zero test
    sub_480E90(obj) = sub_28D8A0(*(DWORD*)(obj + 1639776))   <- the accessor

So **a PRIVATE match is advertisable whenever `*(DWORD*)(obj + 1639776)` is non-zero.**
Same object as the session type (+1598460), host flag (+1598540), dedicated (+1598544).

Corroborating use, sub_47F6E0:
    return !obj[1598460] && (off_87F4AA8[16] || obj[1639776] != 0);
i.e. the field is an ALTERNATIVE to the dvar at off_87F4AA8 (the same dvar sub_9CDA0's
hub ladder tests). Reads like an invite/joinable capability, but NOT PROVEN â€” no writer
located, so do not name it and do not poke it blind.

## â›” WHAT IS NOT ACHIEVABLE CLIENT-SIDE â€” say this before anyone builds on it

"Make every playlist combine so everyone searching finds MY match" CANNOT be done from
this machine. Matchmaking is SERVICE-BROKERED: other players' clients send their own
searches, with their own playlist ids, to Demonware, and Demonware decides. Nothing
local changes another client's query or the service's matching.

What IS in local reach is only:
  (a) what WE search for      -- our own filters/results (the join gate, the counts)
  (b) what WE advertise       -- our own session's properties (playlist id, params)

So the achievable approximation is the GRIIMS tool's own trick: advertise under a
DIFFERENT, busier playlist than the one actually being run ("change to the spoofed
playlist when the match is about to begin, then back when it has started"). That does
not combine playlists; it moves us into the biggest existing pool.

## âš  PING: the MW2 spoof does not transfer, and the direction is why

On MW2 a client could spoof the ping it REPORTED about itself. Here the ping fields in
the search-result records (sub_2A1820's telemetry names them: ping_ours, ping_average,
ping_median, ping_aggregate, ping_lobby, rating_ping) are on the SEARCHER's side --
they are what WE measured about THEM. Other players QoS-probe our host directly.

Therefore:
  * making US ignore ping (accept any lobby regardless) IS locally achievable;
  * making OTHERS ignore OUR ping is NOT, unless a ping value we self-report is found
    in the advertised session properties. Not located; unproven either way.

## â­ S2's ihping/ihpong EQUIVALENT â€” `doqos` / `qosres` (2026-08-09)

USER KNOWLEDGE (MW2/IW4): clients send `ihping`, the host replies `ihpong`, the client
times the round trip. Editing the HOST's reply made that server the preferred one.

S2 has the same shape. Party/lobby OOB message names (the `%i` prefix is the message
version field), found in the OOB string region alongside pa_joinrequest / kickedFromParty:

    0xB72F28  'doqos'        the PROBE request        0xB74040  '%idoqos'
    0xB72F30  'stopqos'                               0xB74058  '%istopqos'
    0xB730C8  '%iqosres'     the RESPONSE  <-- ours   0xB73F50  'qosres'

So a searcher probes with `doqos` and WE reply `qosres`; they time it. That is host-side,
which CORRECTS the earlier note in this file saying ping is "measured, therefore not
locally influenceable". Measured, yes -- but WE are the thing being measured, so the
reply is ours to control. The MW2 technique ports in principle.

Supporting: search-result records carry ping_average/median/aggregate/ours/lobby and a
`qos_error_code` (sub_2A1820's telemetry), and the lobby config has qos_min_received,
qos_max_unresponsive, qos_match_time -- i.e. a real probe protocol with tunables.

### NOT YET LOCATED â€” the qosres sender

None of these strings has a code xref (computed/Arxan, as with every other string in
this binary). The handler that compares incoming OOB names and builds the reply has not
been found statically.

RUNTIME IS THE EFFICIENT ROUTE HERE, and it is cheap:
  * the string ADDRESSES are known, so with the game running, break on / search for the
    code that loads 0xB730C8 or 0xB73F50 (VA = module_base + those), or
  * breakpoint the OOB dispatcher and send a probe.
This is one of the rare cases where static analysis is genuinely exhausted first --
per the Cheat Engine Rule, use a DIRECT address, never an unscoped scan.

### âš  Scope reminder before anyone builds on this

Winning the ping comparison only matters for candidates the SERVICE already returned to
a searcher. It does not make other players search our playlist, and it does not bypass
the advertise gate (sub_4810F0). Order of work is: be advertisable -> be returned as a
candidate -> then win the QoS comparison. Doing the third first changes nothing.

## â­â­â­ THE HOST FLAG AND ITS WRITER â€” PROVEN (2026-08-10)

    Script_AreWeHost @0x297D80 = *(DWORD*)(Lobby_GetParams(lobby) + 1598540) != 0

PROVEN BY NAME, not inference: the GSC binding is literally "AreWeHost" and it reads
that field and nothing else. So **obj + 1598540 IS "are we the host"**, and it is the
same field the [host] ADVERTISABLE probe has been printing as `host=` all along.
Sibling: obj + 1598544 is the dedicated flag (Script_IsServerDedicated).
Also: Script_IsServerListen @0x297C40 = sub_481750(params) != 0.

### The writer

Exactly THREE instructions touch +1598540 (0x18644C) in 0x400000-0x520000:

    0x478046  sub_478030   mov [rcx+18644Ch], edi        computed value
    0x484870  sub_4843C0   mov qword [rdi+18644Ch], 0    clear
    0x490F3F  sub_490E70   mov dword [rbx+18644Ch], 1    <-- BECOMES HOST

~80 other sites are `cmp [X+18644Ch], 0` -- the whole session layer constantly asks
"are we host?", including SystemLink_BroadcastServerInfo @0x479E32.

`sub_490E70` is a BECOME-HOST / session-init routine. It sets both flags
UNCONDITIONALLY (no guard):

    *((DWORD*)a1 + 399635) = 1;    // 399635*4 = 1598540  AreWeHost
    *((DWORD*)a1 + 399636) = 1;    // 399636*4 = 1598544  dedicated

and additionally calls sub_4810F0 (advertise eligibility) -> sub_700950 when eligible,
clears the client arrays at qword_90B8BC8 / qword_90B8BD0, and calls sub_485090.

Callers: **sub_473BE0** (0x473D11) and **sub_491DE0** (0x4924A9), plus data references
at 0xCF0ADC and 0xCF0B10 (adjacent -- looks like a state-machine/dispatch table, so
becoming host may be a session state transition).

NEXT: read sub_473BE0 / sub_491DE0 for the conditions that reach sub_490E70. That is
the LEGITIMATE become-host path -- preferable to forcing the byte, because it gives the
engine's own preconditions.

## âš  THREE HEX-CONVERSION ERRORS IN ONE SESSION â€” RULE A1 IS NOT OPTIONAL

All three were "did the hex in my head", all three produced confident but wrong
conclusions:

  1. 1598460 -> wrote 0x1863BC, correct is 0x1863FC. Made me declare the lobby-params
     object "the wrong base" when it was right.
  2. 1639776 -> wrote 0x190CE0, correct is 0x190560. Every CE read of privateEscape was
     meaningless, and a stray 1 was written ~1.1 KB past the field into the next slot.
  3. 1598540 -> searched 0x18640C, correct is 0x18644C. Reported sub_4A18A0 as the
     AreWeHost writer; it writes a DIFFERENT field (1598476).

The fix that worked: make the SCRIPT compute the hex (`'%X' % OFF`) and never type a
converted constant. Do that from now on.

## WHAT THIS MAKES ACTIONABLE, in order of confidence

  1. Advertising an EXISTING session. Call sub_29B510(*(QWORD*)(lobbyObj+16), client)
     directly. That is exactly what sub_80290 does after hosting, it is the body of a

     misses it because the publish is edge-triggered at creation.
  2. The force-closed dvar at 0x1BD3768. If it is non-zero when the session is created,
     R+136 gets bits 7,8,9,10 and GetRealPartyPrivacyOption reads 3 (closed).
     Read it live first; do not write it blind.
  3. R+136 directly. Clearing bits 8 and 9 on the live raw session object moves

  4. Playlist flags bit0/bit7 Ã¢â‚¬â€ only ranked sets them, so for normal playlists there is
     nothing to clear. Do not spend time here.

## SHIPPED Ã¢â‚¬â€ build 1BF40782 (2026-08-10, deployed + hash-verified, NOT yet tested)

Per the Fix Declaration Rules this is a CANDIDATE, not "fixed": it builds, deploys and
is hash-verified, but it has not been run in game.

### The button

GUI -> Host tab -> "Advertise this session" -> **ADVERTISE MY SESSION NOW**.
Queues `fh_readvertise`, which calls Matchmaking_Start (IDA 0x29B510) on lobby slot 0's
matchmaking object -- the same call sub_80290 makes right after hosting, and the body of
the shipped LUI binding GameMatchmakingStart. Console command `fh_readvertise [slot]`.

Safety, in order:
  * queued as a console command so it runs on the CLIENT thread, not the DXGI Present
    thread (same pattern as fh_kick).
  * every pointer step validated with VirtualQuery before dereference (RULE A6).
  * M is only accepted when `*(QWORD*)(M + 31552) == L` -- a free consistency check that
    catches a wrong base outright. If it fails we refuse to call rather than guess.
  * the signature is transcribed verbatim: `__int64 __fastcall(__int64, unsigned int)`.
    RULE A17 -- no widening or narrowing.
  * it reports lobby/mm/raw/privacy/advertised/host BEFORE it calls, so a run that
    changes nothing is still diagnostic (RULE A15).

### The readout (Host tab)

    lobby 0        : host=  sessionType=  privateEscape=      (L+1598540 / +1598460 / +1639776)
    advertised flag: 0 or 1                                    (R+122)
    privacy        : 0 OPEN .. 3 CLOSED, visibility=0x...      (R+136, slot 2 = what
                                                                GetRealPartyPrivacyOption reads)
    force-closed sw: the bool dvar at IDA 0x1BD3768            (read-only)

### Ã¢Â­Â A REAL BUG FIXED ON THE WAY Ã¢â‚¬â€ the republish walk used the wrong base

`tick()`'s forced re-publish walked

    L -> *(L + 31552) -> deref -> +122

but **+31552 is a field on the MATCHMAKING object M, not on the lobby L**. It could never
reach the advertised flag from there. sub_4816A0 is `sub_4810F0(p) && sub_827760(*p)`, and
sub_491DE0 calls `sub_6FFEE0(*a1, ...)` with a1 = L -- so the raw session is simply `*L`,
ONE indirection. Corrected. This is why `fh_republish`'s counter never meant anything.

Root cause of the mistake: "Lobby_GetParams" (0x29A890) is `*(QWORD*)(a1 + 31552)` and the
name made it read as "lobby -> params". It is the reverse -- it takes the MATCHMAKING
object and returns the LOBBY. Do not trust that name.

### What to expect in game

  1. Host tab shows the session graph immediately (no match needed for the dvar line).
  2. In a private match, press the button. Console prints
     `[host] readvertise slot 0: lobby=... mm=... raw=... privacy=N (NAME) advertised=N host=N`
     then `[host] Matchmaking_Start(mm, 0) returned R (call #1)`.
  3. If `advertised` flips 0 -> 1, the client-side publish worked.
  4. Whether anyone actually arrives is the UNPROVEN half -- that is Demonware's call and
     no amount of client-side work settles it.

If the button is greyed out, the matchmaking object did not verify: either no lobby yet,
or the back-pointer check failed. It refuses rather than calling into a wrong pointer.

### Ã¢â€ºâ€ CORRECTION Ã¢â‚¬â€ "privacy != 0 means the session is closed" is WRONG

I coloured the GUI red on `privacy != 0` and told the user privacy 2 was a concern.
Both were wrong.

  * **GetRealPartyPrivacyOption (0x3355E0) has NO CODE CALLERS.** It is reachable only
    through the LUI binding table. It is a DISPLAY value for menus and gates nothing.
  * **sub_4810F0, the advertise-eligibility test, never reads R+136 at all.** It reads
    session type, the private flag, privateEscape, systemlink and online. So the privacy
    bits cannot block advertising, by construction.
  * The bit that actually matters is **BIT 8**:
        GameInvitationsEnabled  sub_33C1F0  (PROVEN BY NAME, LUI table 0xB5FE.. region)
            = *(DWORD*)(L + 1598544) != 0  &&  sub_827570(R) == 0     // dedicated && !bit8
        sub_8303D0 = lobby && ( !bit9 || !bit8 || (sub_480F00(lobby) && !private) )
            -> passes on !bit8 alone
        sub_82FF90 returns a 0..3 code; on bit9 it returns 3 when
           (sub_480F00 && !private), else 0.
  * Measured session has **bit 9 set, bit 8 CLEAR**, dedicated = 1
    -> GameInvitationsEnabled TRUE, sub_8303D0 passes. **Nothing is blocked.**

So bit 9 on its own (privacy enum 2) is harmless. The indicator now colours on bit 8 and
says "invites enabled / disabled" instead of parroting a menu-only enum.

Where bit 9 came from is still UNKNOWN and worth noting: none of sub_80290's paths
produce bit 9 alone (they set 0x780, 0x700 or 0x300, all of which include bit 8). So this
session was created by a path other than sub_80290, or bit 9 was set later by a writer we
have not located. Do not assume sub_80290 is the only session creator.

### Two self-inflicted problems fixed the same day

  1. **The republish latch became harmful the moment I fixed it.** It clears the
     advertised flag every 10 s so the next AdvertiseServer sees a transition -- a
     workaround from when we could not publish directly. It had never actually run
     (wrong base). Fixing the base made it start working, so it began undoing the very
     publish the button performs, ten seconds later, forever. NOW DEFAULT OFF; still
     available as `fh_republish 1`.
  2. **The GUI session readouts ran ~20 VirtualQuery calls per frame** (9 per
     session_view slot, x2 slots, plus the dvar) on the Present thread, to redraw state
     that changes once a minute. Now cached at 4 Hz.
     GENERAL RULE: anything the GUI reads out of engine memory must be cached. `readable()`
     is a VirtualQuery, i.e. a kernel transition, and the GUI runs per frame.

### NEW Ã¢â‚¬â€ "did anyone hear us?" peer tracker

`NET_GetPacket` @ IDA 0x7B0D00 is hooked (nothing else in src/ hooks it; RULE A3.1
checked). Behaviour-proven from its own body: two sockets at qword_D8B0540 /
qword_D8B0730, `recvfrom(sock, msg->data, msg->maxsize, 0, &sockaddr, &len)`, sockaddr ->
netadr via sub_75FA30 then `from->type = 3`, a 3-byte trailer (byteswapped u16 checksum +
a nibble pair) validated, `msg->cursize = len - 3`, returns 1 when a packet arrived.

    netadr_t: +0 dword type (3 = IP)   +4 four IPv4 bytes   +8 u16 port (network order)
    msg_t   : +8 data   +24 maxsize   +28 cursize      (matches the MSG_Init layout)

WHY the packet source and not the OOB dispatcher: the QoS strings 'doqos' (0xB72F28),
'stopqos' (0xB72F30), 'qosres' (0xB73F50) have NO code xrefs (computed/Arxan), so the
dispatcher cannot be reached statically. Hooking the packet source sidesteps that
entirely and sees every datagram whatever rides on top.

Records up to 64 endpoints: ip:port, packet/OOB counts, bytes, first/last seen, and the
first printable token after a 0xFFFFFFFF connectionless prefix. The signal that matters is
`after_advertise` -- an endpoint whose FIRST packet arrived after we published. Anything
already talking to us before that is the platform backend.

Hot-path discipline: fixed table, no allocation, no printf, no VirtualQuery, short
CRITICAL_SECTION; the GUI copies at 4 Hz rather than taking the network lock per frame.

Commands: `fh_peers`, `fh_peers clear`, `fh_peers 0|1`.

HONEST LIMIT: a new endpoint proves contact, not necessarily matchmaking -- NAT
punchthrough and the backend also produce new addresses. What makes it conclusive is the
command column reading `doqos`, because a QoS probe means we were returned as a candidate.

# Ã¢Â­ÂÃ¢Â­ÂÃ¢Â­Â THE SESSION PUBLISH PATH, RECOVERED (2026-08-10, offline, no game)

Worked out entirely from the IDB while the game was closed. Several of my own
earlier claims are CORRECTED here; read the corrections before the findings.

## Ã¢â€ºâ€ CORRECTION 1 Ã¢â‚¬â€ the 0x29Exxx-0x2A4xxx family is TELEMETRY, not the transport

I read `msgType=51, inProgress=1` in the request block and told the user a
matchmaking request was "built but stuck pending". That was WRONG.

What the family actually is:
  * `sub_2A4290` opens a DDL analytics record against **"mp/ddl/matchmaking.ddl"**
    and fills fields named `lobby_type`, `is_rollover`, `state_machine_records`,
    `exit_time_utc`.
  * `sub_2A5F90(client, idx, name)` logs events named `matchmaking_start`,
    `matchmaking_stop`, `matchmaking_lobbycreated`.
  * `sub_2A4010` flushes it with `sub_64EEC0(client, isIdx0, blk+5, 0x40000)`.
  * The flush is driven from **CL_ParseGamestate** (0x462DA7) and from
    `sub_2A4C30` (via Matchmaking_Stop) Ã¢â‚¬â€ i.e. at CONNECT or STOP time.

So "in progress" simply means an analytics record is open, which is NORMAL between
starting matchmaking and connecting. It is not a publish status and says nothing
about whether Demonware advertised us.

**The flag has exactly TWO writers in the whole image** (searched every `+40038h`
reference, 0x1F0000-0x2B0000):

    0x2A4397  sub_2A4290   mov byte ptr [rax+40038h], 1     SET
    0x2A4263  sub_2A4010   mov byte ptr [rax+40038h], 0     CLEAR (the only one)

**HARM I SHIPPED AND REVERTED:** build 5EE2E1B3 made the advertise button REFUSE
while that flag was set. Since the flag is telemetry, that skipped the REAL publish
(the five session-property setters that run before the telemetry call) to avoid a
harmless analytics no-op. Reverted in build 0E0988BC Ã¢â‚¬â€ report it, never gate on it.

## Ã¢Â­Â THE REAL PUBLISH CHAIN

    Script_AdvertiseServer -> sub_828170(R, client, 1)
        R[122] = 1                                   (the advertised flag)
        -> sub_7009A0(R, client, 1, n)
             P = sub_6FDE20(R)                       (session-properties object)
             P[400] = 1   (published state)
             P[401] = 1   (DIRTY)
             -> sub_828890(R, client)                (re-publish on slot change)

    and Matchmaking_Start's REAL work, before any telemetry, is the five
    property setters, each of which marks P[401] dirty:
        sub_700BE0 / sub_700AF0 / sub_700810 / sub_700A70 / sub_7007D0
        pattern: `if (sub_827710(R)) { P = sub_6FDE20(R); ...; P[401] = 1; }`

## Ã¢Â­ÂÃ¢Â­Â PROVEN Ã¢â‚¬â€ sub_827980 IS THE PUBLISH DECISION, AND IT IS CHANGE-DRIVEN

`sub_827980(R, maxSlots, privSlots, third, flags)`, verified in disassembly:

    return ((R[136] ^ flags) & 0xF40) != 0    // visibility bits 6,8,9,10,11 changed
        || R[124] != privSlots                 // private slots changed
        || R[128] != maxSlots                  // max slots changed
        || R[132] != third;

    0x827984 xor eax,[rcx+88h] / test eax,0F40h / cmp [rcx+7Ch],r8d
             / cmp [rcx+80h],edx / cmp [rcx+84h],r9d

Three of `sub_700320`'s five callers gate on it (sub_7F880, sub_476D70, sub_436C50).

**THE ENGINE ONLY TRANSMITS WHEN THE VISIBILITY BITS (mask 0xF40) OR THE SLOT
COUNTS ACTUALLY CHANGE.** Mask 0xF40 = bits 6,8,9,10,11 Ã¢â‚¬â€ exactly the privacy
group decoded earlier.

### Consequence: our old fh_republish was provably useless

It cleared **R+122**, and `sub_827980` does not read R+122 at all. It could never
have forced a re-publish, even after the wrong-base bug in its pointer walk was
fixed. Already default OFF; this is why it must stay off.

### The correct way to force a re-publish (NOT YET IMPLEMENTED)

Change something `sub_827980` actually watches Ã¢â‚¬â€ a masked visibility bit in R[136],
or a slot count Ã¢â‚¬â€ and let the engine's own path notice. Do NOT poke R+122.

## PROVEN Ã¢â‚¬â€ sub_828890 publishes iff R[124] != 0, and R[124] is PRIVATE SLOTS

Verified at instruction level (0x828B4D..0x828B68): the three-way condition
collapses algebraically to `R[124] != 0`, because `v2 == R[128]+R[124]` and
`result == R[132]` are both computed before a clearing loop that touches neither.

Field semantics, proven from the LUI binding table:

    GetMaxSlotsForLobby     0x33BA80 -> sub_197110(lobby) = *(lobby + 596) = params[1]
    GetPrivateSlotsForLobby 0x33B9F0 -> sub_197170(lobby) = *(lobby + 604) = params[3]
    setter for params[3]: sub_197420(lobby, n)      (params base = lobby + 592)

    R[124] = private slots      R[128] = max slots      R[136] = visibility bitfield

**`Party_SetLobbyParamFromCmd` handles params 0,1,2,4,6,13,15,17 Ã¢â‚¬â€ params[3] is NOT
settable by console command.** Only sub_197420 or a direct write reaches it.

And `sub_80290` explicitly zeroes it before creating a session:

    sub_197420(v2, 0);   // private slots = 0
    sub_197460(v2, 0);   // params[11] = 0
    sub_491DE0(v2, 0, client, flags, 0, maxplayers);

Ã¢Å¡Â  DO NOT over-read this. `sub_700320` has FIVE callers (sub_7F880, sub_436C50,
sub_476D70, sub_48AD10, sub_828890), so sub_828890 is the "slot counts changed ->
re-publish" path, NOT the only publisher. `R[124] != 0` gates that ONE path. I was
about to call it the blocker and the caller check stopped me.

## Ã¢Â­Â TWO SEPARATE UDP STACKS Ã¢â‚¬â€ and a third, TCP, for the service

`recvfrom` has exactly two callers, and they are different subsystems:

    NET_GetPacket 0x7B0D00  (0x7Bxxxx)   the GAME netchan
    sub_A7EB90    0xA7EB90  (0xA7xxxx)   the PLATFORM socket, via sub_A7B160
        __int64 sub_A7EB90(int sock, DWORD* outIp, u_short* outPort, char* buf, int len)
        returns length >= 0, or a negative error code; port is ALREADY ntohs'd
        counters: qword_10F5D648 (bytes + 28/pkt), qword_10F5D650 (packets)

Demonware's SERVICE connection is TCP: `recv`/`send` callers cluster in
0xAC7xxx / 0xA7Fxxx / 0x662510. So the advertisement goes to the broker over TCP,
and another player only sends us UDP when they actually probe or connect.

MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-10: `qword_10F5D650` = 37 packets, STATIC, 1659 bytes total
(~17 B each) across a whole session. So the platform UDP path is essentially idle
and **nobody has QoS-probed us**. That reading comes from the ENGINE's own counter,
not from our hook, so it does not depend on our instrumentation being right.

## Ã¢â€ºâ€ CORRECTION 2 Ã¢â‚¬â€ the first peer tracker watched the wrong pipe

Build 5EE2E1B3 hooked only NET_GetPacket. Matchmaking/QoS ride the platform stack,
and in a lobby the game netchan is largely idle, so the table came back empty and
LOOKED like "nobody contacted us". Both stacks are hooked from build 29A0B746; rows
are tagged `[plat]`. An empty table is only meaningful once the platform hook
reports OK.

## Ã¢â€ºâ€ CORRECTION 3 Ã¢â‚¬â€ "privacy != 0 means closed" (already recorded, restated)

GetRealPartyPrivacyOption has NO code callers; it is a LUI display value. The gate
that matters is BIT 8 (GameInvitationsEnabled = dedicated && !bit8). Measured
sessions had bit 9 set and bit 8 CLEAR -> nothing blocked.

## WHERE THIS LEAVES THE INVESTIGATION

Client side, everything we can see is healthy and PROVEN: AreWeHost=1, dedicated=1,
advertised (R+122)=1, invites enabled (bit8 clear), 18 slots, the publish chain runs
and the property setters mark P dirty.

What is NOT established, and is the only thing left:
  * whether the change-driven publish (sub_827980) ever saw a CHANGE worth
    transmitting for our session, or considered it already published;
  * whether Demonware returns a client-hosted session to other searchers at all.

The measured negative Ã¢â‚¬â€ platform UDP static at 37 packets while advertised=1 Ã¢â‚¬â€
is consistent with either. It is NOT consistent with "someone found us and chose
not to join", because that would still require a QoS probe.

## NEXT STEP, cheapest first

  1. Read R[124] / R[128] / R[132] / R[136] live at the moment of advertising, and
     again a minute later. If nothing in mask 0xF40 or the counts ever changes,
     sub_827980 returns false every time and the session is never re-transmitted.
  2. If so, the legitimate lever is to change a watched field (private slots via
     sub_197420, or a masked visibility bit) so the engine's own path publishes.
     Do NOT poke R+122 Ã¢â‚¬â€ sub_827980 does not read it.
  3. Only after that does it make sense to blame the service.

# RETRACTED - "a real player found our advertised lobby" (2026-08-10)

I recorded this as a MILESTONE and as settling whether Demonware honours an
advertised client host. **The user retracted it within the hour**: the addresses
seen were almost certainly Demonware's own, not a searcher's.

**So the standing caveat STANDS: it is still NOT established that the service ever
hands our session to another player.** Do not build on the retracted claim, and do
not repeat my mistake of promoting a single ambiguous observation to PROVEN on the
strength of one hopeful reading.

This is exactly why the peer table flags `after_advertise` AND surfaces the OOB
command token: the only unambiguous evidence is a **`doqos`** probe from an address
first seen after we published. Backend traffic and NAT punchthrough both produce
new addresses, and neither means we were found.

# Ã¢Â­ÂÃ¢Â­ÂÃ¢Â­Â DEDICATED vs LISTEN Ã¢â‚¬â€ ONE PREDICATE (2026-08-10, offline)

USER'S OWN HYPOTHESIS, and it was right: "when the game has enough players and the
match starts it will pick the dedicated server route and I won't be the host".

    sub_480D80 IsDedicated(L) = advertiseEligible(sub_4810F0)
                              && L[1598460] != 1            (session type)
                              && sub_1FD110(*(QWORD*)(L + 8))

    sub_481750 IsListen(L)    = L[1598544]
                              && ...same shape...
                              && !sub_1FD110(*(QWORD*)(L + 8))

    sub_1FD110(o) = (o[0] - 5) <= 2 && (int)o[3] >= 2

So `o` is the SERVER-ACQUIRE state object at L+8, and once the acquire completes
(state 5..7 with o[3] >= 2) IsDedicated flips true and IsServerListen flips false.
**That is the exact moment the match leaves our machine.**

Both predicates are exposed to LUI by name, which is what made them findable:
    Script_IsServerDedicated 0x297BA0 -> sub_481720 = L[1598544] && sub_480D80(L)
    Script_IsServerListen    0x297C40 -> sub_481750

GSC drives the acquire:
    CanStartAcquiringDSNow 0x298230 -> sub_6FC1E0 -> sub_207EE0(11, client)
    StartServerAcquire     0x2982C0 -> sub_1FED20 -> sub_1FEF50      (async)
    AssignServer           0x297170 -> sub_29A620 -> sub_700850(*params, serverId)

The `ASSIGN #1: serverId=124` line seen in earlier logs is that final step.

`sub_1FD110` (IDA 0x1FD110 - 0x1000 = 0x1FC110) is hooked and returns false while

Ã¢Å¡Â  HONEST BLAST RADIUS: sub_1FD110 has FIVE callers Ã¢â‚¬â€ sub_480D80, sub_481750,

# The playlist question, answered (2026-08-10)

MEASURED live in a private match: `params[11]` (playlist, lobby+636) = **0**,
`params[10]` (private) = 1, maxplayers = 18, private slots = 0.

force_host does NOT choose a playlist Ã¢â‚¬â€ `fh_playlist` defaults to -1 (not forcing)
and start_hosting() never touches it. Playlist 0 in a private match reads as
"no playlist": sub_80290 explicitly zeroes it via sub_197460(lobby, 0), and
sub_8274B0 only consults playlist flags when sub_853660() is true, which requires
`!private`. So in a private match the playlist is not even read.

Consequence: a private match with playlist 0 gives matchmaking nothing to match
against. A PUBLIC playlist is the better test bed; `fh_playlist <id>` is the
alternative if staying private.

# BULK NAMING VIA MW3 STRING ANCHORS — 128 FUNCTIONS NAMED (2026-08-10)

A repeatable, evidence-based method for naming S2 functions from the MW3 IDB at
scale. Use this again; it is far better than one-at-a-time twin diffing.

## The method

String literals survive across builds. So:

  1. In MW3, build {distinctive string -> the named function that references it},
     keeping ONLY strings referenced by exactly ONE named function.
     Result: 6,855 strings.
  2. In S2, read `.rdata` (0xB1B000-0xD90000, 2.5 MB) ONCE with ida_bytes.get_bytes
     and substring-search it in Python. Result: 1,022 of those strings also exist
     in S2.
     ⚠ Do NOT use idautils.Strings() / ida_strlist.build_strlist() on S2 — it
     triggers a full rebuild and TIMES OUT the MCP on this 300 MB image. Twice.
  3. For each shared string, take its S2 code xrefs. Keep only strings referenced
     by exactly ONE S2 function (unambiguous on both sides).
  4. Vote: an S2 function is a candidate only if every string backing it implies
     the SAME MW3 name.
  5. Reject:
       - S2 functions that already have a non-sub_ name
       - MW3 names claimed by more than one S2 function (12 dropped: CG_OwnerDraw,
         CG_RegisterSounds, CG_StartClientSideEffects, CL_ConnectionLessPacketCmd,
         Com_SetRecommended, R_Cinematic_BinkOpenPath, ...)
       - names that already exist elsewhere in the IDB (1 dropped: DB_LoadXAssets
         wanted 0xA58D0 but is already established at 0xA4F60)
  6. Apply, with a function comment recording the basis.

Confidence tiers actually applied:
    round 1: unique name AND >= 2 distinct shared strings          -> 71 named
    round 2: unique name, 1 string, but the anchor is >= 20 chars   -> 57 named

## Independent corroboration (why this is trustworthy)

Five results matched things CLAUDE.md had ALREADY established by other means,
without the method being told about them:

    0x747DF0  UI_SetActiveMenu       - already noted as issuing
                                       "UI_SetActiveMenu_SYSTEMLINKJOINGAME"
    0x93260   Com_InitDvars          - already documented as the dvar block
                                       containing gamePreventListenServer
    0x6DC350  SV_SpawnServer         - already known as a DB_LoadLevelXAssets caller
    0x49F1B0  Party_SetUIPlayerCount - already seen called from sub_491DE0
    0x6D6CC0  SV_KickClient          - already named by hand from its own body

## ⭐ Immediately useful: the engine's own map-change idiom

`UI_RunMenuScript` (0x74A440) formats **"wait ; wait ; map %s\n"** and appends it
to the command ring at off_AA764A8 (guarded by sub_7729B0(193)/sub_772A20(193)).

So the engine never issues a bare `map` — it prefixes two waits so the current
frame finishes first. `fh_changemap` now does the same (build F19E7841), which
also gives the asset release a frame to settle before the load begins.

## Left deliberately unnamed

157 single-string candidates with a short (<20 char) anchor were NOT applied — a
short shared string is weak evidence and the Function Naming Rule says an honest
sub_ beats a wrong name. They are recoverable by re-running the method.

The IDB was saved after applying (RULE A10).

# ⛔ cg_draw2D IS NOT A FIX FOR THE STRANDED DIVISION WIDGETS (2026-08-10)

I hid the stranded playback HUD widgets with cg_draw2D. **That was the lazy route and
it was wrong.** User: *"cg_draw2d disables all the hud, even hitmarkers and killfeed
and score popup."* Recorded so nobody reaches for it again.

## PROVEN — every reader of the cg_draw2D global

Registered `sub_B06A0("2562", 1, 4)` at 0x41D7C2 inside sub_41D690; global
**off_8B0DA20**. Three code references, and only two are real:

    CG_DrawActiveFrame @0x69CF8   NOT A READ. Arxan integrity noise — it uses
                                  off_8B0DA20+16 as an int inside XOR chains.
    sub_E7980 @0xE79D4            if (globals[5729] || !Dvar_GetBool(cg_draw2D))
                                      return;
                                  Gates a 0x108D-byte draw function: the whole
                                  native 2D HUD — hitmarkers, killfeed, score.
    sub_EB030 @0xEB04D            Same shape, gates a second 0x14E-byte drawer.

So it is two blanket gates over the native HUD. And the stranded widgets are **LUI**,
drawn by a different system entirely, so it very likely never removed them — it only
deleted the HUD that was working. Two failures in one change.

## The actual cause, from the console log

    ui/s2/mphud_uc.lua:35 -> equippedperks_uc.lua:10 -> :129 -> :80
      -> ui/utility/mp/divisions_utils.lua
    "Error while handling model subscription: Name unavailable in ship builds"

`sub_36A550` / `sub_36A790` are the LUI model-subscription dispatchers: they walk the
dirty flags at `byte_896D650[0..0x3E7F]` and call each subscriber through `sub_2E40A0`
(lua_pcall), reporting on failure. The divisions callback throws, the widget stops
mid-build, and whatever was already laid out stays on screen. The checkerboard is its
unresolved division icon — a missing-material placeholder, the same customization
family as the viewmodel bug.

## Routes checked and closed

  - **MW3's CL_Demo_CloseAllCgameOpenedMenus** is just `UI_CloseMenu(client,
    "endgameupdate")`. S2 has NO named UI_CloseMenu equivalent.
  - **The LUI element names are not in .rdata.** `mphud`, `equippedperks`, `perks_uc`
    live in fastfile Lua, so there is no native handle to close them by name.

## CANDIDATE (shipped opt-in, UNPROVEN) — divisionsGlobalOverhaul

`Perks_RegisterDvars` does `sub_B05E0("divisionsGlobalOverhaul", 1, 64)` — bool,
default 1, flags 0x40, global **off_8A99838**. It has exactly ONE reference in the
whole image: its own registration write. **Nothing native reads it**, so it is
consumed from Lua — by the very divisions code that throws. Turning it off should
send divisions_utils down its pre-overhaul path.

Shipped as an explicit checkbox (build E7E300B6), never automatic, because it is a
gameplay-data flag. It does NOT touch the HUD, so hitmarkers/killfeed/score are
unaffected either way.

## ⭐ PROVEN — S2 dvar FLAG CLASSES, by differential inside Com_InitDvars

Worth keeping: this is how to judge whether any S2 dvar is settable, without guessing
at a flag enum. Registrations in one function, so the comparison is free:

    0x400001   com_maxfps, win_useWmInput            user-settable + archived
    0x2000     com_sv_running, sv_paused, cl_paused  ENGINE-OWNED / read-only
               (also "1916", "4817", "1278", "5071", "4278", "5369")
    0x80       dvar_online ("2291"), "393", "932",   script / server-visible
               every scorestreak_enabled_*
    0x40       divisionsGlobalOverhaul,              live-service feature flags
               allow_hub_vendor_menu, "1789",
               "5674", "2917", "5887", "6027",
               "1258", "2196", and the perk
               dvars "6017".."6021"
    0x4        cg_draw2D "2562", cg_drawGun "1762", "299", "5049"
    0x1        "2464"                                archived
    0x10000    "1265"        0x2000|other for paused-family

**divisionsGlobalOverhaul is NOT in the read-only class.** It shares 0x40 with
`allow_hub_vendor_menu`, an obvious backend toggle. That makes it LIKELY settable
from the console — but likely is not measured, so `set_divisions_overhaul()` prints
the raw byte at `dvar+16` before each write. Toggle the checkbox twice: if the byte
never moves, the console cannot write this dvar and the approach is dead.

⚠ Do NOT read 0x40 as "ROM" from the Quake3 dvar enum. That enum does not apply here
— under it com_sv_running would not be 0x2000.

## LESSON

The instruction was *"I never want you to take a lazy route."* The failure mode here
was reaching for the first switch that made the symptom disappear without checking
what else it gated. Mapping the three xrefs took one decompile and would have
prevented the whole thing. **Before flipping an engine-wide switch, enumerate its
readers.**

# ⭐⭐ THE LUI HUD MODEL PUBLISHER — AND THE ONE MODEL BEHIND THE DIVISION WIDGETS
# (2026-08-10)

Two failed attempts preceded this (cg_draw2D, then divisionsGlobalOverhaul — the
latter tested in game and did nothing). Both were guesses at a lever. This is the
producer, found by tracing the consumer backwards.

## PROVEN — sub_357AD0 publishes the entire LUI HUD model set every frame

    sub_3573B0(client, descIndex, "cg.hud.<name>")     CG_PublishHudModel

~70 calls per frame from sub_357AD0, table-driven off the descriptor array
**off_F7D220** (32-byte stride). Per descriptor: `+12` type (0/1 int, 2 ptr,
3 string, 4 bool), `+17` array count, `[i+1]` value-source id, `[i+2]` scope,
`[i+3]` cache. The value comes from `sub_356560(client, sourceId, index, &out...)`
and is pushed with sub_36ABF0 / sub_36AC60 / sub_36ACE0 / sub_36AAF0.

The whole block is gated on `connstate >= 10` and on
`*(DWORD*)(LCG + 4704 * LCG[22904] + 3878296 + 4)`.

## ⭐ The id that matters

    sub_3573B0(client, 86, "cg.hud.currentDivision")    @ 0x35807A

`cg.hud.currentDivision` @ **0xB647C8** has exactly ONE code xref — that call site
— so the id is unambiguous. It is precisely the model the failing Lua subscribes to:

    ui/s2/mphud_uc.lua:35 -> equippedperks_uc.lua:10 -> :129 -> :80
      -> ui/utility/mp/divisions_utils.lua
    "Error while handling model subscription: Name unavailable in ship builds"

Neighbouring ids worth knowing: **49..57** are `cg.hud.currentWeapon.perks.perk*Index`
(also drawn by equippedperks_uc.lua), 84 killCounter, 85 clanTag, 83
weaponCustomization, 78 currentTeam, 79/80 the scores.

## Useful discovery — the LUI model namespace IS in .rdata

`cg.hud.*` / `cg.HUD.*` / `cg.Shared.*` model paths are plain strings in .rdata, so
the LUI model tree is reachable statically even though the Lua is inside fastfiles.
Method that found them: read .rdata (0xB1B000-0xD90000) once with
`ida_bytes.get_bytes` and substring-search in Python — NEVER `idautils.Strings()`,
which times out the MCP on this image.

`endgameupdate` (MW3's demo menu-close target) also exists, at 0xBCEAA8, sitting
inside the MENU_DEMO_* string block. Only a data xref at 0xFBF980. Not yet chased.

## CANDIDATE shipped — build 4919FDAF

Hook `CG_PublishHudModel` (IDA 0x3573B0 - 0x1000 = 0x3563B0; nothing else hooks it)
and withhold model 86 while `g_native_playing`. Early-outs on !g_native_playing
because it is HOT (~70 calls/frame), so live play pays only a trampoline.

Runtime-settable id list so ONE build can test several ids:
    demo_hud_suppress              report current list + how many were withheld
    demo_hud_suppress 86 49 50     suppress those ids
    demo_hud_suppress none         stock behaviour
    demo_hud_models                dump every id -> name the engine publishes

⚠ UNPROVEN that withholding clears the widget: suppressing a publish stops the model
CHANGING, so a widget already built from an earlier publish may persist. That is
exactly why the list is runtime-settable rather than baked in.

## ⭐ SPACEBAR — I broke it with a DOUBLE TOGGLE

Our CL_Demo_HandleAction hook passes every action through except the blocked one, so
during native playback the ENGINE still handles space itself (action 1/32 toggles
cl_demo_pause). The GUI hotkey then toggled it AGAIN in the same frame, and the two
cancelled — "space does nothing since it was added to the GUI", exactly as reported.

FIX: the engine owns space during native playback. We only handle it when the engine
cannot see the key, i.e. while our overlay holds key-catcher bit 0. The custom
theater has no engine-side binding, so `demopause` stays ours there.

GENERALISE: before binding a key the engine already binds, check whether the engine
still receives it. Two handlers on one toggle is a silent no-op, not a double action.


## ⭐ MINIMAL HUD — why "keep only hitmarkers/killfeed/score" needs the model split

Requested as one toggle. There is no single engine switch for it, because the three
keepers do NOT share a system. Established from MWR PS4 (the fully-named build):

    hitmarkers   NATIVE, in the crosshair path      MWR CG_DrawCrosshair @0x295180
    killfeed     LUI, EVENT-driven                  MWR LUI_Obituary     @0x1857E0
    score popup  LUI, EVENT-driven
    everything else on screen (ammo, division, perks, health, morale, combat roles,
    killCounter, clan tag, vehicle, netPerf)
                 LUI, MODEL-driven via sub_3573B0

That asymmetry is what makes the mode possible: the clutter is exactly the
model-driven half, and none of the three keepers is model-driven. So withholding
the model-driven ids drops the clutter and leaves both event-driven LUI and the
whole native HUD untouched.

Two switches were considered and REJECTED, each for a measured reason:
  - `cg_draw2D` — gates two ENTIRE native draw functions; takes the hitmarkers with
    it (user-confirmed in game).
  - the `CG_ShouldDrawHud` twin — MWR shows it also gates CG_DrawCrosshair
    (callers: CG_PreDraw2D, CG_DrawCrosshair, CG_AddDrawSurfsFor3dHudElems,
    CG_FadeHudMenu, CG_OwnerDraw), so the S2 equivalent would kill hitmarkers too.
    It bottoms out in CL_ShouldDisplayHud.

Shipped build 71ABA975: `demo_hud_minimal` + a "Minimal HUD" checkbox.

⚠ HONEST LIMITS, both stated in the UI: withholding a publish stops a model
CHANGING, it does not tear down an element already built — so enable it BEFORE
playback. And "killfeed and score popups survive" is STRONG INFERENCE (the ~70
id->name list contains nothing resembling an obituary or points feed), not a
measurement. `demo_hud_suppress` retunes the list with no rebuild.

## MCP NOTE — MWR-PS4 reachable by direct JSON-RPC when its namespace is missing

Claude Code spawns MCP stdio servers at SESSION START. If IDA is not yet listening

The IDB is still reachable meanwhile — the same fallback already recorded for MW3:

Helper written this session: scratchpad/ida_rpc.py (`python ida_rpc.py 9999 <tool> '<json>'`).

## ⭐ THE COMPLETE LUI HUD MODEL ID SET — measured, not inferred

`demo_hud_models` over a full playback yields **73 distinct ids, 1..104**, and they
match sub_357AD0's call sites exactly — so there is NO second publisher.

    1-5 clip/stock/altMode ammo      47,48 lethal/tactical material
    8-11 lethal/tactical counts      49-57 perks A1..C3
    12-17 ads/breath                 62 reloadPercent
    25,26 lastStand/dead             67 isPlayerOnLadder

**id 100 = cg.Shared.connectionStateActive** is published OUTSIDE the connstate gate,

## ⚠ RULE A18 — A DISCOVERY PROBE REPORTS EACH DISTINCT THING ONCE

`demo_hud_models` logged every publish. The publisher runs ~70 times PER FRAME, so
one session wrote **187,096 lines out of 187,693 — 99.7% of a 10 MB log** — and
buried every other diagnostic in it.

The fix is not "log less often", it is to log each distinct VALUE once (a `std::set`
of ids seen) and print a summary on the way out. A probe that answers "what ids
exist" has a finite answer; streaming it is always wrong.

Generalise: before adding a per-call log, ask how many times per frame the call
happens. If the answer is more than one, dedupe or rate-limit at the point of
logging, not by remembering to turn it off.
