# ⭐⭐⭐ SERVER BROWSER — THE SEARCH-RESULT TABLE, AND WHERE IT ARRIVES (2026-08-10)

## PROVEN — the search result record, named by the engine's own telemetry

`sub_2A1820` writes every field below to a DDL analytics record under these exact
names, so none of this is inferred. Walk base `searchObj + 80`, **stride 596**,
count at `searchObj + 29808` (0x7470 — the field Search_GetResultCount returns):

    p[0]        slots_available_count      p[-2]   occupied  (total = p[0] + p[-2])
    p[-4] u16   datacenter                 p[4]    status: 1 or 2 == joinable
    p[8]  u32   qos_error_code             p[412]  lobby_throttle
    p[396/400/404] rating_result / rating_ping / rating_skill
    p[416..420] ping_aggregate / median / average / ours / lobby
    p-64        host address blob

The joinable test is the engine's own: Search_GetJoinableCount @0x29C780 walks
`obj + 84` with stride 149 ints and counts `(status - 1) <= 1`.

## ⭐ PROVEN — sub_6FED70 is the Demonware search-results callback

    scratch = alloc(29816); memset(scratch, 0, 0x7478)
    for each Demonware result (stride 432 from v3+248):
        if (scratch[7452] >= 50) break            <- MAX 50 RESULTS
        idx = 149 * scratch[7452]++                <- 596-byte stride, count at
                                                      int 7452 == byte 29808
        sub_A788E0(result, &scratch[idx+4])        <- host address at byte 596*i+16
        ...
    sub_2A1630(...)                                <- telemetry
    sub_29D720(searchState, scratch)               <- HANDS THE TABLE OVER

`&scratch[idx+4]` == byte `596*i + 16` is exactly the `p - 64` host_address slot
named by sub_2A1820. Two independent derivations of the same layout.

## ⭐ THE CAPTURE POINT — sub_29D720, NOT the accept or count hooks

USER OBSERVATION that pinned it: "it only picks up servers when I'm searching AND
join it." Exactly right, and it names the bug:

  - `Search_GetResultCount` @0x29CEC0 is a **LUI-facing getter**. The results
    screen calls it; if that screen is not up it never fires. WRONG capture point.
  - `Lobby_AcceptSearchResult` @0x29BFF0 runs from the search-result LOOP
    (sub_29BE20), which only runs once the engine COMMITS to a join. So it
    captures at join time only. WRONG for browsing.
  - **`sub_29D720(searchState, table)`** is called by the results callback the
    moment results arrive, before any join decision. RIGHT.

Hooked as `Search_PublishResults`, IDA 0x29D720 - 0x1000 = 0x29C720. RULE A3.1
checked: nothing else in src/ referenced either form.

## ⚠ WHAT A SERVER BROWSER CAN AND CANNOT BE HERE

It is NOT a global list of every live lobby and no client can produce one:
matchmaking is SERVICE-BROKERED. Demonware answers OUR search, for the playlist WE
asked for, with a candidate set IT chose. The tab therefore shows what the service
offered us — the most any client can see. One search covers ONE playlist.

Join is implemented through the engine's own accept path: every result except the
chosen index is refused, so the engine joins the pick by its own code. Nothing is
synthesised.

## Two self-inflicted defects in the first build, both avoidable

1. **The browse button never started a search.** It issued `playlist N` and
   stopped. Setting a playlist queries nothing, so the tab was correctly empty.
   The log showed `playlist 54` issued 17 times with no search. Now it also drives
   Matchmaking_Start (the engine's own entry, body of the LUI GameMatchmakingStart
   binding, already used by fh_readvertise).

2. **RULE A15 broken in the same session it was written down.** The snapshot path
   had NO diagnostics, so "no servers show up" was indistinguishable from "the hook
   never fired" / "the count was rejected". It now reports the object, whether the
   count was readable, the count itself and the first row — one line per change,
   capped at 40 so it can never become the 187k-line flood the HUD probe produced.
   `fh_servers` dumps the table AND the attempt counters on demand.

# ⭐⭐⭐ TWO CRASHES, BOTH OURS, BOTH NAMED BY A DUMP + THE MWR TWIN (2026-08-10)

User: "the change map thing just always crashed our game". RULE A13 answered it
without a single probe, and the named MWR IDB named the second one.

## ⭐ CRASH 1 — "change map always crashes" = WE FREED ui_mp WHILE IT WAS RENDERING

Three of the four most recent dumps agree:

    fault IDA_0x88E307   READ from 0x58   (NULL struct + 0x58)
    stack: SCR_DrawScreen(0xF20D0) -> sub_F25A0 -> sub_8BBB10 -> sub_88E680

**The fault is in the DRAW path, not the load path.** `fh_changemap` called
`release_for_external_map_change()`, which released the FRONTEND (ui_mp, mask 388)
and the level, then issued `wait ; wait ; map X`. A map change is issued while the
menu is up and RENDERING, so freeing ui_mp pulls material/image data out from under
the very next frame.

This is the SAME mistake as the gibraltar crash recorded earlier — release the
frontend at the wrong lifecycle point and whatever is bound to it dies. The lesson
was already written down ("WHERE you call it is part of the contract") and I broke
it again in a different function.

FIX: an external map change now releases the LEVEL ONLY, exactly as the engine's own
map change (sub_837E0, {NULL, 0, 136}) does. It never drops ui_mp, because you are
not leaving the frontend. Keeps the original benefit — the previous level's zones are
freed, so a bare `map` no longer overflows the 40192 image pool — with none of the
use-after-free.

## ⭐⭐ CRASH 2 — sub_6DA820 IS SV_ChangeMaxClients, AND OUR BYTE POKES BREAK IT

    fault IDA_0x6DA8C5   READ unmapped
    stack includes SV_SpawnServer (0x6DC350) at 0x6DC8D4

TWIN-PROVEN against MWR PS4 `SV_ChangeMaxClients` @0x833E90: same highest-active-slot
scan (state >= 3), same `Dvar_RegisterInt(sv_maxclients)` then `Dvar_SetInt` to raise
it, same temp-alloc(stride * count) -> memcpy live clients -> memset array -> copy
back, same recompute of derived sizes.

**MWR carries the assert that names our crash:**

    assert(sv_maxclients->current.integer <= svs.clientCount)
    D:\h1\code_source\Runtime\server_mp\sv_init_mp.cpp:1061

S2 ships without asserts, so violating it is an ACCESS VIOLATION instead: the SSE
loop at 0x6DA8C5 walks `svs.clients` with stride 1173616 bounded by the raised count
and reads past the allocation.

Our force_host poked FIVE unverified bytes (`ADDR_MAXPLAYERS`, zero xrefs, inherited
from GRIIMS-WWII-Tool) with 18. That sets a player count WITHOUT SV_ChangeMaxClients
reallocating the client array — precisely the asserted-against condition.

FIX: those pokes are now DEFAULT OFF (`fh_pokemaxplayers` re-enables them).
`set_forced_maxplayers` drives the ENGINE's own party_maxplayers setter instead:

    party_maxplayers = lobby params[1] = lobby + 596
    setter sub_1973D0  IDA 0x1973D0 - 0x1000 = 0x1963D0
    getter sub_197110  (already used by read_params, so set-then-read self-checks)

Clamped to 1..48: sv_maxclients is registered with max = dvar "2813" (default 48).

## S2 dvar names decoded from the twin

    "2299" = sv_maxclients   (default 48, max from "2813")
    "2813" = the sv_maxclients upper bound

## Named / commented in the IDB (saved)

    0x6DA820   SV_ChangeMaxClients      twin-proven, full comment incl. the assert
    0xC60D8E8  dvar_sv_maxclients       (data)
    0xC5FBA50  commented: allocated server client slot count; maps onto MWR's
               svs.clientCount, the operand of that assert

## GENERAL RULE THIS REINFORCES

Both crashes came from writing state the engine owns instead of calling the engine's
own setter for it. The doctrine already says this ("Do Not Manufacture Missing
State", "Never write a recorded value into a native state field until its ownership
is proven"). Byte pokes inherited from another tool are the worst case: empirically
effective somewhere, unverifiable here, and they fail as memory corruption rather
than as an error message.


## ⭐⭐ WHY THE SERVER LIST IS EMPTY — NO SEARCH IS EVER ISSUED (2026-08-10)

User pressed TDM and Shipment at the menu, waited, got nothing, and asked whether
the PING RANGE was the variable. It is not. The log settles it:

    [host] search-results hook (IDA 0x29D720): OK (orig=...)   <- installed fine
    [host] search snapshot via count: countReadable=1 count=0  <- fired once, zero
    (no "via results" line at all)                             <- sub_29D720 NEVER ran
    [host] Matchmaking_Start(mm, 0) returned 0 (call #5)       <- did run

So the capture is healthy and Matchmaking_Start runs; the service is simply never
asked. Nothing downstream can fix that.

## The chain, mapped against the named MWR IDB

    MWR                                     S2
    dwMatchMakingManager_Update  0x5F9E0    (state machine)
    dwMatchMakingManager_StartServerSearch 0x5F940
                                            sub_29D9C0   the search TICK
    bdMatchMaking__findSessions  0xC0A800   sub_6FF930   find-sessions issuer
                                              dw task type 11, opcode 118,
                                              240-byte param blob (sub_285DA0 builds it),
                                              success cb sub_6FED70, failure sub_6FECE0
    Session_RandomSearchSessionsComplete 0x8734F0
                                            sub_6FED70   results callback
                                            sub_29D720   publishes the table  <- we hook this

## PROVEN — the gate that decides whether a search happens

sub_29D9C0 issues a search only when

    sub_6FC1C0(controller, n)  ==  sub_207E00(11, controller, 118, n)
      = sub_834640(controller)            // controller usable
        && sub_839160(118)                // dw service for opcode 118 available
        && (active opcode-118 tasks) < n  // 32 task slots

Otherwise it just bumps a failure counter and returns 0. `sub_839160` has only two
code xrefs, both in the task allocators, so it is specifically "is this dw opcode
available".

Second branch worth knowing: when `sub_480F20(params)` (sessionType == 2) and
`sub_1FF290`, the tick takes the DEDICATED-SERVER search (sub_1FED90) instead and no
lobby search is issued at all.

## ⚠ CORRECTION — "Search this playlist" cannot start a search by itself

Calling Matchmaking_Start sets state and publishes session properties; it does NOT
query the service. The query comes from the tick, which the lobby state machine
drives. Measured: Matchmaking_Start returned and sub_29D720 never fired. The button
now says so and runs the gate probe instead of implying it searched.

`fh_searchgate` reports each term of the gate, so "no servers" resolves to a named
cause rather than a guess.

## On the ping hypothesis

There IS a ping concept in matchmaking — MWR has dwMatchMakingSettings_GetMinPing
@0x609B0 and dwMatchMakingManager_UpdateMinPing @0x5EA90, and the result record
carries ping_ours/average/median/aggregate/lobby. But ping filters candidates
returned BY a search; with no search issued there is nothing to filter. Ping is not
why the list is empty.

# ⭐⭐⭐ OUR OWN HOOKS WERE BREAKING MATCHMAKING — PROVEN BY A/B (2026-08-10)

## The control that settled it

The DLL cannot simply be removed (with IDA attached the game will not start
without it), so init() now checks for a marker file and returns BEFORE installing
any hook — a real control, not a flag tested inside a live detour:

    s2mp_no_forcehost.txt   next to the game exe -> force_host installs NOTHING

    WITH our hooks:     20 searches issued, 12 completed, 0 errors, 0 discards,
                        ZERO candidates, no match ever found
    WITHOUT our hooks:  match found ALMOST INSTANTLY

Same account, same session, minutes apart. That is decisive: the empty server list
and the inability to find a match were the SAME defect, and it was ours.

Everything I had concluded from the instrumented runs was true and useless: the gate
passed, the query went out unfiltered (three 0xFFFFFFFF wildcards), the service
answered without error. All of that was measured through a search path we had
already broken.

## PROVEN — at least one concrete defect: sub_29D720 declared `void`

    __int64 __fastcall sub_29D720(__int64 a1, __int64 a2)
    {
        return sub_29D8E0(a1, (a2 & ~0xFF) | 1, a2);
    }

Two things wrong with how it was hooked:

  1. It returns **__int64**; the stub was declared **void**. That is RULE A17 in the
     NARROWING direction, which is worse than widening — the caller reads RAX and a
     void stub does not guarantee what is in it.
  2. It is NOT a passive notifier. It forwards into sub_29D8E0, which reads and
     compares the result count at +0x7470 — i.e. the hook sat INSIDE the
     results-INSTALL path, not beside it.

Fixed to return std::int64_t and forward the original's value.

## THE STRUCTURAL FIX — search-path hooks are now OPT-IN

They exist only to diagnose the server browser, which does not work anyway. Working
matchmaking is worth far more, so by default NOTHING on the search path is patched:

    s2mp_search_trace.txt   next to the exe -> install them (debugging only)

Covers Search_PublishResults, Search_Tick, Search_FindSessions, Search_Failed,
Search_Complete, Search_Discard, Search_GetResultCount, Search_GetJoinableCount.
The session hooks (accept / assign / advertise / dedicated-ready) are unchanged and
still install, so force host itself is unaffected — that half must be re-tested
separately before it is trusted.

## ⚠ RULE A19 — A HOOK IS NEVER A PASSIVE OBSERVER

I installed ~10 hooks on the matchmaking path purely to WATCH it, on the assumption
that a pass-through detour changes nothing. It is not true:

  * a wrong return width corrupts the caller (RULE A17, both directions)
  * a function that "looks like" a notifier may be a forwarder into the real work
  * the cost is paid on the engine's own threads

Before hooking a function to observe it, decompile it far enough to know whether it
RETURNS anything and whether it DOES anything, and prefer capture points that are
genuinely leaf-like. When a subsystem misbehaves, suspect your own instrumentation
FIRST — it is the newest code in the process.

## ⚠ RULE A20 — KEEP A ZERO-HOOK CONTROL AVAILABLE FROM DAY ONE

This cost several build/test cycles of increasingly elaborate instrumentation, all
of it measuring a path we had already broken. A marker file that skips installation
entirely is trivial to add and would have found this immediately. Any module that
patches engine state should ship one.


## ⭐ ABI AUDIT OF EVERY ALWAYS-ON force_host HOOK (2026-08-10)

After the sub_29D720 defect broke matchmaking, audited all SEVEN hooks that still
install by default, comparing each declared signature against the S2 decompile
(RULE A17) and checking whether each is a passive observer or a forwarder into real
work (RULE A19). Result: **all seven are ABI-correct and behaviourally pass-through
or read-only in the default (not-force-hosting) state.** No second sub_29D720.

    hook target                       true signature (S2 decompile)          verdict
    Lobby_AcceptSearchResult 0x29BFF0 bool(__int64,uint,char)                CLEAN, pure predicate
    Lobby_AssignServer       0x29A620 __int64(__int64,__int64,uint8)         CLEAN, forwards orig
    Lobby_IsAdvertiseEligible 0x4810F0 _BOOL8(__int64)                       CLEAN (8-byte ret)
    Script_AdvertiseServer   0x2972B0 __int64(__int64)                       CLEAN, forwards orig
    Lobby_IsDedicatedServerReady 0x1FD110 bool(_DWORD*)                      CLEAN, pass-through off
    NET_GetPacket            0x7B0D00 __int64(__int64,__int64)               CLEAN, read-only
    PlatformSocket_Recv      0xA7EB90 __int64(int,DWORD*,u_short*,char*,int) CLEAN, read-only

Both packet stubs call the original FIRST, return its value unchanged, and only READ
the buffers (never write). platform_recv reads *out_ip/*out_port only when the return
is a non-negative length, and the true function writes both on every success, so no
uninitialised read. net_getpacket reads msg+8/msg+28 only when the original returned
1, when both are valid. tick() writes NO engine state in the default state -- every
write branch is behind a flag that defaults false (g_auto_reassert, g_want_republish,
g_force_solo_start, g_force_hosting, g_dlc_forced_off).

So the ONLY thing that broke matchmaking was the now-removed search-hook set. The
default build should find matches.

## TWO DIAGNOSTIC-ON-HOT-PATH RESIDUALS FIXED (same lesson, applied proactively)

The audit is clean, but two diagnostic-only things were still running on the
matchmaking/packet path by default -- the exact anti-pattern that just cost a working
matchmaker. Both removed from the default path (build 874AFAAE):

  1. The always-on accept stub called snapshot_search_results (a VirtualQuery-heavy
     browser scan) on EVERY accept-result pass. Now gated behind g_search_hooks_enabled
     (s2mp_search_trace.txt). The force-host JOIN BLOCK stays always-on -- it is
     functional, not diagnostic.
  2. g_peer_track defaulted TRUE, so the fh_peers tracker did a GetTickCount +
     critical section + 64-entry scan on every inbound datagram, including the
     platform socket matchmaking/QoS ride. Now DEFAULT FALSE; `fh_peers 1` enables it
     at runtime (hooks stay installed, no restart). Read-only and almost certainly not
     the breaker, but nothing diagnostic runs on the packet path unless asked for.

Neither changes matchmaking or force-host LOGIC, so any result measured on 5629450C
still holds; 874AFAAE only removes diagnostic overhead.


## ⭐⭐⭐ FORCE HOST vs SEARCH — WHY THEY CONFLICT, AND THE host=0 LIMBO (2026-08-10)

User: force host active stops them searching, nobody joins them, Join button dead.
Traced statically (no deploy). All three reduce to ONE design flaw.

### PROVEN — start_hosting()'s only search-breaking act is block_joining

start_hosting() sets local flags only (g_want_hosting, g_want_allow_listen,
g_auto_reassert, g_force_listen) PLUS **set_block_joining(true)**. It does NOT touch
online / systemlink / sessionType, so the session stays online and the search still
ISSUES (sub_29D9C0 -> sub_6FF930, confirmed by the user's "SEARCH ISSUED" logs).

The break is g_block_joining -> accept_search_result_stub returns FALSE for EVERY
search result. That is force host's "semi-host" mechanism (refuse all joins so the
matchmaker gives up and you host), and it is fundamentally incompatible with browsing
or joining. It is WHY, while force hosting:
  - the Servers tab shows nothing joinable,
  - the Join button does nothing,
  - "can't find servers to connect to".

Searching and force-hosting are OPPOSITE operations and cannot both be active.

### ⭐ THE host=0 LIMBO — we advertise a session we don't host

Every ADVERTISABLE line in the user's log reads `host=0 dedicated=0`. sub_4810F0 can
return "advertisable" while AreWeHost (obj+1598540) is still 0 -- so we advertise a
session we are NOT hosting. Nobody can join a host that does not exist, which is the
"nobody joins us" half. block_joining is supposed to make us host by exhausting the
search, but the evidence says host_flag never actually flips.

### PROVEN (MWR twin) — the ENGINE's intended host path is SELECT-HOST, not refuse-all

MWR dwMatchMakingManager_Update @0x5F9E0 + dwMatchMakingManager_ShouldHost @0x5FD50:
matchmaking has a MODE (dword_1D56CD0). Mode 2 = search
(dwMatchMakingManager_StartServerSearch). Mode 1 = host: after a time-based
dwMatchMakingSettings_ShouldHost(elapsedSeconds), when no server is assigned and the
session info is valid, it calls **DSCL_SelectHostAsServer()** -- a clean "make me the
host" primitive.

So the CORRECT force host drives the engine's own host-select, which sets AreWeHost=1
and produces a REAL joinable host. The S2 equivalent is the become-host/session-create
path: sub_490E70 (sets AreWeHost=1 at +1598540) via sub_491DE0, and sub_80290 (already
in CLAUDE.md) = "create a hosted session AND advertise it". That is what force host
SHOULD call, instead of sabotaging the search with block_joining.

### The fix plan (staged; needs a live 2-player test, so NOT shipped blind)

  1. Replace block_joining as the host mechanism with the engine's own host-select
     (sub_80290 / the sub_491DE0 path), so host_flag actually becomes 1 and others can
     join a real session. block_joining stays as an OPTIONAL "don't let matchmaking
     put me in someone else's game" toggle, off by default.
  2. Because a real host does not need to search, "host" and "browse/join" become
     explicit, mutually-exclusive modes in the GUI.

### Shipped now (9E19180B) — the one safe fix

The Join button's g_join_index handling was gated behind the search-trace marker (a
regression from making browser capture opt-in). Un-gated: the explicit "join this
result" pick is a user action, takes priority over block_joining, and works without
the marker. The browser CAPTURE stays behind the marker (diagnostic, hot-path).

### Runtime tests that need NO deploy

  - Force host OFF + Find Match on 874AFAAE/9E19180B: tests whether peer-tracker-off
    fixed the "zero candidates". (Peer tracker on <=5629450C added a lock to every
    matchmaking/QoS datagram -- the most likely remaining interference.)
  - fh_on then `fh_blockjoin 0`: host + advertise WITHOUT refusing joins, so you can
    still search. Confirms block_joining is the search-breaker.

### Honest limit

Whether other players can actually JOIN a correctly-hosted session is the Demonware
discoverability question and can only be settled with a second player. Everything
above is client-side and static; the host=0 finding says the current build never even
presents a real host to test.


## ⭐⭐⭐ `fh_off` WAS TEARING DOWN MATCHMAKING — that is why searching stayed dead

User: "I did fh_off and I still can't find a game." Found live with CE attached,
game running, no restart. The log said it outright:

    [host] force hosting OFF — you can join other lobbies again.
    [host] Matchmaking_Stop: inProgress 0 -> 0 ... The engine's own teardown

`stop_hosting()` called `queue_stop_advertise()`, which calls **Matchmaking_Stop**
(sub_29B640). That is NOT an un-advertise. Decompiled, it is a FULL TEARDOWN:

    sub_29D870(a1 + 1656) / sub_29C510(a1 + 1688)   DESTROY the search state
    sub_828170(*v2, ..., 0)                          un-advertise
    sub_1FD540 / sub_1FDDC0 / sub_483D20(v2, 0)      release the server assignment
    a1[0] = 0; a1[1] = 0; *(DWORD*)(a1 + 4) = 0      clear the ACTIVE flags

So turning force hosting OFF demolished the matchmaking session itself and left the
player unable to search at all. Both states were broken for DIFFERENT reasons:
  force host ON  -> block_joining refuses every search result
  force host OFF -> Matchmaking_Stop destroyed the search state

FIXED (CECA160F): stop_hosting() no longer calls Matchmaking_Stop. It releases only
OUR overrides (join gate, hosting latch, and now g_force_listen too, which it also
used to leave set). `fh_stopadvertise` still un-advertises explicitly when wanted.

GENERAL: releasing a latch is not the same operation as destroying the thing it was
latching. An "off" switch must undo what "on" did and NOTHING MORE.

### Live recovery WITHOUT a restart — PROVEN from the twin pair

Matchmaking_Start (sub_29B510) re-initialises exactly what Stop destroyed:
sub_29D870(+1656), sub_29C510(+1688), sub_2868C0(+8), then sets the active flag
`*(BYTE*)a1 = 1` and stamps `a1+4` -- the flags Stop had zeroed. It is exposed as
**`fh_readvertise`**, so a player whose matchmaking was killed by the old fh_off can
recover in-session with that command instead of restarting.

### Verification notes for this session

  * RULE A9 confirmed: loaded module hash 9E19180B == deployed. The test was on the
    build I thought.
  * MinHook trampoline-overflow check on every installed target: all >= 0x16 bytes.
    Worth recording that **sub_29D720 is only 0xA (10) bytes** -- genuinely risky to
    hook, and now opt-in.
  * CE base verified per RULE A2 (EXE_ERR_PROCESS_DEMO_FILE_FAILED at base+0xBCE9E0)
    and independently corroborated: ADDR_LOBBY_OBJ0 computes to 0x7FF62EFF6040, the
    exact `obj=` value in the logs.
  * Live lobby params read (lobby+592): minplayers=2 maxplayers=12 private=0
    playlist=31 requireOpenNat=1 allowJoiningListenServer=0. So fh_off HAD stopped
    re-asserting the listen-server param correctly; the damage was the teardown.
  * Build gotcha: a stale bin/Release/s2mp-mod.pdb caused LNK1201 twice. Deleting the
    pdb fixed it; it was not a lock from the running game or from CE.


### ⛔ CORRECTION — fh_readvertise does NOT recover a torn-down session

I wrote above that Matchmaking_Start "re-initialises exactly what Stop destroyed" and
called live recovery PROVEN. **Tested by the user: it did not fix it.** Withdrawn.

Re-reading the pair, Start restores strictly less than Stop destroys:

    Stop (sub_29B640)                        Start (sub_29B510)
      sub_29D870(a1+1656)                      sub_29D870(a1+1656)      same
      sub_29C510(a1+1688)                      sub_29C510(a1+1688)      same
      sub_2868C0(a1+8)                         sub_2868C0(a1+8)         same
      a1[0]=0 a1[1]=0 (a1+4)=0                 sets a1[0]=1, stamps +4  same
      sub_1FDDC0(v2[1])                        -- NOT RESTORED --
      sub_483D20(v2, 0)                        -- NOT RESTORED --
      sub_1FD540(...)  (release DS)            -- NOT RESTORED --
      sub_828170(*v2, client, 0) un-advertise  (5 property setters only)

sub_483D20 is the SAME function Lobby_AssignServer calls with 1, so Stop clears the
**server-assigned** state on the LOBBY, and Start only re-arms the matchmaking
object's own search sub-objects. The lobby-side assignment is never re-acquired, so
the session stays unable to search. Recovery therefore needs the session RECREATED
(restart, or a full back-out that runs the session-create path), not Matchmaking_Start.

LESSON (my error, twice in two turns): I compared two functions, saw the matching
calls, and called it proven while skipping the lines that had NO counterpart. When
claiming "X undoes Y", diff BOTH directions and account for every call on each side --
the unmatched ones are the whole answer.

The real fix is prevention, which is what shipped: stop_hosting() no longer calls
Matchmaking_Stop, so the session is never damaged in the first place.


## ⭐ TEST 1 FAILED — the hooks break matchmaking BY BEING INSTALLED (2026-08-10)

Clean boot, force host NEVER switched on, Find Match -> still no game. So this is not
about fh_on/fh_off state at all: merely INSTALLING the force-host hooks breaks
matchmaking. That reproduces the original A/B (marker present = no hooks = works).

Ruled out first, so the bisect starts from a clean base:
  * RULE A9: loaded module hash == deployed. Right build under test.
  * ABI audit of all 7 always-on hooks vs the S2 decompile: every signature correct,
    every stub pass-through or read-only in the default state.
  * MinHook trampoline overflow: every installed target >= 0x16 bytes.
    (sub_29D720 is only 0xA = 10 bytes -- genuinely risky, and already opt-in.)
  * tick() writes no engine state unless a flag that defaults false is set.

So the mechanism is NOT a wrong signature or a logic branch. Remaining candidates are
the act of patching these specific functions -- most plausibly the two on the network
path, which are called at high frequency from Demonware's own threads.

### Shipped: the packet hooks are now OPT-IN (leading suspect + principled anyway)

NET_GetPacket (0x7B0D00) and PlatformSocket_Recv (0xA7EB90) are DIAGNOSTIC ONLY --
they feed `fh_peers` and nothing else -- and they sit on the exact socket matchmaking
and QoS ride on. Default OFF; enable with s2mp_net_trace.txt.

### Bisect groups, so this costs boots and not rebuilds

s2mp_no_forcehost.txt now selects groups instead of being all-or-nothing:

    empty / "all"        install NOTHING (the full control)
    a line of group names skip only those groups

    net     NET_GetPacket + PlatformSocket_Recv    (now off by default anyway)
    ded     Lobby_IsDedicatedServerReady
    accept  Lobby_AcceptSearchResult               (the join gate)
    assign  Lobby_AssignServer
    adv     Lobby_IsAdvertiseEligible + Script_AdvertiseServer

Parsing is STRICT: a line counts only if EVERY whitespace-separated token on it is a
known group name, so the file's own explanatory prose cannot accidentally match (a
substring search would have matched "adv" inside "advertised" and silently
half-disabled the control run).

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# REBUILD FROM SCRATCH — SERVER BROWSER + HOSTING, THE QUAKE3/CoD WAY
# (2026-08-11). The old force_host + Demonware-search browser was DELETED.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

## Why the old approach was wrong, stated plainly

The deleted implementation tried to bend **Demonware matchmaking** to our will:
refuse every search result so the matchmaker gives up and makes us host
(`block_joining`), then read the search-result table to populate a "server list".
Every symptom traced back to that premise:

  * refusing all results also stops YOU finding/joining anything
  * we advertised while `AreWeHost == 0` -- a host that does not exist
  * the browser could only ever show what the SERVICE offered us, per playlist
  * hooking the search path broke matchmaking outright (proven by A/B)

It was fighting a brokered, server-authoritative system from the client. The user
was right that this "can be done so easily and is proven in other cods".

## ⭐⭐⭐ THE PROVEN DESIGN IS STILL FULLY PRESENT IN S2

S2 retains the entire Quake3/CoD out-of-band (OOB) netcode. Strings, live code
references, both directions. This is the mechanism every CoD server browser uses.

### Client -> server probe: `LAN_GetServers` @ sub_808F0 (IDA 0x808F0)

    clears a 128-entry server table at unk_1C7E228 (256 bytes per entry)
    Com_sprintf(buf, 32, "%igetinfo xxx", 3)          <- protocol 3 prefix
    for pass in 0..1:                                  (sends TWICE)
        for i in 0..3:
            port = sub_76BAA0(27016 + i)               <- FOUR PORTS FROM 27016
            sub_66E080(sub_66DE60(client), &addr, buf, len)   <- broadcast send

Caller: sub_74A610 (the UI refresh path). So the engine ALREADY has a working LAN
scan; it is simply not reachable from the shipped menus.

### Server -> client reply: `SV_ConnectionlessPacket` @ sub_6DEE70 (IDA 0x6DEE70)

Dispatches OOB commands by name: **getchallenge, getstatus, getinfo, connect**,
stats, steamauth, disconnect, ihear/icanthear, joinvoice/leavevoice, keepalive.

`getinfo` -> sub_6DDB00, which builds a full **infoResponse** infostring:

    challenge, protocol, checksum, hostname, "1673"(mapname), ingame,
    clients, botcount, "2299"(sv_maxclients), gametype, pure, game,
    con_disabled, ff, kc, st, hw, agtCnt, bots, seckey, secid, hostaddr
    -> I_strncpyz("infoResponse\n"), sub_66E130(2, &addr, buf)

**That is a complete server-browser row: hostname, map, gametype, players,
bots, maxplayers.** Nothing needs inventing.

⚠ GATE: the getinfo reply is wrapped in
    `if (Com_IsSystemLink() && !(BYTE)word_1BD36F8)`
i.e. only answered in SYSTEM LINK mode and not in the hub. That matches the
existing finding that Session_CanHostServer returns 1 unconditionally under
systemlink -- system link is the engine's own "host without Demonware" path.

### Connect handshake (client side)

    "getchallenge 0 \"%s\""   @0xB344E8, referenced by sub_6AF20
    "connect %s \"%s\""       @0xB344D8, referenced by sub_6B220
    "challengeResponse"       @0xB34698     "connectResponse" @0xB346B0
    "connect" console command @0xB34DE8, referenced by sub_9A130 / sub_6DEE70

So DIRECT CONNECT by address exists on both sides.

### What is ABSENT, and why that is fine

`getservers` / `getserversResponse` (the id master-server protocol) are NOT in the
binary -- Demonware replaced the master server. So there is no internet server LIST
to query. Discovery is LAN broadcast (4 ports from 27016), which over a virtual LAN
(ZeroTier/Radmin) is exactly how the MW3/BO2 system-link communities operate.

## THE NEW DESIGN (completely different from the deleted one)

  1. HOST  = system link listen server. Com_IsSystemLink() true -> CanHostServer
     returns 1 unconditionally, map/gametype come from LOCAL dvars, and the engine
     answers getinfo so we are discoverable. No Demonware, no block_joining, no
     refusing search results, no advertise-vs-AreWeHost limbo.
  2. BROWSE = drive the engine's own LAN_GetServers (sub_808F0) and read the
     engine's own 128-entry table, OR send getinfo ourselves to a specific address.
     Real player counts from infoResponse, not from a matchmaking candidate set.
  3. JOIN   = the engine's own `connect <ip>` console command. Direct, no
     matchmaking involvement at all.

Nothing here hooks the matchmaking path, so it CANNOT break Find Match -- which
was the recurring failure of the old design.


## ⭐⭐ THE SERVER TABLE, FIELD BY FIELD — from CL_SetServerInfo (sub_87400)

Every offset below is a STORE in that function. Nothing is inferred, which is the
whole point after the old implementation's offset guessing.

    serverInfo_t, 256 bytes/entry, 128 entries at unk_1C7E228 (IDA 0x1C7E228)
    count at dword_1C7E224 (IDA 0x1C7E224)

    +0    hostaddr blob (37 bytes)      +112  clients        <- PLAYERS
    +37   seckey                        +113  "2299" maxclients
    +53   secid                         +114  botcount
    +64   pslots   +68 pused            +116  ff  +117 kc  +118 st  +119 hw
    +72   prslots  +76 prused           +121  voice +123 agtCnt +124 bots
    +88   netadr  -> +92 ip[4], +96 port  <- the address
    +108  "248"    +109 pure            +126  minping  +128 maxping
    +110  con_disabled  +111 nettype    +136  hostname[36]   <- SERVER NAME
    +172  "1673" mapname[36]            +208  game[24]
    +232  gametype[16]                  +248  ingame

The netadr copy at +88 independently CONFIRMS the two offsets used elsewhere:
CL_ServerInfoPacket compares ip at unk_1C7E284 (= +92) and tests the free slot on
the port at unk_1C7E288 (= +96). Two derivations, same answer.

⚠ The port is stored in NETWORK order (it comes from sockaddr_in), so it must be
byte-swapped for display and for `connect`.

## NEW MODULE — src/net/server_browser.{hpp,cpp}

    net_scan              drive LAN_GetServers (broadcast getinfo, 27016-27019)
    net_servers           dump the engine's table
    net_connect <ip>      the engine's own `connect` -- direct, no matchmaking
    net_systemlink <0|1>  the engine's own host-without-Demonware mode
    net_host <map> <gt>   set ui_mapname/ui_gametype, then `wait ; wait ; map`
    GUI: a "Servers" tab (host controls + scan + direct connect + the list)

### ⭐ THE DESIGN RULE THAT MATTERS: **ZERO HOOKS**

Not one Hook::create in the module. It only READS engine memory and issues console
commands. That is structural, not stylistic: the deleted implementation broke Find
Match three separate ways purely by having hooks on the matchmaking path (proven by
A/B), and this design makes that class of failure impossible.

### Verified live before shipping (game running, CE attached)

  * base confirmed by RULE A2 (EXE_ERR_PROCESS_DEMO_FILE_FAILED at base+0xBCE9E0)
  * server table + count region readable at base+0x1C7E228 / +0x1C7E224 (count 0,
    correct -- no scan had been run)
  * dvar_systemlink resolves to a valid dvar, value 0 (correct default)

### ⚠ CORRECTED BEFORE SHIPPING — `g_gametype` DOES NOT EXIST IN S2

I nearly shipped `g_gametype <gt>`. An exact-string check of .rdata proves it is
absent. What exists: **ui_gametype** (0xB46750), **ui_mapname** (0xB46740), `map`,
`map_restart`, `systemlink`, `connect`. `sv_maxclients` is likewise absent -- it is
the numeric "2299", consistent with the earlier finding.

ui_mapname/ui_gametype are exactly the two fields Party_SetLobbyParamFromCmd writes,
and Cmd_ExecuteString runs that for EVERY console command, so issuing them as
commands is the engine's own route. This matters because under system link the
engine reads map/gametype from these LOCAL values rather than the playlist
(sub_745050 case 389: `private || systemlink || !online`).

Generalise: S2 names most dvars numerically. Before issuing any `<name> <value>`
command, verify the name exists as an exact NUL-terminated string in .rdata --
a wrong name fails SILENTLY, which is the worst possible failure mode here.

## HONEST LIMITS OF THE NEW DESIGN

  * Discovery is LAN broadcast. `getservers` (the id master-server protocol) is NOT
    in the binary, so there is no internet-wide list to query. Over the internet
    this needs a virtual LAN (ZeroTier/Radmin), which is how the MW3/BO2 system-link
    communities work -- or just direct connect by address, which always works.
  * A server only answers `getinfo` while Com_IsSystemLink() is true and it is not
    in the hub. So both ends must be in system link for browsing to find anything.
  * Whether a system-link listen server is reachable across the internet depends on
    NAT/port-forwarding (27016-27019 / the game port), exactly as it does in every
    other CoD. Untested end-to-end; it needs two machines.

## STATUS

Built and deployed (A71BBB62). NOT yet tested in game -- per the Fix Declaration
Rules this is a CANDIDATE. Stale markers from the deleted design (s2mp_no_forcehost,
s2mp_net_trace, s2mp_search_trace, s2mp_forcehost_report) were removed.


## ⛔ CORRECTION — SYSTEM LINK IS NOT WHAT WAS ASKED FOR, AND THE HOST BUTTON CRASHED

User: "this is not intended to use with system link, it needs to be an online
browser connected to s2 that shows the demonware servers and lets me host."

I read "proven in other cods" as "the LAN/system-link browser". Wrong. The
requirement is ONLINE, Demonware-brokered. Two separate errors:

### 1. The host button crashed the game — MY recorded finding, not applied

RULE A13, dump 1786404259: exception 0x80000003 (breakpoint/fatal, not an AV) with
**DB_AllocXAssetEntry_Checked (IDA 0x9E640) on the stack at 0x9E5F4 / 0x9E6DA** --
the ASSET POOL limit path.

`net_host` issued a bare `map`, which releases NOTHING, so the level loaded on top
of the frontend and overflowed the 40192 image pool. CLAUDE.md ALREADY documents
this exact failure ("the 'Change now' map button caused Exceeded limit of 40192
image assets") and demo_native::release_for_external_map_change() exists precisely
to prevent it. I failed to apply my own finding. Host is now DISABLED (0F9044F7)
rather than patched, because the design was wrong regardless.

### 2. System link is mutually exclusive with online

sub_4810F0 requires `!Com_IsSystemLink()` for advertise eligibility, and
Com_IsSystemLink/Com_IsOnlineGame select different session kinds outright. So
forcing systemlink takes the session OUT of online mode -- the opposite of the goal.
The LAN getinfo/infoResponse browser is real and works, but it is a SYSTEM LINK
feature and therefore the wrong tool here.

## ⭐ THE ONLINE PATH — dwFindDSSessions, mapped (2026-08-11)

WWII's "Demonware servers" are DEDICATED SERVER instances brokered by the service.
The client-side query chain is now mapped:

    sub_29D9C0  the matchmaking search tick
      if (sessionType == 2 && sub_1FF290) -> sub_1FED90   <- the DS branch
    sub_1FED90  set state=1, stamp time, -> sub_1FEF50
    sub_1FEF50  gathers the datacenter list (sub_286390); if count <= 0 it BAILS,
                else -> sub_6FFA90
    sub_6FFA90  == dwFindDSSessions. Builds a dw task (type 11) and registers
                  success cb sub_6FF0F0, failure cb sub_6FF040
    sub_6FF0F0  == DSCL_FindDSSessionsComplete. Builds a table of up to **20**
                  entries at **596-byte stride** (the same stride as the lobby
                  search results), writes each host address via sub_A788E0 at
                  entry+8, then hands the table over with
                      sub_1FE1B0(target, count, table)

So **sub_1FE1B0 is the "here are the Demonware dedicated servers" handoff** -- the
DS analogue of sub_29D720 for lobbies.

### ⚠ HONEST ARCHITECTURAL LIMIT — read before building a browser on this

These are DEDICATED SERVER INSTANCES to be assigned, not populated matches with
players in them. WWII's matchmaking picks a server FOR you; there is no shipped
concept of "a list of running games you browse and choose from", which is what a
CoD4/MW2-era browser shows. So a DS list would show *available server slots*, not
"servers with N players playing Domination".

Populated-lobby data DOES exist -- it is the lobby search result table already
mapped (596-byte stride, slots_total_count / slots_available_count / ping_ours,
sub_2A1820's telemetry names) -- but that is only ever filled for OUR OWN search,
for the playlist WE asked for, and hooking that path is what broke Find Match.

### THE DECISION THAT NEEDS MAKING (do not guess it again)

Three genuinely different products are possible, and they are not the same thing:

  A. DIRECT CONNECT ONLY -- `connect <ip:port>`, works online today, no discovery,
     no hooks, cannot break anything. Already shipped and working.
  B. DS LIST -- read sub_1FE1B0's table to show the dedicated servers Demonware
     offers. Requires a hook on the DS path. Shows server slots, not populated
     games.
  C. ONLINE HOST -- the engine's own host-as-server select (MWR twin
     DSCL_SelectHostAsServer, reached from dwMatchMakingManager_Update in HOST
     mode, dword_1D56CD0 == 1). This is the correct force-host primitive and the
     one the deleted implementation should have used instead of refusing search
     results. S2 twin NOT yet located.

C is the highest value and the least explored. It is also the one that makes "lets
me host" real. Locate S2's DSCL_SelectHostAsServer twin before writing any code.


## ⭐ THE ONLINE SERVER BROWSER, REBUILT READ-ONLY (2026-08-11, build E6AA96B2)

Matchmaking works again after the deletion, so the browser was rebuilt -- but on a
rule that makes the old failure impossible: **ZERO HOOKS**.

We never isolated WHICH hook broke Find Match; the only proven fact is "all
force_host hooks removed = matchmaking works". So nothing may patch that path.

### The result table is reachable by a PURE POINTER WALK

    L = lobby 0                       IDA 0x8BE6040
    M = *(QWORD*)(L + 16)             the matchmaking object
        verify *(QWORD*)(M + 31552) == L      <- the engine's OWN back-pointer
    R = M + 1712                      sub_29A8B0(M) = M + 1712   (results object)
    count = *(u32*)(R + 29808)        Search_GetResultCount
    entry i = R + 8 + 596*i           sub_29CEA0(R, i) = R + 8 + 596*i
    field ptr p = R + 80 + 596*i      (sub_2A1820's walk base)

Every one of those is an engine accessor decompiled from the IDB. VERIFIED LIVE
before any code was written: M read back as 0x7FF62EB03730 -- matching the `mm=`
in earlier logs -- and *(M + 31552) read back as lobby 0 exactly.

Layout is self-consistent, which is a good sign the struct is understood rather
than pattern-matched: R = M+1712, count at R+29808 = M+31520, and the lobby
back-pointer at M+31552 sits 32 bytes later.

The module REFUSES if the back-pointer check fails, instead of rendering a
plausible-looking table of nonsense.

### DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT, and why

  * **No Join button.** Steering the engine to one result means hooking
    Lobby_AcceptSearchResult -- the search path. Matchmaking already joins the
    best result itself, so the browser's value here is visibility.

  * **No multi-playlist sweep.** It cannot be made safe. A sweep must set a
    playlist AND make the engine search it, but Matchmaking_Start does NOT issue
    a search (measured: it returned, no query went out) -- the search comes from
    the game's own flow. So a sweep could only change the playlist MID-SEARCH,
    and CLAUDE.md records `playlist N` spam breaking matchmaking outright. Not
    worth gambling a just-restored matchmaker on.

If either is wanted later, do it deliberately WITH a zero-hook control switch in
place from the start -- never as a quiet addition.

## ⭐⭐⭐ CORRECTED — SEARCHING WITHOUT FIND MATCH *IS* POSSIBLE, AND SO IS A SWEEP

I told the user a search could only come from the game's Find Match flow, and that a
multi-playlist sweep was impossible. **Both were wrong.** They pushed back and asked
me to find "the bit that separates the requirement of find match". It exists.

### The tick is an ordinary CALL, not a flow

    sub_29A780(i) = &unk_86F3730 + 31672*i     the MM object is a PLAIN INDEXED
                                               ARRAY -- no flow needed to reach it
    sub_29A8C0(M) = M + 1656                   the search state
    sub_2960E0                                 a LUI BINDING whose whole body is
                                                 sub_29D9C0(sub_29A8C0(sub_29A780(idx)))
                                               i.e. Lua triggers the search tick
                                               with a normal function call

So `sub_29D9C0(M + 1656)` issues a real query from anywhere. What I mistook for "only
Find Match can search" was really "Matchmaking_Start does not search" -- true, but
Matchmaking_Start is the wrong function. The tick is the one that searches.

`sub_29D410` clears the result table (memset(R+8, 0, 0x7468), count=0) at the top of
each tick, so consecutive scans are cleanly separated.

### The playlist is a LOBBY PARAM, not the `playlist` console command

sub_285DA0, the search-params builder:

    v6 = sub_1971A0(lobby + 592);          sub_1971A0(x) = *(u32*)(x + 44)
    if (!private && !privateEscape) v6 = sub_6554E0(controller, v6);
    *(DWORD *)blob = v6;                   <- the FIRST dword of the search blob

    => playlist == params[11] == *(u32*)(lobby + 636)

PROVEN by two independent readings agreeing: the dumped search blob began
`1F 00 00 00` (= 31) and the live params[11] read 31.

This matters because the thing that broke matchmaking before was spamming the
`playlist N` CONSOLE COMMAND, which runs Party_SetLobbyParamFromCmd and a great deal
more. Writing params[11] directly is a single dword store to the field the blob is
built from.

"X is impossible" deserves the same evidential bar as "X works". I asserted the

## ⭐ PLAYLIST IDs ARE ORDINALS, NOT TABLE INDICES (2026-08-11)

User: "shipment is 31, domination is 13, the table you are looking at is wrong."
Correct, and the bug was worse than a wrong constant.

### The mapping function proves it

    sub_6554E0(controller, n):
        v4 = &unk_ABDE22E;                 // table base + 6
        while (!*v4) { ++v5; v4 += 284; }  // skip invalid, 284 WORDS = 568 bytes
        if (v3 != n) { ++v3; goto advance; }
        return v5;                          // returns the table INDEX

So it WALKS the table counting valid records and returns the INDEX of the Nth one.
The id the game uses is therefore an **ORDINAL over valid records**; the array
position is not the id. The browser was returning the index as the id, which is why
Shipment (index 54) was labelled with whatever sat at index 31.

### Confirmed three ways

    ordinal 13 -> index 23 = Domination        (user: "domination is 13")
    ordinal 31 -> index 54 = Shipment 1944     (user: "shipment is 31")
    live params[11] == 31                       -> the lobby WAS on Shipment

That last one also explains the earlier confusion: params[11] read 31 and I reported
it as "Domination" from the bad table. It was Shipment the whole time.

### ⚠ AN UNRESOLVED DISCREPANCY, recorded rather than hidden

sub_6554E0's validity test is `*(u16*)(rec + 6) != 0`. Measured live, that ordinal
scheme does NOT reproduce reality -- it puts 13 on Search and Destroy and 31 on an
unnamed record. The NAME-based ordinal (record has a non-empty name at +32) matches
all three data points above, so that is what params[11] indexes.

Both tests yield 44 valid records, but they select a DIFFERENT 44 (the word@+6 set
starts at index 1 and includes an unnamed index 55). The word@+6 space presumably
serves something else. Do NOT "correct" this back to word@+6 without new evidence.

### Table layout

    base unk_ABDE228 (IDA 0xABDE228 - 0x1000 = 0xABDD228)
    stride 568, 100 records, +6 word (engine's validity test), +32 name[48]
    44 populated playlists live -- the earlier hardcoded list of 12 covered barely
    a quarter of the game, so any sweep over it was near-useless.

Shipped 55DD76FF: playlist table read LIVE, ids are ordinals, and
`browser_playlists` dumps id -> name with the current one marked so the mapping is
checkable in game instead of trusted.

### LESSON

An index and an id are not the same thing, and a lookup function existing at all
(sub_6554E0) was the clue that they differ -- if id were the index, no mapping
function would be needed. When a table has an accessor, read the accessor before
assuming the array position means anything.

# ⭐⭐⭐ FORCE HOST, REBUILT WITHOUT TIMING — THE LOBBY PARAMS, DECODED (2026-08-11)

The user asked for the GRIIMS-WWII-Tool force host "but way better": no hotkey
before Demonware deploys, correct playlist shown in game, "just play and host".
Everything below was recovered from the IDB with the game closed.

## What the old tool actually did (read from its source, not guessed)

    F4 -> ApplySpoofedPlaylist()   Cbuf ";ui_mapname <map>", two mapvote entries,
                                   ";mm_skill_enabled 0", ";raidmode 0|1", and two
                                   raw gametype dwords
    F5 -> ApplyOriginalPlaylist()  put it back, ";party_maxplayers 18"
    ForceHost()                    oDisableJoining=0 + FIVE maxplayers bytes + min

and its own UI printed the procedure: "Change to spoofed playlist when the match
is about to begin then change to original playlist when the match has started."
That IS the timing dependency. Three further defects, all visible in its source:

  * the writes are ONE-SHOT, so any later engine action silently undoes them;
  * `Gametype1` / `Gametype2` are literally **0** in the shipped source, so the
    gametype half never ran at all;
  * it never touches the playlist NUMBER — which is what the game DISPLAYS, hence
    "the game thinks you're in the playlist you searched for".

Its five maxplayers byte pokes are the ones this project already proved crash
SV_ChangeMaxClients (no svs.clients realloc). Not reused.

## ⭐ THE FINDING THAT REMOVES THE TIMING

**The matchmaking search never reads ui_mapname or ui_gametype.**

    sub_285DA0 (search-params builder), the fields that matter:
        Params = Lobby_GetParams(mm);          // NB: returns the LOBBY, not params
        v6 = sub_1971A0(Params + 592);         // params[11], the playlist ordinal
        if (!sub_4810B0(Params) && !sub_480E90(Params))
            v6 = sub_6554E0(client, v6);       // ordinal -> table ROW
        *(DWORD*)searchBlob = v6;              // the FIRST dword of the blob

and the map spawn reads them at the moment it spawns:

    sub_48C0C0(lobby, ...):
        v4 = sub_1970E0(lobby);    // ui_mapname  = *(QWORD*)(lobby + 616)
        v5 = sub_1970A0(lobby);    // ui_gametype = *(QWORD*)(lobby + 624)
        ... sub_7CAD0(v4,v5); sub_80DF0(v4,v5);
        DB_LoadLevelXAssets(v4, 0);            // the map that actually loads

So map and gametype can be HELD at our values permanently without disturbing what
matchmaking searches for. There is no window to hit — keep them correct and
whenever the engine spawns, they are right. Only the playlist NUMBER has a phase,
and only if you deliberately search a different playlist from the one you run.

⚠ Note the naming trap: `Lobby_GetParams` (0x29A890) is `*(QWORD*)(a1 + 31552)`,
which takes the MATCHMAKING object and returns the LOBBY — the reverse of what the
name suggests. Already recorded once; it bit again here.

## PROVEN — the lobby params, every offset from its own accessor

    lobby 0  = IDA 0x8BE6040     sub_470D30(n) = &off_8BE6040 + 205030*n
                                 (205030 qwords = 1640240 B, matches the stride
                                  the browser already uses)
    sub_470F20 is IDENTITY, so params = lobby + 592 (sub_197070).

    +592   params[0]   party_minplayers    set sub_1973E0(lobby,n) get sub_197130
    +596   params[1]   party_maxplayers    set sub_1973D0(lobby,n) get sub_197110
    +616   params[6]   ui_mapname   char*  set sub_1973C0(lobby,s) get sub_1970E0
                                           set sub_1973B0(params,s) get sub_1970D0
    +624   params[8]   ui_gametype  char*  set sub_1973A0(lobby,s) get sub_1970A0
    +632   params[10]  private             get sub_197150
    +636   params[11]  playlist ordinal    set sub_197460(lobby,n) get sub_1971A0(params)
    +644   params[13]  requireOpenNat      +652 params[15] allowJoiningListenServer
    +656   params[16]  set sub_197470      +660 params[17] rankedMatch
    +1598512           0 while there is no session   (LUI IsSearching, sub_335270)
    +1598540           AreWeHost   (PROVEN BY NAME: Script_AreWeHost)
    +1598544           dedicated   (Script_IsServerDedicated)

`sub_197320(params, str)` is the ui_gametype worker: it interns into params+32 and
then classifies the string into params+56 as 2 / 3 / 0|1 via sub_38F550 /
sub_38F4A0 / sub_38F570.

⛔ CORRECTION to this file's earlier note "+0x270 ui_mapname (ptr) get sub_1970A0 /
+0x268 ui_gametype set sub_1973C0" — **they were swapped**. lobby+0x268 (616) is
ui_mapname and lobby+0x270 (624) is ui_gametype, proven from the setters' own
bodies and corroborated by SystemLink_BroadcastServerInfo, which this file already
records as gathering "gametype sub_1970A0".

## ⚠ ui_mapname / ui_gametype ARE INTERNED, REFCOUNTED STRINGS

`sub_688B70(void** dest, char* src)` interns `src` through the pool at
`off_ACA1388` (16-byte stride, string at +8), `_InterlockedDecrement`s the old
entry and frees it at zero, then stores the new pointer. So these fields must
NEVER be written as raw pointers, and the setters must not be called off the main
thread. Our tick runs on the DXGI Present thread, so it issues `ui_mapname <x>` /
`ui_gametype <x>` through Cbuf instead — Cmd_ExecuteString feeds every console
command to Party_SetLobbyParamFromCmd, so the interning happens on the engine's
own thread, on the engine's own path.

## ⭐ THE PLAYLIST NUMBERING RULE, AND A REAL OFF-BY-ONE FOUND IN OUR CODE

`sub_6554E0(client, ordinal)` and `sub_6563D0` walk the same table the same way:

    row_i     = IDA 0xABDE010 + 568*i,  i in [0,100)   (end sentinel word_ABEC00E)
    row + 0   display name       -> Dvar_SetString("playlist_name", row)
    row + 480 icon name          -> Dvar_SetString("1676", row + 480)
    row + 512 char* var-rule blob   ("party_maxplayers 32; ...")
    row + 540 u16 map/gametype list index
    row + 542 u16 VALIDITY -- non-zero means a real playlist

    playlist number = 0-based ORDINAL over rows whose +542 is non-zero
    the SEARCH BLOB carries the ROW INDEX, i.e. sub_6554E0(ordinal), not the ordinal

⛔ `server_browser.cpp` used base IDA 0xABDE228 with the name at +32 — that is
`0xABDE248 + 568*i` = **row_{i+1} + 0**, the NEXT row's name — while testing
validity at +6 = row_i + 542, THIS row's. The two tests were one record apart.
It still produced the right ids only because row 0 is empty and named <=> valid,
so the two off-by-ones cancelled exactly. That is why the old note there says the
word@+6 test "did not match reality". Both are now on the engine's rule.
Do not reintroduce the +32 name offset.

## ⭐ sub_6563D0 IS THE ENGINE'S OWN PLAYLIST APPLIER

`sub_6563D0(localClientNum, gametypeRotationSlot, lobby)` — arg order proven from
sub_482A10, which calls it as `sub_6563D0(a2, v7, a1)` with a1 = the lobby.
It does, in order:

    sub_197280(params)                      // qword_6CF8698 = params (edit guard)
    v12 = params[11]; walk to the table row v15
    v16/v17 = map index + gametype record from 0xABEBDF0 + 4*(slot + row[540])
    sub_1973B0(params, mapName)             // ui_mapname   (names @ 0xABF1B50)
    sub_197320(params, gametypeName)        // ui_gametype  (records @ 0xABF1F60)
    exec default_xboxlive.cfg
    run the playlist's var-rule blob line by line through Cbuf +
        Party_SetLobbyParamFromCmd  -> party_maxplayers etc.
    run the gametype record's own blob the same way
    sub_197280(0)
    Dvar_SetString("playlist_name", row)    // <- THE DISPLAY
    Dvar_SetString("1676", row + 480)       // <- the icon

`GetGameLobbyPlaylistNum` (LUI, sub_33B9B0) = `sub_1971A0(sub_197070())` =
params[11]. So the two things that decide what the game SAYS are params[11] and
the `playlist_name` dvar — exactly the two the old tool never touched.

# ⛔ DISPROVEN BY TEST — "refuse the dedicated-server handover" (2026-08-11)

USER TESTED build 8F7C8C19's `fh_forcelisten`: **the pre-match countdown completes
and the match then never starts.** Removed in build F30964E7.

## Why my reading was backwards

`sub_1FD110(o) = (o[0] - 5) <= 2 && (int)a1[3] >= 2` operates on the SERVER-ACQUIRE
state object at lobby+8. It is **"the server we went and got is READY"**, not "this
is a dedicated server". Both consumers read it:

    sub_480D80 IsDedicated(L) = advertiseEligible && L[1598460] != 1 && THIS
    sub_481750 IsListen(L)    = L[1598544]        && ...            && !THIS

so the two names made it *look* like a dedicated-vs-listen discriminator. It is not:
refusing it does not make us the host, it tells the engine acquisition never
finished, so the launch waits forever. Countdown then nothing is the exact symptom
the correct reading predicts.

CLAUDE.md's earlier note already flagged the risk honestly ("FIVE callers and only
two have been read") — but the error was not the unread callers, it was
misinterpreting the two that HAD been read.

## ⛔ AND THE LARGER FRAME WAS WRONG — stop trying to be the SERVER

User: *"your idea of getting it to pick me as the real host is just fighting against
it."* Correct, and the evidence was already in this file and underweighted.

WWII's public matchmaking **provisions** a server:

    CanStartAcquiringDSNow -> StartServerAcquire -> sub_6FFA90 dwFindDSSessions
      -> sub_6FF0F0 DSCL_FindDSSessionsComplete -> Script_AssignServer -> launch

There is no client-hosting branch for a public playlist. The shipped
`matchmaking_allowJoiningListenServer 1` var-rule blobs are the **4-player**
playlists only (0xABF62B0, 0xABF6343); the large public ones ship 0 (0xABF5560,
0xABF60F6). And the measured result from the advertise work already said so:
`advertised=1` with `AreWeHost=0`, platform UDP static at 37 packets, nobody ever
arrived.

## ⭐ THE CORRECT MODEL — LOBBY HOST, NOT SERVER HOST

From the user, who wrote the original tool: it worked by *blocking joins to other
lobbies until the game made them **lobby** host; other players then joined them.*

The match still runs on Demonware's box. What you own is the **LOBBY**, and the
deploy takes its map, gametype and player counts from the lobby host's params.
That is the only reason a map spoof does anything at all, and it is why HOLDING the
params removes the timing without ever needing to be the server.

Everything in src/net/force_host is correct under this model; the hook was noise.

## RETIRE these lines of work unless new evidence appears

  - hooking / forcing anything on the dedicated-server acquire path
  - "make Demonware route strangers to a client host on a public playlist"
  - the advertise-flag latch (R+122) — already proven inert, sub_827980 does not
    read it

## STILL OPEN — the lobby-host lever

The original tool's `oDisableJoining` (IDA 0x928BEA0, byte, written 0) is the piece
that empirically made you lobby host, and it is UNVERIFIED here: no name, no xrefs,
and in the s2x_dump it falls inside what reads as a 16-byte-stride table of

# ⭐⭐ PLAYER COUNT AND BOTS — THE CEILING IS 48, AND BOTS HAVE NO NATIVE CAP (2026-08-11)

User asked whether more than 18 players is possible, since the hub shows 48.

## PROVEN — 48 is a hard engine ceiling, from SV_ChangeMaxClients itself

    v22 = Dvar_RegisterInt("2813", 48, 1, 48, 3);                       // max 48
    dvar_sv_maxclients = Dvar_RegisterInt("2299", 48, 1, *(DWORD*)(v22+16), 1154);

`sv_maxclients` ("2299") defaults to 48 and its MAX is whatever "2813" holds, which is
itself registered with max 48. `svs.clients` (qword_C5FBA58) is allocated for that at
1173616 bytes per slot, count in dword_C5FBA50 — which is why the hub shows 48 slots.

So 18 was never a server limit. It is `party_maxplayers` (lobby params[1]), a lobby
value. force_host now clamps its max-players control to 48 rather than an arbitrary 64.

Note SV_ChangeMaxClients only ever RAISES sv_maxclients (`if (current < highestActive+1)
Dvar_SetInt(...)`) and reallocs only when the value changed at all. It never shrinks.

## PROVEN — what the engine itself ships in playlist var-rule blobs

Swept the blob text in .rdata (0xABF4000, 0x4000):

    party_maxplayers:  4 (x8), 8 (x6), 12 (x26), 18 (x3), 32 (x1)
    party_minplayers:  1 (x9), 2 (x6), 4 (x24), 6 (x2), 8 (x2), 12 (x1)

**32 has shipped precedent** in a public blob at IDA 0xABF611E:

    party_minlobbytime 0;party_minplayers 1;party_maxplayers 32;
    party_matchedplayercount 1;2507 1;2103 -1;matchmaking_allowJoiningListenServer 0;

## ⭐⭐ BOTS — THERE IS NO UPPER CLAMP IN NATIVE CODE

LUI binding table entries (stride 16, {const char* name, void* fn}) around 0xB5FC70:

    BotsAreAllowed      0xB5FC70 -> 0x335990      GetBotsTeamLimit 0xB5FCE0 -> 0x335E20
    SetBotsTeamLimit    0xB5FCF0 -> 0x335F00      AddBot           0xB60020 -> 0x3393B0
    (also GetBotsConnectType/Count, Get/SetBotsDifficulty, SetBotsConnectType)

Underneath:

    Bots_AreAllowed     0x388210   `return 1`                       <- hardcoded TRUE
    Bots_SetTeamLimit   0x38E350   v6 = (char)count;
                                   if (count <= 0) v6 = 0;          <- the ONLY guard
                                   *(BYTE*)(sub_924670(c) + team + 47) = v6;
    Bots_GetTeamLimit   0x3882C0   if (Com_IsScorestreakTraining())
                                       return *((u32*)off_1BD3710 + 4);   // a dvar
                                   return *(u8*)(sub_924650(c) + team + 47);

**The per-team bot count is ONE BYTE at settingsObject + 47 + team, and the only check
rejects non-positive values.** Whatever cap the private-match menu enforces lives in the
LUI slider, i.e. in Lua — calling the native setter goes under it. 24v24 = 48 = exactly
the allocated svs.clients array.

`LUI_SetBotsTeamLimit`'s own gate is `!Com_IsOnlineGame() || (in a lobby && we are the
game host)`, and `team == 2` means both teams. Calling Bots_SetTeamLimit directly skips
that gate — harmless, it is one byte in our own client's settings object, but the value
only MEANS anything when we are the one starting the match.

Note the getter's asymmetry: the setter always writes the byte, but the getter returns a
DVAR when the gametype is "scorestreak_training". `Com_IsScorestreakTraining` (0xB8C70)
is `qword_A0E8CE8 && strcmp(*(char**)(qword_A0E8CE8+16), "scorestreak_training") == 0`
— the training mode, not private match. In a private match the getter reads our byte.

⛔ `LUI_AddBot` (0x3393B0) ends in `nullsub_93(lobby, a, b, c)` — a NULL STUB in this
build. Do not chase it; the team-limit pair is the working surface.

A private match with bots is entirely LOCAL — com_sv_running on our own machine, no

If it does not work locally, party_maxplayers above 18 was never going to matter online.

## ⭐⭐ THERE ARE THREE LOBBY OBJECTS, AND THE MENUS WRITE DIFFERENT ONES (2026-08-11)

Asked whether S2 has an `ui_maxclients` like MWR/MW3, and what RESETS the player
count back to 18.

### ⛔ S2 HAS NO `ui_maxclients`

Exact-string check of .rdata (0xB1B000..0xD90000): the string does not exist. MWR/MW3's
`ui_maxclients` did not survive into S2. What replaced it is a LUI binding set that
writes the SAME lobby param — and that turned up the real finding.

### ⭐ THE THREE LOBBIES

    lobby 0  IDA 0x8BE6040   Lobby_Get(0)            the GAME lobby
    lobby 1  IDA 0x8D76770   (0x8D76770 - 0x8BE6040 = 0x190730 = exactly one
                              1640240 stride, so this really is lobby 1)
    lobby 2                  Lobby_Get(2)            the PRIVATE PARTY

and the LUI bindings write different ones:

    GetPartyMaxPlayers        0x125F80 -> LobbyParams_GetMaxPlayers(sub_470CB0())
    SetPartyMaxPlayers        0x125FD0 -> LobbyParams_SetMaxPlayers(sub_470CB0(), n)
    GetPrivatePartyMaxPlayers 0x126060 -> LobbyParams_GetMaxPlayers(sub_47E350())
    SetPrivatePartyMaxPlayers 0x1260A0 -> LobbyParams_SetMaxPlayers(sub_47E350(), n)
    SetGamePartyMaxPlayers    0x1261E0 -> LobbyParams_SetMaxPlayers(Lobby_Get(0), n)

    sub_47E350() = sub_470F20(Lobby_Get(2))                     -> LOBBY 2
    sub_470CB0() = (!dword_8EFCBC0 || (dword_8D6C490 && sub_481690(&off_8BE6040)))
                     ? &off_8BE6040 : &off_8D76770              -> lobby 0 or 1

**The private-match menu writes LOBBY 2.** force_host was latching lobby 0 only, so a
private match reading lobby 2 would never see our value — a live suspect for asking
24v24 and getting 9v9. FIXED in build 251E9D73: min/max are now latched on all three,
and `fh_bots` prints all three so which one binds is visible rather than assumed.

### PROVEN — no clamp anywhere in the write path

`LobbyParams_SetMaxPlayers(a1, n)` is literally `*(DWORD*)(a1 + 596) = n`. None of the
LUI setters clamp either. So any cap is in the Lua slider, exactly as with the bot count.

### PROVEN — every writer of params[1], i.e. everything that can reset it

xrefs to LobbyParams_SetMaxPlayers (0x1973D0):

    0x080120  sub_7FE60        (also calls Playlist_ApplyToLobby)
    0x126041  SetPartyMaxPlayers          (LUI)
    0x126104  SetPrivatePartyMaxPlayers   (LUI)
    0x126253  SetGamePartyMaxPlayers      (LUI)
    0x28D510  sub_28D340       (the privateEscape path)
    0x477709  sub_476D70
    0x48E95E  sub_48E8xx
    0x4929D7  sub_491DE0       <- SESSION CREATE

plus `Party_SetLobbyParamFromCmd`, which writes params[1] for the console command
`party_maxplayers` — and that is how the PLAYLIST VAR-RULE BLOBS set it. So:

  **Playlist_ApplyToLobby resets it on every playlist apply**, to the playlist's own
  value (18 for the Ground War blobs, 12 for most, 32 for one, 4 for the small ones).

`Playlist_ParsePlaylists` (0x657270) is where those blob strings are BUILT — it formats
`"party_maxplayers "` + value while parsing downloaded playlist data (the format string
at 0xB96FF0 has exactly one code xref, into that function).

### CONSEQUENCE — this is precisely why the value must be LATCHED, not set once

Session create, every playlist apply, and three separate menu paths all rewrite it. A
one-shot write is guaranteed to be undone; the per-frame compare-then-write survives all
of them. That is the same reason the old tool needed its F4/F5 timing.

# ⭐⭐⭐ THE 18-PLAYER CAP IS sv_maxclients, NOT party_maxplayers (2026-08-11)

Measured LIVE with CE during the user's match (base verified per RULE A2:
`read_string(base + 0xBCE9E0)` == "EXE_ERR_PROCESS_DEMO_FILE_FAILED", base
0x7FF7A75A0000, so VA = base + IDA):

    lobby 0 (game)     + 596  party_maxplayers = 33
    lobby 1 (alt)      + 596  party_maxplayers = 33
    lobby 2 (private)  + 596  party_maxplayers = 33   <- our 3-lobby latch WORKS
    dword_C5FBA50            svs.clientCount  = 18   <- THE CAP
    dvar_sv_maxclients +16   sv_maxclients    = 18

(33 = 16 + 16 bots + 1, i.e. a value only force_host's own "raise to cover the bots"
arithmetic produces — which is how we know the latch was live.)

**So party_maxplayers was never the constraint, and every earlier hypothesis about it
was chasing a downstream value.**

## PROVEN — svs.clientCount has exactly TWO writers, both in SV_Init

`sub_6DCDB0` is SV_Init: it ends with `Dvar_SetBool(dvar_com_sv_running, 1)` and
allocates every server array. Instruction-level xref scan over the whole image finds
only these two writes to dword_C5FBA50:

    0x6DCE0F   mov cs:dword_C5FBA50, 30h        ; 48
    0x6DCE25   mov cs:dword_C5FBA50, ecx

and in context:

    sub_6DA7A0(1);                              // "raise sv_maxclients to >= 1", a no-op
    if ( !HIBYTE(word_1BD36F8) || sub_B8CB0() )
        dword_C5FBA50 = *((DWORD*)dvar_sv_maxclients + 4);   // a normal match
    else
        dword_C5FBA50 = 48;                                   // <- THE HUB's 48
    ...
    qword_C5FBA58 = alloc(1173616 * dword_C5FBA50);           // svs.clients
    (and ~12 more arrays all sized from dword_C5FBA50)

⭐ That `else` branch is why the hub shows 48 while a match shows 18. The hub is not
"expanding" anything — it takes the constant branch.

## ⛔ CORRECTION — the dependency runs the OTHER way

I assumed party_maxplayers fed sv_maxclients. `sub_7FE60` shows the reverse:

    if ( ((dword_D8AF894 - 2) & 0xFFFFFFFB) == 0 && sub_480F20(lobby) )
        LobbyParams_SetMaxPlayers(lobby, *((DWORD*)dvar_sv_maxclients + 4));

**party_maxplayers is set FROM sv_maxclients.** sv_maxclients is upstream of the lobby
param, of svs.clientCount, and of every server array.

Also checked and NOT the source of the 18: no playlist or gametype var-rule blob sets
"2299" — zero occurrences of the token anywhere in .rdata. Whatever lowers it from its
registered default of 48 has not been identified, and does not need to be: the latch
below puts it back before SV_Init reads it.

## THE FIX — build EC62C250 (deployed, hash-verified)

Latch dvar **"2299"** (sv_maxclients) to the configured max, issued through Cbuf the way
the engine sets its own numeric dvars in playlist blobs ("2507 1", "2103 -1", ...).

⚠ **GATED ON `!com_sv_running`, and that gate is not optional.** svs.clientCount is
allocated ONCE at SV_Init. Raising sv_maxclients afterwards, while svs.clients is still
the smaller allocation, is the crash already documented in this file:
`SV_ChangeMaxClients` does `memset(qword_C5FBA58, 0, 1173616 * sv_maxclients)` over the
older array. MWR carries the assert `sv_maxclients <= svs.clientCount`
(sv_init_mp.cpp:1061); S2 ships without it and corrupts the heap instead.

So it must be set IN THE MENU, before the map loads — which is what the latch does by
itself. `fh_bots` now also reports svs.clientCount and serverRunning, and calls out
svs.clientCount explicitly when that is the binding constraint.

New reads: `svs_client_count()` (dword_C5FBA50) and `server_running()`
(dvar_com_sv_running at IDA 0x1BD3778, value at +16).

## METHOD NOTE

Three rounds of static reasoning about party_maxplayers were wrong; one CE read of three
addresses settled it in a minute. When a value is observable live, read it before
theorising about which of several candidates holds it — the doctrine's own
"measure state, don't follow code" lesson, re-learned.

## ⛔⛔ "Memory Error: 6 161" — RAISING sv_maxclients IS FATAL (2026-08-11)

The sv_maxclients latch from build EC62C250 killed the game on match start:

    Fatal Error: Memory Error: 6 161

**A regression I introduced.** Default is now OFF (build DC89BCC4).

### PROVEN — those two numbers name the exact instruction

`"Memory Error: %d %d"` @ IDA 0xB4F418 has ONE xref, and the only site in the whole
image that passes (6, 161) is the server-hunk allocator:

    sub_287740(hunk, size, align):          <- the hunk allocator
        newTop = alignUp(hunk[2], align) + size;
        if (newTop > hunk[1])               // beyond committed
        {
            if (newTop > hunk[0])           // beyond RESERVED
                sub_287720(6, 161);         // -> DB_RaiseAssetLimitError("Memory Error: %d %d", 6, 161)
            ... commit more pages ...
        }
        hunk[2] = newTop;

    hunk[0] = reserved ceiling, hunk[1] = committed, hunk[2] = current top

So it is not an asset limit at all despite going through DB_RaiseAssetLimitError — it is
`g_serverHunkUser` running out of RESERVED address space.

### PROVEN — the hunk is reserved IN ADVANCE from a client count, and it is QUADRATIC

`sub_6DA5F0` sizes and creates it (`sub_2877D0(size, "g_serverHunkUser", 9)`), with a3 =
the client count and the same shape SV_Init then allocates by:

    v7 += ((144*a4 + 127) & ~127)
        + ((2544*a3 + 127) & ~127)
        + ((81408*a3 + 2671) & ~127)
        + ((1173616*a3 + 127) & ~127)
        + ((328*a3*a3 + 127) & ~127)
        + a3 * (11136*a3 + ((sub_769580() + 48 + 4*v12) << 8))
        + v14                                  // 65486080 or 128916736, by mode
        + v12*v13                              // v12 = 512 or 1024
        + 393216*a3;
    hunk = sub_2877D0((v7 + 0xFFFF) & 0xFFFF0000, "g_serverHunkUser", 9);

Dominant terms ~ 11464*N^2 + 1650784*N, i.e. roughly **33 MB at N=18 and 106 MB at
N=48** on top of the fixed base. So raising sv_maxclients from 18 to 48 makes SV_Init
ask for ~72 MB more than was ever reserved, and the first oversized allocation aborts.

### WHY IT CANNOT SIMPLY BE FIXED

The RESERVATION has to agree with the value SV_Init allocates by, and the reservation's
caller is behind an Arxan thunk — `DB_Thread` @0xACE30 is `JUMPOUT(0xFFFFFFFFFFFF0D13)`
— so what a3 is passed is NOT statically visible (RULE A5). Until that is established,
raising sv_maxclients is a fatal change and not a tuning knob.

### SHIPPED — build DC89BCC4 (deployed, hash-verified)

  * `g_raise_svmax` DEFAULT FALSE. The latch only runs when explicitly enabled with
    `fh_svmaxclients 1`, and enabling it prints the failure mode. The GUI checkbox is
    labelled EXPERIMENTAL - can be fatal.
  * NEW `fh_hunk`: reads the hunk header live (reserved / committed / top / free in MB)
    plus svs.clientCount and sv_maxclients — so the real headroom can be MEASURED before
    anyone tries a smaller bump. A raise of 20 or 24 may well fit where 48 does not, and
    now that is answerable instead of guessable.

### What stands from the previous entry

Everything except the fix. The 18-player cap IS sv_maxclients -> svs.clientCount (that
was measured live and remains true); what is now also known is that the server hunk is
sized for the same number in advance, so the two must be raised together or not at all.

Named this session: SV_Init (0x6DCDB0), SV_RaiseMaxClients (0x6DA7A0),
svs_clientCount (0xC5FBA50), svs_clients (0xC5FBA58).

## ⛔ CLOSED — MORE THAN 18 PLAYERS IS NOT REACHABLE FROM THE CLIENT (2026-08-11)

Filed under Failed Attempt Protection. **Do not re-run this without new evidence**, and
"new evidence" here means specifically: a way to reach SV_CreateServerHunk's caller.

**Attempt.** Raise the player count above 18 for a hosted / private match, so 24v24 bots
would fit.

**Result.** Every route ends at the same place, and the one that reaches it is fatal
(`Fatal Error: Memory Error: 6 161` on match start).

**Reason — the chain, all proven this session:**

    party_maxplayers (lobby params[1], all 3 lobbies)   NOT the cap
        - measured live at 33 while the match ran 18
        - sub_7FE60 sets it FROM sv_maxclients, so it is downstream
    Bots_SetTeamLimit / the GSC reader                   NOT the cap
        - no native clamp; sub_6C7050 hands the script our byte unclamped
    svs_clientCount                                      <- THE CAP
        - SV_Init (sub_6DCDB0) is its ONLY writer, two instructions
        - svs_clientCount = sv_maxclients (or the constant 48 on the hub branch)
        - svs_clients = Hunk_Alloc(1173616 * svs_clientCount), + ~12 more arrays
    sv_maxclients                                        raising it is FATAL
        - SV_CreateServerHunk reserves g_serverHunkUser IN ADVANCE from a client
          count, QUADRATICALLY (~33 MB at 18, ~106 MB at 48)
        - SV_Init then allocates for OUR N out of a hunk sized for the engine's N
        - the first oversized allocation hits Hunk_Alloc's
          `if (newTop > hunk[0]) Hunk_RaiseMemoryError(6, 161)`
    SV_CreateServerHunk's caller                         NOT REACHABLE
        - DB_Thread @0xACE30 is JUMPOUT(0xFFFFFFFFFFFF0D13), an Arxan thunk
        - so what client count it is passed is not statically visible (RULE A5)

So the single value that would have to change to make this work is the one value the
Arxan wall hides. 18 is not an oversight — the entire server allocation is dimensioned
for it, and the hub's 48 comes from a hardcoded constant on a different branch of
SV_Init, not from any expansion.

**What would reopen it, and nothing less:** establishing what SV_CreateServerHunk is
passed, i.e. getting past DB_Thread's thunk. A runtime breakpoint on SV_CreateServerHunk
capturing a3 and the return address is the only cheap route, and it is a probe.

**Left in the code, deliberately:** `fh_svmaxclients` (default OFF, labelled fatal) and
`fh_hunk` (reads the live hunk header). If anyone ever wants to test whether a SMALL bump
fits inside the existing reservation -- 20 or 24 has a quarter the quadratic cost of 48 --
fh_hunk makes that arithmetic instead of a guess. Nothing else in force_host depends on
either, and both are no-ops by default.

    Playlist_ApplyToLobby as the automatic apply path                  CONFIRMED
    correct playlist NAME in game (params[11] + playlist_name dvar)    shipped
    bot count per team, under the LUI slider's cap                     shipped
    DLC toggle, zero-hook server browser                               shipped

force_host is ZERO HOOKS. The 18-player ceiling is the only part of the original goal
