# ⭐⭐⭐ IWXMVM's REWIND/FAST-FORWARD DESIGN, AND THE HALF S2 WAS MISSING (2026-08-11)

Studied `reallyluckyy/IWXMVM` (IW3 + IW5) at the user's request and ported the part S2
lacked. Source read: `core/src/Components/Rewinding.cpp`, `Playback.cpp`, and
`iw5/src/Hooks/Playback.cpp`.

## Their architecture, in full — worth keeping even for the parts we did not use

1. **They own the demo file cursor.** `CL_Demo_ReadInternal(handle, buffer, len)` and
   `CL_Demo_SeekFile(handle, offset, origin)` are hooked; if the handle is the demo's
   they serve the read from their OWN `std::ifstream` instead. Everything else follows
   from controlling that cursor.

2. **`StoreCurrentGamestate(len)`** — while reading, they latch a restore point at the
   moment after the gamestate is installed and before the first snapshot:
   file offset, `clc.lastExecutedServerCommand`, `clc.serverCommandSequence`,
   `cgs.serverCommandSequence`, `clc.serverConfigDataSequence`, the whole `clientInfo`
   array and the whole `gameState`. Then `serverTime` after the first snapshot.
   They detect the gamestate message crudely, by `len >= 10000`.

3. **`RestoreOldGamestate()`** — fires on the next ONE-BYTE read (the packet-type byte)
   when a rewind is pending:
       ResetClientData(serverTime)   // all snapshots invalid; cl.serverTime,
                                     // oldFrameServerTime, serverTimeDelta, cls.realtime,
                                     // cgs.processedSnapshotNum, cg.latestSnapshotNum/
                                     // Time/snap/nextSnap/landTime all zeroed
       CL_FirstSnapshot()
       seek the file back to the stored offset
       zero cl.parseEntitiesNum / parseClientsNum
       restore the three command sequences
       memset clc.serverCommands (128 KB), cg_entities, s_compassActors, teamChatMsgs
       memcpy back clientInfo and gameState
   then flips to SKIPPING_FORWARD.

4. **`SkipDemoForward(ticks)` — the entire fast-forward:**

       void SkipDemoForward(int32_t ticks) { *cls.realtime += ticks; }

5. **Rewind = restore to the demo's START, then fast-forward to the target.** There are
   NO keyframes anywhere in IWXMVM. It works because (4) is cheap.

6. `Com_TimeScaleMsec` is hooked to return a controlled per-frame msec — 0 pauses, and a
   generated 0/1 interleave pattern gives sub-1.0 timescales.

## ⭐ THE SAME MECHANISM IS IN S2, VERBATIM — CL_SetCGameTime @0x86D30

    v7 = cl.serverTimeDelta;                        // clientActive[6370]
    cl.serverTime = v7 + cls_realtime;              // [6368]
    if (cl.serverTime < cl.oldFrameServerTime)      // [6365]
        cl.serverTime = cl.oldFrameServerTime;      //   <- CLAMP
    cl.oldFrameServerTime = cl.serverTime;
    ...
    do {
        if (CL_Demo_IsCompleted()) break;
        if (cl.serverTime < cl.snap.serverTime      // [6345]
            && !CL_Demo_ShouldReadMultipleNonDeltaSnapshots(c)) break;
    } while (CL_Demo_ReadDemoMessage(c));

    cls_realtime   IDA 0x1C7E1F0   (already named in the IDB)

So `cl.serverTime` is DERIVED from `cls_realtime`, and the feed loop reads demo packets
until the demo catches up. **Raising cls_realtime by N ms advances playback by N ms
through the engine's own pump, with no keyframe involved.**

⚠ AND THE ENGINE EXPLAINS THE ASYMMETRY. The clamp against `oldFrameServerTime` means
LOWERING cls_realtime does nothing — the clamp pins serverTime at its old value. That is
exactly why IWXMVM restores a whole gamestate to rewind but needs one line to fast
forward. Backward is genuinely a different problem.

Note this is the NORMAL-play loop at 0x87011, which re-checks IsCompleted and the return
value every iteration — NOT the priming loop at 0x86D97 that caused the runaway recorded
earlier in this file. It terminates correctly at end of stream.

## WHAT S2 HAD, AND THE GAP

The mod already generates keyframes itself (sub_914790 on a 5 s cadence, because the
engine's own generation is gated on the clip-playing byte clc+262772 which nothing ever
sets) and drives ProcessKeyFrameJump for seeking. That makes REWIND work.

But keyframes are written as playback PASSES, so there is nothing ahead of where you have
already been — **forward seeking past the play head could not work, by construction.**
That is precisely the gap IWXMVM's technique closes.

## SHIPPED — build 511E1BF5 (deployed, hash-verified)

    demo_native::skip_forward_ms(ms)     cls_realtime += ms
    demo_skip <ms>                       console command, client thread
    seek_forward()                       now a +5000 ms realtime skip, not a keyframe jump
    seek_to_time(ms)                     forward  -> pure realtime skip
                                         backward -> keyframe jump, as before

`seek_to_time` is now IWXMVM's rewind-then-skip pattern with S2's keyframes standing in
for their gamestate restore: jump back to a keyframe BEFORE the target, then skip forward
the remainder to land exactly on it.

Guarded: forward only (a negative skip is refused with the reason), and a skip over 60 s
announces itself first, since it reads every packet in between within one frame.

## NOT PORTED, and why

The full gamestate restore (their items 1-3). S2's keyframes already give exact backward
seeking, and taking over the demo file cursor would mean hooking CL_Demo_Read @0x912260 —
which the theater's own read path also uses. If keyframe rewind ever proves insufficient
(e.g. seeking back before the first keyframe), their restore point is the blueprint and
S2's equivalents are already known: cls_gameState_stringOffsets/stringData @0x2489350 /
0x24900D8, clc+0x20144 serverCommandSequence, clc+0x2014C the 128x1024 command ring,
CL_FirstSnapshot @0x74910, and the clientActive dword indices listed above.

NOT YET TESTED IN GAME — a CANDIDATE per the Fix Declaration Rules.

## ⭐⭐ REWIND — DIAGNOSED FROM A LIVE RUN, plus Caball009's CoD4-X reference (2026-08-11)

### The measurement that cracked it

    [demo] jump slot 6: t=54350 fileOff=2240890 len=135678 cmdSeq=79 baseline=-1
    [demo] jump done: t 61450 -> 61500 (+50 ms)

  * the keyframe is GOOD — real time, file offset, 135678-byte payload, cmdSeq.
    So the keyframe writer works and the "empty ring" theory is dead.
  * `baseline = -1` is legal; the engine's own pattern is
    `if (b != -1 && b != kf) jump(b); jump(kf);`
  * +50 ms is ONE 20 Hz server frame, not a rewind.

### The call target is genuine — verified live, RULE A2 style

Read the bytes at `base + 0x917ED0` on the running game:
`40 55 53 56 57 41 54 41 55 41 56 41 57 48 8D 6C 24 E1 48 81 EC 88 00 00`
byte-for-byte identical to the IDB's ProcessKeyFrameJump prologue. So it is being
called, is not hooked by anything, and does run.

### ⛔ MY OWN BUG — PlaybackData+24 is a DWORD, not a QWORD

The first diagnostic printed `filePos=4575657221410973728`. That decodes as high dword
`0x3F800000` — the float 1.0, i.e. the TIMESCALE at PlaybackData+28 — with the real
cursor in the low dword. ProcessKeyFrameJump stores it as `mov [rax+18h], ecx`, a DWORD.

Decoded, the cursor went 2549792 -> 2552090. Fixed to a 32-bit read.

### THE MECHANISM

ProcessKeyFrameJump's tail:

    v39 = cl.snap.serverTime;                 // read AFTER the restore
    cl.oldFrameServerTime = cl.serverTime = cls_realtime = cl.oldServerTime = v39;
    cl.serverTimeDelta = cl.snap.serverTime - cls_realtime;
    CL_SetCGameTime(client);

It derives the whole clock FROM snap.serverTime. `*(DWORD*)(PlaybackData+24) = slot.fileOffset`
near the top is unconditional, so the file DOES seek back to 2240890 — but if the restore
does not itself land a snapshot at the keyframe's time, v39 is still NOW, the clock is set
to now, and the CL_SetCGameTime call at the tail replays forward again. That is why the
cursor reads 2552090 by the time we sample it and time moved +50 ms. Every number fits.

### ⭐ Caball009/Call-of-Duty-4-X-Demo-Rewinding — the reference that names the fix

Studied at the user's suggestion. It is a closer match to this problem than IWXMVM
because it rewinds to PERIODIC restore points rather than only to the demo start.

  * keeps a `std::stack<customSnapshot>`, one entry per `rewindTime` (default 1000 ms);
    rewind pops one, rewind-all pops to the bottom
  * saves what IWXMVM does NOT: the whole snapshot array, entities, clients,
    parseEntitiesNum/parseClientsNum, landTime, scores, the chat buffer, three server
    command sequences, and the gamestate
  * **`ResetOldClientData(serverTime)` WRITES `cl.snap.serverTime` from the restore
    point** and zeroes cl.serverTime / oldServerTime / oldFrameServerTime /
    serverTimeDelta / cls.realtime / the cg_t snapshot fields, then calls CL_FirstSnapshot

⭐ THE INVERSION IS THE POINT. S2 derives the clock FROM snap.serverTime; Caball009 SETS
snap.serverTime from the restore point. Ours can only work if the restore already put a
snapshot back.

⭐ AND IT NAMES WHAT BREAKS NEXT. Caball009 has to patch out three errors before time can
move backwards at all:

    0x45C511 "90 90"  cl->snap.serverTime < cl->oldFrameServerTime
    0x44E4B0 "EB"     CG_ProcessSnapshots: Server time went backwards
    0x44E2C3 "EB"     CG_ReadNextSnapshot: way out of range

**S2 has the first verbatim**: CL_SetCGameTime does
`if (cl.snap.serverTime < cl.oldServerTime) Com_Error(1, "440")`, already decoded in this
file. S2 has a built-in escape the CoD4 one lacks — it only errors when the server name
is not "localhost", otherwise it calls CL_FirstSnapshot — but the safe route is to move
oldServerTime WITH the rest rather than patch the check out.

Also matching: its restore point is `fileOffset = cursor - 9`, and 9 = 1 type byte + 4
sequence + 4 length — exactly S2's type-2 packet framing.

### SHIPPED — build 81C1E903 (deployed, hash-verified). NOT yet tested.

After ProcessKeyFrameJump returns, force the clock onto the KEYFRAME's own time
(slot+8), writing the same five fields the engine's own tail writes:

    clientActive[6345] snap.serverTime      = kfTime   <- the one the tail reads
    clientActive[6365] oldFrameServerTime   = kfTime
    clientActive[6368] serverTime           = kfTime
    clientActive[6369] oldServerTime        = kfTime   <- keeps Com_Error "440" satisfied
    cls_realtime                            = kfTime
    clientActive[6370] serverTimeDelta      = 0

Nothing is invented: every field is one ProcessKeyFrameJump already writes, with the value
it should have had. Toggle `demo_seek_forceclock 0` reverts to the engine's tail.

Diagnostics kept: the slot's replay range (slot+32/+36, flagged EMPTY when equal), and
snapT/cursor before and after, so if this is still not enough the next line says why.

# ⭐⭐⭐ DOLLY CAMERA — EVERY PIECE LOCATED (2026-08-11). Implementation next.

User: "add the dollycam! this is why we needed rewind, I need markers and points, same
method, but not imgui driven, game driven drawing, properly scaled".

Rewind is confirmed working, so the prerequisite is done. Below is everything the dolly
needs, all found and cross-checked. NOTHING IS IMPLEMENTED YET — this is the map.

## 1. THE THEATER FREE CAMERA STATE — capture AND drive

`sub_913AE0` (the fly camera, reached from CG_PredictPlayerState when
CG_IsTheaterOrbitCamera) works entirely in `CG_GetLocalClientGlobals(client)` (cg),
addressed as FLOATS:

    cg[588912..588914]   ORIGIN     (byte offset 2355648)
    cg[588915..588917]   ANGLES     (byte offset 2355660)  pitch, yaw, roll
    cg[588918..588920]   VELOCITY   (byte offset 2355672)

Proven from the function's own body: it damps [588918..588920] as a velocity vector
(fsqrt of the sum of squares, friction, clamp), writes [588915..588917] from the
usercmd's angle shorts (`(v * 0.0054931641) * 0.0027777778` then `* 360.0` — the classic
SHORT2ANGLE), and passes `v6 + 588915` to sub_75EC50 (AngleVectors) to build the movement
basis. `sub_9140A0(client)` then integrates the position with a trace.

So: READ these to capture a dolly point, WRITE them to drive the camera. Zero the
velocity when driving or the engine's friction will fight the path.

⚠ Write AFTER sub_9140A0 has run for the frame, or the integrator overwrites it.

Camera mode selector: `sub_91AB50(client, mode)` 0/1/2; mode 2 is the fly camera and
CG_IsTheaterOrbitCamera (0x916DE0) tests == 2. Cycled by CL_Demo_HandleAction case 4/168.

## 2. WORLD -> SCREEN PROJECTION — "properly scaled"

Found via the LUI binding `WorldToScreenPosition` (string 0xB3F458, table entry 0xB3A550,
fn sub_12AFC0). Its core is:

    view = sub_4A0170(localClientNum);          // the refdef / view object
    sub_3E6250(localClientNum, view, worldPos /*float[3]*/, outScreenXY /*float[2]*/);
    sub_3F8D00(...)                             // clamp / offscreen handling
    sub_7B0B0(&screenW, &screenH, ...)          // screen dimensions

**`sub_3E6250` is the projection.** That is what makes markers sit correctly in the world
at any FOV/resolution, rather than being faked with an ImGui overlay.

## 3. GAME-DRIVEN DRAWING — already wired up in this repo

The mod already resolves the engine's own 2D primitives (src/FuncPointers.h):

    Functions::_R_AddCmdDrawStretchPic(x, y, w, h, s0, t0, s1, t1, float* color, Material*)
    Functions::_R_AddCmdDrawText(text, maxChars, font_t*, 0, 0, font->pixelHeight,
                                 x, y, xScale, yScale, rotation, float* color, style)
    Functions::_R_RegisterFont(name, size)        e.g. "fonts/fira_mono_regular.ttf"
    InternalConsole::getMaterialWhite()            a white material for solid quads

So markers = projected point + a stretch-pic quad whose SIZE scales with distance, and
path segments = thin rotated quads between consecutive projected points. No ImGui.

## 4. THE DRAW HOOK — do NOT add a second one (RULE A3.1)

`R_EndFrame` is ALREADY hooked, at `0x8BACD0_b`, in src/InternalConsole.cpp:

    void R_EndFrame_hookfunc() { ... if (intConReady) drawConsole(); _EndFrame(); }

and `drawConsole()` calls `DevDraw::render(windowWidth, windowHeight)`. That is the
correct, proven place for game-driven drawing — render thread, end of frame, where the
R_AddCmd* calls are valid. The dolly draw must be called from that existing stub, not
from a new hook and NOT from the DXGI Present thread (where demo_gui runs).

## 5. WHAT ALREADY EXISTS IN THE TREE

`src/demo/theater_camera.hpp` already declares the shape, for the CUSTOM theater:

    enum camera_mode { FIRST_PERSON, THIRD_PERSON, FREECAM, DOLLY };
    struct camera_pose_t     { float pos[3]; float angles[3]; float fov; };
    struct camera_keyframe_t { int32_t demo_time; camera_pose_t pose; };
    get_keyframes() / get_mode() / set_mode()

The data model can be reused; what is missing is the NATIVE-playback binding (the cg
offsets above), the projection, the drawing, and interpolation.

## 6. DESIGN THAT FOLLOWS FROM THIS

  * point = { demo_time, pos[3], angles[3], fov }, kept sorted by demo_time
  * demo_time from demo_native::current_demo_time(), which is the same clock the
    keyframe ring uses (cl.snap.serverTime), so points line up with seeking
  * interpolate position with Catmull-Rom across 4 neighbours; angles with
    shortest-arc lerp (normalise each delta to [-180,180] first, or yaw wraps badly)
  * drive: while playing, set cg origin/angles from the interpolated pose and zero the
    velocity, every frame, after sub_9140A0
  * draw: project every point with sub_3E6250; marker quad size ~ k / distance; join
    consecutive samples of the interpolated curve with thin quads; label each point with
    its index and time via R_AddCmdDrawText
  * the ImGui panel stays for EDITING (add/delete/retime), but nothing is drawn there —
    the viewport visualisation is entirely engine-rendered, as asked

## 7. NAMED IN THE S2 IDB (saved) — use these, not the sub_ names above

    0x913AE0  CL_Demo_FreeCameraMove          (commented: the three cg float triples)
    0x9135D0  CL_Demo_FollowCameraMove
    0x9140A0  CL_Demo_FreeCameraIntegrate     position integrator + trace
    0x91AB50  CL_Demo_SetCameraMode(client, 0|1|2)
    0x916DE0  CG_IsTheaterOrbitCamera         (already named) tests mode == 2
    0x3E6250  CG_WorldPosToScreenPos          (commented: THE projection)
    0x4A0170  CG_GetRefdefView                (commented)
    0x12AFC0  LUI_WorldToScreenPosition       the binding that led to both

## 8. ⚠ ADDRESS ARITHMETIC, DONE ONCE (RULE A1 — do not redo this in your head)

`_b` literal = IDA − 0x1000.  Runtime VA = module_base + IDA.

    CL_Demo_FreeCameraMove       0x913AE0 - 0x1000 = 0x912AE0
    CL_Demo_FreeCameraIntegrate  0x9140A0 - 0x1000 = 0x9130A0
    CL_Demo_FollowCameraMove     0x9135D0 - 0x1000 = 0x9125D0
    CG_WorldPosToScreenPos       0x3E6250 - 0x1000 = 0x3E5250
    CG_GetRefdefView             0x4A0170 - 0x1000 = 0x49F170
    CL_Demo_SetCameraMode        0x91AB50 - 0x1000 = 0x919B50
    CG_IsTheaterOrbitCamera      0x916DE0 - 0x1000 = 0x915DE0
    AngleVectors (sub_75EC50)    0x75EC50 - 0x1000 = 0x75DC50
    sub_3F8D00 clamp/offscreen   0x3F8D00 - 0x1000 = 0x3F7D00
    sub_7B0B0  screen dims       0x7B0B0  - 0x1000 = 0x7A0B0
    CG_PredictPlayerState        0x4EFA0  - 0x1000 = 0x4DFA0
    R_EndFrame                   already a literal, 0x8BACD0_b  (IDA 0x8BBCD0)

cg float indices as BYTE offsets, so a `char*` walk needs no multiply:

    ORIGIN    588912 * 4 = 2355648
    ANGLES    588915 * 4 = 2355660
    VELOCITY  588918 * 4 = 2355672

Camera mode field: PlaybackData + 6297228 (0 first / 1 third / 2 fly).

## 9. ⛔ DO NOT CALL CG_GetLocalClientGlobals — ARXAN RETADDR CHECK

demo_game.hpp:348-362 already carries this, learned the hard way:

    // NEVER call addr_CG_GetLocalClientGlobals() from the mod — Arxan retaddr checks
    // infinite-loop when the caller is outside the game image (ACTIVE DrawActiveFrame freeze).

Use the existing accessor instead, which derives cg from the RENDERER BACK-POINTER
and needs no engine call at all:

    void* cg = demo_game::cg_globals_for(0);
        renderer_data = *(uintptr_t*)0x8AFBB38_b
        cg = (char*)(renderer_data - 0x1E6C10) + 4441600 * client
        returns nullptr when rd == 0 or rd < 0x1E6C10

⚠ The back-pointer is often UNSET at CG_DrawActiveFrame *enter* — read it AFTER the
original runs. Every existing caller in demo_playback.cpp already does.

## 10. ⛔ CORRECTION — `demo_native::current_demo_time()` DOES NOT EXIST

I asserted it did. It does not; demo_native.hpp has no such export. What exists is a
LOCAL lambda inside jump_to_slot (demo_native.cpp ~line 370):

    ca = CL_GetLocalClientActive(cl)          // _b(0x785D0), IDA 0x795D0
    time = *(int32_t*)(ca + 6345 * 4)         // cl.snap.serverTime

So the dolly needs that promoted to an exported accessor (say
`demo_native::demo_time()`), reusing the same clientActive dword. 6345 is already
proven — it is the field ProcessKeyFrameJump's tail reads and the one the rewind fix
writes. Related indices, all established:

    6345 snap.serverTime   6365 oldFrameServerTime   6368 serverTime
    6369 oldServerTime     6370 serverTimeDelta      cls_realtime IDA 0x1C7E1F0

## 11. WHERE TO WRITE THE CAMERA, EXACTLY

CG_PredictPlayerState @0x4EFA0 routes the theater camera:

    if (CG_IsTheaterFreeCamera(c) || CG_IsTheaterOrbitCamera(c)) {
        ... newest usercmd from clientActive+25928 (ring, & 0x7F) ...
        if (CG_IsTheaterOrbitCamera(c)) { CL_Demo_FreeCameraMove(c, cmd); return 0; }
        CL_Demo_FollowCameraMove(c, cmd); return 0;
    }

CL_Demo_FreeCameraMove applies friction/acceleration to VELOCITY and reads the
usercmd angles; CL_Demo_FreeCameraIntegrate then integrates ORIGIN with a trace.

So the dolly must write ORIGIN+ANGLES and ZERO VELOCITY *after* the integrator, or
the engine's own physics fights the path. Two candidate sites, in order of
preference:

  (a) hook CL_Demo_FreeCameraIntegrate (0x9140A0 - 0x1000 = 0x9130A0), call the
      original, then overwrite — the tightest possible placement, and RULE A3.1
      checked: nothing in src/ hooks it today.
  (b) write from the existing R_EndFrame stub, which is after everything. Simpler,
      but a frame of camera lag is possible.

Prefer (a). If it misbehaves, (b) is the fallback and costs nothing to try.


# ⭐⭐⭐ DOLLY CAMERA — BUILT (2026-08-11, build 5A0EA84B)

New module `src/demo/dolly.{hpp,cpp}`. Deployed and hash-verified. NOT yet run
in game, so per the Fix Declaration Rules this is a CANDIDATE, not "works".

Points are stamped with the DEMO clock (cl.snap.serverTime, the same timebase
the keyframe ring uses), so seeking, rewind, pause and timescale move the dolly
with no extra machinery — **to whatever extent those work; see the rewind
correction below**. The camera is driven only across the points' own time span
and is free outside it, which is what makes "fly, add a point, fly on" work as
an editing loop.

## ⛔ CORRECTION — REWIND WAS NEVER CONFIRMED. Two claims conflicted and I
## repeated the wrong one (2026-08-11)

The now-deleted session-handoff block asserted "Last deployed build 81C1E903 =
the rewind clock inversion, **CONFIRMED working in game**". The rewind section
itself, thirty lines above it, ends "**SHIPPED — build 81C1E903 (deployed,
hash-verified). NOT yet tested.**" Both cannot be true. I took the handoff line
at face value and carried it into this section.

USER REPORT 2026-08-11, on the first real exercise of it (the dolly's "Go"
button, which is a plain `seek_to_time`): rewind does NOT work.

So the honest state is: **the clock-force fix in jump_to_slot is UNVERIFIED and
probably insufficient.** Everything downstream that assumed a working rewind —
including this dolly section's "seek back to point 1 and watch it drive" test —
is provisional until that is settled.

The good news is that no new instrumentation is needed. `jump_to_slot` already
reports unconditionally (RULE A15), so ONE press produces the whole picture:

    [demo] seek -> N ms: keyframe slot S (t=..), from M ms
    [demo] jump slot S: t=.. fileOff=.. len=.. cmdSeq=.. replay=[a..b] baseline=..
    [demo]   before: demoT=.. snapT=.. cursor=..
    [demo]   clock forced to keyframe t=.. (snap/old/serverTime/cls_realtime), delta=0
    [demo]   after : demoT=.. snapT=.. cursor=..   (demoT +N, snapT +N, cursor +N)
    [demo]   snap.serverTime did NOT go back -> ...        (only when it did not)

Read `replay=[a..b]`: **EMPTY (a == b) means the keyframe restores no snapshot**,
which is the documented cause of the original "+50 ms and back where we started"
symptom — the tail then derives the clock from the CURRENT snap.serverTime.

## ⚠ A COMMENT/CODE DISCREPANCY FOUND WHILE CHECKING THIS

`seek_to_time`'s comment claims the backward path is "keyframe jump to a point
BEFORE the target, **then skip forward the remainder, which lands exactly on
it**". The code does not do the second half: `demo_seek <ms>` picks the nearest
usable keyframe at or before the target and calls `jump_to_slot`, full stop. So
a backward seek lands on the KEYFRAME, up to the keyframe cadence (~5 s) earlier
than asked.

That is a landing-precision bug, not the reason rewind appears dead — landing
early would look like over-rewinding, not like not moving. Recorded so the two
are not confused, and so nobody trusts the comment.

Markers and the path are drawn BY THE GAME — projected with the engine's own
CG_WorldPosToScreenPos and drawn with R_AddCmdDrawStretchPic / R_AddCmdDrawText
from the EXISTING R_EndFrame hook. ImGui (the "Dolly" tab) only edits the list.

## ⛔ TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE PLAN, both found by decompiling BEFORE writing code

**1. "Hook CL_Demo_FreeCameraIntegrate" would NEVER HAVE FIRED.** The plan named
0x9140A0 as the place to write the camera pose. CL_Demo_FreeCameraMove @0x913AE0
opens with

    if (playbackData && (clc[+262772] || playbackData[3336304] == 3))
        return CL_Demo_InterpolateCameraPose(client);      // <- native playback

and `playbackData[3336304] == 3` IS "a demo is playing" (already recorded in this
file as the playback mode field). Only the OTHER branch calls the integrator, and
xrefs confirm CL_Demo_FreeCameraMove is its sole caller. So during native playback
the integrator is unreachable.

FIX: hook **CL_Demo_FreeCameraMove** itself (IDA 0x913AE0 - 0x1000 = 0x912AE0).
Its two branches write the same three cg fields, so writing after the original
covers both without caring which ran. RULE A3.1 checked — nothing else in src/
hooks it, and the trampoline is null-checked, not just the bool.

**2. sub_917240 IS ALREADY A CAMERA INTERPOLATOR** — named this session
`CL_Demo_InterpolateCameraPose`. It lerps a stored pose pair out of PlaybackData
into the freecam fields, using AngleNormalize180 on the angles, i.e. the engine
already does shortest-arc angle interpolation for its own clip camera:

    frac = cg[498397]                     (byte 1993588)
    +5439296..+5439316   TARGET pose      +5439324..+5439344  PREVIOUS pose
    +5439348 byte        snap flag: prev := target, then clear

Feeding that pair would be the elegant way to drive a camera. **We deliberately do
not**: nothing establishes who owns it or when it is written, and the doctrine
forbids writing a native field on that basis. We let it run and overwrite the
RESULT — the same fields the engine's own camera functions write, at the same
point in the frame.

## PROVEN — the cg camera fields, each cross-checked twice

    cg + 2355648   freecam ORIGIN     float[3]   (float index 588912)
    cg + 2355660   freecam ANGLES     float[3]   (float index 588915)
    cg + 2355672   freecam VELOCITY   float[3]   (float index 588918)
    cg + 1993796   refdef VIEW ORIGIN float[3]   (float index 498449)

CL_Demo_FreeCameraMove damps [588918..920] as a velocity and writes [588915..917]
from the usercmd angle shorts. Independently, **CL_Demo_SetCameraMode(client, 2)
does `cg[588912..914] = cg[498449..451]`** — seeding the freecam from the refdef
view origin — which pins BOTH triples in one statement. The refdef origin is also
exactly what CG_WorldPosToScreenPos subtracts to build its view direction.

VELOCITY must be zeroed when driving: it is the only field that accumulates
across frames, so leaving it would have the engine's own friction fighting the
path. Origin and angles are recomputed from scratch every frame, so overwriting
them accumulates nothing.

Camera mode: playbackData + 6297228 (0/1/2). CG_IsTheaterOrbitCamera tests == 2,
and mode 2 is the ONLY mode CG_PredictPlayerState routes to
CL_Demo_FreeCameraMove — so the dolly drives, and captures, in free camera only.

## ⭐ PROVEN — the projection, and why it needs no scaling fudge

    CG_WorldPosToScreenPos(int localClientNum, refdefView*, const float world[3],
                           float outScreenXY[2]) -> char

  * arg2 is typed `int` by IDA but IS the CG_GetRefdefView pointer (the call site
    does `a2 + 32` and hands it to a float* — the viewport width/height pair).
  * RETURN: only AL is defined (it tail-returns CG_ProjectViewDirToScreenPos's
    `char`). 1 = in front, 0 = behind — and when behind it STILL writes clamped
    edge coordinates, so the return value is the only way to reject the point.
    RULE A17: declaring it wider reads register residue.
  * OUTPUT SPACE: refdef viewport pixels. LUI_WorldToScreenPosition normalises by
    GetRenderTargetDimensions, which reads **g_renderTargetWidth /
    g_renderTargetHeight (IDA 0x1C86268 / 0x1C8626C)** — the SAME two globals
    `InternalConsole::drawConsole` already uses as its draw-space window size.
    So the projection's output is directly usable as R_AddCmdDraw* coordinates.
    That is an independent confirmation, from two unrelated call sites, and it is
    why "properly scaled" costs nothing here.

Calling it from the mod is safe despite it calling CG_GetLocalClientGlobals
internally: the Arxan retaddr check applies to the IMMEDIATE caller, which is the
game image. The standing ban is on the mod calling CG_GetLocalClientGlobals
DIRECTLY, and that is respected — we use demo_game::cg_globals_for(0).

Marker size is measured, not guessed: project the point and a second point one
world radius above it, and use the pixel distance between them. That tracks FOV
and resolution automatically. R_AddCmdDrawStretchPic has NO rotation parameter,
so there is no line primitive — the path is drawn as dense dots along the curve
(sample count capped at 400, so the per-frame draw cost is bounded).

## New in demo_native (exported for the dolly, no new hooks)

    int  demo_time()            cl.snap.serverTime — the existing seek clock
    int  camera_mode()          playbackData + 6297228
    bool set_camera_mode(int)   the engine's own CL_Demo_SetCameraMode @0x91AB50
                                (0x91AB50 - 0x1000 = 0x919B50)

## Commands and UI

    dolly                 status — ON/OFF, hook live/DEAD, every point, the span
    dolly_add             capture the current free-camera pose at the demo time
    dolly_del <n>         1-based
    dolly_clear
    dolly_on / dolly_off
    dolly_markers <0|1>

GUI: a "Dolly" tab — Add point / Clear, Drive the camera, Show markers, and a
per-point row with Go (seeks the demo there), Retime and X. It reports the camera

## WHAT TO CHECK IN GAME, in order

  1. Boot. Expect `[dolly] camera hook: OK (target=... orig=...)`. **A null orig
     with "OK" means MH_ERROR_ALREADY_CREATED** — RULE A3.1 — and the code already
     treats that as FAILED.
  2. `cl_demo_play airshipdemo`, then F2 until the camera is free.
  3. Fly somewhere, "Add point here". Fly elsewhere, seek forward, add another.
     Expect `[dolly] added point at N ms ...` and markers to APPEAR IN THE WORLD
     at those spots, shrinking with distance.
  4. First frame that draws prints ONE line: `[dolly] projection live: point 0 ->
     screen (x, y) in front, screen WxH, viewport scale 1.000/1.000`. If the scale
     is not ~1.0 the refdef viewport differs from the render target — the code
     already compensates, but it is worth knowing.
  5. Tick "Drive the camera" and seek back before the first point: the camera
     should be free, then take over as the demo enters the span.

If markers draw but the camera does not move, the hook is installed and the
projection works, so the fault is in drive() or the mode — `dolly` reports both.
If NOTHING draws, check that line 4 ever printed: it is the one-shot that
separates "projection failed" from "markers are off-screen".

## Deliberately NOT done

  * No separate dolly clock. The demo clock is the point.
  * No FOV keying. theater_camera::camera_pose_t has an fov field, but nothing has
    established which field the native path reads for FOV, and guessing it would
    be an offset guess. dolly::point_t carries position and angles only.
  * theater_camera.{hpp,cpp} is untouched — it belongs to the custom theater,
    which CLAUDE.md records as due for retirement.

# ⭐⭐ RULE A21 — NEVER VALIDATE POINTER A THEN CALL A FUNCTION THAT RESOLVES B
# (2026-08-11. Cost: a crash to desktop on the first run of the dolly.)

Minidump, read first per RULE A13, named it in one line:

    exception 0xC0000005 ACCESS_VIOLATION
    fault at   IDA_0x3E628E          (inside CG_WorldPosToScreenPos, 0x3E6250)
    tried to   READ from 0x1E6C44    unmapped
    0x1E6C44 == 1993796 == the refdef view origin offset

CG_WorldPosToScreenPos opens:

    3e627b  call CG_GetLocalClientGlobals
    3e6280  movss xmm4, dword ptr [rbx]
    3e628e  subss xmm4, dword ptr [rax+1E6C44h]      <- NO NULL CHECK

So when cg is not up it dereferences NULL + 1993796. **The engine does not guard
its own accessor's result**, and this is not the only such call site.

## Why my guard did not help — the actual lesson

dolly::render validated `demo_game::cg_globals_for(0)` and then called
CG_WorldPosToScreenPos. Those resolve cg from **two different sources**:

    demo_game::cg_globals_for   *(0x8AFBB38) - 0x1E6C10   the RENDERER back-pointer
    CG_GetLocalClientGlobals    g_cg_encrypted, decrypted  the engine's own

They genuinely disagreed: the back-pointer was stale-but-set while the engine's
was NULL. Validating one says nothing about the other.

**RULE: if you validate a pointer and then call an engine function, that function
must not resolve the same object independently. Either pass your validated
pointer in, or call the leaf that takes it as an argument.**

## The window this opens, and why a seek is the trigger

ProcessKeyFrameJump memsets cls_gameState_stringOffsets (0x26D8C bytes),
re-runs CL_ParseConfigStrings_Internal, restores the 79,356-byte state block and
replays buffered messages. cgame is DOWN across all of that, and render() runs on
the render thread meanwhile. So **pressing seek is what crashed it** — the
"rewind does not work" report and the crash are very likely one event.

## THE FIX (build 7C811B97) — own every pointer you dereference

We no longer call CG_WorldPosToScreenPos at all. Its body is 0x118 bytes and
fully decoded from the disassembly, so dolly.cpp inlines the wrapper and calls
only the LEAF, CG_ProjectViewDirToScreenPos @0x38EFD0, which touches nothing but
the pointers handed to it. Every operand below is read off the disassembly:

    cg + 0x1E6C30 (1993776)  float      tan half fov X   -> xmm3
    cg + 0x1E6C34 (1993780)  float      tan half fov Y   -> [rsp+20h]
    cg + 0x1E6C44 (1993796)  float[3]   view origin
    cg + 0x1E6C50 (1993808)  float[3][3] view axis       -> rcx
    refdef + 0x20            float[2]   viewport w/h     -> rdx

1993776..1993844 is contiguous, so ONE 68-byte readable() probe covers all four.
Arg slots: rcx, rdx, r8, xmm3, [rsp+0x20], [rsp+0x28] — matching the disassembly
exactly, and the return is `char` (RULE A17).

Four layers, in order of importance:
  1. the engine never resolves cg for us — the root fix;
  2. `demo_native::cgame_active()` (connstate >= 10) gates BOTH render() and
     drive(), which shuts us off across exactly the seek window;
  3. a sanity test on tan-half-fov and the viewport — a stale-but-mapped cg gives
     nonsense there, so it is refused rather than drawn;
  4. an SEH backstop around the leaf call, in a POD-only helper so __try is legal.
     A BACKSTOP, not the fix: it catches a page unmapped between the VirtualQuery
     and the call, and mistakes not yet known. Plus isfinite() on the output, or a
     NaN would propagate silently into every draw call.

`drive()` writes through the same accessor, so it gets the same gate — a
stale-but-mapped cg would be WRITTEN, not merely read.

# ⛔ SEEK PRECISION — A COMMENT THAT DESCRIBED CODE THAT WAS NEVER WRITTEN

`seek_to_time`'s comment claimed the backward path was "keyframe jump to a point
BEFORE the target, **then skip forward the remainder, which lands exactly on
it**". Only the first half existed. `demo_seek <ms>` picks the nearest usable
keyframe at or before the target and jumps, full stop — so every backward seek
landed early by up to the keyframe cadence.

FIXED by adding `demo_skip_to <absolute ms>`, queued on the same Cbuf right after
`demo_seek`. They drain in order on the client thread, so the jump (which calls
CL_SetCGameTime itself) completes before the skip runs — the ordering the skip
needs. Skipping 0 is a no-op, so an exact landing costs nothing.

This is a landing-precision fix. It is NOT the "+50 ms" bug and must not be
confused with it: landing early looks like over-rewinding, not like not moving.

# ⚠ REWIND — THE MECHANISM IS NOW PROVEN, THE CAUSE IS ONE UNREAD NUMBER

ProcessKeyFrameJump @0x917ED0 decompiled in full. Its tail:

    v39 = clientActive[6345];               // snap.serverTime  <- READ, never written
    clientActive[6365] = v39;               // oldFrameServerTime
    clientActive[6368] = v39;               // serverTime
    cls_realtime       = v39;
    clientActive[6369] = v39;               // oldServerTime
    cg[498399]         = v39;
    ...
    clientActive[6370] = clientActive[6345] - cls_realtime;   // serverTimeDelta
    CL_SetCGameTime(client);

**It derives the WHOLE clock from snap.serverTime and never sets it.** So the
seek only lands if something earlier in the function put a snapshot back — and
the only thing that can is the replay loop:

    for (j = slot[+32]; j != slot[+36]; j = (j + 1) % 256)
        CL_Demo_ReadDemoMessage(client, ...);

If `slot[+32] == slot[+36]` the body never runs, snap.serverTime is still NOW,
the clock is set to NOW, and CL_SetCGameTime replays straight forward. That is
EXACTLY the documented "+50 ms and the cursor back where it started".

The writer sub_914790 fills those two from
    slot[+32] = clc[+346128]        slot[+36] = clientActive[+90472]
so whether our generated keyframes carry a non-empty range is the open question.

**`jump_to_slot` ALREADY PRINTS IT** and flags `EMPTY` when the two are equal
(RULE A15). One press produces the answer; do not patch further before reading
it. Adding a second speculative layer on top of the unverified clock-force would
break One Change at a Time.

# ✅ REWIND WORKS — VERIFIED IN GAME (2026-08-11, build 7C811B97)

All five Fix Declaration conditions met. Measured from the user's live session log:

    jump slot 2: t=14350  replay=[0..153]
      before: demoT=24350 snapT=24350 cursor=1107532
      clock forced to keyframe t=14350, delta=0
      after : demoT=14350 snapT=14350 cursor=1040929  (demoT -10000, cursor -66603)

    jump slot 1: t=4350   replay=[0..0] EMPTY
      before: demoT=14350   after: demoT=4350         (demoT -10000, cursor -1169049)

Five consecutive seeks, every one landed: -10000, -2550, -8750, -10000, -10000 ms.
The "+50 ms per press and the cursor back where it started" symptom is GONE, and
the session logged zero Com_Errors with no new minidump.

## ⭐ THE REWIND FAILURE AND THE CRASH WERE THE SAME EVENT

This is the whole explanation, and it is worth remembering as a pattern.

The clock-force fix in jump_to_slot (build 81C1E903) was almost certainly already
correct. It could not be OBSERVED working because pressing seek faulted first:
ProcessKeyFrameJump tears down the gamestate, cg goes NULL for a window, and
dolly::render() dereferenced it from the render thread (RULE A21). The user
reported "rewind is not working" because the game died before the seek could be
seen to land. Fixing the crash revealed a rewind that already worked.

LESSON: when a NEW subsystem and an OLD one both look broken at once, suspect the
new one is masking the old one before concluding the old one is broken. RULE A19
("a hook is never a passive observer") applied to a whole feature.

## Note on the EMPTY replay range

Slot 1 logged `replay=[0..0] EMPTY` and the seek STILL landed, because the
clock-force writes snap.serverTime directly rather than depending on the replay
loop to restore it. The file cursor moved to 82172 against the slot's stored
fileOff of 81439, so playback re-reads from the right place and re-syncs as it
runs forward. So an empty replay range is survivable — but it means no snapshot
was restored at that instant, and world state may be briefly stale. Not a defect
we have seen on screen; recorded so it is not mistaken for one later.

# ⭐⭐ CODE HEALTH AUDIT — 18,426 LINES ADDED, FIRST SYSTEMATIC PASS (2026-08-11)

Audited against the rules this project has already paid for, rather than generic
review: A3.1 duplicate hooks, A6/A21 pointer validation, A14 static-init, A17
return widths, A18/A19 hot-path cost.

## ⭐ FOUND — Com_Error WAS HOOKED TWICE, AND ONE HANDLER NEVER RAN

    src/Errors.cpp:313          Hook::create("Com_Error", 0x8F750_b, ...)
    src/demo/demo_native.cpp    Hook::create("Com_Error", addr_Com_Error(), ...)
    both -> _b 0x8F750 == IDA 0x90750

Init order (src/ExtConsole.cpp): demo::init() line 131, Errors::init() line 139.
So demo_native won, and **Errors.cpp's hook_Com_Error has never executed once** —
its `_Com_Error` trampoline is NULL and its "******** ERROR: ..." formatting has
never appeared. Not a crash (the dead detour is unreachable, and `_Com_Error` is
used nowhere else), but it is the exact silent failure A3.1 describes, and it
survived the entire project undetected.

FIXED: the dead duplicate in Errors.cpp is commented out with the reason.

## ⭐⭐ THE SYSTEMIC FIX — Hook::create NOW REPORTS DUPLICATES

`Hook::create` treated MH_ERROR_ALREADY_CREATED as SUCCESS. That is what made the
above invisible, and it is the same trap that cost a full test cycle on
2026-08-08. It now:

  * sets `*original = nullptr` (never hand back a stale trampoline),
  * prints via **Console::printf, not DEV_PRINTF** — DEV_PRINTF does not reach
    main/s2mp_console.log, so a failure written with it is invisible afterwards,
  * returns **false**, because the caller's detour genuinely will not run.

Callers that already do `const bool ok = Hook::create(...)` now correctly report
FAILED/DUPLICATE. From here on this entire class announces itself at boot.

## CLEAN — checked and found no defects

  * **Unguarded trampoline calls.** ~60 sites call `X_orig(...)` with no null
    check. Every one verified to be INSIDE its own detour, where reaching the
    code proves the hook installed. The multi-call ones (streamsync parse/gate,
    IsRecordingAllowed, delta index) were read individually. NOT a defect — and
    worth recording so the next audit does not re-flag it.
  * **RULE A14 (_b at namespace scope).** Two apparent hits in demo_game.hpp
    (lines 356, 478) are inside inline FUNCTIONS, so `_b` evaluates at call time.
    Clean.
  * **Duplicate hooks.** Exactly one, above. 99 Hook::create sites scanned;
    36 targets are computed and were checked by name.

## NOT YET AUDITED — say so rather than imply coverage

  * per-frame cost on the Present / render / packet paths beyond the two already
    fixed (the peer tracker and the GUI session readouts),
  * thread-safety of GUI reads of engine state generally (dolly is done: mutex +
    copy-under-lock),
  * ABI return widths across all ~60 hooks — only the ones touched this session
    were re-checked against the IDB,
  * demo_playback.cpp (3,927 lines), which is the retiring custom theater.

## Tool

    scratchpad/hookaudit2.py — resolves _b literals and addr_*() accessors,

# ⛔⛔ TWO DOLLY/REWIND DEFECTS, BOTH MINE, BOTH DIAGNOSED FROM ONE REPORT
# (2026-08-11, build 56CAAC56. USER: "rewind works very rarely, glitches out"
#  and "dollycam is jittery, like updating a frame every 2 seconds")

## ⭐ DEFECT 1 — THE DOLLY RAN ON THE SNAPSHOT CLOCK. It is a STEP FUNCTION.

`demo_native::demo_time()` returns **cl.snap.serverTime** (clientActive dword
6345). That value changes ONLY when a new snapshot is consumed, so anything
sampling it per frame sees one value for a whole snapshot interval and then a
jump. The dolly evaluated its spline on it, so the camera held still and
teleported once per snapshot — exactly "updating a frame every 2 seconds".

The continuous clock is **cl.serverTime** (dword 6368), which CL_SetCGameTime
recomputes EVERY FRAME:

    cl.serverTime = cl.serverTimeDelta + cls_realtime;
    if (cl.serverTime < cl.oldFrameServerTime) cl.serverTime = cl.oldFrameServerTime;

⚠ THIS IS THE SAME MISTAKE CLAUDE.md ALREADY RECORDS FOR VIEW ANGLES: "S2 wrote
ps+576 EVERY FRAME ... that replaced the engine's smooth interpolated angle with
one discrete sample. H1 has NO per-frame angle write anywhere." Same defect
class, different subsystem, and I walked straight into it with the file open.

**GENERAL RULE: snap.serverTime is for SEEKING (keyframe slot times are stored
from that same field, slot+8 == clientActive+25380 == dword 6345). cl.serverTime
is for ANYTHING THAT ANIMATES. Never sample the snapshot clock per frame.**

FIXED: added `demo_native::demo_time_smooth()` (dword 6368). The dolly now uses
it for capture, evaluation, the live marker, the GUI "inside the shot" test and
retime. Seeking deliberately still uses demo_time(). The `dolly` command prints
BOTH so a stalled clock is visible rather than inferred.

## ⭐ DEFECT 2 — usable_slots() OFFERED KEYFRAMES THAT RESTORE NOTHING

ProcessKeyFrameJump restores the world with

    for (j = slot[+32]; j != slot[+36]; j = (j + 1) % 256)
        CL_Demo_ReadDemoMessage(...)

so when **slot[+32] == slot[+36]** the loop runs ZERO times and no snapshot is
put back. `usable_slots()` filtered on payload length (s[7] > 0) and time
(s[2] >= 0) but NOT on the replay range, so those slots were offered as seek
targets.

And the clock-force in jump_to_slot then HID it: the clock landed on the
keyframe time while the world state stayed where it was. The seek looked like it
worked and the game glitched — precisely "works very rarely, glitches out".

The user's own log had it in plain sight and I read past it:

    jump slot 2: t=14350  replay=[0..153]     <- real range, worked
    jump slot 3: t=24350  replay=[153..156]   <- real range, worked
    jump slot 1: t=4350   replay=[0..0] EMPTY <- restored NOTHING, still "landed"

I quoted that EMPTY line while declaring rewind verified. Five seeks looked like
5/5 success; three were genuinely fine and the empty one was a false positive
manufactured by my own clock-force.

FIXED: `usable_slots()` now rejects `s[8] == s[9]`. The "no usable keyframes"
message explains the rule so an empty ring is not mistaken for broken seeking.

## ⚠ LESSON — A FIX THAT FORCES STATE CAN MANUFACTURE ITS OWN FALSE POSITIVE

The clock-force was added so a jump would land. It also made a jump that restored
NOTHING report as a success, because the only thing being checked afterwards was
the clock — which the fix itself had just written. **Never verify a fix using the
value the fix writes.** Verify the thing it was supposed to cause: here, that a
snapshot was actually restored (a non-empty replay range), not that the clock
reads what we set it to.

This also retracts "REWIND WORKS — VERIFIED IN GAME" above as OVERSTATED: three
of those five seeks were real, the verification method could not tell the
difference, and the user hit the failures immediately.

# ⭐⭐⭐ OFFLINE REWIND SIMULATION — tools/s2_keyframe_sim.py (2026-08-11)

User asked for an offline simulation of the rewind rather than more in-game
guessing. Correct call, and it immediately found a defect the in-game testing had
not: the keyframe ring and slot table are pure bookkeeping, so they simulate
exactly. RULE A11.

## THE MODEL IS VALIDATED AGAINST REAL DATA BEFORE ANY RESULT IS TRUSTED

From the user's own log, three consecutive slots:

    slot 1 mem_off  88931 + len  88616 = 177547   slot 2 mem_off = 177547  MATCH
    slot 2 mem_off 177547 + len 116730 = 294277   slot 3 mem_off = 294277  MATCH

The ring is written strictly sequentially and the writer model is CONFIRMED, not
assumed. Constants come from sub_914790 and ProcessKeyFrameJump, not guesses:
2 MB payload buffer at PlaybackData+79432, wrap at **0x1FFFFF (not 0x200000)**,
250 slots, index advanced BEFORE the write so widx == newest.

## ⭐ THE SIM HAS A POSITIVE CONTROL, WITHOUT WHICH A "PASS" MEANS NOTHING

It runs three variants of usable_slots(): the build the user tested (no
empty-replay filter), the ordering slip, and current. If the control does not
FAIL, the harness reports INCONCLUSIVE and refuses to endorse the others.

    variant                                  offered   bad    rate
    7C811B97  no empty-replay filter          38550    9010   23%
    ordering slip (filter before counting)    38550    6527   17%
    56CAAC56  current                         38550    6521   17%

## FINDING 1 — the empty-replay filter is real and worth ~3300 bad seeks

Confirmed by the control. Already fixed.

## FINDING 2 — the acc-ordering slip IS load-bearing after all

The "buggy" variant produces **23 CORRUPT payloads** that current does not:
skipping a rejected slot before counting its bytes under-counts the ring and lets
the walk reach back past genuinely overwritten keyframes. I had guessed this was
harmless because the engine invalidates overwritten slots itself. The sim says
otherwise. Keep the byte count ahead of the filter.

## ⚠ FINDING 3 — 256-RING WRAP. THE DOMINANT FAILURE, BUT IT RESTS ON AN INFERENCE

17% of all offered targets fail this test, four times the empty-replay defect,
and it survives every fix so far. ProcessKeyFrameJump counts with

    for (j = slot[+32]; j != slot[+36]; j = (j + 1) % 256)

so it performs ((b - a) mod 256) iterations and **cannot represent a count of 256
or more**. A larger true count aliases and the wrong number of messages is
replayed — silently, because nothing in the slot records the true figure.

⛔ THE ASSUMPTION, STATED PLAINLY: this treats the span as "messages since the
previous keyframe". slot+32 comes from clc+346128 and slot+36 from
clientActive+90472 — TWO DIFFERENT OBJECTS — so that reading is an inference, not
proof. The user's real log is only partly consistent with it:

    slot 2  replay=[0..153]    153 over ~10 s
    slot 3  replay=[153..156]    3 over ~10 s     <- does not fit a steady rate

The ranges ARE contiguous (slot 3 starts where slot 2 ended), which supports a
monotonic message counter; the 153-then-3 rate does not. Unresolved.

**SO NO FIX WAS WRITTEN FOR IT.** Per the doctrine, a hypothesis does not get
patched. Build 28ED503F instead prints the SPAN on every jump and flags
`<<< SPAN NEAR THE 256 RING LIMIT` above 200. One real session settles it:
spans near 256 confirm the mechanism, spans that stay small refute it and this
whole finding is a modelling artefact to be deleted.

## Usage

    python tools/s2_keyframe_sim.py             # validate model + all variants
    python tools/s2_keyframe_sim.py --validate  # only check against the real log
    python tools/s2_keyframe_sim.py --verbose   # print individual failures

Re-run it after ANY change to usable_slots() or to keyframe generation cadence.

# ZERO-HOOK REBUILD IS VOID (flagged 2026-08-11, by the user)

RULE A8 says date the state. This is the same rule at a larger scale: an entire
CLASS of measurement in this file was taken while our own code was breaking the
thing being measured, and must not be quoted as evidence again.

## The proof it was broken

    WITH force_host hooks:     20 searches issued, 12 completed, 0 errors,
                               0 discards, ZERO candidates, no match ever found
    WITHOUT (marker file):     match found ALMOST INSTANTLY

Same account, same session, minutes apart. **We never isolated WHICH hook did
it.** The only proven fact is "all force_host hooks removed = matchmaking works".

## What that voids — do NOT cite these

  * "platform UDP counter static at 37 packets while advertised=1, so nobody has
    ever QoS-probed us"
  * "advertised=1 with AreWeHost=0 and nobody arrived"
  * any candidate-count, search-result or peer-contact reading from that era

If matchmaking never returned us to anyone, nothing would probe us REGARDLESS of
whether the QoS path works. The observation is consistent with both, so it
discriminates nothing. I quoted it repeatedly as though it settled the question;
it does not.

## What SURVIVES, because it is static

Anything read from the IDB is unaffected. In particular the Phase A result
(2026-08-11) stands on its own:

    qos_min_received / qos_max_unresponsive / qos_match_time   ZERO xrefs;
        they are playlist RULE TEXT in the blob region ~0xACAxxxx, not code
    qos_error_code    ONE xref, from sub_2A1820 -- the matchmaking TELEMETRY writer
    QosComplete / QosResultCount / QosTime                     ZERO xrefs
    QosPayload*                                                ABSENT ENTIRELY

So S2 has no reachable game-side QoS PAYLOAD builder -- that logic is inside
Demonware (consistent with AW using XNetQos* and MWR using
dwQoSMultiProbeListener). The payload-content lever does not exist in the binary.

That is a narrow conclusion. It does NOT say whether we are returned as a
candidate, whether anyone probes us, or whether force hosting can work. Those are
OPEN, and the old numbers cannot answer them.

## The re-measurement is now possible for the first time

Conditions are finally clean: force_host is ZERO HOOKS, server_browser is
zero-hooks by design, and the search-path and packet hooks were made opt-in by
the 2026-08-11 audit. So a probe/join log taken now is trustworthy in a way
nothing before it was.

⚠ WITH ONE CAVEAT THAT MUST BE HONOURED: because the breaking hook was never
identified, "the current build is clean" is an INFERENCE, not a proven fact. Any
instrumentation added for the re-measurement has to be able to prove its own
innocence -- i.e. ship with an off switch and an A/B, exactly as the marker file
did. Do not repeat the mistake of measuring through code whose effect on the
subject is unknown.

# ⭐⭐⭐⭐ ADVANCED WARFARE IS THE RIGHT TWIN — 371 FUNCTIONS NAMED (2026-08-11)

AW (`default_mp.pe`, Xbox 360 PPC, imagebase 0x82000000, MCP port 12345) is a
**fully-symboled build with mangled C++ names** — 33,962 functions, 914 with
"party" in the name, 299 "session", 132 "playlist", 119 "matchmaking". Same
studio as S2 (Sledgehammer), direct predecessor. It is a far better twin than
MW3 for anything party/host/session/matchmaking.

## THE METHOD (reusable — this is the third time it has paid off)

Different CPU (PPC vs x64) so no byte matching, but **strings survive builds**:

  1. AW: for every NAMED function, collect referenced string literals; keep only
     strings owned by exactly ONE function.  -> 6,572 unique anchors
  2. S2: read every non-executable segment ONCE with `ida_bytes.get_bytes` and
     substring-search in Python.  **NEVER `idautils.Strings()` on S2** — it
     triggers a full strlist rebuild and times out the MCP on this 300 MB image.
     -> 2,889 anchors present in S2 (44% of AW's, confirming shared lineage)
  3. Keep anchors with exactly ONE S2 owning function; vote; require all anchors
     backing a function to imply the same AW name.
  4. Reject: already-named S2 funcs, AW names claimed by >1 S2 func, names that
     already exist elsewhere in S2, and GENERIC anchors.

⚠ **The filter that matters is DISTINCTIVENESS, not length.** My first pass used
a >=20-char rule and threw away `%idoqos`, `%iqosres`, `%ipa_joinrequest` — the
single most valuable anchors in the whole set. A short string can be a unique
protocol token; a long one (`'%s%s%llu/%s/%llu/tokens/?client=%s'`) can be
generic. Score on "does it contain a real identifier after stripping format
specifiers", then require either 2+ distinctive anchors or 1 long/underscored one.

Scripts kept in the session scratchpad: `aw_anchors_all.py`, `s2_match.py`,
`analyse3.py`, `s2_apply3.py`.

## ⭐⭐⭐ THE PARTY OOB PROTOCOL — THE ihping/ihpong ANSWER

USER QUESTION: MW2's `ihping`/`ihpong` made players join fast; what is S2's?

**S2 has TWO ping systems, and neither is MW2's.** Both are now mapped end to end:

### 1. HOST MIGRATION PING MESH — the true ihping/ihpong analogue

    PartyMigrate_SelectOurNominee  0x49D100
      -> PartyMigrate_GetPings     0x49BA50   sends "%impng %i" to all 48 party slots
    PartyMigrate_HandlePingMsg     0x4983B0   receives it, immediately replies "%impck %i"

`PartyMigrate_HandlePingMsg` is literally receive-ping-send-pong. Rate limited by
the dvar at `off_9099080+16`, whole system gated on `off_9099078+16`.
`PartyMigrate_SelectOurNominee` then calls `Session_CanHostServer` and
`PartyMigrate_SendNomineeMsg` — this is where a client votes on who should host.

### 2. QoS PROBE ORCHESTRATION — how a PARTY picks a server

    PartyHost_SearchComplete  0x29C540
      Live_CancelQoSProbe(params+144)                    0x2A6640
      R = Search_GetResultsObject(M)                     (= M + 1712)
      PartyHost_ShareSearchResults(params, R)            0x4914E0  -> "%idoqos"
      addr[] = { R + 8 + 596*i } for every result
      Live_StartQoSProbe(params+144, addr, count)        0x2A66D0

    PartyClient_Frame          0x475400
      -> PartyClient_SendQoSResults  0x478990            -> "%iqosres"

    PartyHost_TellPartyMembersToStopQoS 0x492D50         -> "%istopqos"

So the party HOST chunks its search results (17 per message: a u16 field plus the
68-byte host-address blob at result+8) and tells every member to probe them.
Members probe and report back. The host aggregates and picks one server for the
whole party. That is why a party joins together and joins fast.

### ⭐ THE LEVER, and it is the direct analogue of the MW2 pong spoof

`PartyClient_SendQoSResults` builds the reply as:

    MSG_WriteString(msg, "%iqosres");
    for each result i with Search_HasQosResult(R,i):        // status at R+596*i+84 > 1
        MSG_WriteData(msg, result, 8);                      // identity
        if (result[19] == 3)  MSG_WriteBit0(msg);           // status 3 = probe failed
        else { MSG_WriteBit1(msg);
               MSG_WriteShort(msg, Search_GetResultPing(R,i)); }   // <-- THE PING WE REPORT
        Search_ClearResultQosStatus(R, i);
    ... max 123 results, then 8 zero bytes as terminator, then send to the party host

**`MSG_WriteShort(msg, ping)` is a value WE choose and send.** In MW2 you spoofed
the pong timing; here the equivalent is the ping we self-report to our own party
host. ⚠ SCOPE: this only influences which server OUR PARTY picks. It does not
influence Demonware, and it does nothing if you are not in a party with others.
NOT TESTED — this is a static reading, not a measured result.

### The receive side is dispatch-by-table, and mostly not statically visible

AW hierarchy (all named there):

    CL_DispatchConnectionlessPacket -> Party_HandlePacket -> PartyHost_HandlePacket
                                                          -> PartyClient_HandlePacket
                                                          -> PartyMigrate_HandlePacket

⛔ CORRECTION to an earlier CLAUDE.md claim. It said the bare OOB names
('doqos', 'qosres', ...) have no xrefs because of "computed/Arxan" references,
and that runtime was the only route. **The same strings have no xrefs in AW
either** — and AW is not Arxan-protected. The real reason is ordinary compiler
behaviour: `strcmp(cmd, "doqos")` gets inlined into dword/word comparisons, so no
string reference is emitted at all. Arxan was never the explanation here. The
SENDERS were statically reachable all along, which is how all of the above was
found with no runtime at all.

# ⭐⭐⭐⭐ THE HOST GATE, FOUND — Session_CanHostServer, AND OUR OWN 18-PLAYER
# LATCH WAS RAISING THE BAR (2026-08-11, entirely offline)

USER REPORT: "host my own match" ticked, still put into another lobby; only ever
game-netchan packets in the Network tab; "stop doing cheap tests. Look."

Both complaints were correct and both had real causes.

## ⛔ CORRECTION — netlog was watching the wrong pipe, and I should have known

`PlatformSocket_Recv` (0xA7EB90) is `recvfrom`, i.e. UDP. CLAUDE.md ALREADY
records that **Demonware's service connection is TCP** (recv/send callers cluster
in 0xAC7xxx / 0xA7Fxxx / 0x662510). So a UDP hook can never see matchmaking, and
the platform counter sitting at zero was guaranteed by construction, not evidence.

Two further by-design reasons nothing appeared: `push()` DISCARDS everything that
is not `FF FF FF FF` (OOB), and both hooks are RECV-only, so nothing "sent" can
ever be listed.

FIXED anyway (build 428B90C0): `net_getpacket_stub` was calling `readable()` THREE
times per received packet, and `readable()` is a `VirtualQuery` -- a kernel
transition -- while the OOB filter that throws the packet away sat at the far end
inside `push()`. Every snapshot paid three syscalls to be discarded. Replaced with
table-based SEH (zero cost on the happy path, the pattern dolly.cpp already uses)
and the OOB test hoisted to the front.

## ⭐ AW IS DEFINITIVE ON THE HOST/SEARCH DECISION

`dwMatchMakingManager_Update` @0x827A3658 -- the whole thing is ONE variable:

    if (s_matchmakingMode == LISTEN_SERVER) {
        if (!xblive_privatematch && !serverAssigned
            && !Session_CreateInProgress(&g_serverSession)
            && Session_IsInfoValid(...))
            DSCL_SelectHostAsServer();                  // WE HOST
    } else if (s_matchmakingMode == DEDICATED_SERVER) {
        dwMatchMakingManager_StartServerSearch(...);     // go find a DS
    }

    enum DW_MATCHMAKING_MANAGER_MODE { NONE=0, LISTEN_SERVER=1, DEDICATED_SERVER=2 }

and `dwMatchMakingManager_Start(bool force_listen)` shows the engine's DEFAULT IS
TO HOST:

    s_matchmakingMode = LISTEN_SERVER;
    if (!force_listen && <scriptvar> != 8999
        && dwMatchMakingManager_ShouldChooseDataCentre(&g_partyData, ...))
        s_matchmakingMode = DEDICATED_SERVER;

`DSCL_SelectHostAsServer` @0x827A8310 = build a ServerInfo from OUR OWN session
info and address with `dataCenterId = 0`, `DSCL_AssignServer`, then
`s_dscl.state = DSCLStateServerAcquired` **and `dword_82B8024C |= 0x200`** -- and
`StartServerSearch` refuses to run while that 0x200 bit is set. That is the
engine's own "I am the server, stop looking for one" latch.

    enum DSCLState { Idle0 PingingServer1 SearchingServers2 ServerSearchComplete3
                     ServerReleased4 AcquiringServer5 ServerAcquired6
                     ServerGameStarting7 ServerGameStarted8 }

## CORRECTED — what S2's sub_1FD110 actually tests

With AW's enum in hand, `(state - 5) <= 2 && (int)o[3] >= 2` is
state in {AcquiringServer, ServerAcquired, ServerGameStarting}. The older note
calling it "the server we went and got is READY" was too narrow: it is also true
while the acquire is still IN PROGRESS. Comment corrected in the IDB.

## S2 HAS NO SelectHostAsServer, AND ITS FORK IS ELSEWHERE

The full 78-entry GSC binding table at 0xB50C60 was dumped and **contains no
SelectHostAsServer**. S2's tick `sub_29D9C0` forks on

    if (sub_480F20(Params) /* sessionType == 2 */ && sub_1FF290(...))
        sub_1FED90(...);            // DEDICATED SERVER search
    else
        sub_6FF930(...);            // LOBBY search (dwFindSessions)

    sub_1FF290 = *(DWORD*)(off_6F34250+16)            // a dvar bool
              && (data-centre list non-empty)          // S2's ShouldChooseDataCentre

So there is no "host" branch in S2's tick at all -- the decision has moved into
GSC, which we cannot read. What we CAN read is every predicate GSC calls.

## ⭐⭐⭐ THE REAL GATE — Session_CanHostServer @0x8534B0, DECOMPILED IN FULL

    1. systemlink                  -> return 1        (takes us offline; unusable)
    2. !g_hostingEnabled           -> 0               (we re-assert this)
    3. requireOpenNat && nat == 3  -> 0               <- params[13], OURS TO CLEAR
    4. !Session_IsBandwidthTestComplete -> CLEARS g_hostingEnabled, return 0
    5. !private && !dvar"393":
         requiredUpload(maxplayers) > measured -> 0
         requiredPing  (maxplayers) > measured -> 0
    6. return 1

### ⚠ STEP 5 IS KEYED ON party_maxplayers, AND THE BAR RISES WITH IT

    players  upload dvar  default   ping dvar
    <=2      "357"          64000   none -- literally 0.0f
    <=4      "2237"        128000   "1925"
    <=8      "2871"        256000   "1925"
    <=12     "3829"        576000   "2737"
    <=18     "889"         725000   "3819"      <- WHERE OUR OWN LATCH PUT US
    >18      "4342"        900000   "134"

**force_host latches party_maxplayers to 18, which raises the host requirement to
725 kbps measured upload plus a ping ceiling.** If the engine's own bandwidth test
does not clear that bar, CanHostServer returns 0, GSC never hosts, the lobby search
runs, and you are placed in someone else's game -- exactly the reported symptom.
That is a self-inflicted defect, found statically, with no test needed.

All ten thresholds are registered by `Com_InitDvars` with **flags 0**, i.e. ordinary
settable dvars, NOT the 0x2000 engine-owned class.

`dvar "393"` (off_1BD3708) also waives step 5 -- but it is written FROM THE GAMESTATE
in CL_ParseGamestate and cleared in four places by UI_SetActiveMenu, so it is
server-controlled and NOT ours to use.

Step 4's byte: `Session_IsBandwidthTestComplete(obj) = *(BYTE*)(obj + 100264)`, and
0x10DC800 + 0x187A8 = **IDA 0x10F4FA8**. When false it LATCHES g_hostingEnabled off,
and Session_ClearHostingEnabled can only ever clear -- a one-way trap.

## PLAYLIST FLAGS — always-search decoded, and the ordinal rule CONFIRMED

`Playlist_IsAlwaysSearch` (0x654780, sole worker of GSC IsPlaylistAlwaysSearch):

    return sub_CECD0() && (*(DWORD*)(0xABDE228 + 568*row) & 0x10) != 0;

0xABDE228 == row(0xABDE010) + 536, so **the flags dword is at row+536 and bit 0x10
== ALWAYS SEARCH**. Measured across the static table: set on only THREE rows
(Sandbox 24/7, Headquarters). NOT set on Team Deathmatch / War / Domination /
Search and Destroy / Shipment 1944 -- so always-search is NOT what forces a search
on the common playlists. Hypothesis checked and dropped.

Same dump CONFIRMS two things previously uncertain:
  - ordinal 13 = Domination and ordinal 31 = Shipment 1944, exactly matching the
    user's live values -> row base 0xABDE010 and "ordinal counted over named rows"
    are both correct;
  - bits 0x01 and 0x80 appear only on Ranked Play (flags 0x81), independently
    re-confirming the earlier sub_655740 / sub_655780 finding from a different base.

## SHIPPED — build 428B90C0 (deployed, hash-verified). STILL ZERO HOOKS.

  - tick() now CLEARS `requireOpenNat` (params[13], lobby+644), skipping step 3.
  - tick() zeroes the ten qualification dvars through the engine's own console
    path, compare-then-write, at 2 Hz. Toggle `fh_relaxqual 0`.
  - **`fh_canhost`** prints every term of the gate AND CALLS
    `Session_CanHostServer(lobby0, maxplayers)` itself, so a refusal names itself
    instead of being inferred. Runs on the CLIENT thread; safe because we clear
    requireOpenNat first, so the branch with the interlocked release and the Arxan
    thunk is not taken. RULE A17: the trampoline returns `char`.

⚠ NOT YET PROVEN that the qualification is what was refusing. It is a
mechanism-level candidate that fits the symptom exactly. `fh_canhost` settles it in
one run, and if the verdict is still 0 it names which term.

66 of the 78 GSC bindings, PROVEN BY NAME (the table pairs the string and the
