# ⭐⭐⭐⭐ THE 18-PLAYER CEILING IS REOPENED — THE ARXAN WALL WAS AN IDA
# MIS-ATTRIBUTION, NOT A WALL (2026-08-11, offline, via the AW twin)

This section formally REOPENS the entry "⛔ CLOSED — MORE THAN 18 PLAYERS IS NOT
REACHABLE FROM THE CLIENT". Failed Attempt Protection requires new evidence to
retry; the new evidence is the Advanced Warfare IDB, which did not exist for that
attempt, plus a straight disassembly read the earlier pass never did.

## ⛔ WHAT THE OLD ENTRY GOT WRONG

It said:

> SV_CreateServerHunk's caller NOT REACHABLE -- DB_Thread @0xACE30 is
> JUMPOUT(0xFFFFFFFFFFFF0D13), an Arxan thunk, so what client count it is passed
> is not statically visible (RULE A5). So the single value that would have to
> change is the one value the Arxan wall hides.

**That is false.** `DB_Thread` at 0xACE30 IS a thunk, but IDA extended its FUNCTION
BOUNDS over the following real code, so xrefs report the call site at 0xAD399 as
"in DB_Thread". The code itself disassembles perfectly. The wall was in the
function attribution, not in the binary.

LESSON, and it generalises: **when a caller looks unreachable, disassemble the call
site's address range directly before concluding Arxan.** `idautils.XrefsTo` gives
you the address; `ida_funcs.get_func` on it can lie. This cost the project a
closed investigation.

## ⭐ THE CHAIN, END TO END

AW named the whole thing, which is how the S2 side became readable:

    AW  CL_AllocatePerLocalClientMemory2 0x825FA288
          CL_GetMaxClients(flags, &maxLocalClients, &maxClients, &maxAgents)
          SV_AllocateClientMemory(flags, maxLocalClients, maxClients, maxAgents)
          CG_AllocateClientMemory / FX_AllocateClientMemory / FX_Mark / SV_Agent

    AW  CL_GetMaxClients 0x825F30A0
          *maxLocalClients = clientUIActives[0].active (+1 if byte_82B6CC38)
          *maxClients      = (flags & 2) ? 12 : <DVAR VALUE at dvar+12>
          *maxAgents       = (flags & 2) ? 24 : (coop ? 14 : GameStateInfo byte)

S2 inlines CL_GetMaxClients, and the same code is at **0xAD2A0..0xAD3E0**, with
the identical downstream call ORDER (SV_Allocate -> CG_Allocate -> FX -> FX_Mark
-> Agent), which is what identifies it:

    000AD2DE  mov  edi, cs:dword_27CA234        ; flags
    000AD2EB  test dil, 2
    000AD2EF  jnz  short loc_AD357
    000AD2F1  mov  rcx, cs:dvar_sv_maxclients   ; <<<< THE COUNT
    000AD2F8  mov  r13d, [rcx+10h]              ;      dvar value (+16, x64)
    loc_AD357:
    000AD363  mov  r13d, 30h                    ; else 48
    000AD37F  mov  esi, 2                       ; maxLocalClients = 2 on that path
    000AD38E  mov  r8d, r13d                    ; arg3 = maxClients
    000AD399  call SV_AllocateClientMemory

S2 reads the dvar at **+16** where AW reads **+12** -- exactly the x64-vs-PPC32
width difference already proven for `com_sv_running`. Two independent confirmations
that this is the same code.

Argument NAMES are twin-proven from AW's mangled symbol
`?SV_AllocateClientMemory@@YAXHHHH@Z` (void, four ints).

## ⭐⭐ THE CONSEQUENCE — THE HUNK AND svs.clients ARE THE SAME NUMBER

    sub_62430 (session/mode setup)
        saves flags        -> dword_27CA234
        saves sv_maxclients-> dword_27CA24C   (restored at 0x625F7)
        sets  sv_maxclients from the game-mode table @0xB2EC08 (stride 0x78,
              index dword_D8AF894)  -- ONLY when NOT online and NOT system link
    0xAD2F1  maxClients = (dword_27CA234 & 2) ? 48 : sv_maxclients->value
    0x6DA5F0 SV_AllocateClientMemory reserves g_serverHunkUser for THAT count
    0x6DCDB0 SV_Init allocates svs.clients for sv_maxclients (or 48 on the hub branch)

**Both ends derive from sv_maxclients. They are not independent, and no hidden
engine constant is involved.** So "Memory Error: 6 161" was not "the hunk is sized
for the engine's N and we allocated for ours" -- it was raising sv_maxclients
AFTER the reservation had already been made.

## ⭐ AND THE ONLINE PATH DOES NOT OVERWRITE IT

    000624D2  call Com_IsOnlineGame
    000624D9  jnz  loc_6253D              ; ONLINE -> skip the Dvar_SetInt
    000624DB  call Com_IsSystemLink
    000624E2  jnz  loc_6253D              ; SYSTEMLINK -> skip
    ...
    00062531  mov  rcx, cs:dvar_sv_maxclients
    00062538  call Dvar_SetInt            ; offline/local only

In an ONLINE match sv_maxclients keeps whatever value it already holds. So a value
set BEFORE this sequence survives into both the hunk reservation and SV_Init.

## WHAT IS AND IS NOT ESTABLISHED

PROVEN:
  - the hunk's maxClients is `(flags & 2) ? 48 : sv_maxclients`
  - the online path does not overwrite sv_maxclients
  - flags come from dword_27CA234, written once, at 0x62667, as `r14d & ~0x10`
  - `flags & 2` reserves the hunk for **48** clients outright

NOT PROVEN, and required before any attempt:
  - the ORDERING: when 0xAD2A0 runs relative to any point the mod could write the
    dvar. This is the whole question now, and it is a TIMING question, not an
    Arxan one.
  - whether anything downstream re-clamps
  - what `flags & 2` actually means (it also forces maxLocalClients = 2 and gates
    the demo-download-memory free at 0x62611, so it is NOT simply "more players")

## STATUS

The 18-player entry moves from CLOSED to **OPEN, with a named mechanism**. The
removal of `fh_svmaxclients` / `fh_hunk` from force_host on 2026-08-11 was done on
the strength of the CLOSED finding; nothing has been re-added, and nothing should
be until the ordering above is established. Do NOT reinstate a naive latch -- the
fatal path is unchanged if the write lands after 0xAD2F1.

## Named / commented this session

    0x6DA5F0  SV_AllocateClientMemory       full chain comment
    0xAD2F1   comment: the maxClients source, and the mis-attribution warning
    0xAD363   comment: the 48 path
    0xAD399   comment: argument mapping from the AW symbol
    0x624D2   comment: THE ONLINE ESCAPE
    0x62531 / 0x62651 / 0x62667  comments: the save/restore of count and flags

## ⭐ THE SERVER-HUNK LIFECYCLE — allocated and freed around ZONE LOADS

Recovered immediately after the above, and it answers the ordering question the
reopening left open.

    ALLOCATE   inside DB_TryLoadXFileInternal @0xACE30, body at 0xAD2A0..0xAD3E0
        if ((flags & 0x108) == 0)          skip
        if (dword_27D10F0 != 0)            skip        <- RUN-ONCE LATCH
        maxClients = (flags & 2) ? 48 : sv_maxclients->value
        SV_AllocateClientMemory -> CG_ -> FX_ -> FX_Mark -> SV_Agent
        dword_27D10F0 = 1

    FREE       inside DB_LoadXAssets @0xA51E0..0xA523B
        if ((flags & 0x108) == 0)          skip
        if (dword_27D10F0 == 0)            skip
        dword_27D10F0 = 0                                <- LATCH CLEARED
        SV_FreeClientMemory -> CG_Free -> FX_Free -> FX_MarkFree -> SV_AgentFree

Twin-proven: AW's `CL_FreePerLocalClientMemory2` (0x825F50A8) does exactly this --
`Hunk_UserDestroy` on the g_serverHunkUser hunk then the same four frees -- and
**its caller is `DB_LoadXAssets`**, matching S2 exactly. The allocate side's caller
in AW is `DB_TryLoadXFileInternal`, matching S2 exactly.

**So the reservation is torn down and re-created around zone loads, not created
once at startup.** A value written to sv_maxclients while at the menu should
therefore be picked up by the next reservation.

## ⚠ BUT THAT DOES NOT YET EXPLAIN THE OLD CRASH — DO NOT ACT ON IT

The removed `fh_svmaxclients` latch was gated on `!com_sv_running`, i.e. it wrote
the dvar at the MENU, before the map load. Under the lifecycle above that should
have been picked up cleanly, and yet it produced `Memory Error: 6 161`.

So something in this model is still incomplete. The leading candidate is the
`flags & 0x108` gate: if the map's zone load does NOT carry those bits, no
free/re-reserve happens, the hunk from the earlier (frontend) load persists at its
original size, and SV_Init then allocates svs.clients for the raised value out of
it -- which is exactly the overflow. `flags` is `dword_27CA234`, written once at
0x62667 as `r14d & ~0x10`, so which zone loads carry 0x108 is knowable but NOT YET
established.

Per the Contradiction Rule, this must be resolved before any attempt. Concretely:
determine which zone loads set `dword_27CA234 & 0x108`, and whether the map load
that precedes SV_Init is one of them.

## Named this session from the fixed call order (twin-proven)

AW's CL_AllocatePerLocalClientMemory2 / CL_FreePerLocalClientMemory2 call these in
a FIXED ORDER (SV_ -> CG_ -> FX_ -> FX_Mark -> SV_Agent), and S2 emits the identical
sequence in both directions, so position identifies each one:

    0x3FF780  CG_AllocateClientMemory        0x409B50  CG_FreeClientMemory
    0x5175B0  FX_AllocateClientMemory        0x5176C0  FX_FreeClientMemory
    0x508C80  FX_MarkAllocateClientMemory    0x509120  FX_MarkFreeClientMemory
    0x69D520  SV_AgentAllocateClientMemory   0x69D980  SV_AgentFreeClientMemory
    0x6DA5F0  SV_AllocateClientMemory        0x6DAD90  SV_FreeClientMemory

## ⭐ NAME DISAGREEMENT RESOLVED — 0xACE30 is DB_TryLoadXFileInternal, not DB_Thread

One of the nine disagreements recorded on 2026-08-11 is settled, in AW's favour,
on two independent grounds:

  1. ANCHOR: `MENU_CONTENT_NOT_AVAILABLE` (0xB36F78) is referenced from 0xACFB7,
     inside this function -- the exact anchor AW's DB_TryLoadXFileInternal carries.
  2. STRUCTURE: AW's DB_TryLoadXFileInternal calls CL_AllocatePerLocalClientMemory2,
     and this function contains that inlined sequence.

AW has BOTH names as separate functions (DB_TryLoadXFileInternal 0x825851F8,
DB_Thread 0x82585818) and it is the former that allocates, so "DB_Thread" was the
wrong one of the pair. Renamed, with the mis-bounding warning in the comment.

Eight disagreements remain open.

## ⛔ CORRECTION TO THE SECTION ABOVE — THE 0x108 GATE IS ZONE FLAGS, NOT SESSION FLAGS

I wrote, one section above: *"flags is dword_27CA234, written once at 0x62667 as
r14d & ~0x10, so which zone loads carry 0x108 is knowable but NOT YET established."*
**That conflated two different flag words.** Corrected here.

There are TWO, and they are unrelated:

    r13d              THE ZONE FLAGS. In DB_TryLoadXFileInternal it is arg2:
                      000ACE7A  mov r13d, edx
                      TWIN-PROVEN -- AW's signature is
                        void DB_TryLoadXFileInternal(const char *zoneName,
                                                     int zoneFlags, int isBaseMap)
                      In DB_LoadXAssets it is the ACCUMULATOR:
                      000A503E  mov r13d, ecx   /  000A50E2  or r13d, eax
                      which is the `v8 |= zf` loop already documented in this file.
                      **This is what the `& 0x108` gate tests, in BOTH functions.**

    dword_27CA234     THE SESSION FLAGS, written once at 0x62667 as r14d & ~0x10.
                      Used ONLY for `& 2` (48 vs sv_maxclients) at 0xAD2EB and as
                      arg1 to SV_AllocateClientMemory at 0xAD391. It does NOT gate
                      whether the allocation happens.

Also established: `sub_79370` (which Lobby_LoadMapForSession and SV_SpawnServer use
to build sub_62430's argument) **returns 0**, so every caller of sub_62430 passes a
session-flags value of 1, 3, 7 or 0x11 -- none of which carries bit 1 (0x2). So the
`(flags & 2) ? 48` branch at 0xAD363 appears to be dead on all observed paths, and
maxClients comes from sv_maxclients. NOT exhaustively proven (the RUNTIME_FUNCTION
entry means there may be paths IDA has not attributed).

## ⭐⭐⭐ AND THAT EXPLAINS THE CRASH — THE LATCH IS SET ONCE AND NEVER CLEARED

Per this file's own asset work, already MEASURED in game:

    DB_LoadLevelXAssets:  v11 = 396;  if (!sub_38F590()) v11 = 512;
                          DB_LoadXAssets({NULL, 0, v11}, 1, 3)
    MEASURED: sub_38F590() == 0, so the mask is 512, and NO LOADED ZONE CARRIES
    BIT 0x200 -- the release is a guaranteed no-op. Zones only ever accumulate
    (11 -> 14 -> 16 -> 17 across a session, released count 0).

Combine that with the lifecycle:

    free  (DB_LoadXAssets)            needs a RELEASED zone with flags & 0x108
                                      -> never happens, because nothing is released
                                      -> dword_27D10F0 is NEVER cleared
    alloc (DB_TryLoadXFileInternal)   needs dword_27D10F0 == 0
                                      -> so it runs EXACTLY ONCE, at the FIRST zone
                                         load carrying flags & 0x108

Map zones carry flag 8 and `<map>_load` carries 0xA, and `common_core_mp` (flags 8)
is in the MENU baseline zone list -- so the one-and-only reservation happens EARLY,
at boot, sized from whatever sv_maxclients holds at that moment.

**THAT is why raising sv_maxclients at the menu produced "Memory Error: 6 161":**
the hunk had already been reserved for the boot-time value, the latch prevented any
re-reservation, and SV_Init then allocated svs.clients for the raised value out of
the smaller hunk. Hunk_Alloc's `if (newTop > hunk[0]) Hunk_RaiseMemoryError(6,161)`.

This is now fully consistent with every prior measurement, and it CORRECTS the
"NOT YET EXPLAINED" note left one section above.

## THE REQUIREMENT, STATED PRECISELY

sv_maxclients must be raised **before the first zone load carrying zoneFlags & 0x108**
-- i.e. before `common_core_mp` loads at boot, not at the menu. The mod is injected
into a SUSPENDED process by Launch-S2.ps1, so that window exists.

STILL UNPROVEN and required before any attempt:
  - that `common_core_mp` really is the first flags-8 zone (the flag values in this
    file are from a live `demo_zones` dump, so they are observed, but which zone
    loads FIRST with 0x108 is not directly measured)
  - what the boot-time value of sv_maxclients actually is
  - whether anything between boot and SV_Init re-clamps it
  - the quadratic cost: ~33 MB at 18 vs ~106 MB at 48, so a large raise materially
    increases the reservation and may fail for ordinary memory reasons

DO NOT reinstate a naive latch. The old one wrote at the menu, which this section
now proves is always too late.

# ⭐⭐ msg_t FULLY NAMED FROM IW8 — FOUR S2 UNKNOWNS RESOLVED (2026-08-11)

Source: `client/engine/iw8/msg_t.hpp` in **iw8-mod** (Modern Warfare 2019 client
mod, cloned to `../iw8-mod`). It is a community-reconstructed but NAMED struct
carrying a size assert, and it matches S2's hand-derived layout field for field.

S2's layout was derived independently from MSG_Init @0xDC750 and MSG_BeginReading
@0xDC690 and recorded earlier in this file with four fields marked UNKNOWN. IW8
names all of them, and the total size agrees exactly.

    off   IW8 name              S2's note before this
    0x00  m_Overflowed          "cleared on BeginReading [overflow-ish]"   confirmed
    0x04  m_ReadOnly            "set to 1 by Init [UNKNOWN]"               ⭐ RESOLVED
    0x08  m_Data                "data pointer" PROVEN
    0x10  m_SplitData           "second data pointer, 0 on Init [split data?]" confirmed
    0x18  m_MaxSize             "size" PROVEN
    0x1C  m_CurSize             "size" PROVEN
    0x20  m_SplitSize           "0 on Init"                                ⭐ RESOLVED
    0x24  m_ReadCount           "read cursor"
    0x28  m_Bit                 "bit position"
    0x2C  m_LastEntityRef       S2's msg+44                                ⭐ NAMED
    0x30  m_TargetLocalNetID    (netsrc_t) -- S2 +48, previously unremarked
    0x34  m_CompressionFlags    S2 called this "useZlib"                   ⭐ RECLASSIFIED
    ENGINE_ASSERT_SZ(msg_t, 0x38)  == 56 bytes. S2 derived 56 independently.

## ⭐ +44 IS `lastEntityRef` — AND THAT CONFIRMS THE 4780 WORK

This file already records, from S2's own code:

    sub_665C00(msg)                 is just `*(DWORD*)(msg + 44) = -1`
                                    (renamed MSG_ResetDeltaIndex)
    MSG_ReadMonotonicDeltaIndex     uses msg[44] as the running index:
                                    `idx = ++msg[44]`, `if (idx <= msg[44]) "4780"`

IW8 names that field **m_LastEntityRef**. So the "monotonic delta index" is the
LAST ENTITY REFERENCE, which is exactly why it must strictly increase across an
entity list and why 2047 terminates it. An independent confirmation of the whole
delta-index investigation, from a different game.

`MSG_ResetDeltaIndex` is therefore well named; consider `MSG_ReadDeltaEntityRef`
for 0x66B9E0 if it is ever revisited (NOT renamed yet -- the current name is
accurate and renaming has its own cost).

## ⚠ +52 IS FLAGS, NOT A BOOL

S2 treats msg+52 as the "useZlib" gate, and CL_ParseServerMessage does branch on it
being non-zero. IW8 calls it **m_CompressionFlags**. So it is a FLAGS WORD and
zlib-vs-other is probably one bit of several. Nothing currently depends on it being
boolean -- the demo path only ever sees 0 or 1 there -- but do not assume a future
non-zero value means zlib.

## PROVENANCE, STATED HONESTLY

iw8-mod's structures are COMMUNITY-RECONSTRUCTED, not official symbols. They are
strong evidence because (a) the struct carries a compile-time size assert that
matches S2's independently derived 56 bytes, and (b) every field S2 had already
proven lines up. But a name from there is STRONG INFERENCE for S2, not PROVEN.
Where a field matters, re-confirm against S2's own code as usual.

## The general lesson

**The IW-engine message/demo layer is highly conserved across titles.** Where one
title in the family has a name, the others very likely have the same field. The
reference set is now S2 (13337), AW (12345, fully symboled), MW3 (14200), MWR-PS4
(9999, debug build) and now IW8 structures in `../iw8-mod/client/engine/iw8/`
(~8400 lines: usercmd_s, netadr_t, ClActiveClient, ClServerInfo, gentity_s,
connstate_t, SvClientConnectionState and more).

# ⭐ THE JOIN GATE — the missing half of force host (build 8F4289EF, 2026-08-11)

Force host had TWO halves and only one was implemented:

    PERMISSION to host   Session_CanHostServer  -- relaxed in 428B90C0/7C962E89
                         (requireOpenNat cleared, the ten thresholds zeroed)
    ACTUALLY becoming    refuse other people's lobbies until the engine gives up
    the lobby host       searching and hosts instead        <- WAS MISSING

The second is what the user's own earlier tool relied on ("blocked joins to other
lobbies until the game made them lobby host; other players then joined them"), and
it went out with the zero-hook rebuild. Nothing else in the current build stops
matchmaking placing you in a stranger's lobby, which is exactly the reported symptom
across three test sessions.

## The hook, and why THIS target is safe

    Lobby_AcceptSearchResult  IDA 0x29BFF0 - 0x1000 = 0x29AFF0
    bool __fastcall sub_29BFF0(__int64 a1, unsigned int a2, char a3)

RULE A17: the return is **bool**. Do not widen it.

RULE A19 says a hook is never truly passive -- so the target was chosen for being
the closest thing to it in the subsystem. The whole body is:

    Params = Lobby_GetParams(*(QWORD*)(a1+16));
    v8 = *(DWORD*)(sub_29CEA0(results, a2) + 8*a3 + 84);   // result status
    v9 = *(BYTE*)(33216*a3 + Params + 1016);               // per-client state
    v10 = dvar || sub_480F10(Params, a3);
    return v9 >= 5 && v10 && v8 == 1;

A **pure predicate**: three reads and a boolean. No writes, no forwarding into real
work, nothing unwinds behind it. Returning false means precisely "do not accept this
candidate". (It also re-confirms status at +84 with 1 == joinable, matching
Search_GetJoinableCount's `(status-1) <= 1` and Search_HasQosResult's `> 1`.)

RULE A3.1 checked: nothing else in src/ hooks this address.

## The safety design — it cannot leave the user stuck

Matchmaking-path hooks broke matchmaking once and the culprit was never isolated,
so this one is built to fail safe:

  * armed ONLY while force host is ON and we are not already host / in a session
  * **disarms itself the moment it succeeds** (AreWeHost != 0, or a session exists)
    and says so: "✔ YOU ARE THE HOST. Join gate released after refusing N lobbies"
  * **disarms itself after 90 s** if it never became host, and says so, so the worst
    case is an ordinary match rather than being unable to find any game
  * `s2mp_nojoingate.txt` next to the exe kills the install entirely (RULE A20)
  * the stub calls the ORIGINAL first and only overrides a `true`, so a result the
    engine already rejected is passed through untouched

## Reporting (RULE A15 — the user should not have to diagnose)

`fh_status` now always prints the join gate line -- installed/armed/idle and the
refusal count -- and the bandwidth-test term, which is the one gate in
Session_CanHostServer that cannot be relaxed with dvars. If the gate is NOT
installed, tick() says so out loud rather than silently doing nothing.

## Status

Built, deployed, hash-verified 8F4289EF. NOT tested in game, so per the Fix
Declaration Rules this is a CANDIDATE.

What would confirm it: the `✔ YOU ARE THE HOST` line. What would falsify it: the
90-second give-up line, in which case `fh_canhost` names which term of
Session_CanHostServer refused -- most likely `bandwidthTest NOT COMPLETE`, which is
the only term left that we cannot open from a dvar.

## ⛔ THE JOIN GATE'S FIRST VERSION NEVER GUARDED ANYTHING (fixed, build 6B1C0925)

Tested 2026-08-12. Still placed in someone else's lobby. The console log named the
bug in one line, with no probing and no effort from the user:

    [host] join gate hook: OK (orig=00007FF7B18200C0)      <- installed correctly
    [host] HOSTING — now refusing other people's lobbies...
    [host] ✔ YOU ARE THE HOST. Join gate released after refusing 0 lobbies
    [host] HOSTING — now refusing other people's lobbies...

**Refused 0 lobbies**, and the arm/disarm pair repeats -- it was oscillating.

CAUSE, and it is mine: the disarm test was `we_host || have_session`. **You are
already AreWeHost of your own party lobby, with a session, before matchmaking even
starts.** So the success condition was true on the very first frame: the gate armed,
immediately declared victory, disarmed, re-armed, and was never up while the search
actually ran. The hook was fine; the arming logic was not.

FIX: arm on CONNECTION STATE instead -- guard while at the menu/searching, stand
down once genuinely in a game.

    clientConnectionState  IDA 0x1BAF4E4 - 0x1000 = 0x1BAE4E4
    (byte_1BAF450 + 148, dword, stride 1976 per client; >= 9 PRIMED, 10 ACTIVE)

    armed  = g_enabled && connstate < 9 && !gave_up
    disarm = in a game (report refusal count + AreWeHost, honestly, either way)
           | 90 s timeout (say so, let them play, re-arm on a fresh toggle)
           | force host turned off

Also removed the false "✔ YOU ARE THE HOST" claim. On entering a game it now reports
`connstate`, the refusal count and `AreWeHost=` and lets those speak, rather than
asserting a win it cannot actually observe.

### ⚠ LESSON — A SUCCESS CONDITION MUST NOT BE TRUE BEFORE THE WORK STARTS

`AreWeHost` and `have_session` describe the PARTY LOBBY, not the match. Both are
true at the menu. Any "did it work" test built on them fires instantly and hides the
fact that nothing happened. Before using a flag as a success signal, check what it
reads in the IDLE state -- if it is already set, it is not a success signal.

This is the same family as the earlier "never verify a fix using the value the fix
writes" note: here the fix verified itself against state that was already true.

## GRIIMS-WWII-Tool — what its ForceHost ACTUALLY does (read 2026-08-12)

The user's own tool works where ours does not, so it was read directly rather than
guessed at. `griim/fucntions.cpp:95`:

    void ForceHost() {
        *(BYTE*)Addr(oDisableJoining) = 0;      // 0x928BEA0
        *(BYTE*)Addr(oMaxPlayers1..5) = maxPlayers;
        *(BYTE*)Addr(oMinPlayers)     = minPlayers;
    }

Called ONCE, from the checkbox in host.cpp. `Addr(x) = ModuleBase() + x`, i.e. **no
0x1000 adjustment -- their offsets are IDA addresses directly**, matching this
project's own `VA = base + IDA` rule. Their `CbufAddress = 0x7729B0` is the same
critical-section function in our IDB, so the offsets do transfer.

⭐ NOTE THE DIRECTION: it writes **0** to a flag named *DisableJoining*, i.e. it
CLEARS a joining-disabled flag. That ENABLES joining -- it does not block joins.
So whatever makes their tool work, it is NOT "refuse other people's lobbies", and
the user's recollection of their own tool's mechanism (and my restatement of it)
should be treated as unreliable.

⛔ DO NOT REPLICATE THE POKE AS-IS. At 0x928BEA0 the dump holds a clean 16-byte
record `{qword ptr, dword size, 0x8043xxxx}`, repeating either side:

    0928BE90  F8 9D 62 BF 01 00 00 00  14 2E 00 00  00 00 43 80
    0928BEA0  0C CC 62 BF 01 00 00 00  D4 A4 00 00  00 00 43 80   <- oDisableJoining
    0928BEB0  E0 70 63 BF 01 00 00 00  CC 2B 02 00  00 00 43 80

That reads as an ALLOCATION TRACKING TABLE, and writing a byte at +0 clobbers the
low byte of a pointer (0x1BF62CC0C -> 0x1BF62CC00). It has zero xrefs and no name.
It may well be something else at the moment their tool writes it -- heap trackers
move -- but poking it on this evidence would violate the Absolute Rule outright.

OPEN: what their ForceHost actually achieves, and whether the five maxplayers byte
pokes (already PROVEN here to crash SV_ChangeMaxClients by raising the count without
reallocating svs.clients) are load-bearing or incidental.

# ⛔ KILLED — "the Xbox/Microsoft Store PC build of WWII runs pure peer-to-peer"
# (2026-08-12, ~10 minutes, entirely offline)

USER HYPOTHESIS: the Xbox app (GDK/Microsoft Store) build of WWII runs P2P rather
than on Demonware dedicated servers, so diffing it against the Steam build would
expose the hosting path we cannot find.

Dumped to `F:\WWII XBOX Dump\s2_mp64_ship_dump.exe` (322 MB), IDA MCP port 12346,
server name **S2-Xbox** (launcher `F:\Coding\ida-launchers\ida-s2xbox-12346.bat`).

**RESULT: DISPROVEN. Do not re-run this.** The Store build uses the SAME lobby /
matchmaking / dedicated-server architecture as the Steam build. Xbox Live is used
only for identity, presence, privacy, achievements, social and INVITES.

## It IS genuinely the Store build (so the test was valid)

    SteamAPI / ISteamMatchmaking / steam_api64.dll   ABSENT
    XCurl.dll        STATICALLY IMPORTED, 18 functions   <- GDK-only component
    xgameruntime.dll present as a string (dynamically loaded, not a static import)
    XboxLive         present (absent from the Steam build)

## The decisive evidence — WHICH Xbox Live APIs

Every Xbl*/XGame*/XUser* token in .rdata:

    XGameRuntimeInitialize    XUserAddAsync            XAsyncGetStatus / XAsyncOp
    XblInitialize             XblPresenceSetPresenceAsync
    XblMultiplayerActivitySetActivityAsync      XblPrivacyCheckPermissionAsync
    XblMultiplayerActivityGetActivityAsync      XblPrivacyBatchCheckPermissionAsync
    XblMultiplayerActivitySendInvitesAsync      XblPrivacyGetAvoidListAsync
    XblMultiplayerActivityDeleteActivityAsync   XblProfileGetUserProfilesForSocialGroupAsync
    XblAchievementsUpdateAchievementAsyncInternal
    XblSocialManagerExtraDetailLevel            XblStringVerifyStringsAsync

⭐ **`XblMultiplayerSession*` / MPSD IS COMPLETELY ABSENT.**

That is the whole answer. `XblMultiplayerActivity` is the LIGHTWEIGHT "this player is
in a joinable activity" + invites API -- presence and invite plumbing. It is NOT
session management and NOT matchmaking. MPSD (`XblMultiplayerSession*`) is the API a
genuinely P2P/Xbox-Live-hosted title would use, and it is not linked at all.

## And the game architecture is byte-for-byte the same shape

The GSC binding table names, checked individually (see the method note below):

    Steam GSC bindings present in the Xbox build:  78 / 78
    Missing from the Xbox build:                   NONE
    Host/P2P-ish names the Xbox build ADDS:        NONE
      SelectHostAsServer, BecomeHost, MakeHost, HostAsServer, StartHosting,
      IsListenServer, IsP2P, PeerToPeer, XblMultiplayerSession, MultiplayerSession,
      JoinViaPresence, ShowInviteUI  -- ALL ABSENT

Same `AllowGameBattlesListenServers`, `IsRestrictedToListenServers`,
`matchmaking_allowJoiningListenServer`, `requireOpenNat`, `party_minlobbytime`,
`gamePreventListenServer`, `CanHostServer`, `AreWeHost`, the whole DS-acquire set.

## ⭐ THE ONE LIVE THREAD THIS DID PRODUCE

`XblMultiplayerActivitySendInvitesAsync` is present, and `SendInvite` appears in
.rdata. That is a real "invite someone straight into my game" path that **bypasses
matchmaking entirely** -- it does not need the matchmaker to route strangers to us.
If force host ever works well enough to hold a match, invites are how other people
would get in without fighting the matchmaker. Not yet investigated on either build.

## ⚠ METHOD NOTE — a false result I caught and must not repeat

My first binding-table diff walked a "contiguous NUL-separated string blob" starting
at `IsJoinComplete`, as the Steam build lays them out. In THIS build the strings are
not contiguous, so the walk stopped after 3 names and the diff reported 75 bindings
"missing from the Xbox build" -- a completely false result produced entirely by the
method. Re-running as an individual `find()` per name gave 78/78.

**Generalise: when a structural assumption (contiguity, stride, ordering) is carried
from one binary to another, a diff built on it reports the ASSUMPTION failing as a
DIFFERENCE.** Verify the assumption in the new binary, or use a method that does not
depend on it. This is the same family as the earlier `get_func()` mis-attribution.

## What this cost, and what it bought

~10 minutes, and it closed a line of work that would otherwise have absorbed days.
It also independently CONFIRMS that our S2 architecture map is complete: if a hosting
primitive existed anywhere in this game, the Store build's 78-entry table would have
shown it. It does not exist. Force host has to be made to work with the bindings we
already have.

## XBOX BUILD NAMED — 587 functions ported from the Steam IDB (2026-08-12)

IDB: `F:\WWII XBOX Dump\s2_mp64_ship_dump.exe.i64`, MCP **S2-Xbox** on port 12346.

Same-game string-anchor port. Far cleaner than the cross-title AW pass, as expected:

    Steam analyst-named functions scanned      900
    uniquely-owned anchor strings             4001   (516 functions carry one)
    anchors resolving to ONE xbox function    3191
    candidate xbox functions                   505
      unanimous                                504      split votes: 0
    APPLIED                                    500      (280 backed by 2+ anchors)
      + GSC bindings named from the table        77
      + workers reached from those bindings       9
    ---------------------------------------------------
    named in the xbox IDB                      587

Rejected on purpose: 4 names claimed by 2+ xbox functions (Com_InitDvars,
PartyAtomic_OnError_Failed and two others). Call-graph propagation added ZERO --
every Steam function with a usable call fingerprint had already been ported by the
string pass.

Every ported function carries a comment recording the anchor count and this warning:
**ADDRESSES DIFFER between the builds; only the NAME is ported.**

### The GSC binding table in this build: 0xBEF700, 78 entries

Found by locating the string "IsJoinComplete" (0xBEFDB8) and searching for a qword
equal to that address. Same {const char* name, void* fn} 16-byte stride. Self-naming,
so all 78 are PROVEN BY NAME, and they are the route to the small dvar predicates
that have no strings of their own (CanHostServer, IsAlwaysSearch, GetNatType, ...).

### VALIDATION — the port is verifiably correct

`MSG_ReadMonotonicDeltaIndex` decompiles structurally IDENTICAL to the Steam version:
same `a2 != 11` special case, same "4780"/"4781" error ids, and the running index is
`a1[11]` -- dword index 11 == byte offset 44 == **m_LastEntityRef**, matching both the
Steam analysis and IW8's named msg_t. Third independent binary, same answer.

## ⭐⭐ THE FINDING THAT MATTERS — Session_CanHostServer DIFFERS BETWEEN BUILDS

Xbox `Session_CanHostServer` @0x849380 (from Script_CanHostServer):

    if (systemlink) return 1;
    if (!g_hostingEnabled) return 0;
    if (LobbyParams_GetRequireOpenNat(a1)) { ...nat...; if (nat == 3) return 0; }
    if (LobbyParams_GetPrivate(a1) || dvar393) return 1;          <- early return
    v6 = requiredUpload(a2);
    if (measuredUpload >= v6 && requiredPing(a2) <= measuredPing) return 1;
    return 0;

Steam `Session_CanHostServer` @0x8534B0 has TWO things this build does NOT:

    if (Session_IsBandwidthTestComplete(unk_10DC800)) {   <- OUTER GATE, absent on Xbox
        ...the private/dvar393 escape and the upload/ping comparison...
        return 1;
    }
    if (g_hostingEnabled) g_hostingEnabled = 0;           <- LATCHES HOSTING OFF
    return 0;

**So the STEAM build carries an EXTRA host gate: an incomplete bandwidth test both
refuses hosting AND latches g_hostingEnabled off** (one-way -- Session_ClearHostingEnabled
can only ever clear). The Xbox build cannot get into that state at all.

That is exactly the one term this project identified as unopenable by dvar. It is a
real, structural difference between the two builds, not a version artefact, and it
raises the priority of the `bandwidthTest` line that fh_status already prints: on
Steam, if it reads NOT COMPLETE, hosting is impossible until it completes, and our
per-frame re-assert of g_hostingEnabled is fighting a latch that CanHostServer
re-applies on every call.

## ⭐ THE SNIPER BREATH-HOLD BLACK BORDER IS ids 13 / 16

USER: "there's also a black border that comes up when you hold your breath on
snipers, doesn't even disable with cg_draw2d".

That it survives cg_draw2D is not a mystery -- it is CONFIRMATION. **cg_draw2D gates
only the NATIVE 2D drawer** (sub_E7980, 4237 bytes, 61 callees). LUI elements are
drawn by the LUI renderer and are NOT in that path at all, so anything LUI-drawn is
immune to cg_draw2D by construction. The border being immune means it is LUI, and
therefore reachable by the model layer.

`currentWeapon.breathVisible` (13) and `currentWeapon.holdingBreath` (16) are exactly
the inputs a breath vignette widget would subscribe to. Blanking them publishes
0/false = "not holding breath, not visible", which should remove the border rather
than freeze it.

## THE GENERAL RULE THIS ESTABLISHES

    drawn by                     gated by cg_draw2D?   reachable by the model layer?
    native 2D HUD (sub_E7980)          YES                      no
    LUI, model-driven                  no                       YES  (blank it)
    LUI, event-driven (obituaries,     no                       no   (never publishes)
      score popups)
    native crosshair (hitmarkers)      YES                      no

So "cg_draw2D does not disable it" is a USEFUL DIAGNOSTIC, not a dead end: it proves
the element is LUI, which means the model layer can reach it. And conversely, anything
that DOES vanish with cg_draw2D can never be fixed by the model layer.

## ⛔ CORRECTION (same day) — THE cg_draw2D TABLE ABOVE IS WRONG

USER, immediately after: "you are wrong with the assumption on cg_draw2d, cos it does
infact disable everything, other than the bit I just mentioned".

So cg_draw2D disables the LUI HUD **as well as** the native 2D HUD. The table above
claiming "LUI, model-driven -> not gated by cg_draw2D" is FALSE and must not be used.

Why I got it wrong: I reasoned from `sub_E7980` being "the native 2D drawer" and
assumed LUI was rendered elsewhere. But sub_E7980 calls LUI_CoD_CheckForFFOTD among
its 61 callees, i.e. the cg_draw2D-gated function drives the LUI HUD too. The evidence
was in the callee list I had already printed, and I read past it.

### What this changes

  * cg_draw2D is ALL-OR-NOTHING for the HUD. It can never produce "everything except
    obituaries + score + hitmarkers" -- it takes those three as well (already recorded
    from the user's own earlier test, and now re-confirmed).
  * Therefore the ONLY route to a selective HUD is removing individual elements, i.e.
    the blanking mechanism (demo_hud_only, build D2DD5450).
  * "cg_draw2D does not disable it" is NOT evidence that something is LUI. It is
    evidence the thing is drawn OUTSIDE the whole 2D pass.

### ⭐ AND THAT RELOCATES THE SNIPER BREATH-HOLD BORDER

Since cg_draw2D kills everything else and the border survives, the border is not a HUD
element at all -- not native 2D, not LUI. It is drawn in the view / post-process pass.

RULED OUT so far:
  * the LUI model layer -- ids 13/16 (breathVisible / holdingBreath) feed LUI widgets,
    and those die with cg_draw2D like the rest, so they are not what draws the border
  * CG_DrawViewWeapon @0x2FC80 -- decompiled its full callee list, no overlay/fullscreen
    material draw; its only WeaponDef slot accessors are the viewmodel/worldmodel ones
    (sub_3B6E40 slots 0x10/0x18 and 0x388/0x390)

STILL UNKNOWN. Leading candidate is a post-process / vision-set effect applied while
holding breath. NEXT TRACE (not yet done): find the NATIVE reader of the hold-breath
player state -- sub_356560's handler for source id 16 returns it to LUI, so the ps
field it reads is the anchor; xref that field and one of the readers will be the
effect. Do NOT chase the LUI models again; they are excluded.

# ⭐⭐⭐ THE LUI SURFACE — 664 BINDINGS, THE lua_State, AND THE ELEMENT ROOT
# (2026-08-12). This is the foundation for anything HUD-related.

Prompted by the user asking whether it would be easier to build a custom LUI. Answer:
you do not need to -- almost all of it is already exposed.

## g_luiLuaBindings @ IDA 0xB37F30 -- 664 entries

`luaL_Reg` shape {const char* name, lua_CFunction fn}, 16-byte stride, ends 0xB3A8B0.
SELF-NAMING (string and pointer in the same record) so every name is PROVEN, not
inferred. Full dump committed to **docs/lui_lua_bindings.txt**.

Registered by sub_140AE0 (its only referencer).

Highlights: GetLuiRoot, SetActiveMenu, Exec, ExecNow, ToggleScoreboard, TogglePause,
AddKeyCatcherSubscriber, the whole Dvar get/set family, Localize, TableLookup,
Inventory_*, AE_* (achievements), the Start*/Menu* flow.

## ⭐ qword_1BD3D08 IS THE LUI lua_State

From LUI_Init @0xC4460:

    qword_1BD3D08 = sub_AF9B70();     // create (through the Arxan dispatch thunk)
    sub_2D9B80(qword_1BD3D08, sub_C7050, 0, "LUI_LuaCall_RootUserData_GC", 0);
    sub_2D9B80(qword_1BD3D08, sub_C62E0, 0, "(LUI_LuaCall_ConstructLUIElement)", 0);
    ... ~20 more ...

So **sub_2D9B80(L, cfunc, 0, name, 0) registers a C function into the state.**
⚠ CLAUDE.md elsewhere calls qword_1BD3D08 "the script VM" in a GSC context
(Script_CallByName_ExpectInt, sub_BD020(0,"cgame_init_complete",qword_1BD3D08)).
LUI_Init assigns it and registers LUI functions into it. Whether GSC and LUI genuinely
share one state is NOT established -- do not assume either way.

## ⭐⭐ sub_318760(localClientNum) RETURNS THE LUI ELEMENT ROOT -- natively

From the GetLuiRoot binding (sub_109E10):

    v5 = sub_318760(clientNum);    // <- THE ROOT ELEMENT, a plain native pointer
    v6 = sub_C3990(v5, L);         // wrap as Lua userdata
    sub_CB280(v6, L);              // push

**So the element tree is reachable from C without touching Lua at all.** That is the
foundation for any real HUD control: walk the tree, identify, hide.

Partial LUIElement layout, from LUIElement_UIScorebarLayout @0x362470 (a2 = element):

    +16   flags qword (|= 2 during layout)      +156/+158  bytes (compared to each other)
    +28   float  rect edge                      +176  ptr
    +36   float  rect edge (bar width written   +200  child/next list ptr (-> sub_BB8C0)
          into one of these two)                +248/+256 ptrs (-> sub_BAD50)
    +148  word   model/source index (-> sub_356430)

The 11 LUIElement_*Layout functions are per-ELEMENT-TYPE handlers
(UIScorebar, UIIntWatch, UICountdown, UIHorizontalList, UITechyDigits, UIBindImage),
so element TYPE is identifiable by which layout runs.

## NO READY-MADE WAY TO RUN LUA

There is no lui_dostring / lua console command; `luafile` is only the asset type name.
`hks__base_loadfile` (0x2BA230) and `hks__base_load_reader` (0x2C9C00) are the BASE
LIBRARY implementations of load/loadfile (lua_CFunction, args on the Lua stack), not
the C API. **luaL_loadbuffer and lua_pcall are NOT yet identified** -- 109 hks/lua*
functions are named and neither is among them. Finding them is the remaining gap for
arbitrary Lua execution.

Since sub_318760 gives the root natively, the tree route does NOT depend on closing
that gap.

## ⛔ CORRECTION — ui_hide_hud ET AL ARE **OMNVARS**, NOT DVARS (2026-08-12)

I registered them as dvars (build D9F2EA75). That was WRONG and the build did nothing.
The dumped LUI bytecode shows it plainly -- the constant table around them:

    #295  GetLuiRoot / Game / GetOmnvar / ui_hide_hud / GetDvarBool / 2562
    #600  registerOmnvarHandler / ui_session_state / ui_hide_hud / ui_killstreak_remote
          registerDvarHandler / 2454 / 2562 / 2523

The DVARs beside them are NUMERIC (2562 == cg_draw2D) exactly as S2 dvars always are.
The `ui_hide_*` names go to GetOmnvar / registerOmnvarHandler. Omnvar names live in
the NetConstStrings TYPE 23 table, which is why none of them appears in .rdata.

### ⭐ THE OMNVAR API — all native, no Lua needed (from SetOmnvar, sub_185250)

    sub_768FC0(name)          -> index, 0xFFFFFFFF if not registered
    sub_768D40(client, index) -> storage slot
    sub_768F80(index)         -> def:  +8 flags (&4 == CLIENT SCOPE), +12 type,
                                       +32 int bias
    sub_769520(slot)          -> notify changed  <- what makes LUI react
    types: 1 bool (BYTE @slot+4) | 2 float | 3/4 int (value - bias) | 5 string
    also sub_768B10(client, name, &out, 0, 0) -- GetOmnvar by name

Shipped as the `omnvar <name> [value]` command (build 36559DB5). It resolves, checks
client scope, writes the typed value and notifies -- the same five steps the engine's
own SetOmnvar performs.

### ⚠ MEASURED: THE WRITE WORKS, THE HUD DOES NOT CHANGE

User: "it notified but didn't disable it still". So the omnvar path is correct and the
notify fires -- but the widgets do not hide. The reason is visible in the same bytecode:

    #453..#500   BroadcasterLayerHud / setAlpha / Scorestreak_List
                 MatchScoresWidget0  / setAlpha / broadcasterShowHud
                 WeaponInfoWidget0   / setAlpha / broadcasterShowHud
                 ObituaryWidget0     / setAlpha / broadcasterShowHud
                 Talkers_List, VictimPlayerCardWidget0, SplashesWidget0 ... same
    #330         IsHardcoreMode / Broadcaster / IsBroadcaster / IsHubMode / ui_hide_minimap

**`broadcasterShowHud` is the ALPHA VALUE for every one of those widgets, and the whole
block is gated on IsBroadcaster.** It is read through `BroadcasterUtils.ProfileVarBool`,
i.e. a LUI-side profile var -- NOT an omnvar and NOT a dvar. So the ui_hide_* omnvars
are secondary switches; the master control is broadcaster mode.

DEAD ENDS ruled out while chasing this (do not repeat):
  * sub_6891F0 is SL_GetString (string interning), NOT a profile-var getter.
  * broadcaster_mode @0xB88C00 is an INFO-STRING key read server-side via
    Info_ValueForKey in sub_547A90, and written by Dvar_InfoString from some prior
    predicate -- not a plain settable client dvar.

NEXT, if this is picked up again: find how IsBroadcaster becomes true and how
BroadcasterUtils.ProfileVarBool resolves (LUI bindings GetProfileData/SetProfileData
are in docs/lui_lua_bindings.txt). Broadcaster mode is a SHIPPED minimal-HUD feature;
enabling it is worth more than fighting individual widgets.

# ⭐⭐⭐⭐ BROADCASTER MODE IS THE MINIMAL HUD, AND IT IS FULLY MAPPED (2026-08-12)

The user's request — "keep only obituaries, score popup and hitmarkers" — is a
feature that SHIPS in this game. Recovered end to end from the binary plus the
dumped LUI Lua, with no game run.

## ⛔ CORRECTION — my reachability table was WRONG about event-driven LUI

An earlier entry in this file states:

    LUI, event-driven (obituaries, score popups)   reachable by the model layer? no

That is too strong and is withdrawn. Event-driven LUI IS reachable, through
**omnvars**: `splasheswidget_uc.lua` does `registerOmnvarHandler` and
`PushSplashOmnvars`, and the splash medals arrive as `ui_player_splash_id_<n>` /
`ui_player_splash_param_<n>`. The score popup is `ui_points_popup_event`. So the
omnvar notify is a second, independent lever on the half the model layer cannot
touch. 460 distinct `ui_*` omnvar names were extracted from the Lua dump.

## ⭐ THE MECHANISM — mphud_uc.lua drives per-widget setAlpha

`ui/s2/mphud_uc.lua` carries a `{SettingName, Function}` table feeding
`broadcasterShowHud(widget, BroadcasterUtils.ProfileVarBool(setting))`, which is a
per-widget `setAlpha`:

    broadcaster_inventory        -> WeaponInfoWidget0
    broadcaster_teamscore        -> MatchScoresWidget0      <- the blue/red score boxes
    broadcaster_scorestreaks     -> Scorestreak_List
    broadcaster_killfeed         -> ObituaryWidget0
    broadcaster_objective_status -> PlayerAliveCount / SD / Hardpoint / CTF / Uplink
    broadcaster_voipdock         -> Talkers_List
    broadcaster_calloutcards     -> VictimPlayerCardWidget0
    broadcaster_minimap          (via the broadcaster_minimap_change event)
    broadcaster_playernotifications / broadcaster_scorestreaks_notification
                                 -> SplashesWidget (the splash medals)

**`pointsPopup` is NOT in that table**, so the score popup survives. Hitmarkers are
native (the sub_E7980 path) and are not LUI at all, so they survive. That is the
requested set exactly, with the engine's own granularity.

## PROVEN — the settings are a DDL blob in the local profile

    ProfileVarValue(name)      = Broadcaster.GetBroadcasterSettings():get(name)
    SetProfileVarValue(name,v) = Broadcaster.GetBroadcasterSettings():set(name,v)
                                 Engine.Exec("updategamerprofile")

    LUI binding table @0xB61A70 (23 entries, separate from the 664-entry table):
        IsBroadcaster           0x33E550
        GetBroadcasterSettings  0x340800

    GetBroadcasterSettings(client):
        if (sub_46B6A0(client,0)) push DDL wrapper else push nil
        sub_46B6A0(c,0) = byte_8BE0A20[6920*c]          <- THE GATE
        sub_46ABF0(c,0) = &off_8BE09F0 + 865*c          <- DDL state (865 qwords = 6920 B)

    sub_46B760 (profile load) builds it:
        qword_8BDEF18 = <find asset> "mp/ddl/broadcastersettings.ddl"
        sub_8E940(0x8BDFB35 + 6920*c, 1024, ddl, 0x8BE09F0 + 6920*c, 0, 0)
        byte_8BE0A20[6920*c] = result
        source text = mp/broadcastersettings.txt via the gamer profile

### ⭐ THE DDL CURSOR API, transcribed from sub_46B760 — NOT inferred

sub_46B760 sets `broadcaster_hasbeenread` with exactly this sequence, so the same
sequence sets any field:

    r      = sub_A1C8E0(scratch40, ((void**)qword_8BDEF18)[0]);   // root cursor
    cur[0] = ((__int128*)r)[0];  cur[1] = ((__int128*)r)[1];      // 32-byte cursor
    sub_A1D010(cur, cur, "<field name>");                          // navigate by NAME
    sub_A1D4D0(cur, 0x8BE09F0 + 6920*client, value);               // WRITE
    sub_A1C860(cur, 0x8BE09F0 + 6920*client)                       // read

## PROVEN — how IsBroadcaster is decided

`sub_33E550`'s tail, under the Arxan flattening:

    v56 = localClientNum;  v57 = sub_411BE0(v56);
    if (CL_IsDemoPlaying(v56)) return 0;                  // pushes nothing -> nil
    cg = CG_GetLocalClientGlobals(v56);
    result = 0;
    if (*(DWORD*)(cg + 3878300 + 4704*v57))               // gate
        result = (*(BYTE*)(cg + 4405240 + 152*v57) != 0); // <- the clientinfo flag

⚠ NOTE: broadcaster is explicitly DISABLED during demo playback (the demo branch
returns before pushing). So this cannot be used to clean up the theater HUD.

The flag is replicated, not local. The full round trip:

    Dvar_InfoString @0x664C62:
        v10 = signedIn(a1) && sub_4813D0(sub_856250(a1));
        userinfo "broadcaster_mode" = v10 ? "1" : "0"       <- NOT a dvar, computed
    sub_4813D0(id):
        L = Lobby_Get(0); P = sub_470F20(L)
        find member i where (state@P+33216*i+1016 & 0xFD) && id@P+33216*i+21568 == id
        return *(DWORD*)(P + 33216*i + 1288)                <- per-member broadcaster dword
    SV_UserinfoChanged @0x547A90 (server):
        *(BYTE*)(client + 23223) = (atoi(userinfo["broadcaster_mode"]) == 1)
    -> replicated in clientinfo (stride 152, the same array byte_A2BAEA4 uses)
    -> cg + 4405240 + 152*slot, which IsBroadcaster reads

The 33216 member stride independently matches `Lobby_AcceptSearchResult`'s state
byte at +1016, so the member layout is cross-checked.

## ⚠ THE ONE HAZARD — BROADCASTER MODE UNBINDS KEYS ON PC

`broadcasterlayerhud_uc.lua`:

    CONDITIONS.IsPC -> Engine.ExecNow("exec mp/broadcaster_unbind_keys.cfg")

BroadcasterLayerHud is built only when IsBroadcaster, so forcing IsBroadcaster true
runs that unbind. Reversible with `exec keys_mp.cfg` (the user's binds live in
players2/keys_mp.cfg — checked, it holds only ordinary gameplay binds), but any
implementation MUST restore them and MUST be opt-in.

## ⭐⭐ qword_1BD3D08 IS THE LUI lua_State, AND NATIVE->LUI CALLS EXIST

From LUI init (sub_318A4B), every LUI helper takes it as its last argument:

    LUI_Init      0xC4460    (already named)
    sub_C6150(moduleName, L)          load+run a LUI module by dotted name
                                      ("LUI.mp_menus.main")
    sub_C3990(elementName, L)         get an element by name ("UIRootFull")
    sub_BD540(0, element, "init_lui", L)   CALL A METHOD/EVENT BY NAME on an element
    sub_CC3E0("immediate", flag, L)   sub_BE860(L)   sub_BE8D0/sub_C5F80 stack guards

⛔ CORRECTION: an earlier entry calls `Script_CallByName_ExpectInt` @0x2A5860 a GSC
driver and concludes "the matchmaking space is decided by SCRIPT ... needs the
LUI/GSC scripts unpacked". It drives **qword_1BD3D08**, i.e. the LUI Lua state, and
its error text ("Expecting an integer on top of the stack after calling '%s'") is a
Lua stack message. So that call is native->LUI, and the matchmaking-space question
is answerable by calling it — not a dead end.

This is the cleanest lever in the whole area: with a native call-by-name we can
drive the game's own widgets instead of manufacturing state.

## SHIPPED — src/hud/broadcaster.{hpp,cpp}, build AE62479C (2026-08-13)

Deployed and hash-verified. NOT yet run in game, so per the Fix Declaration Rules
this is a **CANDIDATE**, not "fixed".

Commands: `hud_on` / `hud_off` / `hud_minimal <0|1>`, `hud_settings` (name, current
value, preset value, what it controls), `hud_set <name> <0|1>`, `hud_binds`.

### ZERO HOOKS

The module installs none. Its once-per-frame latch is a CALL-OUT from
demo_native's existing `CG_PublishHudModel` stub, on **desc == 100**
(`cg.Shared.connectionStateActive`) — published at the top of sub_357AD0 OUTSIDE
the connstate gate, so it fires exactly once per frame, on the client thread, with
cg known valid. Off, it costs one relaxed atomic load; the other ~69 publishes per
frame are untouched.

### What it writes, and where each address came from

    settings   DDL cursor sequence transcribed VERBATIM from sub_46B760, which
               sets "broadcaster_hasbeenread" the same way:
                 MakeRootCursor(scratch, *(void**)qword_8BDEF18)   0xA1C8E0
                 copy 32 bytes -> cursor
                 MoveToName(cursor, cursor, name)                  0xA1D010
                 SetInt(cursor, 0x8BE09F0 + 6920*client, value)    0xA1D4D0
               refuses outright when byte_8BE0A20[6920*c] == 0, because a zero
               gate means the blob never parsed and the buffer must not be written.

    IsBroadcaster   the ONE piece of manufactured state:
                 slot = *(BYTE*)(cg + 22904)                       sub_411BE0
                 gate = *(DWORD*)(cg + 3878300 + 4704*slot)        read only
                 flag =  (BYTE*)(cg + 4405240 + 152*slot)  <- latched to 1
               If the gate reads 0 it says so ONCE and writes nothing — writing
               the flag could not work in that state anyway.

RULE A1 arithmetic, written out rather than done in the head:

    byte_8BE0A20 gate     0x8BE0A20 - 0x1000 = 0x8BDFA20
    0x8BE09F0 DDL data    0x8BE09F0 - 0x1000 = 0x8BDF9F0
    qword_8BDEF18 def     0x8BDEF18 - 0x1000 = 0x8BDDF18
    sub_A1C8E0 root       0xA1C8E0  - 0x1000 = 0xA1B8E0
    sub_A1D010 move       0xA1D010  - 0x1000 = 0xA1C010
    sub_A1D4D0 set        0xA1D4D0  - 0x1000 = 0xA1C4D0
    sub_A1C860 get        0xA1C860  - 0x1000 = 0xA1B860

RULE A17 return widths, taken from the callee that DEFINES them (both are tail
calls, so only AL is defined): sub_A21940 -> `char`, sub_A1D6F0 -> `char`. The
decompiler types sub_A1D010 as `double` because of the thunk — that is wrong and
declaring it that way would corrupt the result.

### Reversibility

  * off by default; nothing is written until `hud_on`
  * every setting is READ AND SNAPSHOTTED before the first change, and `hud_off`
    restores the snapshot, drops the local flag and re-runs the bind restore
  * `exec keys_mp.cfg` is issued automatically at +1.5 s and +4 s after enabling,
    and again on disable, because the broadcaster layer runs
    `exec mp/broadcaster_unbind_keys.cfg` on PC when it builds. That command
    string is a literal the ENGINE itself uses (@0xB33C48), not one we invented.
    `hud_binds` repeats it on demand.

### What to expect, so the test is falsifiable

  gone:  minimap, ammo, score panel + its blue/red chrome, scorestreak list,
         splash medals, objective widgets, callout cards, voip dock
  kept:  obituaries (broadcaster_killfeed = 1), the score popup (`pointsPopup` is
         NOT in mphud_uc.lua's setting->widget table), hitmarkers (native)

If the HUD does not change, `hud_settings` names the cause: an unloaded blob, a
missing DDL field, or the cg gate being closed. It reports unconditionally
(RULE A15), so a run where nothing happens is still diagnostic.

### Known limitation

`IsBroadcaster` is evaluated when the HUD is built, so enabling mid-match may not
take effect until the next spawn/map. Enable before joining if it does not apply
immediately. Also: broadcaster mode is explicitly disabled during demo playback
(sub_33E550 returns early on CL_IsDemoPlaying), so this cannot clean up theater.

### ⛔ MEASURED — build AE62479C did almost nothing, and the reason was in my own header

USER, testing in THEATER: *"the only thing this whole thing does is change my
player arrow icons in the minimap"*, and again with the mode enabled before
`cl_demo_play`.

That result is exactly right and it is diagnostic, not a failure:

  * the minimap arrows changed  -> **the DDL writes landed.** The cursor sequence
    transcribed from sub_46B760 works; broadcaster settings are being written.
  * nothing else changed        -> **everything gated on IsBroadcaster is dead in
    a demo**, because sub_33E550 opens with
        `if (CL_IsDemoPlaying(client)) return 0;`   // pushes nothing -> nil
    so `broadcasterShowHud` / the setAlpha table never runs in theater.

broadcaster.hpp already recorded "NOT USABLE DURING DEMO PLAYBACK ... disabled in
theater by design" and I shipped anyway without acting on it. The whole point of
this mod is demo footage, so theater is the case that mattered.

### FIX — build 2FF8E06C: open that gate for ONE call site

`CL_IsDemoPlaying` is ALREADY hooked (demo_playback.cpp:3796), so per RULE A3.1
its existing stub is extended rather than a second hook installed:

    if (broadcaster::hide_demo_from_isbroadcaster(_ReturnAddress())) return false;

`hide_demo_from_isbroadcaster` returns true only when the minimal HUD is ON and
the return address lands inside sub_33E550. Off, it is one relaxed atomic load.

RULE A1, written out rather than done in the head:

    sub_33E550 (IsBroadcaster)  start 0x33E550, size 0x19EC
    range = [0x33E550, 0x33E550 + 0x19EC) = [0x33E550, 0x33FF3C)
    IDA = VA - module_base  (NO 0x1000 adjustment; game.cpp folds it into `base`)

It prints once when the gate first opens, so a run where it never fires is
distinguishable from a run where it fired and changed nothing (RULE A15).

### ⚠ New risk this introduces IN THEATER

With IsBroadcaster true during playback the broadcaster LAYER can build, which on
PC runs `exec mp/broadcaster_unbind_keys.cfg` and could take camera input. The
preset already sets every toolbar / player-list / camera quick-setting to 0, and
`exec keys_mp.cfg` is re-issued automatically; `hud_off` reverses everything. If
the demo camera misbehaves, `hud_off` is the undo.

### ⛔ FAILED ATTEMPT — broadcaster mode is a DIFFERENT HUD, not a filtered one

Filed under Failed Attempt Protection. **Do not retry without new evidence.**

**Attempt.** Reach the user's minimal HUD (keep obituaries + score popup +
hitmarkers) by turning on the game's own broadcaster/caster HUD and setting its
per-widget display settings, since mphud_uc.lua drives `setAlpha` from them.

**Result (measured in game, build 2FF8E06C, theater).** The theater gate worked —
`IsBroadcaster` became true during playback and the caster HUD engaged. But:

    minimap   gone
    killfeed  drawn as a WHITE BOX
    score popup   GONE
    user: "it's broadcaster mode used for cod tournaments I think"

**Reason the premise was wrong.** `broadcasterShowHud` does not filter the player
HUD — turning IsBroadcaster on REPLACES it with the caster HUD, which builds
BroadcasterLayerHud and swaps the obituary and points widgets for caster
equivalents. Those draw from `broadcaster_score_bg`, `broadcaster_team_base_bg`,
`broadcaster_event_minor_bg` etc., which are NOT loaded for a normal client, so
they render as white placeholder. The `{SettingName, Function}` table is real, but
it tunes a HUD you only get by becoming a caster, and that HUD is not the one the
user wants to film.

So the earlier entry "BROADCASTER MODE IS THE MINIMAL HUD" is **WITHDRAWN as a
solution**. What survives from it is still correct and useful as reference: the
DDL cursor API, the settings list, the IsBroadcaster round trip, and the theater
gate — the mechanism map is right, the conclusion drawn from it was not.

**Kept, relabelled** (build 1D9AD3E4): `hud_broadcaster 1|0`,
`hud_broadcaster_off`, `hud_settings`, `hud_set`, `hud_binds`. Renamed away from
`hud_on` / `hud_minimal` precisely so the name cannot imply "minimal HUD" again,
and the enable path now PRINTS what it actually is.

### WHERE THE MINIMAL HUD ACTUALLY STANDS

`demo_hud_only` (model blanking) remains the working approach. User-confirmed it
removes minimap, killstreak counter, ammo, division, perks, health, morale,
combat roles, clan tag, netPerf and hints. Two items remain:

  1. **score chrome** (the blue/red boxes) — MatchScoresWidget0's static children
     `FriendlyProgressBar` / `EnemyProgressBar` / `TeamIcon`. Blanking zeroes the
     numbers but a model value cannot remove a widget's background.
  2. **splash medals** — SplashesWidget, driven by the `ui_player_splash_id_<n>` /
     `ui_player_splash_param_<n>` omnvars (splasheswidget_uc.lua:
     `registerOmnvarHandler`, `PushSplashOmnvars`).

### ⛔ Levers checked and REJECTED this round, with the reason

  * `2523` — watched by mphud alongside cg_draw2D, so it looked like a HUD dvar.
    It is a game-state STRING dvar compared against "postgame" (sub_CCF20).
    `2454` = virtualLobbyInFiringRange, `5270` = lui_draw_hints. None is a
    granular HUD switch.
  * hooking `OmnvarNotifyChanged` sub_769520 to drop splash notifies — the
    function is only **21 bytes** (`mov edx,1 / cmp / cmovge / mov [rcx],edx /
    ret`) with 10 callers. Under this project's own recorded safe-hook threshold

  * a native LUI *model* binding — `SetModelValue` / `GetModel` are Lua-side; the
    664-entry binding table has no model functions.

### ⭐ THE ROUTE THAT IS STILL OPEN — a native LUI model API exists

Found in sub_CCF20 while chasing dvar 2523, and it is the most promising lead for
the LUI-element layer:

    ctx = sub_369C90(localClientNum);                          // model context
    m   = sub_369F30(ctx, "cg.hud.hostMigration.isActive");    // find model BY DOTTED PATH
    if (m && sub_369B40(m)) ...                                // read bool

So the LUI data-model tree IS reachable natively by name. `CG_PublishHudModel`
(sub_3573B0) writes into the same tree via sub_36ABF0 / sub_36AC60 / sub_36ACE0 /
sub_36AAF0 (int / float / string / bool setters taking a model handle). Pairing
`sub_369F30` with those setters would give a general "write any LUI model by
path", which is what hiding an individual widget needs.

Unknown, and required before writing code: whether a per-widget visibility model
exists to write. `cg.hud.visibility.BroadcasterLayerHud` appears in
datasources.lua and mphud subscribes `DataSources.inGame.HUD.visibility`, so the
namespace exists — but those entries may be created BY LUI rather than published
natively. The 73 natively published ids contain no visibility model.

Also newly identified (from sub_C3990): `sub_104620` = lua_pushlstring,
`sub_2D8580` = lua table index, lua stack top at `L + 72`, base at `L + 80`.
`sub_C3990(name, L)` is `LUI.roots[name]` — ROOT elements only, not arbitrary
widgets, so it cannot reach MatchScoresWidget0 directly.

# ⭐⭐ THE cl_demo_play HANG — THE THREAD IT WAITS ON IS NOW IDENTIFIED (2026-08-13)

User: *"I pretty much always get in a hanging state now... I think our new
broadcaster and other hud stuff is messing with the game"*.

**It is NOT the broadcaster/HUD work.** Measured on the live hung process
(pid 20196, build 1D9AD3E4): no thread has our DLL as its `rip`, and the two
threads that matter carry no frames from our module at all. Broadcaster mode was
off and appears nowhere.

## The signature is IDENTICAL to the 2026-08-11 entry, offset for offset

    tid 26812 (main), rip in ntdll (blocked):
        IDA_0x8BD224   R_SyncRenderThread + 0x34
        IDA_0x8815D    sub_88150 (CL_ShutdownAll) + 0xD
        IDA_0x910B0D   CL_Demo_Play_f + 0x4BD

0x910B0D - 0x910650 = 0x4BD and 0x8BD224 - 0x8BD1F0 = 0x34 — the same two offsets
recorded last time. So this is one recurring hang, not a new one.

## ⭐ NEW — what the main thread is waiting FOR

Last time this was written off as "an engine race" because nothing of ours was on
a stack. That was true but incomplete: nobody identified the thread holding the
render sync. It is:

    tid 28328, 174 s CPU (a full core, rip advancing 0x79DD6 -> 0x79DDE):
        IDA_0x79DDE    CL_GetLocalClientActive + 0x80E   <-- SPINNING
        IDA_0x89E4B2   sub_89E4A0 + 0x12
        IDA_0x8E865E   sub_8E84D0 + 0x18E
        IDA_0x8E6CC9   sub_8E6B20 + 0x1A9
        IDA_0x8E6FFF   sub_8E6CF0 + 0x30F
        IDA_0x675DC0   sub_675D40 + 0x80                 (thread proc)

i.e. a RENDERER WORKER thread, stuck inside `CL_GetLocalClientActive`'s
Arxan control-flow-flattened dispatcher. The disassembly at the spin is the
retaddr check itself:

    79DB4  cmp   rax, 20000000h
    79DC7  cmova edx, r10d          ; pick a different flattened state
    79DD0  cmp   edx, 76179912h
    79DD6  ja    loc_79E7E          ; <- the loop

That thread never returns, so `R_SyncRenderThread` never returns, so
`CL_ShutdownAll` inside `CL_Demo_Play_f` blocks forever. **The whole hang is one
spinning renderer worker.** This also matches demo_playback.cpp:292's existing
note that "the E8 thunk into CL_GetLocalClientActive spins forever".

## Diagnosis state: hang location PROVEN, cause NOT

Two candidates, and they need different fixes:

  (a) a genuine engine race in CL_Demo_Play_f's teardown, which the 2026-08-11
      entry already assumed;
  (b) **our own frontend release**. The log's last lines are

          [native] cl_demo_play xbillytriple
          [assets] cl_demo_play: releasing the frontend up front ...
          [assets] RELEASE frontend/ui_mp: mask 900 (0x384), zones 10 -> 8 (-2)
          Adding fastfile 'mp_shipment_s2_load' to queue
          Loading Zone: cache_mp_shipment_s2_load.ff
          <nothing>

      We free ui_mp at CL_Demo_Play_f's ENTRY, then the engine's own teardown
      runs and syncs the render thread. Freeing zone memory a renderer worker
      still references is exactly the shape of this spin, and it is the SAME
      class of defect already recorded once ("GIBRALTAR — IMAGE LIMIT GONE, THEN
      A CRASH I CAUSED. RETIMED." — the release was moved to entry precisely
      because doing it later killed LUI's bound luafiles).

(b) is the better bet because the release was already in place at the 2026-08-11
hang too, so it explains both occurrences.

## THE TEST — one console command, no build

    demo_release_frontend 0        (the command exists, demo_native.cpp:6741)
    cl_demo_play <a light map demo>

  * hang gone  -> (b) confirmed; the release needs a different lifecycle point or
    must wait for the render thread itself. Note heavy maps may then hit the
    40192 image limit again, so test on a light map (shipment/airship/egypt).
  * hang stays -> (a); the release is exonerated and the target becomes the
    renderer worker chain sub_8E6CF0 -> sub_8E6B20 -> sub_8E84D0 -> sub_89E4A0.

`demo_release_level 0` is the second half if the first changes nothing.

## Method note

`tools/dump_stacks.py` only scans the GAME module, so it cannot answer "is our
DLL involved". A one-off script that enumerates threads with `GetThreadTimes`,
suspends each, reads RIP/RSP and scans the stack for OUR module range answered it
directly — and finding the CPU-burning thread first is what turned "the main
thread is blocked" into "here is what it is blocked on". Worth keeping as a
pattern for hangs: **find the spinner before reading the blocked thread.**

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# NEW AREA — BOT IDENTITY SPOOFING (names + emblem/title/prestige/level)
# Started 2026-08-13. Goal: private match with bots that look like real
# players, for capturing clips.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

## ⭐⭐⭐ THE DEMOS ARE THE PLAYER LIST — 131 REAL ACCOUNTS ALREADY ON DISK

USER QUESTION: "is there a way to automatically get names from a recent session
directly through steam api or in game or do I have to build it myself"

Answered offline, no game, no IDA, no probe. **You do not build it by hand.**

### PROVEN — the recorded gamestate carries one clientinfo per player

Every native `.demo` carries, in its gamestate configstrings, one entry per
player in the lobby. Shape, validated against 208 entries across 39 demos:

    cs[266..277]   <16 hex> <80 hex> <int> <16 hex> 0 0
                   ^SteamID64        ^team ^session id
                            ^40-byte customization blob

Example (mp_london, 11 players):

    cs[266] 011000011cc26fcb 1cb2a8c0ff00...  2 6a61008155084706 0 0
    cs[267] 011000016114d6e4 4701a8c0ff00...  2 f99d0098ae964f51 0 0

The first token is a full **SteamID64 in hex**. Individual accounts always have
high dword **0x01100001** (universe 1 | type 1 | instance 1), which is the exact
validity test — magnitude is NOT sufficient, because bot/offline demos leave junk
in this field (measured: one decoded to high dword 0xb941e4ca).

### ⭐ THERE IS NO NAME IN THE CLIENTINFO

S2 replicates the **Steam ID**, not the display name. Names are resolved from
Steam. That is why a demo cannot be grepped for player names, and it is the
reason the roster tool emits IDs plus a resolver rather than names directly.

Consistent with `SV_UserinfoChanged` @0x547A90, which takes `name` from
USERINFO (not from clientinfo) into the server client struct and the client-side
name array `byte_A2BAEA4[152*client]`.

### MEASURED — the back-catalogue

    39 demos parsed, 208 clientinfo entries, 131 DISTINCT accounts
    lobbies of 5-12 players on mp_london / mp_d_day / mp_shipment_s2 /
    mp_flak_tower / mp_aachen_v2 / mp_canon_farm / mp_sandbox_01 / mp_forest_01

    10 files skipped, all OUR OWN transcode experiments (x_d_day.*, y/z*_forest).
    Expected: those carry the gamestate as the SECOND record in its message, and
    s2_gamestate.parse() only inspects each packet's FIRST 4-bit opcode. Not a
    defect in the recordings — it is the documented framing difference.

### TWO AUTOMATIC ROUTES TO NAMES, neither requiring any typing

  1. **Zero code, works now.** Steam's own recent-players list:
     `https://steamcommunity.com/my/friends/coplay` (or the Steam client's
     Players tab). WWII does use Steam lobbies — `IWSteamClient__OnLobbyCreated`
     / `OnLobbyEntered` are named in this IDB — so coplay tracking is populated.
  2. **From the demos.** `tools/s2_players.py --key <steam web api key>` resolves
     every extracted ID through ISteamUser/GetPlayerSummaries (100 ids per call,
     free key from https://steamcommunity.com/dev/apikey).

Route 2 is strictly better for this feature, because it pairs each name with the
**exact 40-byte cosmetic record that player was wearing in that match**.

## ⭐⭐ THE 40-BYTE BLOB IS PER-ACCOUNT STABLE — so copying a look is viable

Laid out as 20 little-endian u16 across all 131 players:

    varying across players : 0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 14, 16, 17, 19
    constant across players: 3, 8, 10, 11, 12, 13, 15, 18

8 constant columns over 131 unrelated accounts means this is a FIXED RECORD, not
noise. The repeated `00ff` reads as an empty-slot sentinel (255).

⭐ The decisive measurement — ONE account (76561198082526318, the recording
account, present in all 31 of its own recordings, spanning 2026-05 to 2026-08):

    fields 0-13, 15, 18   IDENTICAL in all 31 sightings   <- persistent cosmetics
    field 16              different in nearly every match <- per-session, NOT cosmetic
    field 19              0200 / 0100 / 0300              <- team
    fields 14, 17         4f87 / 7f8c always, EXCEPT one demo where both read
                          00ff and field 16 read 0000 (i.e. unset/default)

**So the cosmetic payload is stable per account across months and maps.** That is
what makes "copy a real player's look" a data-copy job rather than a live lookup.

⚠ WHICH field is the emblem, which is the calling card, which is prestige/level
is NOT established. Do not guess it — see the A/B below, which settles it with no
IDA and no probe.

## THE A/B THAT IDENTIFIES EACH COSMETIC FIELD (no IDA, no probe, no build)

    1. record ~30 s of any match            (the engine's own recorder)
    2. change ONE cosmetic in the menus     (emblem, then separately calling card)
    3. record ~30 s again
    4. python tools/s2_players.py --player <your steamid64>

Step 4 prints every sighting of that account with its blob and reports
`fields that CHANGED between these sightings`. One cosmetic changed -> one field
moves. This is the same controlled-pair method that cracked the type-21 footer
bug after two days of bitstream analysis had failed.

Ignore fields 16 and 19 — they are per-match by construction (measured above).

## TOOL — tools/s2_players.py (offline, no game)

    python tools/s2_players.py                       # scan main/demo
    python tools/s2_players.py --dir <path> | <file.demo> ...
    python tools/s2_players.py --csv players.csv     # name <-> blob table
    python tools/s2_players.py --blob                # 20 u16 layout, marks
                                                     #   varying vs constant
    python tools/s2_players.py --player <steamid64>  # every sighting + field diff
    python tools/s2_players.py --urls                # profile links
    python tools/s2_players.py --key <steam api key> # resolve IDs -> persona names

Clientinfo is matched by SHAPE, not by configstring index, so it keeps working if
the index range moves.

## WHAT IS ALREADY IN HAND FOR THE WRITE SIDE

    SV_UserinfoChanged @0x547A90  (server), client = *(qword*)(qword_9ED4688 + 1048*c)
        name        userinfo "name"        -> +23299 (36 B), mirrored to +23148
                                              and to byte_A2BAEA4[152*client]
        emblem      userinfo "patch"       -> *(WORD*)(client + 23416)
        calling card userinfo "callingcard"-> *(WORD*)(client + 23418)
        clan tag    userinfo "clanAbbrev"  -> +23408 (8 B)
        clan level  userinfo "ec_Level"    -> *(DWORD*)(client + 23432)
        clan tag text                      -> +23424 (8 B)
    Dvar_InfoString @0x664C62 (client) is the other end and also writes `rank`
        (sub_D6F00) and `prestige` (sub_D6C60) into userinfo.

    server client array   qword_C5FBA58, stride 1173616, count dword_C5FBA50
    isBot                 client + 270680
    bots per team         Bots_SetTeamLimit 0x38E350 / Bots_GetTeamLimit 0x3882C0
                          (already shipped as `fh_bots`; 17 bots + you is the cap,
                           see the CLOSED 18-player entry)

⚠ RANK and PRESTIGE are the gap: Dvar_InfoString WRITES them into userinfo but
the decompiled part of SV_UserinfoChanged does not READ them, so they are

⚠ Also unresolved: whether the userinfo `patch`/`callingcard` u16s and the
40-byte clientinfo blob are the same data in two forms. They may well be — but
that is an inference, and the Absolute Rule applies until the A/B above pins the

# ⭐⭐⭐ BOT RENAMING — THE ENGINE'S OWN API ALREADY TAKES A NAME (2026-08-13)

Found in one pass with both IDBs open. No probing, no guessing at a rename path.

## PROVEN — SV_AddBot @ IDA 0xF2650, and it is TWIN-PROVEN

Advanced Warfare exports the mangled symbol outright:

    ?SV_AddBot@@YAPAUgentity_s@@PBD@Z   ==  gentity_s* SV_AddBot(const char*)

S2's equivalent returns `qword_BC6B8C8 + 1048*slot` — a gentity_s* — and takes
the name as arg0. S2 added a second parameter (team/customization index):

    SV_AddBot(const char* name, unsigned int teamIdx)

      if (unk_1BD36F8) return 0;                 // the hub gate force_host also uses
      find a free slot in svs_clients (stride 293404 dwords == 1173616 bytes)
      if ( *a1 )                                 // <<< A NAME WAS SUPPLIED
          Com_sprintf(v34, 0x1F, "%s", a1);      //     use it verbatim, 30 chars + NUL
      else
          v9 = SV_BotGetRandomName();            //     else generate one
      SV_BuildBotUserinfo(v36);                  // the \isbot\1 template
      sub_14B820(&v31, v35, 256);                // serialize the 28-byte customization
      sub_1052B0(Buffer, "connect bot%u \"%s\\name\\%s\\qport\\%d\\ctz\\%s\"");
      sub_64C070(Buffer);                        // execute the connect
      v20[67670] = 2;                            // 67670*4 = 270680 == isBot

**So renaming needs no name-generation hook at all — the engine's own entry
point accepts a name.** Pass ours and every downstream consumer (userinfo ->
SV_UserinfoChanged -> client struct -> clientinfo -> scoreboard, killfeed) just
works, because it is the engine's own path end to end.

## ⭐ THE SAFETY GUARANTEE IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A RUNTIME CHECK

USER REQUIREMENT: "we must never rename or change anything of a real player".

A human NEVER reaches SV_AddBot. Real clients arrive through SV_DirectConnect
from an actual network connect; SV_AddBot is only ever called by the bot
spawner. The live path is:

    GSC maps/mp/bots/_bots  ->  Scr_AddBot @0x5A1B70  ->  SV_AddBot
        Scr_GetString(0)      = the NAME (stock scripts pass empty)
        Scr_GetConstString(1) = team/faction -> 0,1,2,3,4,6

So hooking the BOT-ADD path rather than a rename path means there is no code
path by which a human's name could be rewritten. That is far stronger than
inspecting a client afterwards and judging whether it looks like a bot — a
judgement we never have to make.

Belt and braces anyway: after the original returns, the new client's isBot field
is read back and REPORTED (never used as a gate). The slot is located by
matching the NAME we just supplied at client+23299 — NOT by deriving an index
from the returned gentity, because the gentity array has a different base and a
different stride (1048), and mixing the two would be exactly the offset
inference this file keeps banning.

## Supporting proofs picked up along the way

  * `client + 23299` is the name field — confirmed a second way, independently:
    SV_BotGetRandomName's own duplicate test is `I_stricmp(client + 23299, cand)`.
  * `client + 270680` is isBot and SV_AddBot writes **2** (not 1).
  * SV_BotGetRandomName @0x6C3600 pulls names from the LOCALIZED STRING TABLE
    (keys beginning "bot"), shuffles them into byte_BB4FD30, rejects any already
    in use, and falls back to the literal "BotPlayer".
  * SV_BuildBotUserinfo @0xB8D80 formats `...\clver\0\isbot\1` — a positive bot
    marker written at connect by the bot path only. A real client's userinfo
    (Dvar_InfoString @0x664C62) has no such key.

## ⚠ SUPPLYING A NAME CHANGES THE CUSTOMIZATION BRANCH

This is visible in game, so expect it:

    name given -> sub_14DAC0(&v31, Sys_Milliseconds())   time-seeded
    no name    -> sub_6F72A0(a2)                          per-team PRESET

So bots may look different once renaming is on. The 28-byte struct at v31/v32/v33
is serialized by sub_14B820 into the connect string's `\ctz\` field — that is the
handle for the emblem/calling-card work, and `SV_GeneratePresetTestClientCustomization`
@0xF5070 (already named, references mp/botcostumetable.csv) is the preset source.

## SHIPPED — src/net/bots.{hpp,cpp}, build 2D975A7A (deployed, hash-verified)

NOT yet tested in game, so per the Fix Declaration Rules this is a CANDIDATE.

  * one hook: SV_AddBot, IDA 0xF2650 - 0x1000 = 0xF1650.
    RULE A3.1 checked — nothing else in src/ referenced either form.
    RULE A17 — declared `std::uint64_t(__fastcall*)(const char*, unsigned int)`,
    the exact decompiled signature; the return is a pointer, do not narrow it.
  * name list: `<gamedir>\S2MP-Mod\botnames.txt`, one per line, '#' comments.

  * `bot_names [0|1|reload]` reports hook state, list path, counts and a preview.

## ⭐ THE NAME LIST BUILDS ITSELF FROM YOUR OWN RECORDINGS — DONE 2026-08-13

    python tools/s2_players.py --whoami --key <steam api key> \
        --botnames "<gamedir>\S2MP-Mod\botnames.txt"

RESULT: **129 real player names written**, resolved from 130 accounts across 208
clientinfo entries in 39 demos. Verified: the user's own persona name does NOT
appear in the file.

`--whoami` identifies the recording account without being told: you appear in
EVERY recording you made, so the account with by far the most sightings is you
(measured 31 vs 4 for the next). It only acts when the lead is decisive (>= 3x
the runner-up) and otherwise excludes nothing and says so, rather than risk
dropping a real player from the list. `--exclude <id>...` is the manual form.

Two robustness fixes this forced, both worth keeping:
