## CORRECTED 2026-08-13 — the generated name list needed real cleaning

USER, reading the first generated botnames.txt: colour codes were coming through
verbatim (`SK| ^7Bu^4Ky^1JI9I`, `^1[^7NL^4]^2Aeolus`) and one entry was
`.,.,.,.,..,,,,..,..,.,.,,....` — punctuation with no name in it.

Both were defects in my writer, which only filtered to printable ASCII. Fixed in
`clean_name()`:

  * strip `^` + digit (Quake/CoD colour codes) — they render as a COLOUR, not as
    text, so "^7Bu^4Ky^1JI9I" is really "BuKyJI9I"
  * strip a trailing lone `^` (malformed — not a colour code)
  * collapse whitespace runs
  * REJECT names with fewer than 2 alphanumeric characters, which kills the
    punctuation-only entries while keeping legitimate short names (db, GM)
  * dedupe case-insensitively — two accounts can share a persona name, and two
    bots with the same name in one match would be confusing
  * report what was rejected and why, rather than silently dropping

Result: 128 names (was 129 with junk). Two rejected: the punctuation-only one and
a name with no ASCII at all ('执着').

⚠ The MOD deliberately still PASSES COLOUR CODES THROUGH, so a hand-written
`^1Red` bot name works; only the generated list is stripped, and botnames.txt
says so. The mod does drop a trailing lone `^` (build 37AA79FA), because that is
malformed rather than a style choice and would swallow the next rendered char.

# FAKE-ONLINE LOBBY (bots as "real people") — FEASIBILITY, 2026-08-13

USER REQUEST: make a bot match mimic an online one — a PREGAME LOBBY already
filled with the named "people" before the match starts, remembering their TEAM
and their LOADOUTS, "including variants, not the basic bot loadouts".

Scoped before building. Three separate features with very different costs.

## 1. FILLING THE PREGAME LOBBY — tractable, nothing new needed

`SV_AddBot`'s only timing gate is `if (unk_1BD36F8) return 0` — the hub byte
(1 in the hub, 0 on a real map; the same byte force_host reads and the same one
the record gate uses). So bots can be added at ANY point once a map is up,
including during the pre-match countdown. It also needs a free svs_clients slot.

So "fill the lobby before the match starts" = call SV_AddBot ourselves during
pregame instead of waiting for GSC `maps/mp/bots/_bots` to do it at match start.
We already hook SV_AddBot and own the names.

UNKNOWNS to settle by testing: whether the pregame scoreboard renders bots, and
whether the engine's own spawner then double-adds once the match begins (it walks
for free slots, so a full roster may simply make it a no-op — unverified).

## 2. TEAMS — already supported, no work

`SV_AddBot(const char* name, unsigned int teamIdx)`. `Scr_AddBot` @0x5A1B70 maps
the GSC faction constants onto 0,1,2,3,4,6 and passes them straight through. So
pinning a given name to a given team is a parameter, not a feature.

## 3. LOADOUTS WITH VARIANTS — the hard one. Do NOT promise it cheaply.

Bot loadouts are set in GSC (`maps/mp/bots/_bots`, `mp/botDifficultyTable.csv`),
and BOTH of the mod's script-side levers are unfinished stubs:

    ScriptLoader::loadCustomScripts()   empty
    ScriptLoader::init()                empty
    ScriptLoader::FindXAssetHeader()    returns false  (falls back to the engine)
    StringTableLoader::loadCustom()     "//TODO: finish"

Only the DUMP halves work. `S2MP-Mod/dump` currently holds 941 LUI files and NO
server GSC, so `_bots` has never been dumped either.

So loadouts need one of:
  (a) implement GSC injection — large, but unlocks this and much else;
  (b) a targeted C++ hook on whatever gives a bot its weapon — needs the path
      found first;
  (c) finish StringTableLoader so `mp/botcostumetable.csv` can be overridden —
      that reaches bot APPEARANCE only, not weapons.

## PROVEN on the way — bot appearance is a 28-byte CSV-driven record

`SV_GeneratePresetTestClientCustomization(array, count, a3)` @0xF5070:

    v11 = Sys_Milliseconds();
    if (sub_8555C0() != 1 && sub_388180())
        sub_F4D00("mp/botcostumetable.csv", count, array, &filled, a3, 0);
    for (each entry not filled from the CSV)
        sub_14DAC0(entry, &v11);        // random, time-seeded
    stride 28 bytes

That 28-byte record is what SV_AddBot serializes with sub_14B820 into the connect
string's `\ctz\` field. Confirms both the stride and that bot looks are table
driven, with a random fallback.

## ⭐ LOADOUTS ARE REPLICATED PER PLAYER — so bots CAN show real ones

Found while scoping, and it is the fact that makes (3) worth doing at all:

    ui_broadcaster_loadout_primary_weapon
    ui_broadcaster_loadout_primary_attachment_0 .. _3
    ui_broadcaster_loadout_secondary_weapon
    ui_broadcaster_loadout_secondary_attachment_0 .. _3

are omnvars — i.e. a player's loadout is replicated and readable by other
clients (that is how the caster HUD shows it). So a bot's loadout is not a
local-only cosmetic; set it and it is visible.

Also located: loadouts are DDL blobs — `mp/ddl/privateloadouts.ddl`,
`rankedloadouts.ddl`, `competitiveloadouts.ddl`, with LUI bindings
setPrivateLoadout / setRankedLoadout / setCompetitiveLoadout / GetMemberLoadout /
BroadcastLoadout / SetVirtualLobbyLoadout. The DDL cursor API is ALREADY known
and working from the broadcaster work (MakeRootCursor 0xA1C8E0 / MoveToName
0xA1D010 / SetInt 0xA1D4D0 / GetInt 0xA1C860), so reading and writing a loadout
blob is a solved mechanism looking for the right object.

## RECOMMENDED ORDER

  1. TEST the bot renamer that is already deployed (build 37AA79FA) — it is
     untested, and everything below builds on it.
  2. Pregame fill + per-name team pinning. Small, uses only what exists.
  3. Loadouts: decide (a) vs (b) deliberately. (a) is the bigger prize because
     GSC injection unlocks far more than bots, but it is its own project.

# THE FAKE-ONLINE ASK, RESTATED PRECISELY (2026-08-13)

The user corrected my reading of "pregame". It is NOT the pre-match countdown on
a loaded map. It is **the lobby before the map loads** — players shown as
connected in the pregame lobby, as in a real public match.

Full set of constraints, and they PULL AGAINST EACH OTHER:

  1. bots must MOVE            -> the game must see the match as PRIVATE
                                  (user: "there is a lever that makes bots not
                                  move if it sees the match as a public match")
  2. XP must COUNT             -> the game must see it as an ONLINE/ranked match
  3. we must be the SERVER HOST, not a dedicated server

## ⭐ THE TENSION RESOLVES ONE WAY, AND IT IS NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE

(1) and (3) BOTH want private:
  * bot behaviour is gated on private (see below),
  * and CLAUDE.md's own CLOSED finding is that PUBLIC matchmaking always
    PROVISIONS A DEDICATED SERVER — there is no client-hosting branch for a
    public playlist, proven from the GSC binding table and the DS acquire chain.

Only (2) wants public/ranked. So "host a public match" is the wrong target and
has already been proven unreachable. **The right target is: run a PRIVATE match
(we host, bots move) and find what specifically gates XP so that ONE path can be
made to count.** That is a per-consumer question, not a global flag flip.

## The pregame lobby is a DIFFERENT object from svs_clients

Bots added by SV_AddBot are SERVER CLIENTS and require a running server, i.e. a
loaded map. Players listed in the pregame lobby are LOBBY MEMBERS — the 33216-
stride member array on the lobby params object (state byte at +1016, already
proven via Lobby_AcceptSearchResult).

And the lobby has its OWN bot concept, exposed as LUI bindings:

    AddBot  RemoveMemberBot  IsMemberABot
    GetMemberBotDifficulty / SetMemberBotDifficulty
    GetMemberBotPersonality / SetMemberBotPersonality

So filling the PREGAME LOBBY is the lobby-member path, NOT SV_AddBot. Those
bindings are the place to start, and they are self-naming in the binding table.

## The bot-movement lever is NOT sub_388350

`sub_388350` (= LobbyParams_IsPrivate || Com_IsScorestreakTraining) has exactly
ONE code caller, `Bots_GetTeamLimitForScript` @0x6C7050. So it gates the bot
COUNT only. Whatever freezes bots in a public match is elsewhere — almost
certainly GSC, since bot AI runs from maps/mp/bots/_bots.

## ⭐ NEXT STEP IS ONE CONSOLE COMMAND, NO BUILD — dump the server GSC

`dumpAllScriptFiles` is ALREADY REGISTERED (Console.cpp:230 ->
CustomCommands::dumpAllScriptFiles -> ScriptLoader::dumpScript, which
decompiles via the xsk S2 context and writes S2MP-Mod/dump/scripts/<name>.gsc).
It is the same mechanism that produced the 941-file LUI dump via
`dumpAllLuaFiles`.

Run it IN A MATCH (the scriptfile asset pool must be populated). That gives:
  * maps/mp/bots/_bots  -> the actual bot-movement gate
  * the rank/XP script  -> what actually decides whether XP is awarded

Both open questions are probably answered by that one dump, offline, with no
further reverse engineering.

## ⚠ HONEST CAVEAT ON XP — state it before anyone builds

The user cites Ghosts and MW2, which are the CLIENT-AUTHORITATIVE stats era.
WWII is 2017 and its progression is very likely SERVER-VALIDATED through
Demonware (it already carries rankedloadouts/privateloadouts DDL blobs and a
stats upload path). If XP is awarded client-side but rejected on upload, no
client-side change makes it stick. NOT ESTABLISHED either way — the GSC dump
plus the stats-write path will show which it is. Do not promise levelling until
that is known.

# ⭐⭐⭐ THE BOT-FREEZE LEVER — FOUND VIA AW (2026-08-13)

USER: "there is a lever that makes bots not move if it sees the match as a public
match... I found it before but couldn't use it cos of arxan, can't remember what
it's called." Correct on all counts, and it needs no Arxan work at all.

## PROVEN (AW, symboled) — the chain that freezes bots

    SV_RunFrameBots @0x824000C8
        if (scrVarGlob.childVariableValue[238312].intValue == 2) {
            if (BG_AISystemEnabled())  SV_BotUpdateCommon();
            if (BG_BotSystemEnabled()) SV_BotUpdateBots();   <-- BOT MOVEMENT
        }

    BG_BotSystemEnabled @0x826CB674
        ... if (BG_BotsAreAllowed()) return 1; ...

    BG_BotsAreAllowed @0x826C7194
        if (xblive_privatematch->current.enabled
            || practiceroundgame->current.enabled)              return 1;
        if (splitscreen->enabled && !onlinegame->enabled)       return 1;
        if (systemlink) return systemlink->current.color[0] != 0;
        return 0;                     // <<< PUBLIC MATCH -> BOTS DO NOT UPDATE

So it is `xblive_privatematch` (or practiceround / splitscreen / systemlink).
In a public match BG_BotsAreAllowed is 0, BG_BotSystemEnabled is 0,
SV_BotUpdateBots never runs, and the bots stand still. Exactly as described.

## ⭐ S2's EQUIVALENT IS A PLAIN CONSOLE COMMAND — `setgameprivatematch`

S2 has no `xblive_privatematch` STRING (its dvars are numeric), but it registers
the command directly. `sub_1971F0` ends:

    Cmd_AddCommandInternal("setgameprivatematch", sub_1972B0, &off_6CF86A0);

and the handler is unambiguous:

    sub_1972B0():
        v2 = sub_470F20(Lobby_Get(0));           // == the lobby (identity)
        v0 = (argc > 1) ? (atoi(argv[1]) > 0) : 0;
        *(DWORD *)(v2 + 632) = v0;               // params[10] = PRIVATE
        *(DWORD *)(v2 + 644) = v0 ^ 1;           // params[13] = requireOpenNat

632 and 644 are exactly this file's own lobby-params map (params[10] private,
params[13] requireOpenNat). And `sub_388350`, the bot-count gate, is
`LobbyParams_IsPrivate(sub_197040()) || Com_IsScorestreakTraining()` — the same
params[10].

**So the lever is `setgameprivatematch 1`.** No hook, no patch, no Arxan fight.
The likely reason it was unusable before: the FUNCTION was found and someone
tried to patch it, when a console command already sets the flag.

Related surface, same flag: LUI bindings `SetGameIsPrivateMatch` /
`GetGameIsPrivateMatch` / `SetHubIsPrivateMatch` / `GetHubIsPrivateMatch`.

## NO CONFLICT WITH force_host

force_host writes params[0], [1], [11], [13], [15]. It does NOT write params[10],
so the private flag is ours to set. Note setgameprivatematch also sets
params[13] = !private, i.e. private=1 CLEARS requireOpenNat — which is what
force_host wants anyway.

## ⚠ STRONG INFERENCE, NOT PROVEN, FOR S2 SPECIFICALLY

The freeze chain above is decompiled from AW. In S2, params[10] is PROVEN to gate
the bot COUNT (sub_388350 -> Bots_GetTeamLimitForScript), but S2's twin of
BG_BotsAreAllowed reading it for MOVEMENT has not been located. Same engine
family and same structure, so it is very likely — but say "likely" until tested.

**IT IS TESTABLE WITH ONE COMMAND AND NO BUILD:** `setgameprivatematch 1` in a
match where bots are standing still. If they start moving, proven.

## ⛔ CAUTION — this is also the flag that decides XP

params[10] private is very likely the same flag progression checks, so setting it
may be exactly what STOPS XP counting. That is the (1) vs (2) tension already
recorded: bots move when private, XP counts when ranked. Do not expect one flag
to satisfy both — the resolution, if there is one, is finding the separate XP
consumer, not flipping this harder.

# ⭐ ADDING BOTS WITHOUT THE MENU — `bots_fill` (2026-08-13, build FF96EB16)

USER CORRECTION, third attempt at reading the ask: "bots don't just prefill in an
online game, I have to manually set them." The blocker is not bot MOVEMENT — it
is that in an online-looking match the bot options are not offered at all.

## PROVEN — why the menu cannot do it, and why we do not need the menu

`LUI_SetBotsTeamLimit`'s own gate is

    !Com_IsOnlineGame() || (in a lobby && we are the game host)

so with online mode set the menu path is unavailable and the only route is the
manual private-match menu. That is exactly what the user described.

`SV_AddBot` has NO such gate. Its only checks are the hub byte
(`if (unk_1BD36F8) return 0`) and a free client slot. So calling it directly
sidesteps the menu without faking any state — it is the engine's own entry point,
just reached from code instead of from the UI.

`bots_fill [count]` calls the PATCHED entry with an empty name, so our existing
detour supplies the name and all the tested naming / sanitising / isBot
verification / logging applies unchanged. Default count fills every free slot.
Free slots are counted with SV_AddBot's own test (client state dword == 0).

## ⛔ PROVEN — the LOBBY-member bot API is COMPILED OUT of S2

Re-verified from its own body, because it decides whether "players visible in the
pregame lobby" is reachable at all:

    LUI_AddBot @0x3393B0   parses 3 Lua args, Lobby_Get(0), sub_470F20(...),
                           then calls nullsub_93(lobby, a, b, c)   <- A NULL STUB

Binding table entry at 0xB60020 -> 0x3393B0, so this IS the engine's lobby-level
AddBot, and it does nothing. Combined with SV_AddBot needing a loaded map, the
engine has NO mechanism for putting bots in the pregame lobby.

CONSEQUENCE for the user's step 2 ("names visible in the lobby list before the
map loads"): the only remaining route is writing fake entries into the lobby
MEMBER array (33216 stride) ourselves. That is manufacturing state the engine
never created, so per the doctrine it needs proving before it is attempted, not
a drive-by. Do not start it without deciding that deliberately.

## ⚠ TEAM ASSIGNMENT IS STILL OPEN — do not claim bots_fill does it

`SV_AddBot(name, a2)` uses a2 in exactly ONE place: `sub_6F72A0(a2)`, the costume
preset lookup. And that call is in the `else` branch — i.e. **a2 is not used at
all once a name is supplied**. So a2 is a costume index, NOT a team, and
supplying a name bypasses even that.

`Scr_AddBot` maps its GSC faction argument to 2,1,3,4,0,6 before passing it in,
which is what made it look like a team. It is the costume set for that faction.

So "remember their team" is NOT solved by this build, and neither is the costume
(the name branch skips the preset entirely — the documented appearance side
effect). Both still need the real team-assignment path found.

# ⭐⭐⭐ FAKE PREGAME LOBBY + MAP VOTE — RESEARCH AND PLAN (2026-08-13)

User asked for research only ("just learn and plan for now") while testing
bots_fill. Two halves: fake players in the pregame lobby, and a map vote that
appears contested but lands on our map.

## PART B FIRST — THE MAP VOTE IS ALREADY MOSTLY IN OUR HANDS

### PROVEN — the whole vote surface, from the LUI binding table @0xB5FD20

    GetVoteMapImage             0x336170
    GetVoteMapName              0x3362E0
    GetVoteMapGametype          0x336470
    GetVoteMapGametypeReference 0x336620
    HasVotePassed               0x3363B0
    HasPartyCastVote            0x3363F0
    GetPartyCastVote            0x336430

Those are Lua marshallers; the state is one level down and is tiny:

    HasVotePassed    -> sub_47F680 -> *(BYTE *)(lobby + 1598452)
    GetPartyCastVote -> sub_47EF70 -> *(DWORD*)(lobby + 1598560)
    GetVoteMapName(i)-> sub_743F80 -> Dvar_GetString(i == 1 ? "3533" : "3740")

### ⭐ THE TWO MAP OPTIONS ARE NUMERIC DVARS: "3740" (option 0), "3533" (option 1)

    sub_743F80(a1):  v2 = (a1 == 1) ? "3533" : "3740";
                     return sub_6505A0(sub_AFD20(v2));      // Dvar_FindVar/GetString

These are almost certainly the "two mapvote entries" GRIIMS-WWII-Tool wrote
(CLAUDE.md's read of ApplySpoofedPlaylist: "Cbuf ';ui_mapname <map>', two mapvote
entries, ..."). That independently corroborates the identification.

### ⭐⭐ THE ELEGANT TRICK — SET BOTH OPTIONS TO THE MAP YOU WANT

If both "3740" and "3533" name the same map, then whichever option "wins" the
vote, the result is your map. No vote counts need faking, no result needs
forcing, and the UI still animates a normal contested vote. This is by far the
lowest-risk route and it manufactures nothing — it only sets the two dvars the
engine itself reads for the ballot.

Forcing the outcome directly (writing +1598452 / +1598560) stays available as a
fallback, but should not be needed.

### ⛔ STRUCTURAL — THE VOTE ONLY EXISTS IN A NON-PRIVATE LOBBY

`sub_48D8C0(lobby, a2)`, the lobby state machine, at state
`(*(DWORD*)(lobby + 1598608) & 0xFC) == 4`:

    if ( LobbyParams_GetPrivate(lobby) ) {
        sub_490B70(lobby, a2);  ...                       // PRIVATE: no vote
    } else {
        if ( !*(BYTE*)(lobby + 1598452) && !sub_151720() )
            sub_4886D0(lobby, a2);                        // <- THE VOTE STEP
        if ( !*(DWORD*)(lobby + 1598456) && sub_480F00(lobby)
             && !LobbyParams_GetPrivate(lobby) ) { ... }
    }

So map voting is a PUBLIC-lobby feature and a private lobby skips it entirely.

New lobby offsets, all in the object already mapped:
    +1598452  byte   vote passed / completed        (gates the vote step)
    +1598456  dword  once-flag for sub_47D700/sub_4822A0
    +1598560  dword  the party's cast vote
    +1598608  dword  lobby STATE (masked & 0xFC; == 4 during this phase)

### ⭐ AND THAT SUGGESTS THE PHASE TRICK FOR THE WHOLE FEATURE

The tension recorded earlier — bots move only when PRIVATE, vote exists only when
NOT private — is not necessarily a contradiction, because they happen in
DIFFERENT PHASES:

    lobby phase   non-private  -> the map vote UI runs
    then, before/at map load, `setgameprivatematch 1`
    match phase   private      -> BG_BotsAreAllowed is true, bots move

`setgameprivatematch` is a plain console command writing params[10], so flipping
it at the right moment is cheap. NOT TESTED — but it is the first idea that
satisfies both constraints instead of trading one off against the other.

## PART A — FAKE PLAYERS IN THE PREGAME LOBBY. HARDER, AND STILL UNPROVEN.

Established already:
  * `LUI_AddBot` @0x3393B0 is a NULL STUB (ends in nullsub_93) — the engine's
    own lobby-level bot add does nothing.
  * `SV_AddBot` needs svs_clients, which only exists after SV_Init, i.e. after
    the map loads. Confirmed by com_sv_running gating in bots_fill.

So neither engine path can put a body in the pregame lobby. The only remaining
route is writing entries into the lobby MEMBER array ourselves — manufacturing
state the engine never created, which the doctrine says to prove before doing.

### What must be answered BEFORE writing any of it

  1. What does the lobby player-list UI actually read? If it reads the member
     array, added entries may just appear. If it is fed by LUI models published
     from native, we would publish instead. Start from the LUI lobby list
     bindings and the member-count field.
  2. Where is the member COUNT, and is it authoritative? Known so far: member
     stride 33216, state byte at +1016 (from Lobby_AcceptSearchResult), a
     per-member id at +21568 and a broadcaster dword at +1288 (from sub_4813D0).
  3. What validates members? If the party system heartbeats or reconciles them
     against the session, fabricated members may be dropped, or worse, confuse
     the real session. `PartyHost_SendHeartbeats` @0x48F980 and
     `PartyHost_HandleClientPresence` @0x485ED0 are the ones to read first.

### Honest risk

This is the one part of the whole request that requires inventing state rather
than driving an engine path. It is also the part most likely to destabilise the
lobby/party system, which this project has already broken once (the search-hook
episode). Do it LAST, behind its own toggle, and with a zero-hook control.

## RECOMMENDED ORDER

  1. (user testing now) bots_fill in an online-mode match.
  2. Map vote: set "3740" and "3533" to the same map. Cheap, safe, high payoff.
     Verify with GetVoteMapName in the lobby.
  3. The private-flag phase flip, to get voting AND moving bots.
  4. Only then: fake lobby members, behind a toggle.

## THE HOST QUESTION — what is actually established

    Script_AreWeHost @0x297D80 = *(DWORD*)(lobby + 1598540) != 0
    that field is written by sub_490E70 (sets AreWeHost=1 AND dedicated=1)
    sub_490E70's only callers: sub_491DE0 (session CREATE) and sub_473BE0 (migration)

So **you are the host if and only if YOUR client created the session** (or you
won a migration). Matchmaking into a public playlist means joining someone else's
session, or being assigned a DS — in neither case did you create it.

force_host's join gate exists precisely to force the first case: refuse every
search result so the engine gives up searching and creates a session locally.
That is the intended mechanism and it is already built.

  2. with it ON from the menu, watch `Script_AreWeHost` / the join-gate refusal
     count via fh_status while searching.
If the gate refuses results and a session is still not created locally, THEN the
join-gate approach is insufficient and the target becomes sub_491DE0's callers —
i.e. what decides to create rather than join.

# ⭐⭐⭐ WHY THE JOIN GATE DOES NOT MAKE YOU HOST — THERE ARE TWO SEARCHES
# (2026-08-13)

USER: ticked the host box in the GUI, searched, and was still put on a server
they did not host. So the join-gate approach IS insufficient, and this explains
why in one line.

## PROVEN — the matchmaking tick forks BEFORE the join gate can matter

`sub_29D9C0` (the search tick), already recorded in this file:

    if ( sub_480F20(Params) /* sessionType == 2 */ && sub_1FF290() )
        sub_1FED90(...);      // <-- DEDICATED SERVER search  (dwFindDSSessions)
    else
        sub_6FF930(...);      // <-- LOBBY search             (dwFindSessions)

force_host's join gate hooks `Lobby_AcceptSearchResult`, which only ever sees
**LOBBY** search results. When the tick takes the DS branch the gate is never
consulted at all — the engine acquires a dedicated server and you join it as a
client. Ticking "host" cannot affect that path.

That is the missing piece the user kept asking about, and it was never checked
because the earlier work assumed the gate covered the whole search.

## ⭐ PROVEN — the DS branch is gated by ONE DVAR

    sub_1FF290() = *((_DWORD *)off_6F34250 + 4)          // dvar value at +16
                && (WORD6(xmmword_6F2ABE0) || DWORD2(xmmword_6F2ABE0));  // datacentre list

and the dvar is registered in the dedicated-server config block, `sub_1FCE20`:

    off_6F2ABF8 = Dvar_RegisterInt("1570", 20000, 0, 0x7FFFFFFF, 0);
    off_6F34248 = Dvar_RegisterInt("5180",  2000, 0, 0x7FFFFFFF, 0);
    off_6F34250 = Dvar_RegisterInt("3707",     1, 0, 0x7FFFFFFF, 0);   <-- THIS ONE
    off_6F34258 = Dvar_RegisterInt("2833",     0, 0, 0x7FFFFFFF, 0);
    sub_B05E0("ds_resetDisconnectTimer", 1, 0);

Registered immediately beside `ds_resetDisconnectTimer`, which corroborates that
this whole block is the dedicated-server client config. None of the four numeric
ids has a recorded real name in DvarMappings (4766 ids are unnamed), so refer to
it as "3707" and do NOT invent a name for it.

**`3707` defaults to 1. With it 0, sub_1FF290 is false and the DS branch cannot
be taken** — the tick must fall through to the LOBBY search, which is exactly
where the join gate operates.

## THE TEST — two console commands, no build

    3707 0        (at the MENU, before searching; `3707 1` restores it)
    fh_on         (or the Host tab checkbox)
    then search

Outcomes and what each means:
  * you end up hosting  -> proven; the DS branch was the whole blocker, and the
    join gate works once it is the only search running.
  * no match is ever found -> the DS branch was the ONLY way this playlist gets a
    server, and hosting a public playlist needs more than blocking it.
  * still put on someone else's server -> the lobby search found a real lobby and
    the join gate did not refuse it; check the refusal count in `fh_status`.

⚠ This is a dvar, trivially reversible, and it disables a search rather than
faking anything. But it CAN leave you unable to find any match — expect that as a
legitimate outcome, not a crash.

## Also settled this round

`sub_492980` creates a session on `Lobby_GetPrivateParty()`, i.e. the PRIVATE
PARTY lobby, not the game lobby — so it is not the game-session creator. The
game-session creators remain sub_7FE60 and sub_80290, and sub_80290 has no code
xrefs (Arxan indirect dispatch), which is why the create path has been hard to
reach from callers.

# ⭐⭐⭐ force_host WAS LATCHING THE WRONG LOBBY OBJECT (2026-08-13, build FF72FA9C)

MEASURED with Cheat Engine on the live process (base 0x7FF7523E0000, attachment
verified by reading 'MZ' at the module base BEFORE trusting any value):

    lobby0 + 1598540 (AreWeHost) = 0
    lobby1 + 1598540 (AreWeHost) = 1      <-- the live session was on LOBBY 1

## The bug

`force_host::lobby(0)` was used unconditionally for every read AND every write:
the hosting latch, min/max players, allowJoiningListenServer, requireOpenNat, the
playlist, and the status readout. The engine, meanwhile, picks the active lobby
at runtime:

    sub_470CB0():
        if (!dword_8EFCBC0 || (dword_8D6C490 && sub_481690(&lobby0)))
             return &lobby0;
        else return &s_lobby1;

    Lobby_Get(n) = &off_8BE6040 + 205030*n      (205030 qwords = 1640240 bytes,
                                                 confirming the stride in use)

So whenever the selector picked slot 1, every param force_host latched went to an
object the engine was not reading. **The writes all "succeed" and do nothing** --
exactly the silent-failure class this file keeps having to relearn.

This is a strong candidate for why force host has never behaved as advertised,
including the user's report of being put on a server they did not host.

## The fix

`active_lobby()` CALLS the engine's own selector (IDA 0x470CB0 - 0x1000 =
0x46FCB0) rather than reimplementing its condition, so the choice cannot drift.
It returns a POINTER TO THE SLOT, so it is dereferenced once. Falls back to
slot 0 if the call or the readability check fails.

tick(), status(), apply_playlist_now() and cmd_canhost() now all use it.

`fh_status` now prints, unconditionally:

    [host] ACTIVE LOBBY = slot N  (host=H on slot0=A slot1=B)

so this can never hide again -- if the active slot and the host flag disagree
with what is being latched, it is visible in one line.

## Also measured, and it explains the failed bots_fill runs

    hub byte unk_1BD36F8 = 0x0101 while sitting in the hub
    (it read 0x0000 at the main menu, before the hub server came up)

SV_AddBot's first statement is `if (unk_1BD36F8) return 0;`, so it refuses in the
hub regardless of free slots -- which is correct engine behaviour and matches
every bots_fill refusal so far. Bots need a REAL MAP.

## UNRESOLVED — carry forward

`com_sv_running = 1` while `svs_clientCount = 0` and `svs_clients = NULL`, in the
hub. Per SV_Init's hub branch svs_clientCount should be 48 there, and an earlier
session's log did show "slots now 1 used of 48" in the hub. Not yet explained;
re-measure in both the hub and a real map.

# ⭐⭐⭐⭐ XP AND BOTS ARE **DIFFERENT FLAGS** — THE CONFLICT WAS NEVER REAL
# (2026-08-13, build AF9E6C0D)

USER EVIDENCE that forced this: they ran `fixedtime` in the match. That is a
SERVER-side dvar, so if it does not smooth the game out you are a CLIENT. It
didn't, no bots spawned, and a DS was in front. Conclusive: the engine handed
them a dedicated server. (Good diagnostic -- remember this trick: a server-only
dvar is a free host/client test.)

## PROVEN — a public playlist has NO self-host fallback

Traced the FAILURE path properly rather than asserting it:

    dwFindDSSessions failure cb  sub_6FF040  ->  sub_1FE310 -> sub_1FE630(obj,_,4)
    sub_1FE630: obj[8] = state; obj[0] = 5 (AcquiringServer);
                if (obj[4] == 1) { reset, memset 0x7478, sub_1FE040(),
                                   sub_29D8C0(...) }   // restart the search

There is NO branch to a listen server. Blocking the DS search produces RETRIES,
not self-hosting. So "host a public match" stays unreachable -- but now from the
failure path, not from an old assertion.

## ⭐⭐ AND THAT DOES NOT MATTER, BECAUSE XP IS NOT GATED ON THE SERVER

`GetLoadoutStatsGroupForGameMode` = sub_654100 (via LUI binding @0xB38720):

    if (sub_B8B60())                      return 3;
    if (sub_28D5C0() || sub_28D5D0())     return 2;
    if (sub_151720())                     return 9;
    online = Com_IsOnlineGame();
    if ( sub_471200(lobby) && sub_4712A0(lobby) )  online = 0;
    if ((v3 & online) == 0)               return 2;    // PRIVATE stats group
    return 1;                                          // RANKED stats group

`UsingRankedStatsGroup` = sub_654630, same shape, returns the bool.

**It never checks whether the match is on a dedicated server.** The whole
decision is Com_IsOnlineGame() plus one AND of two lobby flags:

    sub_471200(lobby) = *(DWORD*)(lobby + 1598544) != 0     "dedicated" flag
    sub_4712A0(lobby) = LobbyParams_GetPrivate(lobby) != 0  private flag  (params[10])

## ⭐⭐⭐ THE CONSEQUENCE

  * bots move        needs  private = 1        (BG_BotsAreAllowed / xblive_privatematch)
  * RANKED stats     needs  NOT (dedicated && private)

**Private alone does NOT drop you into the private stats group** -- it takes BOTH
flags. So `private = 1` with `lobby+1598544 == 0` gives bots that move AND the
ranked stats group. These were never the same switch, and every earlier entry in
this file treating "bots need private / XP needs ranked" as a straight
contradiction is CORRECTED by this.

⚠ NOT YET PROVEN: that the ranked stats group actually results in XP being
awarded and ACCEPTED on upload. Demonware may validate server-side. This is the
CLIENT-side gate only. Do not promise levelling until measured.

⚠ Also unresolved: sub_490E70 (become host) sets BOTH AreWeHost=1 and
lobby+1598544=1. So hosting may set the very flag we need clear. That is the next
thing to measure, and it is exactly what fh_statsgroup reports.

## SHIPPED — `fh_statsgroup`, READ-ONLY, no writes (build AF9E6C0D)

Calls the engine's own two functions and prints the group, the bool, and BOTH
input flags with the AND spelled out. Run it in a private match and in a public
match and the difference names itself. RULE A17: both declared __int64, matching
the decompile.

Run `fh_statsgroup` in whatever match you are in -- that single line tells us
whether XP is reachable without giving up bots.

# HOSTING IS A CREATE-TIME ACT — user's read, confirmed (2026-08-14, build 3FEB2EF9)

USER: "probably because you have to create it right?" -- correct, and it is the
right way to think about the whole area.

    AreWeHost (lobby + 1598540) is written ONLY by sub_490E70
    sub_490E70 is reachable ONLY from:
        sub_491DE0   session CREATE
        sub_473BE0   host migration

So you become host by CREATING a session or by WINNING A MIGRATION. There is no
third path, which is exactly why a failed DS search has nothing to fall back
into -- there is no "become host" transition available at failure time.

## sub_80290 -- the create-a-hosted-session routine, re-read on the current IDB

    sub_8BBC50();
    v0 = sub_4A0B80(0);                       // local client
    v2 = sub_470F20(Lobby_Get(0));            // the lobby (identity)
    sub_484250(v2); sub_6FC480(*v2); sub_4843B0(v2);   // reset the session
    sub_47A720(v2, v0, 1);
    ... build visibility flags v8 from sub_8274B0 / 827580 / 827590 / 8275E0 ...
    sub_197420(v2, 0);                        // private slots = 0
    LobbyParams_SetPlaylistNum(v2, 0);        // playlist = 0
    sub_491DE0(v2, 0, v0, v8, 0, LobbyParams_GetMaxPlayers(v2));   // CREATE
    sub_924930(sub_470D50(v1), 1);
    if (sub_480E90(v2)) sub_28D340();                  // privateEscape
    if (sub_4810F0(v2)) sub_29B510(v2[2], v0);         // ADVERTISE
    sub_8BBDB0(...);

Zero arguments, so it is callable. Note it FORCES playlist 0 and clears private
slots, i.e. it builds a fresh hosted session rather than adapting the current
one. Still no code xrefs (Arxan indirect dispatch) -- only .pdata.

## ⛔ CORRECTED — my active_lobby() switch was a REGRESSION, reverted

I changed force_host's param LATCHING to sub_470CB0's "active" lobby after
catching lobby0/lobby1 disagreeing on AreWeHost during a transition. That was
wrong. The ENGINE's own param writers all target slot 0:

    sub_1972B0  setgameprivatematch     -> Lobby_Get(0)
    sub_80290   create hosted session   -> Lobby_Get(0)
    sub_654100  stats-group decision    -> Lobby_Get(0)

sub_470CB0 is used by the LUI-FACING getters (GetPartyMaxPlayers and friends),
not by the writers we care about. So latching slot 0 was correct all along.

REVERTED: tick(), apply_playlist_now() and cmd_canhost() are back on lobby(0).
`active_lobby()` is KEPT for the fh_status readout only, where seeing slot 0 and
slot 1 disagree is genuinely useful. The lesson generalises: **which lobby object
is "right" depends on the consumer -- match the specific engine function you are
trying to influence, never pick one globally.**

# SHIPPED — `fh_createhost`, the engine's own create-hosted-session path
# (2026-08-14, build 89D1E750, deployed + hash-verified). NOT YET TESTED.

Per the Fix Declaration Rules this is a CANDIDATE, not "works".

## What it does

Calls `sub_80290` (IDA 0x80290 - 0x1000 = 0x7F290), zero args, returns __int64
(RULE A17 -- declared exactly, not narrowed). That is the engine's own
"create a hosted session and advertise it" routine:

    reset the session (sub_484250 / sub_6FC480 / sub_4843B0)
    sub_47A720(params, client, 1)
    build the visibility flag word
    sub_197420(params, 0)                 private slots = 0
    LobbyParams_SetPlaylistNum(params, 0) playlist = 0
    sub_491DE0(params, 0, client, flags, 0, maxPlayers)   <- CREATE -> AreWeHost=1
    if (sub_480E90) sub_28D340()          privateEscape
    if (sub_4810F0) sub_29B510(...)       ADVERTISE

Nothing is fabricated: the engine's path, with the engine's own arguments,
reached from a console command instead of from Arxan's indirect dispatch.

## Guards and reporting

  * REFUSES when connstate >= 9 (in a game), because creating a session resets
    the current one and would drop you out of the match. `fh_createhost force`
    overrides, for when that is the intent.
  * prints AreWeHost / dedicated / private / playlist / min / max BEFORE and
    AFTER, plus the return value, so the effect is visible rather than assumed.
  * states plainly whether AreWeHost actually became set, and says "nothing was
    faked, the engine refused somewhere inside" if it did not.

## ⚠ KNOWN SIDE EFFECTS, by design not by accident

  * it FORCES playlist 0 and CLEARS private slots -- it builds a FRESH session
    rather than converting the one you are in. force_host's tick will re-latch a
    configured playlist afterwards.
  * sub_80290 has no code xrefs (Arxan indirect dispatch), so it is normally
    reached through a dispatch table. Calling it directly is the untested part.

## What to watch for

  AreWeHost 0 -> 1   the create took, you are the host
  AreWeHost stays 0  the engine refused inside sub_491DE0; read the BEFORE/AFTER
                     line for which field blocked it
  a hang             would indicate an Arxan return-address check on this path,
                     which is the specific risk of calling a dispatch-only
                     function from outside the image

# ⭐⭐ BOT COSMETICS — THE FORMAT IS THE SAME ONE THE GAME USES FOR YOU (2026-08-14)

## PROVEN — the whole customization payload is SEVEN INTEGERS

    sub_14B820(struct, buf, size) =

            dword@+0, +4, +8, +12, +16, +20, byte@+24);

It travels to the server in the bot's connect string as `\ctz\<that string>`:

    Info_SetValueForKey(userinfo, "ctz", v42);

So bots and humans share ONE customization format. Copying a real player's look
onto a bot is a struct copy, not a translation. That also retires the worry that
bot appearance is a separate system.

i.e. **unk_6CDE8F8, stride 28 bytes per client**, is the live 7-field struct.
IDA 0x6CDE8F8 - 0x1000 = 0x6CDD8F8. Readable and writable directly.

### Why the SERIALIZER is hooked, not the generator

The 7-field struct is a LOCAL inside SV_AddBot, so it cannot be reached directly
-- but sub_14B820 receives a POINTER to it. The stub writes through that pointer
and then calls the ORIGINAL, so the wire format stays the engine's own.

The stub early-outs unless `_ReturnAddress()` is inside SV_AddBot
([0xF2650, 0xF28A0)), so **Dvar_InfoString -- a real player's own ctz -- is never
touched**, even with the feature on. Same structural-safety approach as the
renamer.

RULE A3.1 checked: nothing else in src/ hooks 0x14B820.

# ⭐⭐ LOBBY KICK TOOL — the member array, fully mapped (2026-08-14, build FFFD877D)

USER: dropped the "spawn a server I own" goal, accepted the semi/half force host
(lobby host), and asked for a KICK so blatant cheaters can be removed.

## PROVEN — every offset, from the engine's own accessors

    sub_49E3C0  returns  lobby + 1016 + 33216 * memberIndex
                -> member array base 1016, stride 33216
    sub_481260  gates on *(BYTE*)(lobby + 1016 + 33216*i)
                and reads the id at *(QWORD*)(lobby + 21568 + 33216*i)
    sub_1912F0  walks i in 0..47 requiring state >= 5, matches that id, and
                returns  lobby + 21634 + 33216*i   <- the per-member NAME.
                Its `if (++v2 >= 48)` is where the 48-member cap comes from.

So:

    state  lobby + 1016  + 33216*i     >= 5 means connected
    xuid   lobby + 21568 + 33216*i     SteamID64 on PC
    name   lobby + 21634 + 33216*i
    max    48 members

`PartyHost_KickPlayer` @0x48CD70 (twin-named from AW earlier via the anchors
'%ikickedFromParty' and 'kicked'):

        sub_48AA00(lobby, memberIdx)      // remove from the party

⚠ NOT `SV_KickClient` @0x6D6CC0 -- this file already records that it opens with
`if (!com_sv_running[16]) return;`, i.e. it requires that you ARE the server. In

## WHAT REMAINS -- the whole of it, and why each part is justified

    join gate      the mechanism. Hook on Lobby_AcceptSearchResult (a pure
                   predicate: three reads and a bool, so it is about as close to
                   a passive observer as a hook gets -- see RULE A19). Refuses
                   other people's lobbies while searching, DISARMS on entering a
                   game and gives up after 90 s so it can never strand you.
    g_hostingEnabled re-assert   repairing a one-way latch (its only writer can
                   only CLEAR), not inventing a capability. The re-assert COUNT
                   is reported: a climbing count is inference-free proof that a
                   host predicate is running and failing.
    allowJoiningListenServer     params[15]. Public playlists ship it 0.
    requireOpenNat clear         params[13]. Skips the strict-NAT refusal.
    qualification relax          the ten upload/ping threshold dvars, keyed on

    kick + roster  PartyHost_KickPlayer, and the Players tab.
    fh_status / fh_canhost / fh_statsgroup   READ-ONLY diagnostics. Kept, because
                   when hosting does not work these name the term that refused.

force_host is ONE hook (the join gate) and it ships with an off switch
(s2mp_nojoingate.txt) per RULE A20.

The Host tab used to print "dedicated: YES" with no context, which reads as a

expected. It now leads with what you own, and reports:

## WHY THE SERVER HALF IS CLOSED (kept so it is not re-attempted)

  * the search tick forks `if (sessionType == 2 && sub_1FF290()) DS else lobby`,
    and the join gate only ever sees LOBBY results;
  * the DS FAILURE path (sub_6FF040 -> sub_1FE630) sets state 5 and RESTARTS the
    search -- there is no listen-server branch to fall into;
  * AreWeHost is written only by sub_490E70, reachable only from session CREATE
    and host MIGRATION. Hosting is a create-time act;
  * blocking the DS search with dvar "3707" = 0 just means no match is found.


# ⭐⭐⭐ XBOX / MICROSOFT STORE PORT — FEASIBILITY MEASURED (2026-08-15, offline)

USER: port the WHOLE mod to the Store/Game Pass build, "with arxan lifting and
stuff". Measured before answering. VERDICT: the address port is largely
MECHANICAL; the hard blocker is the LOADER, not the addresses.

## ⭐ THE DECISIVE MEASUREMENT — the two builds are the SAME CODEGEN

Took the 22 functions named in BOTH IDBs and compared their sizes:

    21 of 22 are IDENTICAL to the byte
    the 1 exception is SV_SpawnServer, -16 bytes on Xbox

So this is the same source built with the same settings, RELOCATED -- not a
different game. That is the single best condition for automated matching, and it
is why a binary differ will work here where it often does not.

It also means the diff FINDS THE LOGIC DIFFERENCES FOR FREE: a size delta is a
behavioural change. SV_SpawnServer (-16) joins the already-known
Session_CanHostServer difference (Xbox has NO bandwidth-test outer gate and no
g_hostingEnabled latch -- see the 2026-08-12 entry).

## The scale, measured from src/ rather than estimated

    341 distinct addresses used by the mod
        232  code (resolve to a containing function in the Steam IDB)
        109  DATA globals (no containing function -- need operand-level matching)

    of the 232 code addresses, only 86 are properly NAMED in our own Steam IDB.
    We hardcoded sub_ addresses for the rest, so a NAME-based port covers little:

        TIER A  named in both IDBs, direct lookup :  22
        TIER B  named in Steam only               :  64
        TIER C  unnamed or data                   : 255

## ⛔ SIZE ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH — measured, do not build a matcher on it

    Xbox  63,678 functions, 2,241 distinct sizes,  778 sizes unique to one func
    Steam 61,481 functions, 2,202 distinct sizes,  772 unique

    (the ~2,200 extra Xbox functions are the GDK/XCurl code replacing Steam)

Against the mod's own 232 code addresses:

    UNIQUE same-size candidate  :  30   <- auto
    2-8 candidates              :  30
    9+ candidates               : 172   <- most of them

Large functions are uniquely sized (5209, 2803, 3753 -> exactly 1 match each);
small ones collide hard (183 -> 91 candidates). So size is a SEED, not a matcher.
The real tool is call-graph propagation from confirmed anchors, i.e. BinDiff or
Diaphora. NEITHER IS INSTALLED; both are free.

## ⚠ THE ACTUAL HARD BLOCKER IS THE LOADER

tools/Launch-S2.ps1 does CreateProcessW(SUSPENDED) -> VirtualAllocEx ->
WriteProcessMemory -> CreateRemoteThread(LoadLibraryW). None of that transfers
cleanly:

  * the Store exe lives in C:\Program Files\WindowsApps, ACL-locked to
    TrustedInstaller -- you cannot drop a DLL beside it or read it normally;
  * a Store title is started through AppX ACTIVATION, not CreateProcessW on the
    exe path, so there is no obvious place to pass CREATE_SUSPENDED;
  * SUSPENDED IS NOT OPTIONAL HERE -- this file already records that injecting
    while suspended is why the hooks are installed before the game does anything.

CANDIDATE SOLUTION (untested): an IFEO "Debugger" stub. Set
HKLM\...\Image File Execution Options\s2_mp64_ship.exe\Debugger to our
launcher; the kernel then starts OUR stub with the real command line whatever
activated the game, and the stub does the suspended CreateProcessW itself.
Fallback: IApplicationActivationManager::ActivateApplication returns the PID,
then suspend every thread and inject -- racy, and it loses the "before anything
runs" guarantee.

## Arxan, honestly scoped

STATIC is already solved: the Xbox dump exists (F:\WWII XBOX Dump\, 322 MB) and
587 functions are named in it. What is UNKNOWN is RUNTIME behaviour on that build
-- return-address checks, control-flow flattening and whether it tolerates ~60
MinHook detours the way the Steam build does. Same product, so likely similar;
not measured.

## ⭐ WHY THE FIRST PHASE IS WORTH DOING EVEN IF THE PORT NEVER SHIPS

Today all 341 addresses are scattered literals across 25 files. **A single Steam
patch breaks every one of them and the mod is dead.** Centralising them behind
named symbols in one per-build table, with an automated re-derivation pipeline,
is patch insurance first and a port enabler second.

## Suggested sequencing (NOT started -- scope decision is the user's)

    0. install Diaphora, diff the two IDBs -> a function map. Non-invasive,
       decides everything else. Cheap.
    1. centralise the 341 addresses behind named symbols + build detection at
       init. Invasive but mechanical; valuable on its own (see above).
    2. emit the Xbox table from the diff. The 109 data globals come from matched
       functions' instruction operands, not from names.
    3. the loader (IFEO stub).
    4. test and chase the logic differences. RULE A13 makes this fast -- the game
       writes a minidump next to the exe on every fault.

## Tool added

    tools/s2_port_map.py -- pulls every address out of src/, resolves each in the
    Steam IDB and looks the name up in the Xbox IDB; writes tools/s2_xbox_map.json
    for the ones that resolve today (22).

# ⭐⭐⭐ NAMEPLATES -- THERE ARE **TWO** ENUMERATORS, AND THE GATE IS sub_52610
# (2026-08-16)

## ⛔ CORRECTION -- I hooked the wrong enumerator, and the probe said so

Build 20A821C4 hooked sub_37F00's team gate (sub_38F510) and its visibility test
(sub_5161D0). Measured in game:

    [names] team gate hook : live
    [names] through walls  : ON (hook live)
    [names] gate opened 0 time(s), visibility 0 time(s)

Both hooks INSTALLED (non-null orig) and NEITHER EVER FIRED. Because the probe
reported unconditionally (RULE A15), "0" was decisive rather than ambiguous: the
hooks were fine, the code path was wrong.

## PROVEN -- two nameplate enumerators, and only one is theater-aware

`sub_3C9B0` is the nameplate DRAW. It has exactly two code callers:

    sub_304B0 (0x304B0, 0x1d6)  <- sub_3FA30 (0x3FA30, 0x2da)   sub_3C9B0(..., 0)
    sub_37F00 (0x37F00, 0x43a)  <- sub_E7980 (the cg_draw2D 2D HUD)  sub_3C9B0(..., 1)

The last argument of sub_3C9B0 distinguishes the two styles. **sub_304B0 is the
per-player FADING nameplate** -- it keeps fade state in unk_27C5C70 and takes its
show/hide decision as a PARAMETER from its caller.

⭐ THE TELL: sub_304B0 special-cases `CL_IsDemoPlaying` (uses Sys_Milliseconds for
its fade clock during playback), and sub_52610 special-cases
`CG_IsTheaterFreeCamera` / `CG_IsTheaterOrbitCamera`. **sub_37F00 contains no
theater awareness whatsoever.** For a demo/freecam workflow it was never going to
run -- which is precisely what "0 times" measured.

## ⭐ THE GATE -- sub_52610, ONE CALLER, PURE PREDICATE

`sub_3FA30` walks the active player list (count at `4*client + 21869568`, array at
`448*client + 21868672`) and per player does:

    v24 = sub_49FF0(client, ent) == 0;
    v25 = v24 && v21;                        // v21 = PVS/visibility bits @41704568
    v26 = v24 && v20;                        // v20 = the player I am looking at
    sub_57DC0(client, ent, v26, v25);
    if (!v26) {
        v27 = sub_52610(client, ent, v25);   // <-- THE DECISION
        sub_304B0(client, slot, teamOrSomething, v27);
    }

    char __fastcall sub_52610(unsigned int a1, __int64 a2, char a3)   size 0x1ae

Its own body, abridged:

    v10 = myTeam;   v11 = theirTeam;      // both from cg + 4704*id + 3878308
    if (myClientinfoValid && theirClientinfoValid) {
        if (sub_17ADD0(a1) && sub_17ACD0(a1, theirId) && (... & 0x4000)) return 1;
        if (CG_IsTheaterFreeCamera(a1) || CG_IsTheaterOrbitCamera(a1)) {
            if (v10 != 5 && a3) return 1;              // <-- THEATER: show if visible
        } else if (...) {
            if (v10 && v10 == v11 && dvar) { ... }     // same team
            if (sub_99900(v10, v11)) { ... }           // <-- THE TEAMMATE TEST
        }
    }
    return 0;

**xrefs to sub_52610: exactly ONE code caller, sub_3FA30 @0x3fcbd.** So it needs no
return-address scoping -- nothing else in the engine consults it, unlike sub_38F510
(23 call sites) which had to be scoped.

## ✅ THE FIX -- build B6E39DE9. CONFIRMED IN GAME by the user, all five Fix
## Declaration conditions met ("working exactly as intended, I can easily find
## which player I need to find").

Ask the engine first, only ever upgrade a NO:

    char nameplate_gate_stub(unsigned int client, __int64 entity, char visible)
    {
        const char real = g_gate_orig(client, entity, visible);
        if (real) return real;                       // engine already wants it
        if (!enabled()) return real;
        if (!through_walls() && !visible) return real;
        return 1;
    }

Calling the ORIGINAL FIRST is load-bearing: it preserves every precondition we
cannot see from outside (both clientinfos valid, team != 5, the looked-at-player
case sub_3FA30 handles separately), so a nameplate can never be drawn for a slot
the engine considers invalid. We only ever turn 0 into 1, never 1 into 0.

Honouring `visible` by default MIRRORS sub_52610's own theater branch
(`if (v10 != 5 && a3) return 1;`) rather than inventing a rule. `names_thruwalls`
ignores it -- that is what that toggle is for.

    RULE A1:  sub_52610  IDA 0x52610 - 0x1000 = 0x51610
    RULE A17: returns `char`, args (unsigned int, __int64, char). Transcribed, not
              widened -- the same class of mistake that crashed the game 3 times
              when sub_5161D0 was declared with no parameters.
    RULE A19: pure predicate. Reads state, calls other predicates, writes nothing.

The sub_37F00 hooks are KEPT (they early-out and cost a trampoline) because that
enumerator is a real path under the 2D HUD; they simply do not serve theater.

## The `names` command now names its own cause (RULE A15)

    gate ran 0                  -> sub_3FA30 is not running; not in a live match
    gate ran N, forced 0, yes>0 -> the engine already says yes; names should show
    gate ran N, forced M        -> we upgraded M; if still nothing, the block is
                                   downstream in sub_304B0's fade timer
    gate ran N, always no, 0 forced -> turn on names_thruwalls; the engine's own
                                   visibility flag is false for those players

## NAMED IN THE S2 IDB (saved, RULE A10)

TWIN-PROVEN against AW (which has the whole cluster named). The decisive evidence
is the call SHAPE, not the size: AW's CG_ApplyFadeAndDrawOverheadNames is called
TWICE from CG_FinishDrawVisibleNames, and S2's sub_3FA30 calls sub_304B0 twice in
the same positions (crosshair-target at the top, then per player in the loop).

    0x3FA30   CG_FinishDrawVisibleNames          <- AW 0x82682B48 (0x428)
    0x304B0   CG_ApplyFadeAndDrawOverheadNames   <- AW 0x826824D8 (0x1e4 vs 0x1d6)

AW's full set, for anyone extending this: CG_UpdatePlayerNames (0x826841E8) =
CG_DrawVisibleNames + CG_DrawClonedPlayerNames; CG_FinishUpdatePlayerNames
(0x826835E8); CG_DrawOverheadNamesNew (0x82681A58).

BEHAVIOUR-PROVEN, descriptive -- no AW twin located, do NOT assume it is the real
engine name:

    0x52610   CG_ShouldDrawPlayerName(localClient, entity, visible) -> char

DELIBERATELY NOT NAMED: `sub_99900(myTeam, theirTeam)`, the team-relationship test
inside CG_ShouldDrawPlayerName. Its POLARITY was never confirmed (the same-team
case is handled separately just above it), and the Function Naming Rule's tier 3
applies -- an honest sub_ beats a wrong name. It is not load-bearing for the mod.

    cg + 1993776  tanHalfFovX      cg + 1993780  tanHalfFovY
    cg + 1993796  view origin      (agrees with dolly.cpp / world_project.hpp)
    cg + 1993808  axis forward     cg + 1993820  axis row1   cg + 1993832  axis row2
    cg + 2495924 / +2495928 / +2355480   the aim angles fed to AngleVectors (sub_75EC50)

⭐ **THE OUTPUT IS AN OFFSET FROM SCREEN CENTRE in 640x480 virtual units.** That
is why no draw-path surgery is needed -- adding to those two floats IS the sway,
already in the engine's own units and sign convention.

## ⭐ PROVEN PURELY COSMETIC -- this was the real risk and it is cleared

All FIVE callers are draw paths:

    sub_3E00C0, sub_3E0800, sub_3E1800   <- sub_E7980 (the cg_draw2D 2D HUD)
    sub_3E2FB0                           <- nested under sub_3E1800
    sub_3E3570                           <- CG_DrawActiveFrame

None is an entity scan or gameplay path. The crosshair ENTITY scan (what reddens
the reticle / what a nametag targets) traces from the view independently and
never consults this function. So an offset here cannot affect aim, bullet
direction, hit detection or targeting. **It moves pixels only.**

Corollary that shaped the design: it can run SEVERAL TIMES PER FRAME (normal /
turret / vehicle reticles), so the sway must be integrated ONCE per frame or the
effect scales with however many crosshairs happen to be drawn.

## SHIPPED -- src/hud/dynamic_crosshair.{hpp,cpp}, build 90688AC2

ONE hook (IDA 0x3E10A0 - 0x1000 = 0x3E00A0). RULE A3.1 checked: nothing else in
src/ referenced either form.

  * RULE A17: `std::int64_t __fastcall(std::int64_t, float*, float*)` -- it
    returns AngleVectors' result and takes three args, all forwarded.
  * RULE A21 SIDESTEPPED ENTIRELY: the stub uses the `cg` it is HANDED as
    argument 1, never resolving cg a second way. There is no second source to
    disagree with, which is the exact trap that crashed dolly.
  * Clock is `demo_game::now_ms()` (Sys_Milliseconds), NOT cls_realtime --
    cls_realtime freezes in capture states, cannot go backwards, and ignores
    timescale, all three of which would break a smoothed effect.
  * dt clamped to (0, 250] ms; a jump resets the state, so pause/seek/alt-tab
    cannot fling the reticle.

Model (user chose rotation AND movement):
  ROTATION  dot(forward_now, row_prev) is, for small angles, the radians turned
            toward that axis; / dt gives a RATE, which is bounded by how fast you
            can physically turn, so it cannot blow up. Converted through
            (320/tanX) -- the engine's OWN axis-space -> 640x480 mapping -- so it
            is automatically FOV-correct and in the right sign convention.
  MOVEMENT  camera velocity from the refdef view origin delta, not a playerstate
            velocity field: it is inside the block we already validated, needs no
            unproven ps offset, and behaves correctly in freecam and demos.
  SMOOTHING exponential, framerate-independent (`1 - exp(-dt/tau)`); the target
            returns to 0 by itself when you stop, so the reticle settles.
  CLAMP     as a RADIUS, not per axis, so a diagonal flick cannot reach 1.41x the
            limit and the motion stays circular.

Commands: `crosshair_sway [0|1]`, `crosshair_sway_rot`, `crosshair_sway_move`,
`crosshair_sway_smooth`, `crosshair_sway_max`. Off by default, works in live play
and demo playback. Float args use `strtof` + `end` so a typo is rejected rather
than silently becoming 0 (GameUtil::safeStringToFloat cannot tell "0" from junk).

## THE CENTRE DOT (build 91FF0163)

A small MWII-style dot that rides the crosshair. It does NOT recompute the sway:
the stub captures CG_CalcCrosshairPosition's FINAL output (engine position + our
offset) once per frame, so the dot tracks whatever the reticle actually does --
including engine-side offsets we never modelled (third person, vehicles,
turrets). It also works with the sway OFF, sitting at centre.

  * Drawn from the EXISTING R_EndFrame hook in InternalConsole.cpp via a
    call-out next to `dolly::render()`. NOT a second Hook::create on that target
    (RULE A3.1). That is a proven engine-2D draw context.
  * ⚠ CROSSES A THREAD BOUNDARY: the stub records on the client thread during
    the 2D pass; render_dot() consumes on the RENDER thread inside R_EndFrame.
    Hence the atomics on the position and the pending flag.
  * `g_dot_pending.exchange(false)` CONSUMES the flag, so if no crosshair was
    positioned this frame -- menus, scoreboard, dead, killcam -- the dot vanishes
    with the reticle instead of hanging in the middle of the screen.
  * 640x480 virtual offset -> render-target pixels via the two globals dolly.cpp
    already uses (IDA 0x1C86268 / 0x1C8626C). Size is specified at 1080p and
    scaled by h/1080 so it does not shrink on a 1440p/4K display.
  * Off-screen and non-finite guards before anything reaches the render command
    list.

Commands: `crosshair_dot [0|1]`, `crosshair_dot_size <px>` (default 3 px @1080p).

NOT YET TESTED IN GAME -- CANDIDATE per the Fix Declaration Rules.

## BUILD NOTE -- orphaned mspdbsrv can wedge the build

A parallel build failed with `C1041: cannot open program database
xsk-gsc-s2.pdb`, and the pdb then could not be deleted ("Device or resource
busy") because orphaned `cl` / `MSBuild` / **`mspdbsrv`** processes still held it.
mspdbsrv is the PDB server and persists between builds by design. Killing the
three and rebuilding with `-m:1` cleared it. This is distinct from the recurring
stale-`s2mp-mod.pdb` LNK1201, which is fixed by deleting that file.
