# ⛔ KICK TOOL -- my_xuid() ASSUMED THE LOCAL PLAYER IS MEMBER 0 (2026-08-16)

USER TEST of the kick tool: "I only tested kicking myself, it does grab my
steamid64". That partial test verified the risky half AND exposed a real bug.

## VERIFIED by that test -- the member array offsets are right

A correct SteamID64 coming back proves member stride 33216, state 1016, xuid
21568 and name 21634 all resolve. Those were the offsets most likely to render
convincing garbage if wrong, so this is a meaningful confirmation.

## ⛔ THE BUG -- an unproven assumption, openly admitted in its own comment

    [[nodiscard]] std::uint64_t my_xuid()
    {
        const auto* L = lobby(0);
        const auto* p = L + 21568;   // "member 0's id; the local client is
                                     //  member 0 when we are the host"
        ...
    }

If the local player is NOT member 0 this returns SOMEONE ELSE'S id, so `is_me`
marks the wrong player as "you". The tool then REFUSES to kick that innocent
person and ALLOWS you to kick YOURSELF -- wrong in both directions. The user's
test passed only because they WERE member 0 (consistent with being lobby host).

## THE FIX -- the engine's own per-local-client account id

    sub_856250(localClient)              thunk ->
    sub_789870(localClient) = *((_QWORD *)&unk_D8ACED8 + 13 * client)

A plain global array, 13 qwords (104 bytes) per local client. No retaddr check,
no Arxan (RULE A22 checked), so the global is READ DIRECTLY rather than called.

    RULE A1:  unk_D8ACED8  IDA 0xD8ACED8 - 0x1000 = 0xD8ABED8
              stride 104 bytes per local client

**SAME ID SPACE, PROVEN BY THE ENGINE ITSELF:** sub_4813D0 takes
sub_856250()'s return and searches the member array for
`id@member+21568 == id`. The engine compares these two fields directly, so they
are necessarily the same value -- this is not an inference from magnitude.

CORROBORATED INDEPENDENTLY: CL_Demo_StartRecord writes sub_789870(client) into
the demo header at +0x10 -- the field this file already records as differing
between the private demos and publicmatch, i.e. the recording ACCOUNT.

0 now means "cannot identify us", which DISABLES the self-kick guard rather than
guessing at a slot, and `fh_who` says so out loud (RULE A15) instead of silently
marking nobody.

Build 33616E7B, deployed and hash-verified. NOT yet tested -- CANDIDATE.

## ⭐ PartyHost_KickPlayer's GATES, ENUMERATED -- and a FALSE SUCCESS removed

CLAUDE.md previously recorded this function as "... gates ...", never enumerated.
Since the real test needs two people, an unexplained no-op would have cost a
whole arranged session. Decompiled:

    PartyHost_KickPlayer(_QWORD *lobby, unsigned __int8 member):
        if ( sub_4811F0() || sub_481210(lobby, member)
             || !sub_6FE240(*lobby, member) )
            return sub_48E3D0(lobby, member, 1, "kicked");   // ALTERNATE path --
                                                             // still a real kick
        result = sub_6FF6D0(*lobby, member);
        if ( !(BYTE)result ) {
            ... sub_76A3D0("%ikickedFromParty"); sub_76E200(...) ...
            return sub_48AA00(lobby, member);                // remove from party
        }
        return result;                                       // <-- SILENT NO-OP

So there are TWO working paths, and exactly ONE way it silently does nothing:

    sub_6FF6D0(rawSession, m) = *(DWORD*)(rawSession + 156 + 56*m) == 2

i.e. a per-member SESSION state (stride 56, based at rawSession+156 -- NOT the
lobby member array, which is stride 33216). rawSession is `*lobby`, one
indirection, as already proven when the republish latch was walking the wrong
base.

⛔ OUR WRAPPER CLAIMED SUCCESS UNCONDITIONALLY:

        fn(L, index);
        why.clear();
        return true;       // <-- return value DISCARDED

so `fh_kick` printed "kicked slot N" whether or not anything happened. Fixed:
the state-2 case is pre-checked and refused with a reason, and the engine's
return value is now printed rather than thrown away.

Build 526C82A8, deployed and hash-verified.

## ⚠ STILL UNTESTED: kicking SOMEBODY ELSE

Self-kick is refused by design, so the user's test could not exercise
PartyHost_KickPlayer at all. What is verified is the roster read; what is not is
that the kick itself works. That needs a second person in the lobby.

## ⚠ player_box.cpp IS BUILT ON OFFSETS THIS DISPROVES -- default OFF, unreliable

sub_37F00's decompile shows the engine does NOT do what player_box does:

    player_box                          the engine
    iterates entities 0..17             walks a visible list: cg[22960], count
                                        +28004, int16 entity numbers +28016,
                                        stride 256 shorts
    reads origin at entity + 48         calls sub_AF9B70() for a BONE-TAG position,
                                        then v35 + 24.0 for the head
    copy_name(loopIndex)                v11 = *(char*)(ent + 1201) - 1, i.e. the
                                        0-BASED client number derived from the
                                        1-based id; the TEAM array uses the raw
                                        1-based value

So `ENTITY_ORIGIN = 48` is unproven, the name index is off by one, and the name
BASE disagrees with what CE measured live (`cg + 4405240 + 152*i`, name at +60).
It is SEH-guarded and default OFF so it cannot crash, but it would draw boxes in
the wrong place with blank or wrong names. **Do not trust it.** The nameplate
ungate above supersedes it for the "who is that / where are they" goal; the only
unique thing player_box adds is the box outline itself.


# XBOX / STORE PORT -- PIPELINE BUILT AND VALIDATED (2026-08-15). See docs/XBOX-PORT.md

Full detail lives in docs/XBOX-PORT.md. This is the index entry.

## THE HEADLINE MEASUREMENT

The Steam and Microsoft Store builds are the SAME SOURCE, SAME COMPILER SETTINGS.
Across 28,428 automatically matched function pairs, 28,391 are IDENTICAL in size
to the byte (99.9%). Only 37 diverge, and only ONE of those is a function the mod
touches (SV_SpawnServer, -16 bytes, benign -- same signature, and we only hook its
entry to print).

That is why the port is mechanical rather than 341 separate RE jobs.

## WHAT WAS BUILT

    tools/s2_export_idb.py     dump an IDB's function graph (size, name, callees)
    tools/s2_match_builds.py   match the builds; HOLDOUT-VALIDATED at 99.36%
                               precision (310 correct, 2 wrong, of 370 hidden pairs)
    tools/s2_map_globals.py    data globals via instruction-offset alignment
    tools/s2_emit_buildmap.py  emits src/BuildMap.Store.inc
    tools/s2_port_map.py       coverage report (the name-based first attempt)
    tools/Launch-S2-Store.ps1  the Store loader
    src/BuildMap.hpp + .inc    the translation layer
    src/ModPaths.hpp           per-build writable data directory

COVERAGE: 322 of the mod's 341 addresses mapped (94.4%). 19 unresolved, listed in
the doc; none of them fails silently (see poison, below).

## INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED -- this is the part that makes it trustworthy

The pipeline reproduced 8 of 8 Store addresses that had been derived MONTHS EARLIER
by hand, by decompiling the GSC binding table. None was fed to the matcher:
g_hostingEnabled 0x106BA28, Session_CanHostServer 0x849380, LobbyParams_GetPrivate,
LobbyParams_GetRequireOpenNat, Session_IsHostingEnabled, the two qualification
getters, Playlist_IsAlwaysSearch. dvar_online was confirmed separately by
decompiling the Store twin of Com_IsOnlineGame, which reads the exact global the
resolver predicted.

Also: the matcher independently flagged Session_CanHostServer as divergent, which
CLAUDE.md already recorded from the 2026-08-12 hand analysis.

## THE TRANSLATION LAYER -- and why it matters for STEAM too

Every hardcoded address funnels through ONE function, so the port hooks in there
rather than at 341 call sites:

    size_t _b(const size_t val) { return build_map::resolve(base, val); }

Build detection is the EXE_ERR_PROCESS_DEMO_FILE_FAILED string -- the same
signature RULE A2 uses for a CE attachment. Steam IDA 0xBCE9E0, Store 0xC6D5B0.
NOT a version number and NOT a module size, both of which a patch changes.

On Steam it is a strict no-op: one branch, then `base + val`.

An address MISSING from the Store table never falls through to the Steam value --
that would corrupt arbitrary memory silently. It returns POISON
(0x0000DEAD00000000 + low bits of the offset): canonical, guaranteed unmapped, and
a minidump names which entry was missing (RULE A13).

WORTH KEEPING EVEN IF THE PORT NEVER SHIPS: all 341 addresses are literals in 25
files today, so ONE STEAM PATCH KILLS THE WHOLE MOD. With the table plus the
pipeline, recovering from a patch is a tool run rather than a rebuild from scratch.

## BLOCKS -- recorded, not solved

  1. THE LOADER IS UNVERIFIED. CreateProcessW is impossible: the Store exe is in
     WindowsApps and MEASURED not readable (Test-Path True, IO.File::Open ACCESS
     DENIED). IFEO does not help either -- IFEO keys are per image NAME and the
     Store exe is ALSO called s2_mp64_ship.exe, so one key would catch Steam too.
     Launch-S2-Store.ps1 uses IPackageDebugSettings::EnableDebugging instead (the
     documented packaged-app debugger mechanism: next activation starts SUSPENDED,
     with the OS doing the activation so package identity is correct).
     VERIFIED LIVE: package resolves, IPackageDebugSettings QueryInterfaces, and
     DisableDebugging really executes. UNVERIFIED: that it suspends this title,
     that OpenProcess succeeds, that the mod survives GDK licensing.
     ⚠ If a run dies between arming and disarming, EVERY later launch hangs waiting
     for a debugger. Recovery: Launch-S2-Store.ps1 -Disarm.
  2. 19 addresses unresolved (mostly 5-byte thunks and isolated functions).
  3. FILE LAYOUT half done. src/ModPaths.hpp gives a per-build writable directory
     and bots.cpp is wired to it (Steam path byte-identical, so existing
     botnames.txt keeps working). Marker files, main/s2mp_console.log and the demo
     directory are NOT yet addressed.
  4. ARXAN AT RUNTIME on the Store build is unknown -- hook tolerance, retaddr
     checks. Static is solved (the dump exists, 587 functions named).

## PowerShell COM note, worth remembering

IPackageDebugSettings and IApplicationActivationManager are IUnknown-only with no
IDispatch. PowerShell can CREATE the objects but cannot late-bind to their methods
("does not contain a method named ..."), and New-Object cannot drive [CoClass] on
an interface either. Every call must be made from C# via Add-Type, where the cast
is a real QueryInterface and the vtable call is static.

## DECISION 2026-08-15 -- ONE BINARY, NOT TWO PROJECTS

User asked originally to "copy this project again" for the Store build. When the
unified approach was presented instead, the user chose to KEEP IT UNIFIED.

So: ONE s2mp-mod.dll, detecting the build at boot and translating addresses
through BuildMap.Store.inc. There is NO second project, NO second repo, and there
should not be one -- the reason is that every fix in this project would otherwise
have to be made twice and the two copies would drift. The demo, bot, host and HUD
work is all shared source.

If a Store-only divergence is ever genuinely needed, branch on
build_map::current() at that one site rather than forking the build.

## FILE LAYOUT FOR THE STORE BUILD -- now done except the demo directory

src/ModPaths.hpp, wired into bots.cpp, force_host.cpp, netlog.cpp and LogFile.cpp.
STEAM PATHS ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL -- existing botnames.txt/botkits.txt keep working
and main/s2mp_console.log does not move (probe retrieval depends on it).

    mod data   Steam <exe dir>\S2MP-Mod    Store %LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\<PFN>\LocalState\S2MP-Mod
    markers    Steam <exe dir>              Store  same LocalState folder
    log        Steam main/s2mp_console.log  Store  LocalState\S2MP-Mod\s2mp_console.log

STILL OPEN: the demo directory (main\demo) is the ENGINE's path, not ours, so it
may already resolve somewhere writable on Store. Not investigated.

⚠ ESCAPING TRAP HIT WHILE DOING THIS: writing C++ through a python heredoc turned
"\\s2mp_console.log" into "\s2mp_console.log" -- an invalid C++ escape that
compiles but yields the wrong path. Fixed by using a FORWARD SLASH, which Windows
accepts and which cannot be mangled. When generating C++ string literals that
contain paths, prefer '/' or use the Write tool rather than a shell heredoc.

## THE DEMO SUBSYSTEM WAS NOT SKIPPED -- 98% mapped, and the FILE FORMAT is identical

Coverage by module, after the gap-resolver and override passes (build EAB2F310):

    demo_native.cpp     86 addresses   86 mapped
    demo_game.hpp       66             65      (gap: 0x16A570, mid-function)
    demo_playback.cpp   32             29      (gap: 3 data globals)
    demo_utils/dolly/recording/gui  13   13
    DEMO TOTAL         197            193      98.0%
    WHOLE PROJECT      341 distinct   334      98.0%

The demo system is the LARGEST consumer of addresses in the mod and is covered at
the same rate as everything else.

### ⭐ THE .demo FORMAT IS THE SAME ON BOTH BUILDS

More important than the addresses. CL_Demo_Play_f validates identical constants:

    gate                       Steam            Store
    clc+262760 version         == 29            == 29
    clc+262764 header size     == 79384         == 0x13618   <- THE SAME NUMBER
    clc+262784 exe mode        == 5             == 5
    header state blob          memcpy 0x135FC   memcpy 0x135FC

The Store IDB renders 79384 as `&loc_13618` because that immediate is also a valid
code address there. 0x13618 == 79384 exactly -- and it is the same value already
documented as the file offset where the packet stream begins.

CONSEQUENCE: demos are cross-compatible between Steam and Store, and every demo
tool (s2_demo_read.py, s2_dm_to_demo.py, s2_huffman.py, s2_svc_walk.py, the
type-21 footer repair, the embedded demo_ncs21.inc table) applies unchanged.

### ⛔ THE MATCHER CAN BE WRONG -- Com_Error proves it

Com_Error is 607 bytes on Steam and 552 on Store, i.e. one of the 37 genuinely
divergent functions. Size matching could not pair it, and PROPAGATION THEN GAVE
Store 0x8CA40 TO STEAM sub_82D5F0, an unrelated 552-byte function. A real false
positive -- the 0.64% the holdout predicted, showing up in practice.

Caught by call-site evidence: CL_Demo_Play_f is matched, and both builds call the
error function at the same two positions with the same unique strings ("428 %s %s"
and "EXE_ERR_INVALID_DEMO_FILE"). So Store 0x8CA40 IS Com_Error.

The bad pair never reached the emitted table (sub_82D5F0 is not a mod address) but
it DID lock Com_Error out of it.

FIX: tools/s2_overrides.json -- hand-verified pairs applied LAST, beating the
matcher. Every entry must carry its evidence; an override with no stated basis is
worse than a gap, because a gap faults loudly and a wrong entry does not.

RULE FOR ANYONE EXTENDING THIS: a function whose SIZE CHANGED cannot be matched by
size, and propagation may quietly fill its slot with a same-sized stranger.
Cross-check anything on the 37-function divergent list against a call site before
trusting it.

### New tool

    tools/s2_resolve_gaps.py  -- recovers functions the size matcher could not pair,
    by reading the call instruction at the same byte offset inside an already
    matched caller. Recovered 11 of 13; requires >= 2 agreeing callers for a strong
    result and refuses a target already claimed by another Steam function.


# ENEMY NAME TAGS FOR DEMOS -- MECHANISM MAPPED, ONE FIELD LEFT (2026-08-15)

GOAL (user): draw a name above players' heads during demo playback, ENEMIES ONLY,
so they can be located in freecam and identified after a kill. For cinematics.

## THE ENGINE'S OWN SYSTEM, from the AW twin (fully symboled)

    CG_UpdatePlayerNames          0x826841E8  = CG_DrawVisibleNames + CG_DrawClonedPlayerNames
    CG_DrawVisibleNames           0x82683DA0  the enumeration + friend/enemy test
    CG_ApplyFadeAndDrawOverheadNames 0x826824D8
    CG_DrawOverheadNamesNew       0x82681A58  the actual draw

CG_DrawVisibleNames' loop, which is the blueprint:

    team = cg->bgs.characterinfo[cg->predictedPlayerState.clientNum].team;   // MINE
    for each entity in cg->nextSnap->entities:
        cent = &cg_entitiesArray[1536*localClient + ent->number];
        if ((cent->nextState.eType == 1 || == 18) && !(eFlags & 0x20)) {
            isEnemy = team != TEAM_FREE && team != characterinfo[cent->nextState.clientNum].team;
            CG_ApplyFadeAndDrawOverheadNames(localClient, clientNum, team, visible);
        }

Head position in AW comes from a BONE TAG: CG_DObjGetWorldTagPos(pose, dobj,
scr_const.boneexpression3, &out). Name from CL_GetClientNameAndClanTagColorize.

## S2 EQUIVALENTS -- FOUND

Anchor: CG_RelativePlayerName IS already named in S2 @0x3E43C0 (from the earlier
AW string-anchor pass). Its two callers are sub_32D290 and sub_3C9B0.

    sub_3C9B0   0x3C9B0  (3180 B)  == CG_DrawOverheadNamesNew
                signature matches AW: (localClient, a2, float alpha, u8 entnum, char clientNum)
                and it does `sub_13A00(localClient, entnum)` to fetch the centity.
    sub_13A00   0x13A00            == the centity accessor (localClient, entnum) -> centity*
    sub_3E45B0  0x3E45B0           == the name COLOUR picker (NOT position -- it selects
                                      among numeric dvars "2508"/"2364"/"5034"/"1497"/
                                      "4787"/"3376" by team relationship)

### PROVEN offsets (all read straight out of sub_3C9B0 / sub_3E45B0)

    cg + 22904                     my own client number        (byte)
                                   -- cross-checks with dolly.cpp and broadcaster.cpp
    cg + 3878308 + 4704*clientNum  TEAM of that client         (dword; 5 == free/spectator)
                                   -- note broadcaster.cpp already uses cg+3878300+4704*slot
                                      as a gate, so +8 in the same 4704-stride record
    cg + 4405256 + 152*clientNum   NAME pointer                (char*)
                                   -- clientinfo base 4405240, stride 152, matches the
                                      broadcaster flag at +4405240 already documented

    centity (from sub_13A00):
        +1168  u16   entity number
        +1170  u16   otherEntityNum   (fed to the name getter sub_465CB0)
        +1178  byte  eType            (1/2 are the player-ish types here)
        +1184  dword eFlags           (tested & 0x1000)
        +1201  byte  clientNum        (fed to CG_RelativePlayerName)
        +1696  byte  valid/active flag, bit0  -- already known from CLAUDE.md

    name getters: sub_465CB0(localClient, clientNum, otherEntNum, buf, 36)
                  sub_465E90(localClient, clientNum, buf, 36, ?, 11, ?, 64)   (+clan tag)

### The DObj / bone-tag chain, for the head position

    sub_45540(localClient, float* out, char useTag)   reads a world tag position
        word_AC4EAD0[entnum + 2113*localClient]  -> dobj index   (2113 entities/client)
        qword_AC4EAB8 + 480*idx                  -> the DObj     (480-byte records)
        sub_3E8D60(centity, dobj, tagNameIdx)    -> pose; +16/+20/+24 is the tag pos
        world offset added from qword_8AFCB38 + 108/112/116

## ⚠ THE ONE GAP -- the per-entity WORLD ORIGIN

Everything above is proven. What is NOT yet pinned is the simplest thing: the
lerped ORIGIN of a player entity.

CG_CalcEntityLerpOrigins @0x520D0 turned out to lerp only the LOCAL player's view
origin (into cg+1993852..1993860), from playerstate offsets +132/136/140 (prev)
and +280/284/288 (next). It does not expose a per-entity origin.

DO NOT GUESS THIS OFFSET (Absolute Rule). Two honest routes:
  (a) RUNTIME, cheap: play a demo, take a known player's on-screen position, and
      read candidate offsets off the centity with Cheat Engine until one matches.
      Minutes, and it is a direct read at a computed address (Cheat Engine Rule
      respected -- no scanning).
  (b) STATIC: follow the bone-tag chain above, which is the engine's own method
      and needs the tag name index (dword_A6008F0 is the one sub_45540 passes).

## WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT AND REUSABLE

dolly.cpp solves the two hard halves ALREADY, proven in game:
  * world -> screen via CG_ProjectViewDirToScreenPos @0x38EFD0, called with our OWN
    validated cg pointer (never letting the engine resolve it -- RULE A21)
  * engine-side text/quad drawing from the EXISTING R_EndFrame hook
  * a per-frame cgame_active() gate that shuts off across seek teardown

So the name-tag feature is: enumerate -> filter to enemies -> position -> project ->
draw, and only "position" is missing.


# ENEMY NAME TAGS -- BUILT (2026-08-15, build E0A34104). Live play first.

User asked for names above heads in demos, enemies only, to locate people in
freecam and identify a kill. Built against LIVE PLAY (bot match) first at the
user's suggestion -- cg is fully valid there, no seek teardown, no theater gating,
so a maths error is obviously wrong rather than intermittently wrong.

## ⭐ THE ENTITY ORIGIN IS centity + 48 -- and it is DOUBLE-CONFIRMED

Derived statically from sub_45540's "no bone tag" branch. NOT from the decompiler
(that call goes through an Arxan dispatch thunk whose args it cannot type) but
from the instructions:

    0x4564f  lea  rcx, [rax+30h]     ; src = centity + 48
    0x4565e  mov  rdx, rsi           ; dst = the float* out parameter
    0x45661  call cs:off_B1C688      ; vec3 copy

i.e. a 2-arg fastcall copying a vector out of centity+0x30.

demo-only overlay) already uses ENTITY_ORIGIN = 48, ADDR_GET_ENTITY = 0x12A00 and

# CONTROLLER AIM ASSIST -- CHASED TO A CONCLUSION (2026-08-15, build 0F48A7E6)

## THE ANSWER: IT WAS NEVER REMOVED. THE OPTIONS TOGGLES WERE.

Every step is static; no probing was needed.

### The runtime is fully present, not stubbed

    AimAssist_Init @0x2CDF0   memsets &unk_5C388F0 + 4912*client (0x1330 bytes)
                              and GraphFloat_Loads all five
                              "aim_assist/view_input_%d.graph" curves
    20 references to that state block from ~18 functions at 0x2B3C0..0x2DDF0
    driven per frame by sub_78AC0; sub_2BC60 applies the curves

An earlier guess that "S2 has only AimAssist_Init named, so it was stripped" was
WRONG -- S2's IDB is only partly named. The xref test settled it: the code is there.

### The two gates, both found

    sub_78AC0 (the driver):
        profile = sub_46B230(controllerIdx) = &unk_8BDEF20 + 6920*idx
        if (profile[264])                 <-- GATE 1: the gamepad path
            ...
            state = &unk_5C388F0 + 4912*localClient
            if (state[240])               <-- GATE 2: aim assist enabled
                sub_2DDF0(); sub_2D1A0(); sub_2BC60(); sub_2B3C0(); ...

  * state[240] is SET TO 1 by sub_2D0F0, called UNCONDITIONALLY from sub_43ADA0
    at cgame init. Every function in the cluster was checked for a write of 0 to
    that byte and for a second memset of the block: NOTHING CLEARS IT.
  * profile[264] gates STICK LOOK as a whole, not just aim assist. If it were
    never set, a controller could not turn the camera at all. That is the
    engine's own "controller only" gate -- exactly the constraint the user
    stated.

### What was actually removed: the settings are ORPHANED

Profile settings table @0xB711A0, 24 B/entry {const char* name, u32 id, u64 type}:

    0xB711A0  autoWeaponSwitch        0x111    still in the options menu
    0xB711B8  autoMantle              0x112    still in the options menu
    0xB711D0  aimAssistLockon         0x113    ORPHANED
    0xB711E8  aimAssistSlowdown       0x114    ORPHANED

Every function in the aim-assist cluster was scanned for profile-block reads. It
reads ONLY profile[4]/[8] (look sens), [12] (ADS flag), [16]/[20] (ADS sens) and
[119] (invert Y). It NEVER reads 0x113 or 0x114.

So those two settings are registered and stored but consulted by nothing. The
toggles were cut and the feature was left permanently ON, not off.

For contrast, AW (fully symboled) has 40+ aim-assist functions plus
GamerProfile_AimAssistLockon/Slowdown, LUI bindings
LUI_CoD_LuaCall_ToggleAimAssistSlowdown/Lockon and console commands
AimAssistSlowdownToggle_f / AimAssistLockonToggle_f. S2 has none of those --
which is precisely the "it used to exist and was removed" the user remembers.

## SHIPPED -- src/hud/aimassist.{hpp,cpp}, ZERO hooks

    aimassist          reads and reports state[240], profile[264], the live
                       sensitivities, ADS split and invert-Y, then states a
                       VERDICT rather than dumping bytes
    aimassist_rearm    re-asserts state[240] = 1

⚠ It deliberately WILL NOT write profile[264]. That byte turns on the whole
gamepad look path; forcing it for a keyboard player would hand stick-look input
to someone with no stick. Reported, never set.

`aimassist_rearm` fabricates nothing -- 1 is the value sub_2D0F0 itself writes at
every cgame init. It exists only because if the reading ever comes back 0, that
is the one byte that would need putting back.

## EXPECTED RESULT

With a controller connected and driving look, `aimassist` should print
`AIM ASSIST IS ACTIVE. Both gates are open.` If it does, there is nothing to
restore and the friend's memory is of the TOGGLES disappearing, not the feature.
If it prints state[240]=0, that contradicts the static reading above and is worth
investigating -- per the Contradiction Rule, do not patch around it.

## Addresses (RULE A1, written out)

    unk_5C388F0 aim assist state  0x5C388F0 - 0x1000 = 0x5C378F0  stride 4912
    unk_8BDEF20 profile block     0x8BDEF20 - 0x1000 = 0x8BDDF20  stride 6920
    sub_4A0B80  controller index  0x4A0B80  - 0x1000 = 0x49FB80
    sub_46B230  profile accessor  = &unk_8BDEF20 + 6920*controllerIdx

NOTE the 6920 stride matches the broadcaster DDL work (sub_46ABF0 = &off_8BE09F0

## ⛔ NAME TAGS -- FIRST RUN FAILED. sub_13A00(client, N) IS NOT "GIVE ME ENTITY N"

First in-game run (build E0A34104) printed:

    0  361    team 2  friend  393948556601327616 units
    2  55     team 2  friend  inf units
    8  1000   team 2  friend  6980748858884096 units
    live: 3 player(s) found, 0 drawn this frame (screen 2560x1440)

Two symptoms, ONE cause. Origins were garbage (inf, 3.9e17) and the "names" were
numeric strings -- which are what S2's LOCALISED string ids look like, i.e. we
were reading a completely unrelated table.

CAUSE: I called sub_13A00(0, clientNum) once per client, assuming it returns that
entity. It does not. src/demo/player_box.cpp -- which already enumerates players
and predates this -- calls it ONCE for the array BASE and strides manually:

    base   = sub_13A00(localClient, 0)
    entity = base + 1808 * i          (0x710, marked proven there)

With the wrong pointer, +48 gave a garbage origin AND +1201 gave a garbage
clientNum, which then indexed the name (152*cn) and team (4704*cn) arrays into
unrelated memory. The plausible-looking client numbers 0/2/8 were coincidence.

FIXED in build D0F639BB: base+stride enumeration over the 18 client slots, the
in-use bit alone as the filter (as player_box does), plus its magnitude sanity
check (1.0 < |origin| < 100000) and its PLAYER_HEIGHT of 70 rather than my 62.
Entity index i IS the client number for players, so `i` indexes the clientinfo
arrays directly -- player_box does not even read +1201.

The eType/eFlags/clientNum centity offsets are kept as [[maybe_unused]] with a
note: they are correct as READ BY THE ENGINE's own drawer, but reading them off a
base+stride slot is what produced the garbage, so they are documented and not used.

⚠ A MISSING NAME NO LONGER HIDES A PLAYER. If sane_name() rejects the pointer the
entry is kept and labelled "[slot]", so a wrong NAME offset shows up as "[3]"
above someone's head instead of silently dropping them. The `names` command now
also prints the raw origin, so a bad position offset is visible immediately.

LESSON, and it is the second time this exact shape has bitten: CHECK WHETHER THIS
REPO ALREADY SOLVED IT. player_box.cpp had the accessor's real contract, the
stride, the sanity checks and the head height. I derived centity+48 independently
and correctly, then got the ITERATION wrong -- which the existing code would have
told me for free.

## ⛔ NAME TAGS HUNG THE GAME -- A SYSCALL STORM ON THE RENDER THREAD

User enabled `names 1` before the game started; the game hung. No minidump (a
hang, not a crash -- the newest dump was days old), and the process was still
"Responding=True" while frozen, i.e. stalled rather than deadlocked on a lock.

CAUSE, and it is a rule this file ALREADY carries:

    sane_name() called readable() -- a VirtualQuery, a KERNEL TRANSITION -- once
    PER CHARACTER, up to 39 per player, 18 players, EVERY FRAME, on the RENDER
    THREAD. ~700 syscalls per frame.

CLAUDE.md's own GUI note says it plainly: "anything the GUI reads out of engine
memory must be cached. readable() is a VirtualQuery, i.e. a kernel transition."
I wrote the same defect into a hotter path.

FIXED (build C77F5D1A):
  * sane_name: ONE readable(s, 40) for the whole window instead of per byte
  * team_of:   no probe at all; collect() probes the WHOLE 18-slot team span and
               the whole name-pointer span ONCE before the loop
  * the font:  use InternalConsole::consoleFont, which is registered once at init
               behind a wait loop, instead of calling R_RegisterFont EVERY FRAME
               from the render thread. That call reaches into the asset system
               while the zone loader may hold it -- the same shape as the
               DB_LoadLevelXAssets deadlock already documented here.

    per-frame readable() calls: ~700  ->  ~23 worst case

⚠ NOTE dolly.cpp and DevDraw.cpp ALSO call R_RegisterFont every frame. It has not
bitten them because both only run during native demo playback, well after any
load. If either is ever made to run in live play, cache the font first.

## GENERALISED: WHY THIS MODULE IS RISKIER THAN dolly / player_box

nametags is the FIRST overlay that runs in LIVE PLAY from boot. dolly and
player_box both gate on demo_native::native_playing(), so they never execute
during a map load, a spawn, or the menu. Anything that runs in live play calls
engine functions (CG_GetRefdefView, sub_13A00) in states nothing here has
exercised before. Budget per-frame work accordingly and prefer cached state.

## ⛔⛔ THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE BROKEN NAME TAGS: sub_13A00 IS ARXAN-PROTECTED

Three failed in-game attempts, and the cause was one thing I never checked: I read
sub_13A00's DECLARATIONS but never its BODY. The body contains

    _BYTE *retaddr;                        // [rsp+8h]
    if (*(retaddr - 5) != 0xE8 && *(retaddr - 2) != 0xFF
        && *(retaddr - 3) != 0xFF && *(retaddr - 4) != 0xFF
        && *(retaddr - 6) != 0xFF && *(retaddr - 7) != 0xFF) ...
    if ((unsigned __int64)retaddr > 0x20000000) ...

It verifies its CALLER is a real CALL inside the game image. Called from our DLL
those checks take different paths, so the returned pointer is not what a game-side
caller gets -- garbage origins, ~1 player found, wrong positions.

This is EXACTLY the hazard already recorded here for CG_GetLocalClientGlobals
("Arxan retaddr checks infinite-loop when the caller is outside the game image").
The lesson generalises and is now a rule:

### ⭐ RULE A22 -- READ AN ENGINE FUNCTION'S BODY BEFORE CALLING IT FROM THE MOD

Look for `retaddr` in the decompile. If the function inspects its own return
address, DO NOT CALL IT. Reading the declarations is not enough -- IDA lists
`retaddr` among the locals, which is easy to skim past.

### ⭐ AND THE ESCAPE: EVERY RETURN PATH WAS THE SAME ARITHMETIC

    return qword_8B0DB18 + 1808 * ((localClientNum << 11) + entnum);

~15 return sites, all identical. So the entity address needs no call at all:
compute it. 1808 == 0x710 (matching player_box's stride) and 2048 == 1 << 11 is
the per-local-client entity count.

    entity array base   qword_8B0DB18 - 0x1000 = 0x8B0CB18   (a POINTER; deref it)

⚠ src/demo/player_box.cpp STILL CALLS sub_13A00 and has the same latent defect.
Its arithmetic is right, its call is not. Fix it there when convenient -- and note
this retires my earlier claim that player_box was "tested" and therefore a safe
model. There is no evidence it ever worked; I inherited an unverified assumption.

than guess a fourth time, build D7B0510A SCANS the 152-byte clientinfo record

    [names] name field FOUND at clientinfo+N (inline chars / a char* in the record)

The test rejects digit-only strings, which is what stops the LEVEL field being
picked again. Once the run prints an offset, write it into this file and the scan

Also NOT the answer, checked and excluded:

  * sub_465CB0 -- the BOT/AGENT name path; it walks a 192-byte-stride array in

## ⭐⭐⭐ THE clientinfo LAYOUT, MEASURED LIVE WITH CHEAT ENGINE (2026-08-16)

User's call: "you should use cheat engine to verify the base in real time". Right,
and it ended three rounds of guessing in one pass. Method respected the Cheat
Engine Rule throughout -- DIRECT READS at computed addresses, no scanning.

    PID checked first (13276), module base 0x7FF62C490000
    RULE A2 verified: read_string(base + 0xBCE9E0) == "EXE_ERR_PROCESS_DEMO_FILE_FAILED"
    cg reached the way the mod does: *(base + 0x8AFCB38) - 0x1E6C10

Dumping 8 clientinfo records (base cg + 4405240, stride 152) in a live match:

    slot  +36  +56   +60 name              +96
    0     3    1     19AS04                27
    1     1    2     DzieckoWeMgle         23
    2     1    3     Cannibal 666          26
    3     1    4     MC Lou Tha Killah     25
    4     2    5     simo_106              23
    5     0    6     Ainars.777            20
    6     0    7     Sgt. Wawadawakwa      23
    7     2    8     soil8529              24

    +36  TEAM      (varies 0/1/2/3)
    +56  client id (1,2,3..8 -- a 1-based index, NOT a team)
    +60  NAME      INLINE char[], ~36 bytes
    +96  LEVEL     -- this is what was being drawn on screen

My +16 was a POINTER field, which is why three attempts rendered localised-string
ids and then the level.

### ⛔ cg + 3878308 (stride 4704) IS NOT THE PER-CLIENT TEAM

Measured 2 for BOTH slot 0 and slot 1 while their clientinfo records read 3 and 1.
That is why every player came out "friend" and enemies-only drew nothing. Use
clientinfo+36. (CG_RelativePlayerName does read the 4704 array, so it is SOME
team-ish field -- but it is not indexed the way I assumed.)

### ⛔ qword_8B0DB18 IS ENCRYPTED -- there is no plain entity-array pointer

Read live it holds 0xF5A16DA2226E8E90 (not canonical), and base+0x8B0DB18 is
zeros. Same family as g_clientActive_encrypted. That is why sub_13A00 is huge and
obfuscated: it DECRYPTS this. The build that read the global directly found ZERO
players; the build that CALLED sub_13A00 found players. So:

  * CALL sub_13A00 (guarded). Its retaddr check tests *(retaddr-2) == 0xFF, which
    our register-indirect `call rax` satisfies.
  * My earlier "never call it, compute it instead" conclusion is WITHDRAWN -- the
    arithmetic is right but the input is ciphertext.

### THE ORIGIN OFFSET IS NOW SELF-CALIBRATING, NOT GUESSED

+48 came from sub_45540's disassembly and player_box uses it too, but it produced
inf / 3.9e17 in game and neither of us ever verified it. Rather than guess a fifth
offset, build BD5D1D11 CALIBRATES: the LOCAL player's own entity origin must sit
within a few hundred units of the refdef view origin (a value already known-good,
since the projector depends on it), so it scans the entity for the float triple
closest to it and uses that offset for everyone. It reports:

    [names] origin offset CALIBRATED to entity+N ...

Once that prints, write N here and the scan can become a constant.

### METHOD NOTE, and the user was right to push for it

Three in-game iterations were spent guessing offsets that one CE session settled.
When a value is observable in a running process, READ IT -- this file already says
so ("measure state, don't follow code"), and I defaulted to static archaeology
because I was avoiding asking the user to probe. Reading memory myself is not
"probing"; it costs the user nothing.

## ⛔⛔ RULE A23 -- A HOOK'S ARGUMENT LIST MATTERS AS MUCH AS ITS RETURN WIDTH

Crashed the game THREE TIMES. Diagnosed from one minidump (RULE A13) with no
probing and no guessing:

    exception 0xC0000005 ACCESS_VIOLATION
    fault at IDA_0x516332   READ from 0x20BF98C0310 (unmapped)

0x516332 is inside sub_5162F0 -- the function my visibility hook forwarded to.

### THE DEFECT

IDA types sub_5161D0 as `bool sub_5161D0()` -- NO PARAMETERS. That is wrong. Its
entire body is:

    5161d0  sub    rsp, 28h
    5161d4  call   sub_5162F0          ; rcx/rdx/r8 passed STRAIGHT THROUGH
    5161d9  comiss xmm0, cs:dword_B3767C
    5161e0  setnb  al
    5161e3  add    rsp, 28h
    5161e7  retn

It never sets up the argument registers -- it FORWARDS ITS CALLER'S. And
sub_5162F0 is `__m128 __fastcall(__int64 a1, float *a2, float *a3)` whose first
act is `sub_517710(a1)`.

I declared the stub `bool(__fastcall*)()`. The compiler is then free to clobber
rcx/rdx/r8 (volatile scratch registers) before calling the trampoline, so the
original ran on garbage and faulted on the very first dereference of a1.

### THE RULE

RULE A17 says declare the EXACT return width. This extends it:

  * Declare the EXACT PARAMETER LIST too. Declaring too FEW parameters is just as
    fatal -- MinHook's trampoline is fine, but NOTHING preserves the argument
    registers across your stub.
  * IDA's `()` is not evidence of a nullary function. A thin forwarder that never
    writes rcx/rdx/r8 before its inner call TAKES those arguments, whatever the
    decompiler says. CHECK THE DISASSEMBLY for whether the argument registers are
    set up or merely passed on.
  * The tell: `sub rsp,N / call X / <use return> / ret` with no register setup.

Fixed in build 20A821C4: `bool(__fastcall*)(std::int64_t, float*, float*)`, and the
stub forwards a1/a2/a3 untouched.

### The OTHER hook was checked the same way and IS safe

sub_38F510 (the team gate) disassembles as a genuine nullary function -- it calls
sub_B8C40() with no setup, reads a global, and sets rcx only from sub_197040()'s
own return before calling sub_1970B0. It never reads incoming rcx/rdx/r8, so
`bool(__fastcall*)()` is correct there.

VERIFY BOTH HOOKS THIS WAY BEFORE ADDING ANY MORE.

# REMOVED — player_box and netlog (2026-08-16, user request, build 57AA37A6)

Both deleted outright rather than left switched off. A dead switch is a loaded
gun, and in this project two of them have already fired.

## src/demo/player_box.{cpp,hpp} — the review overlay

Superseded by the nameplate ungate (`CG_ShouldDrawPlayerName` @0x52610), which
uses the engine's own drawer: correct bone-tag head position, correct name,
correct font, fade and scaling. player_box drew ImGui boxes on Present.

It was ALSO unsound, and this is why it is not worth keeping as a fallback:

  * `ENTITY_ORIGIN = 48` was never verified. My own attempt to reuse it produced
    `inf` and 3.9e17 — see the nametags failure log.
  * it called `sub_13A00`, which inspects its own return address (RULE A22), so
    called from our DLL it does not return what a game-side caller gets.
  * its name index was off by one — entity+1201 is a 1-BASED client id.
  * its name base disagreed with what CE measured live (clientinfo is
    `cg + 4405240`, stride 152, NAME INLINE at +60, level at +96).

⚠ It was never confirmed working in game. Earlier notes here treated it as a
tested reference and reused its constants; that was an inherited assumption, and
it cost several nametag iterations. Nothing in the tree depends on it now.

## src/net/netlog.{cpp,hpp} — the Network tab / fh_peers

Built to answer "did anyone hear us?" during the force-host work. Retired with
the goal: force_host is now scoped to the LOBBY host only, and the server half
is CLOSED (a public playlist always provisions a DS; the DS-search failure path
restarts the search and has no listen-server branch).

It was already opt-in behind `s2mp_netlog.txt` and installed ZERO hooks without
it, so this removes no measurement capability that was live. The stale marker
file in the game dir was deleted with it.

Worth remembering if the question ever returns: it hooked `recvfrom` on both
sockets, and **Demonware's service connection is TCP** (recv/send callers cluster
in 0xAC7xxx / 0xA7Fxxx / 0x662510), so a UDP watcher could never see matchmaking
in the first place.

## Also removed

  * the "Player boxes" checkbox and `demo_player_boxes` console command
  * the GUI **Network** tab (six remain: Demos, Servers, Host, Bots, Players, Dolly)
  * `player_box::sample()` from the R_EndFrame stub and `draw_overlay()` from Present
  * both file pairs from s2mp-mod.vcxproj / .filters

# ⛔ KILLED — "make the Store build cross-play with Xbox One consoles by matching
# protocol + game version" (2026-08-16, ~15 min, entirely offline)

USER HYPOTHESIS: the Store build already talks to Xbox Live servers, so cross-play
with Xbox One players should only need the protocol and game version matched — and
maybe SHG left those values in the Xbox IDB unset.

**RESULT: the premise is wrong in both halves. Protocol/version are NOT the gate,
and nothing was left in the binary to find.** Filed under Failed Attempt Protection.

## ⭐ PROVEN — the protocol number is IDENTICAL in both PC builds

`SV_DirectConnect` reads `Info_ValueForKey(userinfo, "protocol")`, `strtoul`s it and
compares against a getter; a mismatch gives `error\nEXE_SERVER_IS_DIFFERENT_VER`.

    Steam  getter sub_764460   `((v1 % 0x1F) << 27) | 0x344001E`  else 4215537694
    Store  getter sub_761470   same expression, same constants     else 0x344001E - 0x8000000

0x344001E - 0x8000000 == 0xFB44001E == 4215537694. Bit-identical. IDA only renders
the Store one differently (it leaves `-31 * (...)` unfolded and shows 0x344001E as
an `unk_` address because that immediate is also a valid address there).

`v1 = (u16)sub_2920C0(sub_292020())`, gated by sub_292290 — obfuscated, derived at
runtime, so the protocol is anti-tamper bound rather than a plain constant.

## ⭐ PROVEN — the VERSION STRING is not a gate at all

    Steam  "2.20"      Store  "2.18"
    0xf32c6  lea rdx, a220 ; "2.20"      <- a FORMAT ARGUMENT to the error text
    0xf32c2  cmp ebx, eax / jz ok        <- the actual gate, protocol only

Different patch levels, and it changes nothing: the comparison is purely the
protocol number, and the version string is only printed in the failure message.

## ⭐⭐ PROVEN — Steam and Store are ONE Demonware partition

    Steam   ww2-pc-auth3.prod / .cert     ww2-pc-lobby.prod / .cert
    Store   ww2-pc-auth3.cert   auth3.prod   ww2-pc-lobby.cert
            lsg.2810.prod.demonware.net   lsg.2805.dev.demonware.net
            cinereous-pc-qbl.dev          ww2-qbl.cert / .prod
    BOTH    umbrella client id `sledgehammer-cod-stronghold-steam`   (identical string)

**`lsg.<N>.prod.demonware.net` carries the Demonware TITLE ID — 2810 prod, 2805 dev
for WWII PC.** That is the partition key, and the `ww2-<platform>-` hostname prefix
is the platform scope. The Store build literally authenticates as the `-steam`
Umbrella client, which is consistent with the already-measured 99.9% identical
codegen: it is the PC build in an MSIX wrapper.

## ⭐ PROVEN — nothing for another platform was left in

    crossplay / cross_play / crossPlatform / cross-play   ZERO hits in .rdata
    ww2- prefixed hosts    only  ww2-pc-*  and  ww2-qbl / ww2-stun
    umbrella client ids    only  sledgehammer-cod-stronghold-steam
    lsg hostnames          only  2810 / 2805

Each platform build ships ONLY its own endpoints. There is no unset/dormant console
title id, host or client id to discover — the console partition's address simply is
not in this binary. WWII (2017) has no cross-play concept anywhere in its data.

## ⚠ THE FALSE POSITIVE THAT WILL CATCH THE NEXT PERSON

`XboxOne`, `Scarlett`, `Win32`, `PlayStation`, `Nintendo`, `iOS`, `Android` DO appear
(0xc70d60, 0xc71058, 0xc74a80 in the Store build). **They are the Xbox Live SDK's
DeviceType enum**, not a WWII platform list — they sit amid `richPresence`,
`userpresence`, `userActivities`, `connectionString`, `joinRestriction`,
`maxPlayers`, `currentPlayers`, i.e. XblPresence and XblMultiplayerActivity. That is
presence and invite plumbing, and CLAUDE.md already records that MPSD
(`XblMultiplayerSession*`) is ABSENT entirely. Seeing "PlayStation" in the binary
does not mean the game can match with one.

## PROVEN — the auth chain, and where the real wall is

    XUserAddAsync (sign in)
      -> User::GetTokenAndSignature      (the XSTS token + signature)
      -> ww2-pc-auth3.*.demonware.net    (Demonware auth)
      -> DW-Client-Ticket / DW-Server-Ticket
      -> lsg.2810.prod.demonware.net     (lobby service gateway, title 2810)

An XSTS token is minted by Microsoft **for a specific title / relying party**. The
Xbox One WWII title and the PC Game Pass title are different Xbox Live titles with
different SCIDs and different entitlements (`BD_ENTITLEMENTS_INVALID_TITLEID`,
`BD_AUTH_BAD_TITLE_ID` both exist). So the partition is enforced SERVER-SIDE, twice
over: by Xbox Live when issuing the token, and by Demonware when validating the
title. Repointing hostname strings is the easy half; the credential is not something
a client patch can forge.

## ⭐ THE ONE GENUINELY USEFUL SPIN-OFF

Steam and Store share the protocol constant, the Demonware endpoints AND the
Umbrella client id. So **Steam <-> Store should already be one player pool**, and
`connect <ip>` between them should work — direct connect bypasses matchmaking and
the only check on that path is the protocol number, which matches. Untested, but it
costs one console command to try.

Not investigated and out of reach: the Xbox One binary itself (we do not have it),
so whether the console's protocol constant matches is UNKNOWN — and moot, since the
backend partition blocks it regardless.

# MASS NAMING PASS — 1,039 → 2,785 NAMED (2026-08-16). METHOD + CORRECTIONS.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Goal set by the user: get the S2 IDB richly named, routing outward from what is

    named in real .text     1,039  ->  2,785   (2.27% -> 6.07%)
    named, substantial      496    ->  1,000   (4.6%  -> 9.22%)
    (real .text = 45,844 functions below 0xb0f000; substantial = >= 256 bytes)

## ⭐ THE SCOPE, MEASURED — the 302 MB module is 89% DATA

Do not quote the module size as a measure of work. Measured from the IDB:

    .text  #1  0x1000    - 0xb0f000     11.6 MB    THE REAL GAME CODE
    .rdata     0xb1b000  - 0xd90000      2.6 MB
    .data      0xd90000  - 0x10f60000  270.3 MB    <- 89% of the image
    .text  #2  0x1126e000- 0x12074000   14.7 MB    Arxan block, 15,631 funcs,
                                                   avg 73 bytes = stubs

    45,844 real functions, 10.86 MB.  10,843 are >= 256 bytes -- that is the
    actual job. 29,208 (48%) are under 64 bytes: thunks and accessors.
    Call graph: 147,395 edges (re/s2_steam_funcs.json).

Middleware, from .rdata DLL strings (the dump's import table is mangled and
unreadable -- expected, imports were resolved before the dump): renderer is
D3D11+DXGI, audio is DirectSound, compression is Oodle (oo2core_5_win64), video
is Bink2. NO Havok/PhysX/Bullet/FMOD/Wwise -- physics and audio mixing are
in-house.

## ⭐⭐ THE METHOD THAT PAID: SCAN FOR SELF-NAMING {name, function} TABLES

The binary pairs a name string with a function pointer in dozens of tables. That
is the STRONGEST evidence tier there is -- stronger than any twin, because it is
the target binary asserting the mapping itself. It had only ever been exploited
by hand (CLAUDE.md previously listed ~4 tables); scanning generically found 38.

Scan: walk .rdata qword-aligned; classify each slot as "points to a printable
NUL-terminated string in .rdata" or "points to a function start in .text"; find
runs of {S,F} at stride 16; merge across gaps <= 0x80.

    38 tables, 2,238 pairs, 2,052 of them targeting a function that was sub_.

WARNING: `py_eval` runs under `exec` with split globals/locals, so a nested `def`
cannot see names bound at the top level of your snippet. Wrap the whole thing in
one `def main(): ...` and call it. This bites on the first try every time.

### The families, separated BY WHAT THE REGISTRAR CALLS (not by guessing)

    registrar calls sub_2E37B0  -> Lua/HKS library table.  sub_2E37B0 is a thin
        wrapper over hksI_openlib, so this is proven from the callee.
        hksI_openlib(L, libname, table, 0, 0) -- ARG 2 IS THE LUA NAMESPACE.
    registrar is luaopen_base / hksI_openlib   -> Havok Script stdlib
    registrar calls I_stricmp on the name      -> NETWORK OOB dispatch table
    registrar is G_CallSpawn                   -> entity spawn table
    IMAP/POP3/SMTP tables                      -> statically linked libcurl

Read the lib name by walking back from the openlib call for `lea rdx, <string>`
-- NOT by "first string in the registrar", which gives wrong answers (it returned
"print"/"coroutine" for the base library, whose table has no single namespace).

    PROVEN namespaces: Engine(744+58) Lobby(183) Game(146) Matchmaking(101)
    CharacterScene(85) Clan(79) UGC_Editor(77) PlayerData(45) LUIRankedPlay(29)
    string(28) Store(28) GameBattles(23) Broadcaster(23) CoDAnywhere(20)
    CreateAClass(11) DataModel(8)

Applied as `Lua_<Lib>_<Binding>`, 1,650 functions, every one carrying an IDB
comment with the table, the registrar, the openlib call, and an explicit warning
that this is the LUA-VISIBLE name, not the engine's internal C name -- these
functions are marshallers.

### Independent corroboration: the dumped HKS bytecode

`re/validate_bindings.py` harvests every identifier-shaped run from the 941
dumped LUI files (they are BYTECODE -- grep finds nothing, but the constant
tables hold the identifiers as plain ASCII) and cross-checks the binding names.

    1,028 of 2,217 confirmed (46%) -- and the SHAPE is what matters:
      Lua tables      51-100%  (DataModel 100%, _targetelement 100%,
                                _customElementData 95%, LUI 72%, Engine 71%)
      OOB / spawn / curl   0%  <- exactly as predicted; Lua never references
                                  network command tokens or entity classnames

The 46% is a floor set by DUMP COVERAGE, not by naming accuracy: every low
scorer is a FRONTEND MENU (Matchmaking 9%, Clan 8%, CharacterScene 8%, Store
21%) and the dump was taken in a match, so those bundles were never loaded.

## ⛔⛔ CORRECTION — 0xB50C60 IS NOT A GSC BINDING TABLE

CLAUDE.md recorded: "⭐ THE SCRIPT BINDING TABLE — the whole force-host surface
... {const char* name, void* func} pairs, stride 16, at 0xB50C60 (~60 entries)
... This is the API the lobby GSC drives." and named 78 functions `Script_*`.

**That is wrong, and it is now disproven twice over:**

    sub_299FF0:  sub_2E37B0(L, "Matchmaking", &off_B50AF0);
                 == hksI_openlib(L, "Matchmaking", &off_B50AF0, 0, 0)
    xrefs to 0xB50C60: ZERO.

0xB50C60 was never a table start -- it is the middle of the table at **0xB50AF0**,
which is the Lua library **`Matchmaking`**. Those functions are called from LUI
Lua as `Matchmaking.CanHostServer()`, NOT from GSC. All 78 `Script_*` names were
renamed to `Lua_Matchmaking_*`.

This completes a correction CLAUDE.md had already half-made elsewhere ("an
earlier entry calls Script_CallByName_ExpectInt a GSC driver... it drives
qword_1BD3D08, i.e. the LUI Lua state") but never propagated back to the names.

CONSEQUENCE: everywhere the force-host work concluded "the decision is made by
SCRIPT (GSC)" it should read **LUI Lua** -- and the 941 dumped LUI files are
therefore the place to look, not an un-dumpable GSC blob.

NOTE `Script_*` IS a real convention -- but it is AW's, for AW's GSC table at
0x82058078 (fadein -> Script_FadeIn). That is presumably where the prefix came
from; it was applied to the wrong S2 table.

## ⭐⭐⭐ THE PARTY / LOBBY OOB PROTOCOL — CRACKED, WITH REAL ENGINE NAMES

CLAUDE.md recorded this as statically unreachable: "None of these strings has a
code xref (computed/Arxan). The handler that compares incoming OOB names and
builds the reply has not been found statically. RUNTIME IS THE EFFICIENT ROUTE."

**It is a DISPATCH TABLE, not inlined strcmp -- five of them.** And AW is fully
symboled, so every handler has its real name.

    S2 0xb72d20 (25)  party client OOB      AW 0x8205d178
    S2 0xb73d20 (19)  party host OOB              "
    S2 0xb75010 (12)  party migration OOB         "
    S2 0xb70870 (6)   lobby OOB             AW 0x8205dbdc   overlap 1.0
    S2 0xb9cde0 (4)   lobby OOB             AW 0x82058468   overlap 1.0
    S2 0xb8e4e0 (19)  entity spawns         AW 0x82059aa8   overlap 0.895

52 names applied, including the three the file said needed runtime:

    doqos   -> PartyClient_HandleDoQoS
    stopqos -> PartyClient_HandleStopQoS
    qosres  -> PartyHost_HandleQoSResultMessage

plus the whole PartyMigrate_* / PartyHost_* / PartyClient_* / PartyAtomic* set,
and SP_trigger_multiple / SP_trigger_hurt / SP_turret / SP_script_model / ...
(AW's spawn symbols demangle to `void SP_x(gentity_s*)`, giving signatures too).

⭐ CORROBORATION WORTH NOTING: the three S2 party tables were split by ADDRESS,
before any AW data was involved. AW's symbols then land as PartyClient_* in the
first, PartyHost_* in the second, PartyMigrate_* in the third. Two independent
lines of evidence agreeing on the same split.

### Match tables to tables, NEVER bindings to bindings

Matching a bare string across two different games is careless ('ping', 'show').
`re/match_aw_tables.py` requires the two TABLES to correspond first -- by shared
name-set -- and only then matches entries inside a corresponding pair.

Accept on ratio >= 0.60 OR absolute shared >= 5. The absolute test is required
because **AW keeps ONE merged party table where S2 splits it into three** and
adds WWII-specific commands, collapsing the ratio to 0.24 even though
`kickedFromParty` / `partystate` / `notpresent` matching exactly is not chance.
Only the shared entries are ever proposed; the rest are left alone.

## AW STRING-ANCHOR PORT — the well is largely dry, and that is the finding

6,613 AW anchors (strings referenced by exactly one NAMED AW function) ->
3,069 present in S2 -> 608 S2 functions voted -> 563 candidates.
**445 of those were ALREADY NAMED** -- the earlier AW pass harvested this well.
Only 118 new, of which 21 met the bar. Do not expect a second big yield here.

Only .rdata was searched (29,669 strings) while the IDB string cache holds
89,974 -- most of S2's strings live elsewhere (.data is 270 MB). Searching .data
for the ~3,500 unmatched anchors is untried and is the obvious next lever.

## ⭐ TWO OF THE NINE OPEN NAME DISAGREEMENTS — RESOLVED

CLAUDE.md listed nine MW3-vs-AW name conflicts as unresolved. Two are settled:

**UI_RunMenuScript.** 0x746A50 carries **45 anchors** (the menu command names
themselves), is 4,670 bytes with 163 distinct strings -- a dispatcher. The name
had sat on 0x74A440, which is 453 bytes whose only real string is
`"wait ; wait ; map %s\n"`. 453 bytes and one map command cannot be that
dispatcher. 0x746A50 takes the name; **0x74A440 -> UI_QueueMapChangeCommand**
(behaviour-proven, descriptive, from its own body).

**SV_DirectConnect.** 0xF31D5 **ends at exactly 0xF336E** -- they are contiguous.
0xF336E is 3,255 bytes with 6 anchors including the literal function name and
`EXE_PLAYERKICKED_BOT_MAKE_ROOM`; 0xF31D5 is a 409-byte lead-in holding the
protocol/challenge/checksum validation strings. **0xF336E -> SV_DirectConnect;
0xF31D5 REVERTED to sub_** with a comment (an honest sub_ beats a name I cannot
prove, and contiguity suggests it is a split-off chunk of the same function).

Not resolved: `PartyAtomicHost_HandleMemberJoin` -- the anchor candidate
(0x48FC40) references `pa_joined`, which AW maps to
`PartyAtomicClient_HandleHostJoined`, so it is a SENDER, not the handler. The
binding-table assignment (0x486BC0) is the stronger evidence and stands.

## CONSOLE COMMAND HANDLERS — 101 named, 16 dispatchers documented

Same self-naming pattern, different shape: the name and the pointer are passed
as ARGUMENTS rather than sitting in a table. Walk every xref to
**Cmd_AddCommandInternal @0x64A6B0**, then walk back <= 20 instructions for
`lea rcx, <string>` (name) and `lea rdx, <func>` (handler).

    157 xrefs -> 150 (name, handler) pairs resolved.
    101 applied as `<command>_f` (the engine's own convention, cf. CL_Demo_Play_f)
    16 handlers serve 2-5 commands each -- NOT named (naming a dispatcher after
       one of its commands would be wrong) but COMMENTED with the full list.

Self-verifying: `setgameprivatematch -> 0x1972B0` reproduces CLAUDE.md's
hand-derived entry exactly.

Useful hits for open investigations: `sub_469DA0` handles
**profile_toggleAutoAim** (+ profile_toggleRenderColorBlind), and `sub_469E20`
handles **profile_toggleAutoMantle** -- directly relevant to the aim-assist work,
which had concluded the aimAssist profile settings (ids 0x113/0x114) are orphaned
while autoMantle (0x112) is still menu-exposed.

## RULE A24 — THE IDB SAVE EXCEEDS THE MCP TIMEOUT BUT SUCCEEDS

`idb_save` on this 1.46 GB database takes >60 s and the MCP call returns a
TimeoutError. **The save completes anyway.** Do NOT blindly retry -- it is a
mutating operation. Verify by file mtime on the .i64/.id0, or issue it by curl
with a long timeout, which returns `{"ok":true}` cleanly:

    curl -s -m 600 -X POST http://127.0.0.1:13337/mcp -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":1,\"method\":\"tools/call\",\"params\":{\"name\":\"idb_save\",\"arguments\":{}}}"

Related: a 4-second health probe is too short to decide an IDA server is down --
AW answered at 6 s. Use >= 10 s before concluding a port is dead.

## RULE A25 — GENERATE FILE CONTENT WITH THE Write TOOL, NOT A SHELL HEREDOC

Appending this section with `cat >> CLAUDE.md << 'EOF'` failed with "unexpected
EOF while looking for matching quote". Prose containing quotes, apostrophes and
embedded JSON is hostile to shell heredocs, and CLAUDE.md already records a
related trap (a python heredoc silently mangling a C++ `\\` escape into `\`).
Write the content to a file with the Write tool -- which does no shell escaping
at all -- then `cat` it into place.

# NAMING PASS, PART 2 — 2,785 → 3,066 (2026-08-16). CROSS-BINARY PROPAGATION.

Continues the pass above. Same session, same rules.

    named in real .text     2,785 -> 3,066     (session total: 1,039 -> 3,066)
    named, substantial      1,000 -> 1,127     (session total:   496 -> 1,127, 10.39%)

## AW WORKER PROPAGATION — 98 names

The 1,650 `Lua_*` functions are MARSHALLERS: they unpack Lua arguments and call
the real implementation. Do NOT name the worker after the Lua binding -- that is
inference. Instead find AW's marshaller for the SAME binding and carry AW's REAL
name for ITS worker across.

Method, both sides identically:
  - callee frequency across all marshallers separates plumbing from workers.
    A callee reached by >= 8 marshallers is Lua stack plumbing; one reached by
    exactly one marshaller is that binding's specific worker.
    (S2: 93 plumbing functions detected, top called 1,132x. AW: 77.)
  - require exactly ONE non-plumbing callee, and require freq == 1 on BOTH sides
    so a shared helper can never be named after one of its callers.

    S2 marshallers 1,650 -> 653 with a unique worker
    AW bindings    1,320 -> 240 with a uniquely-named worker
    overlap: 105 -- of which 98 STRONG, 7 weak.

TIERING: the AW worker name must echo the binding name (shared token) to be
applied. `GetDvarFloat -> Dvar_GetFloat`, `StopMusic -> SND_StopBackground`,
`UserCanPlayOnline -> Live_CanUserPlayOnline`,
`ToggleAutoMantle -> GamerProfile_ToggleAutoMantle` all pass.

The 7 that do NOT share a token are NOT named -- they are generic helpers
(`setcolor -> Float_Parse`, `SetThirdPerson -> SetSpectatorPersoness`,
`GetServerData -> UI_FeederItemText`), where the positional match alone does not
prove S2 calls the same helper in that slot. They carry a
"CANDIDATE, NOT APPLIED" comment naming the AW function, so the lead is kept
without the risk.

⭐ 537 of the 653 S2 workers have NO AW counterpart at all -- WWII-only bindings.
Those cannot be reached this way.

## ⭐⭐ MWR-PS4 IS THE RICHEST ANCHOR SOURCE — 35,882 ANCHORS, 8,068 NAMES

`2-h1_mp.elf` (port 9999) is a DEBUG build with real symbols. Harvested the same
way as AW (strings referenced by exactly one NAMED function):

    AW   6,613 anchors -> 1,481 distinct names
    MWR 35,882 anchors -> 8,068 distinct names      5.4x AW on both counts

### ⚠ BUT THE MATCH RATE INTO S2 IS LOW, AND THE REASON MATTERS

Only ~300 unnamed S2 functions matched. **S2 is a RELEASE build: its asserts are
stripped.** Most of MWR's 35,882 anchors ARE assert text (file paths, condition
expressions) that simply does not exist in S2. So MWR's anchor advantage largely
does not transfer to naming S2 functions.

It should still transfer to STRUCTS -- assert text like
`cls.gameState.stringOffsets[configStringIndex]` names FIELDS, and that is a
different use of the same data. Untapped.

### Multi-source tiering, and a notation trap

Running S2 against AW and MWR together makes agreement its own evidence tier:

    both references agree     43   <- strongest
    MWR only, >= 2 anchors    45
    MWR only, 1 distinctive   75
    AW only                    -
    genuine conflicts       dropped
    TOTAL APPLIED            163

⚠ **Most apparent "conflicts" are the same name in different notation.** AW
writes C++ symbols with `::`, MWR with `__`:

    bdJSONUtility::escapeString   vs  bdJSONUtility__escapeString
    hks::base_collectgarbage      vs  hks__base_collectgarbage
    LuaPlus::ReportStackTrace     vs  LuaPlus__ReportStackTrace

Normalise `::` -> `__` and lowercase before comparing. Doing so moved agreements
from 37 to 43. Real conflicts that survive normalisation (e.g.
`bdLSPEnumerator::pump` vs `NET_NetworkOrderAddrToString`) are dropped per the
Contradiction Rule.

⭐ INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION: MWR put `CL_SetServerInfo` on 0x87400 with 4
anchors. CLAUDE.md had already derived that same identification by hand during
the server-browser work, from the serverInfo_t field layout. Two unrelated routes,
same answer.

## CALL-GRAPH PROPAGATION — 20 names, and an honest note on its ceiling

`re/propagate_callgraph.py`. If S2 function A and reference function B share a
name they are the same function, so their callee SETS correspond. Line the sets
up by the names they already share; if exactly ONE S2 callee is left unnamed and
exactly ONE reference callee name is unaccounted for, those two are each other.

Deliberately the most conservative form -- "set difference of one". Any seed with
two or more unknowns on either side is skipped rather than guessed. Sets, not
call order: positional matching drifts across compilers and years, and the graph
export sorts callees by address anyway.

ITERATED to a fixed point: each name resolved shrinks the unknown set for its
neighbours, so rounds compound WITHOUT loosening the rule.

    MWR: gen1 730 seeds -> 15 new, gen2 745 -> 3, gen3 748 -> 0.  18 total.
    AW : gen1 359 seeds ->  2 new, gen2 361 -> 2, gen3 363 -> 0.   4 total.
    merged and applied: 20 (2 of them agreed on by BOTH references).

⚠ **THE CEILING IS S2'S OWN COVERAGE, NOT THE METHOD.** Only 21 of 730 seeds
qualified, because at 6.6% named almost every function still has several unnamed
callees. This method gets steadily more productive as coverage rises -- it is
worth re-running after every other naming pass, and it costs nothing to do so.

High-value hits despite the low count:

    0x2E31A0 -> luaL_error          the single most-called plumbing function
                                    (1,132 calls from marshallers). BOTH refs agree.
    0x2E2EB0 -> luaL_checkoption    BOTH refs agree.
    0xA1080  -> DB_FindXAssetHeader core asset system
    0x64B830 -> Cmd_RemoveCommand
    0x4A0B80 -> CL_ControllerIndexFromClientNum
    0x59F1F0 -> Scr_SetFog          (3,405 bytes)
    0x72D920 -> SEH_LocalizeTextMessage
    0xA04F40 -> I_strcmp

⭐ `0x4A0B80` is used throughout CLAUDE.md as "sub_4A0B80(client) = local client
num / controller index" -- derived by hand in the force-host and record-gate work.
The propagation reaches the same conclusion independently.

# ACCURACY TOOLING — the naming skill and the audit (2026-08-16)

## ⛔ EVALUATED AND REJECTED — "caveman" (github.com/juliusbrussee/caveman)

Suggested as something that "adds extra rules and tools to help us be more
accurate". It does not. Read the README directly: it is a TOKEN-COST reduction
tool -- "cuts 65% of tokens by talking like caveman", "Same concrete fix, fewer
words" -- and it makes **no accuracy claim anywhere**. It even warns that "on
already-terse workloads they can go net-negative". Nothing in it touches RE, IDA,
or verification.

Two reasons it is wrong for this project specifically:

  1. **It proxies provider traffic.** A local proxy sits between the agent and the
     API and forwards everything: the ~1 MB CLAUDE.md, IDB contents, mod source.
     Third-party middleware in that path is a supply-chain decision, not a plugin
     install. The engine is BSL-1.1, and skills auto-activate.
  2. **It optimises the opposite axis.** This file MANDATES evidence
     classification (PROVEN / STRONG INFERENCE / HYPOTHESIS), and those
     distinctions live entirely in qualifying language. Terse mode compresses
     exactly that away: "these 98 are strong, these 7 are candidates not names"
     becomes "named 105", which is false. RULE A12 exists because of that failure
     mode.

Do not re-evaluate without new evidence that it has grown a verification feature.

## .claude/skills/ida-naming/SKILL.md

The naming discipline that produced ~2,000 names this session, written down so it
does not have to be rediscovered: the four evidence tiers, the mandatory-basis
rule, and the traps that were each paid for in lost time (table-before-entry
matching, absolute-overlap acceptance, `::` vs `__` normalisation, drop-don't-pick
on contradictions, one-name-one-function, distinctiveness-not-length, contiguous
candidates, shared callees, never-verify-with-the-value-you-wrote). Also carries
the reference port table and the operational traps (`py_eval` exec scoping, never
`idautils.Strings()` on S2, the save timeout, Write-not-heredoc).

## re/audit_names.py — run it after every naming pass

    python re/audit_names.py            # exit 1 on any hard finding
    python re/audit_names.py --strict   # also fail on "no recorded basis"

Pulls every named function plus its comment from the IDB and checks four things:

    A  no recorded basis        review    the comment does not say how we know
    B  contradicts own source   HARD      the name clashes with the evidence it
                                          itself cites
    B' evidence suggests other  review    a DIFFERENT source offers another name
    C  duplicate name           HARD      exact repeat
    C' differs only by case     review    legal but confusing
    D  phantom reference        HARD      claims a reference basis the reference
                                          build does not contain

BASELINE AT ADOPTION (3,062 named): 0 hard, 801 no-basis, 179 evidence-suggests-
other, 1 case collision. The 801 are names from earlier sessions that predate the
comment convention -- that is the backlog, and it is the honest measure of how
much of the IDB is currently unjustified.

### ⚠ Getting the severities right mattered more than adding checks

The first run reported 352 hard findings, and **almost all were the tool's fault**.
Each false positive is recorded because the same mistakes will recur in any
cross-binary audit:

  - **A binding table asserts the LUA name, not the function's name.** The OOB and
    spawn entries in those same tables were deliberately named from AW
    (`HandleStartMsg`, `SP_trigger_hurt`). Only audit entries actually applied via
    that route, i.e. `Lua_*`.
  - **Do not substring-match reference labels in comments.** The evidence footer
    names both builds ("References: AW = ...; MWR = ..."), so a loose match fired
    for every anchor-derived name. Read the structured tier marker instead.
  - **Reference exports carry RAW IDA names, and AW's are MANGLED.** Comparing
    `Dvar_GetFloat` against `?Dvar_GetFloat@@YAMPBUdvar_t@@@Z` makes every
    AW-sourced name look like a phantom. Demangle before comparing --
    and note MSVC nests INNERMOST-FIRST (`?method@class@@` -> `class::method`),
    so the parts must be REVERSED. Constructors are `??0Name@@`.
  - **"Two sources disagree" is not "the name is wrong".**
    `Lua_Broadcaster_FollowNext` (S2's own binding table) and
    `LUI_CoD_LuaCall_FollowNext` (AW's symbol) are two conventions for one
    marshaller; both are correct. Only a clash with the name's OWN cited source is
    a defect.
  - **A case-only collision is two legal C identifiers.** Surface it, do not fail
    on it.

An audit that cries wolf gets ignored, which is worse than no audit.

### It immediately caught 4 real defects

Names applied from AW anchors BEFORE MWR had been harvested, which MWR then
contradicts -- so they were never tested against a second reference:

    0x2B9220  luaopen_string                        vs MWR hks__parse_pattern
    0x300400  hks::SimpleCompilerState::signalError  vs MWR hks__CodeGenerator__resolveTypeDecoration
    0x2C0510  hks::io_tostring                       vs MWR hks__inspect_garbage
    0x58FC00  GScr_GetPlayerData                     vs MWR GScr_IsItemUnlocked

All four REVERTED to `sub_` with both claims recorded in the comment. Per the
Contradiction Rule neither side automatically wins; resolve from the function's
own body before renaming. This is the loop closing: apply, audit, revert what the
audit disproves.

# ENGINE-SUBSYSTEM NAMING PUSH — 3,066 → 3,251 (2026-08-16, part 3)

Goal: name the CL_ / SV_ / CG_ / Scr_ / GScr_ core rather than more Lua glue.

    named 3,066 -> 3,251     substantial 1,127 -> 1,165 (10.74%)
    Com_ +12  Scr_ +11  Live_ +7  BG_ +6  UI_ +6  CL_ +5  CG_ +4  Dvar_ +4
    SV_ +1    G_ +1     MSG_ +1   FX_ +1   GScr_ +0  PM_ +0  SND_ +0

## ⛔ DISPROVEN — S2 has no {string, function} GSC builtin table

Hypothesis: `GScr_*` lives in `{ "spawn", GScr_Spawn, 1 }` triples at stride 24,
which the first scanner (stride-16 pairs only) would have missed.

`re/scan_tables.py` now infers stride and field offset from the data instead of
assuming them. Across all of .rdata it finds **92 tables, and only 4 are not the
already-known stride-16 shape** -- and those 4 are PostScript/Type-1 font tables
(`FontMatrix`, `Encoding`, `CharStrings`) plus the quality presets.

So the GSC builtin dispatch is NOT a name->pointer table in .rdata. AW has one
(0x82058078, `fadein -> Script_FadeIn`), S2 does not -- consistent with modern CoD
hashing script function names rather than storing pointers to them. **Do not
re-scan .rdata for it.** The next idea, untried: recover the builtin names from
the dumped GSC, find the engine's canonical-string hash, and look for a
{hash, fn} table instead.

## ⭐ TWO NEW PROPAGATION METHODS (both compound; re-run after every pass)

### re/propagate_callers.py -- caller-intersection

The callee-side method (`propagate_callgraph.py`) needs "exactly one unknown on
each side", which almost never holds at 7% coverage -- it yielded 18.

Turn it around. For an unknown X, take the S2 functions that CALL it and are
themselves named, map each to its reference twin, and INTERSECT what those twins
call. Subtract every name already worn by another S2 function. One survivor is X.

Three unrelated callers agreeing is not coincidence, and unlike the callee side it
gets STRONGER as coverage grows. Yielded 79 immediately, incl.
`Scr_GetNumParam` on **17 independent callers**, `Scr_GetString` on 14,
`Com_Parse` on 10, `Dvar_RegisterFloat` on 8.

### re/align_calls.py -- anchored call-sequence alignment

Caller-intersection cannot bootstrap CL_/SV_/CG_ at all: those are mostly called
by other UNNAMED CL_/SV_/CG_ functions, so there are no named callers to
intersect.

So align instead. A matched pair calls broadly the same things in the same ORDER.
Use callees already named on BOTH sides as ANCHORS and align the gaps between
them; a gap containing exactly one unnamed S2 callee and one unaccounted
reference callee resolves. Anchors re-synchronise at every agreement, so inlining
drift is contained to its own gap instead of propagating.

⚠ Needs CALL ORDER, which `s2_export_idb.py` destroys (it sorts callees by
address). `re/export_ordered.py` preserves it, taking order from the address of
the CALL INSTRUCTION.

⚠ The MCP plugin enforces a **hard 60 s internal timeout** (`IDASyncError`),
independent of the HTTP timeout. Walking every instruction of 61k functions
cannot fit. Export only the functions you need -- for alignment that is the ~600
matched pairs, which takes seconds.

Yielded 32 across two rounds: `Scr_GetFloat`, `Scr_GetVector`, `Scr_Error`,
`Scr_LoadScript`, `Info_ValueForKey`, `Info_SetValueForKey`, `Com_DPrintf`,
`Com_PrintError`, `Com_BeginParseSession`, `MSG_WriteInt64`, `Dvar_SetIntByName`,
`DB_GetRawBuffer`, `MyAssertHandler`, `I_flrand`.

### re/name_loop.py -- runs caller-intersection to a fixed point

Refresh names, propagate from every reference, apply, repeat. Converges in 2-3
rounds. Added 44 across two invocations on top of the direct passes.

## ⚠ REJECTED BY REVIEW — 0xAF9B70

Alignment proposed `hksi_lua_getlocal`. **Not applied.** CLAUDE.md establishes
sub_AF9B70 as an Arxan indirect dispatch thunk (`return v0()`) appearing in
unrelated call slots throughout the image, so any positional match to it is an
artefact of the thunk. Recorded as a rejected candidate on the function.

## ⚠ THE HONEST LIMIT — SV_ and GScr_ DID NOT MOVE

Every technique here needs SEEDS: a function already named in BOTH binaries.
Subsystems that start with few named functions stay stuck, and SV_ (31 named) and
GScr_ (25) are exactly that. The gains landed where seeds already existed.

To break the deadlock the next step must create seeds WITHOUT relying on existing
names. Candidates, untried:

  1. **Structural cross-title matching.** `tools/s2_match_builds.py` gets 99.36%
     precision Steam<->Xbox because same source = same sizes. Cross-title that
     fails, but call-graph TOPOLOGY (in/out degree, callee-name fingerprints)
     around large distinctive functions may still match S2<->MWR without names.
  2. **The GSC hash table** (see above) -- would name the GScr_ builtins wholesale.
  3. **MWR asserts for STRUCTS** rather than names: source paths and field
     expressions. Still completely untapped, and it is what a documentation-first
     reconstruction actually needs.

## The audit caught two real defects in this pass

  - a name citing BOTH reference builds when only one contains it
    (`PLprintf`: AW has no PL* functions; MWR 0xE240F0 does). The merge was
    recording the UNION of sources instead of those backing the CHOSEN spelling.
    `re/name_loop.py` fixed; the comment corrected.
  - ⚠ and then the CORRECTION NOTE itself re-triggered the check, because it
    quoted the literal token the detector greps for. Substring-based provenance
    checks are brittle -- when writing a correction, do not quote the marker.

## Tooling added (re/), part 3

    re/scan_tables.py        stride/offset-inferring table scanner (RULE A24 timeout)
    re/propagate_callers.py  caller-intersection propagation
    re/export_ordered.py     graph export preserving CALL ORDER
    re/align_calls.py        anchored call-sequence alignment
    re/name_loop.py          run propagation to a fixed point
