# ⭐⭐⭐ THE CoD4 READER'S REAL DEFECT — AN INCOMPLETE PLAYERSTATE TAIL (2026-08-17)

Located and bounded. The reader's own comment admits it:

    # objectives / hud / weaponstructs — not needed for POV pose offline v1

`_read_playerstate_tails` reads PS_STATS + two ammo sections and then RETURNS,
while the engine keeps reading. Every unread bit is left in the stream, so the
entity loop starts mid-playerstate. **This is the single upstream cause of the
99.7% entity truncation, and it also poisons the POV pose via the delta chain.**

It then hides itself: `if msg.overflow: msg.overflow = False` after the tail.

## MEASURED — the signature is a bit-phase error, not corruption

    2,050 of 2,057 decoded snapshots truncate in the entity loop
    entities read before truncation: 739 got 0, 401 got 1, 305 got 2, 163 got 3,
        123 got 4, 70, 61, 54, 38, 24, 15, 20 ...   <- a SMOOTH DECAY

A smooth decay is what a leftover-bit-count produces: how far the entity loop gets
depends on how many bits the tail failed to consume. Corruption would be bimodal.

**The FIRST snapshot already truncates**, so this is not propagation from a later
fault. origin is exactly [0,0,0] early (plausible pre-spawn) and only becomes
garbage (5.557e+26) once a bad delta enters the baseline chain and is re-applied.

## PROVEN — the engine's tail order, from its own cl_shownet 4 strings

MSG_ReadDeltaPlayerstate @0x17d2e0 (6,072 bytes, fully inlined bit readers).
Only three sections name themselves; the rest were located by their loop bounds:

    line  420   PS_STATS
    line  770   PS_AMMO       with  for ( j = 0; j != 16; ++j )
    line  888   PS_AMMOCLIP   inside for ( k = 0; k != 128; k += 16 )   <- 8 groups
                              with  for ( m = 0; m != 16; ++m )
    line  973   UNNAMED section @0x17e160
    line 1055   objectives    -> MSG_ReadDeltaField(..., &objectiveFields, 0, 0)
                              x numObjectiveFields (6), twice (read then copy)
    line 1142   UNNAMED section, for ( n = v196; ; n = v196 )

## ⭐ PS_STATS IS ALREADY CORRECT — verified field by field

Worth recording so it is not "fixed" needlessly. CoD4 accumulates FIVE flag bits
(`v30 = bit0`, `v215 = 2*bit1`, ... `v44 = v40 | (16 * bit4)` at line 511) then:

    & 1     short          & 8     6-bit value -> a5[85]
    & 2     short          & 0x10  byte        -> a5[86]
    & 4     short

which is exactly `_skip_ps_stats`: `_read_packed5`, 3 shorts, `_read_packed6`, byte.

## ⚠ MWR IS **NOT** A USABLE TEMPLATE FOR THIS TAIL

MWR-PS4's MSG_ReadDeltaPlayerstate @0x7255d0 is far more readable (real
MSG_ReadBit/MSG_ReadBits calls, not inlined) and its PS_STATS is close
(`MSG_ReadBits(4)` + 3 shorts + byte — FOUR flags where CoD4 has five). But its
ammo section is a `while (MSG_ReadBit())` loop over changed slots with
`ReadBits(4)/ReadBits(1)/ReadBits(31)`, where CoD4 uses fixed 16-iteration loops.
**The tails diverged between the two engines. CoD4's must be transcribed from
CoD4's own decompile.** Do not port MWR's shape across.

## NEXT — this is now a bounded transcription job

Transcribe, in order, from `re/_cod4_ps.txt` (the decompile is saved):
    PS_AMMO (~line 745-860), PS_AMMOCLIP (~861-970), the unnamed section at 973,
    objectives (1055-1093), and the unnamed section at 1142.
Only the BIT COUNT has to be exact - the values themselves are not needed for the
transcode, but every bit must be consumed.

VERIFICATION IS FREE AND UNAMBIGUOUS: `entities_truncated` must fall from 2,050/2,057
toward 0. That single number measures the whole tail, because any residual bit error
shows up immediately as a truncated entity loop.

## ⛔ CORRECTED — the incomplete tail was NOT the cause. Measured, not assumed.

I wrote above that the missing tail sections were "the single upstream cause of the
99.7% entity truncation". **Implementing them barely moved it:**

    baseline (tail stops after ammo)   2,057 snaps   2,050 truncated  99.7%   4,624 ents
    + objectives + hudelems           1,699 snaps   1,690 truncated  99.5%   3,894 ents  <- WORSE
    + objectives, hudelems disabled   1,885 snaps   1,876 truncated  99.5%   4,357 ents

So the desync is UPSTREAM of the tail, in the playerstate field loop or in
`read_delta_field` itself. The tail work is still correct and necessary - it is
simply not what is breaking this - and it must not be credited with a fix it did
not produce.

### ⭐ THE FULL TAIL FORMAT, recovered from the WRITER (keep - this part is solid)

`MSG_WriteDeltaPlayerstate` @0x173210 is 4,629 bytes and calls MSG_WriteBit/Bits/
Short/Byte as REAL FUNCTIONS, where the reader @0x17d2e0 has every accessor
inlined. **For any IW-engine wire format, read the WRITER.** It states the format
directly and took one decompile where the reader took five.

    [bit] predicted        (origin[2]/commandTime comparison - v56)
    MSG_WriteBits(lc, GetMinBitCountForNum(0x8D))    0x8D = 141 -> 8 bits
    field loop
    [bit] PS_STATS      5 flag bits; &1 short  &2 short  &4 short  &8 6-bit  &0x10 byte
    [bit] PS_AMMO       4 groups: per group [bit] -> u16 mask + one short per set bit
    [bit] PS_AMMOCLIP   8 groups, same shape (for n = 0; n != 128; n += 16)
    [bit] OBJECTIVES    16 x { WriteBits(state,3); [bit] -> all 6 objectiveFields }
    [bit] HUDELEMS      2 x MSG_WriteDeltaHudElems(..., 31)
    [bit] 128 raw bytes at ps+2076

`MSG_WriteDeltaHudElems` @0x172880: `WriteBits(count,5)`, then per elem
`WriteBits(lc,6)` and fields `0..lc` INCLUSIVE (`for i = 0; i <= v18; ++i`).
`hudElemFields` @0x40fdc0, 40 entries, dumped to `iw3_hudElemFields.json`.

### ⭐ FOUR ENCODERS ARE MISSING FROM `delta_field.CODECS`

    CODECS has: -100 -98 -97 -96 -95 -94 -93 -92 -91 -90 -89 -88 -87 -86 0
    tables use: -100 -99 -98 -97 -96 -94 -93 -92 -91 -90 -88 -87 -86 -85 -16 -8
    MISSING:    -99  -85  -16  -8

The fallback reads `abs(bits)` RAW BITS, so **-85 reads 85 bits and -99 reads 99**.

    -8   playerStateFields[9] movementDir, [34] viewHeightTarget, [64], [73]
         + playerEntityStateFields[3] / corpseEntityStateFields[18] movementDir
    -16  playerStateFields[13] weaponTime, [38] weaponDelay, [48] pm_time,
         [85] grenadeTimeLeft, [103], [123]
    -85  hudElemFields ONLY: color.rgba, fromColor.rgba, glowColor.rgba
    -99  hudElemFields ONLY: fromX, fromY

-8/-16 are plausibly "signed N-bit", in which case the fallback's BIT COUNT is
right by accident and they do not desync. -85/-99 are catastrophic, which is why
enabling the hudelem section cost 358 snapshots. **The hudelem section is
implemented but gated behind `_HUDELEMS_ENABLED = False` until they exist** - a
section that consumes the wrong number of bits is worse than one that is absent.

From `MSG_WriteDeltaField` @0x171ef0's switch (the authority for all of them):

    case -88   WriteLong(a ^ b)                      float32-XOR, 32 bits
    case -87   WriteAngle16                          16 bits
    case -86   WriteBits(v, 5)
    case -100  [bit] then WriteAngle16
    case -89   [bit] -> {WriteBit0, WriteBits(v,5), WriteByte(v>>5)} | WriteLong(xor)
    case -85   [bit equal] | {[bit], 3 x WriteByte, WriteBits(b3>>3, 5)}
    case -99   [bit] -> {WriteBit0, WriteBits(v,4), WriteByte(v>>4)}

### NEXT — the remaining desync, and how to corner it cheaply

The tail is now excluded by measurement, so the fault is in the field loop or a
codec. In order of cost:

  1. implement -85 / -99 from the switch above and re-enable hudelems; that is
     needed regardless and removes one variable
  2. verify -8 / -16 against `MSG_WriteDeltaField`'s `default:` case rather than
     assuming "signed N-bit"
  3. the decisive instrument: after `parse_snapshot` returns, read the next 4-bit
     svc opcode. If the snapshot consumed exactly the right bits it must be a
     valid opcode (usually svc_EOF). That converts "entities truncated" into a
     per-message pass/fail and will bisect the field loop in one run.

# ⭐⭐⭐⭐ THE "ILLEGAL OPCODE" CLASS IS DISSOLVED — IT WAS TWO MODEL ERRORS OF MINE
# (2026-08-18). This was the one UNBOUNDED risk in the CoD4 -> MWR port. It is gone.

## The symptom, as recorded for weeks

"3.6-30% of MWR messages start with an illegal 4-bit opcode (100% have bit 3 set,
period-40 recurrence, shared byte tails); neither raw nor MWR-Huffman decodes them."

Measured across the whole 15-demo oracle corpus it was **22.5% of 38,608 messages**.

## ⛔ ERROR 1 — MWR HAS NO RAW MESSAGE PATH. EVERYTHING IS COMPRESSED.

`CL_ParseServerMessage` @ MWR-PC 0x3425b0 (441 bytes), both branches:

    if ( *(DWORD *)(msg + 48) )            // the compression flag
        sub_5A3200(data + readcount, cursize - readcount, out, 0x4000)   // ZLIB
    else
        sub_4EB460(data + readcount, ..., cursize - readcount, ...)      // HUFFMAN
    -> CL_ParseMessage(client, decompressed, msg)

Same shape as S2's (`msg+52 != 0 -> zlib 16 KB, else a different codec 128 KB`),
which this file already documented. **There is no third branch.** So reading
`body[0] & 0xF` was reading a COMPRESSED byte as if it were plaintext.

And that explains the thing that made the old reading look credible: Huffman is
deterministic, so every message beginning with the same svc opcode produces the
same leading byte. "50% raw nibble 6" was not 50% svc_snapshot in plaintext - it
was the Huffman CODE for svc_snapshot, whose first byte happens to have low
nibble 6. The 22.5% "invalid" were simply the messages that start with a
different opcode.

## ⛔ ERROR 2 — THE OPCODE IS **3 BITS**, NOT 4

`CL_ParseMessage` @0x341420:

    result = MSG_ReadBits(msg, 3);       // <- THREE
    switch (result) { case 0,2,3,4,5,6; default: }

So `14 & 7 == 6`. The old note's "100% have bit 3 set" was the first bit of the
NEXT field being mistaken for part of the opcode. Both errors compounded: a 4-bit
read of a compressed byte.

## ⭐ THE RESULT — a textbook svc distribution, 0 invalid

    38,608 non-zlib messages, MWR Huffman + 3-bit opcode
    decode failures 179 (0.46%)

        opcode 6   35,012   91.1%   svc_snapshot
        opcode 2    2,494    6.5%
        opcode 3      801    2.1%
        opcode 5      122    0.3%
        ---------------------------------
        INVALID         0

per demo the snapshot share is 87-97%, consistent across all 15. That is exactly
what a real server-message stream looks like.

## WHY THE CLASSIFIER MISSED IT

`tools/classify_msgs.py` imported **`iw3.huffman`** - CoD4's POINTER-TREE decoder -
and ran it against MWR data. `tools/mwr_huff.py` + `tools/mwr_huffread.json`
(MWR's FLAT 16 KB LOOKUP TABLE, transcribed from Huff_offsetReceive @PS4 0x71f760)
already existed and were simply never wired in. The two engines use different
Huffman implementations, and I tested MWR with CoD4's.

## LESSON, and it is the same one twice

Both errors are the same mistake: **I inferred a wire format from the DATA instead
of reading the PARSER**, then treated the resulting pattern as a finding. One
decompile of CL_ParseServerMessage + CL_ParseMessage (10 minutes, and the IDB was
already named) settled what weeks of byte-pattern analysis had turned into a
"structural anomaly" with a period-40 recurrence.

The corollary for the port: **h1-mod's own source is a first-class reference and
was underused.** `demo_utils.cpp` states the container and the feed contract
outright (`[u32 seq][u32 relAck|useZlib<<31][body]`, `msg.readcount` left 0,
`.targetLocalNetID = use_zlib` because the parser reads the flag from msg+0x30).

## WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THE PORT

The write side now has a fully specified target: to emit an MWR message we must
Huffman-COMPRESS the svc stream with MWR's table and set the flag accordingly.
`tools/mwr_huff.py` implements the read direction; the WRITE direction
(Huff_offsetTransmit) still needs transcribing, but it is a bounded, known job
against a table we already have.

No unbounded unknowns remain in the message layer.

---

# CoD4 READER — FOUR STRUCTURAL FIXES, AND THE METRIC STILL HAS NOT MOVED (2026-08-18)

Honest status. Each fix below is individually correct and transcribed from the
engine, several were verified by hand, and the truncation rate went
99.7% -> 99.5%. Something more fundamental is still wrong and I have not found it.

## ⭐ WHAT IS NOW VERIFIED CORRECT (do not re-check these)

    container            .dm_1 walk + [u32 len][compressed] framing
    HUFFMAN              0% invalid first opcode across 2,461 messages:
                         69.9% svc_snapshot(6), 30.0% svc_serverCommand(4),
                         0.04% svc_gamestate(1)
    BYTE reads           697/739 svc_serverCommand strings decode as clean text
                         ('s 41', 'G 10700', 'H 16850')
    svc walk             opcode is MSG_ReadByte - a FULL BYTE in CoD4
                         (⚠ MWR uses MSG_ReadBits(3) - the engines DIFFER)
    snapshot header      MSG_ReadLong(serverTime), ReadByte(deltaNum),
                         ReadByte(snapFlags), then MSG_ReadDeltaPlayerstate.
                         Nothing between them.
    predicted bit        exactly ONE inlined bit read before the lc bit-scan
                         (counted in the disassembly; MWR reads 3-4, CoD4 reads 1)
    lc width             GetMinBitCountForNum @0x176410 hand-evaluated for 141:
                         v2=16, v3=8, v4=v5=0 -> 16-8 = 8 bits. == ceil_log2(141).

## ⭐⭐ FIX 1 — THE DUAL-CURSOR msg_t. The reader had ONE cursor.

`msg_t` keeps TWO independent cursors, and the reader merged them:

    msg+0x1C  readcount   BYTE cursor (MSG_ReadByte/Short/Long/String)
    msg+0x20  bit         BIT  cursor (MSG_ReadBit/ReadBits)

From the inlined MSG_ReadBit in MSG_ReadDeltaPlayerstate:

    if ((msg->bit & 7) == 0) {          // needs a fresh byte
        msg->bit = 8 * msg->readcount;  // RESYNC to the byte cursor
        ++msg->readcount;               // and CLAIM that byte
    }
    result = (data[bit >> 3] >> (bit & 7)) & 1;  ++msg->bit;

The old `read_byte()` called `align()`, rounding the SHARED cursor up and
DISCARDING the partially-consumed byte. Given `3 bits, a byte, 3 bits`:

    engine : data[0] bits 0-2, data[1], then data[0] bits 3-5
    old    : data[0] bits 0-2, data[1], then data[2] bits 0-2

`read_delta_field` does exactly that interleave (change bit, then a 32-bit value)
on nearly every field. Rewritten; `align()` is gone from every byte reader.

## ⭐ FIX 2 — the field loop's TWO EARLY EXITS

From MSG_WriteDeltaPlayerstate's own loop (lines 148-206 of its decompile):

    v11 = j[12];                                 // changeHints
    if (v11 == 2) break;                         // (1)
    ...
    else if (v11 != 3 || a1[13]) { ...normal... }
    else if (v56) break;                         // (2) predicted field + pred bit
    MSG_WriteBit0(a2);
    if (++v49 == v51) done;                      // bounded by lc

(1) changeHints==2 ends the delta-coded region. CoD4 has SIX such fields from
    index 71 (viewHeightLerpDown, offhandSecondary, radarEnabled,
    shellshockDuration, sprintButtonUpRequired, sprintDelay) and nothing past the
    first is in the stream.
(2) with the predicted bit set the writer stops at the first changeHints==3 field
    - index 4, origin[0] - because the client predicts the rest.

Also: `v17 = (v11 == 3)` is passed UNCONDITIONALLY as WriteDeltaField's
zero-baseline flag, so a predicted field always deltas against zero. The reader
had it conditioned on the predicted bit.

Both -87 and the normal branch reduce to "a change bit, then maybe a value" from
the READER's side, so only the two breaks are reader-visible.

## FIX 3 / 4 — the full playerstate tail, and the missing codecs

Recovered from MSG_WriteDeltaPlayerstate @0x173210 (see the earlier entry).
Objectives implemented; hudelems implemented but gated behind
`_HUDELEMS_ENABLED = False` because encoders **-85 and -99** are absent from
`delta_field.CODECS` and the fallback reads abs(bits) RAW BITS (85 and 99).

## ⛔ AND YET — the measurements

    baseline                       2057 snaps  99.7% trunc  4624 ents  4 clients
    + tail (objectives+hudelems)   1699        99.5%        3894       2
    + hudelems disabled            1885        99.5%        4357       2
    + dual-cursor msg_t            1785        99.7%        3899       0
    + field-loop early exits       1890        99.5%        4011       1
    A/B: predicted-break OFF       2029        99.7%        4311       -

The origin garbage (5.557e+26) IS gone - origin now reads a consistent 0.0 - so
the fixes improved signal quality. But the snapshot consumes a median of only
**10% of its message** (mean 15%), and that has not moved.

A per-stage trace shows TWO populations:

    msg_len=155  snapshot 1->149   playerstate 7->146 (139 bytes)   ~96% consumed
    msg_len=232  snapshot 1->37    playerstate 7->35  (28 bytes)    ~16%
    msg_len=198  snapshot 11->22   playerstate 17->21 (4 bytes)     ~6%

so SOME playerstates decode fully and most bail early. Only ~2.6% of snapshots
consume >70% of their message.

## NEXT — what I would do, in order

  1. **Find what separates the two populations.** A full 139-byte playerstate vs a
     4-byte one, in the same demo, is the sharpest signal available and it has not
     been characterised. Check `predicted`, `lc`, and `delta_num` for each group.
  2. Implement -85 / -99 from MSG_WriteDeltaField's switch (already transcribed in
     the earlier entry) and re-enable hudelems - needed regardless.
  3. Verify the -8 / -16 encoders against that switch's `default:` case instead of
     assuming "signed N-bit".
  4. `MSG_ReadEntityIndex` and `MSG_ClearLastReferencedEntity` are UNVERIFIED
     against CoD4. S2/MWR reset lastEntityRef to **-1**; our reader resets to 0,
     which would put every delta-coded entity index off by one.

## LESSON

Four individually-correct fixes moved the number by 0.2 points. That is itself a
finding: it means the dominant fault is elsewhere and I should have built a
BISECTING instrument before fixing anything. The per-stage byte trace (added at
the end) is that instrument and it immediately exposed the two-population split -
it should have been step one, not step five.

# ⭐⭐⭐⭐ CoD4 READER — 99.5% TRUNCATION -> 0.0%. THE STREAM NOW PARSES. (2026-08-18)

    metric                 before      after
    snapshots decoded      2057        2460 / 2490
    entity loop truncated  99.5%       0.0%
    entities decoded          0        78,559
    client records            0        105
    message consumed       median 10%  median 100%   (mean 97.4%)

The snapshot now consumes its ENTIRE message. That is the framing being right.

## ⭐ THE DOMINANT FAULT WAS A NameError, HIDDEN BY A BLANKET except

    NameError: name '_read_packed6' is not defined      x1,881

`_read_packed6` was CALLED at three sites (the entity lastChangedField, the client
lastChangedField, and PS_STATS) and **never defined anywhere**. Every entity read
raised, and the reader's original `except Exception: entities = []` swallowed it
silently - which is exactly why the reader reported zero entities for months while
looking like a decode problem.

That vindicates removing the blanket catch as the first fix of this whole effort;
it just took until an exception PROBE was pointed at the loop to read the message.

## ⭐ THREE REAL CODEC DEFECTS, all fixed from MSG_WriteDeltaField @0x171ef0

**1. The DEFAULT codec was wrong.** The encoder switch cases only
`0, -89, -88, -99, -100, -87, -86, -85, -97, -98, -96, -94, -93`. Everything else
- **-8, -16 and every positive width** - falls through to:

    if (!new) return MSG_WriteBit0;              // a ZERO value is ONE bit
    MSG_WriteBit1;
    v28 = old ^ new;  v27 = abs(bits);
    if (v27 & 7) { MSG_WriteBits(v28, v27 & 7); v28 >>= (v27 & 7); }
    for (; v41; v41 -= 8) { MSG_WriteByte(v28); v28 >>= 8; }

MIXED bit/byte - the remainder on the BIT cursor, the whole bytes through
MSG_WriteByte on the BYTE cursor. The old code read abs(bits) RAW BITS and never
read the leading zero-flag at all. Fixing this alone took truncation 99.3% -> 96.9%
and doubled the entity count.

**2. The coordinate codec (-92/-91/-90) XORed a FLOAT.** From
MSG_WriteOriginFloat @0x171d30 / MSG_WriteOriginZFloat @0x171c60:

    v9 = floor(new + 0.5); v8 = floor(old + 0.5);        // ROUNDED INTS
    if ((unsigned)(v9 - v8 + 64) > 0x7F) {
        WriteBit1; center = mapCenter[axis] + 0.5;
        WriteBits((v9 + 0x8000 - (int)center) ^ (v8 + 0x8000 - (int)center), 16);
    } else {
        WriteBit0; WriteBits(v9 - v8 + 64, 7);           // SEVEN bits, not six
    }

Two errors: the baseline must be the ROUNDED INT (it was XORing the raw float ->
TypeError 2,414 times), and the small-delta case is 7 bits (it read 6). **Fixing
this took truncation 96.9% -> 0.0%.**

**3. `_write_i32` raised on out-of-range values** instead of wrapping like a
32-bit store. Now masks and packs as "<I".

## Also fixed, verified against the engine

    MSG_ClearLastReferencedEntity @0x176a00 sets msg+36 = **-1**, not 0. The
    reader reset to 0, putting every delta-coded entity index off by one. (Two
    clear sites in CL_ParseSnapshot: before entities AND before clients.)

## ⛔ STILL WRONG — THE FRAMING IS RIGHT, THE VALUES ARE NOT

    roster names   b'\xef\xbf\xbdZ', '\x1c\x13'      (binary, not text)
    entity origins x [-1.2e16, 32760]                (astronomical)
    eType          72,269 of 78,559 decode as 0

So the reader consumes the right NUMBER of bits everywhere while decoding wrong
VALUES. That is a genuinely different and much better failure mode than before,
and it is bounded: bit-exact framing means each remaining defect is now isolated
to a single codec or a single struct offset rather than desynchronising everything
downstream.

Prime suspects, in order:
  1. `ENTITY_OFF` in snapshot.py is marked "approximate" in its own comment -
     pos (24,28,32) and angles (168,172,176) are GUESSES. The real offsets are in
     the dumped `iw3_entityStateFields.json` (name -> offset) and should be taken
     from there, exactly as client_summary already does.
  2. `_codec_default` writes `_write_i32` unconditionally; float-typed fields need
     the bit pattern stored, not an int reinterpreted.
  3. -85 / -99 are still absent from CODECS (hudelems remain gated off).

## LESSON

Five structurally-correct fixes moved truncation 99.7% -> 99.5%. The sixth - a
missing function name - took it to 0. **Point an exception probe at the failing
loop BEFORE reasoning about the format.** I spent this whole session transcribing
wire formats from decompiles (all of it correct and worth having) while a
one-line NameError was the thing actually stopping it, and it was visible from
the first minute to anyone who printed the exception instead of catching it.

---

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# CoD4 -> MWR READER — SESSION 2026-08-18. THE METRIC WAS WRONG; 4.17% -> 6.91%
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

## ⛔⛔ FIRST, A CORRECTION THAT INVALIDATES THE PREVIOUS SESSION'S HEADLINE

The last entry claims "99.5% TRUNCATION -> 0.0%. THE STREAM NOW PARSES", on the
strength of `entities_truncated` falling to 0 and the snapshot consuming "a median
of 100% of its message".

**Both numbers are worthless as correctness evidence, and the conclusion is
withdrawn.** A DESYNCED parse also consumes the whole buffer - it reads garbage
until it runs out. "Truncation" only counted the cases where an exception was
raised, and removing the exceptions removed the signal, not the defect.

### THE RIGHT METRIC: does the message terminate at svc_EOF?

A server message is a sequence of svc ops ending in svc_EOF (7). If the snapshot
consumes exactly the right number of bits, the walk lands on that byte with
nothing meaningful left over. If it does not, the walk hits an invalid opcode or
runs off the end. That is a per-message PASS/FAIL and it cannot be faked.

    tools/cod4_to_h1/diag/eofcheck.py  <demos...>

    BASELINE (start of session, 39-demo AZD corpus, 57,235 snapshot messages):
        EOF-terminated  2,385 / 57,235   =  4.17%
        overflow        47,584
    AFTER this session's fixes:
        EOF-terminated  3,957 / 57,235   =  6.91%
        overflow        46,645

So the reader is still fundamentally not working. 6.91% is the honest number.
Everything below is what was proven along the way; several items are corrections
to earlier records, and several are corrections to my OWN probes.

## ⭐ FIX 1 — MSG_ReadEntityIndex had BOTH its branch polarity and its width wrong

TWICE-PROVEN, from the reader's disassembly and then independently from the writer.

`MSG_WriteEntityIndex` @0x171a70 states it in ten lines:

    if (num - lastEntityRef == 1) { Bit1; last = num; }
    else {
        Bit0;
        if (bits != 10)             { WriteBits(num, bits);        last = num; }
        else if (num - last > 15)   { Bit1; WriteBits(num, bits);  last = num; }
        else                        { Bit0; WriteBits(num-last,4); last = num; }
    }

so the read is

    if ReadBit():            last += 1
    elif bits != 10:         last  = ReadBits(bits)
    elif ReadBit():          last  = ReadBits(bits)      # bit SET -> FULL
    else:                    last += ReadBits(4)         # bit CLEAR -> 4-bit delta

The old implementation took the DELTA branch when the second bit was SET (inverted)
and read SIX bits of delta instead of four.

⚠ **THE ENGINE'S OWN DEBUG STRING IS STALE.** `MSG_ReadEntityIndex` prints
`"Entity num: %i bits (delta)"` with the argument **6**, while the code beside it
reads **4** - counted at instruction level over 0x178c9d..0x178d97: `and 1`,
`add eax,eax`, `shl eax,2`, `lea edx,[eax*8]`, shifts 0,1,2,3 and nothing more.
Do not trust that string.

⭐ CONSEQUENCE WORTH KEEPING: the index sequence is STRICTLY INCREASING by
construction, so a decoded index that repeats, decreases or comes out negative is
proof the entity loop started at the wrong bit. That is the strongest offline
validity criterion available for this format.

## ⭐⭐ FIX 2 — MSG_ReadBigString IS NOT LENGTH-PREFIXED (the biggest single find)

`MSG_ReadBigString` @0x176df0 is a plain NUL-terminated byte loop, structurally
identical to `MSG_ReadString` @0x176ea0 and differing only in the destination cap
(0x1FFF vs 0x3FF). It also maps `'%'` (37) -> `'.'` (46).

Our reader consumed a 2-byte length that does not exist, so `svc_gamestate`
desynced at its FIRST configstring.

    before:  configstrings    1        entity baselines   0
    after:   configstrings 1264        entity baselines  48

The gamestate now yields real data - serverinfo, the dvar block, and `cs[12]` =
`'-230.800049 318.150024 -43.500000'`, which is the map centre the -92/-91/-90
coordinate codecs need.

Gamestate format confirmed from `SV_SendClientGameState` @0x1bd210:

    MSG_WriteByte(1)                       svc_gamestate
    MSG_WriteLong(serverCommandSequence)
    MSG_WriteByte(2)                       ONE svc_configstring byte...
    MSG_WriteShort(count)                  ...then a COUNT...
    per string: [bit1 = index is last+1] | [bit0 + WriteBits(index,12)]
                MSG_WriteBigString(value)  ...then all of them
    per baseline: MSG_WriteByte(3); MSG_WriteEntity(...)
    MSG_WriteByte(7); MSG_WriteLong(clientNum); MSG_WriteLong(checksumFeed);
    MSG_WriteByte(7)

## ⭐ FIX 3 — the playerstate field loop has NO EARLY EXITS

The previous implementation had two `break`s transcribed from the WRITER's loop in
`MSG_WriteDeltaPlayerstate` (changeHints==2, and predicted+changeHints==3). **A
reader must not have them.** From `MSG_ReadDeltaPlayerstate` @0x17d2e0 itself
(lines 336-359 of its decompile):

    if (lc > 0) {
        v49 = &playerStateFields;
        if (a6 && v205)   do { MSG_ReadDeltaField(..., v49, ..., v49[12]==3); } while (++n != lc);
        else              do { MSG_ReadDeltaField(..., v49, ..., 0);          } while (++n != lc);
    }
    if (numPlayerStateFields > lc) { copy the rest from the baseline }

Exactly `lc` fields, unconditionally. The writer's breaks are consistent with the
lastChangedField IT computed, so `lc` already accounts for them; stopping early
left every remaining field's bits in the stream.

**`a6` is 1 at BOTH CL_ParseSnapshot call sites** - a hoisted `mov [esp+14h], 1`
at 0xc5056 and 0xc5c86, which is why it is not visible at the call itself. So the
predicted bit's ONLY effect is to select the delta base:

    zeroBase = predicted && changeHints == 3

and in `MSG_ReadDeltaField` that flag chooses the base for BOTH the unchanged-copy
and the codec XOR (`v551 = a7 ? &zero : &from[offset]`).

## ⭐⭐ FIX 4 — MOST CODECS WERE WRONG. delta_field.py rewritten from the switch.

All 17 transcribed from `MSG_WriteDeltaField` @0x171ef0. The worst:

    bits == 0    the zero path writes a SECOND bit (0 -> +0.0, 1 -> 0x80000000)
                 which we never read, AND the small-delta case is 5 bits + a byte
                 where we read 6 + a byte. Two independent 1-bit desyncs, on a
                 codec used by 8 of the 59 entity fields.
    bits == -89  we read an extra leading bit and 6 bits instead of 5, and used
                 the raw long instead of old ^ long.
    bits == -98  is "one bit changed -> Bit0 + 5-bit index; else Bit1 + 3 bytes".
                 We had an unrelated encoding.
    bits == -96  is 1022 -> Bit1; 0 -> Bit0,Bit1; else Bit0,Bit0,2 bits,byte.
    bits == -86  is FIVE bits, we read six.
    bits == -85, -99   were ABSENT, so they fell through to the default codec and
                 read 85 and 99 RAW BITS. Both are hudElemFields-only, which is
                 why the hudelem section had to be disabled - and disabling it set
                 `overflow`, which read_delta_playerstate then CLEARED, so the
                 entity loop silently ran from a wrong cursor. Both now implemented
                 and `_HUDELEMS_ENABLED = True`.

VERIFIED CORRECT and not to be re-checked: -88, -97, -95, -94/-93, and the
coordinate codecs -92/-91/-90 (7-bit small delta / 16-bit large, bias 0x8000
around mapCenter). `MSG_WriteAngle16` @0x176f30 writes a 2-byte WORD through the
BYTE cursor, so -87/-100 read two BYTES, not 16 bits.

## ⛔ FIX 5 — the CLIENT lastChangedField is FIVE bits. CORRECTS a recorded finding.

The record says "PROVEN from the push order at 0x17cc52..0x17cc7a: the
lastChangedField width is a hardcoded 6 bits". The push is real - `[esp+0Ch] = 6`
- but **that slot is `MSG_ReadDeltaStruct`'s `a7`, and a7 is a DEAD ARGUMENT**: it
appears nowhere in the body except the signature. The width is computed:

    v48 = GetMinBitCountForNum(a9)        # a9 = numClientStateFields
    lc  = ReadBits(v48)
    if (lc > a6) { overflow = 1; return } # a6 = numFields

`numClientStateFields == 24`, proven independently of any dump by
`memset(v6, 0, 100)` in MSG_ReadDeltaClient and `memcpy(to, from, 4*a6 + 4) == 100`
in ReadDeltaStruct. GetMinBitCountForNum(24) = **5**.

Entities keep 6 (numEntityStateFields = 59 -> 6), which is why the hardcoded 6 went
unnoticed: right for entities, wrong for clients.

## FIX 6 — entity carry-forward, and the snapshot ring key

`CL_ParsePacketEntities` @0xc5141 is the Q3 merge: a snapshot's entity list is the
packet's entities MERGED with the previous frame's, everything unmentioned carried
over unchanged. Storing only the entities explicitly present made every carried-over
entity fall back to the gamestate baseline one frame later.

The ring is keyed by `clc.serverMessageSequence`, not by a snapshot counter:

    dword_49146C = clc.serverMessageSequence           # clc + 0x20134
    dword_491470 = deltaNum ? dword_49146C - deltaNum : -1
    v3 = 12180 * (dword_491470 & 0x1F)

In a .dm_1 that sequence is the container record's per-packet `seq`, so it is
available offline. Wired through as `ParseState.message_sequence`; the ring now
hits 100% (1383/1383 on the sample demo).

## ✅ VERIFIED CORRECT — do NOT re-investigate these

  * **The playerstate field decode.** A full field-by-field trace of the first
    snapshot gives `holdBreathScale = 1.000`, `viewHeightCurrent = 60.000`,
    `viewHeightTarget = 60`, `weapon = 93`, `aimSpreadScale = 255.0`, plausible
    sprint timestamps, and `commandTime` taking the -97 long path exactly when
    `serverTime - commandTime > 255`. That is not a desynced parse.
  * **`lc` and the head.** `predicted` then `lc = ReadBits(8)`; hand-decoded on a
    real snapshot (0xf4 -> predicted=0, lc=122) and lc is never out of range
    (0 of 1391 samples > 141 or == 0).
  * **The tail structure**, all six sections, checked against the writer:
    PS_STATS (bit + 5-bit mask + conditional short/short/short/6bits/byte),
    AMMO 4 groups, AMMO 8 groups, OBJECTIVES (16 x [3 bits][bit][6 fields]),
    HUDELEMS (bit + TWO MSG_WriteDeltaHudElems), then a bit + 128 raw bytes.
  * **Gamestate baselines decode to plausible map coordinates** (-2592.0, 1800.0,
    -8.0 and similar), so svc_baseline parsing works.
  * **ENTITY_OFF** is right and was never a guess - it matches the dumped
    entityStateFields exactly (eType 4, pos 24/28/32, angles 60/64/68,
    clientNum 140, weapon 196). The comment calling it "approximate" was wrong.
  * **The netfield tables and the logic come from the SAME binary.** The tables at
    0x40c920 / 0x40f300 / 0x40f480 are in the CoD4 macOS build (port 18337,
    imagebase 0x1000), which is the 100%-named reference - so there is no
    cross-build risk between tables and decompiles.

## ⛔ MY OWN PROBES — TWO INFERENCES WITHDRAWN

  1. **The bit-offset brute force (`diag/psoffset.py`) was invalid.** With the dual
     cursor the parse position is the PAIR (readcount, bit); byte reads move only
     readcount and bit reads only `bit`, so readcount can run far ahead of bit/8
     and a single "bit offset" does NOT identify the state. Reconstructing
     readcount from a bit position made every offset it reported an artifact. The
     "+16..+170 bits under-read" histogram is withdrawn. It also passed
     `baseline=None`, so it could not succeed once entities needed real baselines
     - which makes its "no offset within +/-40 works" result meaningless too.
  2. **The delta_num split was over-read.** `delta_num == 0` snapshots reached the
     entity sentinel 10/10 while delta snapshots reached it 23.8%, and I took that
     as proof the reader logic was correct and only baseline carry-forward was
     wrong. But those 10 had NON-MONOTONIC indices ([7, 0, 6, 10, 10, 18, ...]) -
     they hit 1023 by luck. Fixing carry-forward moved the corpus metric by 0.3
     points, consistent with that.

## WHERE THE REMAINING DESYNC IS

Narrowed, not named. On the first snapshot of the sample demo:

    playerstate  decodes correctly (values above), ends at readcount 128
    tail         stats=1, ammo4=1, ammo8=1, obj=0, hud=0, raw128=0 -> ends at 148
    entities     first index 7 (plausible), SECOND index 0 (impossible)

So the desync appears between the end of the tail and the second entity - i.e. in
the tail-to-entity transition or inside `read_delta_entity` for the first entity.
The entity preamble is `[removed bit][changed bit][lc: 6 bits]`, then field[0]
(eType) from the GENERIC table, then the per-eType table for fields 1..lc-1, with
the engine guarding `if (fieldCount >= lc)` - we `break` instead of honouring that
guard, which is one concrete difference still to fix.

## ⭐ THE REMAINING DESYNC, MEASURED — ~150 BITS SHORT AT THE TAIL/ENTITY BOUNDARY

Traced on the first snapshot of `out_vacantquad.dm_1` (seq=156801, dn=0, msglen 4938):

    playerstate  ends  rc=148  bit=1183      (values verified correct - see above)
    tail         stats=1 ammo4=1 ammo8=1 obj=0 hud=0 raw128=0
    IDX -> 7     bits 1183->1189   (6 bits: [0][0][4-bit delta 8], last -1 -> 7)  PLAUSIBLE
    ENT#1        bits 1189->1191   TWO bits: [removed=0][changed=0] -> "unchanged"
    IDX -> 0     bits 1191->1203   (12 bits, full read) -> 0 AFTER 7. IMPOSSIBLE.

Scanning bit offsets 1100..1400 for a start that yields a strictly-increasing entity
list terminating at 1023 with >= 6 entities gives only FOUR candidates, all AFTER our
tail end:

    bit 1333 (+150)  10 entities        bit 1354 (+171)  10 entities
    bit 1338 (+155)  10 entities        bit 1398 (+215)  30 entities

So the playerstate+tail is **under-reading by roughly 150 bits**, and the entity loop
starts inside whatever we failed to consume. `IDX -> 7` decoding plausibly is
coincidence - 6 bits of the missing section happening to look like a small delta.

⚠ NOTE ON THE SEEK MODEL, corrected again: for a state left by a BIT read,
`readcount = ((bit - 1) >> 3) + 1`, which is exactly what the probe computes and
matches the live trace (bit 1189 -> rc 149). So scanning bit offsets IS valid at the
tail boundary (the tail ends on a bit read); it is only invalid after BYTE reads,
where readcount can run ahead of bit/8. The earlier blanket withdrawal of the
offset probe was too strong - what stands is that its `baseline=None` walk was weak,
not that the seek was wrong here.

### What ~150 bits is NOT

    raw128 block      1024 bits   too big
    objectives, all 16 unchanged   16 x (3 + 1) = 64 bits
    two hudelem calls, both empty  2 x 5 = 10 bits
    those three together            ~74 bits   - still only half of 150

So it is not simply "one tail section whose flag we misread". Either PS_STATS or one
of the two AMMO sections is consuming too little, or there is a section between the
field loop and PS_STATS that is not implemented at all.

### NEXT STEP (concrete)

Instrument `_skip_ps_stats` and `_skip_ps_ammo` to print the mask they read and the
exact bits consumed, on this same snapshot, and compare against
`MSG_WriteDeltaPlayerstate`'s own arithmetic:

    PS_STATS    5-bit mask, then per set bit: short, short, short, 6 bits, byte
    AMMO x4     per group [bit]; if set: short mask + one short per set bit
    AMMO x8     same shape, 8 groups

A group whose short mask has many bits set is worth tens of bits, so an off-by-one in
the per-bit loop is the most likely home for the missing ~150. `_skip_ps_ammo`
currently reads `msg.read_short()` for the mask - confirm the engine writes a SHORT
there and not a 16-bit BIT read, since the two land differently on the dual cursor.

## ⛔ CORRECTION — THE POSE-SPLICE PREVIEW FIGHTS THE TEMPLATE'S SNAPSHOTS

`preview_splice.py` (previous entry) kept a real template's snapshots and overlaid
the CoD4 pose through `predicted_data`. **That cannot work, structurally**, and
h1-mod's own source says why (demo_playback.cpp:1099):

    "writing them HERE is too early, CG_DrawActiveFrame re-predicts cg->ps
     from the snapshot and wipes them"

`get_predicted_player_data` (demo_playback.cpp:1035) writes our origin/velocity
into `ps` and our viewangles into `ps.delta_angles` - but that is an OVERLAY on a
re-prediction that restarts from the template's snapshot playerstate every frame.
That playerstate belongs to a different player hundreds of units away, so
prediction-error correction drags the camera between the two. The snapshot is
authoritative for `cg->ps`; an overlay cannot win the argument.

The existing converter already knew this in miniature: its template-fallback mode
notes "per-frame network_data not re-encoded; motion from predicted_data only."

## ⭐ THE HYBRID — real bootstrap + OUR OWN snapshots. `preview_hybrid.py`

The competing thing is the template's SNAPSHOTS, not its BOOTSTRAP, and those are
separable chunks:

    KEEP  gen_header, map_header, update_gamestate_data, and the FIRST
          network_data (the svc_gamestate). This is what reaches CA_ACTIVE and it
          is the genuinely hard half - real configstrings, entity baselines,
          checksums.
    DROP  every later network_data. Those are the snapshots that compete.
    EMIT  one predicted_data + one svc_snapshot per tick carrying the CoD4 pose,
          via mwr/snapshot.py `emit_snapshot_message` on mwr/playerstate.py
          `write_pose_playerstate`, sequences continuing from the gamestate's.

Nothing competes any more: the snapshot IS our pose, the re-prediction starts from
it, and the predicted_data overlay agrees with it.

This is the existing converter's two halves combined - its template-prefix mode
(bootstrap, pose-only) plus its encode_network per-frame loop (real snapshots, but
a synthesised gamestate that never reached CA_ACTIVE).

⚠ ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING: predicted_data must be written BEFORE the snapshot
that needs it. MSG_ReadDeltaPlayerstate calls
CL_GetPredictedPlayerInformationForServerTime during the parse, and h1-mod's ring
is only filled once process_predicted_data has run on an earlier chunk.

Resampled to 20 Hz (50 ms). The archives are per-client-frame (~85 Hz), far above
the rate a client expects snapshots at.

### VERIFIED OFFLINE — round-trip, not just "it parses"

`diag/roundtrip.py` decodes the poses back OUT of the emitted demo and compares
them with the CoD4 archives they came from. `verify_dm_h1.py` only proves each
snapshot parses; this proves the pose survives the encode.

    cod4_holymoly  746 snapshots, 0 unparseable
                   snapshot pose vs CoD4 archive : 746/746 within 1 unit (worst 0.000)
                   snapshot pose vs predicted_data: 746/746 agree
    cod4_r7quad    436 snapshots, same, worst 0.000

The pose-vs-predicted_data check is the one that matters: a disagreement there IS
the fight that killed the splice.

### ⚠ POSE_FIELDS NAMES ARE BACKWARDS (the data is fine)

    POSE_FIELDS: (32, 304, "delta_pitch"), (34, 300, "delta_yaw"), (39, 308, "delta_roll")

Offset 300 is delta_angles[0] = PITCH and 304 is [1] = YAW, so the key called
"delta_yaw" actually holds pitch and vice versa. `_pose_values` compensates
(`"delta_yaw": view_angles[0]`), so the ENCODED DATA IS CORRECT and only the label
misleads. Do not "fix" the names without also swapping `_pose_values`.

`viewHeight = 60` is written explicitly - the eye is `origin.z + viewHeight`, and
leaving it zero puts the camera inside floor geometry (the yellow-void symptom).

## ⭐⭐ THE FIELD, AND THE BUG — ps+0x394, 27 bits, MIXED bit/byte

`playerStateFields[47]` = offset 916 = **ps+0x394**, which h1-mod's own
`game::ps_held_weapon()` reads and hands to `CG_SelectWeapon(client, weapon, alt)`.
(It picks ps+0x388 instead when ps+0x398 & 0x2; we never write +0x398, so it
stays 0 and the +0x394 branch is taken.)

Its `type` column is **27** — a 27-bit default-codec field. And the default codec
is NOT a flat bit run. From MWR `sub_4F72E0` (reached from MSG_WriteDeltaField
@0x4F3B40's `default:`), transcribed verbatim:

    v9 = to ^ from;  if (bits != 32) v9 &= (1 << bits) - 1
    n = abs(bits);  rem = n & 7
    if (rem) { MSG_WriteBits(msg, v9, rem);  n -= rem;  v9 >>= rem; }
    for (; n; n -= 8) { MSG_WriteByte(msg, v9);  v9 >>= 8; }

MSG_WriteBits moves the BIT cursor, MSG_WriteByte the BYTE cursor — the same
dual-cursor msg_t already proven on the CoD4 side. `write_small_int` wrote all
`width` bits inline, so **for any width above 7 it emitted the wrong bytes**.

⭐ IT HAD NEVER BITTEN because the only default-codec field written so far was
view_height at 7 bits, where `rem == 7` and the byte loop never runs — the two
forms agree exactly. A latent bug that only appears the first time a wide field
is added, which is precisely what adding the weapon did.

FIXED: `write_default_field` / `read_default_field` in mwr/playerstate.py, with
the self-test round-tripping the 27-bit weapon at 1 / 80 / 0x7F / 0x1234 /
0x7FFFFFF so the 3-bit + 3-byte path is actually exercised.

## ⛔ THE KILLFEED IS AN ENTITY EVENT, NOT A SERVER COMMAND

Chased to the source rather than guessed. CoD4's whole server-command set decodes
cleanly (697/739 strings are clean text: chat with colour codes, `EXE_LEFTGAME`,
`MP_WAR_RADAR_EXPIRED`, scores) and **there is no obituary verb**. The two
candidates were both something else:

    'K' -> CL_ResetPlayerMuting        (CG_DeployServerCommand case 0x4B)
    'a' -> CG_SelectWeaponIndex        (case 0x61)

The only obituary references in the binary are `EV_OBITUARY` and the string
"CG_Obituary: target out of range", both inside **CG_EntityEvent @0x6ca60**. So
the killfeed rides the ENTITY stream.

MEASURED on holymoly with the current reader: 788 snapshots, **0% entity-
truncated**, and **672 ET_EVENTS(17) entities decode**. But the eType histogram
contains impossible values (58, 75, 255 — the dispatch clamps at 17), which
matches the standing finding that entity FRAMING is right while entity VALUES are
not. So the killfeed is blocked on entity value decoding, not on the MWR side.

## ⚠ "I'm on the floor" is NOT a missing viewheight

`view_height = 60` at offset 208 (type 7, 7 bits) is written and the round-trip
decodes it back as 60 on all 746 snapshots. So the floor-level camera is
something else and the next step is an A/B, not another field. Offset 208 being
viewheight is INFERRED from behaviour, never proven — MWR's ship build strips the
netfield names, and the PS4 debug build has a **271**-entry table against the PC
build's **252**, so indices do not line up and its names cannot be borrowed.

# ⭐⭐⭐ CoD4 OBITUARIES DECODED — THE KILLFEED IS REACHABLE TODAY (2026-08-18)

User: *"lets fix all of this so we can atleast see us walking and killfeed up just

That framing is right and it dissolves two blockers at once. Recorded below.

## ⛔ CORRECTION — "impossible" eTypes were EVENTS, not garbage

An earlier entry dismissed eType 58 / 75 / 255 as proof the entity VALUES were
broken, because the dispatch clamps at 17. Wrong. `G_TempEntity` @0x145970:

    v2 = G_Spawn();
    *(_DWORD *)(v2 + 4) = a2 + 17;      // eType = event + 17

That is the Q3 **ET_EVENTS + N** convention: an eType of 17 or more IS an event,
and `event = eType - 17`. The clamp exists precisely so every event type shares the
event netfield table. So a broad eType histogram above 17 is NORMAL.

## ⭐⭐ PROVEN — the obituary record, field by field

`GScr_Obituary` @0x12e9a0 builds a temp entity:

    v3 = G_TempEntity(vec3_origin, 66);          // 66 = EV_OBITUARY -> eType 83
    *(DWORD *)(v3 + 116) = victim;               // otherEntityNum
    *(DWORD *)(v3 + 120) = attacker;             // attackerEntityNum, 1022 = none
    *(BYTE  *)(v3 + 246) = 8;
    *(DWORD *)(v3 + 156) = (mod in {7,8,9,11,12,15}) ? (mod | 0x80)
                                                    : G_GetWeaponIndexForName(name);

and those three offsets are NAMED in the dumped entityStateFields:

    +116 otherEntityNum    +120 attackerEntityNum    +156 eventParm

So an obituary is fully specified: eType 83, victim, attacker, and either a weapon
index into cs[2258] or a meansOfDeath with bit 0x80 set.

    t+23.10s  10 -> 11  m40a3_mp             t+38.85s  10 -> 38  m40a3_mp

as ps.weapon, and holymoly's own held weapon (m40a3_acog_mp) appears as an obituary

# ⭐⭐⭐ CoD4 READER — THE DESYNC IS IN THE PLAYERSTATE, PROVEN BY ELIMINATION
# (2026-08-18)

User: *"lets decode the values/names and stuff, forget about a preview build for
now. Focus on making it so everything is readable in a cod4 demo"*.

Baseline, holymoly + out_vacantquad (2177 snapshot messages):

    EOF-terminated                 201/2177 =  9.2%
    reached the entity sentinel    529/2177 = 24.3%

## ⭐⭐ THE LOCALISATION — the FIRST entity of a failing snapshot is already bad

The decisive instrument: `lc` (lastChangedField) is a 6-bit read, and every
per-eType table has 58-60 fields, so **an lc of 60-63 is impossible** and proves
the reader is at the wrong bit. Bucketing snapshots by the largest lc they see:

    max lc <= 59   n=  548   reached sentinel 20-100%
    max lc == 60   n=  248   0.0%
    max lc == 61   n=  333   0.0%
    max lc == 62   n=  441   0.0%
    max lc == 63   n=  550   2.5%

72% of snapshots contain an impossible lc. And the set "entity read immediately
BEFORE the first impossible lc" is **EMPTY** - the bad lc is always on the FIRST
entity. Corroborated by the lc distribution over all entities being nearly
UNIFORM from 38 to 59 (204-506 each), which is what reading noise looks like; a
real distribution would be peaky.

**So the entity loop starts at the wrong bit. The playerstate is the fault.**

⚠ This CORRECTS the reading of an earlier probe in this file. "Snapshots that
decode 20+ entities succeed only 22.5%, so it is a rare codec deep in the list"
was wrong: the loop keeps running on garbage after the first bad entity, so a
high entity COUNT is a symptom of the desync, not evidence of where it began.

## VERIFIED CORRECT — do not re-audit these

  * **The field tables are byte-exact.** Re-dumped `entityStateFields` (0x40c920)
    and `playerStateFields` (0x40f480) from the IDB with the proven 16-byte layout
    `{const char* name; i32 offset; i32 bits; i32 changeHints}`:
    **0 mismatches out of 141 and 0 out of 59** against our JSON.
    changeHints: entity all 0; playerstate 126x0, 8x3, 6x2, 1x1.
  * **`read_entity_index`** - LABEL_15 is the FULL read ("Entity num: %i bits
    (full)"), reached when the second bit is SET; the delta branch is FOUR bits
    (blocks at 0x178c58/0x178cad/0x178d01/0x178d58). The engine's own
    "%i bits (delta)" string says 6 and is STALE.
  * **The default codec** - CoD4's own writer tail: `if (!*v32) WriteBit0;
    WriteBit1; v28 = from ^ to; rem = abs(bits) & 7; if (rem) WriteBits(v28, rem);
    for (...) WriteByte(v28)`. Mixed bit/byte, and unlike MWR there is NO
    `(1<<bits)-1` mask. Ours matches.
  * **lc is 6 bits LSB-first** - accumulated as `bit0 | 2*bit1 | 4*bit2 | 8*bit3 |
    16*bit4 | 32*bit5` in the disassembly.
  * **The changed bit is COMMON, not per-codec**, and gated on
    `changeHints != 2`: `if (field->changeHints != 2) { if (!zeroBase) {...if
    unchanged return WriteBit0...} WriteBit1; }` then the codec switch. Ours
    matches. (MWR is DIFFERENT here - it writes a field INDEX DELTA and only sends
    changed fields. Do not port MWR's scheme into the CoD4 reader.)

## RULED OUT BY MEASUREMENT — each with the number that killed it

  * **The playerstate baseline.** Forcing it to zero for every snapshot gives
    529/2177, IDENTICAL to as-is. Playerstate read length is baseline-independent.
  * **The entity baseline / carry-forward chain.** Forcing every entity to delta
    against the gamestate baseline gives 527 vs 529. No effect.
  * **Every tail section.** stats/ammo4/ammo8/objectives/hudelems/raw128 are
    entered in 85/147/105/18/22/14 of 2177 snapshots - they are six gate bits and
    nothing more, most of the time - and entering one IMPROVES the success rate
    (e.g. stats 44.7% entered vs 23.5% skipped). None is a suspect.
  * **Any single playerstate codec.** Conditional success rates are FLAT at
    21-29% against a 24.3% base. ⚠ NOTE THE HOLE IN THAT METHOD: a codec used by
    EVERY snapshot has no contrast and cannot be blamed this way, so this rules
    out the rare codecs, not the universal ones.
  * `_HUDELEMS_ENABLED` and codecs -85/-99 - all present and correct; the comment
    in the code claiming they were missing was stale and is fixed.

## ⭐ ONE REAL DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED (behind a flag)

`MSG_ReadDeltaEntity`:

    if ( StateFieldListForEntityType[1] >= v49 )   // fieldCount >= lc
    { ...read fields 1..lc-1...; copy the rest; return 0; }
    else { *a1 = 1; return 0; }                    // OVERFLOW

**A per-eType table smaller than lc is a hard overflow; we silently `break`.**
Tables are not uniform (helicopter 58, most 59, plane 60) and lc is 6 bits, so it
can legitimately exceed the table.

Honouring it drops EOF-termination 9.2% -> 2.0%, because it converts "limp along"
into "abort" and lc only exceeds the table when the stream is ALREADY wrong.
Shipped as `_STRICT_FIELDCOUNT`, default **False**, so the reader still salvages
what it can. Turning it on measures the true damage.

⚠ SELF-INFLICTED, CAUGHT BY THE METRIC: my first version of that edit deleted the
`if i >= len(fields): break` bounds check, so `fields[i]` raised IndexError and
EOF fell to 3.0%. The metric caught it in one run. **Re-run eofcheck after every
edit to the reader** - it is 30 seconds and it is the only thing that can tell an
improvement from a regression.

## WHERE TO GO NEXT

The playerstate reads the right fields, from byte-exact tables, with a verified
common changed bit and a verified default codec - and still desyncs. What is NOT
yet verified is the individual NEGATIVE codecs against CoD4's own writer:

    -85 -86 -87 -88 -89 -90 -91 -92 -93 -94 -95 -96 -97 -98 -99 -100 and 0

Only the DEFAULT case was checked this session. `re/cod4/write_field.c` holds the
whole switch and each case is a handful of lines; the ones used by nearly every
playerstate (-97 commandTime, -92/-91/-90 coordinates, 0) are the ones the
correlation method structurally cannot blame, so they are the priority.

Note two CoD4-vs-MWR traps already seen: the coordinate codec's small-delta case
is **7 bits, not 6**, and `bits == 0` writes a SECOND bit on its zero path.

## Instruments added (re-usable, all offline)

    diag/entblame.py    last field read before the first non-monotonic entity index
    diag/tailblame.py   per-tail-section success rate, entered vs skipped

# CoD4 READER — THE PLAYERSTATE IS EXONERATED. Full audit, and what is left.
# (2026-08-18, continued)

## ⛔ CORRECTION — "the desync is in the playerstate" was too broad

The previous entry concluded the playerstate was at fault because the first entity
index is already garbage. **Dumping the decoded values of FAILING snapshots shows
the playerstate is CORRECT:**

    FAILING snapshot seq=4450 serverTime=906472100
       commandTime        906471700     (serverTime - 400, plausible)
       origin           4636.0, -816.0, -127.875     (real mp_citystreets coords)
       viewangles[1]      150.002
       viewHeightCurrent   60.000       viewHeightTarget 60
       weapon                  88       (= m40a3_acog_mp, matches cs[2258])
       clientNum               41       pm_type 0 (alive)

So the field loop decodes the right VALUES and still ends at the wrong PLACE.

## AUDITED AGAINST THE ENGINE THIS SESSION — all correct, do not re-check

  * **All 17 codecs** vs `MSG_WriteDeltaField`'s switch (re/cod4/write_field.c):
    0, -85, -86, -87, -88, -89, -90/-91/-92, -93/-94, -95, -96, -97, -98, -99,
    -100 and the default. Spot-checks that matter: `-87` is a bare Angle16 = TWO
    BYTES on the byte cursor (MSG_WriteAngle16 @0x176f30 does
    `*(WORD*)(data+cursize) = ...; cursize += 2`); `bits == 0` really does write a
    SECOND bit on its zero path; `-98` is 3 BYTES or a 5-bit bit-index; `-96` is
    1022/0/2-bits+byte; `-95` is 7 bits x100; the coordinate small delta is 7 bits.
  * **The changed bit is COMMON and gated on `changeHints != 2`**, written by
    MSG_WriteDeltaField, plus the caller's own `MSG_WriteBit0` for an unchanged
    field. One bit per field either way. Ours matches.
  * **The playerstate head**: predicted bit, then lc at
    `GetMinBitCountForNum(0x8D)` = 8 bits, LSB-first (`v217 |= bit << i`). Ours
    matches, and `read_bits` is LSB-first.
  * **All SIX tail sections** vs the writer's tail: stats(5-bit mask),
    ammo(4 groups), ammoclip(8 groups), objectives(16), hudelems(2 x
    MSG_WriteDeltaHudElems(...,31)), then `[bit] + 128 raw bytes` at ps+2076
    (`memcmp(..., 0x80)` then a byte + `for (kk=1; kk!=128; ++kk)`). Exactly six
    gate bits. Ours matches.
  * **Nothing is read between the playerstate and the entity loop** -
    CL_ParseSnapshot does only `MSG_ClearLastReferencedEntity` and sets up the
    old-entity walk. The loop is gated `while (!msg->overflowed)`.
  * **`read_bit` implements the dual cursor correctly** (resync
    `bit = 8*readcount; ++readcount` when `(bit & 7) == 0`).

## ⭐ THE BOUNDARY IS NOT OFF BY A FIXED AMOUNT — measured

`diag/boundary.py` scans BOTH cursors (bit -8..+8 x readcount -3..+24) at the
tail/entity boundary and scores each by the monotonic index chain:

    788 snapshots, only 173 found ANY offset reaching the 1023 sentinel
    best offset is scattered - the most common is bit+8/readcount+0 at 1.8%

So there is no single missing read. The error is VARIABLE per snapshot, which
means a DATA-DEPENDENT length is wrong somewhere - not a constant-size section.

## ⭐ THE LEADING HYPOTHESIS, and the measurement that argues against it

`MSG_WriteDeltaPlayerstate`'s field loop **breaks at the first field whose
changeHints == 2**:

    for ( j = &playerStateFields; ; j += 16 ) {
        v11 = j[12];
        if ( v11 == 2 ) break;              // <-- STOPS HERE
        ...
        MSG_WriteBit0(a2);
        if ( ++v49 == v51 ) goto LABEL_47;  // v51 = lc
    }

The first such field is **index 71, `viewHeightLerpDown`** (the six are 71, 76,
77, 90, 91, 94). But the lc-COMPUTING loop above it (`for (i = 1; i != 142; ++i)`)
walks all 141 fields and has NO changeHints==2 check, so it can produce lc > 71.
And `MSG_ReadDeltaPlayerstate`'s own loop reads exactly lc fields with no break:

    while (1) { MSG_ReadDeltaField(...); if (++v181 == v217) break; v49 += 4; }

If lc > 71 the writer wrote 71 fields and the reader reads lc - a variable
overrun, which is exactly the signature above (right values for the early fields,
wrong end position, no fixed boundary offset).

⚠ BUT THE MEASUREMENT DOES NOT SUPPORT IT: bucketing snapshots by their
playerstate lc gives `lc<=71` 22.9% success (n=1583) and `lc 72-141` 28.1%
(n=594). If overrunning were fatal, lc>71 would be near 0%. **Unresolved
contradiction - do not act on this until it is explained.**

## What is NOT yet audited

  * `MSG_ReadDeltaField`'s own reader-side decompile (only the WRITER was used).
    The writer is the readable side, but the reader may differ - and CoD4's reader
    has every accessor inlined, which is exactly where a transcription slip hides.
  * `GetMinBitCountForNum` is inlined in the reader as a CLZ chain; only its
    result for 141 (= 8) was hand-checked.

## ⭐ THE CHEAPEST REAL ORACLE, NOT YET USED

The CoD4 client has `cl_shownet` and `msg_dumpEnts` built in, and
MSG_ReadDeltaEntity prints `"%3i: changed ent, eType %s"` and
MSG_ReadEntityIndex prints `"Read entity num %i"`. **Playing one of these demos in

entity numbers and field counts**, which turns every guess above into a diff.
That is worth more than any further static analysis and needs the game, not the
IDB.

    ------------------

CONFIRMED by this log - do NOT "fix" the reader to match them:
  * `"Entity num: %i bits (full)"` prints **bits + 2**, so a 10-bit read prints 12.
  * `"Entity num: %i bits (delta)"` prints a hardcoded **6** while the code reads 4.

## ⭐⭐⭐ PROVEN — the field loop and EVERY codec are BIT-EXACT

Comparing the engine's printed field values against ours, field by field:

    snapshot 0:  58 match / 0 differ   (of 58 the engine printed)
    snapshot 1:  44 match / 0 differ
    snapshot 2:  16 match / 15 differ  <- deltas against snapshot 1, whose TAIL we truncated

    engine last field   weaponold[1](105) deltaTime(109) deltaTime(109) weaponold[2](121) ... velocity[2](19)
    => lc should be     106  110  110  122  122  20
    our lc              106  110  110  122  122  20      ALL SIX EXACT

The engine's printed field ORDER is also a clean subsequence of our table order
(eventSequence, legsAnim, weaponTime, torsoTimer, weapAnim, weaponstate,
events[0..3], ...), confirming the table order as well as its contents.

**So: the head, lc, field order, the changed-bit, and all 17 codecs are correct.**

## ⭐⭐⭐ THE BUG — WE READ A THIRD OF THE PLAYERSTATE, AND THE REST IS THE TAIL

    #   engine ps span   our ps span    engine changed fields
    0   6 -> 732 = 726     294                58
    1  84 -> 938 = 854     149                44
    2  88 -> 545 = 457     139                31
    3  93 -> 422 = 329     112                21
    5 182 -> 233 =  51      29                 6

~58 changed fields cannot be 726 bytes; the fields are roughly 240 bytes and the
remaining ~490 is the TAIL. Our tail walk on snapshot 0:

    after_fields    byte=152 bit=1180
    stats  gate=1   -> done byte=158
    ammo4  gate=1   -> done byte=163      <-- FOUR bytes for the whole PS_AMMO
    ammo8  gate=0
    obj    gate=0
    hud    gate=1   -> done byte=172
    raw    gate=1   -> done byte=301      ENGINE ENDS AT 732

On the FIRST snapshot everything has changed, so PS_AMMO and PS_AMMOCLIP must be
fully populated (4x16 and 8x16 shorts = 128 + 256 bytes). We consume 4 bytes for
ammo and skip ammoclip entirely.

⛔ THIS RETIRES `diag/tailblame.py`'s conclusion. It reported the tail sections as
entered in only 4-7% of snapshots and therefore "not a suspect" - but it was
measuring OUR OWN broken gate reads, not reality. **A correlation probe over a
desynced stream measures the desync, not the cause.** The engine trace was the
only thing that could see this.

## Where exactly to look next

The field loop ends bit-exact, so the FIRST tail gate is at the right bit and
`PS_STATS` is entered correctly. The divergence begins at or inside PS_STATS /
PS_AMMO. Both were checked against `MSG_WriteDeltaPlayerstate` and LOOK right:

    PS_STATS   [bit] 5-bit mask, then &1 short &2 short &4 short &8 6bits &0x10 byte
    PS_AMMO    [bit] then 4 groups of { [bit] -> u16 mask + one short per set bit }
    PS_AMMOCLIP same, 8 groups

so the error is subtler than the shape - candidates: the mask is not a byte-cursor
`short`, the per-group gate is not one bit, or the group count is not fixed (the
READER's ammo section is a `while(1)` at read_ps.c:758 where the WRITER uses
`for (k = 1; k != 5; ++k)`).

# ⭐ FIXED — THE PHANTOM PS_AMMOCLIP GATE BIT (2026-08-18)

The `cl_shownet 4` capture named it. The engine prints `"PS_AMMOCLIP"` **once per
PRESENT group** (the Com_Printf is INSIDE the 8-group loop), so the log reads:

    snap 0: ... weaponold[1]:0 PS_STATS PS_AMMO PS_AMMOCLIP PS_AMMOCLIP 732:packet entities
    snap 2: ... deltaTime:0    PS_STATS PS_AMMO PS_AMMOCLIP x3          545:packet entities

i.e. the engine entered two/three clip groups on snapshots where our reader read
its outer gate as 0 and skipped the section entirely.

## PROVEN from MSG_WriteDeltaPlayerstate — the two sections are NOT symmetric

    if ( v66[0]||v66[1]||v66[2]||v66[3] ) {      <- PS_AMMO: OUTER GATE
        MSG_WriteBit1(a2);
        ...4 groups, each { [bit] -> u16 mask + one short per set bit } ...
    } else MSG_WriteBit0(a2);
    LABEL_103:
    for ( n = 0; n != 128; n += 16 ) { ... }     <- PS_AMMOCLIP: NO OUTER GATE

The 8-group clip loop runs UNCONDITIONALLY; only each group carries its own bit.
We read a gate that is not there - one bit - and every section after it was then
read at the wrong offset.

    fixed: `_skip_ps_ammo(msg, groups=8)` is now called with NO preceding read_bit()

MEASURED on snapshot 0 (engine's playerstate ends at byte 732):

    before  after_fields=152  stats=158  ammo4=163  ammo8 gate=0  hud=172  raw -> 301
    after   after_fields=152  stats=158  ammo4=163  ammoclip=172  hud=623  raw -> 624

301 -> 624 against the engine's 732. Corpus EOF-termination 9.23% -> 9.55%.

## ⚠ NOT DONE — snapshots 1 and 2 barely moved

    snap 1  ours 235   engine 938
    snap 2  ours 229   engine 545

Their PS_AMMOCLIP consumes 3 and 2 bytes where the engine has 2 present groups
(>= 8 bytes), so the per-group encoding inside AMMOCLIP is still wrong even though
the outer gate is now right. PS_AMMO's group loop was re-read in full and OURS
MATCHES IT EXACTLY:

    v22 = mask[i]; if (!v22) { WriteBit0; next; }
    WriteBit1; WriteShort(v22); for (m=0..15) if (mask>>m & 1) WriteShort(value)

so the difference is inside the CLIP group loop specifically - read
write_ps.c:357-430 (the `for (n = 0; n != 128; n += 16)` body) field by field
next. Note it builds its mask with `BYTE1(v27) = BYTE1(v25) | 1` style writes,
which is NOT the plain `v25 |= bit` shape PS_AMMO uses, so the mask may not be a
plain 16-bit short.

# (2026-08-18, continued)

## FIX 1 — the phantom PS_AMMOCLIP gate (see the entry above)

## ⭐ FIX 2 — the ammo mask was read SIGNED, with -1 doubling as the error code

    def read_short(self):                       # iw3/bitbuf.py
        if self._readcount + 2 > len(self._data):
            self.overflow = True
            return -1                           # <- failure sentinel
        return struct.unpack_from("<h", ...)     # <- SIGNED

and `_skip_ps_ammo` did `mask = msg.read_short(); if mask < 0: overflow; return`.

**Any PS_AMMO / PS_AMMOCLIP mask with slot 15 set comes back negative and aborted
the entire playerstate.** Measured on holymoly snapshot 1: `clip[0] mask=0x8010`.
A legitimate 0xFFFF is also indistinguishable from the failure sentinel.

Added `BitReader.read_ushort()` and switched the mask to it, with failure tested
via `msg.overflow`. **This is RULE A17's value/error conflation in a new place:
an in-band sentinel on a function whose valid range includes it.** Audit the
others - `read_long()` is signed too and `_c_88` / `_c_97` / `_c_99` all do
`if raw == -1: return`, which silently drops a legitimate 0xFFFFFFFF.

## MEASURED — the playerstate is now close, and the sections MATCH

    snapshot 0   engine ends 732     ours 301 -> 624
    snapshot 1   engine ends 938     ours 235 -> 789

and the section pattern is now IDENTICAL to the engine's cl_shownet 4 trace:

playerstate is far closer but the residual ~110-150 bytes still lands the entity
loop mid-stream, so the end-to-end metric cannot move until it is zero.

## WHERE THE REMAINING ~110 BYTES ARE — OBJ / HUD / RAW

After CLIP we are at byte 172 and the engine ends at 732, so OBJ+HUD+RAW = 560.
We read OBJ gate=0, HUD 451 bytes, RAW gate=0 -> 452. The trace:

    OBJ(0)  byte=172
    HUD gate=1
      hudA: count=2   elem0 lc=23 (20B)  elem1 lc=23 (25B)   -> 219
      hudB: count=31  elem0 lc=63 (40B)  ...                 -> 623
    RAW gate=0

⭐ `hudB count=31` is the MAXIMUM a 5-bit count can hold and `elem0 lc=63` is the
MAXIMUM a 6-bit lc can hold - both are garbage signatures. So hudB is already
reading noise, and the divergence is in **hudA or just before it**.

Arithmetic that fits: RAW=128 and OBJ≈8 would leave HUD≈424, against the 451 we
read - i.e. hudA/hudB over-consume by ~27 bytes.

# ⭐⭐⭐ CoD4 READER — THE ENGINE'S OWN GAMESTATE TRACE IS EXACT GROUND TRUTH
# (2026-08-18). Playerstate 92% exact; ONE codec left.

## ⛔ FIRST — THE METRIC I HAD BEEN USING WAS WORTHLESS

`entities_truncated` counted only the cases where an EXCEPTION was raised. Removing
the exceptions removed the signal, not the defect — a DESYNCED parse also consumes
the whole buffer. The previous session's headline ("99.5% truncation -> 0.0%, THE
STREAM NOW PARSES") is WITHDRAWN on that basis.

**THE RIGHT METRIC: does each stage END where the engine says it does.**
`cl_shownet 2` prints, per snapshot message, `NNN:playerstate`, `NNN:packet
entities`, `NNN:packet clients`, `NNN:END OF MESSAGE`, each as `readcount - 1`. So a
correct read is `ours == engine + 1`, per stage, per snapshot — pass/fail that
cannot be faked.

    diag/sections.py <console_mp.log> <demo.dm_1>

    playerstate end correct : 368/400  (92.0%)
    entity section end      :  32/400  ( 8.0%)
    client section end      :  33/400  ( 8.2%)
    first stage to fail: playerstate 32, entities 337, ok 30

**The playerstate is essentially solved. The entity decoder is the whole remaining
problem**, and it is the same decoder the gamestate baselines use.

## ⭐⭐⭐ 118 EXACT OFFSETS — the best test bed in the project

`msg_dumpEnts` output is not needed. With `cl_shownet >= 2`, MSG_ReadDeltaEntity
itself prints `Com_Printf(16, "%3i: #%-3i ", a1[7], ...)` **before field 0**, so each
number is the record's exact POST-HEADER readcount. holymoly's gamestate emits
**118** of them, 33164..35247, and the block's terminator (`07` + clientNum +
checksumFeed + `07`) sits at 35272.

⚠ Do NOT read the printed VALUES as field values. Only 6 print sites exist in
MSG_ReadDeltaField and the raw path prints `result`, which is loop residue — hence
`eType:0`, `index:0`, `partBits[0]:0` on records whose real values are 6, 7, 9258.
**The field NAMES are meaningful (a printing codec prints only when CHANGED); the
numbers are not.**

Printing codecs: positive widths (`%i`) and the origin floats -92/-91/-90 (`%f`).
-100, -93, -94, -97, -98 and bits==0 do NOT print.

## PROVEN by those 118 — what is RIGHT, and must not be re-investigated

  * **Baselines 1-5 land byte-exact** (33164/33182/33210/33234/33253/33280), and
    their decoded values match the engine's printed floats exactly
    (trBase 5384/68/-128 and 5389/1035/-14).
  * **The eType dispatch is right.** The engine printed `partBits[1]` for record 6,
    and of all 25 tables ONLY eType 6 (scriptMover) has partBits[1] inside the first
    24 fields. Our decode picks 6.
  * **lc is right.** 6 bits; last changed field is partBits[1] at f23 -> lc 24, which
    is what we read. Forcing lc over 1..59 lands NOTHING.
  * **MSG_ReadEntityIndex is right**, re-verified instruction by instruction:
    bit1 set -> ++last; else if bits==10 { bit2 set -> FULL, clear -> +4-bit delta };
    full read is `a2` bits LSB-first, assigned absolutely. The engine's own
    "(delta)" string prints a stale 6 while the code reads 4.
  * **changeHints is handled** (`if (*(BYTE*)(a6+12) != 2)` gates the changed bit).
    NO entity field has changeHints 2; six PLAYER fields do, and our tables carry
    them correctly in `NetField.flags`.
  * **The delta-baseline ring is right** — 553/555 resolve, and FULL snapshots
    (delta_num == 0) fail too, so the ring is not the entity problem.

## RULED OUT by variant sweeps against the 118 (do not retry)

    default codec without the zero-flag        WORSE (1 record)
    -100 without the zero-flag / inverted      WORSE (2 / 1)
    bits==0 full path without its leading bit  no change
    bits==0 small path at 6 bits               no change
    -97 as zeroflag+long                       no change
    -93/-94 as zeroflag+byte / xor / 2 bytes   no change
    every eType table for record 6             none lands

`-93` (20.0%) and `-94` (13.0%) top the per-codec failure ranking against a 6.8%
base rate, but replacing them changes NOTHING — that is correlation from
co-occurrence, exactly the caveat the blame tool prints about itself.

## WHERE THE BUG IS, precisely

Record 6 needs **+47 bits** after its field loop; records 1-5 need 0. The bytes it
fails to consume are `00 00 00 00 48 92` at 33299..33304, with the next `3` at
33305. The engine printed `partBits[0]` and `partBits[1]` for that record — and a
raw-path field prints ONLY when changed — so **both are CHANGED and we read them as
UNCHANGED**. Reading both as changed+nonzero is +66 bits, so that alone is not the
answer either: something between f8 and f12 (`-100`, or bits==0) is already a bit
out by then, and the injection search finds no single insertion point before f24
that repairs it.

## SHIPPED — a labelled RESYNC, not a fix

`_resync_baseline` in iw3/snapshot.py. When the gamestate loop lands on a byte that
is not a sub-opcode, scan forward for the next byte that can genuinely START a
baseline, using the engine's own invariants: sub-opcode 3, an index strictly greater
than the last and below 1024, and a body that decodes without overrunning.

    gamestate baselines recovered:  6  ->  117 of the engine's 118
    header-exact against the engine: 117/118
    records ending cleanly on the next `3`: 109/118 (92.4%)

It is explicitly a symptom patch and says so in its own comment. It did NOT move the
snapshot metric (7.5% -> 8.0%), which is itself informative: the baselines were
never the snapshot bottleneck — the same codec breaks both.

## SECOND PASS ON THE ENTITY CODEC (same day) — TWO REAL FIXES, ROOT CAUSE STILL OPEN

### ⭐ FOUND — CL_ParseGamestate does not exist; it is INSIDE CL_ParseServerMessage

`MSG_ReadDeltaEntity` @0x17cd20 has exactly three callers: CL_ParseSnapshot (x2)
and **CL_ParseServerMessage @0xc5d10** — the gamestate baselines are parsed there,
not in a separate function. Decompile saved to `re/cod4/parse_servermessage.c`. Its
loop matches ours exactly:

    while (1) {
        v8 = MSG_ReadByte(msg);
        if (v8 == 7) break;
        while (v8 != 2) {
            if (v8 != 3) { Com_PrintError("CL_ParseGamestate: bad command byte %d"); }
            idx = MSG_ReadEntityIndex(msg, 10);
            if (idx > 0x3FF) Com_Error("Baseline number out of range: %i");
            memset(from, 0, 244);
            MSG_ReadDeltaEntity(msg, 0, from, &entityBaselines[idx], idx);
            v8 = MSG_ReadByte(msg);
            if (v8 == 7) goto done;
        }
        Short = MSG_ReadShort(msg);   // the configstring batch
        ...
    }

The engine never printed "bad command byte" in the capture, so it parsed all 118.

### ⭐ FIXED — the configstring running index starts at MINUS ONE

    Bits = -1;
    do { if (MSG_ReadBit(msg)) ++Bits; else Bits = MSG_ReadBits(msg, 12); ... }

Ours started at 0, so the first string — encoded as a delta from -1, i.e. index 0 —
landed at index 1, and every later delta inherited the shift until an explicit
12-bit index reset it. Bit consumption is identical, so it never desynced; it
silently mislabelled configstrings. `map_center` (cs[12]) now reads
[3226.0, -408.0, -36.0] instead of a neighbouring string, and cs[2258] still
resolves token[34] = remington700_mp / token[87] = m40a3_acog_mp.

### ⭐ FIXED — MSG_ReadAngle16 is SIGNED

The engine builds it in a variable declared `__int16` and then converts, so an
angle above 180 comes back NEGATIVE. We read it unsigned (0..360). Two bytes either
way, so this never desynced — it mis-signed every angle over 180.

### ⭐ NOTED, NOT IMPLEMENTED — `constantConfigStrings`

The engine keeps a table of CONSTANT configstrings and memcpy's them in at fixed
indices during the batch, so the wire carries only the rest. It consumes no bits,
but it means our configstring map is missing those entries entirely.

### VERIFIED BYTE-EXACT AGAINST THE IDB THIS PASS (do not re-check)

  * `scriptMoverStateFields` (s_netFieldList[6] = 0x40dfa0, 59 fields): all 26
    leading entries match name/offset/bits/changeHints with ZERO mismatches.
  * `s_netFieldList` @0x410040 — 18 entries; eTypes 5,10,11,15,16 alias the generic
    table 0x40c920; counts are 58 (helicopter), 60 (plane), 59 for the rest.
  * `MSG_ReadByte` @0x176840 — reads data[readcount], readcount++, does NOT touch
    the bit cursor.
  * `MSG_ReadBits` @0x176630 — per-bit resync when (bit & 7) == 0, LSB-first.
  * our `_c_default` reads the remainder on the BIT cursor and the whole bytes with
    read_byte, matching the writer's WriteBits/WriteByte split.

### ⛔ THE REMAINING DEFECT, NARROWED TO A CONTRADICTION

Records 5 and 6 are the same eType, the same lc (24, from identical lcbits
[0,0,0,1,1,0]), and cost IDENTICALLY for fields f0..f19. They diverge only at
f20/f22/f23:

    record 5 (works):  f20 = 2 bits + 4 bytes   f22 = 1 bit    f23 = 2 bits + 4 bytes
    record 6 (fails):  f20 = 1 bit              f22 = 2 bits   f23 = 1 bit

The engine's dump proves f20 and f23 are CHANGED in record 6 (raw-path fields print
only when changed). Record 6 must end at 33305 — six bytes past our 33299 — and the
unread bytes are `00 00 00 00 48 92`.

Four ZERO bytes cannot be a raw-path value: the baseline is memset to zero, so
new == old would write changed=0 and new != 0 would XOR to something non-zero. So
those bytes must be consumed by BIT reads, which needs ~32 more flag bits than
lc=24 leaves. Every attempt to reconcile that failed:

    sweep the eType table                     only eType 6 has partBits[1] < f24
    sweep lc 1..60                            56/57/58 end at 33305 but the stream
                                              says 24, and 2/3/5/7 read 24 and work
    sweep table x lc together                 32 candidates, all end at 33305
    sweep the BIT cursor -16..+16 at entry    only +0 gives the engine's post-header
    inject N bits before each field           nothing before f24 repairs it

Per the Contradiction Rule this is left OPEN rather than patched around. The
`_resync_baseline` workaround (117/118 baselines) stands, labelled as such.

## THREE REAL FIXES THE SOURCE HANDED OVER IMMEDIATELY

  1. **The default codec masks the baseline and sign-extends.**

         value = rawValue ^ (mask & *fromF);          // mask = (1<<bits)-1, or -1
         if (sgn && (value & (1 << (bits-1)))) value |= ~mask;

     We XORed the UNMASKED baseline and never sign-extended, so -8/-16 fields came

  2. **MSG_ReadAngle16 is SIGNED.** `return MSG_ReadShort(msg) * 0.0054931640625`
     and MSG_ReadShort returns a `__int16`. We read it unsigned, mis-signing every
     angle over 180 degrees.

  3. **The configstring index starts at -1** (`lastStringIndex = -1`), which was
     already fixed from the decompile the same day and is now confirmed by source.

All three are VALUE bugs; none changes bit consumption.

## ⭐ constantConfigStrings — a whole mechanism we do not implement

CL_ParseGamestate keeps a table of CONSTANT configstrings and memcpy's them into
the gamestate at fixed indices as the wire indices pass them, plus a flush loop
after the batch. The wire carries only the rest. It consumes no bits, so it never
desyncs -- but our configstring map is simply missing those entries.

                          own "(delta)" printf really does say 6 while reading 4

    MSG_ReadLastChangedField(msg, 61)  and GetMinBitCountForNum(n) == n.bit_length()

    MSG_ReadOriginFloat   [bit] ? 16 bits + mapCenter : 7 bits - 64 + old
    MSG_ReadOriginZFloat  same shape on axis 2
    MSG_Read24BitFlag     [bit] ? 3 bytes : 5-bit index XORed into old
