# ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ THE CoD4 READER IS BIT-EXACT. ROOT CAUSE = A HUFFMAN TIE-BREAK.
# (2026-08-18)

    metric (holymoly, 400 snapshots vs the engine's own cl_shownet offsets)
                                 before      after
    playerstate end correct      92.0%       100.0%
    entity section end            8.0%       100.0%
    client section end            8.2%       100.0%
    ALL THREE                     7.5%       100.0%

    gamestate baselines vs msg_dumpEnts:  117/118 header-exact -> 118/118
                                          109/118 clean end    -> 117/118

## ⭐ THE ROOT CAUSE — C's qsort IS NOT STABLE, Python's sort IS

`Huff_BuildFromData` (KisakCOD src/qcommon/huffman.cpp) builds the static tree by
repeatedly `qsort`ing the live node window by weight and merging the two lowest.
**qsort is not stable.** Our port used Python's `sort`, which is.

msg_hData has only two tied weight pairs and the merge hits exactly ONE ambiguous
round -- but that one round is enough to build a DIFFERENT-BUT-VALID tree: same
code lengths, a couple of same-depth leaves swapped. Most bytes then decode
correctly and a few do not.

**That is why the failure looked impossible.** Every codec, table, primitive and
loop was verified byte-exact against the source, the cursor arithmetic was right,
and records either side of a failure landed on the engine's own offsets -- because
the DECODER was never wrong. The DATA was, in a handful of scattered bytes.

Fix, in `iw3/huffman.py`, measured against the 118 engine-verified baselines:

    window = sorted(heap[heap_head:], key=lambda n: n.weight)
    if len(window) >= 3 and window[1].weight == window[2].weight:
        window[1], window[2] = window[2], window[1]     # the engine takes the LATER one

## ⛔ LESSON — I CHASED THE DECODER FOR TWO SESSIONS

Every instrument said "the decoder matches and the data is short". I kept reading
that as "some codec must still be wrong" instead of "then the data is wrong".
**When exhaustive verification says the consumer is correct, suspect the
PRODUCER.** The decompression sits upstream of everything and was never on the
suspect list.

The user's prompt to use the actual CoD4 source (KisakCOD) is what closed it: not
because the codec list was wrong, but because having the source let me EXCLUDE the
decoder quickly enough to look upstream.

## TWO MORE REAL BUGS FIXED ON THE WAY

  * **The client section was not merged.** CL_ParsePacketClients is the same Q3
    merge as entities (carry over old clients below newnum; delta from the OLD
    FRAME when oldnum == newnum; a ZEROED dummy otherwise; carry the tail). We used
    a persistent per-client store and never carried clients forward, so a frame
    listed only the clients that packet mentioned and the roster went blank after
    the first snapshot.
  * **cod4_sidecar.py never collected a name.** `frame["clients"]` is a DICT, so
    `for cl in frame["clients"]` yields the KEYS and `isinstance(cl, dict)` was
    never true; the summary key is `clientNum`, not `number`. Two bugs in four
    lines hid a roster the decoder already had.

# ⭐⭐⭐ CoD4 KILLFEED REPLAY IN MWR — SHIPPED (2026-08-18)

Built and deployed (h1-mod.exe md5 bb6a5d9a...). NOT yet run in game, so per the
Fix Declaration Rules this is a CANDIDATE.

## The pieces

    tools/cod4_to_h1/cod4_sidecar.py     offline: .dm_1 -> <demo>.cod4.json
    h1-mod src/client/component/demo/cod4_feed.cpp   in-game: sidecar -> killfeed
    killfeed.hpp/.cpp  +  push_external() and clear()

## Why a sidecar at all

A .dm_1 carries obituaries as ENTITY EVENTS -- a temp entity with
eType = ET_EVENTS + EV_OBITUARY (17 + 66 = 83) carrying otherEntityNum (victim),
attackerEntityNum and eventParm (a weapon index, or a meansOfDeath with bit 0x80).
G_TempEntity sets `eType = event + 17`.

MWR never sees any of it -- the demo it plays is a transcode -- so the existing
LUI_Obituary hook has nothing to capture. The kills are decoded OFFLINE and pushed
into the same custom feed on the DEMO clock (cl->serverTime), which is what
killfeed.cpp already fades on, so slow-mo and avidemo carry the feed for free.

## Usage

    cod4_feed <demo>.cod4.json     arm  (arm BEFORE demoplay so t=0 lines up)
    cod4_feed off                  disarm
    cod4_feed                      status
    killfeed_custom                already defaults to TRUE; nothing to enable

Deployed for testing:
    demos/client/auto/cod4_holymoly.dm_h1  +  cod4_holymoly.cod4.json
    50-name roster, 70 kills, first at +1.05s

## Design notes

  * Timing anchors on the first tick after arming and re-anchors (and clears the
    feed) on a BACKWARDS serverTime jump, so a restart or a backward seek does not
    replay kills the viewer already scrubbed past.
  * A slot with no decoded name renders as `[12]`, never blank -- a missing name
    must look missing.
  * The icon is passed NULL. killfeed's draw already guards `if (e.icon)`, and
    MWR's weapon-icon material name for a CoD4 weapon is not established; guessing
    one would render a checkerboard. That is the next piece if icons are wanted.

## ⚠ ONE SELF-INFLICTED BUILD ERROR WORTH REMEMBERING

killfeed.hpp first forward-declared `namespace game { struct Material; }` to avoid
including the game headers. The real type is `database::Material` (game::Material
is an alias), so the forward declaration created a SECOND, incomplete type that
shadowed it and broke `R_AddCmdDrawStretchPic` at an EXISTING call site.

**RULE: never forward-declare a type that already exists behind an alias.** Use an
opaque `void*` in the public header and cast inside the .cpp, which is what shipped.

## Build

    tools/premake5.exe vs2022          <- REQUIRED after adding a .cpp
    MSBuild at "C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\18\Insiders\MSBuild\..."
    (NOT the 2026/Insiders path recorded elsewhere -- the folder is "18")

## KILLFEED CONFIRMED IN GAME; WEAPON ICONS WIRED (2026-08-18)

USER: *"it is printing a feed, but it's missing the weapon icon... we're also
missing our player model and gun too cos they also will have different names"*

So the feed itself WORKS. Both remaining gaps are the same problem: a CoD4 weapon
name means nothing to MWR.

### ⭐ BG_KillIcon LOCATED — the engine hands us the exact icon

From the MWR-PS4 NAMED idb, `BG_KillIcon` is a three-instruction thunk:

    movzx esi, sil ; mov edx, 0A28h ; jmp BG_GetWeaponFieldMaterial

i.e. it is nothing but weapon field **0xA28 (killIcon)** -- the sibling of
killIconRatio at 0xA40 that `BG_KillIconRatio` reads, and of
hudProximityWarningIcon at 0xA38.

Ported to the PC dump by byte-searching the **Win64** form of that immediate
(`41 B8 28 0A 00 00` = `mov r8d, 0A28h`; the PS4 System V form `BA 28 0A 00 00`
does NOT appear, because the third argument moves from rdx to r8). Exactly ONE
match: a 20-byte function at **0x2E7330** whose body is
`mov r8d, 0A28h ; call BG_GetWeaponFieldMaterial (0x2E17D0)`.

Verified the IDB uses h1-mod's own `_b` convention before trusting it: 0x2E2500
and 0x26E6F0 are function starts and are exactly what h1-mod already calls
BG_GetWeaponNameComplete and LUI_Obituary.

    WEAK symbol<Material*(unsigned int weapon, bool isAlternate)>
        BG_KillIcon{0x0, 0x2E7330};

### The name -> index resolver ASKS THE ENGINE, it does not ship a table

`cod4_feed.cpp` builds the reverse map once by walking weapon indices 1..2047 and
calling `BG_GetWeaponNameComplete(i, false, ...)`. A CoD4 name is then looked up as
`h1_<name>` first, then bare `<name>` -- matching the observed MWR convention
(h1_mp5_mp, h1_usp_mp). Index 0 means unresolved, and an unresolved weapon yields a
NULL icon, which the draw already guards, so it degrades to a text-only line rather
than a checkerboard.

### `cod4_weapons_dump` -- for the viewmodel, which is baked in offline

The missing player gun is the same lookup on the OFFLINE side: the transcoder
writes ps.weapon (playerstate field at offset 916, 27 bits) and currently uses
DEFAULT_WEAPON_INDEX = 80. The new command writes the engine's whole index->name
table to `mwr_weapons.json` so the transcoder can write a REAL index instead of a
default. Run it in a live match (the table is parse-order and only carries what the
session registered).

### ⚠ RULE A25 EARNED ITS KEEP AGAIN -- FOUR BUILD FAILURES

Writing C++ through a shell heredoc mangled `\n` inside string literals into REAL
newlines four separate times, even with a quoted heredoc, because the escaping is
processed on the way in. `python - <<'EOF'` is not immune.

**When generating C++ that contains backslash escapes, build the backslash from
`chr(92)` (or use the Write/Edit tool).** A one-line self-check that catches it
immediately:

    [i+1 for i, l in enumerate(lines) if l.count('"') % 2 == 1]   # odd quotes = split literal

### ⭐ THE DESYNC ROOT CAUSE — TWO FILES REBASING AGAINST DIFFERENT STREAMS

    preview_hybrid.py   t0 = arcs[0]["server_time"]     first ARCHIVE  (~85 Hz), +BIAS 1000
    cod4_sidecar.py     t0 = frame["server_time"]       first SNAPSHOT (~20 Hz)

Those streams start at different timestamps, so every kill carried a CONSTANT offset.
FIX: the file that WRITES the demo now also emits the kill list, so one file owns
t0/BIAS and the two clocks cannot disagree by construction. The sidecar carries
`server_time` (the exact value stamped into the matching snapshot) plus `demo_span`,
and the mod converts to elapsed at load.

### ⭐ THE REWIND BUG — never re-anchor the base on a backward seek

    if (now < g_last_seen) { g_base = now; g_next = 0; }   // WRONG: elapsed collapses
                                                           // to ~0 and the feed replays

`g_base` is the demo START and must be set ONCE. On a backward jump, keep it and
RE-POSITION the queue by scanning to the first kill after the rewound elapsed time.
A full restart falls out of the same logic for free.

### ⚠ MY OWN INSTRUCTION CAUSED A FALSE "IT DOES NOT WORK"

I told the user `cod4_feed cod4_holymoly.cod4.json` while `resolve()` only checked the
CWD, so it silently found nothing — indistinguishable from a timing bug, and I then
"fixed" working timing on the strength of it. `resolve()` now searches
demos/client/auto, demos/client, demos and the CWD, and accepts the DEMO name.
**A path lookup that can fail must say so, not return the input unchanged.**

## ⭐⭐ THE MWR WEAPON TABLE — DUMPED FROM THE RUNNING GAME (107 weapons)

`cod4_weapons_dump` walks BG_GetWeaponNameComplete over the registered weapon-def array

    h1_mp5_mp 80    h1_remington700_mp 83   h1_m60e4_mp 76    h1_fraggrenade_mp 64

### ⭐ CoD4 AND MWR DISAGREE ON WHAT A "WEAPON" IS

CoD4 names an attachment variant as its own weapon (`m40a3_acog_mp`). **MWR does not** —
from BG_GetWeaponNameComplete @0x2E2500 the value is PACKED:

    bits 0-7    base weapon index    (masked as `(unsigned __int8)a1`)
    bits 8-16   camo                 ((a1 >> 8) & 0x1FF)
    bits 17-26  attachment           (48 * ((a1 >> 17) & 0x3FF))

27 bits total — EXACTLY the width of ps.weapon (ps+0x394, netfield index 47). So MWR
registers only the BASE weapon and every attachment name resolved to nothing, which is
why no kill icon ever drew. Reduce `<base>_<attachment>_mp` to `<base>_mp`, plus a
separator-collapse for `frag_grenade_mp` -> `h1_fraggrenade_mp`.

### ⛔ THE CRASH — 0xC0000005 at 0x2E2554, and it was my scan

BG_GetWeaponNameComplete does `*(_QWORD *)*(&off_389EB40 + (unsigned __int8)index)` and
DEREFERENCES WITH NO NULL CHECK. My table walk ran 1..2047; the index is masked to 8
BITS so only 1..255 can resolve, and unregistered entries are null. Bounded at 256,
null-checked against the def array, SEH backstop.

### BG_KillIcon LOCATED — MWR-PC 0x2E7330

From the MWR-PS4 named IDB, `BG_KillIcon` is a 3-instruction thunk:
`movzx esi,sil ; mov edx,0A28h ; jmp BG_GetWeaponFieldMaterial` — i.e. weapon field
**0xA28 (killIcon)**. Ported by byte-searching the WIN64 form of that immediate
(`41 B8 28 0A 00 00` = `mov r8d, 0A28h`; the PS4 System V form `BA 28 0A 00 00` does
NOT appear, because the 3rd argument moves rdx -> r8). Exactly ONE match.

## ⭐⭐⭐ THE VIEWMODEL CHASE — THREE REAL BUGS FOUND, GUN STILL NOT DRAWN

All three are genuine and are KEPT; none produced a visible gun, which is what finally
proved the approach wrong rather than the details.

### BUG 1 — `handle_demo_patches()` WAS DEAD CODE

demo_playback.cpp:867 defines it; grep found NO CALL SITE. It is the function that calls
the REAL `CG_SelectWeapon` (H1 PC 0x11A300) to equip the weapon, and its own comment
records that an earlier WWII-port STUB "never ran the equip, so the per-hand viewmodel
DObj was never built and sub_128360 drew nothing". Someone fixed it to call the real
function and never wired it in. Now called per-frame from CG_DrawActiveFrame AFTER the
original (the engine re-predicts cg->ps from the snapshot inside that call, so before it
cg->ps does not yet hold the frame's weapon).

### ⭐ BUG 2 — cg_s::weaponSelect IS AT THE WRONG OFFSET (an unverified iw6 port)

    demo_game.hpp:441   weaponSelect_t weaponSelect;   // +0x6418 TODO(h1)
    CG_SelectWeapon     compares and stores v5[239230] -> cg + 239230*4 = cg + 956920

~931 KB adrift, so it read unrelated memory and was permanently 0. The per-frame guard
`weaponSelect != held` therefore NEVER matched and CG_SelectWeapon ran EVERY FRAME. Its
first statement is

    v5[239232] = v5[150266];      // weaponSelectTime = serverTime

so we were restarting the weapon-switch timer 60+ times a second, leaving the view weapon
permanently mid-raise. **That also explains why writing weapAnim=IDLE changed nothing:
the switch timer overrides the anim.** Fixed by reading cg+956920; measured after the
fix: `weaponSelect=74 called=0` — the equip sticks.

### BUG 3 — weapAnim was missing from the synthesized playerstate

`ps+548` = weapState[WEAPON_HAND_RIGHT].weapAnim is derived from weaponState ONLY inside
pmove, and **a demo never runs pmove**, so a synthesized playerstate leaves it zero and
the weapon is selected but never posed. Added (netfield index 7, type 12), along with
bobCycle (index 82, ps+8) and movementDir (index 85, ps+172) which the CoD4 ARCHIVE
record already carries at +24 and +28.

⭐ ALL 15 POSE_FIELDS VERIFIED against the real MWR netfield table: **0 mismatches**.
746/746 snapshots still decode, poses exact to 0.000. So the data was never the problem.

### WHERE IT STOPPED — the DObj

`CG_UpdateViewWeaponAnim` (H1 PC 0x128360, string-anchor named from MWR-PS4) walks the
per-hand viewmodel DObj array **qword_390B130, stride 133 QWORDS**, and draws only when
the entry is non-null, else it emits "no viewmodel set for player %d for '%s' in '%s'
hand". Its gates, in order:

    if (*(BYTE*)(cg+2) >= 7u) return sub_1C8740(...)      // EARLY RETURN, cg+2 unidentified
    result = sub_2E1270(cg)                               // the held-weapon getter
    if ((BYTE)result) { ...the DObj loop... }             // gate on the LOW BYTE of weapon

A diagnostic reporting dobj0/dobj1 was built and deployed but NOT read before the user
called the approach off. **Do not resume this line** — under the entity-layer
architecture the DObj is the engine's problem, not ours.

    +176/178/184/188/192 (sub_2C3F50's anim block), TWO 27-bit weapon-shaped
    fields at +188/+192, apos candidates +144/148/152 all codec −79.
    THE REST needs the PS4 naming pass — **PS4 registry [0] EntityState/72 is
    NAMED** (same method that named the 271 ps fields; dossier warns PS4 offsets
    != PC offsets, cross-check per field).
  * ⛔ **mwr/entity.py has NEVER produced a byte that reached the engine** —

### 3. The anim-index question — ANSWERED from KisakCOD source
  * **Gait selection is INDEX-driven**: BG_PlayerAnimation → BG_RunLerpFrameRate
    (..., es->legsAnim, es) (bg_animation_mp.cpp:1495); even stance/ADS classify

  * **Velocity only scales RATE**: animSpeedScale = measured moveSpeed /
    anim->moveSpeed, measured from POSITION DELTAS between snapshots
    (bg_animation_mp.cpp:1537-1556). "Velocity must agree or the legs do not run"
    = rate, not selection.
  * PREDICTION (stated before any test): trajectory-only entities slide in the
    default anim — same symptom as live injection, different layer.
  * ⭐ Reframe that keeps fork (c)'s boundary: no CoD4→MWR index TRANSLATION
    needed — select MWR-NATIVE indexes from the decoded classification

  * Clean experiment needs: (1) validate the 4-field writer in game first,
    (2) trajectory-only arm = zero further fields (rate uses origin deltas),

###      MISIDENTIFIED FIELD.

                                                        outside origin/velocity

  * ⛔ POSE_FIELDS (41, 208, type 7, "view_height") is NOT viewheight — offset 208

# ⭐⭐⭐ AUDIO TIMESCALE FOR DEMOS — THE ENGINE'S OWN PITCH PIPELINE, FOUND AND
# DRIVEN (2026-08-18, S2). Goal: record in slow-mo, speed up in post, audio
# sounds normal — i.e. tape-style pitch that tracks the demo timescale.

Found entirely offline in ~30 minutes by walking AW (fully symboled) → MWR-PS4
(debug, real asserts) → S2. CANDIDATE per the Fix Declaration Rules: built,
deployed (hash AF8A129A), NOT yet tested in game.

## ⭐ THE MECHANISM IS SHIPPED AND DORMANT — S2 NEUTERED ITS ONLY INPUT

The IW/Sledgehammer sound system carries a native master audio pitch,
`g_snd.timescale` (the engine's own field name, from MWR-PS4's assert in
snd.cpp:7011). Every voice, every frame:

    finalPitch = basePitch * (busLerp * ts + (1 - busLerp))     // per dsp bus

so buses can opt out (lerp 0) — but the live dump shows EVERY bus at lerp 1.0.

The chain, per build:

    AW    Com_GetTimescaleForSnd -> SND_UpdateTimeScale (in SND_Update)
          -> g_snd field -> SND_CalcVoicePitch -> SND_SetVoicePitch
    MWR   same, inlined into SND_Update @0xbb6d43; asserts name both
          "timescale" and "g_snd.timescale"; source = the `fixedtime` dvar
          (int, 0..1000, registered beside com_maxFrameTime)
    S2    same shape, and the source is NEUTERED:
          Com_GetTimescaleForSnd = fminf((float)fixedtime, 1.0) — fixedtime is
          an int, so any nonzero value clamps to 1.0. Effectively CONSTANT 1.0.
          A complete pitch pipeline waiting for a value.

## THE S2 MAP (named in the IDB, saved)

    0x92E60   Com_GetTimescaleForSnd    reads fixedtime dvar ptr @0x14DB7A0
                                        (dvar "299" == fixedtime per DvarMappings,
                                        registered in Com_InitDvars @0x938bf)
    0x7202B0  SND_UpdateTimeScale       read source, <=0 -> 1.0, write-on-change.
                                        SOLE writer of the field (proven by xref)
    0x716A60  SND_Update                AW/MWR twin; calls it once per frame.
                                        Listener from cg+1993808 — the SAME refdef
                                        view-origin offset the dolly work proved
    0x722F40  SND_GetTimescaleLerp      return g_snd_timescaleLerp[busIndex]
    0x705560  SND_SetVoicePitch         stores per-voice pitch into the mixer
                                        records @ dword_D00DC00 (72-byte stride)
    0xD34685C g_snd_timescale   (data)  float, normally 1.0
    0xD3674F8 g_snd_timescaleLerp (data) per-bus float[], ALL 1.0 in the live dump
    formula   sub_71C8A0 @ 0x71ca9b..0x71caf5 (the channel update)

Route that found it: AW symbol search → MWR SND_DumpTimeScale/SetTimeScaleLerp
asserts gave field names → S2 via the fixedtime dvar: DvarMappings said
fixedtime = "299", the "299" registration named the pointer global, and its ONE
sound-cluster reader was the whole chain. No byte-pattern guessing needed.

## SHIPPED — src/demo/demo_timescale.cpp (the file that already merges both clocks)

Hook on SND_UpdateTimeScale (IDA 0x7202B0 - 0x1000 = 0x71F2B0; RULE A3.1 checked,
nothing else in src/ touches it; void(void) verified from its own disassembly per
RULE A17). The stub:

    ts = theater ? demotimescale : native ? engine_timescale() : 1.0
    ts != ~1.0  ->  write g_snd_timescale (0xD34585C_b) directly, skip orig
                    (orig's constant 1.0 would fight the override; it is the
                    sole other writer, so skipping it gives exclusive ownership)
    ts == 1.0   ->  call orig — stock behavior, restores 1.0 on demo end

  * source selection is IDENTICAL to scale_lui_delta's, so HUD and audio can
    never disagree about the demo speed
  * pause deliberately keeps the current scale — snapping to 1.0 on pause would
    pitch-pop lingering voices mid-slow-mo
  * clamped to [0.05, 4.0]: the engine clamps the BASE pitch before this
    multiplier, not the product, so the mixer is not trusted with extremes
  * speeding UP (>1) pitches up — correct for the record-slow/speed-up workflow
  * toggle `demo_snd_timescale 0|1` (default ON), reports state AND whether the
    hook is live (RULE A15), install result printed at boot (RULE A3)

Covers BOTH systems by construction: custom theater (demotimescale) and native
(PlaybackData+28, the arrow keys / GUI speed control).

## WHAT TO TEST IN GAME

  1. boot: expect `[demo] audio timescale hook: OK (orig=...)`
  2. play any demo (native or theater), set timescale 0.5 — all world audio
     should drop an octave and stretch; back to 1.0 — instant normal
  3. record slow-mo footage, speed it back up in the editor — audio should sound
     normal-pitch again (the whole point)
  4. if nothing changes: `demo_snd_timescale` names whether the hook is dead;
     if the hook is live but audio is flat, the first suspect is the per-bus
     lerp array (read 0xD3674F8 live — measured 1.0s in the DUMP, but the dump
     was taken mid-session and a boot-time state could differ)

## Notes

  * MUSIC will pitch too (its bus lerp is 1.0). If that turns out unwanted, the
    surgical fix is writing 0.0 into g_snd_timescaleLerp[musicBus] — the bus
    index for "music" is dword_D36767C, set by SND_ParseDspBusesFile.
  * Store build: 0x71F2B0/0xD34585C are not in BuildMap.Store.inc, so on Store
    they resolve to POISON and the hook install fails loudly — by design.
  * sub_722970 (unnamed) is the SND_Restore twin — it restores the lerp array
    from a memfile (384 bytes = 96 floats). Not needed, recorded for later.

# ⭐⭐⭐ THEATER CAMERA IN THE CUSTOM THEATER — THE ENGINE ALREADY HAS ONE, IT
# JUST COULD NOT ANSWER THE QUESTION (2026-08-18)

USER REPORT, running `demo_camstate` during CUSTOM theater playback:

    [cam] PlaybackData=0000000000000000  cameraMode=-1  (UNREADABLE)
    [cam] native playing=0  custom theater playing=1

and the ask: *"we need to create our own camera separate from our entity, which
might be better anyway because then maybe the issue I had with 2d scopes wont
happen. Could be beneficial to work both on native and custom."*

Built, deployed (hash 2C979A14). CANDIDATE per the Fix Declaration Rules —
NOT yet tested in game.

## ⭐ DO NOT BUILD A CAMERA. THE ENGINE HAS A COMPLETE ONE, GATED ON TWO BOOLS.

    CG_IsTheaterFreeCamera   0x916D90   mode == 1  (third person / follow)
    CG_IsTheaterOrbitCamera  0x916DE0   mode == 2  (the free fly camera)

Both read the mode from `s_clientDemoPlayback` (qword_10F340A0) + 6297228, and
that global is NULL whenever the NATIVE demo system is not running — i.e. always,
in the custom theater. That is the whole bug. Nothing about the camera itself is
broken or missing.

## ⭐⭐ THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDED THE DESIGN — 39 FUNCTIONS GATE ON THESE

Those two predicates are consulted in **39 distinct engine functions** (41 + 43
xref sites). Not a rendering detail — the whole first-person-vs-detached-camera
behaviour set:

    CG_CalcViewValues          the view builder
    CG_PredictPlayerState      routes to the camera movers
    CL_CreateCmd               input
    CG_DrawActiveFrame         sub_E7980 (the 2D HUD drawer)  <- THE SCOPE
    CG_ShouldDrawPlayerName    CG_ClientViewVisionSetUpdate
    CG_ApplyFadeAndDrawOverheadNames   CG_EntityEvent   CG_ServerCommand
    + 28 more

**So writing our own camera into the refdef would leave all 39 sites believing we
are still in first person** — which is exactly where the user's 2D-scope artifact
comes from. Answering the predicate instead makes the entire engine agree.

This is the same lesson as the nameplate work ("BEFORE REIMPLEMENTING ANYTHING,
ASK WHETHER THE ENGINE ALREADY DOES IT AND IS MERELY GATED"), and it applied
again the very next time it came up.

## ⭐ PROVEN SAFE — the NULL-deref risk was measured, not assumed

Of the 39 gating functions, only TWO also dereference PlaybackData:

    CL_Demo_HandleAction  (the native F2 key handler)
    sub_91AC80            (a native demo action helper)

both native-demo KEY ACTION paths, neither on the render/predict path. The other
37 never touch it.

And the camera MOVERS that CG_PredictPlayerState routes to are safe too — every
PlaybackData read in them is NULL-GUARDED, verified in the disassembly:

    CL_Demo_FreeCameraMove    0x913b40  test rcx,rcx / jz 0x913B7C
                              0x91400e  test rdx,rdx / jz 0x91406E
    CL_Demo_FollowCameraMove  0x91361e  test rdx,rdx / jz 0x91365F
                              0x9137d8  test rdx,rdx / jz 0x913822
    CL_Demo_FreeCameraIntegrate   NO PlaybackData reference at all
    CG_PredictPlayerState / CL_CreateCmd / CG_CalcViewValues   likewise NONE

With PlaybackData NULL they skip only the clip-recording / pose-latching extras;
the real movement path runs regardless.

## ⛔ THE ONE FUNCTION WE MUST NEVER CALL — CL_Demo_SetCameraMode

`CL_Demo_SetCameraMode` (0x91AB50) opens with an UNGUARDED
`v4 = *(_DWORD *)(qword_10F340A0 + 6297228)` — instant fault with NULL. Four
unguarded refs total. The custom theater keeps its OWN mode variable; native
keeps using the engine's setter (correct and seeded there).

## ⚠ NAMING TRAP — THE PREDICATE NAMES DO NOT MATCH THEIR BEHAVIOUR

    "FreeCamera"  is mode 1 -> CL_Demo_FollowCameraMove -> THIRD PERSON
    "OrbitCamera" is mode 2 -> CL_Demo_FreeCameraMove   -> the FLY camera

The NUMBERS are what matter. `theater_camera::camera_mode` already used 0/1/2 and
matches the engine exactly, so one enum drives both systems.

## ⭐ THE FREECAM SEED — transcribed from CL_Demo_SetCameraMode's own mode-2 path

Entering free camera without it puts you at the world origin looking wherever the
mouse happens to point. The engine's seed:

    cg[588912..914] = cg[498449..451]              freecam origin = refdef view origin
    sub_759070(cg + 498452*4, clientActive + 25900)   AxisToAngles -> cl.viewangles
    *(float*)(clientActive + 25908) = 0                roll discarded

⭐ That statement INDEPENDENTLY RE-CONFIRMS both offset triples the dolly work
proved: freecam origin at byte 2355648, refdef view origin at 1993796. And
`clientActive + 25900` is already named `CA_CMD_VIEWANGLES` in demo_game.hpp
("Packed into usercmd +0x10/+0x14/+0x18 as ANGLE2SHORT") — a third independent
agreement. The angles live on the USERCMD side because
CL_Demo_FreeCameraMove derives cg's freecam angles from the usercmd.

    sub_759070(float* axis, void* outAngles)   AxisToAngles. A genuine 2-arg
    function (rcx->rbx, rdx->rdi in its prologue), NOT a forwarder — RULE A23.

OUR ONE ADDITION, labelled as such in the code: zero the freecam VELOCITY
(cg+2355672). The engine's integrator damps it rather than clearing it, so
entering with a stale value drifts for the first frames.

## SHIPPED — src/demo/theater_camera.{hpp,cpp} (was an idle stub)

  * hooks the two predicates; `override_active()` early-outs on one relaxed
    atomic load, so the not-overriding case is a trampoline (they are hot,
    ~80 calls/frame)
  * overrides ONLY when the custom theater is playing and native is not, so
    native playback keeps the engine's own camera untouched
  * mode 0 answers false/false — byte-identical to stock, so the default state
    changes nothing until the user picks 3rd/free
  * the seed is DEFERRED: `set_mode` (reachable from the ImGui Present thread)
    only sets a pending flag; the write happens inside the predicate stub, on
    the client thread, with cg validated (RULE A6/A21 — we never let the engine
    resolve cg for us, we use demo_game::cg_globals_for)
  * `demo_camera` reports mode, which system owns it, and whether the hooks are
    live (RULE A15), so "the buttons do nothing" is diagnosable in one line
  * `demo_camera 0` disables the override entirely (RULE A20 control)
  * commands: `demo_camera [0|1|mode]`, `demo_cam_1st/3rd/free`

RULE A3.1 checked: nothing else in src/ hooked either predicate.
RULE A17/A23: both are `bool __fastcall(int)` — one int arg, only AL defined.

## ⭐ THE UI BUTTONS WERE ALREADY THERE AND ALREADY DEAD

demo_gui.cpp:553-566 has called `theater_camera::set_mode` since it was written —
into a stub that stored the value and nothing read it. So the "1st / 3rd /
Freecam" buttons have never done anything. They now work, show the active mode
highlighted, say which system owns the camera, and call out a failed hook install
instead of silently doing nothing.

## WHAT TO TEST

  1. boot: `[cam] theater camera hooks: OK`
  2. play a CUSTOM (.dm_s2) demo, press Freecam — expect
     `[cam] free camera seeded at (x y z)` and a detached fly camera on the
     normal movement keys, starting where you were looking
  3. ⭐ THE ONE THE USER CARES ABOUT: check whether the 2D scope overlay stops
     drawing in 3rd/free. sub_E7980 (the 2D HUD) is one of the 39 gated
     functions, so it should — but that is an INFERENCE from the gate list, not

     narrower than assumed and needs reading.
  4. native playback should be COMPLETELY unchanged (the override is skipped);
     F2 still cycles, the Dolly tab still reads the engine's mode

## Named in the S2 IDB this session

    0x759070  AxisToAngles   behaviour-proven, descriptive: writes roll into
                             a2+8 after delegating pitch/yaw to sub_75E8F0;
                             sole use is CL_Demo_SetCameraMode's freecam seed

## Follow-ups, NOT done (One Change at a Time)

  * dolly.cpp still reads `demo_native::camera_mode()` directly, so the Dolly tab

## WHAT WENT, AND WHY IT WAS SAFE TO GO

    `g_probe_*` residency scaffolding. The compiler never saw them.
  * **Five viewmodel PROBE hooks** (XModel_AreImagesResident, CG_DrawViewWeapon,

  * **The asset-pool tally** — DB_AllocXAssetEntry_Checked and
    DB_RaiseAssetLimitError hooks, `census()`, `dump_asset_census()` and three
    commands. The image limit is FIXED AND VERIFIED; this was the instrument
    that found it.
  * **The 4780 delta-index ring** + its MSG_ReadMonotonicDeltaIndex hook. That
    investigation closed: publicmatch was a missing type-21 footer table.
  * **17 `if (TRACE_HOOKS)` blocks** — `constexpr bool TRACE_HOOKS = false`, so
    provably dead — plus the 17 stubs they orphaned.

    `demo_native_gate` (the probe that CRASHED by running the reconnect path on
    a first connect), `demo_native_gs_install`, `demo_streamsync_local` (a
    measured no-op).
  * **The StreamSync pre-scan** — CLAUDE.md already said "fix or delete it; do
    not read 0 as fact". It walked the whole demo file at load and reported a
    false negative.
  * **Superseded probes**: `demo_camstate` (superseded by `demo_camdiag`),
    `demo_vm_debug`, `demo_hud_models` (its table is recovered statically in
    this file), `demo_lerp` and its per-frame sampler (the stepping bug is fixed
    and user-confirmed smooth).
  * **14 unused public functions** across demo_native/demo_playback/demo_utils/
    server_browser/theater_camera — each verified decl+def with ZERO call sites.

## WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY KEPT

  * `demo_camdiag` — needed for the camera test in flight.
  * `demo_release_frontend` / `demo_release_level` — FEATURE toggles for the
    image-limit fix, not probes. Dropping ui_mp crashed gibraltar once, so the
    off switch is a safety control (RULE A20).
  * `demo_verbose`, `demo_lead` — a gate and a tunable. `demo_lead 0` still
    reproduces the stepping bug on demand, which is the A/B for that fix.
  * ONE line per level load in `db_load_level_xassets_stub`. The zone count
    either side is the only evidence the release actually freed anything; a
    silent regression to the documented "zones only ever accumulate" leak would
    otherwise be invisible. The per-frame dumps and the tally dependency went.
  * All Hook.hpp / memory.h / Hooking.Patterns.h unused API — base-mod
    infrastructure, not this project's accumulated scaffolding.

## ⚠ RULE A26 — REMOVING "FIRST OCCURRENCE TO LAST" DESTROYS INTERLEAVED CODE

I cut from the first `if (TRACE_HOOKS)` to the last one as a single span. **Live
hooks are interleaved between those blocks** — CL_Demo_IsRecordingAllowed,
CL_Demo_StartRecord/StopRecord, CG_PublishHudModel, CG_GetHudModelValue,
CL_Demo_HandleAction, and the three qword_2537508 NULL guards (sub_47D1C0,
sub_1FEB80, sub_47E670) all sat inside the span. The cut took 28 of 39 hooks
instead of the intended 19.

CAUGHT BY COUNTING, not by the build — it compiled fine, because deleting a hook
INSTALL is perfectly legal C++. A silently un-hooked NULL guard would have
crashed native playback at the next gamestate.

**RULE: when removing repeated blocks, remove each block individually by brace
matching. Never span from the first match to the last.** And after any hook
removal, COUNT the surviving `Hook::create` calls against the expected number —
the compiler cannot check this for you.

Recovery was clean because the files were copied to `.cleanup_backup/` first.
Do that before any bulk edit.

## ⚠ TWO MECHANICAL TRAPS, both hit more than once

  * **A line-regex cannot remove a multi-line statement.** Removing the first
    line of a multi-line `using X = ...(` alias or a `Console::printf(` left the
    continuation lines orphaned and the build broken. Use brace/paren matching
    (snip.py's `remove_stmt`), and anchor on the STATEMENT START, not on a
    string in its middle.
  * **These files are CRLF.** Reading with `newline=''` preserves `\r`, so
    `^\s*Console::printf\($` never matches and multi-line string comparisons
    fail. Match with the `\r` in mind or compare on `.strip()`.

## Tool

`.cleanup_backup/snip.py` — brace-matched definition removal, paren-matched
statement removal, and a line-pattern remover, each reporting exactly how many
lines it cut so nothing disappears silently. Reusable for the next pass.

# ⭐⭐⭐ BONE CAM — lock the demo camera to a player's bone, keep mouse look
# (2026-08-19, build 9917F08F). NOT yet tested in game — CANDIDATE.

User: *"locking the camera to one of our player bones in demos, like the hands,
I should still be able to move my camera with my mouse in this mode."*

## ⭐ WHY MOUSE LOOK IS FREE — it falls out of the existing architecture

`CL_Demo_FreeCameraMove` sets the freecam ANGLES from the usercmd (your mouse)
and then integrates POSITION. So overwriting **only the origin**, after it runs,
gives bone-locked position with completely untouched aim. No input work at all.

The velocity (cg+2355672) must be zeroed in the same write, or the engine's
integrator keeps adding motion on top of a position we pin every frame and the
camera fights itself.

## THE BONE POSITION — transcribed from CG_GetWorldTagPos (sub_45540 @0x45540)

    dobjIndex = word_AC4EAD0[entnum + 2113*localClient]      0 = no DObj
    dobj      = qword_AC4EAB8 + 480 * dobjIndex
    mat       = sub_3E8BC0(centity, dobj, boneIndex)
    worldPos  = mat[+16/+20/+24] + qword_8AFCB38[+108/112/116]

`sub_3E8BC0` is the by-INDEX world bone matrix getter. Its tail is

    result = sub_7BF2C0(dobj);  if (result) result += 32 * boneIndex;

which independently confirms BOTH the 32-byte DObjAnimMat stride (quat[4],
trans[3], weight) and that **+16 is the translation**. Everything before that
tail is lazy bone evaluation, so calling it also guarantees the bone is posed
for this frame.

⭐ `qword_8AFCB38` is the SAME renderer global `demo_game::cg_globals_for`
derives cg from (0x8AFCB38 - 0x1000 == 0x8AFBB38). Its +108/112/116 float triple
is a world offset the engine adds to every tag position; omitting it would put
the camera in the wrong place on maps that use one.

## ⭐ BY INDEX, NOT BY NAME — which avoids an Arxan thunk entirely

`sub_3E8D60` (the by-name wrapper) is just

    DObjGetBoneIndex(dobj, tag, &idx) ? sub_3E8BC0(cent, dobj, idx) : 0

so driving by index needs no string interning, and therefore never touches
`SL_GetCanonicalString` — which is an Arxan `JUMPOUT` thunk (RULE A5). Names are
resolved separately for the UI and cannot break the camera.

Newly identified (not named in the IDB pending a confidence check):

    sub_3E8BC0   world bone matrix BY INDEX   -> DObjAnimMat*, +16 = translation
    sub_7BE2B0   DObjGetBoneIndex(dobj, scr_string_t, u16* io)
                 walks the model's scr_string_t bone table; sets *io = 415 and
                 returns 0 when the bone is absent (414 = the caller's "unset")
    SL_ConvertToString @0x688C90 = off_ACA1388 + 16*id + 8   (already named)

## THE NAME TABLE IS AN INFERENCE, AND IS CONTAINED

Bone names for the UI come from an inferred XModel layout
(`dobj+368` models -> `model+8` XModel -> `+88` scr_string_t[], count at
`dobj+18`). Per the Absolute Rule that is NOT proven — so every step is
`readable()`-guarded, the resulting string must be 2..63 printable chars and
NUL-terminated, and any failure falls back to `"bone N"`. It can mislabel a
button; it cannot crash, and **the camera never depends on it**.

## SHIPPED — src/demo/bonecam.{hpp,cpp}, and it adds ZERO hooks

Called from dolly's EXISTING `CL_Demo_FreeCameraMove` stub (RULE A3.1 — that
address must not be hooked twice), after `drive()`, so when both are enabled the
bone wins position and neither touches angles.

  * works in BOTH demo systems — it gates on `theater_camera::get_mode()`, which
    is now the unified camera owner, so the custom theater gets it too
  * **camera-RELATIVE offset** (forward/right/up along where you are looking),
    which is what makes framing practical — world-space offset would be useless
    once you turn
  * optional exponential position damping, with a 512-unit jump threshold so a
    seek or respawn SNAPS instead of sliding across the level
  * `g_have_last` is reset on every enable / bone change / entity change, so it
    never lerps in from a stale position
  * rejects non-finite or |x|>1e6 positions — an unposed bone reads as garbage
    and would fling the camera across the map
  * attach to the demo's own player (default) or any client number

Commands: `bonecam [0|1]`, `bonecam_bone <index|name>`, `bonecam_list`,
`bonecam_offset <f> <r> <u>`, `bonecam_smooth <0..0.95>`, `bonecam_ent <n>`.
GUI: its own **Bone Cam** tab — deliberately not a section of the Dolly tab,
which is native-only. Presets (Head / L hand / R hand / Weapon / Spine) are
substring matches so they work across model naming conventions.

`status()` names the reason it is not running (RULE A15): not freecam, no demo,
no model for that player, bone not on this model, bone not posed, no bone
chosen.

## WHAT TO TEST

  1. play any demo, switch to **Free camera**, open the Bone Cam tab
  2. tick "Lock camera to bone" — the list should populate with real bone names
     (if it shows "bone 0..N" instead, the XModel name inference is wrong for
     this model; the camera still works, only the labels are generic)
  3. press **Head**, then move the mouse — the camera should ride the head while
     aiming freely
  4. `forward -20` to pull back into a chase framing; raise `smoothing` if the
     animation shake is too violent
  5. `bonecam_ent <client>` to ride another player

If nothing moves, `bonecam` prints the reason. The most likely one early on is
"that player has no model right now" — the local player's world model may not
exist in first person, which is why freecam is required anyway.

# ⭐⭐⭐⭐ COD4 → MWR ENTITY-LAYER REPLAY — BUILT END TO END (2026-08-19)

User: *"attempt to one shot everything I want in one go, properly. Until it's done"*,
after confirming the goal in plain language first.

Built, compiled, deployed and hash-verified. **NOT yet run in game**, so per the Fix
Declaration Rules this is a CANDIDATE, not "works".

    h1-mod.exe   f091bfd3a33614958769f5876cf56a7a  (deployed + verified)
    16 tracks    deployed to <game>/demos/*.track.json
    docs         h1-mod/docs/cod4-replay.md

## THE ARCHITECTURE — the mandate, implemented

Every player in the CoD4 recording is spawned as a **genuinely registered MWR
client** (SV_AddBot + SV_SpawnTestClient + the LUI team/class select that bots.cpp
already uses). Real model, real gun, real animation, real muzzle flash. No
synthesized playerstate, no camera on a path. This is the entity-layer mandate
recorded in memory `cod4-demo-entity-layer-mandate`, now actually done.

    .dm_1 -> (bit-exact decoder) -> cod4_export.py -> <name>.track.json -> cod4_play

## OFFLINE — tools/cod4_to_h1/cod4_export.py (NEW)

Built on `cod4_replay.build()`, the authoritative decode. Emits ONLY what the
engine cannot know: who was there, which team, which weapons, and per 50 ms tick
each player's pos/angles/velocity/flags/weapon-index.

  * LOCAL player from the CLIENT ARCHIVE (the snapshot playerstate never carries
    origin/velocity/movementDir — changeHints==3, the writer breaks out of the
    field loop). Every other player from their ET_PLAYER entity.
  * team per frame from clientState, never the roster snapshot (players switch).
  * remote velocity DERIVED from consecutive ticks; a step over 700 u/s is a
    respawn, marked F_SNAP with zero velocity rather than interpolated.
  * relevance score (time in the POV's view cone / proximity / kill involvement)
    so a capped roster keeps what is ON SCREEN. Dropped players are always listed.
  * ⭐ PER-TICK WEAPON. sample[9] indexes that player's own weapon list, so a
    weapon-swap clip replays the swap instead of freezing on the most-used gun.
    Measured on out_+60wepswap: M40A3 → Deagle @4.5s → M40A3 @8.6s → Deagle
    @19.8s → M40A3 @21.1s → AK47 @42.4s.
  * `player_names` is emitted so cod4_feed parses the SAME FILE for the killfeed —
    one file, one clock, so the two cannot drift apart (the documented cause of the
    old desync was two tools rebasing against different streams).

    16 AZD clips exported: 38-50 players each, 35-626 kills, 68-318 weapon swaps,
    every map name and every POV weapon resolved.

## IN GAME — cod4_puppet.cpp (REWRITTEN from the one-bot probe)

ONE hook (SV_GetUsercmd @0x551E30, RULE A3.1 checked) plus the EXISTING
ClientEndFrame call-out in gameplay.cpp. Per tick, per puppet:

    SV_GetUsercmd   PRE-pmove. The engine's own input channel: view angles, a wish
                    direction resolved from the recorded velocity into the player's
                    frame, and the stance/sprint/ADS/fire buttons. Feeding pmove
                    the input that PRODUCED the recorded motion is what animates
                    the legs, the torso and the gun — no CoD4→MWR anim index table.
    Pmove           the engine animates.
    ClientEndFrame  POST-pmove. ps.viewangles and ps.origin forced to the
                    recording, then SetClientOrigin re-derives the entityState.

### ⭐ WHY ORIENTATION IS WRITTEN BEFORE POSITION — from CoD4's own source

`BG_PlayerToEntitySetTrajectory` (KisakCOD bg_misc.cpp:1591-1602) copies
`ps->origin` into `lerp.pos.trBase` AND **all three components of `ps->viewangles`
into `lerp.apos.trBase`**. SetClientOrigin is what runs BG_PlayerStateToEntityState.
So getting both right BEFORE that call makes the entity orientation follow from the
engine's own derivation.

⛔ This CORRECTS the previous revision's note that "BG_PlayerStateToEntityState
writes NO orientation at all". That was true of MWR's `sub_2C3F50` — but that is
only the SetMisc sub-function. The TRAJECTORY setter is a different function and it
does write apos. `ent->currentAngles` (offset 144, matching the entityState apos
candidates at +144/148/152 in the dumped ET_PLAYER table) is still written as belt
and braces.

### ⭐ THE ANGLE DELTA IS MEASURED, NEVER GUESSED

`PM_UpdateViewAngles` computes `viewangles = SHORT2ANGLE(cmd->angles +
delta_angles)`, and MWR's delta_angles offset is NOT established. Rather than guess
it: one observation of (what we sent, what pmove produced) gives it exactly, and it
re-measures every tick so a respawn cannot leave it stale. Measured BEFORE we
overwrite ps+300, or the loop would be degenerate.

### Design points worth keeping

  * **Clock advances on a REPEAT, not on "puppet 0".** g_seen_mask (uint64) tracks
    which puppets ClientEndFrame has visited this server frame; a repeat means a new
    pass. Tying it to one specific puppet stalls the whole replay whenever that
    client is not stepped.
  * **Weapon switches are drained on the SERVER PIPELINE**, not from inside
    ClientEndFrame — `switchtoweapon` runs a script method and a hook is the wrong
    place to re-enter the script VM. All weapons are given at spawn so the switch
    is instant.
  * **Weapons via the SCRIPT path** (`giveweapon`/`givemaxammo`/`switchtoweapon`),
    the same route a real loadout takes, so the viewmodel, world model, ammo and
    attachments come with it.
  * **Godmode on every puppet** (`ent->flags |= 1`). They fire real bullets — that
    is what produces the tracers and impacts — so they must not derail the replay
    by killing each other.
  * **Absent = out of the recorder's PVS or dead.** Hold the last pose for 1 s
    (what CoD4's own client does when an entity stops updating), then park out of
    sight rather than leave a statue standing.
  * **Slot-aware.** Trims to `svs_numclients - 1`, keeping the highest-scoring
    players, and NAMES who was dropped. `h1_sv_slots 64` (already in the tree) fits
    the whole 46-player lobby.
  * The local player is put in **UFO mode** to fly and film.

Commands: `cod4_play` `cod4_stop` `cod4_status` `cod4_list` `cod4_pause`
`cod4_restart` `cod4_time` `cod4_fire`.

## THE WORKFLOW THIS COMPLETES

    h1_sv_slots 64  ->  /map <the clip's map>  ->  demostart <name>
    ->  cod4_play <track>  ->  fly and film  ->  demostop  ->  demoplay <name>

i.e. the result is an ORDINARY MWR demo, so the whole existing theater toolset
(free camera, dolly, bone cam, slow motion, avidemo) applies to CoD4 footage.

## HONEST LIMITS, stated in the doc and in the console

  * deaths are not replayed (no ragdoll) — a dead player parks out of sight
  * grenades, killstreaks and equipment are not replayed
  * the user is NOT the POV player; they fly free and the POV body is a puppet
    (better for filming, and it means the recorded player is visible from any angle)
  * a CoD4 weapon with no MWR equivalent leaves that puppet unarmed but still moving

## ⚠ RULE A25 BIT TWICE MORE IN ONE SESSION

A quoted bash heredoc carrying prose died on an apostrophe, and a python heredoc
turned `\n` inside a replacement string into REAL newlines, producing
`SyntaxError: unterminated string literal` — which then silently wasted a whole
16-demo batch export, because the batch grep filtered the traceback away.

**Use the Write/Edit tools for any generated file content.** And a batch that
filters its own child output must let errors through the filter.

## Verification done offline (no game)

  * holymoly track: POV present 788/788 ticks, x 3360..5861 / y -813..866 /
    z -128..8 (real mp_citystreets volume), speed mean 137 max 301, 24 fire ticks,
    all-player z -133..191, 230 SNAP flags across 30,555 samples (0.75%, matching
    the documented ~2% respawn rate), 57% of remote samples carry derived velocity.
  * `out_+40to+70district.dm_1` and `holymoly.dm_1` are byte-identical (md5) — a
    duplicate in the user's own clip folder, NOT an export bug.

# ⛔ CORRECTED SAME DAY — I BUILT A SPECTATOR, THE USER WANTS TO *BE* THE PLAYER
# (2026-08-19)

USER, after the first build: *"game crashed, also this is not what I want, I want
my own first person correct point of view, one command too, not these 4"*.

Two separate failures, and the design one is mine.

## THE DESIGN ERROR

I read "every player from the recording becomes a real client" and built exactly
that -- 17-46 bot puppets with the user flying free in UFO mode watching them.
The MANDATE says *"a real player (start with myself) is genuinely registered and
moving and shooting with a gun in hand"*. **"start with myself" means the LOCAL
PLAYER is the recorded player.** I treated the recording player as one puppet
among many and put the user outside the scene.

REBUILT: `cod4_play <clip>` binds puppet index 0 to **client 0, the local
player**. No bot is spawned for the POV. The other players are now OPT-IN
(`cod4_bots 1`, default OFF) -- they were also the largest crash surface.

Also: ONE command. It loads the map itself (`wait ; wait ; map <x>`, the engine's
own idiom, then a state machine waits for SV_Loaded with a 60 s give-up) and arms
the killfeed from the same file. The old four-step workflow is gone.

## ⭐ THE THING THAT MAKES A FIRST-PERSON POV DIFFERENT FROM A PUPPET

**The rendered camera is CLIENT-OWNED.** The server's ps.viewangles does not
steer it: the client rebuilds its predicted playerstate every frame from
`cl.viewangles`, so writing only the server's copy leaves the camera on the
mouse. This is why the bot design "worked" for bodies and would never have worked
for the POV.

PROVEN from MWR-PS4's `CL_FinishMove` @0x3803c0 (named build):

    cmd->angles[i] = ANGLE2SHORT( cl[+0x4AE4 + 4i] + cl[+0x4A30 + 4i] )

i.e. the usercmd angle is ANGLE2SHORT of a client-side float triple (plus a
second triple, the kick/recoil offset).

⚠ THOSE ARE PS4 OFFSETS AND MUST NOT BE COPIED. The PC layout differs (h1-mod's
verified PC clientActive_t has snap.serverTime @19012 where PS4 has a float
triple), and h1-mod marks its own `viewangles` member `TODO(h1)`.

## ⭐ SO THE OFFSET IS CALIBRATED, NOT GUESSED

The SV_GetUsercmd hook sees the command the CLIENT ITSELF built, *before* we
overwrite it. Per CL_FinishMove that value is `ANGLE2SHORT(cl.viewangles + kick)`,
and kick is 0 when not shooting -- so it is an exact target needing no knowledge
of delta_angles. The scan looks through clientActive for the float triple whose
ANGLE2SHORT matches it, and requires 12 consecutive frames of agreement while the
value is moving. A static match could be padding; a tracking one cannot be. It
prints the offset it locks onto so it can become a constant.

Bounded to 36700 bytes (clientArchiveIndex @36736 is verified), and the pointer
is VirtualQuery-validated first -- the scan reads 36 KB through it, so a stale
global would be a crash rather than a bad reading.

## ⛔ TWO NAMING TRAPS HIT AND CAUGHT WHILE CHASING THIS

  * `0x27B310_b`, which input.cpp calls a mouse-move hook, decompiles as
    **LUI_CoD_MouseMove** -- the MENU mouse handler, not the in-game view. It is
    installed only under _DEBUG and only for SP, so it was never the view path.
  * On MWR-PS4 `SetClientViewAngle` (0x5558f0) sits IMMEDIATELY BEFORE
    `SetClientOrigin` (0x555D30). The PC function immediately before
    SetClientOrigin (0x405960) is `sub_4058D0`, which decompiles as a **clan-tag
    name formatter**. Position-in-a-twin transferred for neither. Verified from
    the body before use, exactly as the sub_9192E0 lesson requires.

  Useful and PROVEN from that detour: `SetClientViewAngle(ent, int shorts[3])`
  reads `ent+344` as the client pointer -- an independent confirmation of
  h1-mod's gentity_s layout, now asserted in the code.

## THE CRASH — CAUSE NOT PROVEN, BUT THE LIKELY ONE IS FIXED

**No minidump was written** (newest is from the day before), so it was not an
access violation the handler caught. `games_mp.log` shows one bot joining and
then a shutdown.

LEADING CAUSE, and it is a real defect regardless: `cod4_play` ran on the CONSOLE
thread and did `g_puppets.clear()` / `g_frames` rebuild (2 MB+) while the SERVER
thread was iterating them from the ClientEndFrame and SV_GetUsercmd hooks. A
use-after-free by construction.

FIXED: the track is parsed into LOCAL vectors first, `g_active` (now atomic) is
cleared, and the swap happens under a mutex that both hooks also take. Spawning
17-46 bots at once -- the other candidate -- is now off by default.

NOT claimed as proven. If it recurs with `cod4_bots 0`, the cause is elsewhere.

## LESSON

The mandate was in memory, in CLAUDE.md, and I had restated it correctly to the
user in plain language at the start of the session -- and still built the
opposite, because "every player becomes a real client" is a more impressive-
sounding goal than "you are the player". **When a requirement names a person
("myself"), that word is the requirement.**

And: four commands is not one command. The user asked for one; a workflow is not
a feature.

# ⭐ FIRST WORKING RUN — AND THREE DEFECTS THE LOG NAMED (2026-08-19)

USER: *"it does ads and move around map properly"*. So the POV replay drives the
local player: position, movement, stance and ADS all come from the recording and
the engine animates them. That is the entity-layer approach working.

Three faults visible in that same console log.

## ⛔ 1. MY CALIBRATION LOCKED ONTO clientActive+0, WHICH IS WRONG

    cod4_puppet: client view angles found at clientActive+0

clientActive_t begins with `clSnapshot_t snap`, which begins with
`playerState_t ps` -- so offset 0 is ps.clientNum / pm_type, and as floats those
read as near-zero denormals. At spawn the view is also near zero, so a ~0 target
"matched" a ~0 candidate for the twelve consecutive frames the check demanded.
We were then writing three floats over the snapshot playerstate's head.

**The code's own comment described the fix and the code did not implement it**:
*"require it to keep matching over several frames while the value is CHANGING. A
static match could be padding; a tracking one cannot be."* -- the variation test
was never written. Classic: the reasoning was right in the comment and absent
from the logic.

FIXED, and the requirement is load-bearing rather than a refinement:
  * a candidate earns a hit ONLY when the target has moved > 200 shorts (~1.1
    degrees) since the last scored hit, so padding cannot accumulate credit;
  * the scan does not even SEED on a still view;
  * a rejected candidate advances `scan_from` past itself and the scan WRAPS, so
    it cannot re-pick the same false positive forever (the first-match scan would
    otherwise loop on it).

It now needs ~8 distinct mouse movements, and says so.

## ⛔ 2. THE KILLFEED LOST EVERY ICON — A LATCH SET BEFORE THE WORK

    cod4_feed: engine weapon table has 0 entries
    cod4_feed: UNMAPPED weapon 'm40a3_acog_mp' -> ... WITHOUT an icon      (x17)

`build_weapon_index()` set `g_weapon_index_built = true` on ENTRY, before walking
the def array. Its first call lands during the map load -- the console proves it:
every `Loading fastfile mp_vm_*` / `mp_wm_*` line comes AFTER that message. So it
cached zero entries permanently and no kill ever got an icon.

FIXED: latch only once the table is non-empty. A retry is a bounded 255-entry
walk and stops as soon as it succeeds. `mwr_weapon_index` was already re-resolving
per kill, so only the build needed fixing; the once-per-name UNMAPPED report is
correct behaviour (RULE A18) and stays.

## ⛔ 3. layerb FLOODED THE CONSOLE, BURYING EVERYTHING

Hundreds of identical `[layerb] event ring soft-cap (16384) hit` lines. The
condition is STICKY -- once the ring is full, every subsequent packet hits it --
and the message had no throttle, so it printed at network rate and drowned the
replay diagnostics.

FIXED: announced once per fill. Same class as RULE A18: a message whose condition
persists must not be emitted per-event.

## LESSON

All three are the same shape: **a check that cannot fail, a latch set too early,
and a message with no bound.** None is an engine mystery; each was visible in the
first real log and none would have been found by more static analysis. Run it
sooner.

# ⭐⭐ THE DELIVERABLE IS A REAL MWR DEMO, NOT A LIVE SESSION (2026-08-19)

USER: *"I really want a proper one shot on this. Everything to make it so there's
real other players, I'm a real player, inside a demo playing it back. A PROPER
DEMO"* -- and, separately, that they are not willing to keep supplying logs.

## THE REFRAME, AND WHY IT MAKES EVERYTHING EASIER

The end product is a **.dm_h1 demo**, not a live match. And the way to get a
proper one is not to synthesize it (rejected twice) but to **RECORD the live
entity-layer replay with h1-mod's own recorder**. The result is as real as any
demo, because it was recorded from a real match with real registered clients.

⭐ THE CONSEQUENCE THAT MATTERS: **the demo's POV is correct even if the LIVE
first-person camera is not.** The client demo records the network stream, which
carries the SERVER's playerstate for the local client -- and that is exactly what
`on_client_end_frame` forces to the recorded origin and viewangles every tick.
The live camera is a separate, client-owned thing (cl.viewangles) needing runtime
calibration. So the risky, unproven half of the work does not gate the
deliverable at all.

## `cod4_play <clip>` NOW DOES THE WHOLE THING

    load track -> h1_sv_slots N -> demostart -> map -> wait for SV_Loaded
      -> bind local client 0 as the POV, SV_AddBot the rest
      -> team/class select -> give weapons -> replay + killfeed
      -> end of track -> demostop -> print `demoplay <map>.0000`

Other players and recording are now ON by default (`cod4_bots 0`,
`cod4_record 0`, `cod4_slots 0` to opt out).

## ⭐ IT RELOADS THE MAP EVEN WHEN ALREADY ON IT -- DELIBERATE, NOT WASTE

Both prerequisites are load-time only, and both are needed for a demo that plays:
  * `h1_sv_slots` resizes the server's client arrays AT LOAD, so the roster size
    has to be known first;
  * `demostart` only sets the auto-record dvar -- the recorder's own message says
    *"recording begins with the next gamestate"*, so a demo armed after the load
    would be missing its own gamestate and would not play back.

## END-OF-TRACK AUTO-FINISH

The clock advance sets an atomic when the cursor runs off the end; the SERVER
pipeline loop drains it and calls `finish_run()`, which stops the recording and
prints the demo name. Stopping a recording means running a command, so it is not
done from inside the ClientEndFrame hook.

Auto-record writes `demos/client/<mod>/auto/<mapname>.NNNN.dm_h1` (naming from
demo_utils.cpp: mapname + an incrementing number).

## ⭐ CONSOLE OUTPUT IS NOW A FILE -- h1-mod/logs/console_mp.log

The user should not have to paste logs, and on a crash the console tail is lost
exactly when it matters. `console::dispatch_message` is the single choke point
every line already passes through, so it tees there: truncated once per process
(so the file is always THIS session, not a search problem) and flushed per line.

`games_mp.log` is the GAMEPLAY log only -- joins, kills, shutdowns -- which is why
it could never answer "did the calibration lock on".

## What the 21:23 games_mp.log DID establish

Two clean sessions (2m50s, 2m08s), both ending in a normal `ShutdownGame`, no
bots, and NO crash dump (newest is 2026-08-18). So the thread-race fix held and
the earlier crash did not recur.

# ⛔ THE SLOT RAISE CRASHED THE MAP LOAD — AND THE CONSOLE LOG NAMED IT (2026-08-19)

FIRST RUN with the new console tee, and it paid for itself immediately: no
minidump was written, so a dump could not have answered this, but the log's last
lines did.

    76: ]cod4_play holymoly
    78:              raising the server to 47 slots for 46 players
    81: maxclients: ceiling=47 unlocked (ui=18, sv=18, party=... domain.max=47).
        Server-create still stock-18 until `h1_sv_slots_raise` /
        prepare_raised_session. For a 64-slot map: `h1_sv_slots_raise` then map.
    83: Starting map: mp_citystreets
    ...
   179: maxclients: CG clientinfo/characterinfo reloc active for 47 slots.   <- LAST LINE

## THE DEFECT WAS MINE, AND THE COMPONENT SAID SO IN ITS OWN OUTPUT

`h1_sv_slots N` only unlocks the CEILING. The server-create stays stock-18 until
`h1_sv_slots_raise` runs as well. I issued only the first, so the CLIENT
relocated its clientinfo/characterinfo arrays for 47 slots while the SERVER was
still built for 18 — and the log ends on exactly that reloc line.

TWO CHANGES:
  * `g_want_slots` is now **false by default**. Stock 18 gives 17 other players,
    which is the tested configuration and plenty for a clip.
  * the opt-in path now issues BOTH commands in the documented order
    (`h1_sv_slots N` -> `h1_sv_slots_raise` -> `map`), so if it is turned on it is
    at least correct rather than half-applied.

## LESSON

The warning was printed by the engine, in the same console, four lines after my
own message — and I had read the maxclients source earlier in the session and
still only used half the API. **When a component prints a caveat about the call
you just made, that is the highest-signal line in the log; read the output of
your own action before moving on.**

And: the console tee (h1-mod/logs/console_mp.log) turned an unreproducible
"crashed on map load" into a one-line diagnosis with no dump and nothing for the
user to paste. Keep it.

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STUDY PHASE — CoD4 vs MWR. NO BUILDING. (2026-08-20)
# Full document: demo-corpus/docs/cod4-vs-mwr.md
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

USER, after the first working run: *"okay I think you really need to take good
time properly learning both MWR and CoD4 instead of what you're trying, it's
glitchy, it's weird. The m40a3 has no acog it's just the base gun with no scope
attachment at all. This whole design I don't want either, I literally need you to
understand cod4, it's demos, mwr and our custom demos so you can note all
differences and make it look right. Trying to do this quick wont work, you must
only tell me you're ready to make something once you fully understand."*

**IMPLEMENTATION IS PAUSED.** Do not propose or write a design until the study
is complete. The user's own evidence (a missing scope) proved the understanding
was insufficient, and they are right.

## ⭐⭐⭐ THE ACOG — ROOT CAUSE PROVEN. THE TWO ENGINES DISAGREE ON WHAT A
## WEAPON IS.

    CoD4    an attachment is a SEPARATE WEAPON.
            cs[2258] on holymoly: 111 weapons, 60 of them attachment variants.
            m40a3_mp = index 87,  m40a3_acog_mp = index 88.
            The recorded POV holds index 88.

    MWR     an attachment is a BITFIELD on the weapon.
            BG_GetWeaponNameComplete @PC 0x2E2500:
              bits  0-7   base weapon index -> off_389EB40[i], name at +0
              bits  8-16  camo   (0x1FF)
              bits 17-26  attachment COMBO (0x3FF) -> unk_38A0510 + 48*combo
            27 bits -- exactly the ps.weapon netfield width.

The combo is a SET of up to 4 attachments (BG_GetCustomWeaponName @0x2E0E40
sorts them so the name is canonical):

    struct WeaponAttachmentCombo {     // 48 bytes
        WeaponAttachment* attachments[4];  // +0   name at attachment[0]
        int attachmentCount;               // +32
        int customization;                 // +36
        int emblem;                        // +40
        int scope;                         // +44
    };

MEASURED, both sides: CoD4 111 weapons / 60 attachment variants;
MWR live dump 107 weapons / **0** attachment variants.

⭐ MWR's dump has zero because `cod4_weapons_dump` walked indices 1..255 and the
index is only the LOW BYTE. Attachment variants are not separate indices and
COULD NEVER have appeared. The dump was not incomplete -- it asked a question
MWR does not answer that way.

### ⭐ MWR WEAPON NAMES CARRY THE GAME THEY CAME FROM

`sub_2DFC50` decides the attachment separator:

    return n[0]=='h' && (n[1]-'1')<=8 && n[2]=='_'                 // h1_ .. h9_
        || n[0]=='i' && n[1]=='w' && (n[2]-'5')<=4 && n[3]=='_';   // iw5_ .. iw9_

An `h1_`-prefixed weapon uses `_` as its attachment separator; anything else uses
`+`. So the full name is **`h1_m40a3_mp_acog`**.

`G_GetWeaponForName` @0x461180 (ALREADY MAPPED in h1-mod) parses exactly that:
base name, then while the next char is `_` or `+`, a token matched as `camo<N>`,
`scope<N>`, `a#<name>`, `f#<name>`, or an ATTACHMENT NAME. It accepts either
separator on input.

### ⭐ BOTH TABLES ARE BUILT AT RUNTIME -- never hardcode a packed value

`dword_38A0500` (combo count) reads **1** statically and `off_389EB40` is
entirely NULL in the dump. Weapon list and attachment combos are parsed per
session, exactly like `bg_weaponDefs` / `bg_lastParsedWeaponIndex`.

So the only correct route is: carry the NAME offline, resolve it in-engine with
`G_GetWeaponForName`.

### Where it was lost

`cod4_weapon.basename()` strips `_acog`/`_reflex`/`_silencer`/`_gl`/`_grip`/
`_camo` to reach a name MWR's index table would match. The sidecar records it:

    "held_weapon": {"index":88, "cod4":"m40a3_acog_mp",
                    "basename":"m40a3", "h1":"h1_m40a3_mp"}

That was the only thing that COULD work while I believed MWR weapons were an
index namespace. The belief was wrong.

### PROVEN -- MWR spells the sights the same as CoD4

Chunked `get_bytes` scan of the PS4 image (`search_text` hits IDA's 60 s internal
timeout; a self-chunked scan does not):

    0xF91CEB  'mp/camo_reticle_unlockTable.csv' 'ch_%s%s' 'acog' 'reflex' 'eotech' 'hybrid'
    0xFBBC80  tag_reticle_acog / tag_reticle_reflex / tag_reticle_red_dot /
              tag_reticle_hamr / tag_reticle_thermal_scope / tag_eotech_reticle

`acog` and `reflex` carry over verbatim; MWR adds `eotech` and `hybrid`.
`silencer` was NOT found in the scanned region -- spelling unconfirmed.

## ⭐⭐ ANIMATION -- MWR REWROTE THE RATE FORMULA. Best explanation for "glitchy".

Two mechanisms, and they can disagree with each other.

CoD4 (`BG_RunLerpFrameRate`, read from KisakCOD source):

    BG_RunLerpFrameRate(..., &ci->legs,  es->legsAnim,  es);   // SELECTION: an index
    Vec3Sub(es->lerp.pos.trBase, lf->oldFramePos, diff);       // RATE: position delta
    moveSpeed = Vec3Length(diff) / (latestSnapshotTime - lf->oldFrameSnapshotTime);
    lf->animSpeedScale = moveSpeed / anim->moveSpeed;          // clamped [0.1, 2.0]

So WHICH animation plays is an index in the entity state; HOW FAST it plays is
derived from how far the entity actually moved.

MWR @PS4 0x1FD2A0 computes the same position delta, then instead of a plain ratio
calls **`BG_CalculateAnimRateFromCharacterSpeed`** @0x1FA0F0:

    assert(animIndex); assert(!(animIndex & ANIM_TOGGLEBIT /*0x800*/));
    flags = bgs->animations[animIndex].flags;        // 40-byte stride, flags at +24
    if ((flags & 0x4000100) == 0) return <default>;  // <-- NO SPEED SCALING AT ALL
    rate = speed / anim->moveSpeed;                  // moveSpeed at +0x10
    ... different clamp when (flags & 2) [ladder], and a dev-dvar gate on 0x4000000

**In MWR speed scaling applies ONLY to anims flagged 0x100 or 0x4000000.
Everything else plays at its authored rate. CoD4 scales everything.**
(MWR's bg_animation_mp.cpp reaches line 5905; CoD4's equivalent is near 1560 --
the file was substantially rewritten.)

### Why that predicts the symptom

A replay that FORCES POSITION while the engine picks the animation from its own
movement state can have the two inputs disagree: selection says *idle* (engine
velocity ~0) while position says *moving fast*. In CoD4 the rate would at least
scale up. In MWR, if that anim is not flagged, **the rate does not scale at
all** -- an idle animation gliding across the floor. That is what "glitchy" and
"weird" describe.

STRONG INFERENCE -- mechanism proven from both binaries, not yet measured on
screen.

⚠ And the anim INDEX SPACE is per-game: a CoD4 `legsAnim` value means nothing in
MWR. Anything copying indices across is wrong by construction.

## PROVEN -- other structural differences

    eType clamp      CoD4 min(eType,17) -> 18 types, events at 17
                     MWR  min(eType,20) -> 21 types, events at 20
                     MSG_GetStateFieldListForEntityType @PS4 0x73A0C0 is the
                     WHOLE function: `v1=20; if (a1<=20) v1=a1; return &list[2*v1];`
    ⛔ CORRECTS my earlier note claiming MWR has 24 eTypes. The PC registry at
      0x12D4BB0 has 28 entries but only 0..20 are entity types; index 24 is the
      PLAYERSTATE (252 fields) and 21-23/25-26 are other lists.

    playerstate      CoD4 141 netfields (named) | MWR PC 252 | MWR PS4 271 (named)
                     PS4 and PC do NOT line up by index; identify per field.

    means of death   MWR adds MOD_MELEE_ALT, MOD_MELEE_DOG, MOD_MELEE_ALIEN,
                     MOD_ENERGY -- so the enum is RENUMBERED and a CoD4
                     meansOfDeath index is not an MWR one.

    g_speed          CoD4 190, MWR 190. ✅ THE SAME -- recorded CoD4 velocities
                     are directly meaningful in MWR; do NOT rescale.
                     CoD4 stance multipliers: crouch 0.65, walk 0.40, prone 0.15.
                     MWR's stance multipliers UNKNOWN.

## ⭐ THE TWO DEMO CONTAINERS ARE THE SAME DESIGN

    CoD4 .dm_1     [i32 seq][i32 len] + Huffman message records, plus
                   CLIENT ARCHIVE records, 48 bytes
    h1  .dm_h1     [id byte][size] chunks: mod_header 0, map_header 1,
                   network_data 2, predicted_data 3, update_gamestate_data 4,
                   gen_header 5, gen_footer 6, eof 31

The archive record and `predicted_data` carry THE SAME FIELDS IN THE SAME ORDER:

    origin[3]  velocity[3]  bobCycle  movementDir  serverTime  viewangles[3]

Both are "the network stream, plus the local player's predicted pose per client
frame". That equivalence is why a pose splice worked at all.

# ⭐⭐⭐ THE MWR 18-PLAYER CAP IS IN THE **WIRE FORMAT** — PROVEN ON BOTH BUILDS
# (2026-08-20)

USER redirected the target: forget the live bot spawning (bots spawned but would
not behave). **The deliverable is an AUTHORED .dm_h1 that fully recreates a CoD4
demo**, and the hard part is max clients -- "any struct that only holds 18 players
needs its own reroute to hold up to 64".

Studied it. The cap is worse than a struct problem, and better than it looks.

## THE SNAPSHOT READS THREE INDEX STREAMS, EACH WITH ITS OWN WIDTH

    stream      CoD4      MWR       capacity
    entities    10 bits   11 bits   1024 -> 2048
    CLIENTS      6 bits    5 bits   64   -> 32      <<<< THE WALL
    third loop   --        6 bits   64

PC build (`h1_mp64_ship_dump.exe`, the one that runs). `sub_4F04B0` is
MSG_ReadEntityIndex; the snapshot wrapper is `sub_342770` (case 6 of
CL_ParseMessage @0x341420):

    sub_341D30   sub_4F04B0(a2, 11)   entities
    sub_341960   sub_4F04B0(a2,  5)   CLIENTS   <- 5 bits = 0..31
    sub_341580   sub_4F04B0(a2,  6)   third loop

PS4 DEBUG build agrees and names the second limit via its assert:

    v259 = MSG_ReadEntityIndex(&a10, 5u);
    ...
    if ( (unsigned __int8)v251 >= 0x12u )        // 0x12 == 18
        MyAssertHandler("D:\\h1\\code_source\\Runtime\\client_mp\\cl_parse_mp.cpp", 1019, ...)

**So MWR caps clients TWICE: a 5-bit wire field (32) and an explicit `< 18`
check.** CoD4 reads `MSG_ReadEntityIndex(msg, 6)` -- 6 bits, 64 clients -- which
is why a CoD4 demo can carry a 50-player lobby at all.

## CONSEQUENCES FOR AN AUTHORED DEMO

  * **32 is the ceiling inside the existing format.** No struct widening helps --
    the number does not fit in the field.
  * **64 needs a WIRE-FORMAT change**: widen the read 5 -> 6 bits in sub_341960
    and emit 6 bits in our writer. Both ends are ours (we author the file AND
    patch the client), so it is reachable -- but such a demo plays ONLY in
    patched h1-mod, never in stock MWR.
  * The `>= 18` check is independent of the width and must be raised too.

## ⭐ MOST OF THE 18-WIDE WORK IS SERVER-SIDE AND IRRELEVANT TO PLAYBACK

`docs/cod4_to_h1/08_maxclients_18_inventory.md` -- a full inventory of every
18-wide site -- was DELETED at h1-mod commit `be37bac`. RECOVERED to
`demo-corpus/docs/cod4_to_h1/` along with `06_raising_client_slots.md` and
`07_client_slot_patch_sites.md`:

    git show be37bac^:docs/cod4_to_h1/08_maxclients_18_inventory.md

A demo has NO SERVER, so these never apply to playback:
  * `svs.clients` (sizeof(client_t) = 1,011,960 x N) and the SV hunk buffers
  * the party/session PEER tables (stride 0x270 = 624) -- and those are the
    genuinely hard ones: members live in a fixed C struct with fields AFTER the
    [18] array (`memset(a1+456, 0, 18*624)` in sub_1AFD40; a later write at
    a1+12508), so bumping loop counts alone OOBs into following fields.

What playback DOES need, from the same inventory:

    CL_ParseGamestate clientNum clamp `cmp al, 11h` @0x3412EC   ALREADY patched
    cg.clientinfo[18] @ cg+0x174DA8, stride 112                 relocated to a 64 pool
    cg.characterinfo[42], stride 1856                           relocated
    snapshot client index width                                 ⛔ 5 bits -- the wall
    "Full snapshot/clientState bit-width audit"                 listed STILL OPEN

⚠ AND THE RELOCATION IS GATED OFF EXACTLY WHERE WE NEED IT. `cgame_slots.cpp`
requires `in_real_match()` = `SV_Loaded() && !VirtualLobby_Loaded() &&
CL_IsCgameInitialized()`. During demo playback there is no server, so the 64-slot
pools never engage. maxclients.cpp says so itself: *"Keep next server-create on
stock layout so demoplay / Play Online still work"* / *"demoplay stays safe"*.

## EXISTING STATE (h1-mod), so it is not rebuilt

`maxclients.cpp` (378 lines) + `cgame_slots.cpp` (231) already do:
dvar domain raises (ui/sv/party_maxclients), 6 RegisterInt max immediates,
playlist clamps, SV create counts, 4 SV fixed buffers scaled x(N/18), the
gamestate clientNum clamp, cg clientinfo/characterinfo relocation to 64-wide
pools with base-address redirects, and a 250 ms sticky re-assert loop (Play
Online re-clamps asynchronously).

    constants: stock_clients 18 | stock_characterinfo 42 | target_clients 64
               clientinfo_stride 112 | characterinfo_stride 1856
               clientinfo_cg_offset 0x174DA8 | characterinfo_cg_offset 0x161D28

Commands: `h1_sv_slots <n>`, `h1_sv_slots_raise`, `h1_sv_slots_demoplay`.

⚠ Its own warning, worth heeding: raising RegisterInt max / domain / SV alloc at
BOOT makes Play Online **access-violate with no Com_Error**, because the party
tables are still 18-wide. The raise is deliberately opt-in and post-boot.

# ⭐ WHAT 64 CLIENTS ACTUALLY COSTS ON THE PLAYBACK PATH (2026-08-20)

USER DECISION: go straight to 64, not 32. *"otherwise it's just glitchiness at
that point"* -- a 46-player lobby trimmed to 32 still pops players in and out.

Investigated. It is MUCH smaller than "reroute every 18-wide struct".

## ⛔ CORRECTION TO MY OWN REPORT — THERE IS NO 18-CLAMP IN THE RETAIL BUILD

I told the user MWR "caps clients twice: a 5-bit wire field and an explicit
`< 18` check". The second half is WRONG for the build that runs.

The `if ((unsigned __int8)v251 >= 0x12u) MyAssertHandler(...)` seen in the PS4
build is an **assert**, and asserts are compiled out of retail. Decompiling the
PC client loop `sub_341960` shows NO `0x12` comparison anywhere.

**The 5-bit wire width is the only barrier in that loop.** Do not go looking for
a clamp that is not there.

## ⭐ THE CLIENT RING IS ALREADY DYNAMICALLY SIZED — PROVEN

`sub_12BA00` (client-side allocation):

    *(_DWORD *)(cl + 36752) = dword_356378C * v4;                 // ring modulus
    v5 = Hunk_UserAlloc(hunk, 19064 * v4, 4);                     // snapshots array
    v8 = Hunk_UserAlloc(hunk, 212LL * *(int *)(cl + 36752), 4);   // THE CLIENT RING
    *(_QWORD *)(cl + 36784) = v8;                                 // ring base

and the parse loop indexes `ringBase + 212 * (writeIndex % modulus)` -- a RING
BUFFER, not a fixed [18] array. clientState stride is **212** (CoD4's is 100).

`dword_356378C` has exactly one writer, `sub_12BCD0`, which defaults to **18**
and pushes it into the sv_maxclients dvar via `sub_185D20(off_2EC8700, 18)` --
`0x2EC8700` being the same sv_maxclients pointer maxclients.cpp already uses.

STRONG INFERENCE: `dword_356378C` is the client count and `v4` is PACKET_BACKUP
(it also sizes the snapshot array as `19064 * v4`). So raising the count BEFORE
that allocation runs yields a 64-wide ring with NO struct surgery.

## THE ACTUAL WORK LIST

    1  client index 5 -> 6 bits in sub_341960        ⛔ the one real blocker
    2  our writer emits 6 bits                        ours to author
    3  client ring capacity                           ✅ already dynamic
    4  CL_ParseGamestate clamp `cmp al,11h` @0x3412EC ✅ already patched
    5  cg.clientinfo[18] @cg+0x174DA8 stride 112      ✅ 64-pool exists, GATED
    6  cg.characterinfo[42] stride 1856               ✅ same, GATED
    7  the `18` defaults in sub_12BCD0 on the demo path   ⚠ unchecked
    8  LUI scoreboard / playercards (18x42)               ⚠ unchecked

Items 5/6 need `in_real_match()` (= `SV_Loaded() && !VirtualLobby_Loaded() &&
CL_IsCgameInitialized()`) extended to demo playback. The pools exist and work;
they simply never engage without a server.

## WHAT DOES NOT APPLY — A DEMO HAS NO SERVER

`svs.clients` (1,011,960 x N), the SV hunk buffers, and above all the
party/session PEER tables (stride 0x270) are all server/lobby side. The peer
tables are the genuinely nasty ones (fixed C struct, fields AFTER the [18]
array), and playback never touches them.

## ⚠ WIDENING THE WIRE IS A FORMAT CHANGE

A 6-bit client index means such a demo plays ONLY in patched h1-mod, never in
stock MWR. Acceptable here (the mod is the player) but it must be deliberate,
and writer/reader must be versioned together or a mismatched pair silently
desyncs.

## Addresses established this pass (MWR PC, h1_mp64_ship_dump.exe)

    0x341420  CL_ParseMessage        svc dispatcher, 3-bit opcode
    0x3411A0  CL_ParseGamestate      (case 0)  -- matches h1-mod's known addr
    0x342770  snapshot wrapper       (case 6)
    0x341D30  entity loop            MSG_ReadEntityIndex(msg, 11)
    0x341960  CLIENT loop            MSG_ReadEntityIndex(msg,  5)   <- THE BLOCKER
    0x341580  third loop             MSG_ReadEntityIndex(msg,  6)
    0x4F04B0  MSG_ReadEntityIndex
    0x340560  CL_DeltaClient
    0x12BA00  client-side alloc (ring + snapshots)
    0x12BCD0  writes dword_356378C (client count), defaults 18
    0x356378C client count global
    cl+36752  ring modulus   cl+36784 ring base   cl+19180 write index
