# ⭐ THE TWO REMAINING 64-CLIENT GAPS — BOTH CLOSED (2026-08-20)

USER confirmed the format change is fine: *"I never expected the demos to play on
stock mwr without the modifications"*. So the 5 -> 6 bit widening is sanctioned.

## GAP 1 CLOSED — the third 6-bit loop is NOT clients

`sub_341580` writes a ring of its own, entirely separate from the client ring:

    index      MSG_ReadEntityIndex(msg, 6)      <- already 6 bits = 64
    ring base  *(cl + 36808)
    modulus    *(cl + 36800)
    write idx  *(cl + 36804)
    stride     << 7  == 128 bytes  (clients are 212)
    alloc      Hunk_UserAlloc(modulus << 7)

STRONG INFERENCE: this is the **agents** stream (MWR's AI characters) -- the
`max_agents` argument that `SV_AllocateClientMemory` / h1-mod's
`create_server_hunk_stub(flags, a2, client_count, max_agents)` already carries.

It is already 64-capable and needs NOTHING. Do not widen it.

## ⭐⭐ GAP 2 CLOSED — the client count already comes from `sv_maxclients`

`sub_12BC40` (0x82 bytes), the client-count getter:

    mov  ebx, cs:dword_3563794      ; session flags
    and  ebx, 2
    jnz  short loc_12BC61           ; flag SET   -> hardcoded
    mov  rax, cs:off_2EC8700        ; sv_maxclients dvar
    mov  edi, [rax+10h]             ; <- THE DVAR PATH
    jmp  short loc_12BC66
    loc_12BC61:
    mov  edi, 12h                   ; 18 decimal  <- h1-mod ALREADY patches this imm
    loc_12BC66:
    call GameStateInfo_Get
    ...
    mov  ebx, 17h / 18h             ; 23 / 24 -- a DIFFERENT count (agents-ish), not clients

⭐ THIS IS THE SAME PATTERN AS S2/WWII, already in this file:

    S2   000AD2EE  test dil, 2 / jnz -> mov r13d, 30h (48)
                   else mov rcx, dvar_sv_maxclients ; mov r13d, [rcx+10h]
    MWR  0x12BC50  and ebx, 2  / jnz -> mov edi, 12h (18)
                   else mov rax, off_2EC8700 ; mov edi, [rax+10h]

Same `& 2` session-flag fork, same dvar-vs-hardcode choice. Different constant.

CONSEQUENCE: **raising `sv_maxclients` before the client allocation runs sizes
the client ring to 64 by itself** -- and h1-mod already patches the hardcoded
branch, so BOTH forks yield N once `h1_sv_slots 64` has run. No struct reroute
for the ring, on either branch.

⚠ Watch the units: `12h` = 18 (clients) but `18h` = 24 (something else). Reading
`mov ebx, 18h` as "18 clients" would be wrong.

## THE COMPLETE 64-CLIENT PICTURE FOR PLAYBACK

    2  our writer emits 6 bits                          ours to author

# ⭐⭐⭐ THE GLITCHY AIM — ROOT CAUSE PROVEN, AND IT WAS MY EXPORTER (2026-08-20)

USER described the symptoms precisely, and one phrase named the mechanism:
*"it did move our aim but glitchy, not a true smooth getpredicted as it should"*.

That is exactly right, and it is a defect in the EXPORTER, not the engine.

## HOW THE LOCAL PLAYER'S POSE REACHES THE SCREEN IN A DEMO

h1-mod hooks `CL_GetPredictedPlayerInformationForServerTime` (PC 0x3409C0) and
serves it from the demo's `predicted_data` ring
(`demo_playback.cpp:get_predicted_player_data`):

    for (index = pred_data_index - 1; count < 256; ++count, --index) {
        const auto& p = pred_data[index % 256];
        if (p.cad.serverTime != 0 && p.cad.serverTime <= ps_time
            && ps_time - p.cad.serverTime < 500) {
            memcpy(ps.origin,       p.cad.origin);
            memcpy(ps.velocity,     p.cad.velocity);
            memcpy(ps.delta_angles, p.viewangles);      // ps+300 = MWR's ABSOLUTE viewangles
            ps.bobCycle    = p.cad.bobCycle;
            ps.movementDir = p.cad.movementDir;
            break;
        }
    }

**It picks the NEWEST sample <= ps_time and does NOT interpolate.**

That matches this file's own S2-era finding ("H1 selects the newest sample <= t
within 500ms and does NOT interpolate, yet is smooth"). It is smooth ONLY
because the ring is DENSE -- it is fed at CLIENT FRAME rate, so at 100+ fps
there is a fresh sample nearly every rendered frame.

## ⭐⭐ MEASURED — CoD4 GIVES US 83 Hz AND I WROTE 20 Hz

    holymoly.dm_1 client archive:  3632 samples over 43.3 s
                                   median spacing 12 ms  ==  ~83 Hz

`cod4_export.py` **resampled to 20 Hz (50 ms)** -- my own note said so: *"Resampled
to 20 Hz (50 ms). The archives are per-client-frame (~85 Hz), far above the rate
a client expects snapshots at."*

That reasoning was wrong. 20 Hz is the right rate for SNAPSHOTS; it is the wrong
rate for PREDICTED DATA, which is precisely the high-rate channel that exists to
make the local pose smooth. With a 20 Hz ring, getpredicted returns the same
sample for ~4 consecutive rendered frames and the aim visibly steps.

**FIX: emit ONE `predicted_data` chunk per archive record (83 Hz), never
resampled.** The data was always in the file; I discarded 75% of it.

⭐ COROBORATION: h1-mod's own recordings show the same shape --
`citystreets.0000.dm_h1` has net=2337 / pred=22340, i.e. ~10 predicted_data
chunks per network_data. Real MWR demos are predicted-heavy by design.

## ADS — the field is identified; its RATE is an open question

CoD4 playerStateFields:

    i= 32  off= 244  bits=-88  fWeaponPosFrac      <- THE ADS FRACTION (0=hip, 1=aimed)
    i= 14  off=1576  bits=-88  aimSpreadScale
    i=140  off= 248  bits= 32  adsDelayTime
    i=125  off= 252  bits=  6  spreadOverride
    i=126  off= 256  bits=  2  spreadOverrideState

MWR has the same field at **ps+0x4D4** (h1-mod's own structs note
`weapCommon@0x4c0 fWeaponPosFrac@0x4d4`). Same name, same concept, same -88
float encoder family; different offset.

⚠ OPEN: `fWeaponPosFrac` lives in the PLAYERSTATE, so it arrives at SNAPSHOT
rate (20 Hz) -- the client archive (48 bytes: origin, velocity, bobCycle,
movementDir, serverTime, viewangles) does NOT carry it. A demo never runs pmove
(this file's own viewHeight finding), so nothing obviously re-lerps it.
Whether MWR smooths ADS client-side is NOT established. If it does not, ADS is
inherently 20 Hz from a CoD4 source and would need interpolating on our side.

NOTE the live-replay ADS weirdness may not predict demo behaviour at all: there
ADS came from a synthesised usercmd button and pmove computed the fraction. In an
authored demo we write the fraction directly. Different mechanism.

## "the spawned bots didn't die as expected"

User already attributed this to capturing a LIVE MATCH, and that is right. In a
live match a bot dies only if the game's damage logic decides so. In a DEMO there
is no gameplay logic at all -- death is just recorded entity state plus an
obituary event. So the authored-demo route removes this class of problem by
construction rather than needing a fix.

## RESTATEMENT OF THE TARGET (user, verbatim intent)

The first file created is a CUSTOM DEMO we play back, with modified player counts
so it can carry ALL entities. Not a live capture. Not a recording of a live
session.

# ⭐⭐⭐ ANIMATION — MWR REDESIGNED HOW ANIM INDICES TRAVEL (2026-08-20)

This is the largest structural difference found so far, and it lands squarely on
the authored-demo plan: an authored demo must write these fields itself.

## CoD4 — two plain fields, absolute indices

`playerEntityStateFields` (eType 1):

    i= 8  off=204  bits=10   legsAnim
    i= 9  off=208  bits=10   torsoAnim

10 bits each, and the value is an **absolute index** into
`animScriptData_t.animations[512]`. ANIM_TOGGLEBIT = **0x200**
(`animNum & 0xFFFFFDFF` masks it off).

    struct animation_s {        // 0x68 = 104 bytes
        char  name[64];         // +0    NAME IS INLINE
        int   initialLerp;      // +64
        float moveSpeed;        // +68
        int   duration;         // +72
        int   nameHash;         // +76
        int   flags;            // +80
        int64 movetype;         // +88
        int   noteType;         // +96
    };

## ⭐⭐ MWR — ONE packed dword, and the value is MODEL-RELATIVE

`BG_GetLegsAnimation` @PS4 0x1FD1A0 / `BG_GetTorsoAnimation` @0x1FD220:

    v1 = *(_DWORD *)(es + 84);                 // ONE packed dword
    if (v1 & 1) return 0;                      // bit 0 = "no anim"

    legs : lookup = (v1 >> 11) & 0x7FF;        // 11 bits
           toggle = (v1 >> 11) & 0x800;
           index  = modelAnimTable[lookup];    // qword_31D61C0 + 2*lookup
    torso: lookup = (v1 >>  1) & 0x1FF;        //  9 bits
           index  = modelAnimTable2[lookup];   // qword_31D61C0 + 2*lookup + 435702
           toggle = (4 * (v1>>1)) & 0x800;

    assert(index < 0x95B);   // MAX_MODEL_ANIMATIONS == 2395

On the wire it is ET_PLAYER field **i=8, offset 84, encoder -107** -- a codec
CoD4 does not have at all (CoD4's encoders stop at -100). MWR added a custom one
for this composite field.

    struct animation_s (MWR)   40 bytes:  moveSpeed @+16, flags @+24
                               (name is a POINTER, not the 64-byte inline array)
    ANIM_TOGGLEBIT = 0x800     (CoD4's is 0x200)

## ⭐ THE CONSEQUENCE THAT MATTERS

**The transmitted number is not an animation index. It is an index into a
PER-MODEL lookup table.** The same wire value means a different animation for a
different character model.

So there is NO offline translation from a CoD4 anim index to an MWR one:
  * CoD4 gives an absolute index into a 512-entry table we do not have
    (it lives in the animscript loaded per character, not in the demo);
  * MWR wants a model-relative lookup index into a table that is runtime data
    and differs per model.

Two unknowns multiplied together, neither available offline.

## ⭐ THEREFORE: RESOLVE ANIMS IN-ENGINE AT PLAYBACK, NOT IN THE FILE

The demo should carry the **state** -- velocity, stance flags, movementDir --
which is engine-agnostic and which CoD4 gives us directly. The mod then picks the
packed `es+84` value at parse time, using MWR's own loaded tables.

This is the same conclusion CLAUDE.md reached before from a different direction
("select MWR-NATIVE indexes from the decoded classification ... no CoD4->MWR
index TRANSLATION needed"), now with the mechanism proven.

⚠ It also means the earlier plan of "an authored demo writes legsAnim/torsoAnim
directly" is NOT workable as stated -- there is no such pair of fields to write,
and the packed value cannot be computed offline.

## Related, and still open

  * how MWR SELECTS the lookup value server-side (the animscript state machine);
    `BG_AnimScriptAnimation` @0x1F7E40 is the evaluator but is driven by script
    conditions, so calling it directly is not obviously safe
  * MWR anim flags 0x100 / 0x4000000 (which anims speed-scale) -- still needs the
    runtime table
  * whether `modelAnimTable` is per-model or per-animset in practice

## ADS — the field, for the record

    CoD4 playerStateFields:
      i= 32  off= 244  enc=-88  fWeaponPosFrac      <- ADS fraction, 0=hip 1=aimed
      i= 14  off=1576  enc=-88  aimSpreadScale
      i=140  off= 248  bits=32  adsDelayTime
      i=125  off= 252  bits= 6  spreadOverride
      i=126  off= 256  bits= 2  spreadOverrideState

    MWR: fWeaponPosFrac @ ps+0x4D4 (weapCommon @0x4C0)

Same name and concept in both; different offset. It is a PLAYERSTATE field, so it
arrives at snapshot rate (20 Hz) -- the 48-byte client archive does not carry it.
Whether MWR re-smooths it client-side is STILL UNKNOWN.

# ⭐⭐⭐ ANIMATION — THE IN-ENGINE PATH EXISTS. PROBLEM SOLVED. (2026-08-20)

The previous entry concluded the packed `es+84` anim value cannot be computed
offline. True -- but it does not have to be, because MWR exposes both halves as
callable functions.

## THE COMPOSER — BG_SetLegsAnimation @PS4 0x2007A0

    BG_SetLegsAnimation(entityState, legsAnim):
        assert((legsAnim & 0x800) == 0);          // caller passes a RAW index
        assert(legsAnim < 0x95B);                 // < 2395 MAX_MODEL_ANIMATIONS
        v6 = REVERSE[legsAnim];                   // qword_31D61C0 + 2*idx + 436726
        assert(v6 < 0x800);                       // < 2048 MAX_ANIM_LEGS_COUNT
        es[84] = ((legsAnim & 0x800 ^ 0x800 | v6 & 0xFFF) << 11)
               | (es[84] & 0xFF8007FF);

`BG_SetTorsoAnimation` @0x200880 is the same shape for the 9-bit torso half.

**It takes a REAL anim index and does the packing, the toggle bit and the
per-model reverse lookup itself.** So nothing about the wire encoding has to be
understood or reproduced by us.

There is a REVERSE table (index -> packed lookup) as well as the forward one:

    forward legs   qword_31D61C0 + 2*lookup
    forward torso  qword_31D61C0 + 2*lookup + 435702
    reverse legs   qword_31D61C0 + 2*index  + 436726

all one contiguous blob at `qword_31D61C0`.

## THE RESOLVER — BG_AnimationIndexForString @PS4 0x200960

Takes a name and returns an animation index. So:

    "stand_run_f"  --BG_AnimationIndexForString-->  animIndex
    animIndex      --BG_SetLegsAnimation(es, idx)-->  packed es+84

## ⭐ THE ARCHITECTURE THIS SETTLES

The demo carries **state** (velocity, stance flags, movementDir -- all
engine-agnostic, all present in the CoD4 source). At playback the mod classifies
that state into an animation NAME, resolves it with the engine's own resolver,
and sets it with the engine's own setter.

  * no offline anim tables needed
  * no CoD4 -> MWR index translation
  * no reproduction of the packing, the toggle bit, or the per-model lookup
  * a wrong name fails safely at the resolver instead of desyncing the wire

This retires the "authored demo writes legsAnim/torsoAnim directly" plan and
replaces it with something strictly simpler.

## STILL NEEDED

MWR's anim NAME set (e.g. does it still call it `stand_run_f`). The animation
table is runtime (`bgs->animScriptData.animations`, 40-byte stride, name pointer
at +0, moveSpeed +16, flags +24), so this wants the same one-command in-game dump
as weapons/attachments. A wrong guess is safe but produces no animation.

⚠ These are PS4 addresses. The PC equivalents are NOT yet located -- the PC build
strips these names, so they must be found by structure (the `0x95B` / `0x800`
constants and the `<< 11` packing are distinctive) before anything is coded.

# ⭐⭐ THE PC ANIM ADDRESSES — BLOCKER (A) CLOSED (2026-08-20)

Found by structure, not by name (the PC build strips these). Route that worked:
the 2395 (`0x95B`) constant survives in the TABLE INITIALIZER even though the
asserts are gone.

## THE TABLE BLOB — qword_388C610 (PC) == qword_31D61C0 (PS4)

`sub_2B6790` is the initializer and lays the whole blob out:

    v2 = (WORD*)qword_388C610;
    memset16(qword_388C610 + 464908, -1, 2048);   // MAX_ANIM_LEGS_COUNT
    memset16(v2 + 229547,            -1,  512);   // == byte +459094
    v9 = 2395;                                    // MAX_MODEL_ANIMATIONS
    v10 = v2 + 230059;                            // == byte +460118
    do { *(v10 - 2907) = -1; *v10++ = -1; --v9; } // == byte +454304, two tables

    byte offset   entries   role
    +459094         512     FORWARD torso   (lookup -> anim index)
    +464908        2048     FORWARD legs    (lookup -> anim index)
    +454304        2395     REVERSE (a)     (anim index -> lookup)
    +460118        2395     REVERSE (b)     (anim index -> lookup)

## THE GETTERS — CONFIRMED ON PC

    sub_2B5D30  = BG_GetLegsAnimation   (0x36 bytes; PS4 0x1FD1A0 is 0x71 w/ asserts)
        v1 = *(DWORD*)(es + 84);
        if (v1 & 1) return 0;
        return (v1 >> 11) & 0x800
             | *(int16*)(qword_388C610 + 2*((v1 >> 11) & 0x7FF) + 464908);

    sub_2B5DD0  = BG_GetTorsoAnimation  (0x38 bytes; PS4 0x1FD220 is 0x73)
        return (4 * ((v1 >> 1) & 0x200))
             | *(int16*)(qword_388C610 + 2*((v1 >> 1) & 0x1FF) + 459094);

PC's torso toggle `4 * ((v1>>1) & 0x200)` is algebraically PS4's
`(4 * (v1>>1)) & 0x800`. Same function, different instruction selection.

Two more functions read +84 with the same shape and are probably variants /
inlined copies: `sub_2BA030` (0x32) and `sub_2B90F0` (0x73). Not identified.

## ⚠ THE SETTERS ARE INLINED ON PC — and it does not matter

No xref to `qword_388C610` writes `es+84`, so `BG_SetLegsAnimation` /
`BG_SetTorsoAnimation` were inlined into their (server-side) call sites in the
release build. There is no callable setter to hook.

That is fine: the packing is fully known from the PS4 source-of-truth, and the
mod runs in-process so it can read the engine's own tables directly.

    legs:  v6 = REVERSE_LEGS[animIndex];
           es[84] = ((animIndex & 0x800 ^ 0x800 | v6 & 0xFFF) << 11)
                  | (es[84] & 0xFF8007FF);

⛔ STILL TO VERIFY before coding: WHICH of the two 2395-entry reverse tables
(+454304 vs +460118) is legs and which is torso. One cheap check settles it --
`FORWARD_LEGS[REVERSE_X[i]] == i` for a populated i. Do that against the running
game, not the dump (the tables are memset to -1 until loaded).

## STATUS OF THE READINESS LIST

    A  PC anim addresses            ✅ CLOSED (above)
    B  MWR animation NAME set       ⛔ runtime dump
    C  MWR attachment NAME set      ⛔ runtime dump  (same one command as B)
    D  does MWR smooth fWeaponPosFrac ⛔ unknown -- the "ADS but weirdly" question
    E  cgame_slots gate excludes demo playback   ⛔ known fix, not done
    F  LUI scoreboard 18-wide       ⛔ unchecked
    +  which reverse anim table is which          ⛔ one runtime check

# TOOL — `cod4_study`, the one-command runtime table dump (2026-08-20)

`h1-mod/src/client/component/demo/cod4_study.cpp`. Built + deployed
(h1-mod.exe md5 58bbc884). READ-ONLY: writes nothing to the engine.

    in game:  cod4_study
    output:   h1-mod/logs/cod4_study.json        (Claude reads this directly)

Collects the three tables that CANNOT be read from the static dump because MWR
builds them per session:

    weapons            off_389EB40[1..255] via BG_GetWeaponNameComplete
    ATTACHMENT COMBOS  unk_38A0510, 48-byte stride, count dword_38A0500
                       (each combo = up to 4 WeaponAttachment*, name at +0)
    ANIMATIONS         qword_388C610 + 40*i, count at +95800
                       name ptr +0 (INFERRED), moveSpeed +16, flags +24

plus two things that settle open questions:

    anim_tables  round-trips FORWARD_LEGS[REVERSE_X[i]] == i over both
                 2395-entry reverse tables (+454304 vs +460118) and states
                 WHICH ONE IS LEGS -- the open item from the anim work
    slots        dword_356378C, the client-count global that sizes the ring

## DESIGN NOTES WORTH KEEPING

  * **self-diagnosing.** If the animation name pointer does NOT resolve at +0
    (that offset is an inference -- MWR's animation_s is 40 bytes where CoD4's
    is 104 with an inline name), it emits the RAW 40 bytes of each record
    instead of guessing, so the layout can be worked out offline.
  * every read is VirtualQuery-guarded; names must be printable and
    NUL-terminated in range, so a wrong offset LOOKS wrong rather than
    producing convincing garbage (RULE A6).
  * `BG_GetWeaponNameComplete` is wrapped in a POD-only SEH helper -- it
    dereferences the weapon def with no null check and has crashed before.
  * addresses use `_b` INSIDE functions, never at namespace scope (RULE A14).
  * if a table is not loaded it says so and names the reason, rather than
    writing an empty file that looks like a result (RULE A15).

⚠ THE TABLES ONLY EXIST ONCE A MAP IS LOADED. At the menu it will report
"join a match first" for attachments and animations. That is expected.

## Build note

Files under `src/client/component/demo/` include as `component/command.hpp`,
NOT `command.hpp` -- the include root is `src/client`. Adding any .cpp requires
`tools/premake5.exe vs2022` before building.

# ⭐⭐⭐ THE RUNTIME TABLES — DUMPED. THE ACOG IS SOLVED. (2026-08-21)

`cod4_study` run in a live match. Data preserved at
`demo-corpus/docs/cod4_to_h1/mwr_runtime_tables.json` (210 KB).

    weapons 107 | attachment combos 581 | animations 1709
    anim reverse-table verdict: +460118 is LEGS   (786 round-trip matches vs 1)
    client_count_global (dword_356378C) = 18

## ⭐ THE M40A3 ACOG — the exact numbers

    weapon = 74   combo = 5   ->   h1_m40a3_mp_a#acog_f#base

    packed ps.weapon = 74 | (5 << 17) = 655434

Other variants of the same gun: combo 1 = gl, combo 7 = silencer,
combos 2/3/4/6 = `a#none_f#base`.

## ⭐⭐ THE COMBO INDEX IS GLOBAL, NOT PER-WEAPON

Measured across all 581 combos:

    acog      = combo 5      on all 83 attachable weapons
    gl        = combo 1
    silencer  = combo 7

83 of the 107 weapons accept attachments. **So the attachment is a single global
index**, which makes the CoD4 mapping trivial: strip the suffix to get the base
weapon index, then OR in the combo for the suffix.

    m40a3_acog_mp  ->  base h1_m40a3_mp (74)  |  acog (5 << 17)

## ⛔ CORRECTION — THE NAME FORMAT IS NOT WHAT I PREDICTED

I inferred the full name would be `h1_m40a3_mp_acog`. It is actually:

    h1_m40a3_mp_a#acog_f#base

i.e. the `a#<attachment>` / `f#<finish>` CUSTOMIZATION form, which is
`BG_GetCustomWeaponName`'s `"%ca#%s%cf#%s"` branch (taken when the combo's
`customization` field is non-zero) rather than the plain attachment-list branch.

That matters because `G_GetWeaponForName` parses `a#` and `f#` as distinct token
types -- so a name built as `h1_m40a3_mp_acog` would NOT round-trip. Either feed
it the `a#...f#...` form, or skip names entirely and OR the combo bits directly,
which is simpler and now fully specified.

## ⛔ `reflex` IS NOT AN ATTACHMENT COMBO

Only `gl`, `acog`, `silencer` appear. CoD4's clips also use `_reflex_mp`, and
`reflex` DOES exist in MWR as a reticle name (`tag_reticle_reflex`,
`camo_reticle_unlockTable.csv`). So it is likely a *scope/reticle* selection --
the combo struct has separate `scope` and `emblem` fields -- not an attachment.
UNRESOLVED: how to express a reflex sight. `_grip` likewise absent.

## ⭐⭐ ANIMATION FLAGS — MEASURED, the "glitchy" mechanism confirmed

    1709 animations, ALL named (the name-pointer-at-+0 inference held)
    1617 real (excluding `root` / `unused`)
     308 carry flags & 0x4000100  ==  ONLY 19% SPEED-SCALE

So in MWR four animations out of five play at their AUTHORED rate no matter how
fast the character is actually moving. CoD4 scaled every one. That is why a
selection/motion mismatch does not self-correct in MWR and reads as sliding.

Naming convention, 24 families x 4 directions:

    mp_<weaponclass>_<stance>_<gait>_<dir>

    mp_pistol_stand_run_{f,b,l,r}     mp_pistol_stand_walk_{f,b,l,r}
    mp_pistol_crouch_walk_{f,b,l,r}   mp_akimbo_stand_run_*
    mp_hold_run_*                     mp_rpg_crouch_walk_*
    mp_jug_maniac_*                   pb_sprint_{assault,smg,sniper,lmg,shotgun,hold}

`moveSpeed` is the animation's own authored root-motion speed (e.g.
`pb_sprint_assault` 248.8, `mp_pistol_sprint` 307.8) and is the DENOMINATOR of
the rate calculation -- it is not a player speed.

## ⛔ MY OWN BUG, FIRST RUN — a check that could only hurt

Run 1 reported `weapons: 0`. Cause: I gated the walk on `off_389EB40[i]` being
non-null before calling `BG_GetWeaponNameComplete`. That array reads back empty,
so the loop broke on the first entry -- while `cod4_weapons_dump` has always
worked by simply calling the engine under SEH.

**Adding a validity check on data I had not confirmed was live turned a working
technique into a broken one.** Removed; the walk now trusts the function.

Run 1 also reported `attachments: 1` from `dword_38A0500`. Rather than chase the
address, run 2 enumerates through the proven function instead: pack
`base | (combo << 17)` and ask for the name -- if it differs from the base name,
that combo is real. 581 combos found that way. **Prefer an enumeration built on a
function known to work over a table address believed to be right.**

# MWR ENTITY DELTA FORMAT — RECOVERED, AND WHERE THE WRITER STILL DIVERGES
# (2026-08-21)

First real attempt to make `mwr/entity.py` produce bytes the engine accepts.
CLAUDE.md had recorded that it "has NEVER produced a byte that reached the
engine". Now it has, and it is close but not right.

## THE FORMAT, from the engine (PS4 named build, addresses PS4 unless stated)

    MSG_ReadDeltaEntity      0x7246F0
    MSG_ReadDeltaField       0x7273A0
    MSG_ReadNumFieldsSkipped 0x726F60      PC: sub_4F0780
    MSG_ReadOriginFloat      0x72A600
    MSG_ReadEntityIndex      0x724540      PC: sub_4F04B0

Per entity, in order:

    [entity index]   MSG_ReadEntityIndex(msg, 11), read by the LOOP not by
                     MSG_ReadDeltaEntity:
                        bit1 set        -> last + 1
                        bit1 clear, bit2 CLEAR -> ReadBits(9) delta   (CoD4 uses 4)
                        bit1 clear, bit2 SET   -> ReadBits(11) absolute
                     lastEntityRef resets to -1, not 0.
    [bit] remove     1 = removed
    [bit] hasFields  set -> a delta follows
    [bit] flag       stored; later gates one field read. 0 is the safe value.
    [7 bits] lastChanged, must be < 72   (7 == 32 - lzcnt(72))
    then skip/field pairs.

`MSG_ReadNumFieldsSkipped(msg, skippedFieldBits=3, maxVal)` -- the field gap:

    if (!ReadBit()) {                 // bit SET  => skipped == 1
        Bits = ReadBits(3);
        if (Bits == 7) {              // 7 == (1<<3)-1 is an ESCAPE
            do { v13 = ReadBits(3); v11 += 7; } while (v13 == 7);
        } else v13 = Bits;
        return v11 + v13;             // v11 starts at 1
    }
    return 1;

⭐ `MSG_ReadDeltaField` has NO per-field "changed" bit -- it runs straight into
`switch (field->encoder)`. The skip encoding already states which fields are
present. (CoD4 DOES have a per-field changed bit. This is a real divergence.)

Encoders confirmed:

    0xFFB3 (-77)          MSG_ReadByte              <- eType, field 0
    0xFF96/97/98 (-106..-104)  MSG_ReadOriginFloat  <- origin x/y/z
        if (ReadBit()) { <mapCenter[axis]>; ReadBits(16); }
        else           { ReadBits(7) + floor(old); }
        ONE leading bit, then 16 or 7.

Field 0 (eType) is read from the GENERIC list (`g_netFieldList[12]`, asserted to
be named "eType" with encoder 65459). ONLY THEN is
`MSG_GetStateFieldListForEntityType(eType)` selected for the remaining fields.

ET_PLAYER field indices (from the dumped table): 0 eType, 1/2/4 origin x/y/z.

## ⛔ BUG FOUND AND FIXED — a spurious leading bit in the origin codec

`write_origin_component` emitted an unconditional `write_bit_zero()` before the
16/7 select, on the assumption that every field carries a CoD4-style "changed"
bit. It does not. That desynced the stream on the FIRST body's FIRST coordinate,
which is exactly the symptom: empty map, camera perfectly correct.

## ⛔ MY VERIFIER WAS NOT AN ORACLE

`verify_dm_h1.py` reported "400/400 snapshots ok, 0 failures" on the broken file.
It is a hand-rolled MIRROR OF THE WRITER -- it contained the same spurious
`read_bit()  # origin lead`. Writer and reader agreed on a shared mistake.

When the writer was fixed, the verifier started failing all 400; fixing the
verifier to match the ENGINE made them agree again. **That agreement still proves
nothing.** Both halves are mine. Only the game is an oracle for this.

## ⛔ STILL WRONG — the field loop, most likely a trailing skip

After the origin fix the game crashes with 0xC0000005 inside
MSG_ReadNumFieldsSkipped (PC sub_4F0780) -- the skip decoder reading past the end
of the buffer, i.e. still desynced and now running away through the escape loop.

The reader's shape is READ-AHEAD:

    skip0 -> idx0
    MSG_ReadDeltaField(generic[idx0])          // eType
    if (lastChanged > 0) skip1 = ReadNumFieldsSkipped(3, lastChanged)
    <select per-eType list>
    loop: MSG_ReadDeltaField(...); ReadNumFieldsSkipped(3, lastChanged - idx);

so a skip is read AFTER each field as well as before the first. Whether the loop
tests `idx >= lastChanged` BEFORE or AFTER that trailing read is NOT yet
established -- if AFTER, the writer owes one more skip than it currently emits,
and the reader is consuming the entity-list sentinel as a skip. That fits the
observed runaway exactly. NOT PROVEN.

## ⭐ PROCESS -- THE REAL PROBLEM IS THE TEST LOOP, NOT THE BUG

Each of these single-bit errors is costing a full game launch, because the only
trustworthy oracle is the engine. That is the wrong loop for bit-level work.

**Build an engine-faithful entity DECODER offline** -- transcribed from the
decompiles above, sharing NO code with the writer -- and iterate writer/decoder
until a round-trip is exact. Only then test in game. That converts N game
sessions into one. This should have been built before the first in-game test.

## Test harness in place

`bodytest.py` emits a demo containing N standing bodies and nothing else (no
roster, so no 5-bit client index is involved and no engine patch is needed). It
isolates "can more than 18 BODIES exist" from "can more than 18 ROSTER ENTRIES
exist". bodytest1 / bodytest4 / bodytest40 are deployed.

## ⭐⭐⭐ THE ORACLE PROBLEM — SOLVED IN PRINCIPLE, AND IT CHANGES THE PLAN

After fixing the origin bit the game crashed with 0xC0000005 inside
MSG_ReadNumFieldsSkipped (PC sub_4F0780) -- still desynced, now running away
through the escape loop until it walks off the buffer.

Rather than hunt the next single bit with another game launch, I asked the
question that should have come first: **is there any oracle other than the
game?** There is, and we own 20 of them.

### PROVEN -- verify_dm_h1.py CANNOT read engine-produced data

Pointed at a REAL MWR recording (`loose/loose_22.dm_h1`, 2337 network_data):

    gamestates ok: 1   snapshots ok: 0   failures: 2336

Filtering to only real svc_snapshot messages (opcode 6) and ignoring the policy
assertions still gives **0 of 200 decoded**. The reason is in its own source:

    def _skip_absolute_player_fields(reader):
        if reader.read_bits(3) != 1:
            raise ValueError("entity field 4 gap value")

It does not decode entities -- it asserts MY EXACT FIELD LAYOUT. Same for the
playerstate path. It is a mirror of the writer end to end, which is why it
reported "400/400 ok" on a file the engine could not parse.

**A round-trip between two halves I wrote proves only that I was consistent.**

### ⭐ 20 REAL DEMOS ARE THE GROUND TRUTH

`loose/` holds 20 files with `update_gamestate_data` (the marker of a REAL
recording -- converted ones lack it and contain the string "offline convert").
Those carry real playerstates, real entities, real rosters, produced by the
engine's own writer. A decoder that parses them is CORRECT BY CONSTRUCTION.

This is exactly the method that eventually made the CoD4 reader bit-exact
(the engine's own output as the oracle), and it works here without needing the
game running at all.

### ⭐⭐ THE GENERAL CODEC IS NOT A DETOUR -- IT IS THE REMAINING WORK

`mwr/entity.py` is 122 lines and writes exactly four fields (eType + origin xyz).
`mwr/playerstate.py` writes a fixed pose. There is no general field codec in
either direction.

But the end goal needs one anyway: a real player body requires angles, weapon,
animation indices, clientNum, team and lean -- a dozen more encoders. So
building the general codec is not a step aside from the goal, it IS the goal's
main remaining piece, and it comes with a free correctness test.

### THE ENCODER SWITCH -- EXTRACTED AND PRESERVED

`demo-corpus/docs/cod4_to_h1/mwr_encoder_switch.txt`, from
MSG_ReadDeltaField @PS4 0x7273A0. ~40 encoders, 0xFF92..0xFFBD plus a default.
Shape samples:

    0xFFB3            MSG_ReadByte                        (eType)
    0xFF96/97/98/AE   MSG_ReadOriginFloat  bit ? 16 : 7   (origin)
    0xFFA3            ReadBits(31)
    0xFFA1            ReadBits(7)
    0xFF9F/B6/B8/BA   bit -> ReadBits(8)
    0xFFA9/AA         ReadBits(6)
    0xFFAC/B0/B2/B7/B9/BB/BC   MSG_ReadLong
    0xFFBD            ReadBits(5)
    0xFFB5            bit, then a size switch, then ReadBits(32-lzcnt(16)) == 4
    default           bit; then (width & 7) bits, then whole BYTES -- the same
                      mixed bit/byte tail CoD4 uses

### THE PLAN FROM HERE (no further game launches until it passes)

  1. implement the general READ codec from that switch
  2. decode all 20 real demos; iterate until playerstates AND entities parse and
     produce sane values (origins inside the map volume, eTypes <= 20,
     monotonic entity indices, clean svc_EOF at the end of every message)
  3. only then write the matching ENCODER, and round-trip real demo -> decode ->
     re-encode -> byte-compare. That is a true oracle for the writer.
  4. THEN one game test

This converts an unbounded number of game launches into one, and it is the
process note CLAUDE.md already recorded after the last session and I did not
follow.

# ⭐⭐⭐ THE MWR WIRE FORMAT — TRANSCRIBED FROM THE ENGINE (2026-08-21)

The oracle plan needed a general MWR field codec. This is it, from
`MSG_WriteDeltaField` @PS4 0x73FBA0 (the readable half) cross-checked against
`MSG_ReadDeltaField` @PS4 0x7273A0 and the PC build's own copies.

## ⛔ CORRECTION — THE NETFIELD LAYOUT DIFFERS BETWEEN THE TWO BUILDS

    PS4 (debug)   16 bytes: +0 const char* name, +8 u16 offset, +10 i16 size,
                            +12 i16 type, +14 u16 flags
    PC  (retail)   8 bytes: +0 u16 offset, +2 i16 size, +4 i16 type, +6 u16 flags

The PC build strips the names. `mwr_netfields_full.json` was dumped at stride 8
from the PC IDB and is CORRECT; do not "fix" it against a PS4 decompile.

⚠ AND THE COLUMN NAMED `bits` IS NOT A BIT COUNT. It is the FIELD SIZE IN BYTES,
signed: -4/4 int32, -2 i16, -1 i8, 1 u8, 2 u16. The BIT WIDTH lives in `type`
when `type >= 0`. Transposing the two silently mis-reads most of the struct.

## THE DISPATCH

    lea eax, [type + 6Eh] ; cmp eax, 2Bh ; jbe  ->  jump table

so **type in [-110, -67] uses the jump table (44 cases)**. `type == 0` goes to
MSG_ReadFloatCase. Everything else -- positive widths AND the negatives outside
that window (-112, -111, -66..-61, -16, -8, -6) -- takes the DEFAULT case, which
treats `type` as a SIGNED BIT WIDTH.

## THERE IS NO SHARED PER-FIELD "CHANGED" BIT

MSG_ReadDeltaField runs straight into `switch (type)`. Which fields are present
is stated entirely by the skip counts between them. Individual codecs carry
their own leading bits -- the default case's zero flag, the origin codec's
float-case diversion -- but those belong to the codec. **CoD4 DOES have a shared
changed bit; assuming MWR does too is what desynced the first writer.**

## THE DEFAULT CASE, exactly

    if (!ReadBit()) { field = 0; return }        # the writer sends bit0 when the
                                                 # NEW value is zero
    n = abs(type)
    rem = n & 7
    v = 0; consumed = 0
    if (rem) { v = ReadBits(rem); consumed = rem }
    while (consumed < n) { v |= ReadByte() << consumed; consumed += 8 }
    mask = (n == 32) ? -1 : (1 << n) - 1
    v ^= mask & from[offset]
    if (type < 0 && bit(n-1) of v) v |= ~mask     # SIGN EXTEND, negatives only
    to[offset] = v

MIXED bit/byte -- the remainder on the BIT cursor, whole bytes on the BYTE
cursor. Reading the tail as bits lands somewhere else even though the count
matches. (`MSG_WriteValueNoXor` @0x744370; identical to CoD4's default tail.)

## THE JUMP-TABLE CODECS

    -110  HudData      [bit]->(4 bits + 2 bits into &0x3F) ; [bit]->(4 bits into &0x3C0)
    -108  -> MSG_ReadFloatCase
    -107  AnimData     [branch bit][changed bit] then, per branch, 12+10 bits or
                       4 bits + class-sized reads (a RUNTIME table)
    -106/-105/-104     entityState origin x/y/z
    -92/-91/-90        playerState origin x/y/z
    -83/-82/-81        moving-platform origin x/y/z
          all nine: [bit]->MSG_ReadFloatCase, else MSG_ReadOriginFloat:
              d = floor(new) - floor(old)
              (unsigned)(d+64) > 0x7F ? bit1 + 16 bits of (d - floor(center[axis]) + 0x8000)
                                      : bit0 + 7 bits of (d + 64)
          axis from the engine's own bittest (mask 0x804001 over type+106 / +105)
    -100  angle        [1][sign][3-bit index into g_commonAngleDeltas]
                       [0][1][sign][12 bits]
                       [0][0][angle16]
    -98   29-bit field [1]->29 bits | [0]->5-bit index, old ^ (1 << idx)
                       engine assert names the width: (bitChanged >= 0 && < 29)
    -97/-74/-72/-70    MSG_WriteDeltaTime @0x7442E0:
                          d = value - timeBase
                          d in [-255,0] ? bit0 + 8 bits of (timeBase - value)
                                        : bit1 + MSG_WriteLong(value)
    -96   groundEntity [1] -> 2046 | [0][1] -> 0 | [0][0] -> 3 bits | byte<<3
    -94   event+parm   see below
    -93   31 bits
    -89   [1]->ReadLong xor old | [0]-> 5 bits + byte, ((lo+32*hi) ^ (old+4096)) - 4096
    -88   float32 XOR against the baseline  (same number and meaning as CoD4's -88)
    -87   MSG_ReadAngle16 -- a SHORT on the BYTE cursor, * 360/65536
    -86   6 bits
    -85   [1]->unchanged | [0][1]->keep 24 bits | [0][0]->3 bytes; then 5 bits either way
    -84   13 bits
    -80/-78/-73/-71/-69/-68   MSG_ReadLong -- a raw 32-bit value, NO delta
    -79   angle12      [1][sign][12 bits] | [0][12 bits]
    -77   MSG_ReadByte  (eType and friends)
    -76   movementDir  [1]-> 4 bits, v = bits + old - 8 | [0]-> one byte of XOR
    -75   eventSequence [1]-> 5 bits, v = old + 1 + bits | [0]-> one byte of XOR
    -67   5 bits, value = bits - 10

Not implemented (absent from every entity list 0..20 and from the playerstate):
-109, -103, -102, -101, -99, -95.

## -94, THE EVENT CODEC, AND ITS ASYMMETRY

    if ReadBit():                    # event id changed
        ev = ReadByte()
        bits = g_eventParmBits[ev]
        if bits == 0: parm = 0
        elif ReadBit(): parm = ReadBits(bits)
        else: parm = from.parm & (ev == 183 ? -1 : (1<<bits)-1)
    else:                            # event id unchanged
        ev = from.event
        bits = g_eventParmBits[ev]
        parm = (bits == 0) ? 0 : ReadBits(bits)     # <-- NO GATE BIT HERE

The missing gate on the unchanged path is the engine's, not a transcription
slip. `g_eventParmBits` = PS4 qword_F9BA00 as u32[186] (EV_MAX_EVENTS, from the
engine's own assert); dumped to `mwr_event_parm_bits.json`, values 0..33.

## THE SKIP COUNT (MSG_ReadNumFieldsSkipped)

    if (ReadBit()) return 1                       # the common +1 case
    n = ReadBits(w)                               # w = 3 entities, 4 PLAYERSTATE
    if (n == (1<<w)-1) { do { n = ReadBits(w); acc += (1<<w)-1 } while (n == (1<<w)-1) }
    return 1 + acc + n

⭐ **ENTITIES USE 3 SKIP BITS, THE PLAYERSTATE USES 4.** Easy to get wrong.
The skip is always a DELTA from the previous field index; the first one is
relative to -1.

## MSG_ReadDeltaEntity — the complete record (PC 0x4ECBE0, now named)

    [entity index]  read by the LOOP, MSG_ReadEntityIndex(msg, 11):
                      bit1 set                 -> last + 1
                      bit1 clear, bit2 clear   -> ReadBits(9)  delta
                      bit1 clear, bit2 set     -> ReadBits(11) absolute
                    lastEntityRef resets to -1, not 0
    [bit] remove    1 -> entity removed, nothing follows
    [bit] hasFields 0 -> memcpy(to, from, 256) and nothing follows
    [bit] flag      feeds the zero-baseline decision below
    [7 bits] lastChanged, must be < 72          (7 == 32 - clz(72))
    skip0 = ReadNumFieldsSkipped(3, lastChanged+1); idx = skip0 - 1
    if idx != 0: CopyFieldOver(generic, 0)      # eType unchanged
    else:        ReadDeltaField(generic[0])     # eType, from the GENERIC list
                 if lastChanged > 0: idx = ReadNumFieldsSkipped(3, lastChanged)
    eType = to[10]                              # PC: offset 10, size 1, type -77
    fields = MSG_GetStateFieldListForEntityType(eType)   # clamp at 20
    if lastChanged >= count: OVERFLOW
    if lastChanged != 0:
        loop:
            copy fields (prev+1 .. idx-1) from the baseline
            zeroBase = (from[10] != to[10]) || (flag && typeInMask(fields[idx].type))
            ReadDeltaField(fields[idx])
            if idx >= lastChanged: BREAK        # <-- BEFORE any trailing skip
            prev = idx; idx += ReadNumFieldsSkipped(3, lastChanged - idx)
    for k in 0..idx-1: if (fields[k].flags & 2): ReadDeltaField(fields[k])   # 2nd pass
    for j in idx+1..count-1: CopyFieldOver(fields, j)

⭐ **THERE IS NO TRAILING SKIP.** The `idx >= lastChanged` test sits BEFORE the
in-loop skip read. That answers the question left open in the previous session
("before or after"), and it means the writer owes no extra skip.

⭐ The zero-baseline mask is `0x1807E000001` indexed by `type + 108`, i.e. types
-108, -83..-78, -73, -72.

⚠ The flags&2 SECOND PASS re-reads earlier fields with no gate bit. Measured
across every list: **only eType 13 has any flags&2 fields** (indices 1,2,9-15),
so it does not affect ET_PLAYER or the generic list -- but a decoder must
implement it or eType 13 desyncs.

⚠ For a FIRST-SIGHT entity the baseline is not plain zeros: the engine copies
256 bytes and then patches per-eType defaults (+4 i16 = 2046, +11 = 7,
+12 = entnum, +96 = 3, +132 = 1, +168 = 2047 depending on eType). Bit counts do
not depend on it, but decoded VALUES do -- and so does -94, whose parm width
comes from the baseline event id on the unchanged path.

## CL_ParseSnapshot section order (PC 0x342770, now named)

    MSG_ReadLong    serverTime
    MSG_ReadByte    deltaNum
    MSG_ReadByte    snapFlags
    MSG_ReadBit     (baseline select)
    MSG_ReadDeltaPlayerstate            (sub_4EE4E0 wrapper -> 0x4EE63E)
    sub_4EF6C0                          gated section, starts with a bit
    sub_342240 -> sub_4EE310            gated section
    MSG_ClearLastReferencedEntity
    CL_ParsePacketEntities              MSG_ReadEntityIndex(msg, 11)
    MSG_ClearLastReferencedEntity
    if (deltaNum == 0) MSG_ReadByte     <-- an extra BYTE on a FULL snapshot
    CL_ParsePacketClients               MSG_ReadEntityIndex(msg, 5)
    MSG_ClearLastReferencedEntity
    CL_ParsePacketAgents                MSG_ReadEntityIndex(msg, 6)

## ⛔ A WRONG NAME IN THE PC IDB, CORRECTED

`MSG_ReadShort` @PC 0x73F90 is **MSG_ReadBit**. Its body reads the BIT cursor at
msg+40, resyncs `bit := 8*readcount` when `(bit & 7) == 0`, and returns one bit;
every call site matches MSG_ReadBit in the named PS4 twin. The wrong name came
from my own earlier same-game call-graph propagation pass -- an instance of the
~1.6% error that pass measured, now found in practice. Renamed with the basis
recorded on the function.

## Named in the PC IDB this session (all behaviour-proven or twin-proven)

    0x4EB7D0 MSG_ReadLong          0x4EB510 MSG_ReadByte (Arxan body)
    0x4EB190 MSG_Discard           0x73F90  MSG_ReadBit  (CORRECTED)
    0x4EC1E0 MSG_ClearLastReferencedEntity
    0x4EC1F0 MSG_CopyFieldOver     0x4EC2E0 MSG_FieldTypeInZeroBaseMask
    0x4ECBE0 MSG_ReadDeltaEntity   0x4ED0E0 MSG_ReadDeltaField
    0x4EDB98 MSG_ReadDeltaStruct   0x4F0780 MSG_ReadNumFieldsSkipped
    0x4F04B0 MSG_ReadEntityIndex   0x4F2C30 MSG_GetStateFieldListForEntityType
    0x342770 CL_ParseSnapshot      0x341D30 CL_ParsePacketEntities
    0x341960 CL_ParsePacketClients 0x341580 CL_ParsePacketAgents

## ⛔ DEAD END — the PS4 build cannot supply netfield NAMES

`g_entityStateNetFieldList` is a POINTER to the registry (deref once, then
16 bytes per eType). Following it lands on 0xBB3EA00+, which is uninitialised in
the static image: **the PS4 build constructs its netfield lists at runtime**,
with names, into allocated memory. The PC build's lists are static data with the
names stripped. So there is no way to get field names from either image
statically. Do not spend time on it again.

## Data captured to demo-corpus/docs/cod4_to_h1/

    mwr_netfields_full.json          the PC registry (28 entries) + all 22 lists,
                                     1520 fields, stride 8
    mwr_event_parm_bits.json         g_eventParmBits[186]
    mwr_encoder_switch.txt           the raw switch extract

Code: `tools/cod4_to_h1/mwr/delta_field.py` implements every codec above.

# THE MWR DECODER — BUILT AND MEASURED AGAINST REAL DEMOS (2026-08-21)

`tools/cod4_to_h1/mwr/reader.py` + `mwr/delta_field.py`. Shares NO code with the
writer, which is the whole point: `verify_dm_h1.py` was a mirror of the writer
and passed a file the engine could not parse.

Driven by `realcheck.py` over the 20 REAL recordings in `demo-corpus/loose/`
(identified by carrying an `update_gamestate_data` chunk; converted files lack
it and contain the string "offline convert").

## ⭐ THE RESULT THAT MATTERS

    2,912 real snapshots from 20 engine-recorded demos
      playerstate field loop completes      2,744  (94.2%)
      commandTime decodes SANE               2,689  (98% of those)

`commandTime` is playerstate field 0 (offset 76, encoder -97 = MSG_DeltaTime).
Decoding it to `serverTime - 27..190 ms` on 2,689 independent engine-produced
snapshots is not luck. **It proves the snapshot header (2 bits + an 8-bit
lastChanged), the first skip count, and the -97 codec are correct**, and it is
the first evidence in this project that any of the MWR field decoding is right.

## ⛔ BUT "94.2% ok" IS A WEAK METRIC AND MUST NOT BE QUOTED AS SUCCESS

It only means "did not run off the end of the buffer". The dominant snapshot in
a real demo has `lastChanged == 10` and sends TWO fields -- perhaps 40 bits out
of a 200-byte message -- so not overrunning is nearly free. It is the same class
of mistake as the CoD4 `entities_truncated` metric, which counted only raised
exceptions and collapsed to zero when the exceptions were removed.

**The decisive metric is still the one designed and not yet reachable:** decode
the playerstate, then the two intermediate sections, then the entity list, and
require it to terminate on the 2047 sentinel with monotonic indices and every
eType <= 20.

## ⭐ ONE REAL CODEC BUG FOUND AND FIXED — the origin families are NOT alike

`MSG_WriteDeltaField` treats the three origin families differently, and I had
applied the same shape to all nine encoders:

    -106/-105/-104  entityState  -> MSG_WriteMovingPlatformValidOrigin @0x73BC70
                                    which writes a LEADING BIT:
                                      if (snapshotInfo[118]) { bit1; WriteFloatCase }
                                      else { bit0; OriginZFloat if -104 else OriginFloat }
    -92/-91/-90     playerState  -> MSG_WriteOriginFloat / ZFloat DIRECTLY, NO leading bit
    -83/-82/-81     platform     -> same, NO leading bit

Split into `_c_origin_es` and `_c_origin`. The extra bit was desynchronising
every full snapshot -- visible as `origin=(-0.0, -1.7e38, -0.1)`, the signature
of the float-case branch being taken on data that never encoded one.

⚠ Fixing it moved the headline number by 0.1 points, which is itself the
evidence that the metric is weak, not that the fix was unimportant.

## ⛔ THE ENTITY DECODER IS NOT VALIDATED. Do not treat it as working.

`diag/findents.py` scans forward from the end of the playerstate field loop for
a position where the entity list parses cleanly, so the entity decoder can be
tested without the untranscribed tail. Results:

    small messages (<400 B), min 2 entities   7 / 25 "found"
    large messages (>=400 B), min 6 entities  0 / 4  at span 400 bits
                                              1 / 4  at span 3000 bits

and the one large hit stopped at readcount 396 of 837 with 11 entities all of
eType 0 -- half the message unread and no eType variety. **These are consistent
with chance, not with a correct parse.** A short run of eType-0 records ending
on a 2047 sentinel is not hard to hit by accident.

⚠ AND THE SCAN REPEATED A DOCUMENTED MISTAKE ON ITS FIRST VERSION: it varied
only the BIT cursor and derived readcount from it. The msg_t cursor is a PAIR --
byte reads move `readcount` alone, bit reads move `bit` alone and resync
`bit := 8*readcount` only when `(bit & 7) == 0`. CLAUDE.md already records this
from the CoD4 work ("reconstructing readcount from a bit position made every
offset it reported an artefact") and it was repeated anyway. The scan now
enumerates both reachable families of pairs.

## WHY THE SCAN CANNOT SETTLE IT — and what does

Three untranscribed sections sit between the playerstate field loop and the
entities:

    the playerstate's own gated TAIL      (PC 0x4EE8A3 onward)
    sub_4EF6C0                            gated, starts with a bit
    sub_342240 -> sub_4EE310              gated

so the gap is variable (measured 33..1814 bits) and the search space is large
enough that weak hits are meaningless. **Searching is the wrong tool now; the
tail has to be transcribed.** It is a bounded job: a chain of
`if (MSG_ReadBit())` gates with reads of 4, 1, 27, 2, 8 and 3 bits plus
MSG_ReadByte and a 4-byte primitive, all visible in the PC decompile at
0x4EE8A3..0x4EF698.

## THE NEXT STEP, precisely

  1. transcribe MSG_ReadDeltaPlayerstate's tail from the PC decompile
     (`re/mwr/pc_read_delta_playerstate.c`, saved)
  2. transcribe sub_4EF6C0 and sub_342240/sub_4EE310
  3. then the sentinel test becomes decisive, and the writer can be checked
     against a decoder that is itself checked against the engine

## Two more misnamed PC functions corrected

Both were false positives of my own earlier same-game call-graph propagation
pass -- the ~1.6% error rate that pass measured, now seen twice in practice.

    0x73F90   MSG_ReadShort -> MSG_ReadBit
              body reads the BIT cursor at msg+40 and resyncs to 8*readcount
    0x4EB890  Com_Printf -> MSG_ReadValue32_ByteCursor
              a 9-byte thunk reading msg+36 then jumping into the Arxan block;
              its own basis comment recorded a 72x size mismatch and it was
              believed anyway. Descriptive name: long-vs-float is NOT established.

**GENERALISE: a propagation basis comment that records a wild size ratio is a
flag, not a footnote.** Both of these were readable in one decompile.

## Tools

    mwr/reader.py        the engine-faithful reader (msg_t, entity, playerstate)
    mwr/delta_field.py   the codec table, 36 encoders + the default case
    realcheck.py         decode real demos; reports per-opcode and per-failure
    diag/psblame.py      per-field trace: which field was being read at the failure
    diag/findents.py     dual-cursor search for the entity list start

# ⭐⭐⭐ THE MWR PLAYERSTATE DECODER IS CORRECT — AND BOTH ORACLES I WAS USING
# WERE INVALID (2026-08-21)

Two sessions were spent concluding "the playerstate decode is wrong beyond field 0"
because decoded origin never matched ground truth. **That conclusion is WITHDRAWN.
The decode was right; the test could never have passed.**

## ⛔⛔ ORIGIN CANNOT BE AN ORACLE — THE ENGINE THROWS THE DECODED VALUE AWAY

`MSG_ReadDeltaPlayerstate` ends (PC 0x4EE81C, after the field loop):

    if (headerBit) {
        if (!CL_GetPredictedPlayerInformationForServerTime(cl, ps->commandTime, ps)) {
            ps[0x78] = from[0x78];   ps[0x7C] = from[0x7C];   ps[0x80] = from[0x80];
            ps[0x84] = from[0x84];   ps[0x88] = from[0x88];   ps[0x8C] = from[0x8C];
            ps[0x74] = from[0x74];   ps[0xC8] = from[0xC8];
        }
    }

    0x78/0x7C/0x80 = 120/124/128  origin[3]
    0x84/0x88/0x8C = 132/136/140  velocity[3]
    0x74 = 116 bobCycle           0xC8 = 200 movementDir

**The snapshot's origin bits are CONSUMED and then OVERWRITTEN** from the client's
own prediction ring (or, if that misses, from the baseline frame). So a demo's
`predicted_data` and the snapshot's ps.origin are the SAME NUMBER ARRIVING BY A
DIFFERENT ROUTE — comparing them tests nothing, and can never match, because the
snapshot's copy is discarded before anything reads it.

This is the exact MWR behaviour CLAUDE.md already recorded from the other side
("CL_GetPredictedPlayerInformationForServerTime writes ONLY origin, velocity,
bobCycle, movementDir") and from h1-mod's own hook on that function. I did not
connect the two.

MEASURED, corroborating: across 300 messages the true origin floats appear
**literally nowhere** in any decompressed body, and across 120 snapshots the true
value appears at NO offset of the decoded 18,576-byte playerstate (1 hit at ps+144,
i.e. chance). Both are consistent with "never sent", not with "sent and misparsed".

## ⛔ VIEWANGLES IS NOT AN ORACLE EITHER

Same trap, one level subtler. ps+300/304/308 are encoder -87 (MSG_ReadAngle16,
absolute, no baseline) so they LOOK ideal. But the rendered view is client-owned —
`predicted_data`'s viewangles come from `cl.viewangles`, not from the snapshot — so
there is no reason for the two to agree. Measured: the true yaw appears at no
offset of the decoded state.

**GENERALISE: a field that the CLIENT owns, or that the engine overwrites after
parsing, cannot validate a PARSE.** Before adopting an oracle, check who WRITES the
field last, not just who declares it.

## ⭐⭐ THE EVIDENCE THAT THE FIELD LOOP IS ACTUALLY RIGHT

A structural test that needs no field semantics: read the 12 bits that follow the
field loop. If the loop ends at the right bit they are the tail's GATE bits and
must be skewed toward zero; if it desyncs they are uniform noise.

    700 snapshots, percent ONE by bit position:
        9.6  8.6  10.9  9.4  11.3  13.1  10.7  15.9  10.0  10.4  11.4  35.7

~10%, not ~50%. **The loop ends where the engine ends it.** Corroborating:
`lastChanged` takes 37 distinct values over 2..243 with a real shape
(10 x400, 44 x73, 45 x59, 193 x43, ...), and `commandTime` decodes to EXACTLY
serverTime. `lc == 10` dominating is a genuine minimal-update pattern, not a
symptom — most frames change only commandTime and a couple of timers, because
origin and velocity are client-predicted and therefore not sent.

## ⛔ A REGRESSION I NEARLY SHIPPED, AND WHY IT LOOKED LIKE A FIX

CL_ParseSnapshot's decompile shows `MSG_ReadShort(a2)` between the snapshot header
and the playerstate. Modelling it as 16 bits turned the `lastChanged` histogram
from "pinned at 10" into a broad plausible spread, which read as a decisive fix.

**It is MSG_ReadBit.** Verified in the disassembly: `0x3428b3 call MSG_ReadBit`.
The decompile text was generated BEFORE this project renamed 0x73F90 from
MSG_ReadShort to MSG_ReadBit (itself a corrected call-graph-propagation false
positive), so the saved .c file carries the stale name.

⚠ **A SAVED DECOMPILE IS A SNAPSHOT OF THE IDB AT DUMP TIME.** After renaming
anything, saved decompiles are stale and will quietly disagree with the database.
Re-dump, or read the disassembly, before trusting a call name in an old .c file.

And the deeper lesson: the histogram was never an oracle. Origin stayed zero under
BOTH models, so "one of these makes a number look nicer" was the only signal, and
it pointed the wrong way.

## PROVEN — the PC snapshot + playerstate preamble, end to end

    CL_ParseMessage (PC 0x341420) is a LOOP of 3-bit opcodes terminating at 7:
        0 gamestate | 2 cmd | 3 ReadBits(8)+cmd | 4 | 5 | 6 snapshot | 7 EOF
      so ONE message can carry commands BEFORE the snapshot.  A reader that gives
      up when the first opcode is not 6 silently drops those snapshots (291 of
      2024 in loose_22 alone).

    CL_ParseSnapshot (PC 0x342770):
        serverTime = MSG_ReadLong        0x3427e2
        deltaNum   = MSG_ReadByte        0x3427fc      frame = messageNum - deltaNum
        snapFlags  = MSG_ReadByte        0x342826
        MSG_ReadBit                      0x3428b3      selects the baseline
        sub_4EE4E0(...) -> MSG_ReadDeltaPlayerstate

    MSG_ReadDeltaPlayerstate: IDA bounds it at 0x4EE63E but the REAL entry is
      ~0x4EE4E0 (the wrapper) -- 0x4EE63E is the middle of the function and the
      header sits BELOW it.  A `jl MSG_ReadDeltaPlayerstate / jmp loc_4EE631` stub
      at 0x361D25 is what gives that away.
        wrapper 0x4EE4E0   if (from == NULL) { zero 0x4890 bytes; sub_4EC4C0(defaults) }
        0x4ee567           memcpy 0x91*128 + 16 = 18576 bytes  from -> to
        0x4ee5ce           MSG_ReadBit    b0
        0x4ee5dd           MSG_ReadBit    b1                  <- TWO bits, not three
        0x4ee5f9           count = [off_12D4BA8][0x38]        = 252
        0x4ee5fc           list  = [off_12D4BA8][0x30]        = 0x12D7490
        0x4ee61e           lastChanged = MSG_ReadBits(32 - lzcnt(count+1)) - 1   (8 bits)
        loop 0x4EE660      skipped = MSG_ReadNumFieldsSkipped(msg, 4, lc - idx)
                           <copy the skipped fields -- NO reads>
                           zeroBase = (b1 == 0) && (field.flags & 4) && a6
                           MSG_ReadDeltaField(...)
                           while (idx < lc)
        0x4EE7E1           SECOND PASS: fields 0..lc-1 with (flags & 2) get another
                           MSG_ReadDeltaField.  **NO playerstate or ET_PLAYER field
                           has flags & 2 (0 of 252 and 0 of 64), so it never runs.**
        0x4EE81C           the CL_GetPredictedPlayerInformation overwrite, above
        0x4EE89B..0x4EF6BB the gated TAIL

⚠ **PS4 IS A DEBUG BUILD AND ITS PLAYERSTATE DIFFERS.** It reads THREE header bits
plus a conditional fourth (`v157`, `v142`), memcpys 18048 not 18576, and carries a
reset-on-spawn verification pass with an extra per-field bit. All of that is
compiled out of retail. Its tail also differs in at least one constant (PS4 reads
31 bits where PC reads 27). **Use PS4 for NAMES and SHAPE; use PC for anything
that must be bit-exact.**

## ⭐ FRAME CHAINING IS MANDATORY, AND NOT ONLY FOR VALUES

Several codecs size their READ from the baseline: `-94` (event) looks the parm
width up from the baseline's event id when the id is unchanged; `-76`/`-75` XOR a
byte against it; the default case XORs against it. So an all-zero baseline
produces a wrong BIT COUNT, not merely a wrong value.

In a demo the message number is the chunk's own `seq`, so
`baseline = frames[seq - deltaNum]` rebuilds the chain offline. Implemented in
`diag/chain.py`; `baseline-missing` counts the frames the recording starts before.

⚠ The chain has NO ANCHOR in a mid-game recording: loose_22's first snapshots are
already `deltaNum = 2` against frames that are not in the file. Absolute values
before the first full snapshot are unrecoverable in principle.

## VERIFIED AGAINST THE ENGINE THIS SESSION (do not re-audit)

    -88   ReadLong then XOR baseline, NO gate bit          case 0xFFA8
    -87   MSG_ReadAngle16, absolute                        case 0xFFA9 -> LABEL_144
    -97/-74/-72/-70  shared time codec: bit ? ReadLong : timeBase - ReadBits(8)
                                                          cases 0xFF9F/B6/B8/BA
    default   bit ? (mixed remainder-bits + whole bytes, XOR masked baseline,
              sign-extend when type < 0) : set 0           PS4 line 1481
    type == 0 -> MSG_ReadFloatCase
    MSG_ReadNumFieldsSkipped @0x4F0780 -- has an `a2 == 1` unary special case;
              for a2 != 1 it is exactly the escape loop already implemented
    netfield record, PC: +0 u16 offset, +2 i16 size, +4 i16 type, +6 u16 flags (8 B)
                    PS4: name ptr first, then +8/+10/+12/+14 (16 B)
    playerstate flags histogram: 0 x158, 1, 4 x5, 16 x66, 20 x4, 64, 128 x9,
                                 256 x3, 528 x5   -- and NO flags & 2 anywhere

## WHERE IT NOW STANDS, HONESTLY

    playerstate field loop     CORRECT (the gate-skew test above)
    frame chaining             implemented
    the gated TAIL             NOT transcribed  <- THE BLOCKER
    sub_4EF6C0, sub_4EE380     NOT transcribed
    entity decoder             STILL UNVALIDATED

End-to-end (playerstate -> N zero gates -> entity list -> 2047 sentinel) passes
5/400, and sweeping the gate count 0..30 gives a scattered histogram with no

**Searching for the entity list is exhausted. The tail has to be transcribed**, and

reads of 4, 1, 27, 2, 8 and 3 bits plus MSG_ReadByte and a 4-byte primitive.

# ⭐⭐⭐⭐ THE MWR SNAPSHOT DECODES END TO END — 0% -> 77% ON svc_EOF (2026-08-21)

Continues the entry above. That one established the playerstate field loop was
right and both oracles I had been using were invalid. This one closes the rest of
the snapshot.

## THE METRIC — and why it is the only one worth quoting

`diag/mwr_eof.py`. CL_ParseMessage is a LOOP of 3-bit opcodes terminating at 7, so
a parse that consumed exactly the right number of bits lands on opcode 7 with the
message spent. A desync lands on a different opcode or runs off the end.

ONE attempt per message. No sweeping, no retries — a metric you can tune is not a
metric. (`diag/eofcheck.py` is the CoD4 equivalent; do not confuse them.)

    loose_37   844 / 1100   76.7%
    loose_33   336 /  432   77.8%
    every other real demo    0.0%

The split is CATEGORICAL, not a gradient, and the cause is known — see ANCHOR below.

## ⭐ THE FULL SNAPSHOT LAYOUT, ALL OF IT TRANSCRIBED FROM THE ENGINE

    3 bits    svc opcode (6)
    MSG_ReadLong    serverTime            0x3427e2
    MSG_ReadByte    deltaNum              0x3427fc
    MSG_ReadByte    snapFlags             0x342826
    MSG_ReadBit     baseline select       0x3428b3
    -- MSG_ReadDeltaPlayerstate (wrapper 0x4EE4E0, body 0x4EE63E) --
    2 bits    b0, b1                      0x4ee5ce / 0x4ee5dd
    8 bits    lastChanged, then -1        0x4ee61e   width = 32 - lzcnt(count+1)
    field loop, skip width 4              0x4EE660
    -- the TAIL: 7 gated sections, each ONE zero bit when empty --
    A 0x4EE89F   mask=ReadBits(4); 3x ReadLong + 1x ReadByte, individually gated
    B 0x4EE970   while(bit): ReadBits(4), bit, ReadBits(27), 2x (bit ? ReadBits(8))
    C 0x4EEAD7   15 records at ps+604/+664         NOT transcribed
    D 0x4EF2A0   while(bit): ReadBits(4),
                   bit ? ReadBits(1) : (ReadBits(27), bit),
                   ReadBits(10)
    E 0x4EF487   hudelems ps+7780, 36 x (3 bits + sub_4F47F0)   NOT transcribed
    F 0x4EF57E   ps+9088 / ps+14848, two sub_4F4B90             NOT transcribed
    G sub_4EE380 (called at 0x4EF68B)     `if (!ReadBit()) return`
    -- back in CL_ParseSnapshot --
    sub_4EF6C0                            `if (!ReadBit()) ...` -> 1 bit empty
    sub_342240 -> sub_4EE310 -> sub_4EE380                      -> 1 bit empty
    ENTITIES  sub_341D30, MSG_ReadEntityIndex(msg, 11)
    if (deltaNum == 0) MSG_ReadByte       0x3429a1   FULL SNAPSHOTS ONLY
    CLIENTS   sub_341960, continue-bit loop, 5-bit index
    AGENTS    sub_341580 CL_ParsePacketAgents, continue-bit loop, 6-bit index
    sub_308550                            `if (!ReadBit()) return`
    sub_342300 -> sub_5008D0              `if (!ReadBit()) return;
                                           if (ReadBit()) ReadValue32 else from[0]`
    3 bits    svc_EOF (7)

**9 zero bits between the playerstate field loop and the entity list** (7 + 1 + 1),
derived TWICE and independently: the all-zero path through the PC disassembly, and
our own WRITER — playerstate.py's TRAILING_SECTIONS emits 7 and entity.py's
write_entity_stream opens with 2 more, and demos built that way play in the engine.
My earlier model said 8.

## ⭐⭐ THE TRAILING RUN, ACCOUNTED FOR BIT BY BIT

400 of 400 snapshots put svc_EOF exactly 5 bits after the entity list, with an
IDENTICAL trailing pattern `0001011100`. Every bit is explained by a function
that was read, not fitted:

    bit0 = 0   clients: continue bit clear -> empty
    bit1 = 0   agents:  continue bit clear -> empty
    bit2 = 0   sub_308550 gate clear
    bit3 = 1   sub_5008D0 gate SET
    bit4 = 0   sub_5008D0's second bit -> take the value from the baseline, no read
    bits 5,6,7 = 1,1,1 = svc_EOF

400/400 agreeing on the position AND the pattern is not chance; it is proof the
playerstate, the 9-gate tail and the entity list all end where the engine ends them.

## ⭐ THE ANCHOR — why most demos read 0%

MWR's gamestate carries NO entity baselines (configstrings and EOF only). Entity
baselines can therefore come only from previous snapshots, and an entity's eType is
usually NOT SENT — measured: `firstSkip = 2` on every sampled record, so field 0 is
skipped and copied from the baseline.

With no baseline, eType reads 0, `MSG_GetStateFieldListForEntityType(0)` returns the
GENERIC list (63 fields) instead of ET_PLAYER (64), and every field after is read at
the wrong width.

So the chain needs an anchor: a snapshot with `deltaNum == 0`.

    loose_37   first snapshot seq 36,   deltaNum 0      ANCHORED   76.7%
    loose_33                                            ANCHORED   77.8%
    loose_22   first snapshot seq 13,   deltaNum 2      NO ANCHOR   0.0%

Measured effect on loose_37 of chaining entity baselines across snapshots:
**entities-fail 1217 -> 3.** That single change is what turned the entity list from
"never parses" into "parses".

⚠ The same anchor problem applies to the PLAYERSTATE, and to a demo recorded
mid-match it is unfixable in principle: the frames the first snapshots delta against
are not in the file.

## ⭐ FRAME AND ENTITY CHAINING ARE BOTH MANDATORY, AND FOR THE SAME REASON

Several codecs size their READ from the baseline — `-94` (event) looks the parm
width up from the baseline's event id when the id is unchanged, `-76`/`-75` XOR a
byte against it, and the default case XORs against it. An all-zero baseline gets the
BIT COUNT wrong, not merely the value.

    playerstate  baseline = frames[seq - deltaNum]   (seq is the chunk's own number)
    entities     baseline = the same entity number in the previous frame, carried
                 forward across snapshots

## ⭐ THE SECOND FIELD-LIST REGISTRY — neither playerstate nor clientState is in the
## eType table

MSG_ReadDeltaPlayerstate and MSG_ReadDeltaClient both index a SECOND registry: the
object at `*0x12D4BA8 == 0x12D4D00`, {ptr, count} at stride 16.

    +0x00  0x12D6E40   71
    +0x10  0x12D7080   92    clientState   (MSG_ReadDeltaClient @0x4ECB00)
    +0x20  0x12D7360   37
    +0x30  0x12D7490  252    playerState   (0x4EE5F9 / 0x4EE5FC)
    +0x40  0x12D7C70    7

`clientState` is 212 bytes (0xD4, from MSG_ReadDeltaClient's own memset) and its
"absent" marker is 0x7FF written at +12.

MSG_ReadDeltaClient is: `if (ReadBit() == 1) return;` then a delta-struct read —
so a client that did not change costs ONE BIT.

## ⛔ WHAT IS STILL NOT DONE

  * **tail sections C, E, F** are gated, not parsed. C is transcribable in shape but
    its bit count depends on a client-side mode flag (writer local v82) that is not
    in the stream, so decoding it offline would be a guess. Together they account
    for ~9k of the 38.7k corpus attempts.
  * **the client and agent sections are gated, not parsed.** The shape is known
    (continue-bit loop, 5/6-bit index, then MSG_ReadDeltaClient) but sub_4EDAF0 is a
    5-byte Arxan thunk, so the delta-struct's lastChanged width, skip width and
    whether it carries the playerstate's `-1` are unread. A sweep of all 18
    combinations against the svc_EOF oracle scored ZERO, so the shape is wrong
    somewhere too — do not just re-run the sweep.
  * **the entity decoder is validated only for EMPTY lists.** All 1492 corpus passes
    have 0 entities, and the handful of non-empty ones decode eTypes of 253/212/175,
    which are impossible after the engine's clamp at 20. Non-empty entity lists are
    still wrong.

## Method notes worth keeping

  * **`re/mwr/bitflow.py`** collapses the inlined MSG_ReadBit idiom in a
    DISASSEMBLY into one `ReadBit() -> jz loc_X` line each. The PC build inlines it
    ~20 instructions deep at every gate, which hides the structure completely; the
    reduced form made the whole 3.6 KB tail readable in one pass. Anything it does
    not recognise is printed verbatim, so a missed read shows as noise rather than
    vanishing.
  * **READ THE WRITER.** MSG_WriteDeltaPlayerstate (PC 0x4F52E0) states each tail
    section's format directly in a few lines where the reader takes pages. Same
    lesson the CoD4 work recorded and it paid off again immediately.
  * **A saved decompile goes stale the moment you rename anything.** Every
    `MSG_ReadShort` in the .c files under re/mwr/ is really MSG_ReadBit — the dumps
    predate that correction. Re-dump, or read the disassembly.
  * `py_eval` runs under `exec` with split globals/locals, so a genexpr or nested
    def cannot see names bound at the top level. Wrap the body in `def main(): ...`
    and call it. Hit again this session.
  * JSON-RPC payloads: use FORWARD SLASHES in Windows paths. A backslash makes the
    request unparseable ("Invalid \escape").

## ⚠ ADDENDUM, SAME SESSION — WHAT THE 77% IS AND IS NOT

The two demos that score ~77% (loose_33, loose_37) are **near-empty recordings**.

So that number validates the FRAMING -- header, playerstate field loop, the nine

## ⛔ THE REMAINING DEFECT, LOCALISED PRECISELY

`loose_12` carries real content: 1449 FULL snapshots (deltaNum 0), 329 bytes each,
playerstate `lastChanged = 251` of 252 -- i.e. nearly every field is sent, so the
codec table is fully exercised for the first time.

All 1449 fail identically:

    ValueError: entity index out of range: 2067

and the decoded entity index sequence is **byte-for-byte identical across all of
them** -- [513, 673, 737, 981, 2019, 2019, 2067] -- while the 1449 message bodies
are all DISTINCT (1459 distinct md5s). Identical output from distinct inputs can
only mean the entity list is being entered far past its real position, in a
constant tail region of the message.

**So a large-lastChanged playerstate desynchronises, and the fault is in the codec
table or the field loop under full load.** That is the next thing to fix, and it is
now sharply bounded: one demo, one reproducible failure, 251 fields per snapshot to
bisect, and `diag/mwr_eof.py` as the pass/fail oracle.

## ⭐ THE ENTITY DECODER IS CAPABLE — the residual is a VARIABLE under-read

Scanning a full snapshot for any bit position at which the entity list parses
cleanly (>= 3 entities, strictly increasing indices, every eType <= 20,
terminating on the 2047 sentinel) finds real lists:

    loose_12 seq 39, my entity start = bit 981
        bit 1014  (+33)   10 entities   eTypes {0, 10}
        bit 1233  (+252)  17 entities   eTypes {0, 1}   <- ET_PLAYER
        bit 1997  (+1016)  4 entities   eTypes {0}

**So `read_delta_entity` and `read_entity_list` can decode a real MWR entity
list, ET_PLAYER records included.** They are not the defect.

Taking the BEST list within +/-400 bits over 80 full snapshots:

    delta +252 -> 17 entities   29 snapshots
    delta +165 -> 22 entities    6
    no clean list at all        45

⚠ **The shortfall is VARIABLE (165 vs 252), not a fixed missing field.** A constant
would mean one unread scalar; a variable one means a DATA-DEPENDENT length is
being read too short. And it is upstream of the entity list, because the tail
gates C/E/F/G all read 0 on these snapshots and A/B parse with byte accounting
that checks out (mask 13 -> two 4-byte reads + one 1-byte, rc 108 -> 118).

## PRIME SUSPECT — the `-94` event codec

It is the one codec whose BIT COUNT comes from a runtime table:

    id changed   -> ReadByte(id); bits = g_eventParmBits[id]; then a GATED parm
    id unchanged -> bits = g_eventParmBits[baseline id]; parm read UNGATED

The playerstate has FOUR of them (fields 20/21/22/23, offsets 224/232/240/248,
size 8) and in the failing trace they sit 26 bits apart each -- so a wrong width
on all four is easily a hundred bits, and it varies with the data, which matches
the observed 165-vs-252 spread exactly.

Check `mwr_event_parm_bits.json` against `g_eventParmBits` in the PC IDB, and
re-read the case-0xFFA6 body for the gated/ungated asymmetry, before anything else.

Both are transcribed from the engine and are required for correctness; neither
changed the failure, which is worth recording so they are not re-attempted:

  * `reader.playerstate_defaults()` -- sub_4EC4C0, the baseline a FULL snapshot
    deltas against (2046/2047 sentinels, 1.0f floats, 800). NOT zeros.
  * `reader.entity_defaults()` -- MSG_ReadDeltaEntity's `if (a6)` block, the
    per-eType baseline for a brand-new entity.

## ⭐ TELLING A REAL RECORDING FROM ONE OF OUR CONVERSIONS

Two independent markers, both cheap:

    real       has an `update_gamestate_data` chunk;  predicted_data >> network_data
               (loose_22: 22340 vs 2337, about 10:1)
    converted  no gamestate chunk; contains the string "offline convert";
               predicted_data ~= network_data (1:1)

17 of the 38 files in `loose/` are our own conversions. Testing the reader against

## ⛔ THE EVENT-PARM TABLE WAS THE PS4's — 54 OF 186 ENTRIES WRONG

`mwr_event_parm_bits.json` was dumped from the PS4 build. The `-94` codec sizes its
parm read from that table, so on the PC build it was reading the wrong width for
every event whose entry differs -- and it differs a lot:

    ev  5..9, 15, 16, 35..37   PS4 31  ->  PC 27
    ev 39, 40, 44, 45          PS4 12  ->  PC  6
    54 of 186 entries differ in total

The PC table is **`dword_91F690`** (186 dwords), reached from PC case 0xFFA2 ->
`sub_4ED000`. The PS4's is `qword_F9BA00` -- reading THAT address in the PC IDB
gives all zeros, which is how the mix-up went unnoticed.

Installed as `mwr_event_parm_bits.json`; the PS4 copy is kept alongside as
`mwr_event_parm_bits.ps4.json`.

MEASURED effect on loose_12's full snapshots: "no clean entity list found anywhere
in the message" fell from **45 of 60 to 25 of 60**. Real, and necessary -- but it
did not move the start offset, so it was not the position error.

⚠ ALSO CORRECTED in `_c_event`: the parm's unchanged-path mask is
`bits < 32 ? ~(-1 << bits) : -1` -- a test on the WIDTH. I had it as
`ev == 183 ? -1 : (1 << bits) - 1`, a test on the event ID, which came from the
PS4 decompile. Value-only, no bit-count effect.

**GENERALISE, again: a table dumped from one build is not the other build's table.**
Same lesson as the 271-vs-252 playerstate field counts and the 31-vs-27 tail read.
Use PS4 for NAMES and SHAPE; take every NUMBER from the PC build that actually runs.

## STATE AT THE END OF THIS SESSION

    framing (header, playerstate loop, 9-gate tail, trailing run)   PROVEN
       loose_37  844/1100  76.3%      loose_33  336/438  76.7%
       and 400/400 land on svc_EOF exactly 5 bits after the entity list,
       with every one of those 5 bits accounted for by a function that was read
    entity decoder    CAPABLE -- 17 entities including ET_PLAYER at the right offset
    residual          a +252 (29/60) or +165 (6/60) bit gap before the entity list
                      on FULL snapshots.  Bimodal, not continuous, so it reads more
                      like two message shapes than a data-dependent length.

NEXT: bisect that gap. The playerstate reads only 36 fields of lastChanged=251 in
853 bits (32% of a 329-byte message), the tail then parses cleanly (A mask=13,
B one record, C..G and both trailing gates zero), and the entity list wants to
start 252 bits later. Either a tail section's BODY under-reads, or a codec inside
the 36 fields does. `diag/mwr_eof.py` is the pass/fail oracle and loose_12 is the
reproducer.
