# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PRODUCTISATION PASS — 2026-08-31. THE MOD IS NOW A PRODUCT WITH A
# WORKBENCH BEHIND IT, NOT A WORKBENCH WITH A PRODUCT IN IT.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

USER: *"lets make our s2mp-mod into a usable product, at it's current state it's
heavily experimental and not really usable reliably, and it's confusing. I want
this to be super simplistic, clean and working"*.

Scope decided WITH the user (AskUserQuestion), and the answers matter:

  1. demo systems  -> **keep both, unified UI**  (not "delete the custom one")
  2. probe commands -> **hide behind a dev flag** (not delete)
  3. features       -> **keep all**, but hide everything except the demo
                       CAMERA TOOLS

So nothing was removed for being experimental. The change is entirely about
what is VISIBLE by default.

## THE MEASURED PROBLEM

    150 console commands, ~60 of them one-off investigation probes
    two demo systems presented side by side in one tab, with two record
      buttons, two Play buttons, two transports and two folders
    4 dead stub files (killfeed, demo_avidemo, MapEntLoader, FontLoader)
      still being compiled and init()-ed
    comment blocks drifted away from the code they describe

## ⭐ WHAT WAS BUILT

**`src/DevMode.{hpp,cpp}`** — the product / workbench split.

    dev_mode::init()                read the persisted flag (<mod dir>/dev_mode)
    dev_mode::enabled()
    dev_mode::set(bool)             persist + fire pending callbacks
    dev_mode::on_enable(fn)         fires now if already on, else on the switch
    dev_mode::add_command(name, fn) the common case, same shape as
                                    GameUtil::addCommand

⭐ THE CALLBACK DESIGN IS LOAD-BEARING, not decoration. A module cannot simply
test `enabled()` at init time, because turning developer mode on at RUNTIME must
register the extra commands too. And `Cmd_AddCommandInternal` has NO duplicate
check — a second entry silently shadows the first — so every callback is fired
AT MOST ONCE and `add_command` drains its pending list exactly once.

`dev_mode::init()` runs in ExtConsole BEFORE any module init, and after the
build-map detection (mod_dir() needs to know Steam vs Store).

Turning it OFF hides the UI but leaves already-registered commands alive for the
session. Unregistering mid-session buys nothing and risks the engine's command
list.

**`src/demo/demo_player.{hpp,cpp}`** — one list, one transport, two engines.

Dispatches on the file EXTENSION: `.demo` -> demo_native, `.dm_s2` ->
demo_playback. Adds NO hooks and owns no engine state; it is a router.

    demo_list / demo_play <name> / demo_stop / demo_pause
    demo_seek <seconds>  (negative rewinds)
    demo_speed <0.1..4.0>
    demo_record <0|1>

`demo_play` resolves a BARE NAME against both libraries (exact filename, then
stem) so the user never types an extension or a path. The library is sorted
NEWEST FIRST — the demo you just recorded is the one you want.

Seek is asymmetric by necessity and that is hidden here: native forward is a
cheap realtime skip, native backward has to land on a keyframe, and the custom
theater takes an absolute time. One `demo_seek -5` drives all three.

## RESULT

    console commands   150  ->  41 product  +  108 developer
    the 41 are ALL demo / camera / filming, plus map, clear, unlockall, s2_dev
    GUI tabs           7 always  ->  3 always (Demos, Dolly, Bone Cam)
                                     + 4 in developer mode
    src                40,986  ->  ~39,900 lines (4 dead stubs deleted)
    build              clean, deployed, hash-verified

The Demos tab is now: a recording switch, one library list, Play/Stop/Repair,
and — only while something is playing — progress, transport, speed, camera and
HUD. The old tab interleaved custom controls, engine controls, an engine
transport, HUD toggles, a freecam slider, a Com_Error log, a custom scrub bar
and an avidemo button.

## ⚠ ONE REAL BUG THE REWRITE INTRODUCED AND CAUGHT

Removing `demoforward` / `demorewind` orphaned the ARROW-KEY seek in
`demo_gui.cpp`, which still issued those commands — so Left/Right would have
silently done nothing during custom playback. Found by grepping for every
removed command name across the tree, not by the compiler: a `Cbuf_AddText` of a
command that no longer exists compiles perfectly and fails at runtime, silently.

**RULE: after removing a console command, grep the WHOLE tree (including .cfg
and .ps1) for its name.** The build cannot help you.

## ⚠ RULE A25 FIRED FOUR MORE TIMES IN ONE SESSION

A quoted bash heredoc (`<<'PYEOF'`) ate backslashes on four separate occasions:

    "\\dev_mode"         -> "\dev_mode"     C4129 unrecognized escape
    "...tabs, and\\n"    -> a REAL NEWLINE inside a C++ string literal (C2001)
    stub.replace('/','\\')  -> unterminated Python string literal

Only the third failed loudly. The other two compiled or nearly compiled.

**Use the Write/Edit tools for generated content. If a shell layer is
unavoidable, build the backslash from `chr(92)`.** The one-line detector that
catches the C++ case instantly:

    awk '{c=gsub(/"/,"&"); if (c%2==1) print FILENAME": "NR}' <file>

## ⚠ AND A SILENT `str.replace` NO-OP

`demo_playback.hpp` was "patched" with new declarations and the patch matched
nothing — the anchor assumed no blank line between two declarations. The script
printed "patched" because it only tested whether the TARGET was already present,
not whether the replace succeeded. The compiler caught it, but only two builds
later.

**A replace-based patch must assert its anchor matched, not assert the goal is
not yet met.** Already recorded once in this file; repeated anyway.

## ⚠ `grep -E 'error' | tail` MASKS THE BUILD EXIT CODE

`msbuild ... 2>&1 | grep ... | tail` exits with GREP's status, so a failing
build reported `[exited with code 0]`. Redirect to a log and echo `$?` BEFORE
the pipe, or check the log for `: error`.

## WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE

  * **Neither demo system was deleted.** The user chose "both, unified UI".
  * **No engine-facing behaviour was changed.** Every hook, fix and address is
    exactly as it was. This pass moved command REGISTRATION and rewrote UI; it
    did not touch a single stub or offset.
  * `src/s2mp-mod.vcxproj` — a stale orphan project file from June that the
    solution does not reference. Left alone; it is confusing but harmless, and
    deleting a tracked file is the user's call.
  * `src/ei.txt` — a 2-byte stray containing "ei". Untracked, harmless, left.

## FILES

    NEW      src/DevMode.{hpp,cpp}            src/demo/demo_player.{hpp,cpp}
             README.md                        (the product's own documentation)
    DELETED  src/demo/killfeed.{cpp,hpp}      src/demo/demo_avidemo.{cpp,hpp}
             src/MapEntLoader.{cpp,hpp}       src/FontLoader.{cpp,hpp}
    API      demo_playback:: play / stop / seek_to      (were command-only)
             demo_recording:: start
             demo_native::    auto_record / set_auto_record

NOT YET RUN IN GAME. Per the Fix Declaration Rules this is a CANDIDATE: it
builds, deploys and is hash-verified, but the UI has not been exercised.

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# FILMING FEATURES — FIVE ENGINE CAPABILITIES FOUND AND EXPOSED (2026-08-31)
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Follows the productisation pass above. The user asked what else a demo tool
should have; four of the five answers turned out to be capabilities the engine
ALREADY SHIPS with no front-end.

## ⚠ THE IDB USED WAS **NOT** THE AUTHORITATIVE ONE

    server_health  idb   C:\Users\joshu\OneDrive\Documents\s2x_dump.exe (1).i64
                   input F:\SteamLibrary\...\Call of Duty WWII\s2x_dump.exe
                   port  11224          (13337 was NOT listening)

RULE A10 names `E:\SteamLibrary\...\s2x_dump.exe.i64` as authoritative. RULE A2
PASSES on this copy (0xBCE9E0 == "EXE_ERR_PROCESS_DEMO_FILE_FAILED"), so IDA
addresses match CLAUDE.md with no shift and every finding below transfers.

⭐ BUT IT CARRIES A DIFFERENT NAME SET — 2,746 named functions, independently
applied, and they DISAGREE with CLAUDE.md on the same addresses:

    address     CLAUDE.md                    this IDB
    0x9135D0    CL_Demo_FollowCameraMove     CL_Demo_UpdatePlaybackView
    0x913AE0    CL_Demo_FreeCameraMove       CL_Demo_UpdateViewOrigin
    0x915E40    CL_Demo_HandleAction         CL_Demo_OnCommandFromGame
    0x916740    CL_Demo_HiResScreenshot      CL_Demo_CaptureScreenshot
    0x91AB50    CL_Demo_SetCameraMode        CL_Demo_SetHudViewMode
    0x8C9C0     CG_CalcViewValues            sub_8C9C0  (not named here)

Neither set is wrong; they are two independent naming passes. **Work from
ADDRESSES across the two databases, never from names.** Helper for this server:
`re/s2ida.py`.

## ⭐⭐⭐ 1. THE CLIP SYSTEM IS COMPLETE AND THE ARGUMENT IS THE WHOLE INTERFACE

`CL_Demo_SaveSegment_f` @0x911060, decompiled in full:

    if (argc != 2) return;
    if (clc[+262752] != 2) return;              // == CL_IsDemoPlaying
    v2 = atoi(argv[1]);
    if (v2)  { markIn = currentTime; }                       // NON-ZERO -> MARK IN
    else     { segment[count].start = markIn - base;
               segment[count].end   = CL_Demo_SetPlaybackEndTimeMs() - base;
               count++; CL_Demo_SetSegmentsDirty(); }        // ZERO -> MARK OUT

So the entire in/out interface is:

    cl_demo_savesegment 1     mark IN
    cl_demo_savesegment 0     mark OUT and append the segment

Corroborated by its siblings, all at the same gate:

    CL_Demo_PreviewSegment_f @0x910D30   seek to segment n (-1 = current)
    CL_Demo_PreviewClip_f    @0x910CB0   WriteClipSnapshot, set preview, seek 0
    CL_Demo_DeleteClip_f     @0x90FC50   zeroes playbackData+6096400

⭐ `CL_Demo_DeleteClip_f` zeroing exactly one field is what IDENTIFIES
**playbackData + 6096400 = the segment COUNT** — proof from the engine rather
than an offset guess.

The gate is `clc+262752 == 2`, which is true during native playback, so this
needed NO hook and NO patch. Four buttons.

## ⭐⭐ 2. FOV IS A PLAIN DVAR, AND THERE IS A SHIPPED OVERRIDE

`sub_45760` is the FOV chooser (found via the dvar registration `sub_507E0`,
which registers cg_fov / cg_fov1 / cg_fov_intermission / cg_fov_override / "3078"):

    intermission?              -> cg_fov_intermission   off_11111C8
    splitscreen client 1?      -> cg_fov1               off_11111C0
    per-client scale > 0       -> cg_fov * scale        (clientObf + 4431600)
    cg_fov_override > 0        -> the override          off_11111E0
    else                       -> cg_fov                off_11111B8

    cg_fov          flags 0x400001 = user-settable + archived
    cg_fov_override flags 0, default -1.0 (disabled)
    cg_fovScale     is the numeric dvar "3078"          off_11111D0

`off_11111E0 = cg_fov_override` confirmed from the registration itself
(`v14 = sub_B0B60("cg_fov_override", ..., 0); ... off_11111E0 = v14;`).

⚠ NOTE THE PRIORITY: the per-client scale at `clientObf + 4431600` BEATS the
override when it is > 0, so an active ADS/zoom scale wins. Not a defect, but it
means the slider will appear to do nothing while scoped.

`sub_AF220` is the obfuscated float getter (sibling of the already-documented
`Dvar_GetBool_Obfuscated` @0xAF180) — it decompiles as a stub returning 0, so
read the value at `dvar+16` directly instead of calling it.

## ⭐ 3. THIRD-PERSON FRAMING — TWO INSTRUCTIONS, NOT TWO CONSTANTS

`CL_Demo_UpdatePlaybackView` @0x9135D0 and `CL_Demo_TraceViewForward` @0x913830:

    0x9137C1   F3 0F 58 05 disp32   addss xmm0, [rip+d]   dword_B378E8 = 35.0  eye height
    0x913939   F3 0F 10 0D disp32   movss xmm1, [rip+d]   dword_B2D3A4 = 85.0  pull-back

⛔ **DO NOT PATCH THE CONSTANTS.** dword_B378E8 has **17 xrefs** and
dword_B2D3A4 has **12** — they are shared across the engine. Repoint the two
INSTRUCTIONS' rip-relative displacements at floats we own, exactly as the
free-camera speed patch already does. That touches one call site each.

The same decompile also re-confirms the camera field block, independently of the
dolly work:

    cg + 2355648/52/56   origin      (+2355656 is the one that gets +35.0)
    cg + 2355660/64/68   angles      pitch, yaw, ROLL
    cg + 2355672/76/80   velocity    zeroed here every frame

## ⭐ 4. ROLL IS PLUMBED AND SIMPLY NEVER FED

Both camera movers write `cg+2355668` from usercmd angle[2] every frame — and a
mouse only ever produces pitch and yaw, so the field is written with zero
forever. Writing it AFTER the mover runs gives a dutch angle, and because the
engine rewrites it every frame there is no stale-state risk.

⛔ CORRECTS an earlier note in this file that said roll is "discarded". What
`CL_Demo_SetCameraMode` zeroes is the SEED (`clientActive+25908`), not the field.

## 5. THE HI-RES SCREENSHOT WAS BEING BLOCKED BY US

`CL_Demo_CaptureScreenshot` @0x916740 is the engine's own TILED capture
(240x180 tiles at 1440). It is action 17, which we block by default because it
"freezes the demo and moves the camera" — which is exactly what a tiled capture
does. `demo_native::transport()` calls the ORIGINAL handler, so it can be offered
as a deliberate button while F3 stays blocked.

## ⭐ THE DEMO LIBRARY — new, and it needed no RE at all

`src/demo/demo_library.{hpp,cpp}`. Everything to describe a demo is in the file
and the format was already fully proven:

    header +0x00 version 29, +0x04 headerSize 79384 (ALSO the body offset),
           +0x08 recording client
    footer last 8 bytes [u32 size][u32 magic 29]; body begins [29, 3984]
           and carries the MAP NAME at body + 272
    body   byte-tagged packets from +79384

⭐ DURATION WITHOUT DECOMPRESSING ANYTHING: the type-1 client archive is
UNCOMPRESSED and carries serverTime at packet offset 37 (from the corrected
"THE ARCHIVE PACKET, EXACT" read order). First-to-last archive = the duration.

Two tiers, so the list stays fast:
  * `describe()`      header + footer only, two seeks. Every row.
  * `describe_full()` adds duration by walking the stream. Selected row only,
                      cached per selection change.

A demo whose footer is missing (the game was killed mid-recording) is flagged IN
THE LIST as "will not play", instead of failing when Play is pressed.

## SHIPPED

    NEW   src/demo/demo_library.{hpp,cpp}   describe / rename / delete
          src/demo/demo_camera.{hpp,cpp}    FOV, framing, roll, screenshot
          re/s2ida.py                       JSON-RPC helper for port 11224
    API   demo_native:: clip_count / clip_mark_in / clip_mark_out
                        clip_preview / clip_clear
          demo_player:: selected_details / tidy_names, Entry::info
    CMD   demo_fov  demo_thirdperson  demo_roll  demo_screenshot  demo_autoname
    UI    demo list now shows map / date / size and flags unplayable demos;
          Tidy names, Rename, Delete (two-step);
          Clip panel (Mark In / Mark Out / Preview / Clear + segment count);
          Framing panel (FOV, 3rd-person distance + height, roll, screenshot).

Recordings are auto-renamed to `<map>_<date>_<time>` when recording stops —
AFTER the type-21 repair, deliberately: renaming first would leave a
nicely-named demo that does not play if the repair failed.

Builds clean, deployed, hash-verified. **NOT run in game — a CANDIDATE.**

## What to watch for on the first run

    [cam] third-person framing: adjustable (height 35, distance 85)
          -- if it says "stock, one or both patches declined", the opcode check
             refused, which is the guard working, not a fault.
    [rec] saved as mp_shipment_s2_2026-08-31_1900.demo
    the Clip panel's segment count moving 0 -> 1 after Mark In + Mark Out

## Honest limits

  * FOV: the per-client scale beats it while scoped (see above).
  * Roll: applied through dolly's existing free-camera hook, so it affects the
    FREE camera. Third person writes the same field, but is not hooked.
  * Duration: only for ENGINE demos. The .dm_s2 container is a different format.
  * Clip export writes SEGMENTS into the engine's clip state. Whether that
    produces a standalone file, and where, is NOT established -- previewclip
    plays them back in-engine, which is what the buttons promise.

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# NEW TARGET -- MW3-STEAM (iw5mp_dumpx64.exe, port 13999) NAMING PASS
# 2026-09-06. 54 -> 2,194 named. IDB SAVED.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Steam pushed a 64-bit MW3 client update (Windows PE, `iw5mp_dumpx64.exe`, was
previously 32-bit `iw5mp.exe`). Dumped and opened in IDA on port **13999**.
Registered in `.mcp.json` as `MW3-Steam` and in `re/ida.py`'s PORTS dict as
`"mw3steam"`. The user pointed out the two builds have different imagebases
but that does not matter for the method here -- MW3 has no ASLR, so every
address in each build is a fixed, deterministic constant; cross-referencing
between the two IDBs is done by RVA/name, never a raw literal, exactly as the
Steam<->Xbox and CoD4<->CoD4X passes already required.

## THE PAIR

    port 14200  MW3          COD_MW3_MPsub          macOS Mach-O, imagebase 0x1000
                             99.31% named (17,758 funcs), Itanium-mangled C++
                             -- the REFERENCE. Same shape as the CoD4-Mac
                             reference at port 18337: Aspyr Mac port, fully
                             symboled, same segment naming convention
                             (__symbol_stub / __stub_helper / __la_symbol_ptr).
    port 13999  MW3-Steam    iw5mp_dumpx64.exe      Windows PE, imagebase 0x140000000
                             0.37% named (14,716 funcs) -- the TARGET.

`.text` sizes are almost identical (4.31 MB Mac vs 4.27 MB Steam), and
`strprobe.py` confirmed shared string literals with matching owner counts
(`cg_fov`, `sv_maxclients`, `cl_paused`, `clientinfo`, `connect`) before any
naming was attempted -- the same sanity check CLAUDE.md's CoD4 work already
established as step one.

## METHOD -- reused the CoD4-Mac -> CoD4X pipeline verbatim, retargeted

Copied `cod4x_common.py` / `cod4x_score.py` / `cod4x_propagate.py` /
`cod4x_crossval.py` into `re/mw3_common.py` / `mw3_score.py` / `mw3_propagate.py`
/ `mw3_crossval.py`, pointed at `mw3_*` / `mw3steam_*` JSON instead of
`cod4_*` / `cod4x_*`. `re/baseline2.py`, `strprobe.py`, `xsegs.py`,
`xstrings.py`, `xexport.py` were already generic (take any `PORTS` key) and
needed no changes at all.

Same evidence tiers, same filters (Itanium demangling via
`demangle_itanium.py`, the segment-based / underscore-based Apple-API
blocklist -- never a bare prefix guess, per the CoD4 lesson about `CG` also
matching `CG_`), same DOMINANCE collision-recovery rule (>=3x runner-up, >=3
anchors), same "function size is never evidence" rule (cross-compiler).

## RESULTS

    string anchors            5,850 usable  ->  838 applicable proposals
      multi 323 | dominant 15 | single_strong 149 | single_weak 351
    call-graph propagation    838 seed -> converged at round 12, +1,219
                              (total map 2,057; MIN_SUPPORT=2)

### Cross-validated BEFORE applying (mw3_crossval.py, 4 repeats x 5 folds)

    MIN_SUPPORT=2: 1443 answers, 1421 correct, 98.48% precision
        multi 98.63%  dominant 100.00%  single_strong 99.27%  single_weak 97.80%
    MIN_SUPPORT=3: 924 answers, 919 correct, 99.46% precision
    16 contradictions found and EXCLUDED (union over both support levels),
    e.g. 0x1400c5890 anchor='CL_Demo_ReadDemoMessage' vs propagated
    'CG_ScoresDown' -- dropped, not adjudicated, per the skill.

Confirms the CoD4X-pass finding generalises: for a SAME-GAME cross-platform
pair, `single_weak` is not meaningfully weaker than `multi` (97.80% vs
98.63%) -- unlike the cross-TITLE AW->S2 pass, where a shared generic string
really can be coincidence. All four tiers were applied.

### Applied -- 2,040 names (822 anchor + 1,218 propagation), then a second pass

Every name carries a `Basis:` comment with the tier, reference address,
anchor strings or propagation support, and the measured precision figure
(`[mw3mac-anchor:<tier>]` / `[mw3mac-propagation gen N]` markers).

`ida_name.set_name(..., SN_FORCE)` was verified by READING BACK the name
after every write (RULE A3.1/mismatch trap: `SN_FORCE` silently appends
`_0` on a collision instead of failing) -- 0 mismatches across both passes.

### Second source, tier 1 -- console command self-naming

`Cmd_AddCommandInternal` was itself named by propagation
(`char *Cmd_AddCommandInternal(char *name, __int64 handler, __int64 slot)`,
fastcall rcx/rdx/r8). Harvested every call site by walking backward from the
`call` instruction tracking the last `lea`/`mov` into rcx and rdx (a decompile
regex over quoted-string literals did NOT work here -- IDA renders string data
refs as symbol names like `aHidehud`, not inline string literals, unlike the
S2 pass where a regex sufficed):

    149 call sites -> 147 resolved -> 124 after dropping 2 CFG-guard-thunk
    misresolutions (`_guard_check_icall_nop`) -> 120 single-command handlers,
    2 multi-command dispatchers (`cl_demo_play`/`cl_demo_timedemo` sharing one
    handler -- EXACTLY the pair CLAUDE.md's S2 doctrine already documents from
    the Mac CoD4-family reference, independent confirmation of the harvest).

Applied `<command>_f` (the proven engine convention -- 8 functions already
carried it from the anchor pass, e.g. `CL_Demo_Play_f`, `CL_Connect_f`) to
100 previously-unnamed handlers (20 were already correctly named by the
anchor/propagation pass -- zero disagreement). The one surviving dispatcher
was left `sub_` with a comment listing every command it serves (`toggle`,
`togglep`), never named after one caller.

## AUDIT -- `re/audit_names.py`, extended with an MW3MAC reference set

Added `MW3MAC` alongside the existing `COD4MAC`/`AW`/`MWR` phantom-reference
checks (loads `mw3_funcs.json`, cleans names via `mw3_common.clean_ref_name`,
matches on the `[mw3mac-` comment marker) -- same shape as the CoD4MAC
addition, so a name claiming the MW3-Mac reference as its basis is checked
against what that reference actually contains.

    python re/audit_names.py --port 13999 --evidence none \
        --dump <abs>/mw3steam_named_dump.json --report <abs>/mw3steam_audit_report.json

Both runs: **PASS, 0 hard findings** (0 contradiction, 0 duplicate, 0 phantom
reference). The 54 "no recorded basis" are the ORIGINAL import/CRT stub names
that predate this pass entirely (`fnInternetCallback`, `__CxxFrameHandler4`,
`__GSHandlerCheck_EH4`, ...) -- expected, not a defect. The one "differs only
by case" (`SL_GetString` / `SL_GetString_`) is two genuinely distinct
functions, reviewed and left alone.

WARNING: `--dump`/`--report` paths MUST be absolute -- IDA writes the dump from
its own working directory, so a relative path fails with `FileNotFoundError` on
this side (RULE, already documented for the CoD4X pass, hit again here).

## COVERAGE

    named   0.37% (54)     ->  14.23% (2,094)   after the anchor+propagation pass
                            ->  14.91% (2,194)   after the command-table pass
    >=256B  0.07% (3/4544)  ->  22.95% (1,043/4,544)

IDB saved both times (`idb_save` via curl with `-m 600`, per RULE A10 -- the
call exceeds the MCP tool's default timeout but the save itself succeeds).

     exist as seeds instead of 838 -- propagation compounds with density,
     exactly as the S2 and CoD4X passes measured. Not yet re-run this session.
  2. `Dvar_Register*` self-naming tables (the S2/CoD4X precedent's other big
     tier-1 source) -- not attempted yet for MW3.
  3. GSC/script builtin dispatch table, if MW3 has a name/function-pointer
     form of it (S2 turned out NOT to -- see the S2 doctrine's "GSC hash
     table" dead-end -- untested here).
  4. The remaining 12,522 `sub_` functions, most of which currently have zero
     mapped neighbour and so cannot be reached by graph propagation at all
     (the same "density is the ceiling, not method cleverness" finding from
     the CoD4X pass 2 applies here too, unverified but likely).

# ⛔ FAILED ATTEMPT — demo_release_frontend WAS NOT THE cl_demo_play HANG CAUSE
# (2026-09-15). The 2026-08-13 test finally ran; it disproves candidate (b).

Attempt: per the 2026-08-13 entry's own prescribed test -- `demo_release_frontend 0`
then `cl_demo_play` a light map (mp_shipment_s2) -- to distinguish "our own frontend
release" from "a genuine engine race in CL_Demo_Play_f's teardown" as the cause of
the recurring cl_demo_play hang.

Result: the hang reproduced IDENTICALLY with the release disabled. A full game
restart followed by `cl_demo_play` on a DIFFERENT map ALSO hung, in the same shape.
Confirmed via `tools/dump_stacks.py` against the live process before killing it --
same IDA addresses as the 2026-08-13 occurrence:

    main thread     R_SyncRenderThread+0x34 (0x8BD224) <- CL_ShutdownAll+0xD (0x8815D)
                    <- CL_Demo_Play_f+0x4BD (0x910B0D)
    renderer worker 0x8E865E -> 0x8E6CC9 -> 0x8E6FFF -> 0x675DC0 (thread proc)

Reason the release was never the cause: candidate (a) -- a genuine race inside the
engine's own CL_Demo_Play_f teardown -- is what remains. The mod's asset-release
code (`demo_release_frontend`/`demo_release_level`) is EXONERATED for this hang; do
not re-test it for this again.

Consequence: native `.demo` PLAYBACK (cl_demo_play / CL_Demo_Play_f specifically) is
currently unreliable across at least two maps and survives a full restart, so it is
not a one-off state issue. Native RECORDING is a different code path
(CL_Demo_StartRecord/StopRecord, not CL_Demo_Play_f) and is NOT implicated by this
evidence either way.

## What changed as a result -- the custom (.dm_s2) recorder promoted to product-level

demo_playback::play (the .dm_s2 replay path) never calls CL_Demo_Play_f at all -- it
replays by feeding recorded messages back through CL_ParseServerMessage, a
structurally separate path unaffected by this hang. Its recorder
(demo_recording.cpp) was already fully hooked and running in the background
(CL_ParseServerMessage + CL_SavePredicted hooks install unconditionally at init),
but its start/stop commands (demo_start/demostart/demo_stop_record/demostop) were
registered via `dev_mode::add_command`, i.e. hidden unless developer mode is on --
so there was no product-facing way to trigger it, even though everything underneath
already worked.

Fixed by promoting those four commands to `GameUtil::addCommand` (dev_mode::
add_command is documented as "same contract... so a module can gate a command by
changing one call" -- this is that one call). Added `demo_recording::is_armed()`
(reads the demo_autorecord dvar) so the GUI can show "recording" the moment it is
requested rather than flickering unchecked until a file actually opens. Added a
second checkbox in the Demos tab, "Record with our own capture (.dm_s2)", next to
the existing native toggle, wired to demo_start/demo_stop_record.

NOT YET CONFIRMED IN GAME per the Fix Declaration Rules -- built, deployed
(hash-verified against the injection staging path C:\Users\joshu\OneDrive\Documents\
WWII\s2mp-mod.dll), and the game relaunched with it loaded via Launch-S2.ps1, but
the checkbox itself has not been exercised yet.

## Where this leaves native cl_demo_play PLAYBACK

Root cause still unknown -- only narrowed to "not the mod's frontend release,
something inside the engine's own CL_Demo_Play_f teardown." The renderer-worker
spin (0x8E6CF0 -> 0x8E6B20 -> 0x8E84D0 -> sub_89E4A0 -> CL_GetLocalClientActive's
Arxan dispatcher) is the next thing that would need real disassembly work to
resolve, not a console toggle. Until then: prefer the custom (.dm_s2) recorder for
anything that needs to be reliably PLAYED BACK.

# CUSTOM-THEATER CAMERA: THIRD-PERSON CRASH + FREECAM WON'T MOVE (2026-09-15)

User report: in CUSTOM (.dm_s2) playback the free camera turns but cannot move, and
third person crashes to desktop. Both root-caused statically plus one minidump.
Built + deployed. NOT yet tested in game -- CANDIDATE per the Fix Declaration Rules.

## THIRD PERSON CRASH -- PROVEN

Minidump s2_mp64_ship.exe.CL0.1789463143.dmp (10:05, built with the current DLL):
AV reading 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF inside sub_AF9B70. The dump tool's printed thread is
the dump writer; walking the EXCEPTION context's RSP gives the real top frame:
**IDA 0x9137B4** = the instruction after `sub_AF9B70()` @0x9137AE in
CL_Demo_FollowCameraMove (0x9135D0):

    CG_GetEntity(client, *((u16*)dvar_cl_demo_client + 8));   // value at +16
    ... sub_AF9B70();          // vec-copy entity origin -> freecam origin

CL_Demo_RegisterDvars: `dvar_cl_demo_client = sub_B0C70("2669", -1, -1, 48, 0)` --
DEFAULT -1. Only CL_Demo_Play_f sets it (from header +0x08). Custom theater never
does -> entity 0xFFFF -> garbage pointer -> crash.

FIX (theater_camera.cpp, ensure_follow_target): in the CG_IsTheaterFreeCamera stub,
before answering "third person", set cl_demo_client to the demo's own slot
(cg+22904, same value bonecam rides) via the engine's Dvar_SetInt (IDA 0xB29C0,
_b 0xB19C0; dvar ptr IDA 0x10F1AFF0, _b 0x10F19FF0). Verifies the value stuck;
on any failure answers false (stays first person) and prints once instead of
crashing. Dvar_SetInt/Dvar_SetVariant read in full: no retaddr check; SetVariant
enforces the -1..48 domain.

NOTE: tools/s2_crash_dump.py's "thread registers" block is the dump-writing thread
(rip in ntdll). For the faulting frame, read the exception stream's CONTEXT
(RSP @ +0x98, RIP @ +0xF8) and scan from there -- that is what named 0x9137B4.
The earlier 09:14 dump faulted inside s2mp-mod.dll but its PDB was overwritten by
the 09:58 rebuild, so it cannot be resolved now.

## FREECAM WON'T MOVE -- PROVEN, AND IT WAS OUR OWN STUB

CL_Demo_FreeCameraMove (0x913AE0) builds velocity from the usercmd CG_PredictPlayerState
takes out of the clientActive cmd ring (+25928, stride 128, & 0x7F):
    forwardmove (char) cmd+52   rightmove (char) cmd+53
    buttons cmd+8: bit0 -> up (+127), 0x800000 -> down (-127)
    angles cmd+16/+20/+24

demo_playback.cpp cl_create_cmd_stub zeroed cmd+0x8, +0x1C..+0x33, +0x34, +0x35,
+0x38 whenever the theater is armed. Angles (+0x10..+0x1B) were never stripped, so
look worked and movement did not -- exactly the report.

FIX: when theater_camera::custom_theater_freecam_active(), restore forwardmove,
rightmove and only buttons & (1 | 0x800000). Fire/ADS/weapon still stripped.
Residual risk: the loopback server also receives that movement; with CG_PredictPlayerState's
theater branch returning early there is no client-side pmove, so no visible effect
expected, but not measured.

## Also established
    CL_Demo_FreeCameraMove / FollowCameraMove extra gates: sub_91D920 / sub_91DA40
      (key-catcher 16 + a menu-name list open), sub_91D910 ("demo_error" menu open),
      and cg+22924 != 0. None implicated here.
    CL_CreateCmd (0x9DC60): pitch clamp -30..60 in third person, -88..88 in free cam.


# SEEK HANG + FOV "NOT FOUND" -- BOTH PROVEN, BOTH FIXED IN CODE (2026-09-15, later)

User report after the camera fix: freecam markers place correctly in the custom
theater, but a seek hung the game and FOV "can't find cg_fov". Built + deployed
(hash c06869c0...). NOT yet tested in game -- CANDIDATE.

## THE SEEK HANG -- a command NAME COLLISION left by the productisation pass

Log line: `[demo] seek -> 287634276 ms (forward from 288350)` after a dolly point
at 287346 ms.  288276 + 287346 x 1000 = 287,634,276 exactly.

Chain:
  dolly "Go" (demo_gui.cpp)  -> demo_native::seek_to_time(ms)
  seek_to_time               -> Cbuf "demo_seek <ms>"   (old native keyframe cmd)
  BUT demo_seek now belongs to demo_player = RELATIVE SECONDS
  -> seek_relative(287346 * 1000) -> custom seek_to(now + 287,346,000)

The productisation pass renamed the native command to `demo_seek_kf` and moved
`demo_skip` / `demo_skip_to` / `demo_seek_kf` under dev_mode::add_command, but
seek_to_time and seek_back still queued the OLD names. Two consequences:
  * backward native seeks (and Go) queued the relative-seconds command -> runaway
  * forward native seeks queued dev-only commands -> silently nothing outside dev mode
The CUSTOM theater has no footer bounds on an unfinalised .dm_s2 (battleship_2.0000
has 10,111 chunks, zero gen_footer, no eof), so nothing clamped the target.

Live evidence before killing the hung process (tools/dump_stacks.py --process):
the only in-module running thread sat at IDA 0x51B502 (FX update region), i.e.
the clock had jumped ~80 h via serverTimeDelta and the FX system was stepping it.

FIXES:
  * seek_back / seek_to_time queue `demo_seek_kf` (never bare `demo_seek`)
  * demo_skip, demo_skip_to, demo_seek_kf registered with GameUtil::addCommand
    (always) -- they are part of the product transport
  * dolly::go_to_point(i) + dolly::current_time(): Go/Retime now use the active
    system's absolute seek and clock (Retime used native-only demo_time_smooth)
  * backstops: demo_playback::seek_to_ms refuses a forward gap > 1 h;
    demo_native::skip_forward_ms refuses a skip > 1 h. Both print why.

LESSON (third time this file records it): after renaming or re-registering a
console command, grep the whole tree for its name. A Cbuf_AddText of a command
whose meaning changed compiles fine and fails at runtime -- here, as a hang.

## FOV -- cg_fov IS registered; it is an OBFUSCATED FLOAT

Live read (ReadProcessMemory, base verified per RULE A2):
    IDA 0x11111B8 -> dvar 'cg_fov'           type byte 0x0B
    IDA 0x11111C0 -> 'cg_fov1'               0x0B
    IDA 0x11111C8 -> 'cg_fov_intermission'   0x0B
    IDA 0x11111D0 -> '3078' (fovScale)       0x0B
    IDA 0x11111E0 -> 'cg_fov_override'       0x0B

0x0B = DVAR_TYPE_FLOAT_SECURE. Dvar_SetVariant (IDA 0xB30C0) case 0xB XOR-encodes
the value across +16..+31 with keys IDA 0xD90164..0xD90170 and a per-session slot
offset (dword_14DB5E8). demo_camera::fov() read +16 as a plain float -> junk ->
failed its 1..200 check -> "unavailable". The FOV feature never worked in EITHER
demo system.

GameUtil.cpp already had a file-local decodeDvarSecureFloat, verified here as the
exact inverse of that case-0xB chain. Exported as GameUtil::getDvarSecureFloat;
fov() now decodes by type byte. Setting still goes through `cg_fov N` on Cbuf.

⚠ sub_AF220 (the engine's obfuscated float getter) decompiles as `memset; return 0`
-- an Arxan stub. Do not call it; decode in-mod.
⚠ Remaining FOV caveat (unchanged): per-client scale at clientObf+4431600 beats
cg_fov_override when > 0, so FOV may appear stuck while scoped.


# CUSTOM-THEATER REWIND "GLITCHY" -- THREE DEFECTS, ALL READ OFF THE [rw] TRACE (2026-09-15)

User: rewind works but it is hard to land where you want; "press rewind twice then
forward once, and it doesn't always do it". The existing bounded [rw] trace in
main/s2mp_console.log named all three causes without a new probe.
Demo: battleship_2.0000.dm_s2 -- first snapshot 263950, NO footer (never finalised),
so g_play.bounds is empty and nothing clamps a seek. CANDIDATE, not yet tested.

## 1. Rewinding before the recording starts
Targets 258950 / 254003 / 249065 / 244106 while the file starts at 263950. Repeated
presses stack (rewind() subtracts from demo_clock_ms(), which is the PARKED target
while a seek is outstanding). No data exists there, so the seek never completes.
FIX: playback_t::earliest_snap -- min first-snapshot time, survives restarts; seek_to_ms
clamps targets below it to it.

## 2. The rewind freshness test fails at the start
service_seek treated a rewind as landed only when a snapshot arrived BELOW
rewind_from. Rewinding from the start makes the replay's first snapshot EQUAL
rewind_from (log 4482: 263950 vs 263950; 4568: 264150 vs 264150) -> never fresh ->
clock parked on the target forever (trace: serverTime frozen at 259004 while delta
keeps falling). This is the "press twice" glitch.
FIX: reset_snap_clock_for_rewind (demo_game.hpp:748) forces CA_SNAP_VALID = 0 at
restart, and only CL_ParseSnapshot on a replayed message sets it back. Fresh now =
snap < rewind_from OR snap.valid != 0. Works for finalised demos too, where
restart_time == bounds.first == the first replayed snapshot.

## 3. Forward seeks inherited a stalled rewind
seek_to_ms's forward path cleared rewind_ff_target but not rewind_from/rewind_fresh.
Log 4515-4544: forward to 268950, snap reached 269100, but 269100 is not below the
stale rewind_from 263950 -> never "done" -> clock parked at 269000. "Forward doesn't
always work". FIX: forward path clears rewind_from and rewind_fresh.

## Reading the [rw] trace, for next time
    service ... target=N  repeating with no `fresh` / `done`   -> the seek is stuck
    serverTime constant while delta keeps drifting            -> clock parked by service_seek
    [demo] first_snap seeded from snap.serverTime=T           -> T is the file's start


# ONE RECORDER AT A TIME + ON-SCREEN NOTICE FOR OUR CAPTURE (2026-09-15)

User request: only one demo recorder active at a time; show an on-screen notice of
which .dm_s2 is being recorded, as native does. Built + deployed. CANDIDATE.

## PROVEN -- the two engine functions that make exclusivity safe mid-match

    sub_910440 (IDA 0x910440, _b 0x90F440)
        return clc && &clc[client] && clc[client].demoState == 1;
      -> the per-message append gate (demo_utils already uses it as record_ready).
         Exposed as demo_native::native_recording().

    CL_Demo_StopRecord (IDA 0x90FCA0, _b 0x90ECA0), decompiled:
        gate connstate >= 5; reads demoState, ZEROES it; state 1 -> writes type-0
        terminator, footer body, NetConstStrings (sub_5DC650), closes via
        sub_9112F0, demoFileHandle = 0.
      -> after it, the append gate is false, so no further writes. It is the
         disconnect teardown. Exposed as demo_native::stop_native_recording(),
         called through the ENGINE address so cl_demo_stop_record_stub still runs
         the public-match type-21 repair and the auto-rename. CLIENT THREAD ONLY.

CL_Demo_StartRecord contains NO on-screen notice call, so native's notice comes
from elsewhere (not traced). Ours is drawn by the mod.

## Behaviour
  demo_start (custom on):  native auto-record off; if native is writing THIS
                           match, StopRecord it now (file saved) -> no double capture
  demo_record 1 (native):  cancel our capture (demo_recording::cancel = disarm +
                           close/save); native starts at the next connect
  GUI checkboxes already route through those commands, so the rule holds for
  console use too. Tooltips say so.

## Notice
demo_recording::render_notice(), called from the existing R_EndFrame stub (no new
hook). "Recording demo: <file>" (red dot) on flush_buffer_to_file success,
"Saved demo: <file>" (green dot) in clear_session. 6 s, 1 s fade, top-centre at
8% height. Uses InternalConsole::consoleFont + getMaterialWhite (registered once,
never per frame). Written on the client thread, drawn on the render thread ->
mutex. No text-width function is mapped, so the panel is sized from the glyph count.

User: "very hard to distinguish what is a custom demo and native demo in the list".
Built + deployed (hash d9b5538a). User accepted the result ("perfect").

  * demo_library::describe_custom(path) -- reads only the first 4 KB of a .dm_s2,

    (filter hides rows only -- selection index is unchanged, so Play/Rename/Delete
    still target the same file), split count line, custom rows show map+date,

# DEMO FOV + SEEK PARITY (NATIVE == CUSTOM) + REPLAY CRASH (2026-09-15, later)

User: FOV "doesn't work for cinematics", seek/rewind "still buggy", third-person
crash fix confirmed working. "Must be identical for both native and custom."
Built + deployed. CANDIDATE -- not yet tested in game.

## FOV -- PROVEN why the dvar route could never work

    CG_RegisterFovDvars @0x507E0: cg_fov = sub_B0B60("cg_fov", default 65.0,
        min 50.0, max 100.0)  (dword_B37914 / B37904 / B37930, read from the IDB)
    then v15[10] = sub_3E750 -- the domain callback -- which accepts only
        sub_45830's range: floor 50, ceiling clamped into 70..100.
So `cg_fov 120` / `cg_fov 30` is REJECTED silently. The slider offered 45..160.

sub_48460 = the FINAL fov (callers CG_ApplyFov @0x4A850, sub_33CF0, sub_3F050 x2,
sub_2C4E0, sub_4EAD60). In theater third/free camera it does
`if (CG_IsTheaterFreeCamera || CG_IsTheaterOrbitCamera) v = sub_45760(client)`
(the cg_fov chooser) and returns clamp(max(dvar off_8B0DB00, v), 170).

FIX: hook sub_48460 (IDA 0x48460 - 0x1000 = 0x47460), `float __fastcall(unsigned
int)` (`mov edi, ecx` @0x4847B; not a forwarder; no retaddr check). While a demo
plays (native or custom), client 0: dolly key (fresh <250 ms) > override > engine.
Live play untouched. Display tab keeps cg_fov, clamped 50..100 honestly.
Dolly points now carry `fov` (captured from what is on screen), Catmull-Rom'd.

## NATIVE SEEK -- three PROVEN defects

1. SEEK WHILE PAUSED. CL_SetCGameTime @0x86D30, ACTIVE branch:
       if (CL_Demo_IsPaused() || CL_Demo_IsCompleted()) { ...;
           cls_realtime = serverTime - serverTimeDelta - 5; return; }
   BEFORE the feed loop. So `cls_realtime += gap` was undone next frame, no packets
   read: paused forward seek = nothing; paused rewind = stops on the keyframe.
   Engine's own answer, sub_919CE0 (reset/replay):
       *(BYTE*)(PlaybackData + 10) = 1; CL_SetCGameTime(c); *(BYTE*)(PlaybackData+10) = 0;
   CL_Demo_IsPaused = PlaybackData && cl_demo_pause && !PlaybackData[10].
   pump_cgame_time_now() transcribes that.
2. END OF DEMO KILLED THE SESSION. note_read_result on the 0 return set
   g_eof_seen AND g_native_playing = false, never reset. Afterwards every read was
   refused, demo_skip / demo_seek_kf said "no native demo playing", demo_player
   lost the transport, Stop could not disconnect. Rewind from the end: impossible.
   Now: session lives until clc.demoState (clc+262752) leaves 2 (poll_session, from
   Present, only after having SEEN 2); g_eof_seen cleared after every jump
   (ProcessKeyFrameJump sets PlaybackData[8] = 0).
3. seek_to_time was a Cbuf chain (demo_seek_kf; demo_skip_to). Now ONE synchronous
   seek_absolute_now(target) on the client thread: keyframe jump if backward
   (nearest <= target, else earliest), then skip + pump. Lands on the target, pause
   untouched. demo_skip / demo_skip_to / demo_seek_kf <ms> all route through it.

CL_Demo_JumpToStart_f @0x910480 read: scans slots, index != 0 -> sub_919CE0, else
ProcessKeyFrameJump(0). sub_919CE0 memsets the slot ring first, so its later reads
of slot 0 look like zeros in the decompile -- NOT trusted, not used.

## PARITY -- one contract in demo_player

    demo_player::current_time()   native cl.serverTime | custom clock (pending
                                   target while a seek is outstanding)
    demo_player::seek_absolute()  native seek_absolute_now | custom seek_to
    demo_player::seek_relative()  current_time() + ms  -> presses ACCUMULATE
    `demo_seek_to <ms> [play]`    the only way the GUI thread seeks

⛔ THREADING DEFECT FIXED: dolly Go and J called demo_playback::seek_to (custom)
directly from the DXGI Present thread -- it rewinds the ifstream and rewrites clock
state the client thread is feeding from. Now queued as demo_seek_to.

Custom: finish_playback's pause is tracked (paused_by_finish) and lifted by a rewind,
matching native resuming after a rewind from the end.

## THE 13:47 CRASH -- demo_player::play() called stop() then play()

Dump s2_mp64_ship.exe.CL0.1789476438.dmp: AV @ IDA_0x6DA8C5 SV_ChangeMaxClients,
SV_SpawnServer on the stack; log `[demo] playback stopped` -> `playback started`
-> `bootstrap StartServer` -> dead. The 12:51 dump (1789473081) is the same shape on
the asset limit (DB_RaiseAssetLimitError 0x78AC90 + SV_SpawnServer 0x6DC350).
Custom stop left the map + loopback server up, and Play started a second server.
FIX: same custom file -> `demo_seek_to 0 play`; anything else while a demo is loaded
-> stop (BOTH kinds now disconnect) + deferred `demo_play` from poll_pending()
once playing() is false for 1.5 s (30 s give-up).

## LOG EVIDENCE WAS BEING DELETED

Logfile::init removed main/s2mp_console.log on every launch, so the seek test the
user ran had left nothing. It now rotates to s2mp_console.prev.log.
